children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. That is the Real. Salutation to <s>Brahman</s>.
The <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Mādhava</s>.
<s>Vāgīśa</s> (Bṛhaspati) and the other gods, at the commencement of all undertakings,

children.text: yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanam // MJaiNy_1.0.1 //
children.translated_text: having bowed to whom they become accomplished in their purposes — to that <s>Gajānana</s> (Gaṇeśa) I bow. (MJaiNy 1.0.1)

children.text: yuktiṃ mānavatīṃ vidansthiradhṛtirbhede viśeṣārthabhāg āptohaḥ kramakṛtprayuktinipuṇaḥ ślādhyātideśonnatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowing reasoning possessed of authority, firm in resolve, gaining special advantage in [matters of] distinction, skilled in deliberation among trusted [counselors], expert in the arrangement of diplomacy, eminent through praiseworthy extension [of domain],

children.text: nityasphūrtyadhikāravāngatasadābādhaḥ svatantreśvaro jāgarti śrutimatprasaṅgacaritaḥ śrī bukkaṇakṣmāpatiḥ // MJaiNy_1.0.2 //
children.translated_text: ever-alert in [exercising] jurisdiction, eloquent, free from ever-present obstruction, a sovereign independent [ruler] — he shines forth, [his] conduct characterized by scriptural [observance] — the illustrious King <s>Bukkaṇa</s>. (MJaiNy 1.0.2)

children.text: yadbrahma pratipādyate praguṇayattatpañcamūrtiprathāṃ tatrāyaṃ sthitimūrtimākalayati śrī bukkaṇakṣmāpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Brahman</s> which is taught [in the Upaniṣads] — he promotes the manifestation of Its five forms; therein, this illustrious King <s>Bukkaṇa</s> embodies the 'form of maintenance' (<s>sthitimūrti</s>).

children.text: vidyātīrthamunistadātmani lasanmūrtistvanugrāhikā tenāsya svaguṇairakhaṇḍitaradaṃ sārvajñamuddyotate // MJaiNy_1.0.3 //
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Vidyātīrtha</s> is the 'gracious form' shining within that [king's] self; therefore, by his own qualities, the omniscience [of this king] shines forth with unbroken radiance. (MJaiNy 1.0.3)

children.text: indrasyā'ṅgiraso nalasya sumatiḥ śaibyasya medhātithir dhaumyo dharmasutasya vainyanṛpateḥ svaujā nimergautamiḥ /
children.translated_text: As <s>Aṅgiras</s> [was] to <s>Indra</s>, <s>Sumati</s> to <s>Nala</s>, <s>Medhātithi</s> to [King] <s>Śaibya</s>, <s>Dhaumya</s> to the son of <s>Dharma</s> (Yudhiṣṭhira), <s>Svaujā</s> to King <s>Vainya</s> (Pṛthu), <s>Gautamī</s> to <s>Nimer</s> (?),

children.text: pratyagdṛṣṭirarundhatīsahacaro rāmasya puṇyātmano yadvattasya vibhorabhūtkulagururmantrī tathā mādhavaḥ // MJaiNy_1.0.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pratyagdṛṣṭi</s>, the companion of <s>Arundhatī</s>, to the meritorious <s>Rāma</s> — just so is <s>Mādhava</s> the minister and family preceptor to that mighty lord. (MJaiNy 1.0.4)
He indeed, the life-breath of the learned, proficient in all scriptures,
composed the great <s>Nyāyamālā</s> on the doctrine of <s>Jaimini</s>. (MJaiNy 1.0.5)
Having praised it in the royal assembly, the heroic illustrious King <s>Bukka</s>
commanded <s>Mādhava</s>: 'Let there be an expansion (<s>vistara</s>) of this by you.' (MJaiNy 1.0.6)
He, having obtained unobstructed grace from the eminent <s>Bhāratītīrtha</s>,
the four-faced (Brahmā-like) lord of ascetics, became incomparably excellent. (MJaiNy 1.0.7)
Having composed [it], the teacher <s>Mādhava</s>, [making it] a source of delight to the learned,
expounds the <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālā</s> for the understanding of the young. (MJaiNy 1.0.8)

children.text: nyāyamālāyā ādau svakīyagranthatvadyotanāya svamudrārūpamanekārthagarbhe devatānamaskārapratipādakaṃ ślokaṃ paṭhati -
children.translated_text: At the beginning of the <s>Nyāyamālā</s>, in order to indicate that it is his own work, he recites a verse that serves as his seal (<s>mudrā</s>), pregnant with multiple meanings, and that conveys salutation to the deity:
[Start of MJaiNy 1,1.1]
<s>Vāgīśa</s> and the other gods, at the commencement of all undertakings,

children.text: yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanam // MJaiNy_1,1.1 //
children.translated_text: having bowed to whom they become accomplished in their purposes — to that <s>Gajānana</s> I bow. (MJaiNy 1,1.1)
[Start of MJaiNy 1,1.2]

children.text: iṣṭadevatāṃ namaskṛtya cikīrṣitārthaparipālanāya pālake svāmini vidyamānaṃ mahimānamanusmarati --
children.translated_text: Having saluted the chosen deity, in order to celebrate the greatness present in the patron lord who protects the intended purpose, [the author] recalls [his glory]:

children.text: yuktiṃ mānavatīṃ vidansthiradhṛtirbhede viśeṣārthabhāg āptohaḥ kramakṛtprayuktinipuṇaḥ ślādhyātideśonnatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowing reasoning possessed of authority, firm in resolve, gaining special advantage in [matters of] distinction, skilled in deliberation among trusted [counselors], expert in the arrangement of diplomacy, eminent through praiseworthy extension [of domain],

children.text: nityasphūrtyadhikāravāngatasadābādhaḥ svatantreśvaro jāgarti śrutimatprasaṅgacaritaḥ śrībukkaṇakṣmāpatiḥ // MJaiNy_1,1.2 //
children.translated_text: ever-alert in [exercising] jurisdiction, eloquent, free from ever-present obstruction, a sovereign independent [ruler] — he shines forth, [his] conduct characterized by scriptural [observance] — the illustrious King <s>Bukkaṇa</s>. (MJaiNy 1,1.2)

children.text:
atra cikīrṣite dharmaśāstre vartamānānāṃ dvādaśānāmadhyāyānāṃ ye pratipādyā arthāḥ, ye ca nītiśāstroktā rājadharmāḥ, te sarve 'pyasminbhūpatāvupalabhyante |
nītipakṣe - yuktiryogaḥ saṃdhiḥ |
sā ca yuktirmānavatī |
mānaḥ satkāraścaturṣu sāmabhedadānadaṇḍeṣūpāyeṣu prathama upāyaḥ |
vairiṇo buddhibhedo dvitīyaḥ |
etābhyāṃ dānadaṇḍāvapyupalakṣyete |
etaiścaturbhirūpāyairviśeṣeṇārthaṃ dhanaṃ bhajati prāpnoti |
etāvatā śatrukṣayaḥ kathitaḥ |
avaśiṣṭena svarājyapratipālanaprakāraḥ pratipadyate -- āpteṣvamātyaprabhṛtiṣu puruṣeṣu 'ayamīdṛśasya vyāpārasya yogyo nānyasya' ityevamūhāpohakuśalaḥ |
'rājasabhāyāmete
tapasvinaḥ pūjyā viprā dakṣiṇabhāga upaveśanīyāḥ, ete ca bhṛtyā vāmabhāge' iti kramaṃ karoti tattadgrāmeṣvadhikṛtānpuruṣānucitabuddhipradānena prayoktuṃ nipuṇaḥ |
samudraparyantatvenātibahalasya deśasyonnatiḥ samastavastusaṃpattiḥ |
sā ca pararāṣṭranivāsibhiḥ sakalapraṇibhiḥ ślāghyate |
'idaṃ kartavyam, idaṃ na' ityevaṃ kāryākāryaviṣayā sphūrtistasyāmadhikāro 'sya rājño nityaḥ sarvatrāpratihatabuddhitvāt |
gato nivāritaḥ satāṃ tapasvināmābādho vighno yenāsau gatasadābādhaḥ |
deśāntarādhipatīnāṃ rājñāmetadadhīnatvenāparapreṣyatvādayaṃ svatantraḥ |
jagadīśvarasya vidyātīrthamunerbhogamūrtitvenāyamīśvaraḥ |
yasya sabhāyāṃ goṣṭhīrūpaḥ prasaṅgo vedārthaviṣayatvena śrutimān |
yadīyaṃ caritamapi nirantaraṃ vedoktarahasyārthandhyānarūpatvena śrutimadbhavati so 'yaṃ śrutimatprasaṅgcaritaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whose conduct too, being constantly of the nature of meditation on the esoteric meaning taught in the <s>Vedas</s>, is 'scriptural' — he is one 'whose conduct and discourse are scriptural.'

children.text: evaṃvidho bukkabhūpatirantaḥ parameśvaradhyāne, bahiḥ prajāpālane ca nityaṃ jāgarti |
children.translated_text: Such a King <s>Bukka</s> is ever-wakeful — inwardly in meditation on the Supreme Lord, outwardly in the protection of his subjects.

children.text: yathā nītiśāstrokteṣu sāmabhedādiṣvayaṃ kuśalastathā sarvajñāvatāratvāddharmaśāstrokteṣu pramāṇādiprasaṅgānteṣvadhyāyārtheṣu kuśalaḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as he is skilled in the strategies of conciliation and the rest taught in <s>nītiśāstra</s>, so too, being an incarnation of omniscience, he is skilled in the subjects of the [twelve] chapters — from <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) to <s>prasaṅga</s> (incidental application) — as taught in <s>dharmaśāstra</s>.
And those chapter-subjects will be shown below. (Commentary on MJaiNy 1,1.2)

Here, in the present <s>dharmaśāstra</s>, the subjects taught in the twelve chapters, as well as all the royal duties stated in the <s>nītiśāstra</s> (political science), are all found in this king.
In the political aspect: <s>yukti</s> means alliance (<s>saṃdhi</s>). And that alliance is 'possessed of authority' (<s>mānavatī</s>). <s>Māna</s> means honor — i.e. the first among the four strategies of conciliation (<s>sāma</s>), dissension (<s>bheda</s>), gifts (<s>dāna</s>), and punishment (<s>daṇḍa</s>). The intellectual splitting of the enemy is the second. By these two, gifts and punishment are also implied. Through these four strategies, he specially obtains wealth. By this much, the destruction of enemies is described.
With the remainder, the manner of protecting one's own kingdom is conveyed: he is skilled in the deliberation 'this person is fit for this kind of task and not another' regarding trusted persons such as ministers. He maintains order: 'these ascetics and Brahmins are to be honored and seated on the right in the royal assembly, and these servants on the left.' He is expert in employing through proper judgment the persons appointed in their respective villages. The eminence of the territory, which extends to the ocean and is exceedingly vast, is its prosperity in all goods. And that [prosperity] is praised by all beings residing in foreign lands.
The alertness regarding 'this is to be done, this is not' — jurisdiction in this [matter] belongs to this king perpetually, since his intelligence is unobstructed everywhere. 'Free from ever-present obstruction' — he by whom the obstruction of the virtuous and ascetics is removed. This [king] is independent, since other regional rulers are subordinate to him and are like his servants. He is 'lord' (<s>īśvara</s>) by virtue of being the embodiment of enjoyment of the Lord of the Universe, the sage <s>Vidyātīrtha</s>. In whose assembly the discourse (<s>prasaṅga</s>), being in the form of deliberation, has Vedic content — thus it is 'scriptural' (<s>śrutimat</s>).
[Start of MJaiNy 1,1.3]
He demonstrates the king's omniscience with supporting reasoning:

children.text: yadbrahma pratipādyate praguṇayattatpañcamūrtiprathāṃ tatrāyaṃ sthitimūrtimākalayati śrī bukkaṇakṣmāpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Brahman</s> which is taught [in the Upaniṣads] — he promotes the manifestation of Its five forms; therein, this illustrious King <s>Bukkaṇa</s> embodies the 'form of maintenance.'

children.text: vidyātīrthamunistadātmani lasanmūrtistvanugrāhikā tenāsya svaguṇairakhaṇḍitapadaṃ sārva muddyotate // MJaiNy_1,1.3 //
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Vidyātīrtha</s> is the 'gracious form' shining within that [king's] self; therefore, by his own qualities, the omniscience [of this king] shines forth with unbroken splendor. (MJaiNy 1,1.3)

children.text: sarvāsūpaniṣatsu pratīyamānaṃ yatparaṃ brahma tadeva śaivāgameṣu sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhāranirodhanānugrahalakṣaṇapañcakṛtya siddhyarthamīśānatatpuruṣāghoravāmadevasadyojātalakṣaṇānāṃ pañcānāṃ mūrtīnāṃ prathāṃ prasiddhiṃ vistāraṃ vā praguṇayati prakaṭī karotīti pratipādyate |
children.translated_text: The supreme <s>Brahman</s> that is apprehended in all the Upaniṣads — that very [Brahman] is taught in the Śaiva <s>āgamas</s> as promoting the manifestation — i.e. the fame, or the expansion — of the five forms characterized as <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, and <s>Sadyojāta</s>, for the accomplishment of the five activities of creation, maintenance, dissolution, concealment, and grace.

children.text: tatra tāsu mūrtiṣvayaṃ bhūpālaḥ sthitimūrtiṃ dhatte |
children.translated_text: Therein, among those forms, this king bears the 'form of maintenance' (<s>sthitimūrti</s>).

children.text: tasyā mūrterātmani lasanvidyātīrthamuniḥ kṛtsnasya jagato 'nugrāhikā mūrtirityucyate |
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Vidyātīrtha</s>, shining within the self of that [maintenance-]form, is said to be the 'gracious form' for the entire world.

children.text: yasmādayaṃ bhūpo vedāntoktaṃ paraṃ brahma, yasmāccā'gamoktā maheśvarasya sthitimūrtiḥ, yasmācca śrīvidyātīrthamunistadātmani saṃnidhāya prakāśate, tasmātsarvajñatvamasya rājña utkarṣeṇā'vidva- daṅganāgopālamavivādena pratibhāsate || MJaiNyC_1,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: Since this king is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> taught in <s>Vedānta</s>, since he is the 'maintenance-form' of <s>Maheśvara</s> taught in the <s>āgamas</s>, and since the illustrious sage <s>Vidyātīrtha</s> shines forth in proximity within his self — therefore, the omniscience of this king manifests eminently, undisputed even by the unlearned, women, cowherds, and all. (Commentary on MJaiNy 1,1.3)
[Start of MJaiNy 1,1.4]
He praises the minister of the king endowed with the stated qualities, using illustrative examples well-known from various <s>Purāṇas</s>, as one who acts for [the king's] benefit:

children.text: indrasyāṅgiraso nalasya sumatiḥ śaivyasya medhātithir dhaumyo dharmasutasya vainyanṛpateḥ svaujā nimergautamiḥ /
children.translated_text: As <s>Aṅgiras</s> to <s>Indra</s>, <s>Sumati</s> to <s>Nala</s>, <s>Medhātithi</s> to <s>Śaibya</s>, <s>Dhaumya</s> to the son of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Svaujā</s> to King <s>Vainya</s>, <s>Gautamī</s> to <s>Nimer</s>,

children.text: pratyagdṛṣṭirarundhatīsahacaro rāmasya puṇyātmano yadvattasya vibhorabhūtkulagururmantrī tathā mādhavaḥ // MJaiNy_1,1.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pratyagdṛṣṭi</s>, the companion of <s>Arundhatī</s>, to the meritorious <s>Rāma</s> — just so is <s>Mādhava</s> the minister and family preceptor to that mighty lord. (MJaiNy 1,1.4)
[Start of MJaiNy 1,1.5]
To generate great faith in the treatise to be composed, he reveals the authority of the author:
The wise <s>Mādhava</s>, upholder of <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, and righteous conduct,

children.text: smārtaṃ vyākhyāya sarvārthaṃ dvijārthaṃ śrauta udyataḥ // MJaiNy_1,1.5 //
children.translated_text: having expounded all the <s>smārta</s> (Smṛti-based) matters, now undertakes the <s>śrauta</s> (Vedic ritual-based [exposition]) for the sake of the twice-born. (MJaiNy 1,1.5)
For the benefit of all varṇas and āśramas, the <s>smārta dharma</s> was previously expounded through commentaries on the essence of the Purāṇas, the <s>Pārāśarasmṛti</s>, and the like.

children.text: idānīṃ dvijānāṃ viśeṣānu grahāya śrautadharmavyākhyānāya pravṛttaḥ || MJaiNyC_1,1.5 ||
children.translated_text: Now, for the special benefit of the twice-born, [he] has undertaken the exposition of <s>śrauta dharma</s>. (Commentary on MJaiNy 1,1.5)
[Start of MJaiNy 1,1.6]

children.text: granthamāripsurgurumūrtyupādhikaṃ sakalavedaśāstrapravartakatvenātrociteṣṭadevatārūpaṃ parameśvaramādau namaskṛtya śrotṛpravṛttisiddhyarthaṃ viṣayaprayojane darśayaṃstaṃ granthaṃ pratijānīte --
children.translated_text: Wishing to compose the treatise, having first saluted <s>Parameśvara</s> — who is in the form of the chosen deity appropriate here, by virtue of being the cause of all <s>Vedas</s> and <s>śāstras</s>, through the medium of the preceptor's form — and showing the subject-matter and purpose in order to secure the audience's engagement, he declares the treatise:
Having bowed to the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) in the form of <s>Śrī Vidyātīrtha</s>,
the <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālā</s> is clearly summarized in verses. (MJaiNy 1,1.6)
The <s>adhikaraṇas</s> (topics of inquiry) that determine <s>dharma</s>, as propounded by <s>Jaimini</s>, are the <s>nyāyas</s> (principles).
They are the subject-matter of this treatise.

children.text: paṭhituṃ suśakaiḥ katipayaireva ślokaisteṣāṃ sphuṭībhāvaḥ prayojanam |
children.translated_text: The purpose is their clarification through merely a few verses, easy to recite.

children.text: nyāyamālā saṃgṛhyata iti granthanāmanirdeśapūrvikā pratijñā || MJaiNyC_1,1.6 ||
children.translated_text: The statement of the name of the treatise, preceded by the thesis, is: 'the <s>Nyāyamālā</s> is summarized.' (Commentary on MJaiNy 1,1.6)
[Start of MJaiNy 1,1.7-8]
He shows the method of the treatise to be composed:
One verse expresses the subject-matter, doubt, prima facie view, and their appearance;
the other verse states the established conclusion — this is generally the case. (MJaiNy 1,1.7)
The four components are stated in one verse in some places;

children.text: yatra kvāpi bahuślokairucyante 'to na vistaraḥ // MJaiNy_1,1.8 //
children.translated_text: where they are stated in many verses, no expansion [beyond two thousand is intended]. (MJaiNy 1,1.8)

children.text: ekaikasyādhikaraṇasya viṣayaḥ, saṃdehaḥ, saṃgatiḥ, pūrvapakṣaḥ, siddhāntaśceti paścāvayavāḥ |
children.translated_text: Each <s>adhikaraṇa</s> has five components: subject-matter (<s>viṣaya</s>), doubt (<s>saṃdeha</s>), connection (<s>saṃgati</s>), prima facie view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>), and established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>).

children.text: tatra saṃgatiranantarameva vyutpādayiṣyamāṇena prakāreṇa pratyadhikaraṇaṃ svayamevohituṃ śakyate |
children.translated_text: Therein, the connection (<s>saṃgati</s>) can be inferred by oneself for each <s>adhikaraṇa</s> by the method that will be explained shortly.

children.text: avaśiṣṭānāṃ caturṇāmavayavānāṃ saṃgrāhakāḥ kvacidbhahavaḥ ślokāḥ, kvacideka ityāvāpodvāpābhyāmantataḥ pratyadhikaraṇaṃ ślokadvitve saṃkhyā paryavasyati |
children.translated_text: Of the remaining four components, the summarizing verses are many in some places, one in others — thus, by inclusion and exclusion, the count settles at a minimum of two verses per <s>adhikaraṇa</s>.

children.text: ato bahutvādbibhyatā granthagauravaśaṅkā na kartavyā || MJaiNyC_1,1.7 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, one who fears prolixity should not entertain the apprehension of textual heaviness. (Commentary on MJaiNy 1,1.7)
[Start of MJaiNy 1,1.9]
Making that very non-heaviness of the treatise clear, and showing its easy comprehensibility through a poetic figure:
In every case, the compendium does not exceed two thousand [verses];
thereby, the ocean of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> becomes [like] a pleasure-lake. (MJaiNy 1,1.9)

children.text:
ślokena ślokābhyāṃ ślokairvā yathāsaṃbhavaṃ nyāyaḥ saṃgṛhyatām |
sarvathāpisahasranyāyasaṃgraharūpo granthaḥ ślokasahasradvayapūrterarvāgeva samāṃpsyate, na tu sahasradvayamattikrāmati |
bhāṣyaṭīkādīnāṃ bahutvādduravagāhatvācca mīmāṃsā sāgarasabhā pūrvamāsīt |
kriyamāṇenānena granthena doṣadvayarahitena rājaputrāṇāṃ bālānāṃ krīḍārthaṃ nirmitayā nābhidaghnyā puṣkariṇyā samā bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: Through this treatise being composed, free from both defects [of prolixity and obscurity], it will become like a pleasure-lake built for the sport of princes and young ones, reaching only to the navel.

children.text: yadyapi śāstradīpikādau kvacitkvacitsaṃgrahaśloko 'sti, tathāpi na sarvatra vidyate |
children.translated_text: Although in the <s>Śāstradīpikā</s> and similar [works] there is occasionally a summary verse here and there, nevertheless it is not found everywhere.
And where it exists, since the subject-matter and doubt are not summarized [together], an <s>adhikaraṇa</s> cannot be presented by the mere recitation of a verse.

children.text: ato na kvāpi gatārthatvaṃ śaṅkanīyam || MJaiNyC_1,1.9 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, the suspicion of redundancy should not be entertained anywhere. (Commentary on MJaiNy 1,1.9)

Whether by one verse, two verses, or more as appropriate, each <s>nyāya</s> is summarized. In every case, the treatise, being in the form of a summary of a thousand <s>nyāyas</s>, will be completed well within the limit of two thousand verses, and does not exceed two thousand. Due to the multiplicity and inaccessibility of the <s>bhāṣyas</s> (commentaries), <s>ṭīkās</s> (sub-commentaries), and the like, <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> was previously like an ocean.
[Start of MJaiNy 1,1.10]
He teaches the [method of] connection (<s>saṃgati</s>):
Connections (<s>saṃgatis</s>) are threefold: in the treatise [as a whole], in the chapter, and in the quarter (<s>pāda</s>).
When the subject-matter of the treatise and the like is known, the respective connection should be inferred. (MJaiNy 1,1.10)
Connection is threefold: connection of the treatise, connection of the chapter, and connection of the quarter.

children.text: sā ca śāstrādīnāṃ trayāṇāmasādharaṇe viṣaye jñāte sati svayamepvohituṃ śakyā || MJaiNyC_1,1.10 ||
children.translated_text: And that [connection], when the uncommon subject-matter of the three — treatise, etc. — is known, can be inferred by oneself. (Commentary on MJaiNy 1,1.10)
[Start of MJaiNy 1,1.11-12]
He shows the uncommon subject-matter of the treatise and of the chapters:
<s>Dharma</s> is to be ascertained through twelve characteristics; those characteristics are named:
<s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge), <s>bheda</s> (distinction), <s>śeṣatva</s> (subsidiarity), <s>prayukti</s> (application), <s>krama</s> (order), <s>saṃjñā</s> (designation), (MJaiNy 1,1.11)
<s>adhikāra</s> (eligibility), <s>atideśa</s> (extension), <s>sāmānya</s> (generality) and <s>viśeṣa</s> (particularity),

children.text: ūho bādhaśca tantraṃ ca prasaṅgaścoditāḥ kramāt // MJaiNy_1,1.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>ūha</s> (adaptation), <s>bādha</s> (abrogation), <s>tantra</s> (economy), and <s>prasaṅga</s> (incidental application) — these are stated in order. (MJaiNy 1,1.12)

children.text:
lakṣaṇānyadhyāyāḥ |
dvādaśānāṃ lakṣaṇānāṃ samāhāro dvādaśalakṣaṇī |
tādṛśasya dvādaśalakṣaṇopetasya śāstrasya dharmo viṣayaḥ |
pramāṇādayaḥ prasaṅgāntā dvādaśa padārthāḥ kramāddvādaśānāmadhyāyānāṃ viṣayāḥ |
prathame 'dhyāye - vidhyarthavādādirūpaṃ pramāṇaṃ nirūpitam |
dvitīye-yāgadānādi karmabhedaḥ |
tṛtīye - prayājādīnāṃ darśapūrṇamāsādyarthatvena taccheṣatvam |
caturthe - 'godohanasya puruṣārthatvaprayuktyānuṣṭhānam, na tu kratvarthatvaprayuktyā' ityevamādayaḥ |
pañcame - kramaniyatividheyatvādayaḥ |
ṣaṣṭhe - 'karturadhikāro nāndhādeḥ' ityādayaḥ |
saptame -"samānaṣitaracchayenena"ityādipratyakṣavacanena, agnihotrādināmnānumitavacanena ca sāṃmānyato 'tideśaḥ |
aṣṭame -"saurye caruṃ nirvapet"ityatra nirvāpastaddhitena devatānirdeśa ekadevatātvamauṣadhadravyakatvamiti liṅgenā'gneyapuroḍāśetikartavyataiva, nānyasyetyevamādirviśeṣato 'tideśaḥ |
navame - prakṛtau"agnaye juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi"iti paṭhite mantre vikṛtau sauryacarāvagnipadaparityāgena sūryapadaprakṣepeṇa 'sūryāya juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi ' ityevamādyūhaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the ninth, when the mantra 'I offer to <s>Agni</s> what is pleasing' is recited in the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>), in the ectype (<s>vikṛti</s>) — the <s>Saurya</s> cooked-rice offering — by dropping the word '<s>Agni</s>' and inserting the word '<s>Sūrya</s>,' [the mantra becomes] 'I offer to <s>Sūrya</s> what is pleasing' — this and similar [adaptations] constitute <s>ūha</s> (modification).

children.text: daśame - kṛṣṇaleṣu codakaprāptasyāvaghātasya vituṣīkaraṇāsaṃbhavena lopa ityevamādirbādhaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the tenth, since husking (<s>vituṣīkaraṇa</s>) is impossible for black seeds, the pounding (<s>avaghāta</s>) that is scripturally prescribed is dropped — this and similar [cases] constitute <s>bādha</s> (supersession).

children.text: ekādaśe - bahūnāmagneyādīnāṃ pradhānānāṃ sakṛdanuṣṭhitena prayājādyaṅgenopakāra iti tantram |
children.translated_text: In the eleventh, when a subsidiary [rite] such as a preliminary offering (<s>prayāja</s>), performed once, serves multiple principal [rites] like the <s>Āgneya</s> and others — this is <s>tantra</s> (economy of rites).

children.text: dvādaśe - pradhānasya paśorupakārāyānuṣṭhitena prayājādyaṅgena paśvaṅgapuroḍāṣe 'pyupakāra ityādiprasaṅgaḥ || MJaiNyC_1,1.11-12 ||
children.translated_text: In the twelfth, when a subsidiary such as the preliminary offering, performed to serve the principal animal [sacrifice], also serves the animal's subsidiary rice-cake — this and similar [cases] constitute <s>prasaṅga</s> (incidental application). (MJaiNyC 1.1.11-12)

The defining characteristics [are the topics of the] chapters. The collection of twelve defining characteristics is the 'twelve-characteristic [treatise]' (<s>dvādaśalakṣaṇī</s>). <s>Dharma</s> is the subject of such a treatise possessing twelve defining characteristics. The twelve categories, from <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) through to <s>prasaṅga</s> (incidental application), are the subjects of the twelve chapters in order. In the first chapter, the means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), consisting of injunctions (<s>vidhi</s>), explanatory passages (<s>arthavāda</s>), and the like, is examined. In the second, the classification of rites (<s>karmabheda</s>) — sacrifice, gift, and the like. In the third, the subsidiary nature (<s>śeṣatva</s>) of preliminary rites (<s>prayāja</s>) and the like with respect to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and other [principal rites]. In the fourth, [topics] such as: 'The milking of the cow is performed as a human purpose (<s>puruṣārtha</s>), not as a purpose of the ritual (<s>kratvārtha</s>).' In the fifth, [topics like] what is to be enjoined regarding the fixed order (<s>kramaniyati</s>), and the like. In the sixth, [topics like] 'The qualified person (<s>adhikārin</s>) is the performer; not a blind person, and the like.' In the seventh, the general extension (<s>atideśa</s>) through explicit statement, as in '<s>samāna</s> with the <s>Iṣṭaracchyena</s>,' and through inferred statement in the case of <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like. In the eighth, the specific extension (<s>atideśa</s>) [illustrated by]: in the passage 'One should offer cooked rice in the Saurya [sacrifice],' the offering (<s>nirvāpa</s>), the indication of the deity through the <s>taddhita</s> suffix, the single-deity nature, and the herbal-substance nature — through these signs (<s>liṅga</s>), only the procedure of the <s>Āgneya</s> rice-cake [is extended], and no other.
[Beginning of MJaiNy 1.1.13]
He shows the specific subject matter of the [four] sections (<s>pādas</s>):
Injunction (<s>vidhi</s>), explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>), tradition (<s>smṛti</s>), and name (<s>nāma</s>) — these four [types],
through the four sections of the first chapter, the means of knowledge (<s>māna</s>) is declared. (MJaiNy 1.1.13)

children.text:
prathame pāde - vidhirūpaṃ mānamīritam |
dvitīye - arthavādarūpam |
arthavādo mantrasyāpyupalakṣakaḥ |
tṛtīye - smṛtirūpam | smṛtirācāramapyupalakṣayati |

children.translated_text: In the fourth, [the means of knowledge] in the form of name, as in '<s>ubhdiñcitrādi</s>' and the like. (MJaiNyC 1.1.13)

In the first section, the means of knowledge in the form of injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) is declared. In the second, in the form of explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>). <s>Arthavāda</s> also implies (<s>upalakṣaka</s>) mantra. In the third, in the form of tradition (<s>smṛti</s>). <s>Smṛti</s> also implies customary practice (<s>ācāra</s>).
[Beginning of MJaiNy 1.1.14]
Introduction, the means of [establishing] rite-classification, the exception to that,
and the difference of application — these are the [topics] belonging to the sections of the second chapter. (MJaiNy 1.1.14)

children.text: dvitīyādhyāyasya prathame pāde - ākhyātamevāpūrvabodhakam, apūrvasabhdāvaścetyādikaḥ karmabhedacintopayukta upodghāto varṇitaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the first section of the second chapter, the introduction useful for the inquiry into rite-classification is described — [topics] such as: 'Only the verbal root (<s>ākhyāta</s>) conveys the unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>), and [the question of] the word <s>apūrva</s>,' and the like.
In the second, rite-classification through verbal root differentiation, repetition, and the like.
In the third, the refutation of the authority [for establishing] rite-classification regarding <s>Rathantara</s> and the like.
In the fourth, the difference of application between obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) and desire-motivated (<s>kāmya</s>) [rites]. (MJaiNyC 1.1.14)
[Beginning of MJaiNy 1.1.15]
Scripture (<s>śruti</s>), indication (<s>liṅga</s>), sentence (<s>vākya</s>) and the like, conflict, apprehension,
non-inaugural statements (<s>anārabhyokti</s>), multiple-purposefulness (<s>bahvartha</s>), and ownership (<s>svāmyartha</s>) — these are the [topics of the] eight sections. (MJaiNy 1.1.15)

children.text:
tṛtīyādhyāyasya prathame pāde - śeṣatvabodhakānāṃ śrutiliṅgādīnāṃ madhye śrutirvicāritā |
dvitīye - liṅgam |
tṛtīye - vākyaprakaraṇādi |
caturthe - nivītopavītādiṣvarthavādatvavidhitvādinirṇayahetuḥ śrutyādeḥ parasparavirodhasadasabhdāvaḥ |

children.translated_text: In the fifth, the rites of apprehension (<s>pratipatti</s>).
In the sixth, [passages that are] studied without inaugurating [a new rite] (<s>anārabhyādhīta</s>).
In the seventh, preliminary offerings and the like that serve multiple principal [rites].
In the eighth, [rites belonging to] the sacrificer (<s>yājamāna</s>). (MJaiNyC 1.1.15)

In the first section of the third chapter, among the means of conveying subsidiary status — scripture (<s>śruti</s>), indication (<s>liṅga</s>), and the like — scripture is examined. In the second, indication. In the third, sentence and context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) and the like. In the fourth, the cause for determining whether [passages] concerning <s>nivīta</s>, <s>upavīta</s>, and the like are explanatory passages (<s>arthavāda</s>) or injunctions (<s>vidhi</s>) — [namely,] the presence or absence of mutual conflict among scripture and the other [means].
[Beginning of MJaiNy 1.1.16]
The prompting role of the principal, the prompting role of the non-principal,
the inquiry into fruits, and the inquiry into the lowest subsidiary — these are the [topics] of the fourth [chapter]. (MJaiNy 1.1.16)

children.text: caturthādhyāyasya prathame pāde - pradhānabhūtā'mikṣā dadhyānayanasya prayojikesyādi pradhānaprayoktṛtvaṃ vicāritam |
children.translated_text: In the first section of the fourth chapter, the prompting role of the principal is examined — [for example,] 'The <s>āmikṣā</s> (curd-mixture), being principal, is the prompter of the fetching of curd,' and the like.
In the second, the prompting role of the non-principal — 'The non-principal removal of the calf is the prompter of the branch-cutting,' and the like.

In the third, the inquiry into whether effects such as the avoidance of evil reputation (<s>apāpāśloka</s>) are or are not the fruits of [rites involving] ladles made of <s>palāśa</s> leaf and the like.
In the fourth, the inquiry into the lowest subsidiary — the dice-play and the like belonging to the <s>Rājasūya</s>. (MJaiNyC 1.1.16)
[Beginning of MJaiNy 1.1.17]
Order through scripture and the like, its special features, increase and non-increase,
and the relative strength of scripture and the like — these are the [topics] belonging to the sections of the fifth chapter. (MJaiNy 1.1.17)

children.text: pañcamādhyāyasya prathame pāde - śrutyarthapāṭhādibhiḥ kramo nirūpitaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the first section of the fifth chapter, order (<s>krama</s>) is determined through scripture, meaning, recitation-order (<s>pāṭha</s>), and the like.
In the second, special features of order — such as 'In the seventeen animals belonging to the <s>Vājapeya</s>, one property is completed at a time,' and the like.

In the third, increase (<s>vṛddhi</s>) — 'By repeating the five preliminary offerings and the like, [they become] eleven' and the like — and non-increase — 'The <s>Adābhya</s>, <s>Graha</s>, and <s>Citriṇī</s> are not repeated,' and the like.
In the fourth, the relative strength and weakness of the determinants of order — scripture, meaning, recitation-order, and the like. (MJaiNyC 1.1.17)
[Beginning of MJaiNy 1.1.18]
The qualified person (<s>adhikārin</s>), his properties, substitution (<s>pratinidhi</s>), dropping of elements (<s>arthalopa</s>),

children.text: dīkṣā satraṃ deyuhnī ṣaṣṭhe pādeṣvamī sthitāḥ // MJaiNy_1,1.18 //
children.translated_text: consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>), session (<s>satra</s>), what is to be given (<s>deya</s>), and fire (<s>agni</s>) — these are established in the sections of the sixth [chapter]. (MJaiNy 1.1.18)

children.text:
ṣaṣṭhādhyāyasya prathame pāde - karmādhikāraḥ karturasti, andhādernāsti, striyā asti, sa ca patyā saha, ityevamādinādhikārī nirūpitaḥ |
dvitīye - tatrādhikāriṇāṃ pratyekaṃ kṛtsnnaṃ phalam, darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ kartraikyaniyamaḥ, kāmyaṃ karma samāpanīyam, ityevamādayo 'dhikāridharmā uktāḥ |
tṛtīye - dravyasya pratinidhirasti, devādīnāmagnyādīnāmadhikāriṇaśca sa nāsti, ityādinirūpaṇam |
caturthe - padārthalopanaṃ vicāritam, 'avattanāśe tatyājyena yajet, iḍājyasya nāśe sati śeṣānnaṃ grāhyam' ityādikam |
pañcame - kālāparādhena candrodaye satyabhyudayeṣṭiḥ prāyaścittam , jyotiṣṭomasyaikādayo dīkṣāḥ, dvādaśāhasya dvādaśa dīkṣāḥ, ityādi nirūpitam |
children.translated_text: In the fifth, [topics like] 'When there is a lapse of time, the <s>Abhyudayeṣṭi</s> at moonrise is an expiation; the consecrations (<s>dīkṣā</s>) for the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> are first [performed]; for the twelve-day [rite], twelve consecrations,' and the like.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe - tatrādhikāriṇastulyakalpā eva, satraṃ viprasyaiva, ityevamādikaṃ cintitam |
children.translated_text: In the sixth, [topics like] 'The qualified persons there are of equal status; the session (<s>satra</s>) is for the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> alone,' and the like.

children.text: saptame - pitrādikaṃ na deyam, mahābhūmirna deyā, ityevamādirdeyavicāraḥ |
children.translated_text: In the seventh, the inquiry into what is to be given — 'The patrimony and the like should not be given; the great land should not be given,' and the like.

children.text: aṣṭame - laukikāgnā vupanayanahomaḥ, sthapatīṣṭistathaiva, ityevamādyagnivicāraḥ kṛtaḥ || MJaiNyC_1,1.18 ||
children.translated_text: In the eighth, the inquiry into fire — 'The <s>upanayana</s> <s>homa</s> is in the domestic fire; the <s>sthapati-iṣṭi</s> likewise,' and the like. (MJaiNyC 1.1.18)

In the first section of the sixth chapter, the qualified person is determined — 'The right to perform rites belongs to the performer; it does not belong to a blind person and the like; it does belong to a woman, but together with her husband,' and the like. In the second, the properties of the qualified person — 'Each individual qualified person receives the complete fruit; the unity of performer is the rule for the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>; a desire-motivated rite must be completed,' and the like. In the third, the examination: 'There is substitution for substances; there is no substitution for deities, fires, and the qualified person,' and the like. In the fourth, the dropping of elements is examined — 'When butter is destroyed, one should sacrifice with ghee; when the <s>iḍā</s>-ghee is destroyed, the remaining food should be taken,' and the like.
[Beginning of MJaiNy 1.1.19]
Extension through explicit statement, its remainder, the examination of <s>Sāman</s>,
and the two extensions through name and indication — these are the [topics] belonging to the sections of the seventh chapter. (MJaiNy 1.1.19)
In the first section of the seventh chapter, extension through explicit statement — as in '<s>samāna</s> with the <s>Iṣṭaracchyena</s>,' and the like.

children.text: dvitīye - rathantaraśabdena gānamātrābhidhāyinā gānasyaivātideśyatvamityetādṛśaḥ pūrvoktātideśasya śeṣo vicāritaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the second, the remainder of the previously stated extension is examined — such as: 'By the word <s>Rathantara</s>, which denotes merely a chant (<s>gāna</s>), it is the chant alone that is extended.'
In the third, extension through the name — [as in the case of] <s>Agnihotra</s>.
In the fourth, extension through indication — [as in the case of] the offering substance (<s>nirvāpa</s>), the herbal ingredient, and the like. (MJaiNyC 1.1.19)
[Beginning of MJaiNy 1.1.20]
From a clear indication, then from an unclear one, from a stronger [indication], and through exceptions —
the specific features of extension are the [topics] belonging to the sections of the eighth chapter. (MJaiNy 1.1.20)

children.text:
aṣṭamādhyāyasya prathame pāde - spaṣṭena liṅgenātideśaviśeṣaḥ |
tadyathā sauryacarārvatideśakāni nirvāpaḥ, taddhitena devatānirdeśaḥ, ekadevatatvam, auṣadhadravyakatvam, ityādīni spaṣṭānyagniyaliṅgāni |
dvitīye tu-aspaṣṭairliṅgaratideśaḥ |
tadyathā - vājine haviḥ sāmānyena liṅgena payovidhyanto 'tidiśyate |
tatra liṅgamaspaṣṭam |
śīghraṃ tadbuddhyanutpādanāt |
tṛtīye - prabalena liṅgenātideśaḥ |
tadyathā - ābhicārikaṣṭāvāgnāvaiṣṇavasārasvatabārhaspatyeṣu haviḥṣu tritvena liṅgena yathākramamāgneyādividhyante prāpte dvidaivatyatvena liṅgena prathama āgnāvaiṣṇave tṛtīyasāyāgnīṣomīyasya vidhyanto 'tidiṣṭaḥ |

children.translated_text: The two-deity nature is the stronger [indication],
because it produces immediate understanding from the mere utterance of the word.
But order, being of slow understanding, is weaker.
In the fourth, the extension in ladle-oblations (<s>darvihoma</s>) is disputed. (MJaiNyC 1.1.20)

In the first section of the eighth chapter, the specific features of extension through a clear indication [are discussed]. For example, the indicators of extension for the <s>Saurya</s> cooked-rice offering are: the offering (<s>nirvāpa</s>), the indication of deity through the <s>taddhita</s> suffix, the single-deity nature, and the herbal-substance nature — these are clear signs of the <s>Āgneya</s> [model]. In the second, extension through unclear indications. For example, in the <s>Vājin</s> [sacrifice], through the general indication, the injunction of milk as an offering is extended. There, the indication is unclear, because it does not quickly produce understanding. In the third, extension through a stronger indication. For example, when in the sorcery rites (<s>ābhicārika</s>), among the oblations of <s>Āgni-Vaiṣṇava</s>, <s>Sārasvata</s>, and <s>Bārhaspatya</s>, through the indication of [each having] three [deities], the <s>Āgneya</s> and other [procedures] are to be extended in order; but through the stronger indication of having two deities (<s>dvidaivatya</s>), in the first <s>Āgni-Vaiṣṇava</s> [oblation], the procedure of the third <s>Sāyāgni-Saumya</s> (Āgnīṣomīya) is extended.
[Beginning of MJaiNy 1.1.21]
The commencement of <s>ūha</s> (modification), the <s>Sāman</s>-modification, the mantra-modification, and matters arising from that —
these are declared in the four sections of the ninth chapter. (MJaiNy 1.1.21)

children.text:
navamādhyāyasya prathame pāde - upodghātapūrvakamūhavicāraprārambhaḥ |
tatra prayājādayo dharmā apūrvaprayuktāḥ |
avadhātamantrādiṣvavivakṣitaṃ vrīhyagnyādisvarūpaṃ sādhanaviśeṣatvamātraṃ vivakṣitamityādirūpoddhātaḥ |
savitraśvipūṣaśabdānāṃ vikṛtiṣu nāstyūhaḥ |

children.translated_text: 'the word <s>Agni</s> is to be modified' — this and the like constitutes the commencement of the <s>ūha</s> inquiry.
In the second, the <s>Sāman</s>-modification with its accessories.
In the third, the mantra-modification.
In the fourth, the inquiry arising from the mantra-modification [as an incidental topic]. (MJaiNyC 1.1.21)

In the first section of the ninth chapter, the commencement of the inquiry into <s>ūha</s> (modification), preceded by an introduction [is presented]. There, properties such as the preliminary offerings are motivated by the unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>). In mantras concerning pounding and the like, the specific nature of rice, fire, and the like is not intended; only the specific nature of the means [of the rite] is intended — this and the like constitutes the introduction. 'The words <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Aśvin</s>, and <s>Pūṣan</s> are not modified in the ectypes;'
[Beginning of MJaiNy 1.1.22]
The dropping of a prerequisite (<s>dvāralopa</s>), its elaboration, the unity of effect (<s>kāryaikatva</s>), accumulation (<s>samuccaya</s>),
the <s>Graha</s> [vessel], the <s>Sāman</s>, miscellaneous topics, and the meaning of the negative particle (<s>nañ</s>) — these are the [topics of the] eight sections. (MJaiNy 1.1.22)

children.text:
daśamādhyāyasya prathame pāde - bādhaheturdvāralopo nirūpitaḥ |
tadyathā - 'svayaṅkṛtā vedirbhavati 'ityatra vediniṣpādanarūpasya dvārasya lopena niṣpādakānāmuddhananādīnāṃ bādhaḥ |
kṛṣṇaleṣu vituṣīkaraṇarūpasya dvārasya lopenāvaghātasya bādhaḥ |
dvitīye - saṃkṣepeṇoktasya dvāralopasya bahubhirudāharaṇairvistāraḥ |
tṛtīye - bādhakāraṇaṃ kāryaikatvam |
tadyathā - prakṛtau gavāśvādidakṣiṇāyā ṛtvikparikrayaḥ kāryam |

children.translated_text: In the eighth, 'Not in the after-offerings' is an exception (<s>paryudāsa</s>); 'not in the <s>Soma</s>' is an explanatory passage; 'not in the <s>Atirātra</s>' is a prohibition — this and similar inquiry into the meaning of the negative particle (<s>nañ</s>) is useful for supersession. (MJaiNyC 1.1.22)

In the first section of the tenth chapter, the cause of supersession — the dropping of a prerequisite (<s>dvāralopa</s>) — is examined. For example: in 'The altar is self-made,' by dropping the prerequisite — namely, the fashioning of the altar — the fashioning-steps such as digging and the like are superseded. In the case of black seeds, by dropping the prerequisite of husking, the pounding is superseded. In the second, the elaboration of the briefly stated prerequisite-dropping with many examples. In the third, the cause of supersession is the unity of effect (<s>kāryaikatva</s>). For example: in the archetype, the purpose of the fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) consisting of cows, horses, and the like is the compensation of the priests. Similarly in the ectype, the <s>Bhūnāmni</s> one-day [rite], the purpose of the fee in the form of a cow is the same. Therefore, the fee of cows, horses, and the like that would be scripturally obtained in the ectype is superseded by the cow. In the fourth, the [offerings such as] subsidiary oblations (<s>upahoma</s>) prescribed in the <s>Nakṣatreṣṭi</s> are accumulated with the scripturally obtained <s>Nāriṣṭha</s> oblations — this and the like is accumulation (<s>samuccaya</s>). In the fifth, the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> cup goes to the archetype; it should be drawn from the <s>Agrayaṇa</s> vessel itself — this and similar inquiry into cups and the like arises from the context of supersession.
[Beginning of MJaiNy 1.1.23]
Introduction, <s>tantra</s> (economy) and <s>āvāpa</s> (individual application), the elaboration of <s>tantra</s>,
and the elaboration of <s>āvāpa</s> — these are the [topics] belonging to the sections of the eleventh chapter. (MJaiNy 1.1.23)
In the first section of the eleventh chapter, the introduction to <s>tantra</s> is described.
In the second, <s>tantra</s> and <s>āvāpa</s> are stated briefly.
In the third [<s>pāda</s> (quarter)] — the <s>tantra</s> (principle of extension) is elaborated with an abundance of examples.
In the fourth — likewise the <s>āvāpa</s> (principle of restriction) is elaborated. || MJaiNyC_1,1.23 ||

<s>Prasaṅga</s> (incidental application), determination of <s>tantra</s>, <s>samuccaya</s> (combination), and <s>vikalpa</s> (option) —
these are the topics of the twelfth <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter); thus ends the summary of the topics of the <s>pādas</s> (quarters). // MJaiNy_1,1.24 //

children.translated_text: And that is of many forms — connection by objection, connection by illustration, connection by counter-example, incidental connection, introductory connection, and connection by exception — such are its various forms. || MJaiNyC_1,1.27* ||

When a topic is connected to an <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (section) by virtue of its relation to the subject matter of the <s>śāstra</s> and so forth, three connections of that <s>adhikaraṇa</s> are inferred: connection with the <s>śāstra</s>, connection with the <s>adhyāya</s>, and connection with the <s>pāda</s>.
For example, in the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the first <s>pāda</s> of the first <s>adhyāya</s>, the absence of definition and means of knowledge for <s>dharma</s> is presented as the prima facie view, and its existence is established.
That <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, by virtue of its relation to <s>dharma</s>, has connection with the <s>śāstra</s> on the investigation of <s>dharma</s>.

children.translated_text: In the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the third <s>pāda</s> of the first <s>adhyāya</s> — the validity of <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) such as <s>aṣṭakā</s> rites is stated.
In the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> — the validity obtained in the same manner as before for the <s>smṛti</s> of complete enveloping is refuted.
This is the connection by exception.
In this manner, the connection should be inferred everywhere. || MJaiNyC_1,1.28 ||

All this, having been applied, is demonstrated: In the first <s>adhyāya</s>, the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) of the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the first <s>pāda</s> is 'the <s>śāstra</s> for the investigation of <s>dharma</s> is enjoined.'
Its reasoning is: 'because a restrictive injunction is possible in study devoid of knowledge of meaning.'
In the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> — the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) is: '<s>dharma</s> has neither definition nor means of knowledge.'
Its reasoning is: 'because it lacks worldly characteristics, and because perception and other [means of knowledge] do not operate [regarding it].'
By that reasoning, if <s>dharma</s> lacks definition and means of knowledge, then <s>dharma</s> would be like a man's horn [i.e., non-existent], so the enjoinability of the <s>śāstra</s> investigating it would be unestablished — this is the connection by objection.
Just as in the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> the enjoinability of the investigative <s>śāstra</s> was stated by the reason of the possibility of a restrictive injunction, so in the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, by the reason of lacking worldly characteristics and non-operation of perception etc., <s>dharma</s> has no definition or means of knowledge — this is the connection by illustration.
Just as the reasoning stated above is observed in the <s>siddhānta</s> of the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, so we do not see any such reasoning in the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> — this is the connection by counter-example.
These connections by illustration and counter-example can be inferred everywhere even by those of dull intellect.
In the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the validity of the injunctive sentence is described as being independent.
Since that sentence falls under the category of word among word and meaning, the permanence of word is discussed in the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> incidentally — this is the incidental connection.
In the fourth <s>pāda</s> of the seventh <s>adhyāya</s>, in order to teach the Vedic <s>aṅga</s> (subsidiary) elements in the <s>Saurya</s> and other modifications through the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the dependence of <s>dharma</s> [on subsidiaries] is established in the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> as being useful for that purpose.
There the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> is the introduction.
This is the introductory connection of the prior <s>adhikaraṇa</s> with the subsequent one.
(In the first [section]: the <s>sūtra</s> on the topic of the commencement-pledge of the <s>dharmaśāstra</s>)
Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>dharma</s>. / Jaim_1,1.1 /
START MJaiNy 1,1.29-31

children.translated_text: Therefore it has been said—
'When a visible result is obtainable, there is no need to postulate an unseen one.
Since the injunction has the purpose of restriction, it will not become purposeless.' Thus.

Beginning with '<s>codanālakṣaṇo 'rtho dharmaḥ</s>' (dharma is that purpose which is characterized by Vedic injunction) and ending with '<s>anvāhārye ca darśanāt</s>' (and because it is seen in the supplementary offering), the collection of <s>sūtras</s> proclaimed by <s>Jaimini</s> constitutes the <s>dharma-vicāra-śāstra</s> (science of inquiry into dharma). The subject of this first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic) is as follows: some hold that the injunction of study in '<s>svādhyāyo 'dhyetavyaḥ</s>' (one's own Veda should be studied) terminates merely in the grasping of syllables (<s>akṣaragrahaṇamātra</s>). Others, however, say: 'This study is enjoined for the visible purpose of knowledge of meaning (<s>arthajñāna</s>). Knowledge of meaning is not possible without inquiry (<s>vicāra</s>). Therefore the injunction motivates the science of inquiry.' The doubt therein is: 'Should this science of inquiry not be commenced on the ground of being motivated by injunction, or should it be commenced?' The one who says 'the injunction is for the sake of knowledge of meaning through study' should be asked: Is the study enjoined as something entirely unobtained (<s>aprāpta</s>), or is it, being already obtained in some way, restricted (<s>niyamyate</s>) like the pounding (<s>avaghāta</s>)? Not the first — because the matter in question, Vedic study, is a cause of knowledge of meaning, since it is study, like the study of the <s>Mahābhārata</s> — this being already established by inference alone, independent of any injunction. Then let the second alternative hold: because restriction-injunction (<s>niyama-vidhi</s>) is possible, like the pounding. Just as, because rice can be produced either by fingernails or by pounding, the pounding — which is obtained on one alternative — is restricted by injunction as necessarily to be done, so too, because knowledge of meaning is possible either by reading written texts or by study under a teacher, the study — obtained on one alternative — is restricted by injunction. No. Because of dissimilarity. Only rice produced by pounding generates the supreme <s>apūrva</s> (unseen merit) through the intermediate <s>apūrva</s> of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) sacrifices, and not otherwise. Therefore the <s>apūrva</s> of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> is the reason for the restriction of pounding. But here, since the performance of sacrificial acts is accomplished even by knowledge of meaning born from reading written texts, there is no reason for restricting study. Therefore, since neither type of injunction is possible, the commencement of the science of inquiry for the sake of knowledge of meaning is not enjoined. If asked, what then is the fate of the injunction that is heard? — we say that what is enjoined is merely the grasping of syllables for the sake of heaven (<s>svarga</s>). Even though heaven is not explicitly mentioned, it should be supplied by the <s>Viśvajit</s> principle. By the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>sa svargaḥ syāt sarvān praty aviśeṣāt</s>' (that would be heaven, since there is no distinction for all) [PMS 4.3.15], in order to supply the unheard qualifier of the person entitled to the <s>Viśvajit</s> sacrifice, the fruit of heaven was established by reasoning as a qualification thereof. Let the same apply to study as well. With this very intention it has been said: 'Since without even an injunction there is attainment of the visible result, there is no purposiveness for that (injunction). But heaven should be supplied by the power of the injunction, as in the <s>Viśvajit</s> and similar cases.' This being so, the scripture '<s>vedamadhītya snāyāt</s>' (having studied the Veda, one should perform the concluding bath) is supported. In this (our) system, continuity between Vedic study and the <s>samāvartana</s> (return ceremony) is understood. But in your view — even after studying the Veda, one must remain in the guru's house for the purpose of dharma-inquiry. In that case, the continuity between them is obstructed. Therefore, since the science of inquiry is not enjoined, and since dharma is established by mere recitation, and because of the scripture on <s>samāvartana</s>, the science of dharma-inquiry should not be commenced — this is the prior view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>). To this we reply: As for what was said — 'since it is established in common experience, there is no injunction of the unobtained' — let that be so. But restriction-injunction (<s>niyama-vidhi</s>) cannot be prevented. Just as the supreme <s>apūrva</s> produced by the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> sacrifice — restriction-injunction cannot be prevented. Just as the supreme <s>apūrva</s> produced by the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> will generate the intermediate <s>apūrva</s> of the restriction. And if the unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) of restriction is not accepted, the injunction that is heard would become purposeless. Nor is it correct to assign heaven as the purpose by the <s>Viśvajit</s> principle — because when knowledge of meaning, which has a visible result, is possible, it is impossible to supply an unseen one.

children.translated_text: But the science of inquiry will ascertain the matter from the complementary passage '<s>tejo vai ghṛtam</s>' (ghee is indeed radiance).
Therefore inquiry is enjoined.

children.text: ' vedamadhītya snāyāt ' iti śāstraṃ tvadhyayanasamāvartanayoḥ pūrvāparībhāvasamānakartṛkatve evācaṣṭe, na tvānantaryam |
children.translated_text: The scripture '<s>vedamadhītya snāyāt</s>' (having studied the Veda, one should perform the concluding bath) merely states that study and <s>samāvartana</s> have the same agent and a sequence of before and after — it does not state immediate succession.
Therefore, the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>) is that the science of inquiry should be commenced by the force of injunction alone.

If it be objected that even so, since knowledge of meaning is possible for a person who has studied the Veda along with <s>Vyākaraṇa</s> (grammar) and other ancillary sciences, the science of inquiry would be useless — no. Because even though mere knowledge is possible, ascertainment (<s>nirṇaya</s>) depends on inquiry. In the case of '<s>aktāḥ śarkarā upadadhāti</s>' (one places anointed gravel pieces), the ascertainment that 'it is with ghee alone, not with oil and such' is not established by grammar, etymology (<s>nirukta</s>), or Vedic concordance (<s>nigama</s>).
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 1.1.32-34]
In this very <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, he states the teacher's view—
Or rather, since accomplishment comes from teaching (<s>adhyāpana</s>), there is indeed no injunction regarding study (<s>adhyayana</s>);
therefore both the prior and subsequent views should be established by other reasoning.
The enjoined teaching would succeed even without the student's knowledge of meaning;

children.text: tena nirviṣayaṃ śāstraṃ niṣphalaṃ cetyupekṣyatām // MJaiNy_1,1.33 //
children.translated_text: therefore the <s>śāstra</s> would be without subject matter and without fruit — hence it should be disregarded.
For one who naturally attains knowledge of meaning, since the intention (of the Veda) cannot be denied,
the subject matter and so forth are easily established — therefore the <s>śāstra</s> is commenced.

children.translated_text: But regarding the Veda — why would the meaning not be intended?

children.text: vivakṣite ca vedārthe yatra yatra puruṣasya saṃdehaḥ sa sarvo 'pi vicāraśāstrasya viṣayaḥ |
children.translated_text: And when the meaning of the Veda is intended, wherever a person has doubt — all of that is the subject matter of the science of inquiry.
The ascertainment of that is the purpose.

children.text: tato 'dhyāpanavidhiprayuktenādhyayanena budhyamānasyārthasya vicārthatvādvicāraśāstrasya vaidhatvaṃ siddham || MJaiNyC_1,1.32-34 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the meaning comprehended through study motivated by the injunction of teaching is subject to inquiry, the enjoined nature of the science of inquiry is established.

'<s>Aṣṭavarṣe brāhmaṇam upanayīta, tam adhyāpayīta</s>' (one should initiate a Brahmin at age eight and teach him) — thus teaching (<s>adhyāpana</s>) is enjoined. Nor is there an absence of the person to be enjoined here, because those desiring the status of teacher (<s>ācāryatva</s>) are the ones to be enjoined. By the word '<s>upanayīta</s>' (should initiate), through the <s>ātmanepada</s> ending enjoined by <s>Pāṇini</s>'s <s>sūtra</s> '<s>saṃmānanotsañjanācāryakaraṇajñānabhṛtivigaṇanavyayeṣu niyaḥ</s>' [Pā. Sū. 1.3.36], the qualifier of the person enjoined — namely the status of being a teacher — is understood in the act of initiation. The one who is enjoined regarding initiation is the same one regarding teaching, since both have a single purpose. This being so, teaching performed by the teacher is not accomplished without study performed by the student — therefore, since the performance of study is established as a reciprocal entailment of the injunction of teaching, no separate injunction (for study) need be postulated. The injunctive sentence that is heard can also be explained as a perpetual restatement (<s>nityānuvāda</s>). Therefore, setting aside the injunction of study, the prior and subsequent views presented above must be argued differently. Regarding subject matter and doubt, however, there is no disagreement: the science of inquiry is the subject matter; the doubt is whether it is enjoined or not. Therein, the one who asserts it is enjoined should be asked: Does the enjoined teaching performed by the teacher also motivate the student's knowledge of meaning, or only recitation? Not the first — because teaching is accomplished even without knowledge of meaning. But if it is merely recitation, inquiry has no subject matter. The subject matter is a meaning that is understood at first glance but is doubtful. In that case, where there is no apprehension of meaning at all, what question can there be of doubt? Ascertainment (<s>nirṇaya</s>) is the fruit of inquiry. That too is far removed in the absence of a subject matter. Therefore, due to the absence of subject matter and purpose, the science of inquiry should not be commenced — this is the prior view. To this we reply: Let it be that meaning-comprehension is not motivated by the injunction of teaching. Even so, for one who has studied the Veda with its ancillaries — one who is learned in <s>Nigama</s>, <s>Nirukta</s>, and <s>Vyākaraṇa</s> — comprehension of meaning in the Veda arises naturally, just as in human-authored works. If it be objected that just as in 'eat poison,' the meaning, though understood, is not intended, so too the meaning of the Veda may not be the subject matter due to the absence of such (intention) — no. Because intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>) cannot be denied. In the case of the sentence 'eat poison,' the primary meaning is abandoned because it is contradicted, since it is composed by a trustworthy person and the meaning is 'do not be afraid' (i.e., do not eat).
(In the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the definition of <s>dharma</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
<s>Codanālakṣaṇo 'rtho dharmaḥ</s> — Dharma is that purpose which is characterized by Vedic injunction. [<s>Jaimini</s> 1.1.2]
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 1.1.35-37]
He composes the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> according to the <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> view—
<s>Dharma</s>, the subject of inquiry, is devoid of a defining characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>);
it is to be examined whether it possesses a means of knowledge (<s>māna</s>) or not, or both.
What could be the defining characteristic of that which lacks any worldly form?
And the suspicion of a means of knowledge is far-fetched here, since perception and the like do not operate.
The form apprehended through Vedic injunction (<s>codanā</s>), when it pertains to something purposeful, is the defining characteristic;

children.text: ata eva pramāṇaṃ ca codanaivātra no kutaḥ // MJaiNy_1,1.37 //
children.translated_text: and for that very reason, <s>codanā</s> (Vedic injunction) alone is the means of knowledge here — whence any other?
