children.translated_text: Therefore, being purposeful while being apprehensible through <s>codanā</s> is the defining characteristic of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: ata eva garme dharme gamakaṃ vidhivākyaṃ pramāṇam |
children.translated_text: For that very reason, the injunctive sentence (<s>vidhi-vākya</s>) is the means of knowledge regarding <s>dharma</s> thus characterized.

children.text: yadyapi pratyakṣānumānayoraviṣayo dharmaḥ, tathāpi prasiddhepadasamabhivyāhāreṇa vyutpattiḥ saṃbhavati |
children.translated_text: Although <s>dharma</s> is not the object of perception and inference, nevertheless, etymological knowledge (<s>vyutpatti</s>) is possible through association with well-known words in connected usage.
Therefore, <s>dharma</s> is endowed with both a defining characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) and a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). || MJaiNyC_1,1.35-37 ||

For the establishment of a thing depends on both its defining characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) and its means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Hence they say: 'The establishment of the object of knowledge depends on the means of knowledge, and the establishment of the means of knowledge depends on the defining characteristic.' A defining characteristic is some feature belonging to the thing to be defined that is well-known in the world and that distinguishes it from things of the same class and of different classes. When, by means of that defining characteristic, a cognitive expectation (<s>saṃbhāvanābuddhi</s>) regarding the thing to be defined arises, one who is motivated to know apprehends it through a means of knowledge. For example: having heard '<s>sāsnādimatī gauḥ</s>' (a cow is that which possesses a dewlap and so on), one searches among four-footed living beings for the entity marked by that characteristic and apprehends 'this is a cow' through the eye. This being so, since <s>dharma</s> is not of this world (<s>alaukika</s>), it has no defining characteristic. How then could there be motivation to know it? Even if somehow there were use for it, the possibility of a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) cannot even be suspected there. Perception does not operate here, because <s>dharma</s> is devoid of form and the like. For the same reason, there is no inference, due to the impossibility of grasping the invariable concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>). And the apprehension of the fitness of verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) is rooted in perception and inference. Therefore, due to the absence of etymological knowledge (<s>vyutpatti</s>), scriptural testimony (<s>āgama</s>) too does not operate there. Thus it is concluded that <s>dharma</s> is devoid of both defining characteristic and means of knowledge — having arrived at this position, we say: Let there be no worldly characteristic apprehensible by the eye and the like. Even so, there exists a characteristic apprehensible through Vedic injunction (<s>codanā</s>) — namely, being the means to the fruit of heaven and the like. Thus 'that which is purposeful and apprehensible through <s>codanā</s> is <s>dharma</s>' — this becomes the definition. If one merely says '<s>artho dharmaḥ</s>' (dharma is purpose), there would be over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) to <s>Brahman</s>, worship of a <s>caitya</s>, a pot, and so on. To exclude these, '<s>codanāgamyaḥ</s>' (apprehensible through Vedic injunction) is stated. Even with that much stated, there would be over-extension to the <s>Śyena</s> and other black-magic rites, which are apprehensible through injunction but have harmful effects and are thus purposeless (<s>anartha</s>). To exclude these, '<s>arthaḥ</s>' (purposeful) is stated. Although the result of the <s>Śyena</s> is the death of an enemy and not hell, nevertheless, since that killing is a cause of hell, the <s>Śyena</s> is purposeless (<s>anartha</s>) through the medium of killing. Nor should it be suspected that similarly, the animal slaughter in the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> sacrifice, being also killing, would be a cause of hell — because that slaughter, being an ancillary of the sacrifice (<s>kratvaṅga</s>), has no separate result apart from the sacrificial fruit of heaven.
START MJaiNy 1,1.38-40
In this very <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, he states the most senior teacher's view—
Or rather, is the Vedic meaning that is to be inquired into known through <s>mantras</s> and the like,

children.text: siddhārtho 'pyatha vidhyekagamyaḥ kāryārtha eva vā // MJaiNy_1,1.38 //
children.translated_text: even conveying established meaning, or is it accessible only through injunction and of the nature of action alone? // MJaiNy_1,1.38 //
Even in the case of established facts such as the birth of a son, since etymological derivation (<s>vyutpatti</s>) is justified,
what harm is there even if what is established as knowable through <s>mantras</s> and the like is also considered Vedic meaning? // MJaiNy_1,1.39 //
Due to the multiplicity of causes of joy, the etymological derivation in the case of the birth of a son

children.text: durlabhā sulabhā kārye vedārtho 'taḥ sa eva hi // MJaiNy_1,1.40 //
children.translated_text: is difficult to ascertain, whereas it is easy in the case of injunctive action — therefore that alone is indeed the Vedic meaning. // MJaiNy_1,1.40 //

children.text:
"athāto dharmajijñāsā" [pū.mī.sū.1.1.1 ] ityatrāthaśabdena kṛtsna vedādhyayanānantaryamucyate |
ataḥśabdena kṛtsnasya vedasya vivakṣitārthatvaṃ hetū"kriyate |
uktaśabdadvayānusāreṇa dharmaśabdo 'pi kṛtsnaṃ vedārthamācaṣṭe |
tataḥ sūtre 'vedārtho jijñāsyaḥ ' iti pratijñā kṛtā |
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kiṃ mantrārthavādapratītaḥ siddhārtho 'pi vedārtho bhavati, kiṃvā vidhivākyapratītaḥ kāryārthaṃ eva vedārthaḥ, iti |
tatra -
"lokāvagatasāmarthyaḥ śabdo vede 'pi bodhakaḥ" iti jñāyena vyutpattyanusārī vedārtho varṇanīyaḥ |
vyutpattiśca siddhārthe 'pyasti |
'putraste jātaḥ ' iti vārtāharavyāhārajanyaṃ śroturharṣamanumāya harṣahetau putrajanmani saṃgatiṃ pratipadyate |
children.translated_text: Upon inferring the joy of the listener produced by the utterance of a news-bearer saying '<s>putraste jātaḥ</s>' (a son is born to you), one grasps the connection with the birth of a son as the cause of joy.

children.text: ato mantrārthavādapratīto 'pyartho vedārtha iti prāpte brūmaḥ - putrajanmavaddharṣahetūnāṃ dhanalābhādīnāṃ bahutvādasya vākyaskaya putrajanmaivārtha iti nirṇayo durlabhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, even the meaning apprehended through <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> is Vedic meaning — having arrived at this position, we say: just as in the case of the birth of a son, due to the multiplicity of causes of joy such as the acquisition of wealth and the like, the determination that the meaning of this sentence is the birth of a son alone is difficult.

children.text: 'gāmānaya ' iti vākye tu gavānayanarūpāṃ madhyamabṛddhapravattimavalokya saṃgatigrahaṇaṃ sulabham |
children.translated_text: But in the sentence '<s>gāmānaya</s>' (bring the cow), by observing the activity of a middling or grown person directed toward the bringing of cows, the grasping of the connection is easy.
Therefore, the Vedic meaning is of the nature of action alone. || MJaiNyC_1,1.38-40 ||

In the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>athāto dharmajijñāsā</s>' [PMS 1.1.1], by the word '<s>atha</s>' the succession after the complete study of the entire Veda is stated. By the word '<s>ataḥ</s>', the intended purposefulness of the entire Veda is made the reason. Following these two stated words, the word '<s>dharma</s>' also denotes the entire meaning of the Veda. Thus in the <s>sūtra</s>, the proposition 'the meaning of the Veda is to be inquired into' has been made. Therein arises the doubt: Does the Vedic meaning apprehended through <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> (laudatory passages), even if it conveys established facts, constitute Vedic meaning? Or is Vedic meaning only that which pertains to action and is apprehended through injunctive sentences? Therein — by the principle '<s>lokāvagatasāmarthyaḥ śabdo vede 'pi bodhakaḥ</s>' (a word whose capacity is known in common usage is informative in the Veda as well), the Vedic meaning to be described should follow etymological derivation. And etymological derivation exists even in established facts.
(In the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the examination of the means of knowledge regarding <s>dharma</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
The examination of its cause. / Jaim_1,1.3 /
START MJaiNy 1,1.41-42
He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> according to the <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> view—
The means of knowledge (<s>māna</s>) that has been stated as the indicator of <s>dharma</s>, having the nature of Vedic injunction (<s>codanā</s>) —

children.text: etatkiṃ na parīkṣyaṃ syātkiṃvā samyakparīkṣyatām // MJaiNy_1,1.41 //
children.translated_text: should this not be examined, or should it be properly examined? // MJaiNy_1,1.41 //
Since the object of knowledge (<s>meya</s>) is established by the teaching of the means of knowledge, what need is there for examination?
Not so — in this science of inquiry (<s>vicāra-śāstra</s>), how can the examination be disregarded? // MJaiNy_1,1.42 //
The meaning is clear. || MJaiNyC_1,1.41-42 ||
START MJaiNy 1,1.43-44
In this very <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, he states the teacher's view—
Should the Vedic meaning be examined first, or rather the validity of <s>codanā</s> (Vedic injunction) as a means of knowledge?
Since the Vedic meaning is primary, let that be examined first. // MJaiNy_1,1.43 //
But it is the validity of <s>codanā</s> as a means of knowledge that has here been taken up for establishment first,
because its primacy is based on its independence (<s>anapekṣatā</s>). // MJaiNy_1,1.44 //

children.text:
dvitīyādhyāyādyaiḥ karmabhedaśeṣaśeṣitvādirūpo vedārthaḥ sūtrakāreṇa parīkṣiṣyate |
cojanāprāmāṇyaṃ tu prathamādhyāye parīkṣyate |
tadaitadayuktam |
kutaḥ |
vedārthasya pradhānatvenā'dau parīkṣyayītvāt |
pradhānabhāge hi vedaḥ |
purūṣārthatvenānuṣṭheyatvāt |
pradhāṇaṃ tu tadvevanāya pravṛttaṃ sattaccheṣatayāna pradhānamiti prāpte brūmaḥ- astvanuṣṭhānopāyo vedārthapramāṇayoḥ pradhānotsarjatabhāvaḥ |
pramāṇaprameyabhāvopāyau tu pramāṇasyaiva mukhyatvaṃ nirapekṣatvāt |
nahi svataḥ pramāṇyavādināṃ mate sāpekṣayā pramāṇasyāsti |
prameyaṃ tu sārekṣam |

children.translated_text: Because it has been stated: 'Without a means of knowledge, there is no establishment of the object of knowledge.'
It is precisely this primacy that the <s>sūtrakāra</s> relied upon when he undertook the examination of the means of knowledge first — this is fitting.

children.text: ayānvatprā athānyatprādhānyamāśritya dharmavicāra evādau kasmānna kṛtaḥ? |
children.translated_text: If that is so, why was the inquiry into <s>dharma</s> not undertaken first based on the other kind of primacy?

children.text: na kṛtaḥ - aparīkṣitena pramāṇena dharmasyāsiddhau tadvicārasyā'śrayāsiddheḥ ||
children.translated_text: It was not — because when <s>dharma</s> is not established due to the means of knowledge being unexamined, the inquiry into it would suffer from the defect of an unestablished basis (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>).

From the second <s>adhyāya</s> onwards, the Vedic meaning in the form of differentiation of rites, subsidiary-principal relationships, and the like will be examined by the <s>sūtrakāra</s>. But the validity of <s>codanā</s> (Vedic injunction) is examined in the first <s>adhyāya</s>. Now this is inappropriate. Why? Because the Vedic meaning, being primary, should be examined first. For the Veda constitutes the primary portion, since it is to be performed for the sake of human ends (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). The primary is that for whose own sake one engages, and what serves it is secondary and not primary — having arrived at this position, we say: Let there be this primary-secondary relationship between Vedic meaning and means of knowledge with respect to the means of practice. But between a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) and the object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>), the means of knowledge alone has primacy, because of its independence. For in the view of the <s>svataḥ prāmāṇya</s> (intrinsic validity) proponents, the means of knowledge has no dependence. But the object of knowledge is dependent.
Thus, in these three <s>adhikaraṇas</s>, the difference between the <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> and <s>Prābhākara</s> views has been presented for the purpose of instruction. || MJaiNyC_1,1.43-44 ||
<s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the topic that <s>dharma</s> is not apprehensible by perception and the like,
the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
Now, for the most part, only the <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> view is presented — (In the fourth

children.text: satsaṃprayoge puruṣasyendriyāṇāṃ buddhijanma tatpratyakṣam animittaṃ vidyamānopalambhanatvāt / Jaim_1,1.4 /
children.translated_text: <s>satsaṃprayoge puruṣasyendriyāṇāṃ buddhijanma tatpratyakṣam animittaṃ vidyamānopalambhanatvāt</s> — When there is contact of a person's senses [with an object], the cognition that arises is perception; that is not the cause [of knowing <s>dharma</s>], because it apprehends only what exists [at present]. / Jaim_1,1.4 /
START MJaiNy 1,1.45-46
He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>—
Is <s>dharma</s> apprehensible by perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and other means, or only by injunction (<s>vidhi</s>)?
Since perception and the like are valid means of knowledge, they should illuminate <s>dharma</s> as an object of knowledge. // MJaiNy_1,1.45 //
Perception has only present objects as its domain, but <s>dharma</s> pertains to what is yet to be accomplished (<s>bhāvya</s>);
inference and the like are rooted in perception — therefore <s>dharma</s> is knowable through injunction alone. // MJaiNy_1,1.46 //

children.text:
akṣaṃ pratyakṣam /
pratyakṣādīnāṃ pramāṇatvātprameyāvabhāsakatvaṃ tāvadavivādam |
dharmaśca prameyaḥ, asaṃdigdhāviparyastatve sati budhyamānatvāt, ghaṭādivat |
tasmātpratyakṣādibhirapyeṣa dharmo gamyata iti

children.translated_text: the prima facie view arises.
We say:

children.text: - dharmasya prameyatve 'pi pratyakṣayogyatā nāsti, pratyakṣasya vartamānamātraviṣayatvāt |
children.translated_text: — Even though <s>dharma</s> is an object of knowledge, it is not fit for perception, because perception has only present objects as its domain.
And for that which is entirely beyond the scope of perception, what question can there be of inference and the like?
Only when the invariable concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>) and such are first grasped through perception does inference and the like operate subsequently.
Therefore, <s>dharma</s> is knowable through injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) alone. || MJaiNyC_1,1.45-46 ||

<s>Akṣa</s> means perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). That perception and the like, being valid means of knowledge, illuminate the object of knowledge — this much is undisputed. And <s>dharma</s> is an object of knowledge, because it is cognized while being free from doubt and error, like a pot and the like. Therefore, <s>dharma</s> is also apprehensible by perception and the like — thus
<s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the topic of the validity of injunction regarding <s>dharma</s>,
the <s>sūtras</s> are:)
(In the fifth

children.text: autpattikas tu śabdasyārthena saṃbandhas tasya jñānam upadeśo 'vyatirekaś cārthe 'nupalabdhe tatpramāṇaṃ bādarāyaṇasyānapekṣatvāt / Jaim_1,1.5 /
children.translated_text: <s>autpattikas tu śabdasyārthena saṃbandhas tasya jñānam upadeśo 'vyatirekaś cārthe 'nupalabdhe tatpramāṇaṃ bādarāyaṇasyānapekṣatvāt</s> — But the relation of a word with its meaning is innate; the knowledge of that [meaning] is instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>); and [this relation is] without exception; and when the meaning is not apprehended [by other means], that [word] is a valid means of knowledge — according to <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, because of its independence. / Jaim_1,1.5 /
START MJaiNy 1,1.47-48
He composes the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>—

children.text: abodhako bodhako vā na tāvadbodhako vidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Is injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) non-informative or informative? It is not informative,

children.text: śakteralaukike dharme grahaṇaṃ durghaṭaṃ yataḥ // MJaiNy_1,1.47 //
children.translated_text: because the apprehension of its capacity (<s>śakti</s>) regarding the supramundane <s>dharma</s> is impossible. // MJaiNy_1,1.47 //
Since the apprehension of capacity is possible when <s>dharma</s> is mentioned in connected usage (<s>samabhivyāhāra</s>),
the validity of injunction as informative is established by its independence (<s>anapekṣatā</s>). // MJaiNy_1,1.48 //

children.text:
yathā dharme pratyakṣādīnāṃ prāmāṇyaṃ nāsti, tathā vidherapi nāsti prāmāṇyam |
śaktigrahaṇapūrvakaṃ hi prāmāṇyamāptavākyasya loke dṛṣṭam |
śaktiśca lokaprasiddhe gavādau gṛhyate |
dharmastvalaukikaḥ |
atastatra śaktigrahaṇaṃ durghaṭam |
tasmādvidherabodhakatvānna dharme prāmāṇyamiti

children.translated_text: the prima facie view arises.
We say:

children.text: - yathā 'prabhinnakamalodare madhūni madhukaraḥ pibati' ityatra madhukarapadasyārthamajānannanyapadārthamavagatya tatyamabhivyāhārāt kamalasya madhyagate madhupānaṃ kurvati dṛśyamānabhramare madhukaraśabdasya saṅgatiṃ gṛhītvā vākyārthaṃ pratipadyate, tathā 'kārīryā vṛṣṭikāmo yajeta' ityatra lokaprasiddhārthavṛṣṭyādipadasamabhivyāhārādalaukikabhāvanāyāṃ vidheḥ saṅgatiṃ gṛhītvā vidhivākyārthaṃ puruṣo budhyate |
children.translated_text: — Just as in the sentence '<s>prabhinnakamalodare madhūni madhukaraḥ pibati</s>' (the bee drinks honey in the interior of a blossoming lotus), one who does not know the meaning of the word '<s>madhukara</s>' (bee), having understood the meanings of the other words and then, from the connected usage (<s>samabhivyāhāra</s>) with those words, upon seeing a bee drinking honey situated in the middle of a lotus, grasps the connection of the word '<s>madhukara</s>' and understands the sentence meaning — similarly, in the sentence '<s>kārīryā vṛṣṭikāmo yajeta</s>' (one desiring rain should perform the <s>Kārīrī</s> sacrifice), a person, from the connected usage with words like '<s>vṛṣṭi</s>' (rain) whose meanings are well-known in the world, grasps the connection of injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) with the supramundane <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive activity) and understands the meaning of the injunctive sentence.
Therefore, the absence of validity characterized as non-informativeness does not exist.

children.text: na ca saṃvādābhāvādaprāmāṇyam, samanantarabhāvipratiniyataphale vṛṣṭyādau saṃvādasyāpi saṃbhavāt |
children.translated_text: Nor is there invalidity due to the absence of corroboration (<s>saṃvāda</s>), because corroboration is also possible in the case of results such as rain that are definite and immediately subsequent.

children.text: aniyatadṛṣṭaphale citrayāgādau, pratiniyatajanmāntaraphale jyotiṣṭomādau ca saṃvādaḥ kathamiti cet, evaṃ tarhi svataḥprāmaṇyābhyupagamānnāsti kvāpi saṃvādādyapekṣā |
children.translated_text: If it be asked how there can be corroboration in the case of the <s>Citrā</s> sacrifice and the like whose results are indefinite and unfixed, or in the case of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like whose specific results manifest only in another birth — then, by the acceptance of intrinsic validity (<s>svataḥ prāmāṇya</s>), there is no dependence on corroboration or anything else anywhere.

Therefore, since the two causes of invalidity — non-informativeness and dependence — are absent, the intrinsically established validity of injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) cannot be denied. || MJaiNyC_1,1.47-48 ||

Just as perception and the like have no validity regarding <s>dharma</s>, so too injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) has no validity. For the validity of authoritative speech (<s>āptavākya</s>) in the world is seen to be preceded by the apprehension of its capacity (<s>śaktigrahaṇa</s>). And capacity is grasped regarding worldly things such as cows and the like. But <s>dharma</s> is supramundane (<s>alaukika</s>). Therefore, the apprehension of capacity regarding it is impossible. Hence, due to injunction being non-informative, there is no validity regarding <s>dharma</s> — thus
<s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the topic of the eternality of words,
the <s>sūtras</s> are 6-23:)
(In the sixth
Some hold that [the word] is a product, because it is seen [to arise]. / Jaim_1,1.6 /
Because of the absence of a [permanent] locus. / Jaim_1,1.7 /
Because of the use of the word '<s>karoti</s>' (makes). / Jaim_1,1.8 /
And because of simultaneity in different beings. / Jaim_1,1.9 /
And of the original and the modified forms. / Jaim_1,1.10 /
And the augment (<s>vṛddhi</s>) [is produced] by the agent, because of plurality thereof. / Jaim_1,1.11 /
But the perception there is the same. / Jaim_1,1.12 /
The perception of an existent [word] is supreme, because of the non-arrival of the object [otherwise]. / Jaim_1,1.13 /
The application (<s>prayoga</s>) is subsequent [to the word itself]. / Jaim_1,1.14 /
Like the sun, there is simultaneity. / Jaim_1,1.15 /
A different phoneme is not a modification [of the original]. / Jaim_1,1.16 /
Sound (<s>nāda</s>) and augment (<s>vṛddhi</s>) are not supreme [i.e., not newly produced]. / Jaim_1,1.17 /

children.text: nityas tu syād darśanasya parārthatvāt / Jaim_1,1.18 /
children.translated_text: But [the word] would be eternal, because perception serves another's purpose. / Jaim_1,1.18 /
Because of simultaneity everywhere. / Jaim_1,1.19 /
Because of the absence of [fixed] number. / Jaim_1,1.20 /
Because of independence [from any cause]. / Jaim_1,1.21 /
And because of the absence of resemblance in the conjunction [of atoms]. / Jaim_1,1.22 /
And because of the observation of indicatory marks (<s>liṅga</s>). / Jaim_1,1.23 /

He composes the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>—
Is the word in the form of injunction and the like non-eternal or imperishable?
It is non-eternal, because it consists of phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>), and because origination is observed in phonemes. // MJaiNy_1,1.49 //
By the force of uncontradicted recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), the eternality of phonemes is established;
they are manifested, not produced, by the effort of utterance. // MJaiNy_1,1.50 //

children.text:
śabdanityatvavādino vaiyākaraṇāstāvadevaṃ manyante - varṇasamūhaśravaṇānantaraṃ 'idamekaṃ padam' iti pratyayo mānasapratyakṣeṇotpadyate |

sa ca nityaḥ |
sa eva śabdaḥ, na tu varṇā iti |
tadetannaiyāyikādayo na sahante |
varṇeṣvevaikārthāvacchedopādhinā padaikyabuddherupapattau varṇātiriktasphoṭakalpanā nirarthikā |
tasmādvarṇānāmeva śabdatvam |
varṇāśca pratipuruṣaṃ pratyuccāraṇaṃ ca janmavināśavanta upalabhyante |
tasmādanityaḥ śabdaḥ |
tasya ca kāraṇadoṣasaṃbhavādvidheraprāmāṇyamiti

children.translated_text: the prior view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>)

The <s>Vaiyākaraṇas</s> (grammarians), who hold the doctrine of the eternality of words, maintain as follows: After hearing a collection of phonemes, the cognition 'this is one word' arises through mental perception (<s>mānasa-pratyakṣa</s>). The object of that cognition is some entity called <s>sphoṭa</s>, which is distinct from the phonemes. And that is eternal. That alone is the word, not the phonemes — thus they hold. But the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> (logicians) and others do not accept this. When the unity-cognition of a word can be explained by the limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>) of delimitation by a single meaning among the phonemes themselves, the postulation of a <s>sphoṭa</s> distinct from the phonemes is purposeless. Therefore, it is the phonemes alone that have the nature of words. And phonemes are observed to have origination and destruction for each person and for each utterance. Therefore, the word is non-eternal. And since there is the possibility of a defect in its cause, injunction lacks validity — thus

children.text: bahubhiḥ puruṣaiḥ pratyekaṃ bahukṛtva uccārite gośabde 'ta eveme gakārādayo varṇāḥ' ityabādhitapratyabhijñā jāyate |

children.translated_text: By the force of that [recognition], the phonemes are eternal.

children.text: na ca varṇānāṃ janmābhāve bahukṛtva uccāraṇaprayatno vyartha iti śaṅkanīyam, tatprayatnasya vyañjakatvāṅgīkārāt |
children.translated_text: Nor should it be objected that if there is no origination of phonemes, the repeated effort of utterance would be purposeless — because the effort of utterance is accepted as having a manifesting function (<s>vyañjakatva</s>).

children.text: evaṃ sati puruṣabhedāduccāraṇabhedāśca yathāyogamudāttādibhedaiḥ paṭumṛdutvādibhedaiścopetāndhvaniviśeṣānutpādya caritārthā bhaviṣyanti |
children.translated_text: This being so, the differences of utterance arising from differences of persons will have fulfilled their purpose by producing particular varieties of sound (<s>dhvani</s>) endowed with distinctions of <s>udātta</s> (acute accent) and the like, and distinctions of clarity, softness, and the like, as appropriate.
Therefore, since the word is eternal and there is no defect in the cause, there is no invalidity [of injunction]. || MJaiNyC_1,1.49-50 ||
When the word '<s>go</s>' (cow) is uttered many times by many persons individually, the uncontradicted recognition arises: 'These are the very same phonemes — <s>gakāra</s> and the rest.'
(In the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the topic of the Veda's capacity to convey meaning, the <s>sūtras</s> are 24-26:)
At the time of origination, [words] would be [merely] names, because the meaning is not caused by that [origination]. / Jaim_1,1.24 /
The traditional teaching (<s>sāmāmnāya</s>) of those [words] that constitute it is for the purpose of action, because the meaning is caused by that [teaching]. / Jaim_1,1.25 /
Due to fixed convention in the world, there would be proximity with usage. / Jaim_1,1.26 /
START MJaiNy 1,1.51-52
He composes the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s>—
Is the Vedic sentence a valid means of knowledge or not? It would not be a valid means of knowledge,
because in the case of dependence on a separate connection (<s>saṅgati</s>), independence would be abandoned. // MJaiNy_1,1.51 //
Even in the Veda, just as in ordinary usage, the connection (<s>saṅgati</s>) in the sentence-meaning is not

children.text: grahītavyā tato vākyaṃ pramāṇaṃ nairapekṣyataḥ // MJaiNy_1,1.52 //
children.translated_text: to be separately grasped; therefore the sentence is a means of knowledge due to its independence. // MJaiNy_1,1.52 //

children.text: yadyapi varṇānāṃ nityatvādekārthāvacchedakasya padasyāpi varṇarūpatayānityatvādvarṇapadadvārā vedasya kāraṇasāpekṣatvaṃ nāsti, tathāpi 'agnihotraṃ juhuyātsvargakāmaḥ' ityādivākyasya vākyārthe saṅgatigrahaṇamapekṣitam |

children.translated_text: Therefore, since there is no independence, there is no validity — having arrived at this position,
we say: In ordinary usage, in the employment by elders such as '<s>gām ānaya</s>' (bring the cow), the connection is grasped only between words and their meanings.
But the sentence conveys its own meaning by virtue of mutual expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>), fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>), and proximity (<s>sannidhi</s>) — this is undisputed.
Similarly, the Vedic sentence too, being capable of conveying meaning, has uncontested validity due to its independence. || MJaiNyC_1,1.51-52 ||

Although, due to the eternality of phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>), the word that delimits a single meaning — being itself of the nature of phonemes — is also non-eternal, and thus the Veda has no dependence on a cause through the medium of phonemes and words, nevertheless the grasping of the connection of sentence-meaning in the sentence '<s>agnihotraṃ juhuyāt svargakāmaḥ</s>' (one desiring heaven should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>) and so on is required.
the topic of the non-human authorship (<s>apauruṣeyatva</s>) of the Veda —
<s>sūtras</s> 27-32)
(In the eighth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>]:
And some declare the Vedas to be connected with a person (<s>puruṣa</s>). / Jaim_1,1.27 /
And because of the observation of impermanence. / Jaim_1,1.28 /
But the precedence of the word has been stated. / Jaim_1,1.29 /
The name is from teaching (<s>pravacana</s>). / Jaim_1,1.30 /
But that is merely a similarity of expression (<s>śruti</s>). / Jaim_1,1.31 /

children.text: kṛte vā viniyogaḥ syāt karmaṇaḥ saṃbandhāt / Jaim_1,1.32 /
children.translated_text: Or the application would be due to the connection with an already accomplished act. / Jaim_1,1.32 /

He composes the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Should the Vedic sentence be of human origin (<s>pauruṣeya</s>) or not? Its human authorship
would follow from the designation as <s>Kāṭhaka</s> and the like, and from its being a sentence, like other sentences. // MJaiNy_1,1.53 //
The designation is explained by the role of teacher, and the nature of being a sentence is refuted [as a reason];
due to the non-apprehension of its author, there would therefore be non-human authorship (<s>apauruṣeyatā</s>). // MJaiNy_1,1.54 //

children.text:
'kāṭhakam, kauthumam, taittirīyakam' ityādisamākhyā tattadvedaviṣayā loke dṛṣṭā |
taddhitapratyayaśca 'tena proktam' [pāṇi. sū. 4.3.101] ityarthe vartate |
tathā sati 'vyāsena proktaṃ vaiyāsikaṃ bhāratam' ityādāviva pauruṣeyatvaṃ pratīyate |
kiñca 'vimataṃ vedavākyaṃ pauruṣeyam, vākyatvāt, kālidāsādivākyavat' iti

children.translated_text: having arrived at this position,
we say:

children.text:
- adhyayanasaṃpradāyapravartakatvena samākhyopapadyate |
kālidāsādigrantheṣu tattatsargāvasāne kartāra upalabhyante |
tathā vedasyāpi pauruṣeyatve tatkartopalabhyeta |
children.translated_text:
— the designation is explained by the role of propagating the tradition of study (<s>adhyayana-saṃpradāya</s>).
In the works of <s>Kālidāsa</s> and others, the authors are apprehended at the end of each respective section.
Similarly, if the Veda too were of human origin, its author would be apprehended.
But no such [author] is apprehended.
Therefore the reason of 'being a sentence' is defeated by a counter-argument (<s>pratikūla-tarka</s>).
Therefore the Veda is of non-human origin (<s>apauruṣeya</s>).

children.text: tathā sati puruṣabuddhidoṣakṛtasyāprāmāṇyasyānāśaṅkanīyatvādvidhivākyasya dharme prāmāṇyaṃ susthitam || MJaiNyC_1,1.53-54 ||
children.translated_text: This being so, since the invalidity caused by defects in human cognition need not be suspected, the validity of injunctive sentences regarding <s>dharma</s> is well-established. || MJaiNyC_1,1.53-54 ||

The designations '<s>Kāṭhakam</s>, <s>Kauthumam</s>, <s>Taittirīyakam</s>' and so on, pertaining to their respective Vedas, are observed in the world.
The <s>taddhita</s> suffix is used in the sense of 'taught by him' [<s>Pāṇini Sūtra</s> 4.3.101].
This being so, just as in '<s>Vaiyāsikaṃ Bhāratam</s>' (the <s>Bhārata</s> taught by <s>Vyāsa</s>) and the like, human authorship is understood.
Furthermore, 'the Vedic sentence under discussion is of human origin, because it is a sentence, like the sentences of <s>Kālidāsa</s> and others' — thus

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīye jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistare prathamādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>pāda</s> of the first <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Mādhavīya Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s>. //
