(In the first [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>]:

children.text: āmnāyasya kriyārthatvād ānarthakyam atadarthānāṃ tasmād anityam ucyate / Jaim_1,2.1 /
children.translated_text: Since the scripture (<s>āmnāya</s>) has its purpose in action, there is purposelessness of those [passages] not serving that purpose; therefore it is said to be non-eternal. / Jaim_1,2.1 /
And because there is no conflict with what is observed in scripture. / Jaim_1,2.2 /
Similarly, because there is no fruit. / Jaim_1,2.3 /
Because of the purposelessness of the other [interpretation]. / Jaim_1,2.4 /
And because of the prohibition of what has no share. / Jaim_1,2.5 /
Because of the connection with the non-eternal. / Jaim_1,2.6 /

children.text: vidhinā tv ekavākyatvāt stutyarthena vidhīnāṃ syuḥ / Jaim_1,2.7 /
children.translated_text: But because of forming a single sentence (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) with the injunction, they would serve the purpose of praise for the injunctions. / Jaim_1,2.7 /
And the traditional [teaching] is the same. / Jaim_1,2.8 /

children.text: aprāptā cānupapattiḥ prayoge hi virodhaḥ syāc chabdārthas tv aprayogabhūtas tasmād upapadyeta / Jaim_1,2.9 /
children.translated_text: And what is not obtained would be inapplicable; for there would be contradiction in practice, but since the meaning of the word is not in practice, therefore it would be applicable. / Jaim_1,2.9 /
But it is a <s>guṇavāda</s> (subsidiary statement). / Jaim_1,2.10 /
From the form, for the most part. / Jaim_1,2.11 /
Because of the preponderance of remoteness. / Jaim_1,2.12 /
And the seeing of a son would be due to the fault of the agent. / Jaim_1,2.13 /
The desire would be without temporal restriction. / Jaim_1,2.14 /
It is a praise of knowledge. / Jaim_1,2.15 /
The universality pertains to the principal [injunction]. / Jaim_1,2.16 /

children.text: phalasya karmaniṣpattes teṣāṃ lokavatparimāṇataḥ phalaviśeṣaḥ syāt / Jaim_1,2.17 /
children.translated_text: Since the fruit is accomplished by the ritual act, their specific fruit would be determined by measure, as in ordinary experience. / Jaim_1,2.17 /
For the last two, as stated. / Jaim_1,2.18 /
He composes the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the second <s>pāda</s> —
START MJaiNy 1,2.1-3
Does the <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage) such as '<s>vāyur vai</s>' (Vāyu indeed) and so on have authority (<s>mānatā</s>)?

children.text: na vidheye 'sti dharme kiṃ kiṃvāsau tatra vidyate // MJaiNy_1,2.1 //
children.translated_text: Does it not possess it regarding <s>dharma</s>, the object of injunction, or does it indeed possess it there? // MJaiNy_1,2.1 //
Since the mutual expectancy (<s>apekṣā</s>) between injunctive words and <s>arthavāda</s> words is not observed,
there is no forming of a single sentence (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) — how could there be authority regarding <s>dharma</s>? // MJaiNy_1,2.2 //
The injunction and the <s>arthavāda</s> are mutually expectant with respect to excellence (<s>prāśastya</s>) and human purpose (<s>puruṣārtha</s>);
therefore there is unity of sentence (<s>ekavākyatā</s>), and hence the <s>arthavāda</s> passages have authority regarding <s>dharma</s>. // MJaiNy_1,2.3 //

children.text:
kāmyapaśukāṇḍe vidhyarthavādau śrūyete |
'vāyavyaṃ śvetamālabheta bhūtikāmaḥ' iti vidhiḥ |
'vāyurvai kṣepiṣṭhā devatā, vāyumeva svena bhāgadheyenopadhāvati, sa evainaṃ bhūtiṃ gamayati' ityarthavādaḥ |
tatra vidhivākyagatā vāyavyādiśabdā arthavādaśabdanairapekṣyeṇaiva viśiṣṭamarthaṃ vidadhati |
arthavādaśabdaścetaranairapekṣyeṇaiva bhūtārthamanvācakṣate |
'kṣipragāmī vāyuḥ svocitena bhāgena toṣito bhāgapradāyaiśvaryaṃ prayacchati' ityukte rāmāyaṇabhāratādāviva vṛttāntaḥ kaścit pratīyate, na tvanuṣṭheyaṃ kiñcit |
ata ekavākyatvābhāvānnāstyarthavādasya dharme prāmāṇyamiti

children.translated_text: having arrived at this position,
we say:

children.text:
- mā bhūtpadaikavākyatā |
vākyaikavākyatā tu vidyate |
vidhivākyaṃ tāvat puruṣaṃ prerayituṃ vidheyārthasya prāśastyamapekṣate |
children.translated_text:
— let there be no unity of sentence at the level of individual words.
But unity of sentence at the level of complete sentences does exist.
The injunctive sentence, in order to motivate a person, requires the excellence (<s>prāśastya</s>) of the enjoined act.
And the <s>arthavāda</s> sentence requires a human purpose (<s>puruṣārtha</s>), since it is included in the injunction of study which culminates in the comprehension of a purposeful meaning.

children.text: tatra puruṣārthaparyavasitavidhyapekṣitaṃ prāśastyaṃ lakṣaṇāvṛttyā samarpayadarthavādavākyaṃ vidhivākyena sahaikavākyatāmāpadyate |
children.translated_text: Therein, the <s>arthavāda</s> sentence, by conveying through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) the excellence required by the injunction whose culmination is human purpose, attains unity of sentence (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) with the injunctive sentence.

children.text: 'yataḥ kṣipragāmisvabhāvatayā śīghraphalaprado vāyurasya paśordevatā, tataḥ praśastamimaṃ vāyavyaṃ paśumālabheta' iti vākyayoranvayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Since <s>Vāyu</s>, being by nature swift-moving, is a quick bestower of fruit and is the deity of this animal, therefore one should sacrifice this excellent <s>vāyavya</s> animal' — this is the construal of the two sentences.
Therefore, <s>arthavāda</s> passages are a means of knowledge regarding <s>dharma</s>. || MJaiNyC_1,2.1-3 ||

In the <s>Kāmyapaśukāṇḍa</s> (section on desire-motivated animal sacrifices), both injunction and <s>arthavāda</s> are heard.
'<s>Vāyavyaṃ śvetam ālabheta bhūtikāmaḥ</s>' (one desiring prosperity should sacrifice a white animal to <s>Vāyu</s>) — this is the injunction.
'<s>Vāyur vai kṣepiṣṭhā devatā, vāyum eva svena bhāgadheyena upadhāvati, sa eva enam bhūtiṃ gamayati</s>' (<s>Vāyu</s> is indeed the swiftest deity; one approaches <s>Vāyu</s> with his proper share, and he alone leads one to prosperity) — this is the <s>arthavāda</s>.
Therein, the words such as '<s>vāyavya</s>' occurring in the injunctive sentence convey their specific meaning independently of the <s>arthavāda</s> words.
And the <s>arthavāda</s> words independently of the other narrate a factual matter.
When it is said '<s>Vāyu</s>, being swift-moving, when pleased by his proper share, bestows prosperity to the share-giver,' a certain narrative is understood, as in the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> and <s>Mahābhārata</s> and such works, but nothing to be performed is [understood].
Therefore, since there is no forming of a single sentence (<s>ekavākyatā</s>), the <s>arthavāda</s> has no authority regarding <s>dharma</s> — thus
START MJaiNy 1,2.4
In this very <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, following another school of thought, he states the prior and subsequent views —
If it be said that the injunction has no authority because it depends on a reason stated in the <s>arthavāda</s>,
the teacher has declared that it does not depend [on it], because through praise the true connection [is established]. // MJaiNy_1,2.4 //

children.text:
'yato vāyuḥ kṣiprameva phalapradaḥ, ato vāyavyamālabheta' ityevamarthavādoktaṃ hetumapekṣya vidhiḥ puruṣaṃ niyuṅkte |
tataḥ sāpekṣatvādapramāṇamiti

children.translated_text: is the prior view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>)

The injunction commands a person depending on the reason stated in the <s>arthavāda</s>, namely 'since <s>Vāyu</s> quickly bestows fruit, therefore one should sacrifice the <s>vāyavya</s> animal.'
Therefore, due to dependence, it is not a valid means of knowledge — thus

children.text:
'vimataṃ karmānuṣṭheyam, phalapradadevatopetatvāt, rājasevādivat' ityanumānaṃ yadyarthavāde vivakṣyate, tadānīmāgamapramāṇasya vidhivākyasya pramāṇāntarasāpekṣatvaṃ syāt |
na tvevaṃ vivakṣitam |
kintu phalapradadevatātoṣakatvopanyāsamukhena karmaprāśastyamupalakṣyate |
tathā sati 'praśastaṃ karmānuṣṭheyam' ityasminnarthe sārthavādasya videḥ paryavasānādekavākyatā labhyate |
tatra kutaḥ sāpekṣatvam |
tasmāt vidhiḥ pramāṇam iti

children.translated_text: is the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>)
|| MJaiNyC_1,2.4 ||

If what is intended in the <s>arthavāda</s> is an inference such as 'the ritual act under discussion should be performed, because it involves a fruit-bestowing deity, like royal service' — then the injunctive sentence, being a scriptural authority, would be dependent on another means of knowledge.
But this is not what is intended.
Rather, through the mention that the deity is one who delights in bestowing fruit, the excellence (<s>prāśastya</s>) of the ritual act is indicated.
This being so, since the injunction culminates in the meaning 'the excellent ritual should be performed,' unity of sentence with the <s>arthavāda</s> is obtained.
Therein, how could there be dependence?
Therefore the injunction is a valid means of knowledge — thus
the topic of <s>nigada</s> (recitation) similar to injunction —
<s>sūtras</s> 19-25)
(In the second [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>]:

children.text: vidhir vā syād apūrvatvād vādamātrama hy anarthakam / Jaim_1,2.19 /
children.translated_text: It would be an injunction, because of its unprecedentedness (<s>apūrvatva</s>); mere <s>arthavāda</s> would indeed be purposeless. / Jaim_1,2.19 /
If [one says] it is like ordinary usage. / Jaim_1,2.20 /
No, because of its precedence. / Jaim_1,2.21 /
But it has been stated to be a complement of the sentence. / Jaim_1,2.22 /

children.text: vidhiś cānarthakaḥ kvacit tasmāt stutiḥ pratīyeta tatsāmānyād itareṣu tathātvam / Jaim_1,2.23 /
children.translated_text: And an injunction would sometimes be purposeless; therefore praise should be understood; and due to similarity, the same applies to others. / Jaim_1,2.23 /

children.text: prakaraṇe sambhavannapakarṣo na kalpyeta vidhyānarthakyaṃ hi taṃ prati / Jaim_1,2.24 /
children.translated_text: When it is possible in the context, demotion should not be postulated, for there would be purposelessness of the injunction with respect to that. / Jaim_1,2.24 /
And in the case of an injunction, there would be splitting of the sentence. / Jaim_1,2.25 /
START MJaiNy 1,2.5-7
He composes the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is this [passage] '<s>ūrjo 'varudhyai</s>' (for the securing of vital sap) an injunction-like <s>nigada</s> (recitation), or not?

children.text: yūpaudumbaratāṃ stauti stauti vā tadvidhitsayā // MJaiNy_1,2.5 //
children.translated_text: Does it praise the <s>audumbara</s> nature (being made of fig-wood) of the sacrificial post, or does it praise with the intention of enjoining it? // MJaiNy_1,2.5 //
Since there is no indication of fruit through a dative case ending, the <s>audumbara</s> nature of the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) is the fruit;
while stating the securing of vital sap (<s>ūrjas</s>), how could it be intent on praise? // MJaiNy_1,2.6 //
Since the <s>audumbara</s> nature, without being praised, is not enjoined — for whom would that be the fruit?

children.text: arthadvaidhe vākyabhedastena stāvaka eva saḥ // MJaiNy_1,2.7 //
children.translated_text: When there is ambiguity of meaning, sentence-splitting [results]; therefore that [passage] is indeed laudatory (<s>stāvaka</s>). // MJaiNy_1,2.7 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate - 'audumbaro yūpo bhavati, ūrgvā udumbaraḥ, ūrkpaśavaḥ, ūrjaivāsmā ūrjaṃ paśūnāpnoti, ūrjo 'varudhyai' iti |
amṛtaśabdābhidheyo 'tyantasārabhūtaḥ sūkṣmo 'nnarasaḥ ūrgucyate |
udumbararūpayorjā yajamānārthamadhvaryuḥ paśurūpāmūrjamāpnoti |
tato yūpasyaudumbaratvamūrjaḥ sampādanāya bhavatītyarthaḥ |
atra 'avarudhyai' iti tādarthye caturthī |
tayā phalatvaṃ gamyate |
'dhanalābhāya rājasevā' ityādau taddarśanāt |
na ca phalaparasya vacanasya stāvakatvaṃ yujyate |
anyathā svargakāma ityatra svargaśabdasyāpi jyotiṣṭomastāvakatvaprasaṅgāditi

children.translated_text: having arrived at this position,
we say:

children.text:
- ayamūrjo 'varodhaḥ kasya phalaṃ syāt - kimavihitasyaudumbaratvasya, uta vihitasya |
nā'dyaḥ, anuṣṭhānamantareṇa dravyamātrāt phalānutpatteḥ |
dvitīye kimatra vidhiḥ pratyakṣaḥ, utonneyaḥ |
nā'dyaḥ, 'audumbaro yūpo bhavati' ityatra liṅpratyayāśravaṇāt |
dvitīye stutyā sa unneyaḥ |
children.translated_text:
— this securing of vital sap — of what would it be the fruit? Is it of the un-enjoined <s>audumbara</s> nature, or of the enjoined [nature]?
Not the first, because without performance, fruit does not arise from mere material.
In the second case, is the injunction here explicit, or to be inferred?
Not the first, because in '<s>audumbaro yūpo bhavati</s>' (the sacrificial post is made of fig-wood), no <s>liṅ</s> (optative) suffix is heard.
In the second case, that [injunction] would have to be inferred through praise.
But you do not accept praise here.
If it be said that 'the <s>audumbara</s> nature is praised for the purpose of enjoining it, and the fruit is also made known' —
then the sentence would be split.
Therefore, even though this sentence is recited as if it were a fruit-enjoining injunction, it is indeed merely laudatory (<s>stāvaka</s>). || MJaiNyC_1,2.5-7 ||

This is what is recited in scripture: '<s>Audumbaro yūpo bhavati, ūrg vā udumbaraḥ, ūrk paśavaḥ, ūrjaivāsmā ūrjaṃ paśūn āpnoti, ūrjo 'varudhyai</s>' (The sacrificial post is made of fig-wood; fig-wood is indeed vital sap; vital sap is cattle; by vital sap alone one obtains vital sap and cattle for him; for the securing of vital sap).
The extremely essential subtle essence of food, denoted by the word '<s>amṛta</s>' (nectar), is called '<s>ūrj</s>' (vital sap).
The priest (<s>adhvaryu</s>), through the <s>ūrj</s> in the form of fig-wood, obtains <s>ūrj</s> in the form of cattle for the sacrificer.
Therefore the meaning is that the fig-wood nature of the sacrificial post is for the procurement of vital sap.
Here, '<s>avarudhyai</s>' is a dative of purpose.
By that, the status of being a fruit is understood.
Because it is seen in [expressions like] '<s>dhanalābhāya rājasevā</s>' (royal service for the attainment of wealth).
And it is not proper for a statement conveying a fruit to be laudatory.
Otherwise, the word '<s>svarga</s>' (heaven) in '<s>svargakāmaḥ</s>' (one desiring heaven) too would absurdly become a praise of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice — thus
START MJaiNy 1,2.8
In this very [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], following the teacher's view, he states the prior and subsequent views —
Since there is no determination whether '<s>āpnoti</s>' (obtains) has the nature of an injunction or of an <s>arthavāda</s>,

children.text: na pramā codanetyetan vādo hyekavākyataḥ // MJaiNy_1,2.8 //
children.translated_text: there is no valid knowledge from the injunctive sentence (<s>codanā</s>) — this is because the <s>arthavāda</s> [forms] a unity of sentence [with the injunction]. // MJaiNy_1,2.8 //

children.text:
ūrjaṃ paśūnāpnoti ityapūrvārthatvādvidhitvaṃ pratibhāsate, liṅṅādyabhāvādarthavādatvam |
ataḥ sandigdhatvānna prāmāṇyaṃ codanāyā iti

children.translated_text: is the prior view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>)

'<s>Ūrjaṃ paśūn āpnoti</s>' (one obtains vital sap and cattle) — since it conveys an unprecedented meaning, the nature of an injunction appears; [but] due to the absence of the <s>liṅ</s> suffix and the like, [it also has] the nature of an <s>arthavāda</s>.
Therefore, due to the doubtful nature, there is no validity of the injunctive sentence (<s>codanā</s>) — thus

children.text:
ekavākyatvalābhenārthavādatvaṃ nirṇīyate |
ataḥ pramāṇaṃ codanā iti

children.translated_text: is the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>)
|| MJaiNyC_1,2.8 ||

By obtaining unity of sentence (<s>ekavākyatā</s>), the nature as <s>arthavāda</s> is determined.
Therefore, the injunctive sentence (<s>codanā</s>) is a valid means of knowledge — thus
(In the third [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>]: the topic of <s>nigada</s> (recitation) similar to a reason — <s>sūtras</s> 26-30)
Or it would be a reason, because of its meaningfulness and logical fitness. / Jaim_1,2.26 /

children.text: stutis tu śabdapūrvatvād acodanā tasya / Jaim_1,2.27 /
children.translated_text: But praise, being preceded by the word [alone], is not an injunction (<s>codanā</s>) of that. / Jaim_1,2.27 /
If [one says] that praise of the meaning is improper. / Jaim_1,2.28 /

children.text: arthas tu vidhiśeṣatvād yathā loke / Jaim_1,2.29 /
children.translated_text: But the meaning is a complement of the injunction, as in ordinary usage. / Jaim_1,2.29 /

children.text: yadi ca hetur avatiṣṭheta nirdeśāt sāmānyād iti ced avasthā vidhīnāṃ syāt / Jaim_1,2.30 /
children.translated_text: And if a reason were to remain [independently], then from the indication and similarity, there would be a fixed state of the injunctions. / Jaim_1,2.30 /
He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
START MJaiNy 1,2.9-10

children.text: tena hyannamiti prokto vādo heturuta stutiḥ /
children.translated_text: Is the <s>arthavāda</s> passage '<s>tena hy annam</s>' (for by that, food) stated as a reason, or is it praise?

children.text: hinā śrutā hetutātaḥ śūrpamanyacca sādhanam // MJaiNy_1,2.9 //
children.translated_text: Since '<s>hinā</s>' is heard [as indicating] the nature of a reason, [it follows that] the winnowing basket (<s>śūrpa</s>) and other things are means [of the ritual]. // MJaiNy_1,2.9 //
The status of the winnowing basket as a means is derived from scripture (<s>śrauta</s>); it is not to be weighed against non-scriptural [considerations].
Therefore the reason is purposeless; hence the praise is motivating. // MJaiNy_1,2.10 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyeta - 'śūrpeṇa juhoti tena hyannaṃ kriyate' ayamarthavādo vidheye śūrpe hetutvenānveti |
hiśabdasya hetuvāyitvāt |
' yasmādannasādhanaṃ, tasmācchūrpeṇa hotavyam ' ityukte ' yadyadannasādhanaṃ darvīpiṭharādikaṃ tena sarveṇa hotavyam ' iti labhyate |
tataḥ ' piṭharādayaḥ śūrpeṇa saha vikalpyante ' iti prāpte -
brūmaḥ-- śūrpasya homasādhanatvaṃ śrautam, tṛtīyayā tadavagamāt |

children.translated_text: But that of pots and other [instruments] is merely inferential.
Therefore, since they are not of equal strength, alternation is not appropriate.
Hence the reason is superfluous.
The praise is useful for the purpose of commendation; therefore the connection is as praise. || MJaiNyC_1,2.9-10 ||

This is taught: 'One offers with a winnowing basket (<s>śūrpa</s>), for thereby food is prepared.' This <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage) is connected as a reason to the prescribed <s>śūrpa</s>, because the particle '<s>hi</s>' has the nature of indicating a reason. When it is stated 'because it is a means of preparing food, therefore one should offer with the winnowing basket,' it follows that 'whatever is a means of preparing food — ladle, pot, and the like — one should offer with all of them.' Thereupon, when it is suggested that 'pots and such are to be optionally used along with the winnowing basket' — we say: the <s>śūrpa</s>'s capacity as an instrument for oblation is Vedic (<s>śrauta</s>), since that is understood from the instrumental case ending.
(In the fourth [topic] — the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on indication from <s>mantras</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 31 to 53)
Because of the scripture being for that purpose. / Jaim_1,2.31 /
Because of the restriction of the sentence. / Jaim_1,2.32 /
Because of the scripture being for cognition. / Jaim_1,2.33 /
Because of the statement of what is non-existent. / Jaim_1,2.34 /
Because of the attribution of purpose to an insentient entity. / Jaim_1,2.35 /
Because of the contradiction of meaning. / Jaim_1,2.36 /
Because of the statement being like self-study. / Jaim_1,2.37 /
Because of being unknowable. / Jaim_1,2.38 /
Because of the non-permanent connection, the meaning of <s>mantras</s> is purposeless. / Jaim_1,2.39 /
But the sentence-meaning is undifferentiated. / Jaim_1,2.40 /
The scripture is again for a subsidiary purpose. / Jaim_1,2.41 /
Enumeration (<s>parisaṃkhyā</s>). / Jaim_1,2.42 /
Or it is an <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage). / Jaim_1,2.43 /
The latter is non-contradictory. / Jaim_1,2.44 /
In the directive (<s>saṃpraiṣa</s>), the censure of the ritual act is not a reproach, because it is a preparatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>). / Jaim_1,2.45 /
In the statement, it is an <s>arthavāda</s>. / Jaim_1,2.46 /
There would be no prohibition from a subsidiary element. / Jaim_1,2.47 /
The statement of knowledge is due to the absence of connection. / Jaim_1,2.48 /
The supreme knowledge of that which exists. / Jaim_1,2.49 /
And the non-permanent connection has been stated. / Jaim_1,2.50 /
And the teaching of the indicatory mark is as having that purpose. / Jaim_1,2.51 /
Substitution (<s>ūha</s>). / Jaim_1,2.52 /
And the injunctive words. / Jaim_1,2.53 /
He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 1.2.11-12]
Are <s>mantras</s> such as '<s>uru prathasva</s>' (expand widely) solely causes of unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>)?
Or in sacrifices, do they also illuminate [visible actions] such as the spreading of the sacrificial cake (<s>puroḍāśa</s>)? // MJaiNy_1,2.11 //
Since that [spreading] is also illuminated by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> text, are <s>mantras</s> solely causes of merit (<s>puṇya</s>)?
No — since illuminating that [meaning] is a visible [purpose], the visible is preferable to the unseen. // MJaiNy_1,2.12 //

children.text:
'uru prathasva' ityayaṃ kaścinmantraḥ |
tasyāyamarthaḥ - bhoḥ puroḍāśa, svamuruvipulatā yathā bhavati tathā prasara ' iti |
evamādayo mantrā yāgaprayogepūccāryamāṇā adṛṣṭameva janayanti |
natvarthaprakāśanāya taduccāraṇam |
puroḍāśaprathana lakṣaṇasyārthasya vrāhmaṇavākyenāpi bhāsanāt tha 'uru prathasveti puroḍāśaṃ prathayati' iti hi brāhmaṇavākyam ,[iti cetṭa |

children.translated_text: this is not proper.

children.text: arthapratyāyanasya dṛṣṭaprayojanaskaya saṃbhave sati kevalādṛṣṭasya kalpayitumaśakyatvāt |
children.translated_text: Because when a visible purpose — namely, the conveyance of meaning — is possible, the postulation of unseen merit alone is not feasible.
Therefore, the visible purpose of <s>mantra</s>-recitation in the course of a sacrifice is the recollection of meaning alone.

children.text: brāhmaṇavākyenāpyarthānusmaraṇasaṃbhave 'mantreṇaivānusmapaṇīyam ' iti yo niyamaḥ, tasya dṛṣṭāsaṃbhavādadṛṣṭaṃ prayojanamastu || MJaiNyC_1,2.11-12 ||
children.translated_text: Even though recollection of meaning is possible through the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage, the restriction that 'meaning should be recollected through the <s>mantra</s> alone' — since a visible [purpose] for that [restriction] is not possible, let its purpose be unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>). || MJaiNyC_1,2.11-12 ||

'<s>Uru prathasva</s>' (expand widely) — this is a certain <s>mantra</s>. Its meaning is: 'O sacrificial cake, spread forth such that your own wide expansion comes about.' Such <s>mantras</s>, when recited in the course of the sacrifice, generate unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) alone. Their recitation is not for the illumination of meaning, because the meaning characterized by the spreading of the sacrificial cake is illuminated also by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage — for '<s>uru prathasveti puroḍāśaṃ prathayati</s>' (he spreads the sacrificial cake saying '<s>uru prathasva</s>') is indeed the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage — if this be argued,
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 1.2.13]
In this very [topic], he states the prior and established views according to another opinion —
Or rather, there is a conflict between <s>mantra</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> regarding application (<s>viniyoga</s>);
the other [<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] does not restate the meaning established by the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of the <s>mantra</s>, since [it has independent force]. // MJaiNy_1,2.13 //

children.text: asya mantrasya liṅgena viniyoge brāhmaṇavākyamavivakṣitārthe syāt |

children.translated_text: When application is [established] by the [<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] sentence, the indicatory mark of the <s>mantra</s> would not be intended.
Thus, due to the contradiction of both, the injunction (<s>codanā</s>) is invalid — this is the prior view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>).

children.text: nāyaṃ virodhaḥ, prabalena hi liṅgena viniyogasiddhau vākyasyānuvādakatvāditi -
children.translated_text: This is not a contradiction, for when application is established by the stronger indicatory mark, the sentence merely restates [what is already established] — thus
this is the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>). || MJaiNyC_1,2.13 ||
When application is [established] by the indicatory mark of this <s>mantra</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage would have an unintended meaning.

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīye jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistare prathamādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second quarter (<s>pāda</s>) of the first chapter (<s>adhyāya</s>) in the illustrious <s>Mādhava</s>'s <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s>.
Now the third quarter (<s>pāda</s>).
(In the first [topic] — the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the validity of <s>smṛti</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 1–2)

children.text: dharmasya śabdamūlatvād aśabdam anapekṣaṃ syāt / Jaim_1,3.1 /
children.translated_text: Since <s>dharma</s> is rooted in verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>), what is non-verbal should be disregarded. / Jaim_1,3.1 /

children.text: api vā kartṛsāmānyāt pramāṇam anumānaṃ syāt / Jaim_1,3.2 /
children.translated_text: Or rather, inference may be a valid means of knowledge due to the commonality of the agent. / Jaim_1,3.2 /
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 1.3.1-2]
He composes the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the third <s>pāda</s> —
The <s>smṛti</s> of <s>aṣṭakā</s> rites and the like — is it a valid means of knowledge regarding <s>dharma</s>, or is it not?

children.text: nirmūlatvānna mānaṃ sā vedārthoktau nirarthatā // MJaiNy_1,3.1 //
children.translated_text: It is not valid due to being without a Vedic root; and if it merely states the meaning of the Veda, it is purposeless. // MJaiNy_1,3.1 //
Since it is remembered by those versed in the Vedas, its rootedness in the Veda is to be presumed;
and since it serves the purpose of condensing meanings scattered [across the Vedas], it has purposefulness, and hence validity. // MJaiNy_1,3.2 //

children.text:
"aṣṭakāḥ kartavyāḥ"ityādi smṛtivākyaṃ na dharme pramāṇama , pauruṣeyavākyatve sati mūlapramāṇarahitatvāt , vipralambhakavākyatvāt |
atha mūlapramāṇavattvāya vedārtha eva smṛtiranarthā syāt |
tadānīmanuvādakatvādaprāmāṇyamiti prāpte - brūmaḥ -- ' vimatā smṛtirvedamūlā, vaidikamanvādipraṇītasmṛtitvāt , upanayānādhyayanādismṛtivat ' |
children.translated_text: When it is concluded that due to being merely a restatement it is invalid — we say: 'The disputed <s>smṛti</s> has a Vedic root, because it is a <s>smṛti</s> composed by one who follows the Vedas, like the <s>smṛti</s> regarding initiation (<s>upanayana</s>), study (<s>adhyayana</s>), and the like.'
And purposelessness should not be suspected,

children.text: asmadādīnāṃ pratyakṣeṣu parokṣeṣu caṃ nānāvedeṣu viprakīrṇasyānuṣṭheyārthasyaikatra saṃkṣipyamāṇatvāt |
children.translated_text: because the content to be practiced, which is scattered across various Vedas — both those directly known to us and those beyond our reach — is condensed into a single place.
Therefore this <s>smṛti</s> is a valid means of knowledge regarding <s>dharma</s>. || MJaiNyC_1,2.1-2 ||

The <s>smṛti</s> statement '<s>aṣṭakāḥ kartavyāḥ</s>' (the <s>aṣṭakā</s> rites should be performed) and the like is not a valid means of knowledge regarding <s>dharma</s>, because being a human-authored statement (<s>pauruṣeya</s>), it is devoid of a root source of valid knowledge, and because it is a deceptive statement. If, for the purpose of having a root source of validity, the <s>smṛti</s> merely [restates] the meaning of the Veda, then the <s>smṛti</s> would be purposeless.
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 1.3.3]
In this very [topic], he states the prior and established views according to another opinion —

children.text: na mā smārtāṣṭaṅkāṅgatvādyāṃ janā iti mantragīḥ /
children.translated_text: It is not valid, because the hymnic <s>mantra</s> '<s>yāṃ janāḥ</s>' (whom people [praise]) is a subsidiary of the <s>smārta</s> (tradition-based) <s>aṣṭakā</s> rite;
that is not so — because when the root Veda of the <s>smṛti</s> is inferred, the possibility of validity exists. // MJaiNy_1,3.3 //

children.text:
'yāṃ janāḥ pratinandati ' ityayaṃ mantroṣṭakāśrāddhasyāṅgam |
tecca śrāddhaṃ smārtam |
na hi tasya pratipādakaṃ vedavākyamupalabhāmahe |
tasmādidaṃ mantravākyaṃ na dharme pramāṇamiti cet |

children.translated_text: No.
Because the Veda that is its root can be inferred.
And the inference has been demonstrated [earlier].
Therefore that <s>mantra</s> is a valid means of knowledge regarding <s>dharma</s>. || MJaiNyC_1,2.3 ||

The <s>mantra</s> '<s>yāṃ janāḥ pratinandanti</s>' (whom people praise) is a subsidiary of the <s>aṣṭakā</s>-<s>śrāddha</s>. And that <s>śrāddha</s> is <s>smārta</s> (based on <s>smṛti</s>). For we do not find a Vedic sentence that establishes it. Therefore, if it is argued that this <s>mantra</s> sentence is not a valid means of knowledge regarding <s>dharma</s> —
(In the second [topic] — the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the predominance of <s>śruti</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: virodhe tv anapekṣyaṃ syād asati hy anumānam / Jaim_1,3.3 /
children.translated_text: But in case of conflict, [<s>smṛti</s>] should be disregarded, for inference operates [only] in the absence [of direct scripture]. / Jaim_1,3.3 /
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 1.3.4-5]
He composes the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The <s>smṛti</s> that 'the <s>audumbarī</s> (fig-wood branch) should be entirely wrapped' is a valid cognition;
whether it is valid or invalid being in doubt, it should be valid, like [the <s>smṛti</s> of] <s>aṣṭakā</s> and the like. // MJaiNy_1,3.4 //
From the directly known Vedic [text], 'One should sing the <s>udgītha</s> while touching the <s>audumbarī</s>';
due to the conflict, the root Veda [of the <s>smṛti</s>] cannot be inferred, and hence [the <s>smṛti</s>] is invalid. // MJaiNy_1,3.5 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome sadonāmakasya maṇḍapasya madhye kācidaudumbarī śākhā nikhanyate |
tasyāśrca vāsasā veṣṭanaṃ smaryate- ' audumbarī sarvā veṣṭayitavyā' iti |
sā smṛtiḥ pramāṇam, aṣṭakādismṛtiṣviva mūlavedasyānumātuṃ śakyatvāditi prāpte -
brūmaḥ - ' audumbarīṃ spṛṣṭvodgāyet ' iti pratyakṣevadavacanena sparśo vidhīyate |
children.translated_text: We say: by the directly known Vedic statement '<s>audumbarīṃ spṛṣṭvā udgāyet</s>' (one should sing the <s>udgītha</s> while touching the <s>audumbarī</s>), touch is prescribed.
And touch is not possible when [the branch] is entirely wrapped.
Therefore the inference of a root Veda [for that <s>smṛti</s>] is vitiated by contradiction (<s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭa</s>).
Therefore, like a deceptive statement, this rootless <s>smṛti</s> is invalid. || MJaiNyC_1,2.4-5 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice, a certain <s>audumbarī</s> (fig-wood) branch is planted in the middle of the pavilion called the <s>sadas</s>. And its wrapping with cloth is remembered in tradition: '<s>audumbarī sarvā veṣṭayitavyā</s>' (the entire <s>audumbarī</s> should be wrapped). This <s>smṛti</s> is valid, since, as with <s>smṛtis</s> regarding <s>aṣṭakā</s> and the like, a root Veda can be inferred — when this is the position arrived at —
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 1.3.6-7]
In this very <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, he states another opinion —
Or rather, since a conflict between the directly known and inferred <s>śruti</s> is observed,
when invalidity is suspected, the overriding of inference is described here. // MJaiNy_1,3.6 //
If the Veda directly known to another person is the root here for [the <s>smṛti</s> of] wrapping,
even so, the practice should conform to one's own directly known [Vedic text]. // MJaiNy_1,3.7 //

Due to the mutual contradiction between the directly known and inferred <s>śrutis</s> concerning touch and complete wrapping respectively, both are invalid — this is the prior view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>).

children.text: anumānasya kālātyayāpadiṣṭatayā viruddhaśrutyabhāvena sparśaśrutiḥ svārthe pramāṇam |
children.translated_text: Since the inference is vitiated by contradiction, and there is no conflicting <s>śruti</s>, the <s>śruti</s> regarding touch is valid in its own domain.

children.text: yadi puruṣāntarapratyakṣavedaḥ sarvaveṣṭanasmṛtermūlamityucyate, tarhi mā bhūttasyā aprāmāṇyam |
children.translated_text: If it is said that the Veda directly known to another person is the root of the <s>smṛti</s> of complete wrapping, then let there be no invalidity of that [<s>smṛti</s>].

children.text: tathāpi parapratyakṣātsvapratyakṣasyābhyarhitatvena sparśa evātrānuṣṭheyo natu sarvaveṣṭanam || MJaiNyC_1,2.6-7 ||
children.translated_text: Even so, since one's own directly known [Vedic text] is more authoritative than another's, touch alone should be practiced here, not complete wrapping. || MJaiNyC_1,2.6-7 ||
(In the third [topic] — the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the invalidity of <s>smṛti</s> having a visible motive, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
And because a [mundane] motive is observed. / Jaim_1,3.4 /
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 1.3.8-9]
He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The <s>smṛti</s> regarding the taking of the cloth used for the oblation called <s>vaisarjana</s> —

children.text: pramā na vā śrutyabādhātpramā syādaṣṭakādivat // MJaiNy_1,3.8 //
children.translated_text: is it valid or not? Since there is no overriding by <s>śruti</s>, it should be valid, like [the <s>smṛti</s> of] <s>aṣṭakā</s> and the like. // MJaiNy_1,3.8 //
Since, when the possibility of its having a single visible root in greed exists, no [root] <s>śruti</s> need be postulated;
even though it is not overridden like [the <s>smṛti</s> of] complete wrapping, this [<s>smṛti</s>] is indeed not valid. // MJaiNy_1,3.9 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭom'gnīṣomīyasya paśostantre prakrānte vaisarjanahomo vihitaḥ |
tatra yajamānaṃ patnīṃ putrāṃśrca bhrātṝṃśrcāhatena vāsasā pracchādya vāsaso 'nte strugdaṇḍamupanibadhya juhoti |
tasminvāsasyevaṃ smaryate - ' vaisarjanahomīyaṃ vāso 'dhvaryurgṛhṇāti' iti |
seyaṃ smṛtiḥ sarvaveṣṭanasmṛtivatpratyakṣaśrutyā na bādhyate |
tato 'ṣṭakādismṛtivatpramāṇamiti prāpte -
brūmaḥ- kadācitkaśrcidadhvaryurlobhādatadvāso jagrāha |
tanmūlaivaiṣā smṛtirityapi kalpanā saṃbhavati |

children.translated_text: And this supposition follows observed [behavior],
because greed is observed among priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>) who are hired for ritual fees (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>).
This being so, since this <s>smṛti</s> can also be explained otherwise, a root <s>śruti</s> cannot be postulated for it, unlike the <s>smṛti</s> of <s>aṣṭakā</s> and the like.

children.text: ato bādhābhāve 'pi mūlabhedābhāvānneyaṃ smṛtiḥ pramāṇam || MJaiNyC_1,2.8-9 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, even in the absence of overriding [<s>śruti</s>], due to the absence of a [Vedic] root distinct [from greed], this <s>smṛti</s> is not valid. || MJaiNyC_1,2.8-9 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, when the procedure of the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal sacrifice is being performed, the <s>vaisarjana</s> oblation is prescribed. There, having covered the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>), his wife, sons, and brothers with an unwashed cloth, and having tied the handle of the ladle (<s>sruc</s>) to the end of the cloth, he offers. Regarding that cloth, this is remembered in tradition: '<s>vaisarjanahomīyaṃ vāso 'dhvaryurgṛhṇāti</s>' (the <s>Adhvaryu</s> takes the cloth used for the <s>vaisarjana</s> oblation). This <s>smṛti</s>, unlike the <s>smṛti</s> of complete wrapping, is not overridden by directly known <s>śruti</s>. Therefore, like the <s>smṛti</s> of <s>aṣṭakā</s> and the like, it should be valid — when this position is arrived at — we say: at some point, a certain <s>Adhvaryu</s>, out of greed, took that cloth which was not [rightfully] his. The supposition that this <s>smṛti</s> has that [greedy act] as its root is also possible.
(In the fourth [topic] — the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the predominance of word-meaning, <s>sūtras</s> 5–7)
If [it be argued that <s>smṛti</s>] is non-contradicted because the learned (<s>śiṣṭa</s>) would be angered [if it were rejected]. / Jaim_1,3.5 /
No, because scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) is the measure [of <s>dharma</s>]. / Jaim_1,3.6 /

children.text: api vā kāraṇagrahaṇe prayuktāni pratīyeran / Jaim_1,3.7 /
children.translated_text: Or rather, [words] employed in grasping causes should be understood [in their primary sense]. / Jaim_1,3.7 /
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 1.3.10-11]
He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> according to the <s>Bhāṣya</s> view —

children.text: ācāntenetyamā mā vā smṛtireṣā na mā bhavet /
children.translated_text: The <s>smṛti</s> that [one should offer] 'having sipped water (<s>ācamya</s>)' — is it valid or invalid?

children.text: vedaṃ kṛtveti yaḥ śrautaḥ kramastena virodhataḥ // MJaiNy_1,3.10 //
children.translated_text: It conflicts with the Vedic sequence stated as 'having performed the Vedic [act].' // MJaiNy_1,3.10 //
Here <s>ācamana</s> (sipping) and the like is the word-meaning; the sequence is the <s>dharma</s> that is subordinate to the word-meaning;
since <s>dharma</s> depends on the <s>dharmin</s> (substratum), and since there is no overriding, [the <s>smṛti</s>] has validity. // MJaiNy_1,3.11 //

children.text:
'kṣuta ācāmet ' iti vihitaṃ puruṣārthamācamanam |
yadā tu kratumadhye kṣutādi nimittaṃ prapnoti tadā naimittikamācamanaṃ kratvaṅgatvena smṛtyā vidhīyate |
' ācāntena kartavyam ' iti |
seyaṃ smṛtirna pramāṇam |
kutaḥ |
virūddhatvāt |
'vedaṃ kṛtvā vediṃ karoti ' iti śrutau pūrvakālavācinā tvāpratyayena kramaḥ pratīyate |
vedo nāma darbhamayaṃ saṃmārjanasādhanam |
vedirāhavanīyagārhapatyamadhyavartinī caturaṅgulakhātā bhūmiḥ |
tayormadhye yadi kṣutādinimittamācamanaṃ kuryāt , tadā śrutyuktaṃ nairantaryaṃ virūdhyeta |
tasmādveṣṭanasmṛtivadācamanasmṛtirna pramāṇamiti prapte -
brūmaḥ- vedavedyādiśrutyuktapadārthavadācamanādayaḥ smṛtyuktā anuṣṭheyapadārthāḥ |
kramastu padārthaniṣṭho dharmaḥ |
sa ca padārthānupajīvati |

children.translated_text: Therefore, due to conflict with what it depends upon, it is the sequence itself that is overridden.
But <s>ācamana</s> is not overridden by the sequence.
Therefore this <s>smṛti</s> is authoritative.

children.text: asminneva vārtikakāraḥ prakārāntareṇa vicāradvayaṃ cakāra || MJaiNyC_1,2.10-11 ||
children.translated_text: In this very [topic], the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> conducted a twofold investigation in another manner. || MJaiNyC_1,2.10-11 ||

'When one sneezes, one should perform <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping)' — thus <s>ācamana</s> for personal benefit is enjoined. But when, in the midst of a sacrifice, the occasion of sneezing and the like arises, then occasional <s>ācamana</s> is enjoined by <s>smṛti</s> as an ancillary of the sacrifice: 'It should be performed by one who has sipped water.' This <s>smṛti</s> is not authoritative. Why? Because of contradiction. In the <s>śruti</s> '<s>vedaṃ kṛtvā vediṃ karoti</s>' (having made the <s>veda</s>, one makes the <s>vedi</s>), by the <s>tvā</s>-suffix indicating prior time, a sequence is understood. <s>Veda</s> here means a broom-instrument made of <s>darbha</s> grass. <s>Vedi</s> is the ground dug four fingers deep, situated between the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and <s>Gārhapatya</s> fires. If between these two [acts], one were to perform <s>ācamana</s> occasioned by sneezing and the like, then the unbroken sequence stated in the <s>śruti</s> would be contradicted. Therefore, like the <s>smṛti</s> of enveloping, the <s>smṛti</s> of <s>ācamana</s> is not authoritative — having arrived at this position, we say: Just as the objects stated in the <s>śruti</s> such as <s>veda</s>, <s>vedi</s>, and so on, <s>ācamana</s> and the like are objects to be performed as stated in <s>smṛti</s>. But sequence (<s>krama</s>) is a property pertaining to the objects. And it depends upon the objects.
START MJaiNy 1,3.12
There he shows the first investigation —

children.text: śākyoktāhiṃsanaṃ dharmo na vā dharmaḥ śrutatvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Is non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) as taught by the <s>Śākyas</s> (Buddhists) <s>dharma</s> or not, since it is heard [in the Veda]?

children.text: na dharmo nahi pūtaṃ syādgokṣīraṃ śrvadṛtau dhṛtam // MJaiNy_1,3.12 //
children.translated_text: It is not <s>dharma</s>, for cow's milk would not be pure if kept in a vessel made of dog-skin. // MJaiNy_1,3.12 //

children.text:
'brahmacaryamahiṃsāṃ cāparigrahaṃ ca satyaṃ ca yatnena rakṣet ' iti śrutāvahiṃsādirdharmatvenoktaḥ |
sa eva dharmaḥ śākyenāpyuktaḥ |
tasmācchākyasmṛtirdharme pramāṇamiti cet |

children.translated_text: No.
Because, by the analogy of cow's milk, even <s>dharma</s> itself, through association with the <s>Śākyas</s>, would face the absurd consequence of losing its nature as <s>dharma</s>.
<s>Ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence) and the like should not be learned from their texts.
Therefore that <s>smṛti</s> is not authoritative regarding <s>dharma</s>. || MJaiNyC_1,2.12 ||

'One should carefully protect celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), non-possession (<s>aparigraha</s>), and truth (<s>satya</s>)' — thus in the <s>śruti</s>, <s>ahiṃsā</s> and other [virtues] are stated as constituting <s>dharma</s>. That very <s>dharma</s> is also taught by the <s>Śākyas</s> (Buddhists). Therefore, the <s>smṛti</s> of the <s>Śākyas</s> is authoritative regarding <s>dharma</s> — if this be argued:
START MJaiNy 1,3.13
He shows the other investigation —
Is virtuous conduct (<s>sadācāra</s>) valid or not? Due to having no root, it is not authoritative;
Like the <s>aṣṭakā</s> rites, it is authoritative because of having a root. // MJaiNy_1,3.13 //
Because, being accepted by the Vedic-observing learned (<s>śiṣṭas</s>), it is rooted in the Veda, like the <s>aṣṭakā</s> rites.
For this very reason, <s>sadācāra</s> (virtuous conduct), though not specifically taught by <s>Manu</s> and others out of fear of prolixity in their texts, is taught by them in general terms.
'<s>Śrutiḥ smṛtiḥ sadācāraḥ</s>' — thus, by this enumeration of authoritative sources regarding <s>dharma</s>.
Therefore, the conduct of the learned (<s>śiṣṭa</s>) is authoritative. || MJaiNyC_1,2.13 ||
Since virtuous conduct such as the <s>Holāka</s> festival and the like has no root-Veda, it is not authoritative — if this be argued: No.
(In the fifth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>] on the authority of meanings established in <s>śāstra</s> — [also called] the <s>Ārya-Mleccha adhikaraṇa</s> — <s>sūtras</s> 8-9)

children.text: teṣv adarśanād virodhasya samā vipratipattiḥ syāt / Jaim_1,3.8 /
children.translated_text: Since no contradiction is seen in them, the conflicting views would be equal. / Jaim_1,3.8 /
Or, [the meaning] established in <s>śāstra</s> [prevails], because it is caused by that. / Jaim_1,3.9 /
START MJaiNy 1,3.14-15
He composes the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Are words like <s>yava</s> ('barley') of double meaning or not, given the equality of <s>Ārya</s> and <s>Mleccha</s> [usage]?
For <s>dīrghaśūka</s> (long-awned grain) and <s>priyaṅgu</s> (millet), meanings are alternatively assigned in both [usages]. // MJaiNy_1,3.14 //
Where there is another [meaning], the establishment in <s>śāstra</s> is stronger;

children.text: śāstrīyadharme tenātra priyaṅgvādi na gṛhyate // MJaiNy_1,3.15 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in scriptural <s>dharma</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s> and the like are not taken [as the meaning]. // MJaiNy_1,3.15 //

children.text:
'yavamayaśrcarurbhavati ' 'vārāhī upānahāvupamuñcate ' iti śrūyate |
tatra yava śabdamāryā dīrghaśūkeṣu prayuñjate varāhaśabdaṃ ca sūkare |
mlecchāstu yavaśabdaṃ priyaṅguṣu , varāhaśabdaṃ ca kṛṣṇaśakunau |
tathā sati lokavyavahāreṇa niśrcetavyeṣu śabdārtheṣvāryamlecchaprasiddhyoḥ samānabalatvādubhayavidhā aṣyarthā vikalpena svīkāryā iti prapte -
brūmaḥ- śāstrīyadharmāvabodhe śāstraprasiddhirbalīyasī |
pratyāsannatvādavicchinnapāramparyāgatatvācca |
śāstre yavavidhyarthavāda evaṃ śrūyate - ' yatrānyā oṣadhayo mlāyante, athaite modamānā ivotiṣṭhanti ' iti |
itarauṣadhivināśakāle 'bhivṛddhirghaśūkeṣu dṛśyate, na tu priyaṅguṣu |
teṣāmitarauṣadhiparipākātpūrve pacyamānatvāt |
vārāhopānadvidhyarthavādaśrcaivaṃ bhavati - ' varāhaṃ gāvo 'nudhāvanti ' iti |
gavāmanudhāvanaṃ śūkare saṃbhavati na tu kṛṣṇaśakunau |

children.translated_text: Therefore, long-awned grain (barley) is the meaning of the word <s>yava</s> and similar terms.
Here the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> cited the word <s>pīlu</s> as an example.

children.text: taṃ ca mlecchā hastini prayuñjate, āryāstu vṛkṣe |
children.translated_text: The <s>Mlecchas</s> use it for an elephant, but the <s>Āryas</s> use it for a tree.
Since uninterrupted usage is found among the <s>Āryas</s>, the tree alone is the meaning of the word <s>pīlu</s>. || MJaiNyC_1,2.14-15 ||

'The offering cake is made of <s>yava</s> (barley),' 'One puts on <s>vārāhī</s> (boar-skin) sandals' — thus it is heard in the <s>śruti</s>. There, the <s>Āryas</s> use the word <s>yava</s> for long-awned grain (barley), and the word <s>varāha</s> for the boar. But the <s>Mlecchas</s> use the word <s>yava</s> for <s>priyaṅgu</s> (millet), and the word <s>varāha</s> for the black bird. This being so, when the meanings of words are to be determined by common usage, since the <s>Ārya</s> and <s>Mleccha</s> conventions are of equal strength, both types of meanings should be accepted alternatively — having arrived at this position, we say: In understanding scriptural <s>dharma</s>, the convention established in <s>śāstra</s> is stronger, because of proximity and because it comes through unbroken tradition. In the <s>śāstra</s>, the <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage) of the <s>yava</s>-injunction is heard thus: 'Where other plants wither, there these stand up as if rejoicing.' Such thriving at the time when other plants perish is seen in the case of long-awned grain (barley), not in <s>priyaṅgu</s> (millet), since the latter ripens before the other plants mature. Similarly, the <s>arthavāda</s> of the <s>vārāhī</s>-sandal injunction states: 'The cows chase after the <s>varāha</s>.' The chasing by cows is possible in the case of a boar, not in the case of a black bird.
START MJaiNy 1,3.16
In this very <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, he states the teacher's view —
If it be said that the injunctive sentence is not authoritative because the meaning of <s>yava</s> and similar terms is undetermined —
No, because the <s>śāstra</s> is stronger, and the meaning is determined through scriptural convention. // MJaiNy_1,3.16 //
The meaning is clear. || MJaiNyC_1,2.16 ||
START MJaiNy 1,3.17-18
In this very <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, he composes another topic according to the view of the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> —

children.text: yo mātulavivāhādau śiṣṭācāraḥ sa mā na vā /
children.translated_text: Is the conduct of the learned (<s>śiṣṭa</s>) regarding marriage with a maternal uncle's daughter and similar [practices] authoritative or not?
Like [the invalidity of] other practices [contradicted by <s>smṛti</s>], the maternal and non-maternal relationship [should be established] from the overriding by <s>smṛti</s>. // MJaiNy_1,3.17 //
For everywhere the conduct of the learned is rooted in <s>smṛti</s>; therefore here too,

children.text: anumeyā smṛtiḥ smṛtyā bādhyā pratyakṣayā tu sā // MJaiNy_1,3.18 //
children.translated_text: a <s>smṛti</s> should be inferred; but that [inferred <s>smṛti</s>] is overridden by a directly perceived <s>smṛti</s>. // MJaiNy_1,3.18 //

children.text:
keṣuciddakṣiṇadeśeṣu mātulasya duhitaraṃ śiṣṭāḥ pariṇayanti |
so 'yamāyāraḥ pramāṇaṃ, śiṣṭācāratvāt , holākādyācāravat , iti cet |
na |
smṛtiviruddhatvena kālātyayāpadiṣṭatvāt |
tathā ca smṛtiḥ-
"mātulasya sutāmūḍhvā mātṛgotrāṃ tathaiva ca |
samānapravarāṃ caiva tyaktvā cāndrāyaṇaṃ caret" || iti |
na ca smṛtyācārayormūlavaidānumāpakasāmyātsamabalatvamiti śaṅkanīyam |
holākādisadācārasya manvādismṛtivadvedānumāpakatvāyogāt |
nahīdānīntanāḥ śiṣṭā manvādivaddeśakālaviprakṛṣṭaṃ vedaṃ divyajñānena sākṣātkartu śaknuvanti |
yena śiṣṭacāro mūlavedamanumāpayet |
śaknoti ca yaḥ kopi śiṣṭo yatra kvāpi deśaviśeṣe kālaviśeṣe ca yaṃ kañcanāpi holākādyācarasya mūlabhūtaṃ smṛtigranthamavalokayitum |
tasmācchiṣṭācāreṇa smṛtirevānumātuṃ śakyate, natu śrutiḥ |
anumitā ca smṛtirvirūddhayā pratyakṣayā smṛtyā bādhyate |
ata evā'huḥ-
"ācārāttu smṛtiṃ jñātvā smṛtiśrca śrutikalpamam |
tena dvayantaritaṃ teṣāṃ prāmāṇyaṃ viprakaṣyate" || iti |

children.translated_text: Therefore, the non-authority of such conduct should be accepted. || MJaiNyC_1,2.17-18 ||

In certain southern regions, the learned (<s>śiṣṭas</s>) marry the daughter of a maternal uncle. This practice is authoritative, being the conduct of the learned, like the <s>Holāka</s> and similar practices — if this be argued: No. Because it is invalidated by time-lapse (<s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭa</s>), being contradicted by <s>smṛti</s>. Thus the <s>smṛti</s> states: 'Having married the daughter of a maternal uncle, or one of the maternal <s>gotra</s>, or one of the same <s>pravara</s>, one should perform the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> penance.' Nor should it be objected that since both <s>smṛti</s> and conduct equally infer a Vedic root, they are of equal strength. Because the virtuous conduct such as the <s>Holāka</s> festival cannot, like the <s>smṛti</s> of <s>Manu</s> and others, serve as evidence for inferring the Veda. For the present-day learned (<s>śiṣṭas</s>) cannot directly perceive the Veda, which is remote in place and time, through divine knowledge, as <s>Manu</s> and others could — so that the conduct of the learned might infer a root-Veda. But any particular learned person, in any particular region and time, can examine some particular <s>smṛti</s> text that is the root of conduct like the <s>Holāka</s> and similar practices. Therefore, through the conduct of the learned, only a <s>smṛti</s> can be inferred, not a <s>śruti</s>. And the inferred <s>smṛti</s> is overridden by a directly perceived contradictory <s>smṛti</s>. For this very reason they say: 'From conduct one infers a <s>smṛti</s>, and <s>smṛti</s> is said to be equivalent to <s>śruti</s>. Therefore, being twice removed, the authority of those [conducts] is diminished.'
START MJaiNy 1,3.19
In that very [topic], he composes another section —
Is the meaning of '<s>trivṛt</s>' and similar [terms] worldly or sentence-derived, since both are equal?
Let the latter [sentence-derived meaning] be [accepted] here, since the injunction and <s>arthavāda</s> form a single sentence (<s>ekavākyatā</s>). // MJaiNy_1,3.19 //

children.text:
'trivṛdvahiṣpavamānam' iti śrutau vivṛcchabdasya traiguṇyaṃ lokasiddhor'thaḥ |
vākyaśeṣādṛktrayātmakeṣu triṣu sūkteṣvavasthitānāṃ bahiṣpavamānātmakastotraniṣpādanakṣamāṇām ' upāsmai gāyatā naraḥ ' -- ityādīnāmṛcāṃ navakamarthaḥ |
tatra dharmaniṇaye vedasya prabalatve 'pi padapadārthanirṇaye lokavedayoḥ samānabalatvādubhāvapyarthau vikalpeva grahītavyāviti cet |
children.translated_text: Therein, even though the Veda is stronger in determining <s>dharma</s>, since the Veda and common usage are of equal strength in determining the meanings of words, both meanings should be accepted alternatively — if this be argued:
Not so.

children.text: laukikārthasvīkārapakṣe vidhivākyer'thastraiguṇyam, arthavādavākye stotriyāṇāmṛcāṃ navakam , ityevaṃ vidhyarthavādayorvaiyadhikaraṇyādekavākyatvaṃ na syāt |
children.translated_text: If the worldly meaning is accepted, then the meaning of the injunctive sentence would be 'triple,' and the meaning of the <s>arthavāda</s> sentence would be 'the group of nine <s>ṛcs</s> for the <s>stotra</s>' — thus, since the injunction and <s>arthavāda</s> would belong to different subjects, their unity as a single sentence (<s>ekavākyatva</s>) would not be established.

children.text: ata ekavākyatvāya stotriyāṇāṃ navakamityeva vidhivākye niyator'thaḥ || MJaiNyC_1,2.19 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, for the sake of unity as a single sentence, 'the group of nine <s>stotriyas</s> (praise-verses)' alone is the fixed meaning in the injunctive sentence. || MJaiNyC_1,2.19 ||

In the <s>śruti</s> '<s>trivṛd bahiṣpavamānam</s>' (the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> is threefold), if the meaning of the word <s>trivṛt</s> is worldly, it means 'triple' — having three qualities. If the meaning is from the complementary sentence, it refers to a group of nine <s>ṛcs</s> (verses) stationed in three <s>sūktas</s> (hymns) that are capable of producing the <s>stotra</s> (chant) called <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s>, beginning with '<s>upāsmai gāyata naraḥ</s>' (sing unto him, O men).
(In the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the authority of meanings established by <s>Mlecchas</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
But what is enjoined would be understood without contradiction through authoritative means. / Jaim_1,3.10 /
START MJaiNy 1,3.20-21
He composes the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Should the meaning of words like <s>pika</s> be conjectured, or taken from <s>Mleccha</s> convention?
It should be conjectured, since it is not established among the <s>Āryas</s>, and the non-<s>Āryas</s> are not regarded [as authoritative]. // MJaiNy_1,3.20 //
The <s>Mleccha</s> convention should be taken when no contradiction is seen;
Therefore, for words like <s>pika</s> and <s>nema</s>, the meanings are <s>kokila</s> (cuckoo) and so on. // MJaiNy_1,3.21 //

children.text:
āryāḥ pikādiśabdaṃ na kvāpyarthe prayuñjate, mlecchāśrca na pramāṇabhūtāḥ |
tasmānnigamanirūktavyākaraṇaiḥ pikanemādiśabdānāmarthaḥ kalpanīya iti cet |
maivam |

children.translated_text: Because, since no conflict with <s>Ārya</s> convention is seen, in such a case even <s>Mleccha</s> convention is to be respected.
<s>Mleccha</s> convention is preferable to a conjectured and uncertain meaning.
Where even such convention is absent, <s>Nirukta</s> and the like serve their purpose.

children.text: tasmādanārya prasiddhyā pikaḥ kokilaḥ, nemaśabdor'dhavācī , tāmarasaśabdaḥ padmavācī, ityevaṃ draṣṭavyam || MJaiNyC_1,2.20-21 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, by non-<s>Ārya</s> convention, <s>pika</s> means <s>kokila</s> (cuckoo), the word <s>nema</s> means 'half,' the word <s>tāmarasa</s> means 'lotus' — thus it should be understood. || MJaiNyC_1,2.20-21 ||

The <s>Āryas</s> do not use the word <s>pika</s> and similar terms anywhere for any meaning, and the <s>Mlecchas</s> are not authoritative. Therefore, the meanings of words like <s>pika</s> and <s>nema</s> should be conjectured through <s>Nigama</s> (Vedic concordance), <s>Nirukta</s> (etymology), and <s>Vyākaraṇa</s> (grammar) — if this be argued: Not so.
START MJaiNy 1,3.22
In this very <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, he states the teacher's view —
The injunction regarding the taking of a <s>pika</s> (cuckoo) is not authoritative because the meaning is not understood;
Not so, because the meaning is understood even through <s>Mleccha</s> convention, which is not contradictory. // MJaiNy_1,3.22 //
The meaning is clear. || MJaiNyC_1,2.22 ||
(In the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the inherent authority of <s>Kalpa-sūtras</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 11-14)
[If it be said that it is merely] a manual of practice — / Jaim_1,3.11 /
No, because of the absence of restriction. / Jaim_1,3.12 /
And because it is not a complementary passage. / Jaim_1,3.13 /

children.text: sarvatra ca prayogāt saṃnidhānaśāstrāc ca / Jaim_1,3.14 /
children.translated_text: And because of application everywhere, and because of the text of proximity. / Jaim_1,3.14 /
START MJaiNy 1,3.23-24
He composes the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: apauruṣeyāḥ kalpādyāḥ kṛtrimā vā na kṛtrimāḥ /
children.translated_text: Are the <s>Kalpa</s> [sūtras] and other [ancillary texts] unauthored (<s>apauruṣeya</s>), or are they man-made?

children.text: śrutismatyordharmabuddheḥ svato mātvaṃ yataḥ samam // MJaiNy_1,3.23 //
children.translated_text: They are not man-made, since the cognition of <s>dharma</s> from both <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> has equal inherent validity (<s>svataḥ prāmāṇya</s>). // MJaiNy_1,3.23 //
They are man-made (<s>pauruṣeya</s>), because they are designated by personal names, and because they are not equal to the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> and similar [Vedic texts];
In that regard, some have ascertained the authorship of <s>Āpastamba</s> and others. // MJaiNy_1,3.24 //

children.text:
baudhāyanāpastambā śrvalāyanakātyāyanādināmāṅkitāḥ kalparsūtragranthāḥ, nigamaniruktādiṣaḍaṅgagranthāḥ, manvādismṛtayaśrcāṣauruṣeyāḥ, dharmabuddhijanakatvāt, vedavat |
na ca mūlapramāṇasāpekṣatvena vedavaiṣamyamiti śaṅkanīyam |
utpannāyā buddheḥ svataḥ- prāmāṇyāṅgīkāreṇa nirapekṣatvāt |
maivam |
uktānumānasya kālātyayāpadiṣṭatvāt |
baudhāyanasūtram , āpastambasūtram, ityevaṃ puruṣanāmnā te granthā ucyante |
na ca kāṭhakādisamākhyavatpravacananimittatvaṃ yuktam |

children.translated_text: Because they were observed by some contemporaries at the time those texts were composed.
And that [observation] continues through unbroken tradition.
Therefore, they are man-made (<s>pauruṣeya</s>), like the works of <s>Kālidāsa</s> and others.
Even so, being rooted in the Veda, they are authoritative. || MJaiNyC_1,2.23-24 ||

The <s>Kalpa-sūtra</s> texts attributed to <s>Baudhāyana</s>, <s>Āpastamba</s>, <s>Āśvalāyana</s>, <s>Kātyāyana</s>, and others, the <s>Nigama</s> (Vedic concordance), <s>Nirukta</s> (etymology), and other six ancillary texts, and the <s>smṛtis</s> of <s>Manu</s> and others — are they unauthored (<s>apauruṣeya</s>), since they generate cognition of <s>dharma</s>, like the Veda? Nor should it be objected that they differ from the Veda because they depend on a root authority — because, by accepting the inherent validity (<s>svataḥ prāmāṇya</s>) of the cognition that has arisen, they are independent. Not so. Because the aforementioned inference is invalidated by time-lapse (<s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭa</s>). Those texts are called by personal names — '<s>Baudhāyana-sūtra</s>,' '<s>Āpastamba-sūtra</s>,' and so on. Nor is it appropriate that the naming is merely based on being the promulgator, as in the case of the name '<s>Kāṭhaka</s>' and similar [Vedic recensions].
START MJaiNy 1,3.25
In this very [topic], he states the teacher's view —
In the <s>Kalpa</s>, regarding every <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), the injunction stating the object to be performed — is it <s>śruti</s> or not?
In a <s>Kalpa</s> [text], because the Vedic status that needs to be established is abandoned, it is weak. // MJaiNy_1,3.25 //

children.text:
sarvatithau darśayāgakartavyatāṃ kalpasūtrakāra āha -"sarvāsu tithiṣvamāvāsyā kartavyā"iti |
śrutistvamāvāsyāyāmeva tithau kartavyatāṃ brūte |
tataḥ kalpasūtrarūpeṃṇa vedena viruddhatvādiyaṃ śrutirna mānamiti cet |
maivam |
kalpasya vedatvaṃ nādyāpi siddham |

children.translated_text: Rather, it must be established with effort.
And it cannot be so established.
Because its human authorship (<s>pauruṣeyatva</s>) has been proven by the designation [of its author] and by the apprehension of its composer.

children.text: ataḥ kalpasūtrasya durbalatayā na śruteraprāmāṇyam || MJaiNyC_1,2.25 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, due to the weakness of the <s>Kalpasūtra</s>, the authoritativeness of <s>śruti</s> is not negated. || MJaiNyC_1,2.25 ||

The author of the <s>Kalpasūtra</s> states the obligatory nature of the <s>Darśa</s> sacrifice on all <s>tithis</s> (lunar days): '<s>sarvāsu tithiṣv amāvāsyā kartavyā</s>' (the new-moon sacrifice is to be performed on all lunar days). But the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) declares its obligatory nature only on the <s>amāvāsyā</s> (new-moon) day. Therefore, if it be argued that since the <s>Kalpasūtra</s> — being a form of Veda — contradicts the <s>śruti</s>, this <s>śruti</s> is not authoritative — that is not correct. The Vedic status of the <s>Kalpa</s> has not been established even now.
(In the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the topic of <s>Holākā</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 14–23)
Since inference is established, that which is connected with it would be authoritative. / Jaim_1,3.15 /

children.text: api vā sarvadharmaḥ syāt tannyāyatvād vidhānasya / Jaim_1,3.16 /
children.translated_text: Or rather, it should apply to all <s>dharmas</s>, since the injunction has that same logical basis. / Jaim_1,3.16 /
From observation, the application would be [restricted]. / Jaim_1,3.17 /
And because of the absence of an indicatory mark for the permanent [rule]. / Jaim_1,3.18 /
For the designation [is derived] from association with a place. / Jaim_1,3.19 /

children.text: na syād deśāntareṣv iti cet / Jaim_1,3.20 /
children.translated_text: If it be said that [the practice] would not exist in other regions — / Jaim_1,3.20 /
The designation based on connection would apply, like [the designation] '<s>Māthura</s>' (of Mathurā). / Jaim_1,3.21 /
Or it is a property of the rite, like [the designation] '<s>Pravaṇa</s>.' / Jaim_1,3.22 /
But it is equal to [being] a property of the agent. / Jaim_1,3.23 /
START MJaiNy 1,3.26
He expounds the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Whether there is a restricted application of <s>Holākā</s> and similar [practices], or universality, is the next [question].
Because they are observed [only] in particular regions, [there is restricted application]; [but there is] equality, because of the sameness of the root [source]. // MJaiNy_1,3.26 //

children.text:
holākādiśiṣṭācārāṇāṃ hārītādismṛtiviśeṣāṇāṃ cānuṣṭhātṛpuruṣabhedena vyavasthitaṃ prāmāṇyam |
kutaḥ |
deśaviśeṣe teṣāṃ dṛṣṭatvāt |
holākādayaḥ prācyaireva kriyante |
vasantotsavo holākā |
āhnīnaibukādayo dākṣiṇātyai svasvakulāgataṃ karañjārkādisthāvaradevatāpūjādikamāhnīnaibukaśabdenocyate |
udvṛṣabhayajñādaya udīcyaiḥ |
jyeṣṭhamāsasya paurṇamāsyāṃ balīvardānabhyarcya dhāvayanti so 'yamudvṛṣabhayajñaḥ |

children.translated_text: Similarly, a particular <s>smṛti</s> such as that of <s>Hārīta</s> is observed only in certain specific regions.
Therefore, the authoritativeness is restricted — if so it is argued,
that is not correct.

children.text: tanmūlatvenānumitasya vedasya sarvasādhāraṇatvena teṣāmapi sarvasādhāraṇatvāt || MJaiNyC_1,2.26 ||
children.translated_text: Because the Veda inferred as the root source of these [practices] is universally applicable to all, these [practices] too are universally applicable. || MJaiNyC_1,2.26 ||

The authoritativeness of the <s>Holākā</s> and other practices sanctioned by the learned (<s>śiṣṭācāra</s>), as well as particular <s>smṛtis</s> such as those of <s>Hārīta</s> and others, is established with restriction according to the distinction of the persons who practice them. Why? Because they are observed only in particular regions. The <s>Holākā</s> and similar rites are performed only by the Easterners (<s>prācya</s>). <s>Holākā</s> is the spring festival. The <s>Āhnīnaibuka</s> and similar rites are performed by the Southerners (<s>dākṣiṇātya</s>) — the worship of stationary deities such as <s>Karañja</s>, <s>Arka</s>, and others, which has come down through their respective families, is called <s>Āhnīnaibuka</s>. The <s>Udvṛṣabhayajña</s> and similar rites are performed by the Northerners (<s>udīcya</s>). On the full-moon day of the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, they worship and race bulls — that is the <s>Udvṛṣabhayajña</s>.
START MJaiNy 1,3.27
On this very topic, he states the teacher's view —
When the <s>śruti</s> connected with the words '<s>prācya</s>' (Eastern) and the like is inferred as the basis,
if it be said that due to non-comprehension of the meaning, it is not authoritative — no, because of the general inference. // MJaiNy_1,3.27 //

children.text:
prācyādibhirvyavasthayā holākādiṣvanuṣṭhīyamāneṣu tanmūlaśrutirapi prācyādipadayuktaivānumātavyā |
tatra prācyādipadasyārtho na budhyate |
ye puruṣāḥ kañcitkālaṃ prācyāṃ nivasanti , ta eva kālāntare pratīcyāṃ nivasanta upalabhyante |

children.translated_text: If it be argued that, due to non-comprehension of the meaning of the words '<s>prācya</s>' and the like in the scriptural [source], the <s>śruti</s> is not authoritative —
that is not correct.
Because the generality of practice is sufficient to postulate a root <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: ataḥ prācyādipadarāhitye satyarthabodhādanumitā śrutiḥ pramāṇam || MJaiNyC_1,2.27 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, the inferred <s>śruti</s> — being free from the words '<s>prācya</s>' and the like, and thus having comprehensible meaning — is authoritative. || MJaiNyC_1,2.27 ||

When the <s>Holākā</s> and similar rites are practiced with regional restriction by the Easterners and others, the root <s>śruti</s> from which they are inferred must also be inferred as containing the words '<s>prācya</s>' (Eastern) and the like. But the meaning of the words '<s>prācya</s>' and the like cannot be ascertained — persons who reside for some time in the East are observed to reside later in the West.
(In the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the topic of the use of correct words, <s>sūtras</s> 24–29)

children.text: prayogotpatyaśāstratvāc chabdeṣu na vyavasthā syāt / Jaim_1,3.24 /
children.translated_text: Since words arise from usage and are not governed by <s>śāstra</s>, there would be no fixed rule regarding [correct] words. / Jaim_1,3.24 /
Since words are produced by effort, [the speaker] shares in the fault [of incorrect usage]. / Jaim_1,3.25 /
And the use of multiple words [for the same object] would be improper. / Jaim_1,3.26 /
The correct form in that case would result from a particular application. / Jaim_1,3.27 /
And the inability [to determine the correct word] would be due to similarity. / Jaim_1,3.28 /

children.text: eka deśatvāc ca vibhāktivyatyaye syāt / Jaim_1,3.29 /
children.translated_text: And since it is [merely] a part, there would be [correctness] even when case-endings are interchanged. / Jaim_1,3.29 /
START MJaiNy 1,3.28-29
He composes the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: gogāvyādiṣu sādhutve prayoge vā na kaśrcana /
children.translated_text: Regarding whether '<s>go</s>' or '<s>gāvī</s>' and the like are correct, and regarding usage, there is either
no restrictive rule here, or there is — due to the rejection of grammar as the root [authority]. // MJaiNy_1,3.28 //
One should use only correct forms; words like '<s>gav</s>' and the like alone are correct —
thus there is a restrictive rule, based on the successive [tradition of] grammar as its root. // MJaiNy_1,3.29 //

children.text:
vyākaraṇābhijñaiḥ sāsnādimadvastuni 'gauḥ ' ityeṣa śabdaḥ prayujyate |
tadanabhijñaistu svasvadeśīyabhāṣāmanusṛtya gāvī, goṇī, gopotalikā, ityevamādayaḥ śabdaḥ prayujyante |
tatra - 'īdṛṣa eva śabdaḥ sādhuḥ, nedṛśaḥ ' -- ityasminnarthe niyāmakaṃ nāsti |
tathā yoge 'pi tannāsti - ' īdṛśa eva śabdaḥ prayoktavyaḥ , nedṛśaḥ ' iti na tāvadvṛddhavyavahāro niyāmakaḥ |
tasya sarveṣu śabdeṣu samānatvāt |
nāpi vyākaraṇasmṛtirniyāmikā |
tasyā nirmūlatvenāpramāṇatvāt |
na hyabhiyuktaprayogastanmūlama |
anyonyāśrayatvaprasaṅgāt |
vyākaraṇasmṛteḥ prāmāṇyasiddhau tadanusāreṇa prayoktṝṇāmamiyuktatvasiddhiḥ |
tatsiddhau tatprayogamūlatayā vyākaraṇasya prāmāṇyam |
tasmānnāsti sādhutvaprayogayorniyamaḥ , iti prāpte --
brūmaḥ- ' sādhūneva prayuñjati, na tvapabhraṃśān ' ityasti niyamaḥ |
ubhayatra krameṇa doṣaguṇavādinorvedavākyayoḥ śravaṇāt |
"ekaḥ śabdaḥ samyagjñātaḥ suprayuktaḥ svarge loke kāmadhugbhavati"iti guṇavākyam |
"tasmādbrāhmaṇena na mlecchitavai ' nāpabhāṣitavai , mleccho ha vā eṣa yadapaśabdaḥ"iti doṣavākyam |
yathā prayoge niyamastathā sādhutve 'pi niyamo draṣṭavyaḥ - 'gavādyā eva sādhavaḥ, na tu gāvyādayaḥ ' iti |
asminnarthe vyākaraṇasya niyāmakatvāt |
na ca nirmūlatvam , pūrvapūrvavyākaraṇasya tanmūlatvāt |
etadevābhipretyoktam - ' tatra yūpādhikaraṇavadvyākaraṇaparamparānāditvādanupālambhaḥ ' iti vyākaraṇa prāmāṇyaṃ vedenaiva sākṣādupanyastam |
tathā'cārthavaṇikā āmananti -"dve vidye veditavye iti ha sma yadbrahmavido vadanti parā caivāparā ca |
tatrāparā - ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo 'tharvavedaḥ śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ chando jyotiṣama"iti |
taittirīyakabrāhmaṇe 'pi vyākaraṇasyopādeyatā śrūyate - 'vāgvai parācyavyākṛtāvadat |
te devā indramabruvan - 'imāṃ no vācaṃ vyākuru, iti tāmindro madhyato 'pakramya vyākarot |
children.translated_text: The gods said to <s>Indra</s>: 'Analyze this speech for us.' <s>Indra</s>, approaching it from the middle, analyzed it.
Therefore this speech is spoken in an analyzed (grammatical) form.'
And the analyzers — <s>Pāṇini</s>, <s>Kātyāyana</s>, and <s>Patañjali</s> — are equal [in authority] to <s>Manu</s> and others.

children.text: tasmātsādhūnāmeva prayoge gavādīnāmeva sādhutve vyākaraṇasmṛtiḥ pramāṇam || MJaiNyC_1,2.28-29 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, for the usage of correct forms alone and for the correctness of words like '<s>gav</s>' and the like alone, the <s>smṛti</s> of grammar is authoritative. || MJaiNyC_1,2.28-29 ||

Those proficient in grammar use the word '<s>gauḥ</s>' for the object possessing a dewlap and the like. But those not proficient in grammar, following the dialect of their own region, use words such as '<s>gāvī</s>,' '<s>goṇī</s>,' '<s>gopotalikā</s>,' and so on. In this matter — there is no restrictive rule determining 'only such a word is correct, not such another.' Similarly, there is no restrictive rule regarding usage — 'only such a word should be used, not such another.' Firstly, common practice of elders is not a restrictive factor, because it is the same for all words. Nor is the <s>smṛti</s> of grammar a restrictive factor, because it is rootless and therefore not authoritative. For the usage of the proficient is not the root of grammar — because there would be the fallacy of mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>). The establishment of the authoritativeness of the grammar-<s>smṛti</s> depends on establishing the proficiency of the users [of correct words], and the establishment of that [proficiency] depends on the authoritativeness of grammar whose root is their usage. Therefore there is no restrictive rule regarding correctness or usage — having arrived at this conclusion, we say: 'One should use only correct forms, not corruptions (<s>apabhraṃśa</s>)' — thus there is a restrictive rule. Because in both cases, Vedic sentences declaring faults and merits are heard in sequence. '<s>ekaḥ śabdaḥ samyag jñātaḥ suprayuktaḥ svarge loke kāmadhug bhavati</s>' (a single word, correctly known and properly used, becomes a wish-fulfilling cow in the heavenly world) — this is the merit-declaring sentence. '<s>tasmād brāhmaṇena na mlecchitavai, nāpabhāṣitavai; mleccho ha vā eṣa yad apaśabdaḥ</s>' (therefore a Brahmin should not speak barbarously nor use incorrect words; for an incorrect word is indeed barbarism) — this is the fault-declaring sentence. Just as there is a restrictive rule regarding usage, so too a restrictive rule regarding correctness should be recognized — 'words like <s>gav</s> and the like alone are correct, not <s>gāvī</s> and the like.' Because grammar is the restrictive factor in this matter. Nor is it rootless — because the successive tradition of prior grammarians is its root. With this very intention it has been said: 'Just as in the <s>Yūpa</s> adhikaraṇa, because the lineage of grammar is beginningless, there is no fault [of rootlessness].' The authoritativeness of grammar has been directly declared by the Veda itself. Thus the <s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> states: '<s>dve vidye veditavye iti ha sma yad brahmavido vadanti parā caivāparā ca | tatrāparā — ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo 'tharvavedaḥ śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ chando jyotiṣam</s>' (two kinds of knowledge are to be known, say the knowers of Brahman — the higher and the lower; of these, the lower is the Ṛgveda, Yajurveda, Sāmaveda, Atharvaveda, phonetics, ritual, grammar, etymology, meter, and astronomy). In the <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> too, the importance of grammar is heard: 'Speech indeed was unrefined and formless (<s>vyākṛtā</s>).

START MJaiNy 1,3.30
On this very topic, he states the teacher's view —
When there is doubt whether the dental or the palatal [consonant] should be read in the scriptural passage about the '<s>aśrva</s>' sacrifice,
the non-authoritativeness [of the scripture] due to ambiguity is resolved by the force of the authoritative grammar. // MJaiNy_1,3.30 //

children.text:
"aśrvamālabheta"ityatrākāravakārayormadhyavartino varṇasya dantyatve ' svaṃ dhanam , tadrahitaṃ daridramālabheta' ityartho bhavati |
tālavyatve turaṅgamavācitvam |

children.translated_text: If it be argued that due to this doubt, [the scripture] is not authoritative —
no.
Because the palatal reading is ascertained according to grammar: from the root '<s>aśū vyāptau</s>' (aś, to pervade), when the <s>Uṇādi</s> suffix '<s>va</s>' is applied, the palatal is determined.
Therefore, the scriptural passage about the <s>aśrva</s> (horse) sacrifice is authoritative. || MJaiNyC_1,2.30 ||

In the passage '<s>aśrvam ālabheta</s>' (one should sacrifice an <s>aśrva</s>), regarding the consonant between the vowels 'a' and 'va,' if it is dental [śa → meaning wealth], the meaning would be 'one should sacrifice one's wealth, and the one without it is a pauper.' If it is palatal [śva → meaning horse], it denotes a horse.
(In the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the identity of words in worldly and Vedic [usage] — also called the <s>ākṛti</s> [universal form] <s>adhikaraṇa</s> — <s>sūtras</s> 30–35)
Due to the absence of a separate injunction for usage, there would be identity of meaning, since there is no distinction. / Jaim_1,3.30 /
Because [the word] does not denote a [specific] substance. / Jaim_1,3.31 /
And because a different [meaning] is observed. / Jaim_1,3.32 /
But the universal form (<s>ākṛti</s>) [is the word's meaning], because [words] serve the purpose of action. / Jaim_1,3.33 /

children.text: na kriyā syād iti cedarthāntare vidhānaṃ na dravyam iti cet / Jaim_1,3.34 /
children.translated_text: If it be said that there would be no action — [then we say] the injunction pertains to something else; and if it be said that [the meaning] is not a substance — / Jaim_1,3.34 /
Since [usage] is for the purpose of that [action], the non-distinction [of meaning] follows. / Jaim_1,3.35 /
START MJaiNy 1,3.31-32
In the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, he composes the first <s>varṇaka</s> (section) —

children.text: loke padāpadārthau yau na tau vede 'thavātra tau /
children.translated_text: The words and their meanings in the world are either different from those in the Veda, or they are the same;
due to difference in form, the word is distinct — the distinction through plain meaning and the like is evident. // MJaiNy_1,3.31 //
Due to identity of phonemes, there is identity of words; the difference in form is occasional.
Due to the general identity of words, the identity of their meanings is likewise established. // MJaiNy_1,3.32 //

children.text:
vaidikau padapadārthau laukikābhyāṃ padapadārthābhyāmanyau |
kutaḥ |
rūpabhedāt |
pade tāvadrūpabhedo dṛśyate |
ātmaśabda ākārāditvena loke niyataḥ |
vede tu kvacidākārarahitaḥ paṭhyate -"prayataṃ purūṣaṃ tmanā"iti |
'brāhmaṇāḥ ' iti loke |
vede tvanyathā paṭhyate -"brāhmaṇāsaḥ pitaraḥ somyāsaḥ"iti |
arthabhedo 'pi sphuṭaḥ |
uttānā vai devagavā vahanti"iti śrūyate - devebhyo vanaspate havīṃṣi hiraṇyaparṇa pradivaste artham"iti |
tasmāt ' lokavedayoḥ padapadārthāvanyau ' iti prāpte -
brūmaḥ- ya eva laukikāḥ padārthāḥ, ta eva vaidikāḥ |
tathā hi - varṇānāṃ tāvannityatvaṃ prathamapāde sādhitam |
yathā prayoktṝṇāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ bhede 'pyekaikasya puruṣasya bahukṛtva uccāraṇabhede 'pi ' ta evāmī varṇāḥ ' iti pratyabhijñānādvarṇaikyam |
tathā ' yāni loke gavādipadāni , tānyeva vede 'dhīyamānāni ' ityavādhitapratyabhijñayā padaikatvamabhyupeyam |
' tmanā, devāsaḥ ' ityādipadabhedastu kvācitkaḥ |
naitāvatā bahutarapratyabhijñāvagataṃ padaikyamapoḍhuṃ śakyam |
anyathā 'so 'yaṃ devadattaḥ ' iti pratyabhijñātaṃ devadattaikyamapi deśādibhedamātreṇāpodyeta |
padaikye cārthaikatvamavaśyaṃbhāvi |
anyathā vede pṛthagvyutpattyabhāvādabodhakatvaṃ prasajyeta |
etadevābhipretyoktam -
"lokāvagatasāmarththaḥ śabde vede 'pi bodhakaḥ"iti |
svaruyūpāhavanīyāndiśabdānāṃ tadarthānāṃ cālaukikatve 'pi prasiddhapadasamabhivyāhārādva yuptattiḥ saṃbhavati |
children.translated_text: Even regarding words like '<s>svaru</s>' (sacrificial post), '<s>yūpa</s>' (sacrificial stake), '<s>āhavanīya</s>' (the eastern fire), and similar terms — though these words and their referents are not worldly — etymological derivation (<s>vyutpatti</s>) is possible through their being used together with well-known words.
The [passages] about carrying upward and the like are <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passages).

children.text: astu vā tathāvahanam , tathāpyuttānādiśābdāstadarthāśrca lokaprasiddhā eva |
children.translated_text: Or even if such carrying upward is [literally true], nevertheless the words '<s>uttānā</s>' and the like and their meanings are well-known in the world alone.

children.text: tasmādya eva laukikāḥ padapadārthāsta eva vaidikāḥ || MJaiNyC_1,2.31-32 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, the very same worldly words and meanings are also the Vedic ones. || MJaiNyC_1,2.31-32 ||

The words and meanings in the Veda are different from the words and meanings in the world. Why? Because of difference in form. Firstly, a difference in form is observed in words. The word '<s>ātman</s>' is fixed in the world as beginning with the vowel '<s>ā</s>.' But in the Veda, it is sometimes read without the initial '<s>ā</s>' — '<s>prayataṃ purūṣaṃ tmanā</s>' (the pure person, by himself). [Similarly,] '<s>brāhmaṇāḥ</s>' [is the form] in the world. But in the Veda, it is read differently — '<s>brāhmaṇāsaḥ pitaraḥ somyāsaḥ</s>' (the Brahmins, the fathers, the Soma-pressers). The difference in meaning is also evident: '<s>uttānā vai devagavā vahanti</s>' (the divine cows carry upwards) is heard — '<s>devebhyo vanaspate havīṃṣi hiraṇyaparṇa pradivas te artham</s>' (O lord of trees, with golden leaves, convey the oblations for the gods from heaven). Therefore, since worldly and Vedic words and meanings are different — having arrived at this position, we say: The very same worldly meanings are also the Vedic meanings. For the permanence of phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) was established in the first <s>pāda</s>. Just as, despite difference among speakers and despite multiple utterances by the same person, the recognition 'these are the very same phonemes' [establishes] the identity of phonemes — so too, the identity of words should be accepted through the uncontradicted recognition that 'the very words read in the Veda are the same as those in the world.' The difference in words such as '<s>tmanā</s>' and '<s>devāsaḥ</s>' is only occasional. This much [occasional difference] cannot refute the identity of words established by the more extensive recognition. Otherwise, the identity of <s>Devadatta</s> recognized through '<s>sa ayaṃ devadattaḥ</s>' (this is that same Devadatta) would also be refuted merely by difference of place and the like. And when the identity of words is [established], the identity of meaning necessarily follows — otherwise, since there is no separate etymological derivation (<s>vyutpatti</s>) in the Veda, it would lead to the absurdity of [Vedic words] being non-communicative. With this very intention it has been said: '<s>lokāvagatāsāmarthyaḥ śabde vede 'pi bodhakaḥ</s>' (the word, whose capacity is understood from the world, is communicative in the Veda as well).
START MJaiNy 1,3.33-34
He composes the second <s>varṇaka</s> (section) —

Is the particular individual (<s>vyakti</s>) the meaning of words like '<s>vrīhi</s>' (rice) and the like, or is it the universal form (<s>ākṛti</s>) — [the latter] because of its connection with action?
The individual is [the meaning] at the time of etymological derivation (<s>vyutpatti</s>), but is indicated by the universal form. // MJaiNy_1,3.33 //
Through reasoning such as the apprehension of [word-meaning] capacity and the like, the meaning of the universal form (<s>ākṛti</s>) is appropriate.
For the culmination in action, let the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) be indicated therein. // MJaiNy_1,3.34 //
