children.translated_text: Because the sacrifice, being not yet obtained (<s>aprāpta</s>), is enjoined as a single sacrifice qualified by both attributes through a single sentence.
Therefore — by the word '<s>Āgneya</s>', the qualifying attribute of deity is enjoined. || MJaiNyC_1,4.19-20 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) sacrifices, it is heard: '<s>yadāgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo 'māvāsyāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ cācyuto bhavati</s>' (the <s>Āgneya</s> eight-potsherded [offering] is constant on the new-moon and full-moon days). Therein, just as the word '<s>Agnihotra</s>' is a name of the sacrifice, based on the meaning 'the offering (<s>hotra</s>) for <s>Agni</s>' as its occasion, so too the word '<s>Āgneya</s>' should be a name of the sacrifice, based on the connection with <s>Agni</s> as its occasion — if this be argued: Not so. Because if it were a name, the absurd consequence would be the absence of a deity. In the <s>Agnihotra</s>, however, the <s>mantra</s> enjoined by the passage '<s>agnir jyotir jyotir agniḥ svāhā</s>' (Fire is light, light is fire, <s>svāhā</s>) — being a directly enjoined <s>mantra</s> — provides the deity through the <s>mantra</s>-text (<s>māntravarṇikī devatā</s>). But here no such <s>mantra</s> exists. The word '<s>Āgneya</s>', however, is able to enjoin the deity.
START MJaiNy 1,4.21
On this [topic], he states the teacher's view —

children.text: yadāgneya iti proktaṃ na mānaṃ vidhyasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: If it be said that the cited passage regarding '<s>yadāgneya</s>' is not authoritative because no injunction is possible —

children.text: iti cenna viśiṣṭārthavidhau satyapramā kutaḥ // MJaiNy_1,4.21 //
children.translated_text: not so, because when an injunction of the [sacrifice] qualified by [both] attributes is possible, how can it be non-authoritative? // MJaiNy_1,4.21 //

children.text: udāhṛtavākye devatārāhityaprasaṅgena nāmatvābhāvādguṇayorvidhau vākkayabhedāñca vidhyasaṃbhavādaprāmāṇyamiti pūrvapakṣaḥ | guṇadvayaviśiṣṭakarmavidhisaṃbhavātprāmāṇyamiti siddhāntaḥ || MJaiNyC_1,4.21 ||
children.translated_text: The prior view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) is: since in the cited sentence the absence of deity [if taken as a name] makes name-status impossible, and since the injunction of two qualifying attributes would split the sentence, no injunction is possible, hence it is not authoritative. The established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>) is: since it is possible to enjoin the sacrifice qualified by both attributes, it is authoritative. || MJaiNyC_1,4.21 ||
START MJaiNy 1,4.22-23
(In the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the generic-denotation (<s>jātivācitā</s>) of words like '<s>barhis</s>' and the like, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

In the case of <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass) and <s>ājya</s> (ghee), since the designation is obtained even without ritual modification (<s>saṃskāra</s>), [the word applies to] what is without that modification. / Jaim_1,4.10 /
He composes the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Do the words '<s>barhis</s>' (sacrificial grass), '<s>ājya</s>' (ghee), and '<s>puroḍāśa</s>' (offering cake) denote ritual modification (<s>saṃskāra</s>),

children.text: jātyarthā vā śāstrarūḍheste syuḥ saṃskāravācinaḥ // MJaiNy_1,4.22 //
children.translated_text: or genus (<s>jāti</s>)? Being established in <s>śāstra</s> by convention, they would denote ritual modification. // MJaiNy_1,4.22 //

children.text: jātiṃ tyaktvā na saṃskāre prayuktā lokavedayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Setting aside genus, they are not used for ritual modification in either the world or the Veda;
since they are seen in the world even without ritual modification, they denote genus. // MJaiNy_1,4.23 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate -"barhirlunāti" "ājyaṃ vilāpayati" "puroḍāśaṃ paryāgni karoti" iti |
atra barhirādiśabdānāṃ śāstre sarvartra saṃskṛteṣu tṛṇādiṣu prayogāt, pīlvādiśabdeṣu śāstrīyarūḍhiprābalyasyoktatvāt, yūpāhavanīyādiśabdavatsaṃskāravācino barhirādiśabdā iti cet |
maivam |
anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ jātivācitvāt |
yatra yatra barhirādiśabdaprayogaḥ, tatra tatra jātiḥ ' ityasyā vyāpterloke vede ca nāsti vyabhicāraḥ |

children.translated_text: But the concomitance with ritual modification shows deviation in worldly usage.

children.text: kvaciddeśaviśeṣe laukikavyavahāro jātimātramupajīvya vinā saṃskāraṃ te śabdāḥ prayujyante - ' barhirādāya gāvo gatāḥ ' iti, ' ktayyamājyam ' iti, ' puroḍāśena me mātā prahelakaṃ dadāti ' iti ca |
children.translated_text: In certain regional dialects, worldly usage employs those words depending merely on the genus, without ritual modification — '<s>barhir ādāya gāvo gatāḥ</s>' (the cows went, having taken the grass), '<s>kṣayyam ājyam</s>' (the ghee is spent), '<s>puroḍāśena me mātā prahelakaṃ dadāti</s>' (my mother gives me a <s>prahelaka</s> [sweet] with the <s>puroḍāśa</s> [cake]).
Therefore they denote genus.

children.text: prayojanaṃ tu"barhiṣā yūpāvaṭamavastṛṇāti"ityatra vinā saṃskāreṇa staraṇasiddhiḥ || MJaiNyC_1,4.22-23 ||
children.translated_text: The practical consequence is that in '<s>barhiṣā yūpāvaṭam avastṛṇāti</s>' (one spreads the <s>barhis</s> in the pit of the sacrificial post), the spreading is accomplished even without ritual modification. || MJaiNyC_1,4.22-23 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) sacrifices, it is heard: '<s>barhir lunāti</s>' (one cuts the <s>barhis</s>), '<s>ājyaṃ vilāpayati</s>' (one melts the <s>ājya</s>), '<s>puroḍāśaṃ paryāgni karoti</s>' (one passes the <s>puroḍāśa</s> around the fire). Here, since the words '<s>barhis</s>' and the like are used in the <s>śāstra</s> everywhere in reference to ritually modified grasses and the like, and since it has been stated that scriptural convention (<s>rūḍhi</s>) is stronger for words like <s>pīlu</s> and the like, the words '<s>barhis</s>' and the like denote ritual modification, like the words '<s>yūpa</s>' (sacrificial post) and '<s>āhavanīya</s>' (the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire) — if this be argued: Not so. Because they denote genus, as established through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>). The invariable concomitance 'wherever there is the use of the word <s>barhis</s> and the like, there is genus' has no deviation in either the world or the Veda.
START MJaiNy 1,4.24
On this [topic], he states the teacher's view —
If it be said that [the injunction] regarding <s>barhis</s> and the like is not authoritative because the basis (<s>nimitta</s>) is hard to specify —
since genus is the basis there, the injunction having that [as its basis] is authoritative. // MJaiNy_1,4.24 //
The meaning is clear. || MJaiNyC_1,4.24 ||
START MJaiNy 1,4.25-26
(In the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the etymological derivation (<s>yaugikatā</s>) of words like '<s>prokṣaṇī</s>' and the like, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
In the case of the <s>prokṣaṇīs</s> (sprinkling waters), due to the connection with meaning [through etymology]. / Jaim_1,4.11 /
He composes the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Do the <s>prokṣaṇīs</s> (sprinkling waters) denote ritual modification (<s>saṃskṛti</s>), genus (<s>jāti</s>), or etymological derivation (<s>yoga</s>) — in all contexts?
Since it is so stated, [they denote] ritual modification; [or] genus, due to the strength of convention (<s>rūḍhi</s>). // MJaiNy_1,4.25 //
Not the first, due to mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>); not genus, because the denotative power would need to be postulated;
etymological derivation (<s>yoga</s>) should be [the answer], because the denotative power is [already] established through grammar (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>). // MJaiNy_1,4.26 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate -"prokṣaṇīrāsādaya"iti |
tatra prokṣaṇīśabdasyābhimantraṇāsādamādisaṃskṛtiḥ pravṛttinimitam | kutaḥ- sarveṣu vaidikaprayogapradeśeṣu saṃskṛtānāmevāpāṃ prokṣaṇīśabdenocyamānatvādityekaḥ pakṣaḥ |
loke jalakrīḍāyāṃ ' prokṣaṇībhirudvejitāḥ smaḥ ' ityasaṃskṛtāsvapsu prayogādvarhirādiśabdavajjātau rūḍhatvādudakatvajātiḥ pravṛttinimittam |
na ca ' prakarṣeṇokṣyata ābhiḥ ' iti yogo 'tra śaṅkanīyaḥ |
rūḍheḥ prabalatvāditi pakṣāntaram |
tatra na tāvatsaṃskāro yuktaḥ |
anyonyāśrayatvāt |
vihiteṣvabhimantraṇādiṣu saṃskāreṣvanuṣṭhiteṣu paścātsaṃskṛtāsvapsu prokṣaṇīśabdapravṛttiḥ |
tatpravṛttau satyāṃ prokṣaṇīśabdenāpo 'mūdyābhimantraṇasiddhiriti |
nāpi jātipakṣo yuktaḥ |
udakajātau prokṣaṇī śabdasya vṛddhavya vahāre pūrvamakḷptatvenetaḥ paraṃ śakteḥ kalpanīyatvāt |
tato gośabdavadaśvakarṇaśabdavacca rūḍho na bhavati |

children.translated_text: But the etymological derivation (<s>yoga</s>) is established through grammar.
Because it is etymologically derived by the <s>lyuṭ</s> suffix in the sense of instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) from the root with prefix (<s>sopasarga</s>).
Therefore — the word '<s>prokṣaṇī</s>' is etymological (<s>yaugika</s>).
The purpose is the fitness for sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇatva</s>) of ghee and the like. || MJaiNyC_1,4.25-26 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) sacrifices, it is heard: '<s>prokṣaṇīr āsādaya</s>' (arrange the sprinkling waters).
Therein, one view is that the cause of application of the word '<s>prokṣaṇī</s>' is the consecration (<s>saṃskṛti</s>) consisting of invocation (<s>abhimantraṇa</s>), placing (<s>āsādana</s>), and so on — because in all Vedic ritual contexts, only consecrated waters are referred to by the word '<s>prokṣaṇī</s>'.
The alternative view is that, since in ordinary usage in water-sports [we find] '<s>prokṣaṇībhir udvejitāḥ smaḥ</s>' (we were startled by the sprinkling waters) the word is used even for unconsecrated waters, and since, like the word '<s>barhis</s>' (sacrificial grass) and the like, it is conventionally established (<s>rūḍha</s>) in the generic sense, the water-nature as a genus is the cause of its application.
Nor should the etymological derivation '<s>prakarṣeṇa ukṣyate ābhiḥ</s>' (that by which one sprinkles excellently) be suspected here,
because conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>) is stronger — this is the alternative view.
Therein, the consecration-view is not tenable in the first place,
because of mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>).
Only after the enjoined consecrations of invocation and the like are performed does the word '<s>prokṣaṇī</s>' apply to the consecrated waters;
and only when that word applies can those particular waters be identified for the consecration through the word '<s>prokṣaṇī</s>' — [hence the circularity].
Nor is the genus-view tenable,
because the word '<s>prokṣaṇī</s>' for the genus of water has not been established first through the usage of the learned (<s>vṛddha-vyavahāra</s>), and therefore a denotative power must be postulated from this point onward.
Hence, unlike the word '<s>go</s>' (cow), and like the word '<s>aśvakarṇa</s>' (name of a tree, literally 'horse-ear'), it is not conventionally established (<s>rūḍha</s>).
START MJaiNy 1,4.27
(In the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the etymological nature of the word '<s>nirmanthya</s>', the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
Similarly with '<s>nirmanthya</s>' (fire produced by churning). / Jaim_1,4.12 /
He composes the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the usage of [the word] '<s>nirmanthya</s>' conventional (<s>rūḍhi</s>), etymological (<s>yoga</s>), or a combination of both (<s>yogarūḍhi</s>)?
The first two [are refuted] as before; the third [applies] — because of [its restriction to fire] produced by quick churning, and not like [fresh] butter (<s>navanīta</s>). // MJaiNy_1,4.27 //

children.text:
agnicayane śrūyate -"nirmanthyeneṣṭakāḥ pacanti"iti |
tatra nirmanthyaśabdasya svārthe kīdṛśī vṛttiḥ, iti saṃśaye barhirādiśabdavallaukikavaidikasādhāraṇyādūvahnijātau rūḍhirityekaḥ pakṣaḥ |
prokṣaṇīśabdavadgūḍherakḷptatvādaraṇinirmanthanajanyasācca yoga iti pakṣāntaram |
laukikanirmanthanena ciranirmanthanena ca janyaṃ vārayituṃ yogarūḍhiḥ paṅkajādivadāśrayaṇīyā |
ādhānakāle nirmathya gārhapatye nityaṃ dhṛto 'gniściranirmathitaḥ |

children.translated_text: The fire that is churned at the time of the [altar] construction and maintained in the cooking vessels (<s>ukhā</s>) is fire produced by recent churning (<s>aciranirmathita</s>).
Fire that is produced immediately by ordinary churning is [also] recently churned fire.
It is with that [recently churned fire] that the bricks are baked.

children.text: yathā purāṇamūtamayorghṛtayornavanītajanyatve samāne 'pi yogarūḍhyā nūtanameva ' nāvanītam ' iti vyavahriyate tadvat || MJaiNyC_1,4.27 ||
children.translated_text: Just as, although both old and fresh ghee are equally produced from butter, by <s>yogarūḍhi</s> only the fresh [ghee] is designated as '<s>navanīta</s>' (fresh butter) — so too here. || MJaiNyC_1,4.27 ||

In the <s>Agnicayana</s> (fire-altar construction), it is heard: '<s>nirmanthyena iṣṭakāḥ pacanti</s>' (they bake the bricks with fire produced by churning).
Therein, regarding the question of what kind of denotative function the word '<s>nirmanthya</s>' has for its own meaning, one view is that, like the word '<s>barhis</s>' and the like, since it is common to both worldly and Vedic usage, it is conventionally established (<s>rūḍha</s>) in the fire-genus.
The alternative view is that, like the word '<s>prokṣaṇī</s>', since conventional usage is not established, and since it denotes [fire] produced by the churning of fire-sticks (<s>araṇi</s>), it is etymological (<s>yoga</s>).
In order to exclude fire produced by ordinary churning and by prolonged churning, a combined etymological-conventional meaning (<s>yogarūḍhi</s>), like [the word] '<s>paṅkaja</s>' (lotus, literally 'born in mud'), should be resorted to.
The fire that is churned at the time of the establishment [of sacred fires] and constantly maintained in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [hearth] is fire produced by prolonged churning (<s>ciranirmathita</s>).
START MJaiNy 1,4.28-31
(In the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the name-status of words like '<s>Vaiśvadeva</s>', <s>sūtras</s> 13-16)
In the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [sacrifice], there would be an option. / Jaim_1,4.13 /

children.text: na vā prakaraṇāt pratyakṣavidhānāc ca na hi prakaraṇaṃ dravyasya / Jaim_1,4.14 /
children.translated_text: Or not, because of the context and because of the direct injunction; for the context does not [pertain to] the substance. / Jaim_1,4.14 /
And there is mutual connection of meaningfulness. / Jaim_1,4.15 /
Because the qualifying attributes serve another purpose. / Jaim_1,4.16 /
He composes the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

In [the section] ending with the <s>Āgneyādi</s> [offerings] and the eight [sacrifices] stated in the first <s>parvan</s> (seasonal festival) of the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (four-monthly sacrifices) and the like,

children.text: vaiśvadeveti śabdokto guṇaḥ saṃghasya nāma vā // MJaiNy_1,4.28 //
children.translated_text: is [the word] '<s>Vaiśvadeva</s>' stated as a qualifying attribute (<s>guṇa</s>) of the group, or is it a name? // MJaiNy_1,4.28 //
If it is a name, since it lacks the form [of an injunction], it would not be an injunction; if it is a qualifying attribute, it exists [already] —
the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> (All-Gods) would be in optional alternation with <s>Agni</s> and the other [deities] in the seven [sacrifices]. // MJaiNy_1,4.29 //
The eight [sacrifices] being referred to anaphorically (<s>anūdya</s>), 'one should sacrifice' — in their group, the name has been described;
even though it is not an injunction, it would be meaningful, as in [the case of words like] '<s>prācīnavaṇa</s>' and the like. // MJaiNy_1,4.30 //

children.text: ijyante 'tra yajante vā viśve devā itīdṛśī /
children.translated_text: The etymology '<s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> are worshipped here' or 'the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> sacrifice here' — such
is the etymological derivation; there would be no option [of deities], because of the teaching at the time of origination (<s>utpatti</s>). // MJaiNy_1,4.31 //

children.text:
cāturmāsyayāgasya catvāri parvāṇi --- vaiśvadevaḥ , varuṇapraghāsaḥ , sākamedhaḥ , śunāsārīyaśceti |
teṣu prathame parvaṇyaṣṭau yāgā vihitāḥ --- āgneyamaṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapati, saumyaṃ carum, sāvitraṃ dvādaśakapālam, sārasvataṃ carum, pauṣṇaṃ carum , mārutaṃ saptakapālakam, vaiśvadevīmāmikṣām, dyāvāpṛthivyamekakapālam, iti |
teṣāmaṣṭhānāṃ yāgānāṃ saṃnidhāvidamāmnāyate ---"vaiśvadevena yajeta"iti |
tatrā'gneyādīnyāgān ' yajeta ' ityanūdya vaiśvadevaśabdena devatārūpo guṇasteṣu vidhīyate |
yadyapi vaiśvadevyāmikṣāyāṃ viśve devāḥ prāptāḥ, tathāpyāgneyādiṣu saptasu yāgeṣvaprāptasvādvidhīyante |
teṣvapyagnyādidevatāḥ santīti cet, tarhi gatyabhāvātteṣu devatā vikalpyantām |
nāmadheyatve tu nāmamātrasyābhidheyatvāddravyadevatayorabhāvena yāgasyātra svarūpāsaṃbhavācchūyamāṇo vidhiranarthakaḥ syāt -- tasmāt ' guṇavidhiḥ ' -- iti prāpte - ' brūmaḥ- utpattivākyairvihitānāgneyādīnaṣṭau yāgān 'yajeta' ityanūdyāṣṭānāṃ saṃghe vaiśvadevaśabdo nāmatvenopavarṇyate |
na ca vidhitvāsaṃbhave 'pi nāmopadeśavaiyarthyam, 'prācīnapravaṇe vaiśvadevena yajeta ' ityādiṣu vaiśvadevaśabdenaikenaivāṣṭānāṃ saṃghasya vyavahartavyatvāt |
nāmapravṛttinimittabhūtā niruktirdvidhā - āmikṣāyāge viśveṣāṃ devānāmijyamānatayā tatsahacaritārthānāṃ sarveṣāṃ chatrinyāyena vaiśvadevatvam |
athavā ' viśve devā aṣṭānāṃ kartāraḥ ' iti vaiśvadevatvam |
tathā ca brāhmaṇam -"yadviśve devāḥ samayajanta, tadvaiśvadevasya vaiśvadevatvam"iti |
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [states]: '<s>yad viśve devāḥ samayajanta, tad vaiśvadevasya vaiśvadevatvam</s>' (that the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> sacrificed together — that is the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>-nature of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>).
But the optional alternation of deities is not tenable, due to the absence of equal strength.

<s>Agni</s> and the other [deities] are stronger because they are taught at the time of origination (<s>utpattiśiṣṭa</s>); the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> are weaker because they are taught after origination (<s>utpannaśiṣṭa</s>).
Therefore — the word '<s>Vaiśvadeva</s>' is a name of the sacrifice (<s>karmanāmadheya</s>). || MJaiNyC_1,4.28-31 ||

The <s>Cāturmāsya</s> sacrifice has four seasonal festivals (<s>parvan</s>): <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s>, <s>Sākamedha</s>, and <s>Śunāsīrīya</s>.
In the first festival, eight offerings are enjoined: 'He prepares the <s>Āgneya</s> eight-<s>kapāla</s> [cake], the <s>Saumya</s> porridge (<s>caru</s>), the <s>Sāvitra</s> twelve-<s>kapāla</s> [cake], the <s>Sārasvata</s> porridge, the <s>Pauṣṇa</s> porridge, the <s>Māruta</s> seven-<s>kapāla</s> [cake], the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> curds (<s>āmikṣā</s>), and the <s>Dyāvāpṛthivya</s> one-<s>kapāla</s> [cake].'
In the proximity of those eight offerings, this is recited: '<s>Vaiśvadevena yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice with the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>).
Therein, the offerings <s>Āgneya</s> and the like are referred to anaphorically by '<s>yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice), and the qualifying attribute in the form of the deity is enjoined in them by the word '<s>Vaiśvadeva</s>'.
Although the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> (All-Gods) are already obtained in the <s>Vaiśvadevī āmikṣā</s> (curds offered to the All-Gods), they are nevertheless enjoined in the seven offerings to <s>Agni</s> and the like where they are not [otherwise] obtained.
If it be objected that in those [seven] too the deities <s>Agni</s> and the like already exist, then in the absence of any other recourse, let the deities be in optional alternation in those.
But if it is a name (<s>nāmadheya</s>), since a mere name only denotes [an appellation], the sacrifice would have no actual form (<s>svarūpa</s>) here due to the absence of substance and deity, and the injunction that is heard would be purposeless — therefore [the conclusion would be] 'it is a qualifying-attribute injunction' — having arrived at this position, we say: The word '<s>Vaiśvadeva</s>' is described as a name (<s>nāmadheya</s>) for the group of eight offerings — <s>Āgneya</s> and the like — which are enjoined by their origination-sentences and referred to anaphorically by '<s>yajeta</s>'.
Nor is there purposelessness of the name-instruction even in the absence of injunctive force, since in passages like '<s>prācīnapravaṇe vaiśvadevena yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice with the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> on an eastward slope) and the like, the single word '<s>Vaiśvadeva</s>' suffices for the practical designation of the group of eight.
The etymological derivation (<s>nirukti</s>) that is the cause for the application of the name is twofold: in the <s>āmikṣā</s> offering, since the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> are being worshipped, all the [other offerings] that accompany it receive the designation '<s>Vaiśvadeva</s>' by the principle of the umbrella (<s>chatri-nyāya</s>).
Alternatively, '<s>Vaiśvadeva</s>-ness' [means] 'the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> are the agents of the eight [offerings].'
START MJaiNy 1,4.32
On this, he states the teacher's view —
If [it be said that] the injunctive sentence (<s>codanā</s>) lacks validity due to the doubt between qualifying-attribute and name-status,
[we say] no — because the name-status of the group is determined by the reasoning stated above. // MJaiNy_1,4.32 //
The meaning is clear. || MJaiNyC_1,4.32 ||
START MJaiNy 1,4.33-35
(In the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the <s>arthavāda</s>-nature of the eight-<s>kapāla</s> and the like in the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [sacrifice], <s>sūtras</s> 17-22)
Those that have a prior [reference] are not for the purpose of injunction; their efficacy is in the scripture. / Jaim_1,4.17 /

children.text: guṇasya tu vidhānārthe tadguṇāḥ prayoge syur anarthakā na hi taṃ pratyarthavattāsti / Jaim_1,4.18 /
children.translated_text: But in the case of a qualifying attribute being for the purpose of injunction, its [further] qualifications would be purposeless in practice; for there is no meaningfulness with respect to that. / Jaim_1,4.18 /
Being a complement of that is not tenable. / Jaim_1,4.19 /
Since there is no distinction, they would be applicable as praise for the purpose of injunction. / Jaim_1,4.20 /
If it be said that it would be a reason. / Jaim_1,4.21 /

children.text: ānarthakyād akāraṇaṃ kartur hi kāraṇāni guṇārtho hi vidhīyate / Jaim_1,4.22 /
children.translated_text: Due to purposelessness, it is not a reason; for reasons pertain to the agent, and the qualifying attribute is enjoined for [another] purpose. / Jaim_1,4.22 /
He composes the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
That which is heard immediately after the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> twelve-<s>kapāla</s> offering,

children.text: śrutamaṣṭākapālādi tadguṇo nāma vā stutiḥ // MJaiNy_1,4.33 //
children.translated_text: [namely] the eight-<s>kapāla</s> and the like — is it a qualifying attribute, a name, or praise? // MJaiNy_1,4.33 //
Since [numbers like] eight and the like are included [in twelve], it would be a name, like '<s>Agnihotra</s>';

children.text: dravyaṃ dravyāntare no cedguṇastarhi phale tvasau // MJaiNy_1,4.34 //
children.translated_text: a substance is not [included] in another substance — if not [a name], then it is a qualifying attribute; but that [would be] regarding the fruit. // MJaiNy_1,4.34 //
The unity of the sentence is clearly [established] from the concluding statement (<s>upasaṃhāra</s>); but that [qualifying-attribute view] is overruled;
therefore, when there is an injunction of multiple qualifying attributes, [what we have is] praise of the whole (<s>aṃśin</s>) through its parts (<s>aṃśa</s>). // MJaiNy_1,4.35 //

children.text:
kāmyeṣṭikāṇḍe śrūyate -"vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapetputre jāte" "yadaṣṭākapālo bhavati gāyatryaivainaṃ brahmavarcasena punāti, yannavakapālastrivṛtaivāsmiṃstejo dadhāti, yaddaśakapālo virājaivāsminnannādyaṃ dadhāti, yadekādaśakapālastriṣṭumaivāsminnindriyaṃ dadhāti, yaddvādaśakapālo jagatyaivāsminpaśūndadhāti, yasmiñjāta etāmiṣṭiṃ nirvapati pūta eva sa tejasvyannāda indrīyāvī paśumānbhavati"iti |
atrāṣṭatvādisaṃkhyāsāmānyātpuroḍāśādīnāṃ gāyatryādirūpatvakalpanā kṛtā |
iṣṭi vidhāyake vākye yeyaṃ dvādaśasaṃkhyā tasyāmaṣṭatvādisaṃkhyānāmantarbhāvāttāḥ saṃkhyā nimittīkṛtyāgnihotraśabdavadaṣṭākapālādiśabdāḥ karmanāmadheyānītyekaḥ pakṣaḥ |
nātra dvādaśakapālaśabdaḥ saṃkhyāparaḥ , kintu puroḍośadravyaparaḥ |
' dvādaśasu kapāleṣu saṃskṛtaḥ ' iti vyutpatteḥ |
evamaṣṭākapālādiśabdā api |
tathā sati dravyasya dravyāntare 'nantarbhāvānnāmadheyasya nimittaṃ nāstīti cet , evaṃ tarhi puroḍāśabdavyarūpo guṇo vidhīyatām |
na cotpattiśiṣṭadvādaśakapālapuroḍāśāvaruddhatvādaṣṭakapālādranavakāśa iti vācyam |
brahmavarcasādiphalāya tadvidhyupapatterityaparaḥ pakṣaḥ |
ayamapyupapannaḥ |

children.translated_text: Because, if multiple qualifying attributes were enjoined, there would be a splitting of the sentence.
Nor should it be said that these are indeed separate sentences,

because the unity of the sentence is understood from the concluding statement (<s>upasaṃhāra</s>): '<s>yasmin jāta etām</s>' (in whose [family] being born, this [offering]) concludes what was enjoined by '<s>Vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet</s>'.
Therefore, the whole (<s>aṃśin</s>) — the twelve-<s>kapāla</s> [offering] — is praised through its parts (<s>aṃśa</s>) — the eight-<s>kapāla</s> and the like. || MJaiNyC_1,4.33-35 ||

In the section on desire-motivated sacrifices (<s>kāmyeṣṭi</s>), it is heard: '<s>Vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet putre jāte</s>' (when a son is born, one should prepare the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> twelve-<s>kapāla</s> offering); '<s>yad aṣṭākapālo bhavati gāyatryā eva enam brahmavarcasena punāti, yan navakapālas trivṛtā eva asmin tejo dadhāti, yad daśakapālo virājā eva asmin annādyaṃ dadhāti, yad ekādaśakapālas triṣṭubhā eva asmin indriyaṃ dadhāti, yad dvādaśakapālo jagatyā eva asmin paśūn dadhāti, yasmin jāta etām iṣṭiṃ nirvapati pūta eva sa tejasvī annāda indriyāvī paśumān bhavati</s>' (that it is eight-<s>kapāla</s>: by <s>Gāyatrī</s> alone it purifies him with <s>brahmavarcas</s>; that it is nine-<s>kapāla</s>: by <s>Trivṛt</s> alone it places splendor in him; that it is ten-<s>kapāla</s>: by <s>Virāj</s> alone it places the enjoyment of food in him; that it is eleven-<s>kapāla</s>: by <s>Triṣṭubh</s> alone it places vital power in him; that it is twelve-<s>kapāla</s>: by <s>Jagatī</s> alone it places cattle in him; in whose [family] being born, one prepares this offering — he becomes purified, splendid, a consumer of food, possessed of vital power, and rich in cattle).
Here, based on the similarity of the number eight and the like, the attribution of the form of <s>Gāyatrī</s> and other [meters] to the sacrificial cakes (<s>puroḍāśa</s>) and the like has been made.
One view is that since the numbers eight and the like are included within the number twelve in the injunctive sentence, taking those numbers as the basis, the words 'eight-<s>kapāla</s>' and the like are names of the sacrifice (<s>karmanāmadheya</s>), like the word '<s>Agnihotra</s>'.
Here, the word 'twelve-<s>kapāla</s>' does not refer to the number, but to the substance of the sacrificial cake.
Because of the etymological derivation: 'that which is prepared (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) in twelve potsherds.'
Similarly the words 'eight-<s>kapāla</s>' and the like.
This being so, since one substance is not included in another substance, there is no basis for name-status — if this is objected, then let the qualifying attribute in the form of varying [numbers of] cakes be enjoined.
Nor should it be said that since the twelve-<s>kapāla</s> cake is restricted by the origination-injunction, there is no scope for the eight-<s>kapāla</s> and the like —
because the injunction of that [eight-<s>kapāla</s> etc.] is tenable for the purpose of fruits such as <s>brahmavarcas</s> and the like — this is the other view.
This [latter view] too is tenable.
START MJaiNy 1,4.36
On this, he states the teacher's view —
If [it be said that] the eight-<s>kapāla</s> and the like lack validity because [they are] neither a qualifying attribute, nor a name, nor a <s>mantra</s>, and hence have no connection —
[we say] no — because the connection is through their nature as praise (<s>arthavāda</s>). // MJaiNy_1,4.36 //

children.text: uktarītyā guṇatvaṃ nāmatvaṃ ca na saṃbhavati |

children.translated_text: <s>Mantra</s>-status [is also not possible] because of the absence of first-person address (<s>uttamapuruṣa</s>), invocation (<s>āmantraṇa</s>), and the like.
Therefore, if [it be said that] the sentence lacks validity because the eight-<s>kapāla</s> and the like have no connection,
that is not so.
Because the connection as praise (<s>stāvaka</s>) has been stated. || MJaiNyC_1,4.36 ||
By the reasoning stated above, neither qualifying-attribute status nor name-status is possible.
START MJaiNy 1,4.37-39
(In the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the praise-function of the word '<s>yajamāna</s>' (sacrificer) for the <s>prastara</s> (grass-bundle), the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
The establishment of that. / Jaim_1,4.23 /
He composes the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: yajamānaḥ prastaro 'tra guṇo vā nāma vā stutiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>yajamānaḥ prastaraḥ</s>' (the sacrificer is the <s>prastara</s>) — is this a qualifying attribute, a name, or praise?
Through co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), it would be an alternative name of one [thing] for another. // MJaiNy_1,4.37 //
Or let '<s>yajamāna</s>' (sacrificer) be a qualifying attribute, with the <s>prastara</s> (grass-bundle) as the object characterized by the ritual;
due to the absence of part-whole relationship and the like, there is no praise here as before. // MJaiNy_1,4.38 //
Due to the difference in meaning, it is not a name; if it were a qualifying attribute, it would be abandoned [as untenable];
through the means of being instrumental to the sacrifice, this is praise of the enjoined <s>prastara</s> (grass-bundle). // MJaiNy_1,4.39 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate -"yajamānaḥ prastaraḥ"iti |
tatra yajamānasya prastaraśabdo nāmadheyam, prastarasya vā yajamānaśabdo nāmadheyam |
kutaḥ - ' udbhidā yānena ' ityādāviva sāmānādhikaraṇyādityekaḥ pakṣaḥ |
guṇavidhirityaparaḥ pakṣaḥ |
tadāpi yajamānakārye japādau prastarasyācetanasya sāmarthyābhāvādguṇatvaṃ nāsti |
prastarakārye strugdhāraṇādau yajamānasya śaktatvādyajamānarūpo guṇo vidhīyate |
evaṃ sati paścācchrutasya prastaraśabdasya kāryalakṣakatve 'pi prathamaśruto yajamānaśabdo mukhyavṛttirbhavati |
na cātra pūrvanyāyena stutiḥ saṃbhavati |
aṣṭākapāladvādaśakapālayoriva prastarayajamānayoraṃśāṃśitvābhāvāt |
"vāyurvai kṣepiṣṭhā devatā"ūrjo 'varudhyai"ityādivatstutiriti cet |
na |
kṣipratvādidharmavatkasyacidutkarṣasyāpratīteḥ |
tasmāt - ' nāmaguṇayoranyataratvam"iti prāpte , --
brūmaḥ- gomahiṣayorivārthabhedasyātyantaprasiddhatvānnāmatvaṃ na yuktam |
guṇapakṣe tu - agnau praharaṇasya prastarakāryatvādyajamāne prahṛte sati karmalopaḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: On the qualifying-attribute view — since throwing [the <s>prastara</s>] into the fire is a function of the <s>prastara</s>, if the sacrificer were thrown [into the fire], there would be destruction of the ritual act.
Therefore — the enjoined <s>prastara</s> is praised by the word '<s>yajamāna</s>'.

children.text: yathā ' siṃho devadattaḥ ' ityatra siṃhaguṇena śauryādinopeto devadattaḥ siṃhaśabdena stūyate, tathā yajamānaguṇena yāgasādhanatvena yuktaḥ prastaro yajamānaśabdena stūyate |
children.translated_text: Just as in '<s>siṃho devadattaḥ</s>' (Devadatta is a lion), <s>Devadatta</s>, endowed with lion-like qualities such as valor, is praised by the word 'lion,' so too the <s>prastara</s>, endowed with the sacrificer-like quality of being instrumental to the sacrifice, is praised by the word '<s>yajamāna</s>'.
The same should be understood in passages like '<s>yajamāna ekakapālaḥ</s>' (the sacrificer is the one-<s>kapāla</s> cake) and the like. || MJaiNyC_1,4.37-39 ||

This is what is recited in scripture: '<s>yajamānaḥ prastaraḥ</s>' (the sacrificer is the grass-bundle).
Therein, one view is that the word '<s>prastara</s>' is a name for the sacrificer, or the word '<s>yajamāna</s>' is a name for the <s>prastara</s> —
because of co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), as in '<s>udbhidā yānena</s>' and the like.
The other view is that it is a qualifying-attribute injunction.
Even on that view, the <s>prastara</s>, being insentient, has no capacity for the functions of the sacrificer such as silent recitation (<s>japa</s>) and the like, so it cannot be a qualifying attribute [of the sacrificer].
Since the sacrificer has the capacity for the functions of the <s>prastara</s> such as holding the ladle (<s>sruk</s>) and the like, the qualifying attribute in the form of the sacrificer is enjoined [for the <s>prastara</s>].
This being so, even if the word '<s>prastara</s>', heard later, indicates the function [of the <s>prastara</s>] through secondary signification, the word '<s>yajamāna</s>', heard first, retains its primary meaning.
Nor is praise possible here by the previous reasoning,
because, unlike the eight-<s>kapāla</s> and twelve-<s>kapāla</s>, there is no part-whole (<s>aṃśa-aṃśin</s>) relationship between the <s>prastara</s> and the sacrificer.
If it be said that the praise is like that in '<s>Vāyur vai kṣepiṣṭhā devatā</s>' or '<s>ūrjo 'varudhyai</s>' and the like —
no.
Because no superiority (<s>utkarṣa</s>) of any kind, like swiftness and the like, is cognized [here].
Therefore — having arrived at the position that 'it is one or the other — name or qualifying attribute' —
we say: Name-status is not appropriate, because the difference in meaning between [<s>yajamāna</s> and <s>prastara</s>] is as thoroughly well-known as that between a cow and a buffalo.
START MJaiNy 1,4.40
(In the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the praise-function of words like '<s>āgneya</s>' for <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and the like, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
The universal (<s>jāti</s>). / Jaim_1,4.24 /
He composes the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Here too, the determination of all [alternatives] is as before for '<s>āgneyo brāhmaṇaḥ</s>' (the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is related to <s>Agni</s>);
but the means for the praise through <s>āgneya</s>-ness (relation to <s>Agni</s>) is being born from the mouth. // MJaiNy_1,4.40 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate -"āgneyo vai brāhmaṇaḥ"iti |
atrātyantaprasiddhārthabhedādāgneyaśabdo na brāhyaṇasya nāmadheyam |
nāpyagnidevatārūpo guṇo vidhīyate |
' āgneyaṃ sūktam ' ' āgneyaṃ haviḥ, ityevaṃ devatātaddhitasya sūktahavirviṣayatvāt |
nahi brāhmaṇaḥ sūktam, nāpi haviḥ |
ataḥ saṃbandhavācitaddhitāntāgneyaśabdena brāhmaṇaḥ stūyate |
yadyapi brāhmaṇe nāgnisaṃbandhaḥ, tathāpyagnisaṃbandho mukhajanyatvaguṇo brāhmaṇe vidyate |
tathā cāgnibrāhmaṇayormukhajanyatvaṃ kvacidarthavāde samāmnāyate -"prajāpatirakāmayata, prajāḥ sṛjeta, iti |
children.translated_text: And thus the shared quality of being born from the mouth of <s>Agni</s> and the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is recited somewhere in an <s>arthavāda</s>: '<s>Prajāpatir akāmayata, prajāḥ sṛjeta, iti</s>' (<s>Prajāpati</s> desired: 'Let me create offspring').

children.text: sa mukhatastrivṛtaṃ niramimīta, tamagnirdevatānvayujyata, gāyatrī chandaḥ, rathantaraṃ sāma, brāhmaṇo manuṣyāṇām, ajaḥ paśūnām, tasmātte mukhyā mukhato hyasṛjyanta"iti |
children.translated_text: 'From his mouth he fashioned the <s>Trivṛt</s> [Stoma]; <s>Agni</s> became joined to it as the deity, <s>Gāyatrī</s> as the meter, <s>Rathantara</s> as the <s>Sāman</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> among humans, the goat among animals — therefore they are foremost, for they were created from the mouth.'
Therefore — the word '<s>āgneya</s>' is laudatory (<s>stāvaka</s>).

The same should be understood in passages like '<s>aindro rājanyaḥ</s>' (the <s>kṣatriya</s> is related to <s>Indra</s>), '<s>vaiśyo vaiśvadevaḥ</s>' (the <s>vaiśya</s> is related to the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s>), and the like. || MJaiNyC_1,4.40 ||

This is what is recited in scripture: '<s>āgneyo vai brāhmaṇaḥ</s>' (the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is indeed related to <s>Agni</s>).
Here, the word '<s>āgneya</s>' is not a name for the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, because the difference in meaning [between them] is thoroughly well-known.
Nor is a qualifying attribute in the form of <s>Agni</s> as the deity being enjoined,
because the <s>taddhita</s> suffix denoting the deity [in '<s>āgneya</s>'] is applicable to <s>sūktas</s> (hymns) and <s>havis</s> (oblations), as in '<s>āgneyaṃ sūktam</s>' (a hymn to <s>Agni</s>), '<s>āgneyaṃ haviḥ</s>' (an oblation to <s>Agni</s>).
For a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is neither a <s>sūkta</s> nor a <s>havis</s>.
Therefore, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is praised by the word '<s>āgneya</s>' with a <s>taddhita</s> suffix denoting relation.
Although the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> does not have [a direct] connection with <s>Agni</s>, nevertheless the qualifying attribute of being born from the mouth (<s>mukhajanyatva</s>), which is the connection with <s>Agni</s>, exists in the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
START MJaiNy 1,4.41
(In the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the praise-function of words like '<s>yūpa</s>' (sacrificial post) for the sacrificer, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
Because of similarity of form (<s>sārūpya</s>). / Jaim_1,4.25 /
He composes the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In '<s>ādityo yūpaḥ</s>' (the sacrificial post is <s>Āditya</s>, the sun), the praise is from the word '<s>āditya</s>';

children.text: dvāraṃ cākṣuṣasārūpyaṃ ghṛtākte taijase 'sti tat // MJaiNy_1,4.41 //
children.translated_text: the means [of praise] is the similarity in visible splendor — that exists in the ghee-anointed [post], which is radiant. // MJaiNy_1,4.41 //
The splendor that is perceived by the eye in <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) exists also in the sacrificial post.
Because one ascertains the radiance of the sacrificial post when anointed with ghee.
Therefore — the sacrificial post is praised by the word '<s>āditya</s>'.

children.text: evaṃ"yajamāno yūpaḥ"ityatra cakṣurgamyasyordhvatvasya samānatvādyajamānaśabdena yūpaḥ stūyate || MJaiNyC_1,4.41 ||
children.translated_text: Similarly, in '<s>yajamāno yūpaḥ</s>' (the sacrificial post is the sacrificer), since the uprightness that is perceived by the eye is shared [by both], the sacrificial post is praised by the word '<s>yajamāna</s>'. || MJaiNyC_1,4.41 ||
START MJaiNy 1,4.42-44
(In the sixteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the praise-function of words like '<s>apaśu</s>' (non-animal) for cows and the like, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
It is a commendation (<s>praśaṃsā</s>). / Jaim_1,4.26 /
He composes the sixteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
It is heard: 'Animals other than cows and horses are non-animals (<s>apaśu</s>)' —
is this non-animal-ness in goats and the like a qualifying attribute, an <s>arthavāda</s>, or what? // MJaiNy_1,4.42 //
Since praise is not apparent, it is a qualifying attribute [that means] a prohibition of the functions pertaining to animals in those [goats etc.];
but since the prohibition is impossible, [this is said] by a word denoting [something else like] a pot and the like. // MJaiNy_1,4.43 //

The [goats and other] animals are designated by the word '<s>apaśu</s>' (non-animal) through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), because of the similarity in the absence of excellence (<s>prāśastya</s>);

children.text: lakṣyāstatra nimittaṃ tu praśaṃsaiva gavāśvayoḥ // MJaiNy_1,4.44 //
children.translated_text: therein, the cause [of the secondary usage] is indeed the commendation (<s>praśaṃsā</s>) of cows and horses. // MJaiNy_1,4.44 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate --"apaśavo vā anye gośvebhyaḥ, paśavo goaśvāḥ"iti |
tatrājādiṣu śrūyamāṇaṃ yadapaśutvaṃ tasyārthavādatvaṃ na saṃbhavati |
paśutvaniṣedhamātreṇa stuterapratibhānāt |
tataḥ paśukāryaniṣedharumo guṇo vidhīyata iti cet |
maivam |
ajādipaśuvidhivaiyarththaprasaṅgena niṣeddhumaśakyatvāt |
apaśuśabdaḥ paśuvyatiriktaṃ ghaṭādipadārthajātamabhidadhāti |
tasminghaṭādau gavāśvavatprāśastyaṃ nāsti |
so 'yaṃ prāśastyābhāvo 'jādiṣu paśuṣvastītyanenābhiprāyeṇa paśava eva santo 'pyajādayo ghaṭādisāmyādapaśuśabdena lakṣyante |
pūrvatra yajamānādiśabdānāṃ prastarādyartheṣu pravṛttinimittam |
tatpravṛttiphalaṃ prastarādipraśaṃsā |
iha tvapaśuśabdasyājādiṣu mavṛttau gavāśvayoḥ praśaṃsaiva nimittaṃ phalaṃ ca |
dviprakārā praśaṃsā- vastūnividyamānaguṇotkarṣa ekaḥ prakāraḥ |
stāvakena śabdena saṃpādito guṇotkarṣo 'paraḥ prakāraḥ |
gavāśvayorajādibhya utkarṣo lokasiddho yaḥ so 'tra nimittam |
' ajādayaḥ svabhāvataḥ paśavo 'pi santo gavāśvau pratyapaśavaḥ saṃpannāḥ |
īdṛśo gavāśvayormahimā ' iti stutiphalam |
tasmāt --"apaśavo vai"ityayamarthavādaḥ |
ayameva nyāya udāharaṇāntare 'pi yojanīyaḥ-"ayajño vā eṣa yo 'sāma"ityekamudāharaṇam |
"asatraṃ vā etadyacchandogam"ityaparamudāharaṇam |
"agnihotradarśapūrṇamāsādiryajño 'pi sāmahīnatvādayajño bhavati |
īdṛśaḥ sāmno mahimā |
chandogaśabdena caturviśaḥ, catuścatvāriṃśaḥ, aṣṭacatvāriṃśa ityete trayaḥ stomā ucyante |
akṣarasaṃkhyāsāmyena gāyatrītriṣṭubjagarīchandobhirgīyamānatvāt |

children.translated_text: Their detailed exposition (<s>viṣṭuti</s>) should be seen in the <s>Sāmabrāhmaṇa</s>.
Therefore, even a <s>satra</s> (sacrificial session) such as the fourteen-night [session] and the like, being devoid of <s>Chandoga</s> [chants], becomes a non-<s>satra</s>.
Such is the greatness of the <s>Chandoga</s> [chants].
Thus, because of being laudatory (<s>stāvaka</s>), it is an <s>arthavāda</s>. || MJaiNyC_1,4.42-44 ||

This is what is recited in scripture: '<s>apaśavo vā anye go-aśvebhyaḥ, paśavo go-aśvāḥ</s>' (others besides cows and horses are non-animals; cows and horses are [true] animals).
Therein, the non-animal-ness (<s>apaśutva</s>) that is heard regarding goats and the like cannot be an <s>arthavāda</s>,
because from the mere negation of animal-status, no praise is apprehended.
If it be said that a qualifying attribute in the form of a prohibition of functions pertaining to animals is being enjoined —
that is not so,
because [such a prohibition] cannot be accomplished without rendering the injunctions regarding goats and other animals purposeless.
The word '<s>apaśu</s>' (non-animal) denotes the entire class of entities such as pots and the like that are other than animals.
In those pots and the like, there is no excellence (<s>prāśastya</s>) as there is in cows and horses.
With the intention that this absence of excellence exists also in goats and other animals, although they are indeed animals, goats and the like are designated by the word '<s>apaśu</s>' through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), because of their similarity to pots and the like.
In the previous cases, the cause of the application of words like '<s>yajamāna</s>' and the like to objects like the <s>prastara</s> and the like [was some shared quality].
The result of that application was the praise of the <s>prastara</s> and the like.
But here, in the application of the word '<s>apaśu</s>' to goats and the like, the commendation of cows and horses is both the cause and the result.
Praise (<s>praśaṃsā</s>) is of two kinds: one kind is the superiority of a quality actually existing in the object;
the other kind is the superiority of a quality produced by a laudatory word.
The superiority of cows and horses over goats and the like that is well-established in the world — that is the cause here.
'Goats and the like, though by nature animals, have become non-animals in comparison to cows and horses —
such is the greatness of cows and horses' — this is the result of the praise.
Therefore — '<s>apaśavo vai</s>' (they are indeed non-animals) is an <s>arthavāda</s>.
This very reasoning should be applied to other examples as well: '<s>ayajño vā eṣa yo 'sāma</s>' (that is indeed a non-sacrifice which is without <s>Sāman</s>) — this is one example.
'<s>asatraṃ vā etad yac chandogam</s>' (that is indeed a non-<s>satra</s> which is a <s>Chandoga</s>) — this is another example.
'The <s>Agnihotra</s>, <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, and the like, though they are sacrifices, become non-sacrifices because they lack <s>Sāman</s> —
such is the greatness of <s>Sāman</s>.
By the word '<s>Chandoga</s>', three <s>Stomas</s> (modes of chanting) are denoted: the <s>Caturviṃśa</s> (twenty-four-fold), the <s>Catuścatvāriṃśa</s> (forty-four-fold), and the <s>Aṣṭacatvāriṃśa</s> (forty-eight-fold),
because they are sung with the meters <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, and <s>Jagatī</s> [respectively] due to the similarity in syllable count.

(In the seventeenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the preponderance [principle] — the topic of the creation-expression being <s>arthavāda</s> for words like '<s>prāṇabhṛt</s>' and the like — the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
Preponderance (<s>bhūmā</s>). / Jaim_1,4.27 /
He composes the seventeenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The <s>mantras</s> bearing creation-marks in '<s>sṛṣṭīr upadadhāti</s>' (he places the creation[-bricks]) —

Because of the connection with the finite verb [<s>upadadhāti</s>], and because of the impossibility of another injunction,

Having referred to those [<s>mantras</s>] anaphorically, the placement of bricks is enjoined; since it will praise [them],

Granted.

children.translated_text: Even so, since the root '<s>sṛj</s>' is used in many <s>mantras</s> — the second, third, and so on — there is a smoky kind of similarity (<s>dhūmarūpaṃ sādṛśyam</s>).

children.translated_text: Where all the sentences contain the word '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>', there the use of the word '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>' [applies] accordingly. || MJaiNyC_1,4.45-48 ||

In the <s>Agnicayana</s> (fire-altar construction), it is heard: '<s>sṛṣṭīr upadadhāti</s>' (he places the creation-bricks).
The bricks whose placement is accompanied by <s>mantras</s> containing the word '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>' (creation) are called '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>' bricks.
[The term is derived] by the grammatical process established by the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>tadvān āsām upadhānaḥ</s>' [<s>Pāṇini</s> 4.4.125] and the like, by analyzing '<s>sṛṣṭimān āsām upadhāno mantraḥ</s>' (the mantra for their placement possessing [the word] <s>sṛṣṭi</s>).
The placement-<s>mantras</s> containing the word '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>' are recited in the <s>anuvāka</s> (section) '<s>ekayā stuvata</s>' (they praised with one).
Because the root '<s>sṛj</s>' (to create) is used in them, as in '<s>brahmā asṛjyata</s>' (<s>Brahman</s> was created), '<s>bhūtāny asṛjyanta</s>' (beings were created), and so on.
Those <s>mantras</s> are enjoined here as qualifying attributes by the word '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>' in the placement —
because of the connection with the finite verb '<s>upadadhāti</s>' (he places).
Nor is <s>arthavāda</s>-status possible for this,
since there is no unity of sentence (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) with another injunction — having arrived at this position,
we say: Since those <s>mantras</s> are recited in the context of the <s>Agnicayana</s>, their general connection with the [fire-altar] construction is understood.
The specific connection should be understood from the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of the root '<s>sṛj</s>' (to create).
This being so, since they are [already] obtained [by other means], those <s>mantras</s> are not being enjoined here; rather — having referred to those <s>mantras</s> anaphorically, the placement of bricks is enjoined.
The anaphoric reference by the word '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>' serves the purpose of supporting the <s>arthavāda</s> that will be stated [later].
For the <s>arthavāda</s> that will be stated is: '<s>yathā sṛṣṭam evāvarūndhe</s>' (one obtains exactly as it was created).
If the word '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>' referring to the <s>mantras</s> were not present in the injunctive sentence, then, due to the use of the word '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>' in the <s>arthavāda</s>, there would be a mistaken impression of non-co-referentiality between the injunction and the <s>arthavāda</s>.
Therefore, the word '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>' that refers to the <s>mantras</s> anaphorically is not an injunction of a qualifying attribute, but rather an <s>arthavāda</s>.
Now, in the first <s>mantra</s>, the root '<s>sṛj</s>' is not used; rather, the root '<s>dhā</s>' (to place) is used.

(In the eighteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the rule of co-occurrence of the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) — the topic of the praise-function of words like '<s>prāṇabhṛt</s>' — the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
Because of the co-occurrence of the mark (<s>liṅgasamavāya</s>). / Jaim_1,4.28 /
He composes the eighteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Like the <s>sṛṣṭi</s> [case], the '<s>prāṇabhṛt</s>' (life-bearing) [case] has similarity there due to the preponderance of the mark (<s>liṅga</s>);
but here, the co-occurrence of the mark in a single <s>mantra</s> (<s>liṅgasamavāya</s>) is the distinguishing feature. // MJaiNy_1,4.49 //

children.translated_text:
In '<s>prāṇabhṛta upadadhāti</s>' (he places the life-bearing [bricks]) as well, the prior view is that the <s>mantras</s> are enjoined by the <s>sṛṣṭi</s>-reasoning.
[The established view is that] the placement of bricks is enjoined through the anaphoric reference to <s>mantras</s> [already] obtained by the mark and the context.
The anaphoric reference to the <s>mantras</s> by the word '<s>prāṇabhṛt</s>' serves the purpose of supporting the <s>arthavāda</s> that will be stated: '<s>etasyaiva prāṇān dadhāti</s>' (it places the vital breaths of this very one).
In the previous case — the mark of <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (creation) was preponderant in the second and subsequent <s>mantras</s>.
But here — the mark of '<s>prāṇabhṛt</s>' is recited in the very first <s>mantra</s>: '<s>ayaṃ purobhuvas tasya prāṇo bhauvāyanaḥ</s>' (this is the front-existing one, its vital breath is <s>Bhauvāyana</s>).
Even though only one <s>mantra</s> has the '<s>prāṇabhṛt</s>' [mark], by the principle '<s>chatriṇo gacchanti</s>' (those with umbrellas are going) — where [even if only some carry umbrellas, the entire group is so designated] — all the <s>mantras</s> accompanying it are designated by the word '<s>prāṇabhṛt</s>' through secondary signification.
Thus the reasons for the secondary usage (<s>gauṇī vṛtti</s>) of words — such as accomplishment of the function of the sacrificer and the like — have been determined.
And thus it has been said:
'By means of six [factors] — accomplishment (<s>tatsiddhi</s>), genus (<s>jāti</s>), similarity of form (<s>sārūpya</s>), commendation (<s>praśaṃsā</s>), mark (<s>liṅga</s>), and preponderance (<s>bhūmā</s>) —
the secondary usage (<s>gauṇī vṛtti</s>) of words is established everywhere.'
|| MJaiNyC_1,4.49 ||
START MJaiNy 1,4.50-53
(In the nineteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the determination of doubtful meaning through the complement of the sentence — the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
In cases of doubt, from the complement of the sentence (<s>vākyaśeṣa</s>). / Jaim_1,4.29 /
He composes the nineteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'<s>Aktāḥ śarkarā upadadhāti</s>' (he places anointed gravel pieces) — '<s>tejo vai ghṛtam</s>' (ghee is indeed radiance) — what is meant here?
Are they anointed with oil and the like, or is the anointing with ghee alone? // MJaiNy_1,4.50 //
[Anointing] with oil and the like is also primary, because no contradiction has arisen,
and because this [injunction] conveys an unprecedented meaning; the injunction is stronger than the <s>arthavāda</s>. // MJaiNy_1,4.51 //
The general [anointing] cannot be performed [as such]; but the specific [substance] is not [stated] in the injunction;
anointing is with ghee alone — from the complement of the sentence (<s>vākyaśeṣa</s>), because it resolves the doubt. // MJaiNy_1,4.52 //
And this praise occurring in the <s>arthavāda</s>, having recourse to ghee,
by making known that ghee is to be enjoined, indicates the injunction [of ghee]. // MJaiNy_1,4.53 //

children.translated_text: Since ghee is praised for its radiance (<s>tejastva</s>) in '<s>tejo vai ghṛtam</s>' (ghee is indeed radiance), its being the object of an injunction is understood.
By the principle: '<s>stūyate sa vidhīyate</s>' (what is praised is what is enjoined).

children.translated_text: And through that status of being enjoined, a word that enjoins is postulated: '<s>ghṛtena aktāḥ</s>' (anointed with ghee).
Therefore — the anointing is with ghee alone. || MJaiNyC_1,4.50-53 ||

It is heard: '<s>aktāḥ śarkarā upadadhāti</s>' (he places anointed gravel pieces), '<s>tejo vai ghṛtam</s>' (ghee is indeed radiance).
The gravel pieces (<s>śarkarā</s>) are small stones mixed with clay.
They should be anointed with any one substance among ghee, oil, fat, and so on.
Why?
Because the injunctive sentence, which conveys only the general sense of anointing, is stronger than [the <s>arthavāda</s>] which conveys the specific sense of ghee, due to semantic non-contradiction.
And for that strength [of the injunction], there are three reasons:
The injunction is primary because it serves its own purpose; it has no arisen contradicting [passage] because it is heard first; and it conveys an unprecedented meaning because it makes known what was not previously known. The <s>arthavāda</s>, on the other hand, is not primary because it is subservient to the injunction as its praise; it has an arisen contradiction because it is heard later; and it conveys an already-obtained meaning because it restates what is already known.
Therefore — 'anointing is with any [substance whatsoever]' — having arrived at this position,
we say: Does the injunctive sentence enjoin the general means of anointing, or a specific [means]?
Not the first,
because the general cannot be performed [as such].
Not the second,
because there is no word specifying ghee, oil, and the like.
Therefore, even though the injunctive sentence is stronger in the manner described, it generates doubt regarding the specific [substance] suitable for performance, and thus it requires the <s>arthavāda</s> as the means of determination — it does not conflict with it.
If it be objected that even in the <s>arthavāda</s> there is no injunction of ghee —
no.
Because the injunction can be inferred.

children.translated_text: The hand is suitable for the compact sacrificial cake (<s>puroḍāśa</s>) — in this manner, the ladle and the like are determined. || MJaiNyC_1,4.54-55 ||

It is heard: '<s>struveṇāvadyati</s>' (he cuts off with the ladle), '<s>svadhitinādyati</s>' (he cuts with the axe), '<s>hastenāvadyati</s>' (he cuts off with the hand).
Therein, with respect to the oblation-materials (<s>havis</s>) to be cut — ghee, meat, and sacrificial cake — these instruments of cutting — the ladle and the like — are intermixed.
Why?
Because there is no word that would determine [which goes with which] — if this is the objection,
that is not so,
because capacity (<s>śakti</s>) serves as the determining factor.
By the principle: '<s>ākhyātānām arthe bruvatāṃ śaktiḥ sahakāriṇī</s>' (capacity is the auxiliary of verbs that express meaning).
In ordinary usage, when one says '<s>kaṭe bhuṅkte</s>' (he eats on a mat) or '<s>kāṃsyapātryāṃ bhuṅkte</s>' (he eats in a bronze vessel), people determine the meaning according to the capacity of the respective objects: 'seated on the mat,' 'having placed the rice in the bronze vessel.'
In the Veda too — in '<s>añjalinā saktūn pradāya juhuyāt</s>' (having offered barley flour with cupped hands, one should make an oblation), although the <s>añjali</s> (cupped hands) is a joining of two hands, nevertheless the joining is not seamless like the <s>añjali</s> [gesture] used for propitiating teachers, deities, and the like.

children.text: iti śrī mādhavīye jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistare prathamādhāyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>pāda</s> of the first <s>adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Mādhavīya Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s>.
And the first <s>adhyāya</s> is completed.
<s>Śrīḥ</s> (auspiciousness).

Now the second <s>adhyāya</s>.
(Therein, the first <s>pāda</s>)
START MJaiNy 2,1.1
Since it is foundational, the means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) was stated in the first <s>adhyāya</s>;

children.text: mānādhīnasya dharmasya dbitīye bheda ucyate // MJaiNy_2,1.1 //
children.translated_text: in the second, the classification of <s>dharma</s>, which depends on the means of knowledge, is stated. // MJaiNy_2,1.1 //
By this [verse], the sequential relationship of the first and second <s>adhyāyas</s> is established. || 1 ||
(In the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the topic of the unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>) being conveyed by the verbal suffix — <s>sūtras</s> 1-4)

children.text: bhāvārthāḥ karmaśabdās tebhyaḥ kriyā pratīyeta eṣa hy artho vidhīyate / Jaim_2,1.1 /
children.translated_text: Words denoting ritual action (<s>karmaśabda</s>) have the sense of bringing into being (<s>bhāva</s>); from them, the action (<s>kriyā</s>) should be understood — for this is the meaning that is enjoined. / Jaim_2,1.1 /
If [one says that] the sense of all [words] is bringing into being (<s>bhāva</s>). / Jaim_2,1.2 /

children.text: yeṣām utpattau sve prayoge rūpopalabdhis tāni nāmāni tasmāt tebhyaḥ parākāṅkṣā bhūtatvāt sve prayogai / Jaim_2,1.3 /
children.translated_text: Those in which, at the time of origination, there is apprehension of form in their own application — those are nouns (<s>nāmāni</s>); therefore, from them there is expectancy for something else, because they have an accomplished nature (<s>bhūtatva</s>) in their own application. / Jaim_2,1.3 /

children.text: yeṣāṃ tūtpattāv arthe sve prayogo na vidyate tāny ākhyātāni tasmāt tebhyaḥ pratīyetāśritatvāt prayogasya / Jaim_2,1.4 /
children.translated_text: But those in which, at origination, there is no application of their own regarding the meaning — those are verbal forms (<s>ākhyāta</s>); therefore, from them it should be understood [that the action is enjoined], because the application is dependent [on another]. / Jaim_2,1.4 /
START MJaiNy 2,1.2-3

children.text: dvitīyādhyāyasya prathame pāde prathamādhikaraṇe prathamaṃ varṇakamāracayati -
children.translated_text: In the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the first <s>pāda</s> of the second <s>adhyāya</s>, he composes the first <s>varṇaka</s> (exposition) —
In the injunctive sentence, is the unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>) conveyed by all the words
individually, or [is it conveyed] by all of them collectively as one? // MJaiNy_2,1.2 //
Since all [words] are connected with the fruit, and since thereby connection with the principal [meaning] is obtained,
by the principle of parsimony, a single [thing] is to be understood [as conveyed]; the other words are subordinate to that. // MJaiNy_2,1.3 //

children.translated_text: In '<s>udbhidā yajeta paśukāmaḥ</s>' (one desiring cattle should sacrifice with the <s>Udbhid</s>), '<s>śyenena abhicaran yajeta</s>' (one performing sorcery should sacrifice with the <s>Śyena</s>), and the like, since words like '<s>udbhid</s>' and the like are connected as names, and since they lack the capacity to denote the instrument of the sacrifice, they do not produce the triad of being the principal referent and the like for '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices).
Therefore, it is a single word alone that conveys the <s>apūrva</s>.

children.text: na ca dharmabhedacintāṃ prastutā parityajya kimityapūrve cintyata iti vācyam |
children.translated_text: Nor should it be objected: 'Why is one deliberating about the <s>apūrva</s>, abandoning the proposed topic of the classification of <s>dharma</s>?'
Because the <s>apūrva</s> itself is <s>dharma</s>. || MJaiNyC_2,1.2-3 ||

An injunctive sentence conveys an unseen purpose (<s>adṛṣṭārtha</s>) — the entire sentence here is the example.
In the injunctive sentence, all the words that exist, disregarding the relationship of action and case-relations (<s>kāraka</s>), each individually convey the <s>apūrva</s> (unprecedented unseen merit).
Why?
Because all words are connected with the fruit, since the <s>apūrva</s> has the nature of fruit.
If it be objected that even without conveying the <s>apūrva</s>, the mutual connection between action and case-relations exists —
true.
But even so, the connection with the principal [meaning] would be obtained.
For the fruit is the principal [meaning],
since it is what is to be accomplished as serving a human purpose — having arrived at this position, we say: Since the <s>apūrva</s> is entirely unseen, when the sentence is justified by postulating just one [<s>apūrva</s>], postulating many would result in the fault of over-complexity (<s>gaurava</s>).
Therefore, a single <s>apūrva</s> is conveyed by a single word.
The other words are connected with it as its subordinates.
Now, if it be objected that the word whose meaning is the postulator of the <s>apūrva</s> — for that word-meaning, the statuses of being subsidiary to the fruit (<s>upādeyatva</s>), being enjoined (<s>vidheyatva</s>), and being a qualifying attribute (<s>guṇatva</s>) must be accepted. And similarly, for the meaning of the remaining subordinate words, the statuses of being the principal referent (<s>uddeśyatva</s>), being referred to (<s>anuvādyatva</s>), and being the principal (<s>pradhānatva</s>) are also obtained — thus there would be the absurd consequence of two contradictory triads — 
that is not so.
He composes the second <s>varṇaka</s> —
START MJaiNy 2,1.4-7
Is the cognition of the <s>apūrva</s> from words denoting substances (<s>dravya</s>) and the like, or from words denoting the productive force (<s>bhāvārtha</s>)?
Since substances and the like serve the purpose of the fruit, the cognition of the <s>apūrva</s> would be through their words. // MJaiNy_2,1.4 //
Without the medium of action (<s>kriyā</s>), substance is not connected with the fruit;
the <s>apūrva</s> is understood from the verbal form (<s>ākhyāta</s>), which denotes the productive force (<s>bhāvanā</s>). // MJaiNy_2,1.5 //
If [one says] that <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force) does not [exist] apart from the meaning of the verbal root — that is not so;
for the meaning of '<s>karoti</s>' (does/makes), which is connected with the meanings of all roots, is indeed <s>bhāvanā</s>. // MJaiNy_2,1.6 //
The root-meaning is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) of that [<s>bhāvanā</s>], described within the same word;
the contribution of substances and the like is observed to consist in the production of the root-meaning. // MJaiNy_2,1.7 //

children.translated_text: Thus it has been said:
'The <s>liṅ</s> and other [suffixes] express one <s>bhāvanā</s> — the verbal one (<s>abhidhā-bhāvanā</s>);
but the objective <s>bhāvanā</s> (<s>arthātma-bhāvanā</s>) is another, which is understood in all verbal forms.' ||

This is recited in scripture: '<s>somena yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>), '<s>hiraṇyam ātreyāya dadāti</s>' (he gives gold to an <s>Ātreya</s>), '<s>tasmāt suvarṇe hiraṇyaṃ dhāryam</s>' (therefore gold should be kept in a golden [vessel]), '<s>śyenena abhicaran yajeta</s>' (one performing sorcery should sacrifice with the <s>Śyena</s>), '<s>citrayā yajeta paśukāmaḥ</s>' (one desiring cattle should sacrifice with the <s>Citrā</s>), and so on.
Therein, the words '<s>soma</s>' and '<s>hiraṇya</s>' denote substances, the word '<s>suvarṇa</s>' denotes a qualifying attribute, and the words '<s>śyena</s>' and '<s>citrā</s>' denote ritual actions.
From these various words denoting substances and the like, the <s>apūrva</s> is understood — why?
Because substances and the like, being of an accomplished nature, can possibly be instruments (<s>sādhana</s>) for accomplishing the fruit which is to be achieved.
But the meaning of <s>bhāva</s> (bringing into being) in the form of sacrifice, giving, and the like, being itself of the nature of something to be accomplished along with the fruit, cannot be an instrument.
Therefore, since substances and the like are instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>) with respect to the fruit, the words for substances and the like convey the <s>apūrva</s> — having arrived at this position, we say: Without action, substances are not capable of accomplishing the fruit.
Because without the action of cooking, firewood, pots, and the like are not seen to accomplish cooked rice.
Therefore, the <s>apūrva</s> is understood from the verbal form '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices), '<s>dadāti</s>' (he gives), which denotes the <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force).
Now, is <s>bhāvanā</s> identical with the root-meaning, or different from it?
Not the first,
because it is stated that the root-meaning is the instrument of <s>bhāvanā</s>.
Not the second,
because an action different from the root-meaning would be difficult to identify — if this is the objection,
that is not so,
because what has the form of '<s>karoti</s>' (does/makes), which is connected with the meanings of all roots, can be identified.
Thus the teachers have said:
'Although <s>bhāvanā</s> cannot be identified apart from the root-meaning,
nevertheless it is understood in the form of a universal [element common to all roots].'
Others too have said:
'The root-meaning is of two kinds — accomplished and to-be-accomplished; of these,
<s>bhāvanā</s> is that which has the nature of being conducive to the production of the other, and is of the nature of what is to be accomplished.'
When one says '<s>pacati</s>' (he cooks), all people understand the meaning 'he does the cooking (<s>pākaṃ karoti</s>).'
Therein, cooking (<s>pāka</s>), called by the words '<s>pakti</s>' (cooking) and '<s>pacana</s>' (the act of cooking), is the root-meaning of accomplished nature, susceptible to gender, case-relation, and number.
The injunctive suffix serves to reveal the to-be-accomplished nature, expressed by '<s>karoti</s>' (does/makes), which is devoid of gender and the like.
And that meaning of the verbal suffix is conducive to the production of cooked rice.
Therefore, since cooked rice is the thing to be brought into being, by the causative-ended word '<s>bhāvanā</s>' (productive force), the impelling activity of the agent is denoted — thus.
Other views on <s>bhāvanā</s> are untenable.
If [one says] <s>bhāvanā</s> is effort (<s>prayatna</s>) —
no,
because in '<s>ratho gacchati</s>' (the chariot goes), the absence of [effort] would be an absurd consequence.
If [one says] it is motion (<s>spanda</s>) —
no,
because it would fail to apply to the sacrifice (<s>yajati</s>), which has the nature of mental renunciation (<s>mānasa-tyāga</s>).
If [one says] <s>bhāvanā</s> is the universal [quality] of cessation of indifference (<s>udāsīnatva-viccheda</s>), common to both [effort and motion] —
no,
because it would fail to apply to verbal <s>bhāvanā</s> (<s>śabda-bhāvanā</s>), since the word (<s>śabda</s>), being all-pervading and insentient, has neither motion nor effort.
Verbal <s>bhāvanā</s> (<s>śabda-bhāvanā</s>) resides only in the suffixes <s>liṅ</s>, <s>leṭ</s>, <s>loṭ</s>, and <s>tavya</s>.
Objective <s>bhāvanā</s> (<s>artha-bhāvanā</s>) is present in all verbal forms.

children.translated_text: And it will be stated that this instrumentality is not possible without the postulation of <s>apūrva</s> (unseen transcendent force).
Therefore, <s>apūrva</s> is understood from the word signifying productive operation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) that ends in the verbal suffix.
The purpose of the inquiry, however, is: 'In the prior view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>), when there is a deficiency in substance and the like, there is no substitution (<s>pratinidhi</s>);
but in the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), that [substitution] does exist.' || MJaiNyC_2,1.4-7 ||

Moreover, even those who advocate the theory of <s>spanda</s> (activity) and the like do not assert that <s>spanda</s> and the like are <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive operation) by their own nature, but rather that their nature is conducive to the production of something else. Therefore, <s>bhāvanā</s> is exactly as we have stated. Just as in '<s>pacati</s>' (he cooks), [<s>bhāvanā</s>] is conducive to the production of the result of rice, so in '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices), it is conducive to the production of the result of heaven and the like. In that <s>phalabhāvanā</s> (result-productive operation) denoted by the verbal suffix — since the verbal root-meaning is proximate, being obtained from a single word — it is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), not substance and the like, because those are remote, being obtained from other words. Even though the verbal root-meaning has the nature of something to be accomplished, once accomplished by its own means, it is capable of accomplishing the result. But the contribution of substances and the like consists only in the visible production of the verbal root-meaning. When the production of the result of heaven and the like occurs through sacrifice and the like as the instrument — denoted by the verbal root and accomplished by substances and the like — this productive activity that is the favorable operation, expressible by the word '<s>kṛti</s>' (effort), namely the production of the result, is not expressed by any one particular verbal root such as '<s>yaj</s>' (to sacrifice) and the like, because it accompanies the meaning of all verbal roots. Therefore it cannot be suspected that <s>bhāvanā</s> is the verbal root-meaning. If it be said: let <s>bhāvanā</s> then be the generality of verbal root-meanings — no, because each verbal root-meaning has a distinctive form. For the conduciveness of cooking toward rice is one thing, and the conduciveness of movement toward conjunction and disjunction is another. Otherwise, the distinction of results could not be accounted for. Let the generality of <s>bhāvanā</s>-hood persist across different instances of <s>bhāvanā</s>; that much does not make it the generality of the verbal root-meaning. Therefore, <s>bhāvanā</s> — denoted by the verbal suffix (<s>ākhyātapratyaya</s>) — is something other than what is denoted by verbal roots like '<s>yaj</s>' and the like, whether in its particular or general form. This being so, in '<s>yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice), the meaning of the verbal ending is '<s>bhāvayet</s>' (one should bring about). There, when the expectancy arises — 'what should one bring about? by what means should one bring about? how should one bring about?' — the answers are: 'one should bring about heaven,' 'one should bring about [it] by sacrifice,' 'one should bring about [it] by accomplishing the contribution of the preliminary rites such as placing the fires (<s>anvādhāna</s>), fore-sacrifices (<s>prayāja</s>), pounding (<s>avaghāta</s>), and the like.' Thus, by the assignment of the object (<s>bhāvya</s>), instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), and procedure (<s>itikartavyatā</s>) to satisfy the expectancies, the entire body of words recited in the context is merely an elaboration of the verbal ending that expresses <s>bhāvanā</s>. That which possesses the three components — the object to be produced and so on — is called <s>ārthī bhāvanā</s> (objective productive operation). All of that <s>ārthī bhāvanā</s> is the object (<s>bhāvya</s>) of <s>śābdī bhāvanā</s> (verbal productive operation); the prescriptive suffix <s>liṅ</s> and the like is the instrument. The praise accomplished by <s>arthavāda</s> is the procedure. This <s>śābdī bhāvanā</s> is understood through the <s>liṅ</s> suffix and the like alone. It has been said that <s>ārthī bhāvanā</s> is understood through all verbal suffixes. And in that <s>ārthī bhāvanā</s>, the status of heaven as the object to be produced is understood from the connection with the desiderative word. The instrumental nature of the verbal root-meaning is understood from the instrumental case ending. And thus it is heard in scripture: '<s>darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta</s>' (one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>) and '<s>citrayā yajeta paśukāmaḥ</s>' (one desiring cattle should sacrifice with the <s>Citrā</s>).
(In the second [topic] — the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the existence of <s>apūrva</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
The injunction (<s>codanā</s>) is the [basis for] commencement again. / Jaim_2,1.5 /
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 2.1.8-10]
He composes the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
When there is doubt about the existence or non-existence of <s>apūrva</s> — it does not exist,
due to the absence of a means of knowledge [for it]; the result should be accomplished from the sacrifice itself by the authority of scripture. // MJaiNy_2,1.8 //
The postulation that something momentary and perished can be a cause of heaven
is contradicted by another means of knowledge; therefore the postulation of <s>apūrva</s> is preferable. // MJaiNy_2,1.9 //
An intermediate operation or a potency born of the sacrifice is called
<s>apūrva</s> — its distinctions should be understood from the procedure (<s>prakriyā</s>). // MJaiNy_2,1.10 //

children.translated_text: And through that [production-<s>apūrva</s>], they [contribute] to the result-<s>apūrva</s>.

children.text: ārādupakārakāṇi tu prayājādīnyutpattyupūrvebhyaḥ phalāpūrvaniṣpattau sākṣādeva vyāpriyante |
children.translated_text: But those that contribute from afar — such as the fore-sacrifices (<s>prayāja</s>) and the like — are directly active in the accomplishment of the result-<s>apūrva</s> from the production-<s>apūrvas</s>.

children.text: evaṃ prakārabhede satyapi sarvāṇyaṅgānyapūrvaniṣpattāvanugrāhakāṇi - ityekarūpeṇetthaṃbhāvena svī kriyante |
children.translated_text: Thus, even though there is a difference in manner, all the subsidiaries are facilitators in the accomplishment of <s>apūrva</s> — they are accepted as having this single uniform nature.
By this very direction, the procedure of <s>apūrva</s> should be understood everywhere. || MJaiNyC_2,1.8-10 ||

What was stated in the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s> by the two verses — 'There is only one word that conveys <s>apūrva</s>,' and that is the word '<s>yajeta</s>' whose meaning is <s>bhāvanā</s> ending in the verbal suffix — this is not established, because there is no means of knowledge for the existence of <s>apūrva</s>, and because by the root and the suffix in '<s>yajeta</s>,' the instrument and <s>bhāvanā</s> are [already] denoted. If it be objected that in the absence of <s>apūrva</s>, it is impossible for the sacrifice — which is perishable — to be a means for the future heaven — no, because that is established by the authority of scripture — when this is the position arrived at, we say: by the instrumental case in '<s>darśapūrṇamāsābhyām</s>,' the sacrifice's capacity as a means for heaven is at any rate established. As it is established, so must you too postulate it. In that case, is it postulated that the sacrifice persists until the result, or that it produces heaven even after perishing? Not the first — because the momentariness of the sacrifice is established by perception. Not the second — because the production of a son from a dead couple is not observed. Therefore, our postulation of <s>apūrva</s>, which is not contradicted, is better than your postulation, which is contradicted by other means of knowledge. If it be objected that even when <s>apūrva</s> is postulated, since <s>apūrva</s> alone would be the means for heaven, the scripture that the sacrifice is the means for heaven would be contradicted — no, because it is accepted that '<s>apūrva</s> is an intermediate operation of the sacrifice.' For the instrumentality of the axe does not cease when intermediate operations such as raising and striking exist. If the operation does not persist when the sacrifice that possessed it perishes, then let <s>apūrva</s> be some potency born of the sacrifice. Even with the intermediary of potency, the instrumentality of the sacrifice is not contradicted, because even when fire has heat as its intermediary, its burning capacity is accepted. Just as the heat produced by embers persists in water even when the embers are extinguished, so let the <s>apūrva</s> born of the sacrifice persist in the self (<s>ātman</s>) of the performer even when the sacrifice has perished. Therefore, <s>apūrva</s> exists. Its specific details should be understood from the procedure of sacrifice established by tradition. For the procedure has been shown by the earlier teachers as follows: 'First, by the result-sentence, the capacity of the act as a means to the result is understood — one should produce heaven through sacrifice. When the question arises: how can the result be produced by something perishable? — the answer is: by producing [it] in <s>apūrva</s>. When the question arises: how is [it] produced in <s>apūrva</s>? — [the answer is:] by the manner of performing the sacrifice.' And that <s>apūrva</s> in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> sacrifices is of many kinds: <s>phalāpūrva</s> (result-<s>apūrva</s>), <s>samudāyāpūrva</s> (aggregate-<s>apūrva</s>), <s>utpattyapūrva</s> (production-<s>apūrva</s>), and <s>aṅgāpūrva</s> (subsidiary-<s>apūrva</s>). That by which heaven is commenced is the result-<s>apūrva</s>. On the new-moon day there is one aggregate of three sacrifices, and on the full-moon day another; since these two, occurring at different times, cannot jointly commence the result-<s>apūrva</s>, two <s>apūrvas</s> born of the two aggregates must be postulated for its commencement. For the commencement of each of these two, since the three sacrifices within each aggregate occur at different moments and cannot form a simultaneous whole, three production-<s>apūrvas</s> born of the three sacrifices must be postulated. And since these cannot be accomplished without the contribution of subsidiaries, and since the subsidiaries occurring at multiple moments cannot form a simultaneous whole, subsidiary-<s>apūrvas</s> must be postulated. Therein, however, the distinction is as follows: those subsidiaries that contribute jointly — such as pounding and the like — are active in producing the production-<s>apūrva</s> by enhancing the very nature of the sacrifice through the channel of substance, deity, and preparatory rites.
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 2.1.11-12]
Here he states the teacher's opinion —
The sacrificial action, in a subtle form, resides in the atoms belonging to the self;

children.text: yāvatphalaṃ niyogākhyaṃ nāpūrvamiti cenna tat // MJaiNy_2,1.11 //

The subtlety of the action is devoid of a means of knowledge; but <s>niyoga</s>, through the <s>liṅ</s> suffix and the like,
is expressible as separate from the sacrifice; therefore there is an effect in [the form of] <s>apūrva</s>. // MJaiNy_2,1.12 //

Nor should the absence of a means of knowledge regarding <s>niyoga</s> be suspected,
because Vedic indicatory marks (<s>liṅga</s>) and the like express it.
Therefore, <s>apūrva</s> — which is distinct from the verbal root-meaning and is the means for the desired result that will occur at a future time — exists. || MJaiNyC_2,1.11-12 ||

What the teacher intends as <s>apūrva</s> called <s>niyoga</s> — that does not exist. Why? Because even without that [kind of] <s>apūrva</s>, the result is accomplished. Nor should it be said: how is the result accomplished when the sacrifice perishes? For the sacrificial action does not entirely perish; rather, being invisible in a subtle form, it resides in the atoms of the substances connected with the sacrifice — those that compose the heavenly body — or in the self (<s>ātman</s>) of the performer, and produces the result — this is the prior view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>). This is not proper,
(In the third [topic] — the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the division of ritual acts into subsidiary (<s>guṇa</s>) and principal (<s>pradhāna</s>), <s>sūtras</s> 6–8)
Those [ritual acts] are of two kinds: subsidiary and principal. / Jaim_2,1.6 /

children.text: yair dravyaṃ na cikīrṣyate tāni pradhānabhūtāni dravyasya guṇabhūtatvāt / Jaim_2,1.7 /
