children.translated_text: But those by which substance is intended to be produced should be understood as subsidiary, because substance is principal in those [acts]. / Jaim_2,1.8 /
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 2.1.13-14]
He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is there or is there not an <s>apūrva</s> to be produced by pounding (<s>avaghāta</s>) and the like?
Just as with '<s>yajati</s>' (one should sacrifice) and the like, it indeed exists; otherwise the sentence would be purposeless. // MJaiNy_2,1.13 //
But since a visible [result] — the husking [of grain] — is observed, there is no <s>apūrva</s>, because [the act] is subordinate to the substance;
the disparity with '<s>yajati</s>' and the like would be because the statement produces the <s>apūrva</s> of restriction (<s>niyama</s>). // MJaiNy_2,1.14 //

children.translated_text: But here, since by the accusative case ending in '<s>vrīhīn</s>' (rice grains) the primacy of the rice grains as the most desired [object] is understood, the pounding — being subordinate to the substance — would produce an enhancement in the substance alone, and does not generate <s>apūrva</s>.
Nor is there purposelessness of the injunction,

children.text: nakhanirbhedanādinā tuṣavimokasaṃbhave 'pi 'avaghātenaivāsau kartavyaḥ ' iti yo niyamastasya niyamasyāpūrvahetutvena vidheyatvāt |
children.translated_text: because even though husking is possible by breaking with fingernails and the like, the restriction that 'it should be done by pounding alone' — that restriction is to be enjoined on account of its being the cause of <s>apūrva</s>.
Therefore, there is no <s>apūrva</s> generated by pounding and the like. || MJaiNyC_2,1.13-14 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [sacrifices], it is heard: '<s>vrīhīn avahanti</s>' (one pounds the rice grains) and '<s>taṇḍulān pinaṣṭi</s>' (one grinds the rice). There, pounding and grinding are generators of <s>apūrva</s>, because they are enjoined verbal root-meanings, like the verbal root-meanings of '<s>yajati</s>' and the like. In the opposite case, the overriding argument in the form of the purposelessness of the injunctive sentence should be understood: since husking and pulverizing, having visible purposes, are established in the world, the injunction of pounding and grinding for those purposes would be purposeless. Therefore — when it is concluded that <s>apūrva</s> exists — we say: when a visible result is possible, <s>apūrva</s> should not be postulated. But the example of '<s>yajati</s>' and the like is dissimilar. For there, since the action is principal and substance is not predominant, the capacity of the action as a means for <s>apūrva</s> is appropriate.
Here he states the teacher's opinion —
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 2.1.15]
Having broken the second [alternative, i.e., the absence of <s>apūrva</s>], as in the case of <s>saktu</s> (barley flour), let the action be connected with <s>niyoga</s> (obligation);
it should not be thought [that it is connected] directly, because the visible [result] is accounted for here. // MJaiNy_2,1.15 //

tathā"vrīhibhiravahanti"iti vipariṇāmena pradhānabhūtā kriyā dravyavyavadhānamantareṇa sākṣādeva niyoge 'nvetavyeti cet |
maivam |

children.translated_text: Because of dissimilarity.

children.text: tatra"homena saktuṣu saṃskāro na bhavati"bhasmībhūtānāmanyatra viniyogāsaṃbhavāt , ityabhipretya saṃskārakarmatvaṃ parityaktam |
children.translated_text: There, in the case of '<s>homa</s>' (oblation) of flour, the ritual modification (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of being the object of the action was abandoned — because it was intended that 'no modification occurs in the flour through the oblation,' since it is impossible to employ elsewhere [substances that have been] reduced to ashes.
Here, however, the visible modification of husk-removal is applicable.
Because it is possible to employ those dehusked [grains] in the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (offering cake). || MJaiNyC_2,1.15 ||

In '<s>saktūñ juhoti</s>' (one offers the flour), setting aside the primacy of the substance and breaking the accusative case, a transposition to the instrumental case as '<s>saktubhir juhoti</s>' (one offers with the flour) will be stated for the sake of the primacy of the action. Similarly, by transposition of '<s>vrīhibhir avahanti</s>' (they thresh with the rice-grains), the action which is primary should be connected directly with the injunction without the intervention of the substance — if this be argued: Not so.

children.text: dharmamātre tu karma syād anirvṛtteḥ prayājavat / Jaim_2,1.9 /
children.translated_text: But in a matter pertaining to <s>dharma</s> alone, it would be an [independent] action, since it does not produce [a substance], like the <s>prayāja</s> (fore-offering). / Jaim_2,1.9 /
(In the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the subsidiary status of <s>saṃmārjana</s> [sweeping] and the like, <s>sūtras</s> 9-12)
Since the scriptural expression is the same, it would have the same property as the others. / Jaim_2,1.10 /
If [it be objected] that there is mention of a substance — / Jaim_2,1.11 /

children.text: na tadarthatvāl lokavat tasya ca śeṣabhūtatvāt / Jaim_2,1.12 /
children.translated_text: No, because [the substance] serves its purpose, as in worldly [usage], and because it [the substance] is subordinate. / Jaim_2,1.12 /

He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In '<s>saṃmārṣṭi strucaḥ</s>' (one sweeps the ladles) — is [the sweeping] a principal action (<s>pradhānakarma</s>),
or a subsidiary action (<s>guṇakarma</s>)? In the absence of a visible [result], it would be like the pounding (<s>avaghāta</s>). // MJaiNy_2,1.16 //

children.text: guṇatvaṃ nahi saṃbhāvyaṃ prādhānyaṃ tu prayājavat /

even by postulating an unseen [result], subsidiary status would be [established] through the accusative case. // MJaiNy_2,1.17 //

children.translated_text: And the most-desired-ness of the ladles is appropriate because they are the instruments of the sacrifice.
Therefore the ladles are the principal [objects].
This being so, the sweeping action would have subsidiary-action status, like the pounding.

children.text: yadi strukṣudṛṣṭo 'tiśayo na syāt, tarhyapūrve kalpanīyam || MJaiNyC_2,1.16-17 ||
children.translated_text: If there is no visible enhancement in the ladles, then an unseen one (<s>apūrva</s>) should be postulated. || MJaiNyC_2,1.16-17 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) sacrifices, the sweeping of the ladles (<s>juhū</s> and others) with <s>darbha</s> grass is prescribed: '<s>strucaḥ saṃmārṣṭi</s>' (one sweeps the ladles). There, the sweeping is a principal action (<s>pradhānakarma</s>). Why? Because it lacks the defining characteristics of a subsidiary action, and possesses the defining characteristics of a principal action. For the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the <s>sūtras</s>), having posited two classes of actions, formulated the definition of each in separate <s>sūtras</s>: '<s>tāni dvaidhaṃ guṇapradhānabhūtāni</s>' (these are of two kinds: subsidiary and principal), '<s>yais tu dravyaṃ cikīrṣyate, guṇas tatra pratīyeta, tasya dravyapradhānatvāt</s>' (those [actions] by which a substance is intended to be produced or modified — in those, subsidiary status is understood, because the substance is primary for them) [PMS 2.1.6-8], '<s>yais tu dravyaṃ na cikīrṣyate, tāni pradhānabhūtāni, dravyasya guṇabhūtatvāt</s>' (those [actions] by which no substance is intended to be produced — those are principal, because the substance is subordinate). Those actions by which a substance is intended to be produced or modified — in those, subsidiary status holds. Why? Because the substance is primary for that action. '<s>Dravyapradhāna</s>' is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound: 'that whose primary [object] is the substance.' In '<s>yūpaṃ takṣati</s>' (one carves the sacrificial post), '<s>āhavanīyam ādaghāti</s>' (one kindles the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire), and the like, the substance — the post, the fire, etc. — is intended to be produced. In '<s>vrīhīn avahanti</s>' (they thresh the rice-grains), '<s>taṇḍulān pinaṣṭi</s>' (one grinds the rice), and the like, the substance is intended to be modified. In the <s>prayāja</s> and similar [actions], the opposite being stated, principal-action status [holds]. This being so, just as through pounding a visible modification — husk-removal — is seen in the rice-grains, we do not perceive any such enhancement in the ladles through sweeping. Therefore, since subsidiary-action status is absent as in the case of pounding, principal-action status like the <s>prayāja</s> — having arrived at this position, we say: The accusative case in '<s>strucaḥ</s>' (the ladles) is employed in the object-sense (<s>karmakāraka</s>). And object-status occurs when there is most-desired-ness (<s>īpsitatama</s>). Because the designation of object (<s>karmasaṃjñā</s>) is ordained by [<s>Pāṇini</s>'s <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>kartur īpsitatamam karma</s>' (that which is most desired by the agent is the object) [Pā. 1.4.49].
(In the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the principality of <s>stotra</s> [chanting] and the like, <s>sūtras</s> 13-29)

children.text: stutaśastrayos tu saṃskāro yājyāvad devatābhidhānatvāt / Jaim_2,1.13 /
children.translated_text: But in the case of praise (<s>stuta</s>) and recitation (<s>śastra</s>), [they would be] a ritual modification, like the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse), because they express the deity. / Jaim_2,1.13 /

children.text: arthena tv apakṛṣyeta devatānām acodanārthasya guṇabhūtatvāt / Jaim_2,1.14 /
children.translated_text: But [the deity] would be subordinated by the [main] purpose, since what is not the object of injunction is subsidiary to the deities. / Jaim_2,1.14 /
Or, it may serve the purpose of the qualifying attribute, as in the case of the barren cow (<s>vaśā</s>). / Jaim_2,1.15 /
No, because [the deity] is inherently connected with the scripture. / Jaim_2,1.16 /
And because of the difference in designation. / Jaim_2,1.17 /
And the qualifying attribute would become purposeless. / Jaim_2,1.18 /
Similarly for the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse) and the <s>puroruc</s> (invitatory formula). / Jaim_2,1.19 /
In the case of the barren cow, because of the inherent connection with purpose. / Jaim_2,1.20 /
Or rather, it would be because of purposefulness in the context of 'where.' / Jaim_2,1.21 /
But not in those that are [directly] prescribed. / Jaim_2,1.22 /
It is seen [to be so]. / Jaim_2,1.23 /

children.text: api vā śrutisaṃyogāt prakaraṇe stautiśaṃsatī kriyotpāttiṃ vidadhyātām / Jaim_2,1.24 /
children.translated_text: Or rather, due to the connection with scripture, in the context, the [verbs] '<s>stauti</s>' (praises) and '<s>śaṃsati</s>' (recites) would enjoin the production of the action. / Jaim_2,1.24 /
And because of the separateness of the word. / Jaim_2,1.25 /
And that statement would become purposeless. / Jaim_2,1.26 /
And a different purpose is understood. / Jaim_2,1.27 /
And the expression [is] like that of an [independent] action. / Jaim_2,1.28 /
And the production of the result [is understood]. / Jaim_2,1.29 /
START MJaiNy 2,1.18-19
He composes the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In '<s>praugaṃ śaṃsati</s>' (one recites the <s>prauga</s>) and the like, is it subsidiary or principal?
The recollection of the deity is visible [as the result]; therefore the <s>stotra</s> (chanting) and <s>śastra</s> (recitation) are subsidiary. // MJaiNy_2,1.18 //
If the roots '<s>stu</s>' (to praise) and '<s>śaṃs</s>' (to recite) have the meaning of [mere] recollection, the scriptural meaning [of the roots] would be overridden;
therefore, even by accepting an unseen [result], principality is held [to be correct] in accordance with the scripture. // MJaiNy_2,1.19 //

kutaḥ |

ṣaṭhyamāneṣu mantreṣvanusmaraṇena devatā saṃskriyata iti prāpte --
brūmaḥ- stotavyāyā devatāyāḥ stāvakairguṇaiḥ saṃbandhakīrtanaṃ stautiśaṃsatidhātvorvācyor'thaḥ |
yadi mantravākyāni guṇasaṃbandhābhidhānaparāṇi , tadā dhātvormukhyārthalābhācchratiranugṛhītā bhaviṣyati |
yadā tu guṇadvāreṇānusmaraṇīyadevatāsvarūpa prakāśanaparāṇi mantravākyāni syuḥ, tadā dhātvormukhyor'tho na syāt |
loke hi ' devadattaścaturvedābhijñaḥ ' ityukte stutiḥ pratīyate |
tasya vākyasya guṇasaṃbandhaparatvābhāvāt |
yadā tu devadattarūpaparatā ' yaścaturvedī tamānaya, ityādau, tatra na stutipratītiḥ |
tasya caturvedasaṃbandhadvāreṇa devadattasvarūpopalakṣaṇaparatvena guṇasaṃbandhaparatvābhāvāt |
tataśca - ' ājyairdevaṃ prakāśayet , ' pṛṣṭairdevaṃ prakāśayet, ityevaṃ vidhyarthaparyavasānāddhātvormukhyārtho bādhyeta |
children.translated_text: Therefore — since [the meaning] ultimately resolves into the injunctive form '<s>ājyair devaṃ prakāśayet</s>' (one should reveal the deity through the <s>ājya</s> [stotras]), '<s>pṛṣṭair devaṃ prakāśayet</s>' (one should reveal the deity through the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> [stotras]) — the primary meaning of the verbal roots would be overridden.
Therefore, to avoid overriding the scriptural meaning of the verbal roots, the principal-action status of <s>stotra</s> and <s>śastra</s> must be accepted.
If it be objected that there is no visible purpose for that —
then let there be an unseen one (<s>apūrva</s>). || MJaiNyC_2,1.18-19 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice, it is heard: '<s>praugaṃ śaṃsati</s>' (one recites the <s>prauga</s>), '<s>niṣkevalyaṃ śaṃsati</s>' (one recites the <s>niṣkevalya</s>), '<s>ājyaiḥ stuvate</s>' (one chants with the <s>ājya</s> [stotras]), '<s>pṛṣṭaiḥ stuvate</s>' (one chants with the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> [stotras]). The words '<s>prauga</s>' and '<s>niṣkevalya</s>' are names of specific recitations (<s>śastra</s>). The words '<s>ājya</s>' and '<s>pṛṣṭha</s>' have already been explained. A praise (<s>stuti</s>) accomplished through unsung <s>mantras</s> is a <s>śastra</s> (recitation). A praise accomplished through sung <s>mantras</s> is a <s>stotra</s> (chanting). The subsidiary-action status of those — the praise and recitation — is appropriate. Why? Because a visible result is obtained, as in the case of husk-removal. When the <s>mantras</s> are recited, the deity is ritually enhanced through recollection — having arrived at this position, we say: The meaning intended by the two verbal roots '<s>stauti</s>' (praises) and '<s>śaṃsati</s>' (recites) is the proclamation of the connection of praiseworthy qualities with the deity to be praised. If the <s>mantra</s>-sentences are aimed at proclaiming the connection of qualifying attributes, then the primary meaning of the verbal roots would be obtained, and the scripture would be supported. But when the <s>mantra</s>-sentences are aimed at revealing the essential nature of the deity to be recollected through the medium of qualifying attributes, then the primary meaning of the verbal roots would not hold. For in common usage, when one says '<s>Devadatta</s> is learned in the four Vedas,' praise is understood — because that sentence is not aimed at proclaiming the connection of qualifying attributes. But when the aim is to identify the person of <s>Devadatta</s>, as in 'bring the one who knows the four Vedas' and so on, there is no apprehension of praise — because, through the medium of the connection with the four Vedas, [the sentence] is aimed at identifying the essential nature of <s>Devadatta</s>, and thus is not aimed at proclaiming the connection of qualifying attributes.
(In the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the non-injunctive nature of <s>mantras</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 30-31)
The injunction and the <s>mantra</s> would have a single purpose, since they have a single designation. / Jaim_2,1.30 /

children.text: api vā prayogasāmarthyān mantro 'bhidhānavācī syāt / Jaim_2,1.31 /
children.translated_text: Or rather, by the capacity of [ritual] application, the <s>mantra</s> would be expressive of designation (<s>abhidhāna</s>). / Jaim_2,1.31 /
START MJaiNy 2,1.20-21
He composes the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'<s>Devāṃś ca yābhir yajate</s>' (and the gods whom one worships with which [cows]) — is the finite verb within the <s>mantra</s>
injunctive or not? Since it is equal [in form] to another [injunctive verb], it is injunctive. // MJaiNy_2,1.20 //

The injunctive power of the [verbal suffix beginning with] '<s>yat</s>' and the like is exhausted; therefore, the finite verb is not an injunction — [and from this follows] the threefold [classification]:,
the finite verb, the designation (<s>abhidhāna</s>), and the principal and subsidiary actions. // MJaiNy_2,1.21 //

maivam |

' barhirdevasadanaṃ dāmi ' ityuttamapurūmaḥ |

children.translated_text: '<s>Agnīd agnīn vihara</s>' (O <s>Agnīdh</s>, spread the fires) — this is [an example of] invocation.
Similarly in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> too, '<s>yasyobhayaṃ havirārtim ārchat</s>' (whose offering reached both) should be cited as an example.

children.text: tasmāt - ' ākhyātasya pradhānakarmavidhāyatvaṃ, guṇavidhāyakatvaṃ vā ' ityevaṃ dvāveva prakārau na bhavataḥ, kiṃtu - ' abhidhāyakatvam ' ityapyasti tṛtīyaḥ prakāraḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore — the two alternatives 'the finite verb is an injunction of a principal action or of a subsidiary action' do not exhaust the possibilities; rather, there is also a third alternative: 'designation' (<s>abhidhāna</s>).
Therefore, the finite verb occurring in a <s>mantra</s> is not injunctive. || MJaiNyC_2,1.20-21 ||

This <s>mantra</s> is prescribed: '<s>devāṃś ca yābhir yajate dadāti ca jyog it tābhiḥ sacate gopatiḥ saha</s>' (the lord of cattle who worships the gods with which [cows] and gives [them] to Brahmins — with those very ones he dwells together for a long time). The meaning is: The sacrificer, the lord of cattle, who worships the gods with which cows and gives which cows to Brahmins — with those very ones he dwells together for a long time in the next world. Therein, just as the finite verb occurring in a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage is injunctive of either a principal or subsidiary action, so too the finite verb occurring in a <s>mantra</s> — if this be argued: Not so. Because the injunctive power is exhausted by the [relative pronoun] '<s>yat</s>' and the like. When the [relative pronoun] '<s>yat</s>' is present, the re-statement (<s>anuvādakatva</s>) of that sentence is understood, not its injunctive nature. The expression 'and the like' after '<s>yat</s>' includes first person, invocation (<s>āmantraṇa</s>), and so on. '<s>Barhir devasadanaṃ dāmi</s>' (I spread the <s>barhis</s>, the seat of the gods) — this is [an example of] the first person.
(In the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the definition of <s>mantra</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
In those [passages] that are accompanied by injunctions, [the portions that are not injunctions bear] the designation '<s>mantra</s>.' / Jaim_2,1.32 /
START MJaiNy 2,1.22-23
He composes the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: ahe budhiṇya mantraṃ ma iti mantrasya lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ahe budhiṇya, mantraṃ me gopāya</s>' (O <s>Ahibudhnya</s>, protect my <s>mantra</s>) — does the <s>mantra</s> have a defining characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>)?
It either does not have one, or if it does — [but] it does not, since faults such as under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>) and the like cannot be prevented. // MJaiNy_2,1.22 //
The designation (<s>samākhyāna</s>) by the ritual experts (<s>yājñikas</s>) is the faultless defining characteristic;
they apply the word '<s>mantra</s>' to [passages that serve as] reminders of performance and the like. // MJaiNy_2,1.23 //

children.translated_text: Therefore — the designation '<s>mantra</s>' by the experts is the defining characteristic. || MJaiNyC_2,1.22-23 ||

In the <s>ādhāna</s> (fire-establishment ritual), this is prescribed: '<s>ahe budhiṇya mantraṃ me gopāya</s>' (O <s>Ahibudhnya</s>, protect my <s>mantra</s>). Therein, the <s>mantra</s> has no defining characteristic, since under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>) and over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) cannot be prevented. If one says 'a <s>mantra</s> is that which expresses a purpose that has been enjoined,' then there is under-extension in the case of the <s>mantra</s> '<s>vasantāya kapiñjalān ālabheta</s>' (one should offer francolins to Spring), because that <s>mantra</s> has the form of an injunction. If one says 'a <s>mantra</s> is that which causes reflection (<s>manana</s>),' then there is over-extension to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [passages]. Similarly, definitions such as 'a <s>mantra</s> is that which ends in a sword-word (<s>asipadānta</s>),' 'a <s>mantra</s> is that which ends in the first person,' and the like — each suffers from mutual under-extension — if this be argued: Not so. Because the designation (<s>samākhyāna</s>) by the ritual experts is a faultless defining characteristic. And that designation indicates the <s>mantra</s>-hood of passages that serve as reminders of performance and the like. '<s>Uru prathasva</s>' (spread wide) and the like are reminders of performance. '<s>Agnim īle purohitam</s>' (I praise <s>Agni</s>, the foremost priest) and the like are in the form of praise. '<s>Iṣe tvā</s>' (for nourishment) and the like are those ending in '<s>tvā</s>.' '<s>Agna ā yāhi vītaye</s>' (O <s>Agni</s>, come for the offering) and the like are those accompanied by invocation. '<s>Agnīd agnīn vihara</s>' (O <s>Agnīdh</s>, spread the fires) and the like are in the form of commands (<s>praiṣa</s>). '<s>Adhaḥ svid āsīd upari svid āsīt</s>' (was it below, or was it above?) and the like are in the form of inquiry. '<s>Ambe ambike ambālike na mā nayati kaścana</s>' (O <s>Ambā</s>, <s>Ambikā</s>, <s>Ambālikā</s>, no one leads me) and the like are in the form of lamentation. '<s>Pṛcchāmi tvā paramantaṃ pṛthivyāḥ</s>' (I ask you about the farthest end of the earth) and the like are in the form of questions. '<s>Vedim āhuḥ paramantaṃ pṛthivyāḥ</s>' (they call the <s>vedi</s> the farthest end of the earth) and the like are in the form of answers. Other examples should also be cited. Among such extremely diverse [passages], apart from the designation [by experts], there is no other common property that could serve as a defining characteristic. And the usefulness of a defining characteristic has been shown by the earlier teachers: 'Even the <s>ṛṣis</s> cannot reach the end of objects individually; but the wise reach the end of those established by a defining characteristic.'
(In the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the definition of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
The word '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' [applies to] the remainder. / Jaim_2,1.33 /
START MJaiNy 2,1.24-25
He composes the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
There is no defining characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in this [passage] '<s>etad brāhmaṇam</s>' — or is there?
The portions of the Veda described as <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — because of the absence of a [clear] postulation [distinguishing them]. // MJaiNy_2,1.24 //

children.text: mantraśca brāhmaṇaṃ ceti dvau bhāgau tena mantrataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Mantra</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — these are the two portions; therefore, what is other than <s>mantra</s>
is <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — this would be the defining characteristic of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. // MJaiNy_2,1.25 //

children.translated_text: Therefore — 'there is no defining characteristic of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' — having arrived at this position,

children.text: brūmaḥ- ' mantrabrāhmaṇarūpau dvāveva vedabhāgau ' ityaṅgīkārānmantralakṣaṇasya pūrvamabhihitatvāt ' avaśiṣṭo vedabhāgo brāhmaṇam ' ityetallakṣaṇaṃ bhavati -- iti || MJaiNyC_2,1.24-25 ||
children.translated_text: we say: Since it is accepted that there are only two portions of the Veda — <s>mantra</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — and since the defining characteristic of <s>mantra</s> has been stated earlier, 'the remaining portion of the Veda is <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' — this becomes the definition. || MJaiNyC_2,1.24-25 ||

In the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) sacrifices, this is recited: '<s>etad brāhmaṇāny eva pañca havīṃṣi</s>' (these five oblations are indeed <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-portions). Therein, there is no defining characteristic of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. Why? Because since the number of Vedic portions cannot be determined, it is impossible to refine the definition to avoid under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>) and over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) in <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> portions and other portions. The previously mentioned <s>mantra</s> portion is one. And certain other portions have been collected and exemplified by the ancients: 'Reason (<s>hetu</s>), etymology (<s>nirvacana</s>), censure (<s>nindā</s>), praise (<s>praśaṃsā</s>), doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), injunction (<s>vidhi</s>), others' action (<s>parakṛti</s>), ancient precedent (<s>purākalpa</s>), and specification-postulation (<s>vyavadhāraṇakalpanā</s>).' '<s>tena hi annaṃ kriyate</s>' (for by it food is made) — this is reason. '<s>tad dadhaṇe dadhitvam</s>' (that is the curds-nature of curds) — this is etymology. '<s>amādhyā vai māṣāḥ</s>' (black beans are indeed unholy) — this is censure. '<s>vāyur vai kṣepiṣṭhā devatā</s>' (Vāyu is indeed the swiftest deity) — this is praise. '<s>tad vyacikitsaj juhavāni mā hauṣam</s>' (he was in doubt: shall I offer or shall I not?) — this is doubt. '<s>yajamānena saṃmitā audumbarī bhavati</s>' (the <s>Audumbarī</s> post should be the same height as the sacrificer) — this is injunction. '<s>bhāṣān eva mahyaṃ pacata</s>' (cook only the allotted portions for me) — this is others' action. '<s>purā brāhmaṇā abhaiṣuḥ</s>' (formerly the Brahmins were afraid) — this is ancient precedent. '<s>yāvato 'śvān pratigṛhṇīyāt tāvato vāruṇāṃś catuṣkapālan nirvaped</s>' (for as many horses as one receives, one should offer that many four-cup cakes to <s>Varuṇa</s>) — this is specification-postulation. Other examples may also be cited. But the definition 'one of these — reason and the like — is <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' does not hold, because reason and the like are also found in <s>mantras</s>. For example: '<s>indavo vām uśanti hi</s>' (the <s>Soma</s> drops indeed desire you) — this is reason. '<s>udāniṣur mahīr iti tasmād udakam ucyate</s>' (the great [waters] rose up, therefore it is called water) — this is etymology. '<s>mogham annaṃ vindate apracetāḥ</s>' (the fool obtains food in vain) — this is censure. '<s>agnir mūrdhā divaḥ kakut patiḥ</s>' (<s>Agni</s> is the head, the peak of heaven, the lord) — this is praise. '<s>adhaḥ svid āsīd upari svid āsīt</s>' (was it below or was it above?) — this is doubt. '<s>kapiñjalān ālabheta</s>' (one should sacrifice partridges) — this is injunction. '<s>sahasram anyutaṃ dadat</s>' (giving thousands and tens of thousands) — this is others' action. '<s>yajñena yajñam ayajanta devāḥ</s>' (the gods worshipped the sacrifice by means of sacrifice) — this is ancient precedent. If it be said that 'a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is characterized by the abundance of the word <s>iti</s>' — no. Because there is over-extension to the <s>mantra</s> to be chanted by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [priest]: '<s>ity adadā ity ayajathā ity apaca iti brāhmaṇo gāyet</s>' (the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should chant: 'thus he gave, thus he sacrificed, thus he cooked'). If it be said that 'a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is that which is connected by the phrase <s>iti āha</s> (thus he said)' — no. Because of over-extension to these two <s>mantras</s>: '<s>rājā cid yaṃ bhagaṃ bhakṣīty āha</s>' (even a king says, 'let me partake of that fortune') and '<s>yo vā rakṣāḥ śucir asmīty āha</s>' (whoever says to the demons, 'I am pure'). If it be said that 'a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has the form of a narrative' —
(In the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the <s>mantra</s>-status of substituted forms (<s>ūha</s>) and the like, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
In those [texts] that are not recited [in the <s>saṃhitā</s>], there is non-<s>mantra</s>-status; but in those that are recited, there is classification. / Jaim_2,1.34 /

He composes the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Do the substituted forms (<s>ūha</s>), the lineage recitations (<s>pravara</s>), and the names possess <s>mantra</s>-status, or not?
They are <s>mantras</s>, due to forming a single sentence with [a <s>mantra</s>]; they are not, due to lacking the defining characteristic [of <s>mantras</s>]. // MJaiNy_2,1.26 //

Because the defining characteristic of a <s>mantra</s>, which consists in being well-known among sacrificial specialists (<s>yājñikaprasiddhi</s>), is absent in these.
For the reciters do not recite the substituted forms (<s>ūha</s>) and the like in the <s>mantra</s> section [of the Veda].
Therefore — there is no <s>mantra</s>-status [for them]. || MJaiNyC_2,1.26 ||

In '<s>agnaye juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi</s>' (I offer what is pleasing to <s>Agni</s>), for the solar ritual, the substitution (<s>ūha</s>) '<s>sūryāya juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi</s>' (I offer what is pleasing to <s>Sūrya</s>) — this insertion of a different word is called <s>ūha</s>. As a completion of the <s>mantra</s> '<s>adīkṣiṣṭāyaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ</s>' (this Brahmin has been initiated), at the time of application they recite the particular name and lineage (<s>pravara</s>) of the Brahmin thus: '<s>asau devadatto 'muṣya putro 'muṣya pautro 'muṣya naptā, amuṣyāḥ putro 'muṣyāḥ pautro 'muṣyā naptā</s>' (this <s>Devadatta</s>, son of so-and-so, grandson of so-and-so, great-grandson of so-and-so, son of such-and-such [mother], grandson of such-and-such, great-granddaughter of such-and-such). And: '<s>āṅgirasa-bārhaspatya-bhāradvāja-gotraḥ</s>' (of the <s>Āṅgirasa</s>-<s>Bārhaspatya</s>-<s>Bhāradvāja</s> lineage). These substituted forms, lineage recitations, and names possess <s>mantra</s>-status. Why? Because they form a single sentence (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) with a <s>mantra</s> — if so it is argued,
(In the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the defining characteristic of <s>Ṛk</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
Among those [<s>mantras</s>], <s>Ṛk</s> is that in which there is an arrangement of metrical feet (<s>pāda</s>) governed by the meaning. / Jaim_2,1.35 /
(In the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the defining characteristic of <s>Sāman</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
The designation [applies] to those [<s>mantras</s> that are] in songs (<s>gīti</s>). / Jaim_2,1.36 /
(In the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the defining characteristic of <s>Yajus</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
The remaining words are <s>Yajus</s>. / Jaim_2,1.37 /
START MJaiNy 2,1.27
He composes the tenth, eleventh, and twelfth <s>adhikaraṇas</s> —
There is no defining characteristic of <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Yajus</s> — because of intermixture; thus when doubt arises,
[we say:] metrical feet (<s>pāda</s>), song (<s>gīti</s>), and continuous recitation (<s>praśliṣṭapāṭha</s>) — thus there is no intermixture. // MJaiNy_2,1.27 //

children.translated_text: Because the defining characteristics based on metrical feet (<s>pāda</s>) and the like are unmixed.
<s>Mantras</s> that are endowed with metrical feet (<s>pāda</s>) and meaning, and that are bound by meter (<s>vṛtta</s>), are <s>Ṛks</s>.
<s>Mantras</s> that have the form of song (<s>gīti</s>) are <s>Sāmans</s>.

children.text: vṛttagītivarjitatvena praśliṣṭapaṭhitā mantrā yajūṃṣi ' ityukte na kvāpi saṃkaraḥ || MJaiNyC_2,1.27 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mantras</s> that are recited in continuous form (<s>praśliṣṭa</s>), being devoid of meter and song, are <s>Yajus</s> formulas — when stated thus, there is no intermixture anywhere. || MJaiNyC_2,1.27 ||

This is recited: '<s>ahe budhṇya mantraṃ me gopāya yam ṛṣayas traividā viduḥ | ṛcaḥ sāmāni yajūṃṣi</s>' (O <s>Ahi Budhnya</s>, protect my <s>mantra</s> which the sages of threefold knowledge know — the <s>Ṛks</s>, <s>Sāmans</s>, and <s>Yajus</s> formulas). '<s>Trīn vedān vidanti</s>' (they know three Vedas) — hence they are <s>trividaḥ</s> (of threefold knowledge); those connected with the threefold are <s>traividāḥ</s>. And that <s>mantra</s>-portion which they declare to be threefold in the form of <s>Ṛk</s> and the like — protect that. Such is the construal. Therein, there is no established defining characteristic of the three — <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Yajus</s>. Why? Because intermixture (<s>sāṃkarya</s>) is difficult to avoid. For the definition to be given is: 'a <s>mantra</s> read in the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and the like, as known to the teachers, is an <s>Ṛk</s> and the like.' But this is intermixed. [For example,] the <s>mantra</s> '<s>devo vaḥ savitā utpūnātv acchidreṇa pavitreṇa vasoḥ sūryasya raśmibhiḥ</s>' (may god <s>Savitṛ</s> purify you with the faultless filter, with the rays of <s>Sūrya</s>) — this <s>mantra</s> is read among the <s>Yajus</s> formulas that are accepted as being in the <s>Yajurveda</s>. But it does not have <s>Yajus</s>-status, because in its <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, it is referred to as '<s>sāvitry arcā</s>' (with the <s>Sāvitrī</s> <s>Ṛk</s>), indicating its <s>Ṛk</s>-status. After declaring '<s>etat sāma gāyann āste</s>' (he sits chanting this <s>Sāman</s>), a certain <s>Sāman</s> is chanted in the <s>Yajurveda</s>. '<s>akṣitam asi</s>' (you are imperishable), '<s>acyutam asi</s>' (you are unfallen), '<s>prāṇasaṃśitam asi</s>' (you are sharpened by breath) — these three <s>Yajus</s> formulas are recited in the <s>Sāmaveda</s>. Similarly, the <s>Ṛk</s> verses that serve as the textual basis for the <s>Sāmans</s> being sung are recited in the <s>Sāmaveda</s>. Therefore — there is no defining characteristic — if so it is argued, no.
(In the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the <s>Yajus</s>-status of <s>Nigadas</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 38–45)

children.text: brūmaḥ- ' vahirbrāhmaṇā bhojyantām ' ' piravrājakāstvantaḥ ' ityatra satyeva parivrājakānāṃ brāhmaṇye pūjānimitto viśeṣo yathā tathā nigadānāṃ yajurlakṣaṇopetatvena yajuṣāmeva satāṃ parapratyāyananimittamuccaistvadharmaḥ |
children.translated_text: we say: Just as in the case '<s>bahir brāhmaṇā bhojyantām</s>' (let the Brahmins be fed outside) and '<s>parivrājakās tv antaḥ</s>' (but the wandering ascetics inside) — where the wandering ascetics, though being Brahmins, receive special honor — so too, the <s>Nigadas</s>, though possessing the defining characteristic of <s>Yajus</s> and being <s>Yajus</s> formulas, have the characteristic of loud recitation (<s>uccaistva</s>) on account of the purpose of communicating to others.
Therefore the threefold classification of <s>mantras</s> is well-established. || MJaiNyC_2,1.28-29 ||

The <s>Nigadas</s> are recited [in scripture] as: '<s>prokṣaṇīr āsādaya</s>' (arrange the sprinkling waters), '<s>idhmaṃ barhir upasādaya</s>' (place the fuel and the sacred grass), '<s>agnīd agnīn vihara</s>' (O fire-kindler, spread the fires), '<s>barhiḥ stṛṇīhi</s>' (strew the sacred grass), '<s>indra āgaccha</s>' (come, O <s>Indra</s>), '<s>hariva āgaccha</s>' (come, O lord of bay horses), and so on. <s>Mantras</s> meant for communicating [instructions] to others are called <s>Nigada</s>. These are outside the three previously mentioned categories — <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> — and constitute a fourth type. Why? Because the defining characteristics of <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s> — namely metrical feet (<s>pāda</s>) and song (<s>gīti</s>) — are absent. And even though the defining characteristic of <s>Yajus</s> — continuous recitation (<s>praśliṣṭapāṭha</s>) — is present, inclusion within <s>Yajus</s> is not appropriate because of the difference in characteristic.
(In the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the defining characteristic of sentence-unity (<s>ekavākyatva</s>), the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

' yadvibhāge sākāṅkṣamavibhāge caikārtham, tadekaṃ vākyam ' iti prayojakasya boddhuṃ śakyatvāt |
'vibhāge sākāṅkṣam ' ityukte 'tivyāptiḥ syāt |
"syonaṃ te sadanaṃ kṛṇomi ghṛtasya dhārayā susevaṃ kalpayāmi, tasminsīdāmṛte pratitiṭha vrīhīṇāṃ medha sumanasyamānaḥ"ityatra 'tasmin' - ityādipadasamūhasya vibhāge sati prakṛtavācitacchabdārthanirṇayāya pūrvapadasamūhasākāṅkatvamasti, atastadvyavacchettum 'ekārtham ' ityucyate |
nahi tatraikārthatvamasti |
pūrvasamūhasya sadanakaraṇamarthaḥ, uttarasamūhasya puroḍāśapratiṣṭhāpanam |
syonaṃ samīcīnam |
susevaṃ suṣṭhu sevituṃ yogyam |
medha sārabhūtapuroḍāśetyarthaḥ |
atra dvayoḥ samṛhayorvākyadvayamubhayavādisiddham |
tat ' ekārtham ' ityanena vyāvartyate |
' ekārtham ' ityukte 'tivyāptiḥ syāt |

"bhago vāṃ vibhajatu, pūṣā vāṃ vibhajatu"ityanayorvibhajanamantratvena saṃmatayoḥ padasamūbayostātparyaviṣayasya dravyavibhāgarūpasyārthasyaikatvāt , tadravyavacchettuṃ ' vibhāge sākāṅkṣam ' ityuktam |
children.translated_text: In the two [sentences] '<s>bhago vāṃ vibhajatu, pūṣā vāṃ vibhajatu</s>' (may <s>Bhaga</s> divide for you two, may <s>Pūṣan</s> divide for you two) — these two word-groups, accepted as being distribution-<s>mantras</s>, have unity of meaning because the meaning — the division of substances — is the same. To exclude this [false case], '<s>vibhāge sākāṅkṣam</s>' (expectancy upon separation) is stated.

children.text: prakṛte tu ' agnaye juṣṭam ' ityādisamūhe pṛthakkṛte pūrvo ' devasya tvā 'iti samūhaḥ sākāṅkṣo bhavati |
children.translated_text: But in the present case, when the group '<s>agnaye juṣṭam</s>' (pleasing to <s>Agni</s>) and so on is separated out, the preceding group '<s>devasya tvā</s>' (of the god, you) has expectancy [for completion].
And when unified, the whole has a single meaning — namely, the [act of] offering (<s>nirvāpa</s>).
By this determination of sentence-unity, the end-point of a <s>Yajus</s> [formula] of indeterminate length can be ascertained. || MJaiNyC_2,1.30-31 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) sacrifices, it is recited: '<s>devasya tvā savituḥ prasave, aśvinor bāhubhyām, pūṣṇo hastābhyām, agnaye juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi</s>' (at the impulse of god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I offer what is pleasing to <s>Agni</s>). Therein, the sentences could well be distinct. Why? Because of the difficulty of understanding the factor that determines unity. If it be said that unity of meaning is the cause of sentence-unity — no. Because of over-extension to a single word. If [it be said that] a sentence is a collection of words, and since many collections are possible here, there would be sentence-division — that is not correct. Because the cause [of unity] can be understood as: 'that which, upon separation, has expectancy (<s>sākāṅkṣa</s>), and which, when unseparated, has unity of meaning (<s>ekārtha</s>) — that is a single sentence.' If merely '<s>vibhāge sākāṅkṣam</s>' (expectancy upon separation) is stated, there would be over-extension. In '<s>syonaṃ te sadanaṃ kṛṇomi ghṛtasya dhārayā susevaṃ kalpayāmi; tasmin sīdā amṛte pratitiṣṭha vrīhīṇāṃ medha sumanasyamānaḥ</s>' (I make your seat pleasant, I prepare it well with a stream of ghee; sit down in it, be established in immortality, O essence of rice, rejoicing) — here, when the word-group '<s>tasmin</s>' and so on is separated, there is expectancy toward the preceding word-group for determining the referent of the pronoun '<s>tat</s>' (that) in the current sentence. To exclude this [false case of expectancy], '<s>ekārtham</s>' (having unity of meaning) is stated. For there is no unity of meaning here — the meaning of the first group is the making of a seat, and the meaning of the latter group is the establishment of the offering cake (<s>puroḍāśa</s>). '<s>Syonam</s>' means proper or comfortable. '<s>Susevam</s>' means well fit to be enjoyed. '<s>Medha</s>' means the essential offering cake. Here, the two groups being distinct sentences is accepted by both sides. That is excluded by '<s>ekārtham</s>' (unity of meaning). If merely '<s>ekārtham</s>' is stated, there would be over-extension.
(In the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on sentence-division, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
When [the component parts] are equal, there would be sentence-division. / Jaim_2,1.47 /
START MJaiNy 2,1.32-33
He composes the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: iṣe tvādirmantra eko bhinno vaikaḥ kriyāpade /
children.translated_text: Is '<s>iṣe tvā</s>' (for food, you) and the like a single <s>mantra</s>, or is it split, being one for each ritual action?
Since it does not remind one of a performable meaning, there is one [<s>mantra</s>], because of the postulation of a single unseen [merit]. // MJaiNy_2,1.32 //
These two are assigned to the [two] ritual actions of cutting and wiping;
since the verbal action-word is to be supplied, the <s>mantras</s> are different because the meanings are different. // MJaiNy_2,1.33 //

children.text:
"iṣe tvorje tvā"iti śrūyate |
so 'yaṃ padasamudāya eko mantraḥ |
kutaḥ |
asya mantrasyādṛṣṭatve tvekasyaivādṛṣṭasya kalpane lāghavāt |
na ca"uru prathasva"ityādimantravadanuṣṭheyārthasmārakatvaṃ saṃbhavati |
kriyāpadābhāvena tadarthapratītyabhāvāt -- iti prāpte, brūmaḥ- ' iṣe tveti cchinatti, ūrje tvetyanumārṣṭi ' iti palāśaśākhāyāśchedanamārjanayoretau viniyuktau |
children.translated_text: Because in the absence of a verb (<s>kriyāpada</s>), there is no cognition of its meaning — having arrived at this position, we say: '<s>iṣe tvā iti chinatti, ūrje tvā iti anumārṣṭi</s>' (with '<s>iṣe tvā</s>' he cuts, with '<s>ūrje tvā</s>' he wipes) — these two are assigned to the cutting and wiping of the <s>palāśa</s> (sacred fig) branch.

Therefore, when the verb '<s>chinnadmi</s>' (I cut) is supplied in accordance with that [assignment], since the <s>mantra</s> reminds one of the performable meaning, by the difference of meaning and hence the splitting of the sentence, there is a difference of <s>yajus</s>-<s>mantras</s>.

children.text: iṣyamāṇāyānnāya bhoḥ palāśaśākhe tvā chinadmi ' ' ūrje rasāya balāya vā tvāmanumārjmi ' ityarthabhedaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'For the sake of desired food, O <s>palāśa</s> branch, I cut you' — 'For the sake of vigor, sap, and strength, I wipe you' — this is the difference of meaning.

children.text: evam"āyuryajñena kalpatām" "prāṇo yajñena kalpatām"ityādau kḷptisāmānyarūpasyārthasyaikatve 'pyāyurādibhirbhinnatvādarthabhedavākya bhedayoḥ spaṣṭatvāt , ' kḷptīrvācayati ' iti kḷptibahutvasya coditatvācca yajurbhedo draṣṭavyaḥ || MJaiNyC_2,1.32-33 ||
children.translated_text: Similarly, in '<s>āyur yajñena kalpatām</s>' (may life be accomplished by the sacrifice), '<s>prāṇo yajñena kalpatām</s>' (may breath be accomplished by the sacrifice), and the like, even though the meaning in the general form of accomplishment (<s>kḷpti</s>) is one, since [the sentences] differ through [the words] '<s>āyus</s>' (life) and the like, the splitting of meaning and sentence is clear; and since the plurality of accomplishments is enjoined by '<s>kḷptīr vācayati</s>' (he recites the accomplishments), a difference of <s>yajus</s>-<s>mantras</s> should be recognized. || MJaiNyC_2,1.32-33 ||

It is heard: '<s>iṣe tvorje tvā</s>' (for food, you; for vigor, you).
This entire collection of words is a single <s>mantra</s>.
Why?
Because if this <s>mantra</s> has an unseen [purpose], parsimony favors the postulation of just one unseen [merit].
Nor is it possible for it to remind one of a performable meaning, as do <s>mantras</s> like '<s>uru prathasva</s>' (expand widely) and the like.
(In the sixteenth (and seventeenth) <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the topic of <s>anuṣaṅga</s> (carryover), the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
<s>Anuṣaṅga</s> (carryover) is the completion of the sentence for all [mantras], because they are equally related. / Jaim_2,1.48 /
START MJaiNy 2,1.34-35
He composes the sixteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In '<s>yā te agne rajeti</s>' (O <s>Agni</s>, that of yours which...) — is what is needed a supply [from ordinary usage] (<s>adhyāhāra</s>), or a carryover (<s>anuṣañjana</s>)?
Since '<s>tanūḥ</s>' (body) is a complement of another [<s>mantra</s>], the supply here is from ordinary [language]. // MJaiNy_2,1.34 //
The expectancy of a Vedic [passage] should be fulfilled by a Vedic [complement] — therefore [it is] carryover (<s>anuṣañjana</s>);

children.text: anyaśeṣo 'pir buddhastho laukikastu na tādṛśaḥ // MJaiNy_2,1.35 //
children.translated_text: even though the complement of another [<s>mantra</s>] is retained in memory, ordinary [supply] is not like that. // MJaiNy_2,1.35 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome upasaddhomeṣvevamāmnāyate --
"yā te agne 'yāśayā tanūrvarṣiṣṭhā gahvareṣṭhā |
ugraṃ vaco apāvadhītveṣaṃ vaco apāvadhītsvāhā |
yā te agne rajāśayā, yā te agne harāśayā"iti |
ayamarthaḥ- ' ayasā rajatena hiraṇye na ca nirmitā agnestistrastanavaḥ, tāsvādyā yeyamuktā tanuḥ sātiśayena vṛddhaṃ, gahvare tīkṣṇe dravye lohe 'vasthitā tayā tanvā kṣutpipāse upapātakam, vīrahatyādi mahāpatakaṃ ca hatavānasmi ' iti |
tathā ca brāhmaṇam,"yadugraṃ vaco apāvadhīttveṣaṃ vaco apāvadhītsvāheti |
aśanāyāpipāse havā ugraṃ vacaḥ |
enaśca vairahatyaṃ ca tveṣaṃ vacaḥ"iti |
tatra svāhāntaḥ prathamo mantraḥ saṃpūrṇavākyatvānniśeṣo 'dhyāhartavyaḥ |
na hi ' tanūrvarṣiṣṭhā ' ityādibhāgastayoranvetuṃ yogyaḥ |
tasya prathamamantraśeṣatvāt, iti prāpte, brūmaḥ- vaidikayormantrayorākāṅkṣā vaidikenaiva vākyaśeṣeṇa pūraṇīyā |
children.translated_text: Because it is a complement of the first <s>mantra</s> — having arrived at this position, we say: The expectancy of two Vedic <s>mantras</s> should be fulfilled by a Vedic sentence-complement alone.
Therefore, the portion '<s>tanūr varṣiṣṭhā</s>' and the like is carried over (<s>anuṣajyate</s>) to the latter two <s>mantras</s>.
Although it is a complement of another [<s>mantra</s>], nevertheless, being retained in memory, it is preferable to a supply that would need to be imagined.
Therefore — carryover (<s>anuṣaṅga</s>) should be applied. || MJaiNyC_2,1.34-35 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, in the <s>Upasad</s> oblations, this is recited:
'<s>yā te agne ayāśayā tanūr varṣiṣṭhā gahvareṣṭhā |
ugraṃ vaco apāvadhīt tveṣaṃ vaco apāvadhīt svāhā |
yā te agne rajāśayā, yā te agne harāśayā</s>'
(O <s>Agni</s>, that body of yours which rests in iron, which is most exalted, which abides in sharp metal —
it has destroyed fierce speech, it has destroyed blazing speech, <s>svāhā</s>.
That of yours, O <s>Agni</s>, which rests in silver; that of yours, O <s>Agni</s>, which rests in gold).
The meaning is: '<s>Agni</s> has three bodies made of iron, silver, and gold; the first of these bodies mentioned here is most excellent and abides in sharp metal, i.e., iron; with that body, hunger and thirst — the minor offenses — and hero-slaying and other major sins have been destroyed.'
And thus the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: '<s>yad ugraṃ vaco apāvadhīt tveṣaṃ vaco apāvadhīt svāhā iti | aśanāyā-pipāse ha vā ugraṃ vacaḥ | enaś ca vairahatyaṃ ca tveṣaṃ vacaḥ</s>' (that it has destroyed fierce speech, it has destroyed blazing speech, <s>svāhā</s> — hunger and thirst are fierce speech; sin and enemy-slaying are blazing speech).
Therein, the first <s>mantra</s>, ending with <s>svāhā</s>, being a complete sentence, requires nothing further to be supplied.
For the portion '<s>tanūr varṣiṣṭhā</s>' and the like is not fit to construe with the [next] two [<s>mantras</s>].
START MJaiNy 2,1.36-37
He composes the seventeenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is there carryover (<s>anuṣaṅga</s>) or not? '<s>Acchidra</s>' (unbroken) and '<s>punātu</s>' (may it purify) are its two complements;
'<s>Citpatis tu</s>' (the Lord of thought) is without expectancy, so it is not carried over here. // MJaiNy_2,1.36 //
Instrumentality requires an action, and the action '<s>punātu</s>' (may it purify) is one [and the same];
in the three <s>mantras</s>, therefore through that [shared action], the entire complement is carried over. // MJaiNy_2,1.37 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome dīkṣāprakaraṇe paṭhyate -"citpatistvā punātu" "vākpatistvā punātu" "devastvā savitā punātvācchidreṇa pavitreṇa vasoḥ sūryasya raśmibhiḥ"iti |
tatra tṛtīyamantraśeṣaḥ ' acchidreṇa ' - ityādibhāgaḥ prathamadvitīyayormantrayornānuṣajyate |
kutaḥ |
nirākāṅkṣatvāt |
na hi"citpatistvā punātu""vākpatistvā punātu"ityanayoḥ śeṣiṇoḥ saṃpūrṇavākyayoḥ kāciccheṣākāṅkṣāsti - iti prāpte -
brūmaḥ- ' mā bhūccheṣiṇorākāṅkṣā, tathāpi śeṣasyā'kāṅkṣāsti ' iti |
' pavitreṇa raśmibhiḥ ' ityuktaṃ karaṇatvaṃ hi kriyāmapekṣate |
children.translated_text: For the instrumentality expressed by '<s>pavitreṇa</s>' (with a strainer) and '<s>raśmibhiḥ</s>' (with rays) requires an action.

children.text: kriyā ca ' punātu ' ityeṣā triṣvapi mantreṣvekā |
children.translated_text: And the action '<s>punātu</s>' (may it purify) is one and the same in all three <s>mantras</s>.

children.text: tayā kriyayā saṃbaddhaḥ śeṣaḥ kriyādvārā tṛtīyamantre nirapekṣe 'pi yathānveti, tathā pūrvayorapyanvetumarhati |
children.translated_text: The complement, being connected with that action, just as it construes through the action with the third <s>mantra</s> which is [already] self-sufficient, so too it is fit to construe with the previous two as well.
Therefore — carryover (<s>anuṣaṅga</s>) does exist. || MJaiNyC_2,1.36-37 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, in the section on consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>), it is recited: '<s>citpatis tvā punātu</s>' (may the Lord of thought purify you), '<s>vākpatis tvā punātu</s>' (may the Lord of speech purify you), '<s>devas tvā savitā punātv acchidreṇa pavitreṇa vasoḥ sūryasya raśmibhiḥ</s>' (may the god <s>Savitṛ</s> purify you with an unbroken strainer, with the rays of the sun of wealth).
Therein, the complement of the third <s>mantra</s> — the portion '<s>acchidreṇa</s>' and the like — is not carried over to the first and second <s>mantras</s>.
Why?
Because they are without expectancy.
For the two complement-possessing [<s>mantras</s>] — '<s>citpatis tvā punātu</s>' and '<s>vākpatis tvā punātu</s>' — being complete sentences, have no expectancy for any complement — having arrived at this position,
we say: 'Let the complement-possessing [sentences] have no expectancy; even so, the complement itself has expectancy.'
(In the eighteenth (seventeenth) <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the non-carryover when there is an intervening [element] — the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
Due to the intervening [element] (<s>vyavāya</s>), it should not be carried over. / Jaim_2,1.49 /
START MJaiNy 2,1.38-39
He composes the eighteenth (seventeenth) <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is there carryover (<s>anuṣaṅga</s>) of the word '<s>gacchatām</s>' (let it go) above [to subsequent <s>mantras</s>], or not?
In '<s>saṃ yajñapatiḥ</s>' (may the lord of sacrifice [be joined]) here, because of fitness, it does exist as before. // MJaiNy_2,1.38 //
That [word '<s>gacchatām</s>'] is singular; in the middle <s>mantra</s>, '<s>aṅgāni</s>' (limbs) [is plural] — by this indeed
it does not construe, due to the intervention (<s>vyavāya</s>); nor is it carried over above [to the third <s>mantra</s>]. // MJaiNy_2,1.39 //

children.text:
agnīṣomīyapaśau śrūyate --"saṃ te aprāṇo vātena gacchatām, samaṅgāni yajatraiḥ, saṃ yajñapatirāśiṣā"iti |
ayamarthaḥ- ' bhoḥ paśo tava prāṇo ' vātena bāhyena vāyunā saṃgacchatām, tava hṛdayādyaṅgāni yāgaviśeṣaiḥ saṃyujyantām, yajñapatirāśiṣā saṃyujyatām ' iti |

tatra"yajñapatiḥ"ityasmiṃstṛtīye mantre 'sam' ityupasargasya kriyāpadākāṅkṣatvātprathamamantragatasya ' gacchatām ' iti padasyaikavacanāntasya yajñapatiśabdenānvetuṃ yogyatvātpūrvavadbuddhisthatvena saṃnihitatvādākāṅkṣāsaṃnidhiyogyatānāṃ sadbhāvena kriyāpadamanuṣajyate -- iti prāpte , -
children.translated_text: Therein, in the third <s>mantra</s> '<s>yajñapatiḥ</s>' (lord of sacrifice), since the prefix '<s>sam</s>' (together) has expectancy for a verb, and since the word '<s>gacchatām</s>' (let it go), which is singular, occurring in the first <s>mantra</s>, is fit to construe with the word '<s>yajñapati</s>', and since, as before, it is proximate by being retained in memory — because of the presence of expectancy, proximity, and fitness — the verb is carried over — having arrived at this position,

children.text: brūmaḥ- madhyamamantre bahuvacanāntena ' aṅgāni ' ityanenānvetumayogyatvāttadvyavāyena buddhisaṃnidhyabhāvānnāstyanuṣaṅgaḥ |
children.translated_text: we say: Since it is unfit to construe with '<s>aṅgāni</s>' (limbs), which is plural, in the middle <s>mantra</s>, due to that intervention (<s>vyavāya</s>), there is no mental proximity, and hence there is no carryover.
Therefore, for the second and third <s>mantras</s>, an appropriate sentence-complement should be supplied. || MJaiNyC_2,1.38-39 ||

In the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal sacrifice, it is heard: '<s>saṃ te aprāṇo vātena gacchatām, sam aṅgāni yajatraiḥ, saṃ yajñapatir āśiṣā</s>' (may your breath go together with the wind; may [your] limbs be joined with the sacrificial [offerings]; may the lord of sacrifice be joined with the blessing).
The meaning is: 'O animal, may your breath go together with the external wind; may your limbs — heart and so on — be joined with the special sacrificial offerings; may the lord of sacrifice be joined with the blessing.'

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīye jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistare dvitīyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>pāda</s> of the second <s>adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Mādhavīya Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s>.
(Now the second <s>pāda</s> of the second <s>adhyāya</s>)
(In the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the differentiation of the <s>apūrva</s> of ancillary rites — the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
When there is a different word, there is a difference of ritual action, because it has become an established connection. / Jaim_2,2.1 /
START MJaiNy 2,2.1-2
He composes the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the second <s>pāda</s> —
In '<s>dadāti</s>' (he gives), '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices), and the like — is the <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force) one, or different?
Due to the unity of the verbal suffix (<s>ākhyāta</s>), it is one; the difference of roots is not a relevant factor. // MJaiNy_2,2.1 //
Due to the difference of roots, a difference is heard in the verbal form; therefore,
since [the verbal suffixes] originate as attached to distinct roots, the <s>bhāvanās</s> are mutually differentiated. // MJaiNy_2,2.2 //

children.text:
ihaikaprakaraṇagatānyaparyāyadhātuniṣpannānyākhyātāni yajati, dadāti, juhoti, ityādīnyudāharaṇam |
tāni caivaṃ śrūyate --"somena yajeta""hiraṇyamātreyāya dadāti" "dākṣiṇāni juhoti"iti |
teṣu bhāvanāvācina ākhyātasyaikatvādbhāvanāyā ekatvaṃ yuktam |
na ca dhātubhedādbhāvanābhedaḥ |
tadvācitvābhāvena dhātostasyāmaprayojakatvāt - iti prāpte , brūmaḥ- astvākhyātameva bhāvanāyāḥ prayojakam |

children.translated_text: But that verbal suffix is different for each root.

children.text: na hi bahūnāṃ dhātūnāmuparyeka ākhyātapratyayaḥ śrūyate |
children.translated_text: For a single verbal suffix (<s>ākhyāta-pratyaya</s>) is not heard on top of many roots.
Nor is a single verbal form prescribed in grammar from a group of roots.

children.text: tata ākhyātānāṃ bahūnāmekaikadhātuviśeṣāmuraktatvenaivotpannānāṃ bhāvanāvācitvena yāgadānahomabhāvanāḥ parasparaṃ bhidyante || 1-2 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the many verbal suffixes originate as attached to their respective individual roots, through their capacity to denote <s>bhāvanā</s>, the <s>bhāvanās</s> of sacrifice, giving, and oblation are mutually differentiated. || 1-2 ||

Here, the verbal forms '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices), '<s>dadāti</s>' (he gives), '<s>juhoti</s>' (he offers) — which occur in the same context and are derived from non-synonymous roots — are the examples.
They are heard thus: '<s>somena yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>), '<s>hiraṇyam ātreyāya dadāti</s>' (he gives gold to an <s>Ātreya</s>), '<s>dākṣiṇāni juhoti</s>' (he offers the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> oblations).
In these, since the verbal suffix (<s>ākhyāta</s>) that denotes <s>bhāvanā</s> is one, the unity of <s>bhāvanā</s> is appropriate.
Nor is there a differentiation of <s>bhāvanā</s> due to the difference of roots,
because the root, not being a denoting word for <s>bhāvanā</s>, is not a relevant factor for it — having arrived at this position, we say: Let the verbal suffix (<s>ākhyāta</s>) alone be the relevant factor for <s>bhāvanā</s>.
START MJaiNy 2,2.3
On this, he states the teacher's view —
If [it be said that] the <s>śāstra</s> (scriptural injunction) is undifferentiated because the <s>niyoga</s> (command) is one — that is not so;
because when the <s>śāstra</s> is differentiated due to the difference of roots, the <s>niyoga</s> too is forcibly differentiated. // MJaiNy_2,2.3 //

children.text: ' karmabhedacintā nādhyāyārthaḥ, kiṃtu śāstrabhedacintā ' iti gurormatam |
children.translated_text: The teacher's view is: 'The topic of this [<s>adhyāya</s>] is not the inquiry into the differentiation of ritual actions (<s>karmabheda</s>), but the inquiry into the differentiation of scriptural injunctions (<s>śāstrabheda</s>).'

children.text: tatra ' yajeta, dadyāt, juhuyāt ' ityeteṣu liṅpratyayabācyasya niyogasyaikatvādhātūnāṃ niyogavācakatvābhāvenāprayojakatvādekaniyogārthe kṛtsnaṃ śāstramekam - iti pūrvapakṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therein, in '<s>yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice), '<s>dadyāt</s>' (one should give), '<s>juhuyāt</s>' (one should offer) — since the <s>niyoga</s> (command) denoted by the <s>liṅ</s> suffix is one, and since the roots lack the capacity to denote <s>niyoga</s> and are therefore not a relevant factor — the entire <s>śāstra</s> is one, serving a single <s>niyoga</s>-meaning — this is the prior view.

children.text: pratidhātu liṅpratyayasya bhinnatvāddhātvarthānubandhabhedena tadviśiṣṭe niyoge 'pi bhedasya vārayitumaśakyatayā niyogānusāri śāstraṃ bhinnam - iti siddhāntaḥ || MJaiNyC_2,2.3 ||
children.translated_text: Since the <s>liṅ</s> suffix is different for each root, and since, due to the difference in the attached root-meaning, the difference even in the <s>niyoga</s> qualified by it cannot be prevented — the <s>śāstra</s>, following the <s>niyoga</s>, is differentiated — this is the established conclusion. || MJaiNyC_2,2.3 ||
(In the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the differentiation of the <s>apūrva</s> of <s>samidh</s> (fuel-stick) and the like — the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: ekasyaivaṃ punaḥ śrutir aviśeṣād anarthakaṃ hi syāt / Jaim_2,2.2 /
children.translated_text: When there is a repeated hearing of one and the same [word], it would be purposeless because of non-distinction. / Jaim_2,2.2 /
START MJaiNy 2,2.4-5
He composes the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In '<s>samidho yajati</s>' (he sacrifices the fuel-sticks) and the like — is it one, or different?
Due to the unity of root and suffix, it is one; whence the difference? // MJaiNy_2,2.4 //
From the repetition, there is a difference of ritual actions here; because of name-status, there is no injunction of a qualifying attribute;
the injunctive character appears from the scriptural statement; [its apparent] anaphoric nature is from proximity. // MJaiNy_2,2.5 //

children.translated_text: In the example to be stated later, '<s>athaiṣa jyotiḥ</s>' (now this is light), since the name is understood before the sacrifice is understood, the name is the cause of the distinction of actions.

children.text: iha tu vidhāyakairyajatipadairyāgeṣvavagateṣu, bhede cābhyāsādavagate, bhinnānāṃ yāgānāṃ samitsaṃjñāyā anyāḥ saṃjñā apekṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: But here, when the sacrifices are understood through the injunctive '<s>yajati</s>' words and the distinction is understood from the repetition, names other than the name '<s>samit</s>' are required for the distinct sacrifices.
Thus the name-status of <s>Tanūnapāt</s> and the like is understood subsequently.
Therefore — the repetition alone is the cause of the distinction here. || MJaiNyC_2,2.4-5 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) sacrifices, it is heard: '<s>samidho yajati</s>' (one offers to the kindling-sticks), '<s>tanūnapātaṃ yajati</s>' (one offers to <s>Tanūnapāt</s>), '<s>iḍo yajati</s>' (one offers to <s>Iḍā</s>), '<s>barhir yajati</s>' (one offers to the sacrificial grass), '<s>svāhākāraṃ yajati</s>' (one offers to the <s>Svāhākāra</s>). Therein, when the word '<s>yajati</s>' (one sacrifices) is heard five times, there is no difference in the verbal root among the previously stated words like '<s>yajati</s>, <s>dadāti</s>' (offers, gives) and the like, such that a difference in <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force) might be suspected. Therefore, the unity of <s>bhāvanā</s> produced by the unity of the finite verb is unavoidable — if this be argued: Not so. Because the distinction of actions is understood from the repetition of the word '<s>yajati</s>.' If the action were one, the repetition would be purposeless. Now, if it be argued: by the first-heard sentence '<s>samidho yajati</s>' (one offers to the kindling-sticks), a sacrifice named <s>samit</s> is enjoined, and the subsequent four occurrences of '<s>yajati</s>' re-state [that sacrifice] and alternatively enjoin four qualifying attributes — either in the form of deities like <s>Tanūnapāt</s> and the like, or in the form of substances — hence the repetition is not purposeless on account of serving re-statement: that is incorrect. Because the words '<s>Tanūnapāt</s>' and the like, being names of sacrifices, cannot function as qualifying-attribute injunctions. There is no deity-injunction here, since neither the dative case nor a <s>taddhita</s> suffix is heard. Nor is there a substance-injunction, since [the words] do not end in the instrumental case. Therefore, since those words ending in the accusative case appropriately function as names, like in '<s>agnihotraṃ juhoti</s>' (one offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>) and similar [cases]. As for the claim that the four subsequent '<s>yajati</s>' words are re-statements — that is wrong. Because they are injunctive. Just as in '<s>samidho yajati</s>' the injunctive nature of the word '<s>yajati</s>' is understood from the scripture, so too in the other four instances the injunctive nature is scriptural. The re-statement status, however, is understood merely from the proximity of the prior statement '<s>samidho yajati</s>.' And proximity is weaker than scripture. When they are injunctive, since a re-injunction of the sacrifice named <s>samit</s> already enjoined by the prior sentence is impossible, other sacrifices named <s>Tanūnapāt</s> and the like are enjoined. Now, if it be objected: in this case, the distinction of actions follows from the difference of names, not from the repetition; and in that case, there would be confusion with the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> to be stated later — Not so. Because of dissimilarity.
(In the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the principal-subsidiary relationship of the <s>āghāra</s> and the <s>Āgneya</s> and the like, <s>sūtras</s> 3-8)
But the context [indicates a connection] with the full-moon [day], because no [other] form is stated. / Jaim_2,2.3 /

children.text: viśeṣadarśanāc ca sarveṣāṃ sameṣu hy apravṛttiḥ syāt / Jaim_2,2.4 /
children.translated_text: And because of the observation of a specific [connection], since in the case of [rituals] that are the same, there would be non-performance. / Jaim_2,2.4 /
But [they are] qualifying attributes, because of the connection with scripture. / Jaim_2,2.5 /

children.text: codanā vā guṇānāṃ yugapacchāstrāc codite hi tadarthatvāt tasya tasyopadiśyeta / Jaim_2,2.6 /
children.translated_text: Or rather, the injunction is for the qualifying attributes simultaneously — because when they are enjoined by <s>śāstra</s>, since they serve that purpose, [the qualifying attributes] would be taught for each [sacrifice]. / Jaim_2,2.6 /
And the designation is similar to that. / Jaim_2,2.7 /
And because of the observation of the mark (<s>liṅga</s>). / Jaim_2,2.8 /
START MJaiNy 2,2.6-10
He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The statement '<s>evaṃ vidvān paurṇamāsīm</s>' (one who knows thus, on the full-moon day) and '<s>amāvāsyām</s>' (on the new-moon day) — is this said [about],
a different sacrifice, or is it a re-statement of the previously mentioned collection [of sacrifices]? // MJaiNy_2,2.6 //
It would be a different sacrifice, because of the repetition [of the verb]; for the substance is the <s>dhruva</s> (permanent ghee), and the deity
is obtained from [the <s>mantras</s>] '<s>vārtraghṇī</s>' and the like; but re-statement is not appropriate. // MJaiNy_2,2.7 //
The '<s>vārtraghṇī</s>' [mantras determine] the subsidiary arrangement of the <s>ājyabhāga</s> (ghee-portions) — they do not [establish] the deity [of a new sacrifice];
the word '<s>paurṇa</s>' (full-moon) re-states [what is known]; appropriately, the triad connected with the full-moon day is [re-stated]. // MJaiNy_2,2.8 //
By the word '<s>amā</s>' (new-moon) too, the purpose is to establish the duality of the collection;
the co-existence [of the triads] on the full-moon day — [this is understood] from the two statements, for each triad. // MJaiNy_2,2.9 //
In the injunction through the '<s>evaṃ vidvān</s>' (one who knows thus) sentence, the repetition of the injunction [is accomplished] through the <s>Āgneya</s> and the like;
since what is enjoined [there] is the principal because it has the fruit, the others are subsidiary. // MJaiNy_2,2.10 //

children.translated_text: But on the re-statement view, since the two triads qualify for the designation '<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' by their connection with the [respective] times,
and since the duality of the collection justifies the dual number, the principality belongs to the <s>Āgneya</s> and the like alone by virtue of their connection with the fruit.

children.text: prayājādīnāṃ tu guṇabhāva iti na ko 'pi doṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>prayāja</s> and the like have subsidiary status — so there is no fault whatsoever.
Therefore — the '<s>evaṃ vidvān</s>' sentence is a re-statement. || MJaiNyC_2,2.6-10 ||

This is prescribed: '<s>ya evaṃ vidvān paurṇamāsīṃ yajate</s>' (one who, knowing thus, sacrifices on the full-moon day), '<s>ya evaṃ vidvān amāvāsyāṃ yajate</s>' (one who, knowing thus, sacrifices on the new-moon day). Here, by the word '<s>yajati</s>' (sacrifices), a different sacrifice is enjoined, and the six previously established sacrifices — <s>Āgneya</s> and the like — are not being re-stated. The <s>Āgneya</s> and the like, connected with [specific] times, are prescribed in that very context thus: '<s>yadāgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo 'māvāsyāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ cācyuto bhavati</s>' (the <s>Āgneya</s> eight-potsherded [offering] is constant on the new-moon and full-moon days), '<s>tāv abrūtām agnīṣomāv ājyasyaiva anāv upāṃśu paurṇamāsyāṃ yajan</s>' (those two — <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> — said: [let the sacrificer offer] ghee alone, in two [portions], in a low voice, on the full-moon day), '<s>tābhyām etam agnīṣomīyam ekādaśakapālaṃ pūrṇamāse prāyacchat</s>' (he gave to those two this <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> eleven-potsherded [offering] at the full-moon), '<s>aindraṃ dadhy amāvāsyāyām</s>' (the <s>Aindra</s> [offering of] curds on the new-moon), '<s>aindraṃ payo 'māvāsyāyām</s>' (the <s>Aindra</s> [offering of] milk on the new-moon). From these six previously established [sacrifices] — <s>Āgneya</s> and the like — if the sacrifice enjoined by the '<s>evaṃ vidvān</s>' sentence is different, then by the reasoning of the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the repetition of the injunction is justified. Nor is there an absence of substance and deity in the different sacrifice, because of the existence of the <s>dhruva</s> (permanent) ghee. Hence it has been said: 'The <s>dhruva</s> ghee is the common substance; the deity is [determined] from the <s>mantra</s>-text; therefore the two sacrifices, possessing [substance and deity as their] form, are enjoined separately.' The commonality of the <s>dhruva</s> is heard from '<s>sarvasmai vā etad yajñāya gṛhyate yad dhruvāyām ājyam</s>' (the ghee on the <s>dhruvā</s> [spoon] is taken for every sacrifice). The <s>mantra</s>-derived nature of the deity should be established thus: '<s>tasmād vārtraghṇī paurṇamāsyām anūcyete, vṛdhanvatī amāvāsyāyām</s>' (therefore the two <s>vārtraghṇī</s> [mantras] are recited on the full-moon day, the two <s>vṛdhanvatī</s> [mantras] on the new-moon day) — the two <s>vārtraghṇī</s> and two <s>vṛdhanvatī</s> recitation-formulas are enjoined for the sacrifice connected with the two times respectively. Among those, '<s>agnir vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanat</s>' (may <s>Agni</s> slay the enemies) is one <s>vārtraghṇī</s> <s>mantra</s>. '<s>Tvaṃ somāsi satpatis tvaṃ rājota vṛtrahā</s>' (you, O <s>Soma</s>, are the lord of truth, you are the king and slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>) is the other. From those two, <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> are stated as the deities of the full-moon [sacrifice]. Similarly, from the two internally prescribed <s>mantras</s> containing the root '<s>vṛdh</s>' (to grow), <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> are stated as the deities of the new-moon [sacrifice]. Since the sacrifice possesses form through these substance and deity, a different sacrifice is enjoined here. If [the '<s>evaṃ vidvān</s>' sentence] were a re-statement of the six sacrifices, then since no other content to be enjoined through that re-statement is seen, the '<s>evaṃ vidvān</s>' sentence would be purposeless. Not only would that be purposeless, but the statements '<s>paurṇamāsyāṃ paurṇamāsyā yajeta</s>' (on the full-moon day, one should sacrifice with the full-moon [offering]) and '<s>amāvāsyāyām amāvāsyayā yajeta</s>' (on the new-moon day, one should sacrifice with the new-moon [offering]) would also be purposeless. These are not [merely] enjoining the time, since the time is already enjoined by the origination-sentences '<s>yadāgneyaḥ</s>' and the like. But if it is a different sacrifice, [these sentences] will enjoin the time [for it]. Therefore, [the '<s>evaṃ vidvān</s>' sentence] is an injunction of a different sacrifice — having arrived at this position, we say: Let the substance be set aside for now. But the deity of the intended different sacrifice is in no way obtainable. Because the <s>vārtraghṇī</s> and <s>vṛdhanvatī</s> [mantras] indicate the deities of the <s>ājyabhāga</s> (ghee-portions). In the <s>Hautra</s> (recitation) section of the <s>mantra</s> collection, after prescribing the <s>sānidhenī</s> [verses], the invocation-formula (<s>āvāhana-nigada</s>), and the <s>prayāja</s>-<s>mantras</s>, the two <s>vārtraghṇī</s> and two <s>vṛdhanvatī</s> [mantras] are prescribed as immediately following the <s>prayājas</s>. And a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) pertaining to <s>Agni</s> and pertaining to <s>Soma</s> is perceived there. Therefore, from the mark and the sequence, their connection with the <s>ājyabhāga</s> is understood. As for the passage '<s>vārtraghṇī paurṇamāsyām</s>' and the like — that passage declares the arrangement over two times for the pair of <s>mantras</s> already established as belonging to the <s>ājyabhāga</s> by the mark and sequence. It does not enjoin their subsidiary status to a new sacrifice. Therefore, since [the new sacrifice] lacks form [i.e., substance and deity], the '<s>evaṃ vidvān</s>' sentence does not enjoin a different sacrifice. Rather, it re-states the two collections of three, each in the form of a triad, among the six previously established [sacrifices] — <s>Āgneya</s> and the like. Nor is there an impossibility of re-stating sacrifices through the time-denoting words '<s>paurṇamāsī</s>' (full-moon) and '<s>amāvāsyā</s>' (new-moon) — because they serve as indicative designations (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) for the triads of sacrifices enjoined at those times. Nor is the re-statement purposeless — because it serves the purpose of establishing the duality of the collection. And when that [duality] is established, in the fruit-sentence '<s>darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta</s>' (one who desires heaven should sacrifice with the new- and full-moon [offerings]), the dual number is justified with reference to the six sacrifices. As for the objection that on the re-statement view, the sentences '<s>paurṇamāsyām</s>' and the like would be purposeless — that is incorrect. Because even when the enjoining of the time is possible, [the sentence serves] to enjoin the simultaneous performance of each triad. The simultaneous performance of the three — <s>Āgneya</s>, <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s>, and <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> — enjoined at the full-moon time, is enjoined by '<s>paurṇamāsyā</s>' (with the full-moon offering) ending in the instrumental singular. Similarly in the other [case]. Now, if it be objected: even without the '<s>evaṃ vidvān</s>' sentence enjoining a different sacrifice, it is not a re-statement either; rather, it is an injunction of the sacrifice, and the '<s>yadāgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaḥ</s>' and similar sentences, by re-stating the already-enjoined sacrifice, enjoin qualifying attributes in the form of substance and deity — not so. Because in that case, the injunction of multiple qualifying attributes by a single sentence would be impossible. If each qualifying attribute were enjoined separately, there would be the fault of repetition of the injunction. But when the <s>Āgneya</s> and similar sentences are injunctive, there is no fault of repetition, because they are injunctions of [sacrifices] qualified [by substance and deity together]. Therefore the <s>Āgneya</s> and similar sentences are injunctions of [the sacrifices], and the '<s>evaṃ vidvān</s>' sentence is a re-statement. Moreover, if one accepts the re-statement [view] yet asserts the injunction of a different sacrifice, the principal-subsidiary relationship of the <s>prayāja</s> and the <s>Āgneya</s> and the like would not be established. For thus: some injunctions are prescribed without connection to time — '<s>samidho yajati</s>' (one offers to the kindling-sticks), '<s>āghāram āghārayati</s>' (one performs the <s>āghāra</s>) and the like. Others are connected with time — '<s>yadāgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo 'māvāsyāyāṃ ca paurṇamāsyāṃ ca</s>' and the like. Since both groups are part of the present context, in the sentence '<s>darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta</s>' (one who desires heaven should sacrifice with the new- and full-moon offerings), the connection of all [these sacrifices] with the fruit must be understood. The dual number '<s>darśapūrṇamāsābhyām</s>' should be construed as plural. [We would have to count as:] two different sacrifices enjoined by the '<s>evaṃ vidvān</s>' sentence, plus the <s>prayājas</s> and the like, plus the <s>Āgneya</s> and the like. Since duality is impossible among these [many sacrifices], and since all would have a connection with the fruit, the <s>prayāja</s> and the like would have equal principality — like the <s>Iṣṭi</s>, <s>Paśu</s>, and <s>Soma</s> [sacrifices] within the <s>Rājasūya</s> — and their subsidiary status would not hold. And in the absence of that [subsidiary status], since they would not be ancillaries, the transfer (<s>atideśa</s>) of the <s>Āgneya</s> and the like to derivative sacrifices (<s>vikṛti</s>) such as the <s>Saurya</s> and the like would not apply.
(In the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the unprecedentedness of the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 9-12)
Like [the sacrifice on] the full-moon day, the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s> (low-voiced offering) would be [a separate sacrifice]. / Jaim_2,2.9 /
Or rather, [it is] an injunction, because it is not the main [sacrifice]. / Jaim_2,2.10 /
Because of subordination to a qualifying attribute. / Jaim_2,2.11 /
And because of the statement regarding the majority. / Jaim_2,2.12 /
START MJaiNy 2,2.11-12
He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the statement '<s>upāṃśuyājam</s>' (the low-voiced offering) here a re-statement, or an injunction?
Since there is a clear injunction in the <s>Viṣṇu</s> and other sentences, it is a re-statement [here]. // MJaiNy_2,2.11 //
Since the statement of identity (<s>jāmitva</s>) falls in between, in the injunction of the qualifying attribute of low voice,
the <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the like serve as <s>arthavāda</s>; its form [is known] from the <s>dhruva</s> (permanent ghee) <s>mantra</s>. // MJaiNy_2,2.12 //

children.translated_text: because the <s>dhruva</s> [oblation material] serves as its substance.
Nor is there an absence of deity.

Because a triad of deities is apprehended through alternative <s>mantras</s> — <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, and <s>Āgnīṣomīya</s> — that are recited in different Vedic recensions (<s>śākhā</s>) at the point of the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> sequence.
Therefore — '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices) is the enjoining [verb]. || MJaiNyC_2,2.11-12 ||

This is recited: '<s>jāmi vā etad yajñasya kriyate | yad anvañcau puroḍāśāv apāṃśuyājam antarā yajati | viṣṇur upāṃśu yaṣṭavyo 'jāmitvāya | prajāpatir upāṃśu yaṣṭavyo 'jāmitvāya | agnīṣomāv upāṃśu yaṣṭavyāv ajāmitvāya</s>' (a blemish [<s>jāmi</s>] in the sacrifice is indeed produced when one sacrifices without the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> between the two successive offering cakes; <s>Viṣṇu</s> should be worshipped silently to remove the blemish; <s>Prajāpati</s> should be worshipped silently to remove the blemish; <s>Agnīṣomau</s> should be worshipped silently to remove the blemish). Therein, if it be said that the sentences about <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the others merely restate (<s>anuvāda</s>) the aggregate of the three sacrifices enjoined [therein] — that is not correct. Because the fault of blemish (<s>jāmitva</s>) caused by the lack of an intermediary between the two offering cakes — the <s>Āgneya</s> and the <s>Āgnīṣomīya</s> — is presented at the beginning of the passage, something is intended to be enjoined in the interval between the two offering cakes. The intention of an offering qualified by an intermediate position is not apprehended in the sentences about <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the others. But in the first sentence, that is apprehended — therefore that sentence is the enjoining one. Nor should the present tense in '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices) be suspected [as indicating mere description], because of the adoption of the fifth [interpretation of the present tense, i.e., as injunctive]. Since the qualifying attribute of silent recitation (<s>upāṃśutva</s>), like the qualifying attribute of intermediate timing, further specifies the rite, the full form of the rite is called '<s>upāṃśuyājana</s>' (silent sacrificing). This being so, when the rite qualified by both attributes is enjoined by the first sentence, the sentences about <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the others would be <s>arthavāda</s>. Nor should it be suspected that these sentences enjoin the deity by restating the already-enjoined sacrifice — because the passage begins with the fault of blemish (<s>jāmitva</s>) that needs to be remedied, and concludes with the remedy of non-blemish (<s>ajāmitva</s>); the entire great sentence from '<s>jāmi vai</s>' to '<s>ajāmitvāya</s>' is apprehended as a single unit. Indeed, in a single sentence, a multiplicity of things to be enjoined is not possible. Nor is there an absence of the substance for the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> intended to be enjoined here,
(In the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the unprecedented status (<s>apūrvatā</s>) of the <s>Āghāra</s> and the like, <s>sūtras</s> 13–16)
The <s>Āghāra</s> and the <s>Agnihotra</s> — because of the absence of the [sacrificial] form (<s>arūpatva</s>). / Jaim_2,2.13 /
Because of the connection with the designation (<s>saṃjñā</s>). / Jaim_2,2.14 /
And because of not being the principal subject (<s>aprakṛtatva</s>). / Jaim_2,2.15 /
