children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>Agnihotra</s> sentence and the like are enjoiners of rites.
Therein, the substance is obtained from the sentences about curds and the like.
And the deity is derived from the <s>mantra</s> (<s>māntravarṇikī</s>).
In the case of <s>Āghāra</s> as well, the substance and deity are to be derived in the same manner. || MJaiNyC_2,2.13-14 ||

This is recited: '<s>agnihotraṃ juhoti</s>' (one offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>), '<s>dadhnā juhoti</s>' (one offers with curds), '<s>payasā juhoti</s>' (one offers with milk). And this other [set] is recited: '<s>āghāram āghārayati</s>' (one pours the <s>āghāra</s>), '<s>ūrdhvam āghārayati</s>' (one pours upward), '<s>ṛjum āghārayati</s>' (one pours straight). Therein, the <s>Agnihotra</s> sentence is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) of the aggregate of rites enjoined by the sentences about curds and the like. And the <s>Āghāra</s> sentence restates [the aggregate of rites] enjoined by the sentences about upward [pouring] and the like. These two sentences are not enjoiners of rites. Why? Because of the absence of the sacrificial form characterized by substance and deity — if so it is argued, then the following must be said: Does the sentence about curds and the like enjoin merely a qualifying attribute (<s>guṇa</s>), or a rite qualified by the attribute? Not the first — because, in your view, since the <s>Agnihotra</s> sentence does not enjoin the rite, the principal (<s>guṇin</s>) is not established, and without a principal, it is impossible to enjoin merely a qualifying attribute preceded by a restatement of the principal. In the second [alternative], there would be the burden of [postulating] an injunction. But that [burden] is inappropriate when another path is available.
(In the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the unprecedented status (<s>apūrvatā</s>) of the animal [sacrifice] and the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice], <s>sūtras</s> 17–20)

children.translated_text: Similarly, the meaning apprehended from '<s>paśum ālabheta</s>' (one should sacrifice an animal) is not apprehended in the cutting-sentences.
Therefore, since there is no prior statement, restatement is impossible; and by '<s>yajati</s>' and '<s>ālabhate</s>', the rites are enjoined.
By the cup-drawing sentences, however, the <s>Soma</s> preparatory rite qualified by specific deities is enjoined.
And by the cutting-sentences, the animal preparatory rite [is enjoined]. || MJaiNyC_2,2.14-16 ||

'<s>Somena yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>) is heard. Therein, '<s>aindravāyavaṃ gṛhṇāti, maitrāvaruṇaṃ gṛhṇāti</s>' (he draws the cup for <s>Indra</s>-<s>Vāyu</s>, he draws the cup for <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s>) and similar [passages] are also heard. Similarly, '<s>agnīṣomīyaṃ paśum ālabheta</s>' (one should sacrifice the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal) is heard. Therein, '<s>hṛdayasyāgre 'vadyati | atha jihvāyāḥ | atha vakṣasaḥ</s>' (he first cuts from the heart; then from the tongue; then from the chest) and similar [passages] are also heard. In the sentences about <s>Indra</s>-<s>Vāyu</s> and the like, sacrifices are enjoined — because the deities are apprehended from the stems '<s>Indra</s>-<s>Vāyu</s>' and the like, and the <s>Soma</s>-juice substance from the <s>taddhita</s>-derived form. The aggregate of sacrifices enjoined by these cup-drawing sentences is restated by '<s>somena yajeta</s>.' Similarly, in the cutting-sentences, the substances — heart and the like — are heard. Therefore rites qualified by [specific] substances are enjoined therein. By restating them, the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> deity is enjoined in the animal-sacrifice sentence. Therefore — the aggregate of rites enjoined by the cutting-sentences is restated by '<s>paśum ālabheta</s>' — having arrived at this position, we say: A restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) is possible only when there is a prior statement (<s>purovāda</s>). But here there is no prior statement. Because the meaning apprehended from '<s>somena yajeta</s>' is not apprehended in the cup-drawing sentences. For drawing (<s>grahaṇa</s>) is not sacrificing (<s>yajana</s>). Nor is the juice (<s>rasa</s>) expressed by the <s>taddhita</s> suffix identical with the <s>Soma</s> plant. Nor should it be suspected that the <s>taddhita</s> suffix, enjoined in the sense of a pronoun, refers to the principal [substance in context] and not to the juice — because in '<s>dhārayā gṛhṇāti</s>' (he draws in a stream), it is the juice alone that is the principal subject.
(In the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the differentiation of rites by number, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
Due to the introduction of separateness, the differentiation of rites would result from number. / Jaim_2,2.21 /
START MJaiNy 2,2.17-21
He composes the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In '<s>āhutīs tisraḥ</s>' (three oblations) — is the rite one, or are they distinct?

It is one, because of the single occurrence of the finite verb (<s>ākhyāta</s>); the number [three] is achieved by repetition (<s>āvṛtti</s>), as in the case of the preliminary offerings (<s>prayāja</s>). // MJaiNy_2,2.17 //
The finite verb alone is not a [sufficient] means of knowledge; the multiplicity of rites is [established] by the number;
the eleven-fold-ness in the <s>prayājas</s>, however, is through repetition, because no other path is available. // MJaiNy_2,2.18 //
In '<s>paśūn saptadaśa prājāpatyān</s>' (seventeen animals sacred to <s>Prajāpati</s>), the commentator (<s>bhāṣyakṛt</s>)
presents the investigation in the earlier [example], because the tri-plicity of the action is obvious [there]. // MJaiNy_2,2.19 //
Animals endowed with plurality [constitute] a single substance [when associated with] a single deity; hence there is no differentiation;

children.text: rūpasya tena karmaikyaṃ saṃkhyā nātra kriyāgatā // MJaiNy_2,2.20 //
children.translated_text: therefore the rite is one by reason of the form; the number here pertains to the substance, not to the action. // MJaiNy_2,2.20 //
The latter [association of] plurality pertains to the <s>taddhita</s>-derived meaning that has no connection with the deity;
the plurality combined with the form — by that number, there is differentiation of the rite. // MJaiNy_2,2.21 //

children.text:
' tistra āhutīrjuhoti ' iti śrūyate |
tatra ' juhoti ' ityetadākhyātaṃ ' samidho yajati ' ityādivannābhyastam, kiṃtu sakṛdevā'mnātam |
tata ekamidaṃ karma |
tritvasaṃkhyā tu tasyaiva karmaṇa āvṛttyā netavyā |
yathā prayājeṣvekādaśatvasaṃkhyā pañcānāmeva prayājānāmāvṛttyā nītā, tadvat - iti prāpte -
brūmaḥ- kimidamākhyātaṃ padāntaranirapekṣameva karmaikye pramāṇam, uta padāntarānvitam |
nā'dyaḥ |
vākyāṃśasya padamātrasya pramitijanakatvābhāvāt |
dvitīye - tri -tvasaṃkhyayā viśeṣitenā'khyātena karmabahutvaṃ gamyate |
prayojānāṃ tu pūrvameva pañcasaṃkhyāvaruddhatvādāvṛttimantareṇaikādaśatvaṃ duḥsaṃpādam |
iha tvetadvidhitaḥ pūrva karmaṇa ekatvasaṃkhyāvarodho nāstīti vaiṣamyam |
tadetadvṛttikārodāharaṇaṃ bhāṣyakāro nānumanyate |
karmavācina āhutiśabdasya viśeṣaṇena triśabdena karmabahutvasya sphuṭatayā pūrvapakṣānutthānāt |
idaṃ tvatrodāharaṇam - ' saptadaśa prājāpatyānpaśūnālabhate ' iti |
atra ' prajāpattirdevatā yeṣāṃ paśūnāṃ te prājāpatyāḥ ' iti taddhitavyutpattau bahutvopotāḥ paśava ekaṃ dravyam |
tato dravyaikyāddevataikyācca yāgasya rūpamabhinnamityekamidaṃ karma |
yā tu 'saptadaśa' iti saṃkhyā, sā paśudravyagatā, na tu pūrvodāhṛtatritvasaṃkhyeva kriyāgatā |
tasmāt -- 'na karmabhedamāpādayati ' iti prāpte -
brūmaḥ- atra ' prajāpatirdevatā yasya paśoḥ sa prājāpatyaḥ ' iti taddhitāntaṃ prātipadikaṃ vyutpādya paścāttaddhitāntaprātipādikārthasya prajāpatidevatāviśiṣṭapaśoḥ karmatvabahutvavivakṣāyāmutpanne ime dvitīyāvibhaktibahuvacane |
tatra prathamabhāvinyā dvitīyāvibhaktereva taddhitotpattivelāyāmanvayo nāsti, kutaḥ paścādbhāvino bahuvacanasyānvayaḥ |
evaṃ sati ' prājāpatyaḥ ' ityanena taddhitāntaprātipadikanaikapaśudravyamekadevatopetaṃ yāgasya rūpaṃ samarpyate |

children.translated_text: The plural number is for the purpose of [indicating] the plurality of such forms.
And the specific degree of plurality is indicated by '<s>saptadaśa</s>' (seventeen).
Therefore — in this case, the number brings about differentiation of rites.

children.text: evaṃ ca sati, aṣṭame vakṣyamāṇaṃ saptadaśapaśūnāmaikādaśinapaśugaṇavikṛtitvamupapadyate || MJaiNyC_2,2.17-21 ||
children.translated_text: And this being so, the status of the seventeen animals as a modification (<s>vikṛti</s>) of the <s>Ekādaśin</s> animal-group, which will be discussed in the eighth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], is well-established. || MJaiNyC_2,2.17-21 ||

'<s>Tisra āhutīr juhoti</s>' (he offers three oblations) is heard. Therein, the finite verb '<s>juhoti</s>' is not repeated like '<s>samidho yajati</s>' (he sacrifices the kindling-sticks) and so on, but is stated only once. Therefore this is a single rite. The number three should be achieved by repetition (<s>āvṛtti</s>) of that same rite — just as in the <s>prayājas</s>, the number eleven is achieved by repetition of [only] five <s>prayājas</s> — having arrived at this position, we say: Is this finite verb, independent of other words, a means of knowledge for the unity of the rite, or is it [a means of knowledge only] when connected with other words? Not the first — because a mere word, being a partial component of a sentence, does not generate certainty. In the second [case] — the finite verb qualified by the number three conveys a multiplicity of rites. But in the <s>prayājas</s>, since the number five was already determined earlier, achieving eleven without repetition would be difficult. But here, no prior determination of the unity of the rite has been made — this is the difference. This illustration of the <s>Vṛttikāra</s> is not approved by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (<s>Śabara</s>) — because, since the number word '<s>tri</s>' qualifies the word '<s>āhuti</s>' which denotes an action, the multiplicity of rites is obvious, and the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (objection) does not even arise. This rather is the [proper] illustration here: '<s>saptadaśa prājāpatyān paśūn ālabhate</s>' (he sacrifices seventeen animals sacred to <s>Prajāpati</s>). Here, by the <s>taddhita</s> derivation '<s>prajāpatir devatā yeṣāṃ paśūnāṃ te prājāpatyāḥ</s>' (those animals whose deity is <s>Prajāpati</s> are <s>prājāpatya</s>), animals endowed with plurality constitute a single substance. Therefore, since the substance is one and the deity is one, the form of the sacrifice is undifferentiated — hence this is a single rite. And the number 'seventeen' pertains to the animal-substance, not to the action, unlike the previously cited number 'three.' Therefore — 'the number does not bring about differentiation of the rite' — having arrived at this position, we say: Here, having derived the <s>taddhita</s>-ending stem as '<s>prajāpatir devatā yasya paśoḥ sa prājāpatyaḥ</s>' (that animal whose deity is <s>Prajāpati</s> is <s>prājāpatya</s>), subsequently, when the plurality of the <s>taddhita</s>-stem meaning — namely, the animal qualified by the deity <s>Prajāpati</s> — is intended in the sense of an object (<s>karman</s>), these accusative plural case-endings are produced. In that [derivational process], the accusative case, which comes into being first, has no connection with the <s>taddhita</s> suffix at the time of its formation — how then could the plural number, which comes into being later, have a connection [with the <s>taddhita</s>]? This being so, by '<s>prājāpatyaḥ</s>' — the <s>taddhita</s>-ending stem — a single animal-substance endowed with a single deity constitutes the form of the sacrifice.
(In the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the differentiation of rites by designation (<s>saṃjñā</s>), the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
And the designation [differentiates], because of its connection with the origination. / Jaim_2,2.22 /
START MJaiNy 2,2.22-23
He composes the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: athaiṣa jyotirityatra guṇo vā karma vā pṛthak /
children.translated_text: In '<s>athaiṣa jyotiḥ</s>' (now this is the <s>Jyotis</s>), is it a qualifying attribute or a distinct rite?
It is a qualifying attribute — consisting of the giving of a thousand — in the [already] restated <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. // MJaiNy_2,2.22 //
The word '<s>atha</s>' (now) [indicates] a break from the current subject; the word '<s>etat</s>' (this) would refer to what follows;
just as with number, a new designation (<s>saṃjñā</s>) [indicates] a distinct rite here. // MJaiNy_2,2.23 //

children.text:
"athaiṣa jyotiḥ, athaiṣa viśvajyotiḥ, athaiṣa sarvajyotiḥ, anena sahastradakṣiṇena yajeta ' iti śrūyate |
atra prakṛtaṃ jyotiṣṭopam 'eṣa jyotiḥ ' ityanūdya tasminsahastradānalakṣaṇo guṇo vidhīyate -- iti cet |
na |
prakṛtasya jyotiṣṭomasya ' atha ' ityanena vicchinnatvāt |
na caivaṃ sati ' ayaiṣa jyotiḥ ' ityukta etacchabdo 'nupapanna iti vācyam |
saṃnihitavācinaitacchabdenātītasaṃnihitasyevā'gāmisaṃnihitasyāpi parāmarśasaṃbhavāt |

children.translated_text: And the meaning of the word '<s>jyotis</s>' that is proximately forthcoming [is the name of a new rite].

children.text: sa ca jyotiḥ śabdo 'tī maparāmṛśannapūrvasaṃjñārūpatvānnūtanaṃ kiṃcitkarmābhidhatte |
children.translated_text: And that word '<s>jyotis</s>', not referring to anything past, being in the form of a new designation (<s>saṃjñā</s>) of an unprecedented [rite], denotes some new sacrifice.

children.text: tato yathā pūrvatra saṃkhyayā karmabhedaḥ, tathātrāpi saṃjñayā karma bhidyate |
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as in the previous [case] the differentiation of rites was [established] by number, so here too the rite is differentiated by the designation.

children.text: viśvajyotiḥ sarvajyotiḥ śabdayorapyayaṃ nyāyo draṣṭavyaḥ || MJaiNyC_2,2.22-23 ||
children.translated_text: The same reasoning should be applied to the words '<s>viśvajyotiḥ</s>' and '<s>sarvajyotiḥ</s>' as well. || MJaiNyC_2,2.22-23 ||

'<s>Athaiṣa jyotiḥ, athaiṣa viśvajyotiḥ, athaiṣa sarvajyotiḥ, anena sahasradakṣiṇena yajeta</s>' (now this is the <s>Jyotis</s>, now this is the <s>Viśvajyotis</s>, now this is the <s>Sarvajyotis</s>, one should sacrifice with this, giving a thousand as the sacrificial fee) — thus it is heard. Here, the previously established <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is re-stated by '<s>eṣa jyotiḥ</s>' (this is the <s>Jyotis</s>), and a qualifying attribute in the form of giving a thousand is enjoined in that [re-stated rite] — if this be argued: No. Because the previously established <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is cut off by the word '<s>atha</s>' (now). Nor should it be said that in this case the demonstrative pronoun '<s>etat</s>' in '<s>ayam eṣa jyotiḥ</s>' (this is the <s>Jyotis</s>) would be unjustified — because with the demonstrative pronoun '<s>etat</s>', which refers to what is proximate, it is possible to refer not only to what is proximate in the past but also to what is proximate in the future.
(In the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the differentiation of rites caused by difference of deity, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
And the qualifying attributes [would differentiate], when connected with what is unprecedented, because of the equality of the sentences. / Jaim_2,2.23 /
START MJaiNy 2,2.24-25
He composes the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: guṇaḥ karmāntaraṃ vā syādvājibhyo vājinaṃ tviti /
children.translated_text: Is it a qualifying attribute or a different rite? In '<s>vājibhyo vājinam</s>' (for the <s>Vājins</s>, the <s>vājina</s>)—
it is a qualifying attribute, because the already stated [deities] are re-stated, through either cumulation or alternation. // MJaiNy_2,2.24 //
Because [the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> rite is] restricted by the residue of the <s>āmikṣā</s> production, the <s>vājina</s> [substance] there is stronger;
without entering [the existing rite] as a qualifying attribute, it [the substance] establishes a different rite with <s>vājin</s> deities. // MJaiNy_2,2.25 //

children.text:
'tapte payasi dadhyānayati , sā vaiśvadevyāmikṣā, vājibhyo vājinam ' iti śrūyate |
ghanībhūtaḥ payaḥpiṇḍa āmikṣā, jalaṃ vājinam |
tatra --- āmikṣādravyabhājo ye viśve devā uktāḥ, te 'vājibhyaḥ' ityanenānūdyante |
'vājo 'nnamāmikṣārūpameṣāmasti ' iti tanniṣpatteḥ |
tānanūdya vājinadravyarūpo guṇo vidhīyate |
tacca dravyamāmikṣādravyeṇa saha samuccīnatāṃ vikalpyatāṃ vā, iti prāpte --
children.translated_text: And that substance should either be cumulated with or alternated with the <s>āmikṣā</s> substance — having arrived at this position,

we say: Since the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> sacrifice is restricted by the <s>āmikṣā</s> substance as the residue of production, the <s>vājina</s> substance — which is also a residue of production — cannot enter [that rite]. Therefore, the word '<s>vājin</s>' brings about a different deity from the meaning of the word '<s>vājin</s>'.
Therefore, since the form characterized by substance and deity is different, it is a different rite. || MJaiNyC_2,2.24-25 ||

'<s>Tapte payasi dadhy ānayati, sā vaiśvadevyāmikṣā, vājibhyo vājinam</s>' (one brings curds into heated milk — that is the <s>āmikṣā</s> for the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the <s>vājina</s> for the <s>Vājins</s>) — thus it is heard. The solidified lump of milk is the <s>āmikṣā</s>; the liquid (whey) is the <s>vājina</s>. Therein — the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods) who share in the <s>āmikṣā</s> substance are re-stated by '<s>vājibhyaḥ</s>' (for the <s>Vājins</s>). [The reasoning is:] '<s>vāja</s> means food in the form of <s>āmikṣā</s> belongs to them' — [hence they are called <s>Vājins</s>] because of the production [of <s>āmikṣā</s>]. Having thus re-stated them, a qualifying attribute in the form of the <s>vājina</s> substance is enjoined.
(In the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the unity of the rite when a specific substance is not stated, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: aguṇe tu karmaśabde guṇas tatra pratīyeta / Jaim_2,2.24 /
children.translated_text: But when the word denoting the action is devoid of a qualifying attribute, the qualifying attribute would be understood in that [action]. / Jaim_2,2.24 /
START MJaiNy 2,2.26
He composes the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In the offering with curds — is it a different rite, or a qualifying attribute? But as before,
since the <s>Agnihotra</s> is devoid of qualifying attributes, curds and the like are appropriate as qualifying attributes. // MJaiNy_2,2.26 //

children.text:
"dadhaṇa juhoti"iti śrūyate |
tatra -"agnihotraṃ juhoti"ityetasmātprakṛtātkarmaṇo 'nyaddadhihomarūpaṃ karma - iti pūrvanyāyenāvagamyate |
yathā pūrvatra vājinadravyeṇa karma bhidyate, tathā dadhidravyeṇeti cet |
na |
vaiṣamyāt |
yathā vaiśvadevo yāga āmikṣāguṇāvaruddhaḥ, tathāgnihotraṃ na guṇāntarāvaruddham |

children.translated_text: On the contrary — being devoid of qualifying attributes, it requires a qualifying attribute.
Therefore this is a qualifying-attribute injunction.
The same should be understood in '<s>payasā juhoti</s>' (one offers with milk) and similar [cases].

children.text: payodadhyādīnāṃ sarveṣāmutpannaśiṣṭatayāṃ samabalatvādekaikena dravyeṇāgnihotraniṣpatteśca vrīhīyavavadvikalpaḥ || MJaiNyC_2,2.26 ||
children.translated_text: Since all of them — milk, curds, and the like — have equal standing as residues of production, and since the <s>Agnihotra</s> is accomplished by each substance individually, there is an alternation, as in the case of rice and barley. || MJaiNyC_2,2.26 ||

'<s>Dadhnā juhoti</s>' (one offers with curds) is heard. Therein, from the previously established rite '<s>agnihotraṃ juhoti</s>' (one offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>), this curds-offering is a different rite — by the previous reasoning, [it is understood thus]. Just as previously the <s>vājina</s> substance differentiates the rite, so too the curds substance — if this be argued: No. Because of dissimilarity. Just as the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> sacrifice is restricted by the <s>āmikṣā</s> qualifying attribute, the <s>Agnihotra</s> is not restricted by any other qualifying attribute.
(In the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the fruitfulness of substances like curds and the like, <s>sūtras</s> 25-26)

children.text: phalaśrutes tu karma syāt phalasya karmayogitvāt / Jaim_2,2.25 /
children.translated_text: Since a fruit is heard, it would be a [separate] rite, because the fruit is connected with the action. / Jaim_2,2.25 /

children.text: atulyatvāt tu vākyayor guṇe tasya pratīyeta / Jaim_2,2.26 /
children.translated_text: But because the two sentences are not equal, the [fruit] would be understood in the qualifying attribute. / Jaim_2,2.26 /
He composes the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
START MJaiNy 2,2.27-28
In '<s>yad dadhnā indriyakāmasya juhuyāt</s>' (if one should offer with curds for one desiring sense-power) — is that [rite] distinct,

children.text: guṇo vā bhidyate karma dhātvarthasya phalitvataḥ // MJaiNy_2,2.27 //
children.translated_text: or a qualifying attribute? The rite is differentiated because the meaning of the verbal root has fruitfulness. // MJaiNy_2,2.27 //
The burden of possessive secondary usage (<s>matvarthalakṣaṇā</s>) and the like [precludes a different rite]; for the sake of the fruit,
when a qualifying attribute is enjoined, the meaning of the verbal root is re-stated since it was [already] enjoined. // MJaiNy_2,2.28 //

children.text:
"daghnedriyakāmasya juhuyāt"iti śrūyate |
tadidaṃ makṛtādagnihotrādanyatkarma |
ma tvatra vidhiḥ |
kutaḥ |
'indriyakāmasya' ityaktasya phalasya dhātvartha mantareṇa dravyamātrādaniṣpatteḥ - iti cet |
naivam |
karmāntaravidhau 'dadhamatā homenondriyaṃ bhāvayet' iti matvarthalakṣaṇā prasaṅgāt |
guṇaviśiṣṭakriyāvidhau, gauravāt |
prakṛtahānāmakṛtaprakriyāprasaṅgācca |
guṇamātraṃ tu phalāya vidhīyate |
yadyapi 'dadhaṇa juhoti' iti prāptam, tathāpi phalasaṃbandho na praptaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even though '<s>dadhnā juhoti</s>' (one offers with curds) is [already] established, the connection with the fruit is not yet established.
If it be objected that the fruit is impossible without the meaning of the verbal root —
No.
Because the meaning of the verbal root, already enjoined by '<s>agnihotraṃ juhoti</s>' (one offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>), is being re-stated [here]. || MJaiNyC_2,2.27-28 ||

'<s>Dadhnā indriyakāmasya juhuyāt</s>' (one should offer with curds for one desiring sense-power) — thus it is heard. This is a different rite from the previously established <s>Agnihotra</s>. Rather, it is not a [qualifying-attribute] injunction here. Why? Because the fruit stated as '<s>indriyakāmasya</s>' (for one desiring sense-power) cannot be produced from mere substance without the meaning of the verbal root — if this be argued: Not so. Because if a different rite is enjoined, there would be the absurd consequence of possessive secondary usage (<s>matvarthalakṣaṇā</s>): 'one should produce sense-power through a curds-possessing offering.' If it is an injunction of an action qualified by a qualifying attribute, there would be excessive burden. And there would be the faults of abandoning the established [rite] and accepting an unestablished procedure. Rather, only the qualifying attribute is enjoined for the sake of the fruit.
(In the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the different-rite-status of the <s>Vāravantīya</s> and the like, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
When [the components] are equal [in status], it would be appropriate for the action. / Jaim_2,2.27 /
START MJaiNy 2,2.29-31
He composes the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Having stated the <s>Agniṣṭut</s> [sacrifice], the <s>Vāravantīya</s> <s>Sāman</s> of this [rite]
is heard as being performed with <s>Revatī</s> <s>ṛks</s> (verses), for the attainment of cattle as the fruit. // MJaiNy_2,2.29 //
Is the <s>Revatī</s> and the like a qualifying attribute, or a separate rite? As before, it is a qualifying attribute;
the connection of the <s>Revatī</s> [verses] with the <s>Vāravantīya</s> [<s>Sāman</s>] is called [the qualifier], and it yields cattle [as fruit]. // MJaiNy_2,2.30 //
Here, the connection of the <s>Sāman</s> with both the fruit and the action [would cause] sentence-division;
therefore, a different rite endowed with the stated qualifying attributes is declared, for the sake of the fruit. // MJaiNy_2,2.31 //

children.text:
' trivṛdagniṣṭudagniṣṭomastasya vāyavyāsvṛkṣvekaviṃśamagniṣṭomasāma kṛtvā brahmavacasakāmo yajeta ' ityasya saṃnidhau śrūyate - ' etasyaiva revatīṣu vāravantīyamagniṣṭomasāma kṛtvā paśukāmo hyetena yajeta ' iti |
asyāyamarthaḥ - ' agniṣṭomasya vikṛtirūpaḥ kaścidekāho 'gniṣṭunnāmakaḥ |
sa ca pṛṣṭhastotre trivṛtsomayuktatayā 'trivṛt' ityucyate |
agniṣṭomokthādīnāṃ saptānāṃ somasaṃsthānāṃ madhye 'gniṣṭomasaṃsthārūpatvāt ' agniṣṭomaḥ ' ityapyucyate |
prakṛtau tṛtīyasavana ārbhavapavamānasyopari yajñāyajñīyaṃ sāma gīyate |
tena ca sāmnāgniṣṭomayāgasya samāpyamānatvāt ' agniṣṭomasāma ' ityucyate |
tacca prakṛtau 'yajñāyajñā vo agnayaḥ ' ityādyāgneyīṣvṛkṣu gīyate |
asmiṃstvagniṣṭuti brahmavarcasakāmena vāyavyāsvṛkṣu tatsāma gātavyam |
tañca prakṛtāvivaikaviṃśastomayuktam |
paśukāmatya tu ' revatīrnaḥ sadhamādaḥ'- ityādiṣu revatīṣvakṣu vāravantīyaṃ sāma gāyet, iti |
tatra revatīnāmṛcāṃ vāravantīyanāmakena sāmnā yaḥ saṃbandhaḥ, so 'yaṃ paśuphalāyāgniṣṭuti vidhīyate |
'etasyaiva ' iti prakṛtaparāmarśakenaitacchabdena, anyavyāvartakenaivakāreṇa cāgniṣṭutaḥ samarpyamāṇatvāt |
yathā pūrvādhikaraṇa indriyaphalāya prakṛte 'gnihotre dadhiguṇo vihitaḥ,tadvat |
iti prāpte, brūmaḥ- viṣamo dṛṣṭāntaḥ |
dadhaṇe homajanakatvaṃ na śāstreṇa bodhanīyam |
tasya lokato 'vagantuṃ śakyatvāt |
phalasaṃbandha eka eva śāstrabodhya iti na tatra vākyabhedaḥ |
children.translated_text: The connection with the fruit alone needs to be taught by <s>śāstra</s> — hence there is no sentence-division there.

children.text: iha tu - revatyugādhārakavāravantīyasāmno 'gniṣṭutkarmasādhanatvaṃ phalasādhanatvaṃ cetyubhayasya śāstraikabodhyatvāddurvāro vākyabhedaḥ |
children.translated_text: But here — since both the capacity of the <s>Revatī</s>-based <s>Vāravantīya</s> <s>Sāman</s> to serve as a means of the <s>Agniṣṭut</s> rite, and its capacity to produce the fruit, are to be taught by <s>śāstra</s> alone — sentence-division is unavoidable.
Therefore, a different rite qualified by the stated attributes and yielding cattle as its fruit is enjoined here.
The demonstrative '<s>etat</s>' and the exclusionary '<s>eva</s>' should be construed as pertaining to the different rite being enjoined. || MJaiNyC_2,2.29-31 ||

In the vicinity of '<s>trivṛd agniṣṭud agniṣṭomas tasya vāyavyāsv ṛkṣv ekaviṃśam agniṣṭomasāma kṛtvā brahmavarcasakāmo yajeta</s>' (the <s>Agniṣṭut</s> is a threefold <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>; having performed the <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s> with the twenty-one-fold [stoma] on the <s>Vāyavya</s> verses, one desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s> should sacrifice), it is heard: '<s>etasyaiva revatīṣu vāravantīyam agniṣṭomasāma kṛtvā paśukāmo hy etena yajeta</s>' (having performed the <s>Vāravantīya</s> <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s> on the <s>Revatī</s> verses of this very [rite], one desiring cattle should indeed sacrifice with it). The meaning is: There is a particular one-day (<s>ekāha</s>) sacrifice called <s>Agniṣṭut</s>, which is a modification of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. It is called '<s>trivṛt</s>' (threefold) because it is connected with the <s>Trivṛt</s> <s>Soma</s> in the <s>Pṛṣṭha-stotra</s>. Among the seven <s>Soma-saṃsthās</s> (forms of <s>Soma</s> sacrifice) — <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, <s>Ukthya</s>, and so on — it is called '<s>Agniṣṭoma</s>' because it has the form of the <s>Agniṣṭoma-saṃsthā</s>. In the archetype, during the third pressing (<s>tṛtīya-savana</s>), above the <s>Ārbhava-pavamāna</s>, the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> <s>Sāman</s> is sung. Because the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> sacrifice is completed by that <s>Sāman</s>, it is called '<s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s>.' In the archetype, it is sung on the <s>Āgneya</s> <s>ṛks</s> beginning with '<s>yajñā yajñā vo agnayaḥ</s>' (O fires of sacrifice). But in this <s>Agniṣṭut</s>, by one desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual lustre), that <s>Sāman</s> should be sung on the <s>Vāyavya</s> <s>ṛks</s> (verses addressed to <s>Vāyu</s>). And that [<s>Sāman</s>], as in the archetype, is connected with the twenty-one-fold <s>Stoma</s>. But for one desiring cattle, one should sing the <s>Vāravantīya</s> <s>Sāman</s> on the <s>Revatī</s> <s>ṛks</s> beginning with '<s>revatīr naḥ sadhamādaḥ</s>' (may the <s>Revatī</s> [verses bless] our fellowship). Therein, the connection of the <s>Revatī</s> <s>ṛks</s> with the <s>Vāravantīya</s> <s>Sāman</s> — this connection is enjoined in the <s>Agniṣṭut</s> for the fruit of cattle. Because [the <s>Agniṣṭut</s>] is being referred to by the demonstrative pronoun '<s>etat</s>' in '<s>etasyaiva</s>' (of this very one) and by the exclusionary word '<s>eva</s>' (alone). Just as in the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the curds qualifying attribute was enjoined in the established <s>Agnihotra</s> for the fruit of sense-power, so too [here] — having arrived at this position, we say: The analogy is not apt. In the case of curds, its capacity to produce an oblation does not need to be taught by <s>śāstra</s>, since it can be known from the world.
(In the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the unity of the desired result in the <s>Saubhara</s> and its <s>nidhana</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 28-29)
In the <s>Saubhara</s>, because of the hearing of [specific] persons, the <s>nidhana</s> (concluding portion) is connected with the desired result. / Jaim_2,2.28 /

children.text: sarvasya voktakāmatvāt tasmin kāmaśrutiḥ syān nidhanārthā punaḥ śrutiḥ / Jaim_2,2.29 /
children.translated_text: Or, because [the <s>Saubhara</s>] fulfills the desires of all, the mention of the desires [in the <s>nidhana</s> passages] would be for the purpose of [specifying] the <s>nidhana</s>; the repeated statement is [merely a re-iteration]. / Jaim_2,2.29 /
START MJaiNy 2,2.32-35
He composes the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
For those desiring rain, food, and heaven, the <s>Saubhara</s> <s>stotra</s> (chant) is prescribed;
the <s>nidhanas</s> (concluding portions) — '<s>hīṣ</s>', '<s>ūrk</s>', etc. — are also for those desiring rain and the like. // MJaiNy_2,2.32 //
Are rain and the like a different fruit for '<s>hīṣ</s>' and the like, or [the same fruit] stated [in the <s>Saubhara</s>]?
When the <s>Saubhara</s>'s fruit is differentiated, the <s>nidhana</s> is being restricted [to a specific form]. // MJaiNy_2,2.33 //
The different fruit is stated with the dative case: '<s>vṛṣṭikāmāya hīṣ iti</s>' (for one desiring rain, [the <s>nidhana</s> is] '<s>hīṣ</s>');
the fruit of the <s>Saubhara</s> is rain [etc.], and this is augmented by the conjunction with '<s>hīṣ</s>' [and so on]. // MJaiNy_2,2.34 //
There is no separateness of those desiring rain, food, and [heaven] as stated, due to recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>);
even in [the case of] restriction, this dative case is justified because of the purposive relationship (<s>tādarthya</s>). // MJaiNy_2,2.35 //

' yo vṛṣṭikāmo yo 'nnādyakāmo yaḥ svargakāmaḥ sa saubhareṇa stuvīta, sarve vai kāmāḥ saubhare ' iti samāmnāya punaḥ samāmnātam - hīṣita vṛṣṭikāmāya nidhanaṃ kuryāt, ūrgityannādyakāmāya, ū iti svargakāmāya ' iti |
saubharaṃ nāma sāmaviśeṣaḥ |

kutaḥ |
hīṣādividhivākye 'vṛṣṭikāmāya ' ityādinā caturthīśravaṇāt |
tādarthye bruvatī [caturthī] hīṣādīnāṃ vṛṣṭyādikāmapuruṣaśeṣatvaṃ gamayati |

children.translated_text: Not so.

children.text: phalatrayakāmāṇāṃ trayāṇāmaniyamenaiva hīṣādiṣu madhye yasya kasyacinnidhanasya prāptau vidherniyamārthatvāt |
children.translated_text: Because the injunction serves the purpose of restriction (<s>niyama</s>): when the three persons desiring the three fruits could, without restriction, use any of the <s>nidhanas</s> like '<s>hīṣ</s>' and the like.

children.text: tādarthya tu phalāntarābhāve 'pi saubharavākyoktavṛṣṭyādiphalasādhane saubhare hīṣādīnāṃ niyamyamānatvādupapadyate |
children.translated_text: And the purposive relationship (<s>tādarthya</s>) [expressed by the dative] is justified even without a separate fruit, because '<s>hīṣ</s>' and the like are being restricted within the <s>Saubhara</s>, which is the means of producing the rain and other fruits stated in the <s>Saubhara</s> sentence.
Therefore — this is an injunction of restriction regarding specific <s>nidhana</s> forms. || MJaiNyC_2,2.32-35 ||

'<s>Yo vṛṣṭikāmo yo 'nnādyakāmo yaḥ svargakāmaḥ sa saubhareṇa stuvīta, sarve vai kāmāḥ saubhare</s>' (one who desires rain, one who desires food, one who desires heaven — he should chant with the <s>Saubhara</s>; for all desires are [fulfilled] in the <s>Saubhara</s>) — having thus prescribed, it is further prescribed: '<s>hīṣ iti vṛṣṭikāmāya nidhanaṃ kuryāt, ūrg ity annādyakāmāya, ū iti svargakāmāya</s>' (one should make the <s>nidhana</s> [concluding portion] as '<s>hīṣ</s>' for one desiring rain, '<s>ūrk</s>' for one desiring food, '<s>ū</s>' for one desiring heaven). The <s>Saubhara</s> is a particular <s>Sāman</s> (chant). The <s>nidhana</s> is the final part of a <s>Sāman</s> that consists of five or seven sections. In that <s>nidhana</s>, the specific forms '<s>hīṣ</s>' and the like are enjoined to produce fruits — rain and the like — that are separate from the <s>stotra</s>-fruits of rain and the like produced by the <s>Saubhara</s> <s>Sāman</s>. Why? Because the dative case is heard in the injunctive sentence of '<s>hīṣ</s>' and the like: '<s>vṛṣṭikāmāya</s>' (for one desiring rain) and so on. The dative case, expressing purpose (<s>tādarthya</s>), conveys that '<s>hīṣ</s>' and the like are subordinate to the person desiring rain and the like. And that subordination is justified when [they are] means to the fruit desired by the person. Therefore, the <s>Saubhara</s> and the specific <s>nidhana</s> form '<s>hīṣ</s>' each produce [separate] rain as fruit. From the combination of both, a great rain [results] — having arrived at this position, we say: The person desiring rain and the like who is [mentioned] in the <s>Saubhara</s> injunction is the very same person recognized (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) in the '<s>hīṣ</s>' and other injunctions. Therefore, the rain and the like that are the fruit of the <s>Saubhara</s> are the very same ones re-stated in the '<s>hīṣ</s>' and other sentences — hence there is no separate fruit. If it be argued: since there is no new separate fruit, and since '<s>hīṣ</s>' and the like are already obtained in the <s>Saubhara</s> through the study of various Vedic recensions (<s>śākhā</s>), this injunction is purposeless —

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīye jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistare dvitīyādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>pāda</s> of the second <s>adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Mādhavīya Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s>.

children.translated_text: But in the case of one [rite], since there is differentiation by indicatory mark, the unity would be stated for the sake of purpose, because of being a qualifying sentence. / Jaim_2,3.2 /
START MJaiNy 2,3.1-3
He composes the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the third <s>pāda</s>—
In a <s>Soma</s> sacrifice, the <s>Rathaṃtara</s> <s>sāman</s> would be present, and likewise <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Jagat</s>;
and the cups (<s>graha</s>) with <s>Aindravāyava</s>, <s>Śukra</s>, and <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> having priority are heard. // MJaiNy_2,3.1 //
Is what is associated with <s>Rathaṃtara</s> and the like a distinct rite, or a qualifying attribute (<s>guṇa</s>)?

Since there is distinction from the prior [<s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>] endowed with <s>Gāyatrī</s> and the like, [the <s>Rathaṃtara</s> etc.] are qualifying attributes [serving that distinction]. // MJaiNy_2,3.2 //
In the context of the word '<s>Soma</s>,' which refers to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>,
the priority of cups is a qualifying attribute, and the distinction is mutual [among the alternatives]. // MJaiNy_2,3.3 //

children.translated_text: For in the archetype, no <s>sāman</s> produced in a <s>Jagatī</s> [meter verse] is prescribed.

children.text: ata eva daśamādhyāye pañcamapādasya pañcadaśādhikaraṇe prathamavarṇake"yadi jagattāmā"iti vākyoktamāgrayaṇāgratvaṃ vikṛtau viṣuvannāmake mukhye 'hani vyavasthāpitam |
children.translated_text: For that very reason, in the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the fifth <s>pāda</s> of the tenth <s>adhyāya</s>, in the first section, the priority of <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> stated in the sentence 'if it has the <s>Jagat</s> <s>sāman</s>' has been established as applicable in the modification (<s>vikṛti</s>) called <s>Viṣuvat</s>, which is the principal day.
Granted, even so there is no contradiction here.

children.text: āgrayaṇāgratvavākyaṃ na karmāntaravidhāyakam, kiṃtu 'anyena vihite somayāge yatra jagatsāma saṃbhavati tatra guṇavidhāyakam - ' ityetāvanmātrasyātra pratipādyatvāt || MJaiNyC_2,3.1-3 ||
children.translated_text: The sentence about <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> priority does not enjoin a separate rite, but rather enjoins a qualifying attribute in any <s>Soma</s> sacrifice prescribed by another [authority] where the <s>Jagat</s> <s>sāman</s> is possible — this much alone is what is established here. || MJaiNyC_2,3.1-3 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> context it is heard: 'If the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice has the <s>Rathaṃtara</s> <s>sāman</s>, one should draw the cups with <s>Aindravāyava</s> having priority. If it has the <s>Bṛhat</s> <s>sāman</s>, with <s>Śukra</s> having priority. If it has the <s>Jagat</s> <s>sāman</s>, with <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> having priority.' Therein, by the word '<s>Soma</s>,' a sacrifice accomplished with the <s>Soma</s> plant is denoted. In that sacrifice, on the pressing day, in the back-chant (<s>pṛṣṭha-stotra</s>), the <s>sāmans</s> named <s>Rathaṃtara</s>, <s>Bṛhat</s>, and <s>Jagat</s> are alternatively prescribed. The <s>Rathaṃtara</s> is produced in the matrix [hymn beginning] '<s>abhi tvā śūra</s>.' The <s>Bṛhat</s> is produced in [the hymn beginning] '<s>tvāmiddhi havāmahe</s>.' The <s>Jagat</s> is produced in a <s>Ṛc</s> verse in the <s>Jagatī</s> meter. The cups named <s>Aindravāyava</s>, <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, <s>Āśvina</s>, <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Manthya</s>, <s>Āgrayaṇa</s>, <s>Ukthya</s>, <s>Dhruva</s>, and so on are drawn in the morning pressing (<s>prātaḥsavana</s>). They are called cups (<s>graha</s>) because of the drawing (<s>grahaṇa</s>) of the <s>Soma</s> juice into wooden vessels. In the case where the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice has the <s>Rathaṃtara</s> <s>sāman</s>, among these cups the <s>Aindravāyava</s> is to be drawn first. In the case of the <s>Bṛhat</s> <s>sāman</s>, the <s>Śukra</s>. In the case of the <s>Jagat</s> <s>sāman</s>, the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> has priority — this is the meaning of the subject-passage. Therein, the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> under discussion is endowed with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and other <s>sāmans</s>; to distinguish from it, the <s>Rathaṃtara</s> and the like are mentioned here as qualifying attributes. Therefore — distinct rites endowed with qualifying attributes such as <s>Aindravāyava</s> priority and the like are here enjoined — having arrived at this position, we say: The word '<s>Soma</s>' stated in 'if the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice has the <s>Rathaṃtara</s> <s>sāman</s>,' along with the context, refers to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> here. When that is identified, the priority of cups as stated is enjoined as a qualifying attribute. Nor is it possible that by the restatement of <s>Rathaṃtara</s> and the like as qualifying attributes, the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is being distinguished [from a separate rite] — because even though [the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>] is endowed with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and other <s>sāmans</s> in its morning pressing and the like, it also has the possibility of being associated with <s>Rathaṃtara</s> and the like in the back-chant. If it be asked 'what then is being distinguished?' — we say: it is the mutual distinction among <s>Rathaṃtara</s>, <s>Bṛhat</s>, and <s>Jagat</s>. The <s>Rathaṃtara</s> and the like are presented as alternatives in the back-chant. Therein, by the restatement of <s>Rathaṃtara</s>, the other two alternatives are distinguished. Similarly in the other cases. Therefore — this is an injunction of a qualifying attribute. But the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> under discussion is the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>) for other <s>Soma</s> sacrifices.
(In the second [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the topic of whether the <s>Aveṣṭi</s> constitutes a separate rite, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
In the <s>Aveṣṭi</s>, because of the connection with the sacrifice, the rite is said to be primary. / Jaim_2,3.3 /
START MJaiNy 2,3.4-6
He composes the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s>—
In the <s>Rājasūya</s>, a sacrifice called <s>Aveṣṭi</s> is heard as the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>); but therein,
due to the distinction of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, and <s>Vaiśya</s>, there is a reversal of the order of oblations (<s>havis</s>). // MJaiNy_2,3.4 //
The mention of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like would be a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>), or the [sentence] having the character of a restatement is for the purpose of conferring [eligibility];

children.text: vyatyayāya trayāṇāṃ ca rājatvāprāptirasti hi // MJaiNy_2,3.5 //
children.translated_text: and for the reversal of the three, there is indeed non-attainment of kingship (<s>rājatva</s>). // MJaiNy_2,3.5 //
Kingship does not arise from the connection with ruling; rather, it is <s>Kṣatriya</s> birth in reality;
therefore this is the conferral of what was not [previously] attained — hence there is no similarity with the <s>Rathaṃtara</s> case. // MJaiNy_2,3.6 //

children.text:
rājasūyaprakaraṇe kācidiṣṭiraveṣṭināmikā śrūyate -
"āgneyamaṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet , hiraṇyaṃ dakṣiṇā |
aindramākādaśakapālam, ṛṣabho dakṣiṇā |
vaiśvadevaṃ carum , piśaṅgī praṣṭhauhī dākṣiṇā |
maitrāvaruṇīmāmikṣām, vaśā dakṣiṇā |
bārhaspatyaṃ carum, śitipṛṣṭho dikṣaṇāṃ"iti |
tasyāmeveṣṭau haviṣāṃ kramavyatyayaḥ śrūyate -"yadi brāhmaṇo yajeta, bārhaspatyaṃ madhye nidhāyā'hutiṃ hutvā tamabhighārayet |
yadi rājanya aindram |
yadi vaiśyo vaiśvadevam"iti |
tatra yathā pūrvādhikaraṇe - aindravāyavāgratvaṃ vyavasthāpayituṃ yadiśabdayuktena vākyena rathaṃtaraṃ nimittatvenānūditam, evamatrāpi pañcamasthāne śrūyamāṇaṃ bārhaspatyaṃ caruṃ madhye tṛtīyasthāne sthāpayituṃ 'yadi rādanyaḥ' ityanuvādaḥ |
vaiśvadevasya tu svata eva tṛtīyasthāne śravaṇāttatra madhye nidhānavidhirnityāmuvādaḥ |
nanu rājakartṛke rājasūye brāhmaṇavaiśyayoḥ prāptyabhāvānnānuvādo yuktaḥ- iti cet |
na |
tayorapi rājyayogaheturājaśabdārthatvāt, iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- rājaśabdaḥ kṣattriyajātau rūḍhaḥ, na tu rājyayogastasya pravṛttinimittam |
pratyuta- rājyaśabdasya rājayogaḥ pravṛttinimittam |
'rājñaḥ karma' iti vigṛhya rājaprātipadikasyopari |
pratyayaviśeṣavidhānāt |
brāhyaṇavaiśyayoḥ prajāpālanena rājyaśabda upacaritaḥ |
tasmāt - aveṣṭau brāhmaṇavaiśyau pūrvamaprāptāvanena vacanena prāpyete |
nanu rājasūyasya rājakartṛkatvāttadantargatāyā aveṣṭerapi tathātvāttasyāṃ brāhmaṇavaiśyayoḥ prāpaṇamayuktam - iti cet |

children.translated_text: Not so.
Although this is impossible in the case of the <s>Aveṣṭi</s> performed within [the <s>Rājasūya</s>], it is possible for the <s>Aveṣṭi</s> when performed outside the <s>Rājasūya</s>.

children.text: tasmāt - atra brāhmaṇādikartṛkaṃ yathoktaguṇaviśiṣṭaṃ karmāntaraṃ vidhīyata iti na rathaṃtarāditulyatvam |
children.translated_text: Therefore — here a distinct rite performed by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the like, qualified by the attributes mentioned, is enjoined; hence there is no similarity with the <s>Rathaṃtara</s> case.
As for the word '<s>yadi</s>' (if) — being a particle (<s>nipāta</s>), whether it is meaningless or denotes a different meaning may be inferred [from context]. || MJaiNyC_2,3.4-6 ||

In the <s>Rājasūya</s> context, a certain sacrifice called <s>Aveṣṭi</s> is heard: 'He should offer an <s>Āgneya</s> cake on eight potsherds; gold is the sacrificial fee. An <s>Aindra</s> cake on eleven potsherds; a bull is the fee. A <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> porridge; a tawny draft-cow is the fee. A <s>Maitrāvaruṇī</s> coagulated milk; a barren cow is the fee. A <s>Bārhaspatya</s> porridge; a white-backed [cow] is the fee.' In that very <s>Aveṣṭi</s>, a reversal of the order of oblations is heard: 'If a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> were to sacrifice, having placed the <s>Bārhaspatya</s> in the middle, having offered the oblation, he should pour ghee over it. If a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, the <s>Aindra</s>. If a <s>Vaiśya</s>, the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.' Therein, just as in the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s> the <s>Rathaṃtara</s> was restated as a cause by means of a sentence containing the word 'if' in order to establish the priority of the <s>Aindravāyava</s> cup, so too here, the <s>Bārhaspatya</s> porridge heard in the fifth position is restated to place it in the middle, third position, [using the sentence] 'if a <s>Kṣatriya</s>.' For the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, since it is already heard in the third position by its own [original placement], the injunction of placing it in the middle is a perpetual restatement (<s>nityānuvāda</s>). But if it be objected that since the <s>Rājasūya</s> is performed by a king, and since <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s> are not eligible, a restatement [of their eligibility] is inappropriate — no. Because even for those two, the word '<s>rāja</s>' (king) means one connected with ruling — having arrived at this position, we say: the word '<s>rāja</s>' is conventionally fixed (<s>rūḍha</s>) in the <s>Kṣatriya</s> caste, and the connection with ruling is not the reason for its application. Rather, the connection with a king is the reason for the application of the word '<s>rājya</s>' (kingdom). [This is known] because, having analyzed it as '<s>rājñaḥ karma</s>' (the action of a king), a specific suffix is prescribed upon the stem '<s>rāja</s>.' For <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s>, the word '<s>rājya</s>' is used figuratively due to their governing of subjects. Therefore — in the <s>Aveṣṭi</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and <s>Vaiśya</s>, who were previously not eligible, are made eligible by this statement. But if it be objected that since the <s>Rājasūya</s> is performed by a king, the <s>Aveṣṭi</s> which is a component thereof is also the same, and making <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s> eligible therein is inappropriate —
(In the third [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the topic of whether <s>Ādhāna</s> (fire-establishment) is to be newly enjoined, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
In the <s>Ādhāna</s> (fire-establishment), because of serving all [sacrifices]. / Jaim_2,3.4 /
START MJaiNy 2,3.7-9
He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s>—
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should establish the [sacrificial] fires in spring; therein one should initiate him;
is this a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>), or is it a conferral [of new eligibility]? The restatement would be for establishing the [specific] time. // MJaiNy_2,3.7 //
Because without fire and Vedic learning (<s>vidyā</s>), the performance of rites is impossible;
when <s>Ādhāna</s> and <s>Upanayana</s> (initiation) are established by presumption (<s>kḷpti</s>), the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the like are [already] eligible. // MJaiNy_2,3.8 //
Since the accomplishment is possible through ordinary fire and books, there is no need for presumption;
therefore what is enjoined here is something not [previously] attained, connected with the specific time, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, and the like. // MJaiNy_2,3.9 //

children.text:
"vasante brāhmaṇo 'gnīnādadhīta |
grīṣme rājanyaḥ |
śaradi vaiśyaḥ"iti śrūyate |
"vasante brāhmaṇamupanayīta |
grīṣme rājanyam |
śaradi vaiśyam"iti ca |
tatra vasantādikālaviśeṣaṃ vidhātuṃ brāhmaṇādayo 'nūdyante |
na ca teṣāṃ prāptyabhāvaḥ |
kratvanuṣṭhānānyathānupapattyā kḷptatvāt |
na hyāhutyādhārabhūtamagnim, anuṣṭhānaprakārajñāpikāṃ vidyāṃ ca vinā karmānuṣṭhānaṃ saṃbhavati |
agniśca nā'dhānamantareṇāstīti brāhmaṇādikartṛkamādhānaṃ kalpayati, vidyā copanayanapūrvakādhyayanamantareṇā saṃbhavantī brāhmaṇādyupanayanaṃ kalpayati - iti tatra prāptiḥ- iti cet |
children.translated_text: And since fire does not exist without <s>Ādhāna</s> (fire-establishment), one postulates by presumption the <s>Ādhāna</s> performed by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the like; and since knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) is impossible without study preceded by <s>Upanayana</s> (initiation), one postulates by presumption the <s>Upanayana</s> of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the like — thus the eligibility is attained — if so it is argued,
not so.

children.text: laukikāgnau hotuṃ, pustakapāṭhenādhigantuṃ ca śakyatvenā'dhānopanayanayorakalpane brāhmaṇādīnāmaprāpteḥ |
children.translated_text: Because, since it is possible to offer oblations in ordinary fire and to acquire [knowledge] by reading from books, the <s>Ādhāna</s> and <s>Upanayana</s> are not postulated by presumption, and hence the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the like have not [already] attained [eligibility].

children.text: tasmāt - vasantādikālaviśiṣṭe brāhmaṇādikartṛke ādhānopanayane atra vidhīyete || MJaiNyC_2,3.7-9 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — the <s>Ādhāna</s> and <s>Upanayana</s> qualified by the specific time of spring and the like, and performed by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the like, are here enjoined [as something new]. || MJaiNyC_2,3.7-9 ||

It is heard: 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should establish the sacrificial fires in spring. A <s>Kṣatriya</s> in summer. A <s>Vaiśya</s> in autumn.' And also: 'One should initiate a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in spring. A <s>Kṣatriya</s> in summer. A <s>Vaiśya</s> in autumn.' Therein, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the like are restated in order to enjoin the specific time — spring and so on. Nor is there a non-attainment of their [eligibility]. Because [their eligibility] is established by presumption (<s>kḷpti</s>) from the otherwise-impossibility of performing rites. For the performance of rites is impossible without fire, which serves as the receptacle of oblations, and without knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), which makes known the manner of performance.
(In the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the status of <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> and the like as qualifying attributes, <s>sūtras</s> 5-11:)
In the half-yearly periods (<s>ayana</s>), the injunction is distinct because of the attachment of a name (<s>saṃjñā</s>). / Jaim_2,3.5 /
And the injunction pertaining to a rite [comes] from what is not a qualifying attribute. / Jaim_2,3.6 /
And the sentence is complete with regard to the result. / Jaim_2,3.7 /
Or it would be a modification (<s>vikāra</s>), because of the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>). / Jaim_2,3.8 /
And because of the observation of indicatory marks (<s>liṅga</s>). / Jaim_2,3.9 /
The attachment of a name is due to the qualifying attribute. / Jaim_2,3.10 /
The completeness [of the sentence] is not distinctive. / Jaim_2,3.11 /
He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>—
That which [is stated as] 'one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice' —
is it a distinct rite, or a qualifying attribute stated in the <s>Darśa</s> and other [sacrifices] for the attainment of the result [of heaven]? // MJaiNy_2,3.10 //
START MJaiNy 2,3.10-11
Since this qualifying attribute is not well-known, this would be a differentiation of rite by name (<s>saṃjñā</s>);

children.text: guṇo vyutpattiśeṣābhyāmāvṛttyākhyo na nāma tat // MJaiNy_2,3.11 //
children.translated_text: [but] it is a qualifying attribute [established] by etymology (<s>vyutpatti</s>) and contextual remainder (<s>śeṣa</s>) — the one called 'repetition' (<s>āvṛtti</s>) — that is not a rite-name. // MJaiNy_2,3.11 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsaprakaraṇe śrūyate -"dākṣāyaṇayajñena svargakāmo yajeta"iti |
tatra - dākṣāyaṇaśabdavācyasya kasyacidguṇasya loke prasiddhyabhāvādudbhidādivadyaṇisāmānādhikaraṇyena karmanāmatvāt |
"athaiṣa jyotiḥ"ityādivadarpūvasaṃjñāyāṃ karmāntaravidhiḥ- iti cet |
na |
dākṣāyaṇaśabdasyā'vṛttivācakatvāt |
tacca śabdanirvacanādvākyaśeṣādvāvagamyate |
tathā hi - 'ayanam' ityāvṛttirucyate |
'dakṣasyeme dākṣāḥ, teṣāmayanam' iti tannirvacanam |
dakṣa utsāhī punaḥ punarāvṛttāvanalasa ityarthaḥ |
tadīyānāṃ prayogāṇāmāvṛttirdākṣāyaṇaśabdārthaḥ |
tathā cā'vṛttyā yuktaḥ prakṛto darśapūrṇamāsātmako yajño dākṣāyaṇayajñaḥ |
āvṛttiprakārastu"dve paurṇamāsyau yajeta |
dve amāvāsye"ityādivākyaśeṣādavagamyate |
tato dadhyādivatprasiddhārthatvāddarśapūrṇamāsayoḥ prakṛtayorayaṃ svargaphalasiddyarthamāvṛttyākhyaguṇavidhiḥ, na tūdbhidādivatkarmanāmadheyam |

children.translated_text: Similarly, in the passage 'one desiring cattle should sacrifice with the <s>Sākaṃprasthāpya</s>,' the same should be observed.

children.text: amāvāsyāyāge dvau dvau dohau saṃpādya catasṛṇāṃ dadhipayasoḥ kumbhīnāṃ saha prasthāpanaṃ sākaṃ prasthāpyaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the new-moon sacrifice, having produced two milkings each of four pots of curds and milk, the simultaneous dispatching [of the pots] constitutes the <s>Sākaṃprasthāpya</s>.
The sacrifice conjoined with that is the <s>Sākaṃprasthāpya</s>.

children.text: tathāsati prakṛte darśayāgo paśuphalāya sākaṃprasthāpyākhyo guṇo vidhīyate || MJaiNyC_2,3.10-11 ||
children.translated_text: This being so, in the <s>Darśa</s> sacrifice under discussion, a qualifying attribute called <s>Sākaṃprasthāpya</s> is enjoined for the attainment of the fruit of cattle. || MJaiNyC_2,3.10-11 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context, it is heard: 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice.' Therein — since no qualifying attribute denoted by the word '<s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s>' is well-known in the world, by virtue of the co-referentiality of the <s>yaṇ</s> suffix with the rite, it would be a rite-name like <s>Udbhid</s> and the like. Since the name has not been previously [encountered], like '<s>athaiṣa jyotiḥ</s>' (now this is the <s>Jyotis</s>) and the like, this would be an injunction of a separate rite — if so it is argued, no. Because the word '<s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s>' denotes 'repetition' (<s>āvṛtti</s>). And this is understood either from the etymological analysis of the word or from the contextual remainder of the sentence. For thus: '<s>ayana</s>' means 'repetition.' 'The <s>Dākṣas</s> are those [rites] belonging to <s>Dakṣa</s>; their <s>ayana</s> (practice) is <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s>' — this is its etymological analysis. <s>Dakṣa</s> means one who is diligent, meaning one who is not lazy in repeated performance. The repetition of his performances is the meaning of the word <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s>. And thus, the sacrifice under discussion in the form of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, conjoined with repetition, is the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice. The manner of repetition is understood from the contextual remainder: 'one should sacrifice on two full-moon days; on two new-moon days' and so on. Therefore, just as curds and the like have well-known meanings, so too this is an injunction of a qualifying attribute called repetition in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> sacrifices, which are the archetype rites under discussion, for the attainment of the fruit of heaven — and not a rite-name like <s>Udbhid</s> and the like.
(In the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the topic of whether [sentences] endowed with substance and deity constitute separate rites, <s>sūtras</s> 12-15:)
And when preparatory rites (<s>saṃskāra</s>) [are mentioned] outside the [main] context, they are due to the name of the rite. / Jaim_2,3.12 /

children.text: yāvad uktaṃ vā karmaṇaḥ śrutimūlatvāt / Jaim_2,3.13 /
children.translated_text: Or [it could be] as much as stated, because the rite is rooted in scripture (<s>śruti</s>). / Jaim_2,3.13 /

children.text: yajatis tu dravyaphalabhoktṛsaṃyogād eteṣāṃ karmasambandhāt / Jaim_2,3.14 /
children.translated_text: But the word '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices), because of the conjunction of substance, fruit, and agent — [these are all] connected with the rite. / Jaim_2,3.14 /
And because of the observation of indicatory marks (<s>liṅga</s>). / Jaim_2,3.15 /
START MJaiNy 2,3.12-14
He composes the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>—

children.text: vāyavyaḥ śveta ālabhyo bhūtyai saurye caruṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: A white [animal] sacred to <s>Vāyu</s> should be sacrificed for prosperity; likewise, in the <s>Saurya</s> [rite], a <s>caru</s> (oblation cake)
should be offered for <s>Brahman</s>-radiance; [the question concerns] the pole-grasping (<s>īṣā</s>) and the handful-offering (<s>muṣṭi</s>). // MJaiNy_2,3.12 //
Are the whiteness and the <s>caru</s> qualifying attributes, or [are these] the rites stated so far?

children.text: phalārthe athavā yāge viśiṣṭau vihitāviha // MJaiNy_2,3.13 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, [are these] sacrifices enjoined here as qualified [by those attributes] for the purpose of [specific] fruits? // MJaiNy_2,3.13 //
Whiteness and [belonging to] <s>Vāyu</s> are [attributes] in the <s>īṣā</s> [rite]; [it is] <s>Āgneya</s> and <s>Sūrya</s>-resplendent;
the <s>caru</s> is a qualifying attribute; <s>caru</s> means a cooking vessel (<s>sthālī</s>); and the offering (<s>nirvāpa</s>) depends on it. // MJaiNy_2,3.14 //
It is not a qualifying attribute because of the abandonment of the [stated] fruit; but what then? It is the rite as far as stated;
since the sacrificial form (<s>yāgatā</s>) is established through the completeness of substance and the like, the purposive [sacrifice] cannot be prevented. // MJaiNy_2,3.15 //

children.text:
anārabhyedamāmnāyat - 'vāyavyaṃ śvetamālabheta bhūtikāmaḥ' iti, 'saurye caruṃ nirvapedbrahmavarcasakāmaḥ' iti ca |
tathā -darśapūrṇamāsayoridamāmnāyater -"iṣāmālabheta"iti,"caturo muṣṭīnnirvapati"iti car |
iṣā śakaṭagato lāṅgaladaṇḍavaddīrghaḥ kāṣṭhaviśeṣaḥ |
tasyā ālambhaḥ sparśaḥ |
tametaṃ darśapūrṇamāsagatamīṣālambhamanūdya tasyāmālabhyāyāmīṣāyāṃ śvetatvaguṇo vidhīyate |
tasya ca śvetakāṣṭhasya vāyunā spṛśyamānatvādvāyavyatā saṃbhavati |
tathā - caturmuṣṭinirvapaṇamanūdya carurguṇatvena vidhīyate |
caruḥ sthālī |
sā ca nirvāpasyā'śrayaḥ |
niruptasya haviṣa āgneyatayā sūryavatprabhāsaṃbandhātsauryavat |
bhūtibrahmavarcase phale ca sarvakāmikayordarśapūrṇamāsayoḥ pūrvasiddhe evānūdyete |
tasmāt - guṇavidhī - ityekaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ |
nahi phalapadayornityavacchrutayoḥ saṃbhavatprayojanayośca pākṣikānuvādatvam, ānarthakyaṃ vā yuktam |
tasmāt --guṇaphalaviśiṣṭe karmāntare vidhīyete |
tadāpi yāgasyāśravaṇādīlambhanirvāpayoreva śravaṇādyāvaduktakarmavidhiḥ- iti dvitīyaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ |

children.translated_text: Since the substance — the white animal and the <s>caru</s> — and the deities — <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Sūrya</s> — are clearly apprehended, and since purposive sacrifices (<s>yāga</s>) that possess the [complete sacrificial] form cannot be prevented, the injunction of sacrifices qualified by [specific] substance and deity must be accepted.

children.text: 'bhūtikāmo vāyavyena śvetena paśunā yajeta' 'brahmavarcasakāmaḥ sauryeṇa caruṇā yajeta' ityevaṃvidhor'thasiddho vidhiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'One desiring prosperity should sacrifice with a white animal sacred to <s>Vāyu</s>'; 'One desiring the radiance of <s>Brahman</s> should sacrifice with a <s>Saurya caru</s>' — thus the injunction is established by the meaning itself (<s>arthasiddha</s>).

children.text: dravyadevatāsaṃbandhakalpitasya yāgasya liṅpratyayena kartavyatāvidhāvālambhanirvāpayordhātvarthayoḥ kā gatiḥ- iti cet |
children.translated_text: If it be asked what is the role of the verbal root-meanings '<s>ālambha</s>' (touching) and '<s>nirvāpa</s>' (offering) in the injunction of obligation (<s>kartavyatā</s>) through the <s>liṅ</s> suffix for the sacrifice constructed from the connection of substance and deity —
we say: '[they are] restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>)' — this is the established conclusion. || MJaiNyC_2,3.12-15 ||

Without a context (<s>anārabhya</s>), this is recited: '<s>vāyavyaṃ śvetam ālabheta bhūtikāmaḥ</s>' (one desiring prosperity should sacrifice a white [animal] sacred to <s>Vāyu</s>), and '<s>saurye caruṃ nirvaped brahmavarcasakāmaḥ</s>' (one desiring the radiance of <s>Brahman</s> should offer a <s>caru</s> in the <s>Saurya</s> rite). Similarly, in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) sacrifices, this is recited: '<s>iṣām ālabheta</s>' (he should touch the <s>iṣā</s>) and '<s>caturo muṣṭīn nirvapati</s>' (he offers four handfuls). The <s>iṣā</s> is a long piece of wood, like a plough-shaft, placed on the cart. Its <s>ālambha</s> (touching) is a [ritual] contact. Having restated this <s>iṣā</s>-touching which belongs to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, the qualifying attribute of whiteness is enjoined for the <s>iṣā</s> to be touched. And the belonging to <s>Vāyu</s> (<s>vāyavyatā</s>) is possible because that white wood is touched by the wind (<s>Vāyu</s>). Similarly, having restated the four-handful offering, the <s>caru</s> is enjoined as a qualifying attribute. <s>Caru</s> means a cooking vessel (<s>sthālī</s>), which is the basis of the offering. The offering substance being <s>Āgneya</s> (sacred to <s>Agni</s>), due to its connection with radiance like the sun, it becomes <s>saurya</s> (solar). The two fruits — prosperity and <s>Brahman</s>-radiance — are merely restated as already established in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites which are for the fulfillment of all desires. Therefore — these are qualifying-attribute injunctions — this is the first prior view. But it is not appropriate that the fruit-words, which are constantly heard independently and have possible purpose [of their own], should be [treated as] optional restatements or purposeless. Therefore — rites qualified by [particular] attributes and fruits are being enjoined here. Even so, since sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) is not heard [explicitly], only as much of the rite as is stated — namely the touching (<s>ālambha</s>) and the offering (<s>nirvāpa</s>) — constitutes the rite-injunction — this is the second prior view.
(In the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the preparatory-rite status of the calf-touching and the like, <s>sūtras</s> 16–17)
Because it is mostly observed in the [same] domain. / Jaim_2,3.16 /
And because of the applicability of <s>arthavāda</s>. / Jaim_2,3.17 /
START MJaiNy 2,3.16
He composes the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the calf-touching (<s>vatsālambha</s>) a sacrifice (<s>yaji</s>), or a mere touching? Like the <s>Vāyavya</s> and the like, it would be a sacrifice;
[but] it would be a [mere] touching — due to the absence of deity, it is a preparatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>), because of its being read among [other] common [rites]. // MJaiNy_2,3.16 //

children.text:
agnihotradohādhikāre śrūyate -"vatsamālabheta"iti |
tatra 'vimato vatsālambho yajiḥ syāt, prāṇidravyakālambhatvāt, vāyavyālambhavat' iti cet |

children.translated_text: no.
Because of its dissimilarity from that [<s>Vāyavya</s> touching], due to the absence of a deity.

Moreover — 'this calf-touching is a preparatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>) ancillary to the <s>Agnihotra</s>, because it is read among the common rites of the <s>Agnihotra</s>, like other preparatory rites.'
Therefore — here, a mere touching is enjoined. || MJaiNyC_2,3.16 ||

In the section on the milking for the <s>Agnihotra</s>, it is heard: '<s>vatsam ālabheta</s>' (one should touch the calf). Therein — 'the calf-touching is a sacrifice, because it involves the touching of a living substance, like the <s>Vāyavya</s> touching' — if so it is argued,
(In the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the purpose of the <s>Nīvāra caru</s> being [merely] a placement, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: saṃyuktas tv arthaśabdena tadarthaḥ śrutisaṃyogāt / Jaim_2,3.18 /
children.translated_text: But [a sentence] connected with the word '<s>artha</s>' (purpose) would serve that purpose, because of its connection with scripture. / Jaim_2,3.18 /
START MJaiNy 2,3.17-18
He composes the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'A <s>caru</s> is made of <s>nīvāra</s> (wild rice)' and 'one places (<s>upadatte</s>) the <s>caru</s>' —

children.text: yāgaḥ syādupadhānaṃ vā yāgaḥ śeṣoktadaivataḥ // MJaiNy_2,3.17 //
children.translated_text: is this a sacrifice or [merely] a placement? It would be a sacrifice, since the deity is stated in the complement. // MJaiNy_2,3.17 //
When the sacrifice-status is uncertain, the complement should not be relied upon — whence then a sacrifice?
Rather, it is merely a placement; [the <s>caru</s>] is established in what has been stated. // MJaiNy_2,3.18 //

children.text:
agnau śrūyate - 'naivāraścarurbhavati' iti, 'carumupadadhāti' iti ca |
tatra - nīvāracarudravyako yāgo vidhīyate |
na cātra devatāyā abhāvaḥ |

children.translated_text: because the deity is established by the complement of the sentence: '<s>bṛhaspater vā etad annaṃ yan nīvārāḥ</s>' (the <s>Nīvāra</s> grains are indeed the food of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>).

children.text: upadhānaṃ tu yāgopayuktasya pratipattiḥ sviṣṭakṛdādivat - iti prāpte, brūmaḥ- 'yāgavidhau niścite sati paścāddevatāyāmapekṣitāyāṃ vākyaśeṣabalāddevatākḷṣṭiḥ, iha tu devatākalpanena yāgavidhitvaniścayaḥ |
children.translated_text: But the placement (<s>upadhāna</s>) is the procurement of what is useful for the sacrifice, like the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> and the like — having arrived at this position, we say: 'When the sacrifice-injunction is first determined, afterwards, when the deity is required, the deity is attracted by the force of the complementary sentence; but here, the determination of the sacrifice-injunction itself [depends on] the postulation of the deity —
hence there is mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>).
Therefore — here, merely the placement is being enjoined.' || MJaiNyC_2,3.17-18 ||

In the [section on the establishment of] the [sacred] fires, it is heard: '<s>naivāraś carur bhavati</s>' (the <s>caru</s> is made of <s>Nīvāra</s> rice) and '<s>carum upadadhāti</s>' (one places the <s>caru</s>). Therein — a sacrifice having <s>Nīvāra caru</s> as its substance is being enjoined. Nor is the deity absent here,
(In the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the <s>Pātnīvata</s> [animal] having circumambulation with fire as its qualifying attribute, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
But in the <s>Pātnīvata</s> [animal sacrifice], the restriction is because of its precedence. / Jaim_2,3.19 /
START MJaiNy 2,3.19-21
He composes the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'The <s>Pātnīvata</s> [animal], having been circumambulated with fire (<s>paryagnikṛta</s>), is released (<s>utsṛjyate</s>)' —

children.text: yāgau guṇo vā yāgaḥ syādanvayāvyavadhānataḥ // MJaiNy_2,3.19 //
children.translated_text: are these two sacrifices, or is it a qualifying attribute? It would be a sacrifice, because of the uninterrupted syntactic connection. // MJaiNy_2,3.19 //
The animal to be sacrificed, being recognized [from the archetype], is restated; by the word '<s>utsarga</s>' (release),
the qualifying attribute called circumambulation with fire (<s>paryagnikaraṇa</s>) is stated — for the purpose of preventing the subsequent [ancillaries]. // MJaiNy_2,3.20 //
The exclusive enumeration (<s>parisaṃkhyā</s>) here is not faulty, since there is an injunction prior to the applicatory rule (<s>codaka</s>);
the procedure of ancillaries ending with circumambulation with fire [is established] because of established utility (<s>kḷptopakāra</s>). // MJaiNy_2,3.21 //

children.text:
'tvāṣṭraṃ pātnīvatamālabheta' iti prakṛtyedamāmnātam-'paryāgnikṛtaṃ pātnīvatamutsṛjanti' iti |
tatra paryagnikṛtaśabdena saṃskṛtapaśudravyasya pātnīvataśabdena patnīvannāmakadevatāsaṃbandhasya ca pratīyamānatvādamaṃ yāgavidhiḥ |
evaṃ sati paryagnikṛtapātnīvataśabdayoravyavahitānvayo labhyate |
siddhānte tu 'paryagnikṛtamutsṛjanti' ityanvayaṃ vāñchanti |
tadā vyavahitānvayo durvāraḥ |
tasmāt-ṣāyavyapaśuvadyāgavidhiḥ- iti prāpte, brūmaḥ- anārabhyādhītatvānnāsti sayavye prakṛtapratyabhijñā |
iha tvālabhyatvena prakṛtaḥ paśuḥ pātnīvataśabdena pratyabhijñāyate |
tamanūdya paryagnikṛtaśabdānvitena 'utsṛjanti' ityākhyātena paryagnikaraṇākhyo guṇo vidhīyate |
na ca prakṛtimatasya paryagnikaraṇasya vikṛtau codakena prāptatvādanarthako 'yaṃ vidhiridhivācyam |
uparitanāṅgānanuvṛtterdidhiprayojanatvāt |
nanvevaṃ sati parisaṃkhyā syāt |
sā ca doṣatrayaduṣṭā |
svārthatyāgaḥ, anyārthasvīkāraḥ, prāptavādhaśceti trayo doṣāḥ |
paryagnikaraṇavākye svārtho bidhistyajyeta, anyārthe niṣedhaḥ svī kriyeta, codakaprāptānyuparitanāṅgāni bādhyeran |
maivam |
'paryagnikaraṇottaramāvīnyaṅgāni nānuṣṭheyāni' ityetasyāḥ parisaṃkhyāyā anaṅgīkārāt |
kathaṃ tarhi tannivṛttiḥ- 'ārthikī' iti brūmaḥ |
codakapravṛtteḥ prāgevāyaṃ vidhiḥ pravartate, pratyakṣopadeśasya śīghrabuddhijanakatayā kalpyātideśātprabalatvāt |
tathāsatyupadiṣṭairevāṅgairnirākāṅkṣāyāṃ vikṛtau codakasyāpravṛtyaivoparitanānyaṅgāni na prāpyante |
na cānena nyāyena paryagnikaraṇātprācīnānāmapya prāptiriti vācyam |
vidhīyamānasya paryāgnikaraṇasya nūtanatve satyupakārakalpanāpattyā prakṛtau yatkḷptopakāraṃ paryagnikaraṇaṃ, tadavasthāpannasyaivātra vidheyatvāt |
children.translated_text: Because when the circumambulation with fire being enjoined is new, and [its] utility must be postulated, it is the circumambulation with fire whose utility is established in the archetype that is the object of the injunction here — [i.e.,] one that has attained the same position [as in the archetype].

children.text: prakṛtau ca prācīnāṅganantaramādina evopakāraḥ kḷpta ityatrāpi tādṛśasyaiva vidhānātparyāgnikaraṇāntāṅgarītiḥ sidhyati |
children.translated_text: And in the archetype, the established utility [of circumambulation] is [that it comes] right after the preceding ancillaries — therefore, since one of the same kind is being enjoined here too, the procedure of ancillaries ending with circumambulation with fire is established.

children.text: evaṃ ca sati 'utsṛjanti' ityākhyātena yathoktaparyagnikaraṇavidhāvarthasiddha uparitanāṅgotsargo dhātunānūdyate |
children.translated_text: This being so, by the finite verb '<s>utsṛjanti</s>' (they release), in the injunction of circumambulation as described, the release of the subsequent ancillaries is restated by the verbal root — being established by the meaning itself.
Therefore here is a qualifying-attribute injunction. || MJaiNyC_2,3.19-21 ||

'<s>Tvāṣṭraṃ pātnīvatam ālabheta</s>' (one should sacrifice the <s>Pātnīvata</s> animal sacred to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>) being the archetype, this is recited: '<s>paryāgnikṛtaṃ pātnīvatam utsṛjanti</s>' (they release the <s>Pātnīvata</s> [animal] after circumambulation with fire). Therein, since the word '<s>paryagnikṛta</s>' conveys the prepared animal-substance and the word '<s>pātnīvata</s>' conveys the connection with the deity named <s>Patnīvat</s>, this would be a sacrifice-injunction. This being so, an uninterrupted syntactic connection of the words '<s>paryagnikṛta</s>' and '<s>pātnīvata</s>' is obtained. But in the established conclusion, they construe the syntactic connection as '<s>paryagnikṛtam utsṛjanti</s>' (they release [it] after circumambulation). Then the interrupted syntactic connection is unavoidable. Therefore — it is a sacrifice-injunction like the <s>Vāyavya</s> animal — having arrived at this position, we say: Since [this passage] is read without an independent context (<s>anārabhyādhīta</s>), there is no recognition of the archetype as in the <s>Vāyavya</s> case. But here, the animal that is the principal subject as something to be sacrificed (<s>ālabhya</s>) is recognized by the word '<s>pātnīvata</s>.' Having restated it, the qualifying attribute called circumambulation with fire (<s>paryagnikaraṇa</s>) is enjoined by the finite verb '<s>utsṛjanti</s>' (they release) connected with the word '<s>paryagnikṛta</s>.' Nor should it be said that this injunction is purposeless because circumambulation with fire, which exists in the archetype, is already obtained in the modification (<s>vikṛti</s>) by the applicatory rule (<s>codaka</s>) — because the purpose of the injunction is to prevent the continuation of the subsequent ancillaries. Now, if so, there would be an exclusive enumeration (<s>parisaṃkhyā</s>). And that is vitiated by three faults: abandonment of its own meaning, acceptance of another's meaning, and obstruction of what is [already] obtained. In the circumambulation-sentence, the injunction — its own meaning — would be abandoned; the prohibition — another's meaning — would be accepted; and the subsequent ancillaries obtained by the applicatory rule would be obstructed. That is not correct. Because the exclusive enumeration — 'the ancillaries after circumambulation with fire should not be performed' — is not accepted. Then how is their cessation [established]? We say: 'by purposive [reasoning].' This injunction operates even before the applicatory rule takes effect, because a direct instruction is more powerful than a postulated application (<s>kalpyātideśa</s>), being faster in generating cognition. This being so, when the need is already fulfilled by the instructed ancillaries alone, the applicatory rule does not operate in the modification, and therefore the subsequent ancillaries are not obtained. Nor should it be said that by this reasoning, even the ancillaries prior to circumambulation would not be obtained.
(In the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the cup-name status of <s>Adābhya</s> and the like, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
Due to being non-substance, the remainder of the rite would apply to the cup (<s>kavela</s>). / Jaim_2,3.20 /
START MJaiNy 2,3.22-23
He composes the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In '<s>yad adābhyaṃ gṛhītvā</s>' (having drawn the <s>Adābhya</s>) and '<s>gṛhṇāty aṃśum</s>' (he draws the <s>Aṃśu</s>) — are these two

children.text: tadyāgo vā guṇo yāgaḥ syādadābhyāṃśunāmataḥ // MJaiNy_2,3.22 //
children.translated_text: [names of] sacrifices or qualifying attributes? They would be sacrifices, since they are named <s>Adābhya</s> and <s>Aṃśu</s>. // MJaiNy_2,3.22 //
They would be names of cups (<s>graha</s>) only, because of the immediate proximity [to the verb '<s>gṛhītvā</s>']; their injunction is [as such];
there is a qualifying attribute for this [<s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>], by the sentence that pertains to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. // MJaiNy_2,3.23 //

children.text:
amārabhya śrūyate - 'eṣa vai ddaviṣā haviryajate, yo 'dābhyaṃ gṛhītvā somāya yajate' iti 'parā vā etasyā'yuḥ prāṇa eti, yoṃ'śuṃ gṛhṇāti' iti ca |
tatra- adābhyaśabdasya jyotirādivadapūrvanāmatvāttannāmako yāgo 'yajate' ityākhyātena vidhīyate |
'aṃśuma' ityatra yajateravaśravaṇe 'pi nāmaviśeṣabalādevāpūrvayāgavidhiḥ |
na cātra dravyadevatayorabhāvaḥ |
grahaṇaliṅgena jyotiṣṭomavikṛtitvādagatau tadīyavidhyantātideśena tatsiddheḥ - iti prāpte, brūmaḥ- bhavatvadābhyāṃśuśabdayornāmatvam |
te ca nāmanī grahayoreva syātām, na tu yāgayoḥ |
'gṛhītvā' itiśabdasyānantarameva pāṭhāt |
yajatistu vyavahitaḥ |
tādṛśo 'pi yajiraṃśuvākye nāsti |
tasmādgrahayorevātra vidhiḥ |
grahaṇaṃ ca jyotiṣṭomagatasya somarasasya saṃskārarūpo guṇaḥ, aindravāyavādigrahaṇasamānatvāt |
yadyapyatra na prakṛto jyotiṣṭhomaḥ, tathāpi tatsaṃbandhigrahaṇadvārā vākyasya jyotiṣṭobhagāmitvam |
children.translated_text: Even though the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is not the immediate subject here, nevertheless through the medium of the cup-drawing that pertains to it, the sentence reaches the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.
For this very reason it is stated: '<s>somāya adābhyaṃ gṛhītvā</s>' (having drawn the <s>Adābhya</s> for <s>Soma</s>).

children.text: athavā-taittirīyāṇāṃ ṣaṣṭhakāṇḍe ṣaṣṭhe prapāṭhake prākaraṇikaṃ viniyojakaṃ vākyaṃ draṣṭavyam |
children.translated_text: Alternatively — the contextual sentence that serves as the viniyojaka (assigning passage) should be seen in the sixth <s>kāṇḍa</s>, sixth <s>prapāṭhaka</s> of the <s>Taittirīya</s> [recension].
Therefore — it is a qualifying-attribute injunction within the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. || MJaiNyC_2,3.22-23 ||

Without a context (<s>anārabhya</s>), it is heard: '<s>eṣa vai dviṣā havir yajate yo 'dābhyaṃ gṛhītvā somāya yajate</s>' (he who, having drawn the <s>Adābhya</s> [cup], sacrifices to <s>Soma</s>, sacrifices with the enemy's oblation) and '<s>parā vā etasyāyuḥ prāṇa eti yo 'ṃśuṃ gṛhṇāti</s>' (the life-breath of one who draws the <s>Aṃśu</s> [cup] departs). Therein — since the word '<s>Adābhya</s>,' like '<s>Jyotis</s>' and the like, is an unprecedented name, a sacrifice bearing that name is enjoined by the finite verb '<s>yajate</s>.' In '<s>aṃśum</s>,' even though the verb '<s>yajati</s>' is not heard, the force of the distinctive name alone suffices for the unprecedented sacrifice-injunction. Nor is there an absence of substance and deity here — because, by the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of the word '<s>grahaṇa</s>' (drawing), it is a modification of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, and in the absence of [other information], the substance and deity are established by application (<s>atideśa</s>) from the archetype — having arrived at this position, we say: Let the name-status of the words '<s>Adābhya</s>' and '<s>Aṃśu</s>' be granted. But those names would belong to cups (<s>graha</s>) only, not to sacrifices — because the word '<s>gṛhītvā</s>' (having drawn) immediately follows [them in the text]. The verb '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices), however, is separated [from them]. And even such a [separated] '<s>yajati</s>' is absent in the <s>Aṃśu</s> passage. Therefore, what is enjoined here pertains to cups alone. And the cup-drawing is a preparatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>) — a qualifying attribute — of the <s>Soma</s> juice that belongs to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, being similar to the drawing of the <s>Aindravāyava</s> and other cups.
(In the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the preparatory-rite status of <s>Agnicayana</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 21–23)

children.text: agnis tu liṅgadarśanāt kratuśabdaḥ pratīyeta / Jaim_2,3.21 /
children.translated_text: But <s>Agni</s> — from the observation of the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) — the word '<s>kratu</s>' (sacrifice) would be understood [to apply]. / Jaim_2,3.21 /

children.text: dravyaṃ vā syāc codanāyās tadarthatvāt / Jaim_2,3.22 /
children.translated_text: Or it would be a substance, since the injunction serves that purpose. / Jaim_2,3.22 /

children.text: tatsaṃyogāt kratus tadākhyaḥ syāt tena dharmavidhānāni / Jaim_2,3.23 /
children.translated_text: Due to the connection with that, it is a <s>kratu</s> (sacrifice) designated by that [name]; therefore the injunctions of <s>dharma</s> [apply]. / Jaim_2,3.23 /
START MJaiNy 2,3.24-25
He composes the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: agniṃ cinuta ityatra yāgo vā saṃskṛtiyaṃjiḥ /
children.translated_text: In '<s>agniṃ cinuta</s>' (construct the fire[-altar]) — is this a sacrifice, or is it a preparatory rite (<s>saṃskṛti</s>)? [Then what of] the sacrifice?
By the mark (<s>liṅga</s>), since <s>Agni</s> has sacrifice-name status, the sacrifice is merely restated. // MJaiNy_2,3.24 //
By conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>), this is the name of a substance — fire (<s>vahni</s>); the construction (<s>citi</s>), like the establishment [of fire] (<s>ādhāna</s>),
is a preparatory rite; when the fire is [thus] prepared, the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is enjoined [to be performed with it]. // MJaiNy_2,3.25 //

children.text:
'ya evaṃ vidvānagniṃ cinute' ityevaṃ vidhāya śrūyate-'athāto 'gnimāgniṣṭomenānuyajati,tamukthyena 'taṃ ṣoḍaśinā, tamatirātreṇa, ityādi |
atra - agniśabdo yāgavācī |
stotraśastrādeḥ kratuliṅgasya śrūyamāṇatvāt |

dbalīyasīti na yāganāmatvam |
