dravyadetayorasiddheḥ |

children.translated_text: Therefore, since the installation is stated as '<s>agnim ādadhīta</s>' (one should install the fire), the construction stated as '<s>agniṃ cinute</s>' (he constructs the fire) is a preparatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the fire-substance.
Nor is there an absence of application for what has been prepared.
Because application [is found] in the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and the like through sentences such as '<s>agnim agniṣṭomena yajate</s>' (he sacrifices the fire with the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>) and the like.
Therefore — it is an injunction of a preparatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>). || MJaiNyC_2,3.24-25 ||

'He who, knowing thus, constructs the fire [altar]' — having thus prescribed, it is heard: 'Then he offers [sacrifice to] the fire with the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, then with the <s>Ukthya</s>, then with the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, then with the <s>Atirātra</s>,' and so on. Here — the word '<s>agni</s>' denotes a sacrifice, because the sacrificial mark — consisting of <s>Stotra</s>, <s>Śastra</s>, and the like — is heard. And that mark is heard thus: 'the <s>Stotra</s> of the fire [sacrifice],' 'the <s>Śastra</s> of the fire [sacrifice],' and 'six <s>Upasads</s> belong to the one [dedicated] to fire.' If the mark depends on a prescriptive [statement], then let it be a restatement by the [verb] '<s>yaj</s>' (to sacrifice) in the prescriptive [statement]. In the sentence '<s>agnim agniṣṭomena anuyajati</s>' (he subsequently sacrifices the fire with the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>), from the co-referentiality of '<s>agni</s>' and '<s>yaj</s>' — just as in '<s>upāṃśu yajati</s>' (he sacrifices quietly) — it is a name of a sacrifice. If it be said that because the prefix '<s>anu</s>' is connected with the word '<s>agni</s>', the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is connected with the verb '<s>yaj</s>' as a subsequent offering — even so, when there is an initial offering to fire, the subsequent offering of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is possible, as in '<s>Yajñadatta</s> follows <s>Devadatta</s>,' where the prior going of <s>Devadatta</s> is observed. Therefore, in '<s>agniṃ cinute</s>' (he constructs the fire), a sacrifice named '<s>Agni</s>' is enjoined by the finite verb. And '<s>cinoti</s>' (constructs) — like the restatement of the aggregate of cups obtained as a modification of the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice — is a restatement of the construction obtained from the sentence '<s>iṣṭakābhir agniṃ cinute</s>' (he constructs the fire with bricks) — when this is the position arrived at, we say: the word '<s>agni</s>' by convention (<s>rūḍhi</s>) denotes the fire-substance. And convention, being established, is stronger than the indication-based postulation of the word's capacity to denote a sacrifice — therefore it is not the name of a sacrifice. Nor is there a sacrificial form here — because substance and deity are not established.
(In the eleventh [topic] — the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the distinct-rite-status of the monthly <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
[There is] a different purpose in a different context. / Jaim_2,3.24 /
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 2.3.26-27]
He composes the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'He offers the <s>Agnihotra</s> for a month' — is the [month] a qualifying attribute, or is it a distinct rite [with the month as] a qualifying attribute?
Having restated the [already] obtained rite, the month — being unobtained — is enjoined here. // MJaiNy_2,3.26 //
'Having observed the <s>upasads</s>' — but since the <s>upasads</s> are impossible in the perpetual [<s>Agnihotra</s>],
and because of the impossibility of enjoining many [qualifying attributes at once], it is a distinct rite due to the different context. // MJaiNy_2,3.27 //

asaṃnihitatvāt |

prakaraṇasyāsamarpakatve 'pyagnihotraśabdenaitatsamarpaṇādeṣā śaṅkā bhavati |

tathā sati svataḥsiddhaṃ prakaraṇabhedaṃ nirākṛtya prakaraṇaikyāpādanena guṇaṃ vidhāpayituṃ pravṛttasyāgnihotraśabdasya śaktau nirūddhāyāṃ tadavasthaḥ prakaraṇabhedo nityāgnihotrādidaṃ karma bhinatti |
agnihotraśabdau dharmātideśārtha iti saptame vakṣyate |

na |
vaiṣamyāt |

children.translated_text: 'In the <s>Vājin</s>, the qualifying attribute is to be enjoined as something to be adopted;
the month is not so' — this is the further dissimilarity.

children.text: paramārthatastvatra prathamatarapratītena prakaraṇabhedena siddhaṃ karmabhedaṃ guṇabheda upodbalayati |
children.translated_text: In truth, however, here the differentiation of qualifying attributes reinforces the differentiation of rites that is [already] established by the contextual difference apprehended earlier.
Therefore, it is the different context alone that is the cause of differentiation here. || MJaiNyC_2,3.26-27 ||

In the <s>ayana</s> (sacrificial session) of the <s>Kuṇḍapāyins</s>, it is heard: 'having observed the <s>upasads</s>,' 'he offers the <s>Agnihotra</s> for a month,' and 'he should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> for a month.' Here — if it be said that the already obtained perpetual <s>Agnihotra</s> is restated, and the qualifying attribute characterized by a month is enjoined because it is unobtained — not so. Is only the month enjoined, or also the <s>upasads</s> stated in 'having observed the <s>upasads</s>'? Not the first — because the <s>upasads</s>, not being obtained through the perpetual <s>Agnihotra</s>, must also be enjoined in your view. Not the second — because when many qualifying attributes are enjoined in an already obtained rite, the sentence would split. If it be said: let there be no injunction of a qualifying attribute then; what is the evidence for it being a distinct rite? — we say: 'a different context.' For this is not the context of the perpetual <s>Agnihotra</s> — because it is not proximate. For this is the context of the <s>ayana</s> — because it is studied beginning from the <s>ayana</s>. If it be asked: what then is the doubt about enjoining a qualifying attribute in the perpetual <s>Agnihotra</s>? — even though the context does not direct [this to the perpetual <s>Agnihotra</s>], this doubt arises because of the directing [force] of the word '<s>Agnihotra</s>.' And that [doubt] is refuted by the splitting of the sentence. This being so, when the capacity of the word '<s>Agnihotra</s>' — which had set out to enjoin a qualifying attribute by establishing contextual unity and overriding the naturally established contextual difference — is blocked, the contextual difference, remaining as it was, separates this rite from the perpetual <s>Agnihotra</s>. It will be stated in the seventh [<s>adhyāya</s>] that the word '<s>Agnihotra</s>' serves the purpose of transfer of properties (<s>dharmātideśa</s>). If it be objected: this rite is enjoined as qualified by the <s>upasads</s> and the month; therefore, by the <s>Vājin</s> principle, the differentiation of the rite comes from the differentiation of qualifying attributes, not from the difference of context — no, because of dissimilarity.
(In the twelfth [topic] — the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the desire-sacrifices (<s>kāmyeṣṭi</s>) beginning with the <s>Āgneya</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
And the result [differentiates a rite] in the absence of proximity to a [previously enjoined] rite. / Jaim_2,3.25 /
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 2.3.28-29]
He composes the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'An <s>Āgneya</s> (offering to <s>Agni</s>) on eight potsherds for one desiring brilliance (<s>rukkāma</s>)' — [is this] a result [enjoined] in the model (<s>prakṛti</s>) sacrifice?
Or is it a distinct rite, because the result is [a newly] illuminated [purpose], and because the previous principle does not apply? // MJaiNy_2,3.28 //
Let there not be a different context; [yet] it is a distinct rite because of non-proximity;
[this passage] is studied without commencement [from a new section]; its form, however, is observed [to be] no less [different than the previous examples]. // MJaiNy_2,3.29 //

rukkāmastejaskāmaḥ |
atra - iṣṭīnāṃ prakṛtibhūtadarśapūrṇamāsagatamāgneyayāgamanūdya tatra tejaskāmarūpaṃ phalaṃ vidhīyate |
kutaḥ |
vākyenā'gneyaphalasaṃbandhasya māsamānatvāt |
na ca pūrvoktamāsāgnihotranyāyena karmāntaratvam |
vaiṣamyāt |
tatrāyanamārabhyādhītatvādasti prakaraṇāntaratvam |
iha tvanārabhyādhītatvena prakaraṇameva tāvannāsti, kuto 'tra prakaraṇāntaratvam |
kiṃca māso 'nupādeyaḥ |
agnihotrānusāreṇa saṃpādayitumaśakyatvāt |
phalaṃ tūpādeyam, dārśapaurṇamāsikāgneyānusāreṇa tejasaḥ kāmayituṃ śakyatvāt |
tasmāt-phalavidhiḥ- iti prāpte, brūmaḥ- prakaraṇāntaratvābhāve 'pyanārabhyādhītatvādasaṃnidhirastyeva |
sa evātra karma bhinatti |
na cātra vājinanyāyena karmabhedaḥ, aṣṭākapāladravyāgnidevatātmano rūpasyobhayatraikavidhatvāt |
yadi prakaraṇāntaratvamapyasaṃnidhikṛtamityasaṃnidhireva māsāgnihotrakarmabhedahetuḥ, tarhi tasyaivāyaṃ prapañco 'stu |

anyathā sādhanavadaphalatvaprasaṅgāt |
kāmanā ca viṣayasaundaryajñānātsvata evotpadyate |

children.translated_text: it does not come about from hearing an injunction.
Whether the reasoning in the two <s>adhikaraṇas</s> is different or the same —
in any case, the sacrifice for one desiring brilliance (<s>tejaskāmeṣṭi</s>) is a distinct rite.

children.text: kāmyeṣṭikāṇḍapaṭhiteṣu 'aindrāgnamekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapetprajākāmaḥ' ityādiṣvayameva nyāyo draṣṭavyaḥ || MJaiNyC_2,3.28-29 ||
children.translated_text: In the passages recited in the section on desire-sacrifices — such as '<s>aindrāgnam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped prajākāmaḥ</s>' (one desiring offspring should prepare an <s>Aindrāgna</s> [offering] on eleven potsherds) and the like — this very reasoning should be applied. || MJaiNyC_2,3.28-29 ||

Without a new beginning, it is heard: '<s>āgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped rukkāmaḥ</s>' (one desiring brilliance should prepare an <s>Āgneya</s> [offering] on eight potsherds). '<s>Rukkāma</s>' means one desiring brilliance (<s>tejas</s>). Here — by restating the <s>Āgneya</s> sacrifice that belongs to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, which is the model for offerings, the result in the form of desire for brilliance is enjoined therein. Why? Because the connection of the <s>Āgneya</s> with the result is established by the sentence alone. Nor is it a distinct rite by the principle of the monthly <s>Agnihotra</s> stated previously — because of dissimilarity. There, because [the passage] is studied beginning from the <s>ayana</s>, there is a different context. But here, since [the passage] is studied without a new beginning, there is not even a context, let alone a different context. Moreover, the month is not adoptable — because it cannot be accomplished by following the [perpetual] <s>Agnihotra</s>. But the result is adoptable — because desiring brilliance is possible by following the <s>Āgneya</s> of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. Therefore — it is an injunction of the result — when this position is arrived at, we say: even in the absence of a different context, non-proximity exists because of being studied without a new beginning. That very [non-proximity] differentiates the rite here. Nor is there differentiation of the rite here by the <s>Vājin</s> principle — because the form consisting of the substance of eight potsherds and the deity <s>Agni</s> is identical in both. If even the different context was produced by non-proximity, then non-proximity alone was the cause of rite-differentiation in the monthly <s>Agnihotra</s> — then let this be an elaboration of that very [principle]. And the result, like the month, is not adoptable — otherwise, the absurdity would follow that, like the means, it would be without result. And desire arises by itself from the knowledge of the beauty of the object;
(In the thirteenth [topic] — the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the <s>Aveṣṭi</s> having food as its result, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: saṃnidhau tv avibhāgāt phalārthena punaḥ śrutiḥ / Jaim_2,3.26 /
children.translated_text: But in [a case of] proximity, due to the absence of differentiation, the scripture is repeated for the purpose of [enjoining] the result. / Jaim_2,3.26 /
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 2.3.30-32]
He composes the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'One should sacrifice' at the conclusion of the [<s>Darśa</s> sacrifice], on the full-moon day, throughout life, and likewise with this [<s>Aveṣṭi</s>];
'one desiring food' and so on — is it a differentiation of rites, or a qualifying attribute? // MJaiNy_2,3.30 //
Since injunction and adoption are identical, and since place and the like are not additionally derived,
in the obligatory injunction of the rite, its differentiation [would result] from mere repetition. // MJaiNy_2,3.31 //
Since the connection with place and the like is unobtained, it is an injunction; for there is no identity of the two;
since the two words [denoting] the person have a function, [the rite] is restated through repetition. // MJaiNy_2,3.32 //

aveṣṭiprakaraṇe phalamāmnātam-'etayānnādyakāmaṃ yājayaṃt' iti |
ādiśabdena saṃskāro gṛhītaḥ |

ata eva na vidheyāḥ |
upādānavidhiśabdayoḥ paryāyatvāt |

sa ca karmavatpūrve na vihita ityaprāptatvādvidhimarhati |
yaduktama- upādānavidhiśabdau paryāyau - iti |
tadasat |

children.translated_text: 'Injunction (<s>vidhāna</s>) is the initiation of what was not [previously] initiated, and that is an operation of words directed at a person;

children.text: ananuṣṭhitasyānuṣṭhānamupādānama, tacca karmāviṣayaḥ puruṣavyāpāraḥ' iti mahānbhedaḥ |
children.translated_text: adoption (<s>upādāna</s>) is the performance of what was not [previously] performed, and that is an operation of a person directed at a rite' — this is the great distinction.

children.text: yo 'pi-darśādīnāṃ punarvidhiḥ so 'pi deśādisaṃbandhaṃ vidhātuṃ karmānuvādaḥ - iti na karmabhedamāvahati |
children.translated_text: Even the re-injunction of the <s>Darśa</s> and the like is merely a restatement of the rite for the purpose of enjoining the connection with place and the like — hence it does not bring about differentiation of rites.

children.text: samidho 'yajati' ityādau vidheyaguṇāntarābhāvenānuvādāṃsabhavātpunarvidhānaṃ bhedahotuḥ- iti vaiṣamyam || MJaiNyC_2,3.30-32 ||
children.translated_text: In '<s>samidho yajati</s>' (he sacrifices the kindling-sticks) and the like, since restatement is impossible — because there is no other qualifying attribute to be enjoined — the re-injunction is the cause of differentiation — this is the dissimilarity. || MJaiNyC_2,3.30-32 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context, place, time, and occasion are taught: '<s>same yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice on level ground), '<s>paurṇamāsyāṃ yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice on the full-moon day), '<s>yāvajjīvaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> throughout life). In the <s>Aveṣṭi</s> context, the result is taught: '<s>etayā annādyakāmaṃ yājayet</s>' (with this [offering], he should cause one desiring food to sacrifice). By the word 'and so on,' the preparatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is included. And that is taught in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context: '<s>śeṣaṃ sviṣṭakṛte samavadyati</s>' (the remainder is distributed for the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>). There — place, time, occasion, result, and preparatory rite, being not to be performed [afresh], are not adoptable. For that very reason, they are not to be enjoined — because the words 'adoption' and 'injunction' are synonymous. Therefore — it must be necessarily accepted that it is an injunction of [a new] rite. There — when the <s>Darśa</s> and the like, which are the subjects of the context and were previously enjoined, are re-enjoined by these sentences, the differentiation of rites arises from repetition alone, as in '<s>samidho yajati</s>' (he sacrifices the kindling-sticks) and the like — when this is the position arrived at, we say: even though place and the like are not to be enjoined, let their connection with the [already] enjoined rite be enjoined. And that [connection], like the rite, was not previously enjoined — hence, being unobtained, it merits injunction. What was said — that the words 'adoption' and 'injunction' are synonymous — that is wrong.
(In the fourteenth [topic] — the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the praise-purpose of the double mention of <s>Āgneya</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 27–29)
Because of being the cause of the <s>Āgneya</s> <s>sūkta</s> (hymn), it should be understood as repetition. / Jaim_2,3.27 /

children.text: avibhāgāt tu karmaṇāṃ dvirukter na vidhīyate / Jaim_2,3.28 /
children.translated_text: But due to the non-differentiation of rites, the double mention is not an injunction. / Jaim_2,3.28 /
Or the repeated scripture is for another purpose. / Jaim_2,3.29 /
[Section: <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s> 2.3.33-34]
He composes the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
That <s>Āgneya</s> [sacrifice], stated in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [context], stands alone; even though
by two sentences in the <s>Darśa</s> [sacrifice, it is mentioned] with '<s>yad</s>' — is it a distinct rite, or is the [second] statement a restatement? // MJaiNy_2,3.33 //
From the repetition, [it would be] a distinct rite; let it be employed twice in the <s>Darśa</s> sacrifice;
but because of the recognition of its identity, it is a restatement; and [the purpose is] the praise of the <s>Aindrāgna</s> [sacrifice]. // MJaiNy_2,3.34 //

children.text:
yadāgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo 'māvasyāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ cācyuto bhavati |
iti kāladvaye vihitam |
'yadāgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo 'māvāsyāyāṃ bhavati' ityekasminkāle punarvihitam |
tatra - aviśeṣapunaḥśrutilakṣaṇenābhyāsena prayājānāmiva bhedaḥ |
tathā satyāgneyayāgasya darśakāle dviḥprayogaḥ- iti cet |
na |
pratyabhijñānādāgneyasyaikatve satyekakālavākyasyānuvādakatvāt |
na cānuvādo vyarthaḥ |
vidheyaindrāgnastutyarthatvāt |
yadyapyāgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo 'māvāsyāyāṃ bhavati, tathāpi na kevalenāgninā sādhurbhavati |
indrasahito 'gniḥ samīcīnataraḥ |

children.translated_text: Therefore —
'The <s>Aindrāgna</s> should be performed' — this is the praise of what is to be enjoined.
But the dissimilarity with the <s>prayājas</s> (fore-sacrifices) should be understood as already stated. || MJaiNyC_2,3.33-34 ||

'The <s>Āgneya</s> on eight potsherds remains unfailing on both the new-moon day and the full-moon day' — thus it is enjoined for both times. 'The <s>Āgneya</s> on eight potsherds is on the new-moon day' — thus it is re-enjoined for one time. There — by repetition characterized by unqualified restatement, there is differentiation, as in the case of the fore-sacrifices (<s>prayāja</s>). If this be so, the <s>Āgneya</s> sacrifice would be employed twice at the time of the <s>Darśa</s> — if this be argued — no, because due to the recognition of identity, when the <s>Āgneya</s> is one, the single-time sentence is a restatement. Nor is the restatement purposeless — because it serves the purpose of praising the <s>Aindrāgna</s> [sacrifice] that is to be enjoined. Although the <s>Āgneya</s> on eight potsherds is on the new-moon day, nevertheless one does not succeed with <s>Agni</s> alone. <s>Agni</s> accompanied by <s>Indra</s> is more appropriate.

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīye jaiminīyanyāyamālavistare dvitīyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third quarter (<s>pāda</s>) of the second chapter (<s>adhyāya</s>) in the illustrious <s>Mādhava</s>'s <s>Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s>.
(Now the fourth quarter of the second chapter)
(In the first [topic] — the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the lifelong <s>Agnihotra</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 1–7)
The lifelong repetition is a property of the rite, [known] from the context. / Jaim_2,4.1 /
Or [it is a property] of the performer, because of the connection with the scripture. / Jaim_2,4.2 /

children.text: liṅgadarśanāc ca karmadharme hi prakrameṇa niyamyeta tatrānarthakam anyat syāt / Jaim_2,4.3 /
children.translated_text: And because an indicatory mark is observed; for if it were a property of the rite, it would be restricted by sequence, and anything else would be purposeless in that case. / Jaim_2,4.3 /

children.text: apavarge ca darśayati kālaś cet karmabhedaḥ syāt / Jaim_2,4.4 /
children.translated_text: And [scripture] shows [it] upon the completion [of a period]; if time [were the basis], there would be differentiation of rites. / Jaim_2,4.4 /
But because of impermanence, it would not be so. / Jaim_2,4.5 /
And there is also contradiction, as before. / Jaim_2,4.6 /

children.text: kartus tu niyamāt kālaśāstraṃ nimittaṃ syāt / Jaim_2,4.7 /
children.translated_text: But due to the restriction pertaining to the agent, the time-scripture would serve as the occasion. / Jaim_2,4.7 /
START MJaiNy 2,4.1-2
He composes the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the fourth <s>pāda</s> —

children.text: yāvajjīvaṃ juhotīti dharmaḥ karmaṇi puṃsi vā /
children.translated_text: In '<s>yāvajjīvaṃ juhoti</s>' (one offers as long as one lives) — does the <s>dharma</s> pertain to the action or to the person?
Because [life-span] is time, it is a property of the action; therefore let the single desiderative (<s>kāmya</s>) performance be carried out. // MJaiNy_2,4.1 //
Life is not time; therefore, from the division of the occasions (<s>nimitta</s>),
the desiderative (<s>kāmya</s>) performance would be distinct from the lifelong (<s>yāvajjīva</s>) performance. // MJaiNy_2,4.2 //

children.text:
bahvṛcabrāhmaṇe śrūyate- 'yāvajjīvamāgnihotraṃ juhoti' iti |
tatraṃ yāvajjīvaśabdo maraṇāvadhikālaparaḥ |
tatkālasaṃbandhaśca prakṛte kāmyāgnihotre pūrvamaprāptatvāt 'juhoti' ityanūdite karmaṇi vidhīyate |
tathā satyasya vākyasya nityaprayogavidhāyakatvābhāvena vākyāntaravihitaḥ kāmyaprayoga eka evāgnihotrasya paryavasyati |
sa ca kāmyaprayogo 'bhyasitavyaḥ |
sakṛdanuṣṭhānasya 'agnihotraṃ juhuyātsvargakāmaḥ' ityanenaiva siddhatvāt |
'yāvajjīvam' ityasya kālavidhervaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt |
tasmāt-ayaṃ kāmyakarmaṇo 'bhyāsasiddhaye kālarūpadharmavidhiḥ |
iti prāpte,- brūmaḥ-
yāvajjīvaśabdo na kālasya vācakaḥ, kiṃtu lakṣakaḥ |
vācyārthastukṛtsnajīvanam |
na ca-jīvanaṃ karmadharmatvena vidhātuṃ śakyam |
tasya puruṣadharmatvāt |
taṃ ca puruṣadharme nimittīkṛtyāgnihotraprayogo vidhīyate |
na ca - atra karmabhedaḥ |
taddhetūnāṃ śabdāntarādīnāmabhāvāt |
na ca-abhyāsastaddhetuḥ |
nimittaviśeṣasadbhāvenāviśeṣapunaḥśruterabhāvāt |
ataḥ prayogabhedaḥ paryavasyati |
jīvanasyātra nimittatvāt |

children.translated_text: Since, when the occasion exists, the occasional [performance] cannot be abandoned, permanence (<s>nityatva</s>) is established by the nature of things.
Nor does the uninterruptedness of the occasion (life) entail uninterrupted performance —
because [the performance] is prescribed for the evening and morning times.
Therefore — since life is a property of the person, the permanent (<s>nitya</s>) and desiderative (<s>kāmya</s>) performances are distinct. || MJaiNyC_2,4.1-2 ||

In the <s>Bahvṛca</s> <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (of the <s>Ṛgveda</s>), it is heard: '<s>yāvajjīvam āgnihotraṃ juhoti</s>' (one offers the <s>Agnihotra</s> as long as one lives). Therein, the word '<s>yāvajjīvam</s>' refers to time extending up to death. And the connection with that time is enjoined in the present desiderative <s>Agnihotra</s>, since it was not previously established, upon the re-stated action '<s>juhoti</s>' (one offers). This being so, since this sentence does not function as an injunction of permanent (<s>nitya</s>) performance, the single desiderative performance of the <s>Agnihotra</s>, already enjoined by another sentence, alone prevails. And that desiderative performance is to be repeated — because a single performance is already accomplished by '<s>agnihotraṃ juhuyāt svargakāmaḥ</s>' (one who desires heaven should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>). [Without repetition,] the time-injunction '<s>yāvajjīvam</s>' would become purposeless. Therefore — this is an injunction of a time-property for the repetition of the desiderative rite — having arrived at this position, we say: The word '<s>yāvajjīvam</s>' does not directly denote time, but rather indicates it (<s>lakṣaka</s>). Its directly expressed meaning is the entire life-span. And life cannot be enjoined as a property of the action, because it is a property of the person. And taking that property of the person as the occasion, the performance of the <s>Agnihotra</s> is enjoined. Nor is there a differentiation of the rite here — because the causes of differentiation such as different words and the like are absent. Nor is repetition (<s>abhyāsa</s>) the cause of differentiation — because since specific occasions exist, there is no purposeless reiteration of the general [injunction]. Therefore, what results is a differentiation of performance. Because life is the occasion here.
(In the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the unity of the rite [established by] the cognitions of all Vedic recensions, <s>sūtras</s> 8-32)

Because of the observation, in other recensions, of [differences in] name, form, property, specific [details], repetition, censure, capacity, completion, statement, and expiation — there would be a differentiation of rites. / Jaim_2,4.8 /
Or it is one [rite], because there is no difference in the connection, form, injunction, and designation. / Jaim_2,4.9 /
There should not be [differentiation] by the name, because it does not express an injunction. / Jaim_2,4.10 /
And all [recensions] would have unity of the rite. / Jaim_2,4.11 /
And the designation is artificial. / Jaim_2,4.12 /
Even in the case of unity, the latter [applies]. / Jaim_2,4.13 /
In [the case of] a branch of learning, [it is like] a <s>dharmaśāstra</s>. / Jaim_2,4.14 /
Like the <s>Āgneya</s>, [it is] a restatement. / Jaim_2,4.15 /
Or it is not a restatement, because there is no difference in the connection with scripture. / Jaim_2,4.16 /
And because the meaning is not immediately present. / Jaim_2,4.17 /
And a single one is not prohibited. / Jaim_2,4.18 /
And the examination is like the completion. / Jaim_2,4.19 /
Even in the case of unity, the others — censure, capacity, and completion-statements — [are explained]. / Jaim_2,4.20 /
The expiation [is explained] by the occasion. / Jaim_2,4.21 /
Or by the commencement, through the injunction. / Jaim_2,4.22 /
The completion would be understood as in what is [already] known, because of similarity to the previous [rite]. / Jaim_2,4.23 /

children.text: liṅgamaviśiṣṭaṃ sarvaśeṣatvān na hi tatra karmacodanā tasmād dvādaśāhasyāhāravyapadeśaḥ syāt / Jaim_2,4.24 /
children.translated_text: The mark is unspecified, being subsidiary to all; for there is no action-injunction therein; therefore the designation of a day-unit (<s>āhāra</s>) would apply to the twelve-day [session]. / Jaim_2,4.24 /

children.text: dravye cācoditatvād vidhīnām avyavasthā syān nirdeśād vyatiṣṭheta tasmān nityānuvādaḥ syāt / Jaim_2,4.25 /
children.translated_text: And since [the substance is] not enjoined, there would be indeterminacy of the injunctions regarding the substance; it would be established by specification; therefore it would be a permanent restatement (<s>nityānuvāda</s>). / Jaim_2,4.25 /
Due to the prohibition of what is [already] enjoined, there would be an excess in the alternative. / Jaim_2,4.26 /
In the <s>Sārasvata</s> [sacrifice], because of conflict, what goes [further] would be [applicable]. / Jaim_2,4.27 /
In the invitatory [offering], there is no counter-exception (<s>pratiprasava</s>). / Jaim_2,4.28 /
Or the restatement serves the purpose of a qualifying attribute. / Jaim_2,4.29 /
And it also shows the cognition. / Jaim_2,4.30 /

children.text: api vā kramasaṃyogād vidhipṛthaktvam ekasyāṃ vyavatiṣṭheta / Jaim_2,4.31 /
children.translated_text: Or rather, due to the connection with sequence, the separateness of the injunction would be established in a single [recension]. / Jaim_2,4.31 /

children.text: virodhinā tv asaṃyogād aikakarmye tatsaṃyogād vidhīnāṃ sarvakarmapratyayaḥ syāt / Jaim_2,4.32 /
children.translated_text: But since there is no connection with what is contradictory, in the case of unity of the rite, because of the connection with that, the cognition of all rites would pertain to the injunctions. / Jaim_2,4.32 /
START MJaiNy 2,4.3-4
He composes the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is there a differentiation of the rite due to the difference of [Vedic] recensions, or not? Here the rite is differentiated;

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ kāṭhakanāmādi bahu bhedasya kāraṇam // MJaiNy_2,4.3 //
children.translated_text: many causes of differentiation are seen, such as the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> name and the like. // MJaiNy_2,4.3 //
But these causes of differentiation are justified through the medium of the text and the like;
from the recognition of the form and the like as non-different, the rite is understood to be non-different. // MJaiNy_2,4.4 //

children.text:
kāṭhakakāṇvamādhyaṃdinataittirīyādiśākhāsu darśapūrṇamāsākhyaṃ karmā'nnātam |
tatra śākhābhedātkarma bhidyate |
kutaḥ |
bhedakāraṇānāṃ nāmabhedādīnāṃ bahūnāmupalambhāt |
kāṭhaka-kāṇvādiko nāmabhedaḥ |
kārīrīvākyānyadhīyānāḥ kecicchākhino bhūmau bhojanamācaranti, śākhāntaradhyāyino nā'caranti, iti dharmabhedaḥ |
ekasyāṃ śākhāyāmadhītāḥ 'iṣe tvā' ityādayo mantrāḥ, palāśaśākhācchedādayaḥ kriyāśca, śākhāntare 'pyadhīyanta iti punaruktiḥ |
evamaśaktyādayo bhedahetava udāhāryāḥ |
na hyalpāyuvā manuṣyeṇa sarvaśākhādhyayanapūrvakaṃ karmānuṣṭhānaṃ kartu śakyam |
tasmāt-śākhābhedena karmabhedaḥ |
iti prāpte-
brūmaḥ- rūpādyabhedādekaṃ karma |
āgneyāṣṭākapālādiyāgarūpaṃ ṣadevaikasyāṃ śākhāyām, tadevānyatrāpyupalabhyate |
'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeta' iti yāgarūpaḥ purūṣavyāpāraścaikavidhaḥ |
'darśapūrṇamāsau' iti karmanāmāpyekam |
'svargakāmaḥ' iti phalasaṃbadho 'pyekaḥ |
tasmāt- abhinnaṃ karma |
pūrvapakṣahetavastvanyathā saṃgacchante |
kāṭhakādikaṃ jyotirādivanna karmasāma, 'kāṭhakena yajeta' ityaśravaṇāt |
'kāṭhakavadhīte' iti prayogādgranthanomatyavagantavyam |

children.translated_text: The practice of eating on the ground and the like is a <s>dharma</s> (rule) pertaining to study [not to the sacrifice].
The repetition is not faulty because the students [of different recensions] are different.
Even a person of short lifespan can perform the rite through the principle of incorporating [elements] from other recensions (<s>śākhāntara-upasaṃhāra</s>).
Therefore — from the recognition of the form and the like as not otherwise established, the rite is not differentiated even when the recensions are different. || MJaiNyC_2,4.3-4 ||

In the <s>Kāṭhaka</s>, <s>Kāṇva</s>, <s>Mādhyandina</s>, <s>Taittirīya</s>, and other recensions (<s>śākhās</s>), a rite called '<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' is heard. Therein, the rite is differentiated by the difference of recensions. Why? Because many causes of differentiation — difference of names and the like — are observed. The difference of names like '<s>Kāṭhaka</s>,' '<s>Kāṇva</s>' and so on. Some adherents of a particular recension who study the <s>Kārīrī</s> passages practice eating on the ground, while adherents of another recension do not — this is a difference of <s>dharma</s> (practice). <s>Mantras</s> like '<s>iṣe tvā</s>' and the like, and acts like the cutting of a <s>palāśa</s> branch and the like, which are studied in one recension, are also studied in another recension — this constitutes repetition (<s>punarukti</s>). Similarly, incapacity and the like should be cited as causes of differentiation. For a human being of short lifespan cannot perform the rite after studying all recensions. Therefore — the rite is differentiated by the difference of recensions — having arrived at this position, we say: The rite is one, because of the non-difference of form and the like. The sacrificial form — the <s>Āgneya</s> eight-potsherded [offering] and the other sacrifices — is the same in one recension as it is observed in another. '<s>Darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice with the new- and full-moon offerings) — the human activity in the form of the sacrifice is of one kind. '<s>Darśapūrṇamāsau</s>' (the new- and full-moon sacrifices) — the name of the rite too is one. '<s>Svargakāmaḥ</s>' (one who desires heaven) — the connection with the fruit too is one. Therefore — the rite is non-different. The causes adduced for the prior view are explained otherwise. '<s>Kāṭhaka</s>' and similar [names], like '<s>Jyotis</s>' and the like, are not names of the rite, because the expression '<s>kāṭhakena yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice with the <s>Kāṭhaka</s>) is not heard. From the usage '<s>kāṭhake 'dhīte</s>' (one studies in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s>), it should be understood as a name of the text.

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīye jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistare dvitīyādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>pāda</s> of the second <s>adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Mādhavīya Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s>.
The second <s>adhyāya</s> is completed.
Now the first <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s>.
START MJaiNy 3,1.1
In the second [<s>adhyāya</s>], when the differentiation of rites was established, with the distinct rites [identified],
the subsidiary-principal relationship (<s>śeṣa-śeṣi-bhāva</s>) was desired to be known; hence it is discussed here. // MJaiNy_3,1.1 //
By this, the sequence of the second and third <s>adhyāyas</s> has been explained. || MJaiNyC_3,1.1 ||
(In the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the pledge [to discuss <s>śeṣa</s>], the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
Now, therefore, the defining characteristic of the subsidiary (<s>śeṣa</s>). / Jaim_3,1.1 /
START MJaiNy 3,1.2-3
He composes the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the first <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> —

children.text: aśābdī śeṣatā śābdī vā na śābdyapratītitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Is subsidiary status (<s>śeṣatā</s>) non-verbal (<s>aśābdī</s>), or verbal (<s>śābdī</s>)? It is not verbal, because it is not apprehended [from words];
since etymological knowledge (<s>vyutpatti</s>) is possible only for the connection of action and <s>kāraka</s> (case-relations). // MJaiNy_3,1.2 //
The principal-subsidiary relationship is subsumed within the connection [of action and <s>kārakas</s>];
since etymological knowledge is possible there, it would be verbal, like action and the like. // MJaiNy_3,1.3 //

children.text:
yadidamasmiṃstṛtīyādhyāye pratipādyaṃ śeṣatvam, na tacchābdam |
kutaḥ |
kenāpi śabdena śeṣatvasyāpratīyamānatvāt |
vyutpanno hi śabdaḥ pratyāyakaḥ |
vyutpatiśca na śeṣaśeṣibhāve kvaciddṛṣṭā |
loke sarvatra kriyākārakānvayasyaiva vyutpattiprayojakatvadarśanāt |
ataḥ śeṣatāyā aśabdatvānnāyamadhyāya ārambhaṇīya iti cet |
maivam |
anvaye śeṣaśeṣibhāvasyāntarbhāvāt |
na hi guṇapradhānabhāvamantareṇānvayaḥ saṃbhavati |

children.translated_text: Because two [entities that are both] subsidiary, being devoid of mutual expectancy, are not fit for connection.
Similarly for two [entities that are both] principal.

children.text: ato vyutpattisaṃbhavātkriyākārakatadanvayā yathā śābdāḥ, tathā tadanvayāntargataḥ śeṣaśeṣibhāvo 'pi śābdaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as action, <s>kāraka</s>, and their connection are verbal because etymological knowledge is possible [for them], so too the subsidiary-principal relationship, which is subsumed within that connection, is verbal.
Therefore this <s>adhyāya</s> should be commenced. || MJaiNyC_3,1.2-3 ||

The subsidiary status (<s>śeṣatva</s>) that is to be taught in this third <s>adhyāya</s> is not verbal (<s>śābda</s>). Why? Because subsidiary status is not apprehended through any word. For a word becomes communicative [only] when etymologically understood. And no etymological knowledge is seen anywhere regarding the subsidiary-principal relationship. Because in the world, only the connection of action and <s>kārakas</s> is observed as the basis of etymological knowledge. Therefore, since subsidiary status is non-verbal, this <s>adhyāya</s> should not be commenced — if this be argued: Not so. Because the subsidiary-principal relationship is subsumed within the connection [of action and <s>kārakas</s>]. For without the principal-subsidiary relationship, connection is impossible.
(In the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the defining characteristic of <s>śeṣa</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
The subsidiary (<s>śeṣa</s>) is [that which exists] for the sake of another. / Jaim_3,1.2 /
START MJaiNy 3,1.4
He composes the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: svarūpahetū na sto 'tra sto vā naivānirūpaṇāt /
children.translated_text: Neither the essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) nor the reason (<s>hetu</s>) [of subsidiary status] exists here — or both do exist, since they can be determined;
in the case of serving another's purpose (<s>pārārthya</s>), the two [reasons] for subsidiary status [exist]; the form indicated by that [is the definition]. // MJaiNy_3,1.4 //

children.text:
na tāvadatra śeṣatvasya svarūpaṃ nirūpayituṃ śakyate |
tathā hi-śeṣatvaṃ nāma kim-avinābhūtatvam, prayojyatvaṃ vā, vidhyantavihitatvaṃ vā |
nā'dyaḥ |
ṣaḍadyāgānāmavinābhūtānāṃ parasparaśeṣatvaprasaṅgāt |
na dvitīyaḥ |
'puroḍāśakapālena tuṣānupavapati' ityatra tuṣopavāpaṃ prati śeṣasyāpi kapālasya tatprayojyatvābhāvāt |
na tṛtīyaḥ |
bidhyādivihitasya palāśaśākhācchedasya satyapi śeṣatve vidhyantavihitatvābhāvāt |
tasmānnāsti śeṣatāyāḥ svarūpam |
nāpi heturasti |
'vimataḥ śeṣaḥ, evaṃtvāt, iti kasyaciddhetoranirūpaṇāt-iti prāpte,-
brūmaḥ- 'vimataḥ prayājādiḥ śeṣaḥ, parārthatvāt, bhṛtyādivat' iti hetuḥ sunirūpaḥ |
avinābhūtatvādīnāṃ lakṣaṇānāṃ duṣṭatve 'pi 'parārthaḥ śeṣaḥ' iti lakṣaṇasyāduṣṭatvāt |
tena lakṣita ākāraḥ svarūpam |
na ca pārārthyasyaiva hetutve lakṣaṇatve ca sāṃkaryam |
ākārabhedena tadbhedāt |
dṛṣṭānte gṛhītavyāptiṃ sahāyīkṛtya bodhaka ākāro hetuḥ |
children.translated_text: To begin with, the essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) of subsidiary status cannot be determined here. For thus: What is subsidiary status? Is it inseparable co-existence (<s>avinābhūtatva</s>), being caused by another (<s>prayojyatva</s>), or being enjoined at the end of an injunction (<s>vidhyantavihitatva</s>)? Not the first — because of the absurd consequence that the six sacrifices, being inseparable from each other, would be mutually subsidiary. Not the second — because in '<s>puroḍāśakapālena tuṣān upavapati</s>' (one scatters the husks with the <s>puroḍāśa</s> potsherd), the potsherd, though subsidiary to the husk-scattering, is not caused by it. Not the third — because the cutting of the <s>palāśa</s> branch, though enjoined by an injunction and having subsidiary status, is not enjoined at the end of an injunction. Therefore, there is no essential nature of subsidiary status. Nor is there a reason (<s>hetu</s>). Because no reason of the form 'the disputed [item] is subsidiary because of such-and-such' can be determined — having arrived at this position, we say: The reason is well-determined: 'the disputed <s>prayāja</s> and the like are subsidiary, because of serving another's purpose (<s>pārārthya</s>), like a servant and the like.' Even though the definitions like 'inseparable co-existence' and the like are flawed, the definition 'that which serves another's purpose is subsidiary' is flawless. The form indicated by that [definition] is the essential nature. Nor is there a confusion between the reason and the definition when both are 'serving another's purpose' — because they differ in aspect. As a reason, the aspect that generates understanding accompanied by the invariable concomitance grasped in an example is the reason.
As a definition, the aspect that generates understanding through frequent use is the definition.
Therefore, both the reason and the essential nature of subsidiary status exist. || MJaiNyC_3,1.4 ||
(In the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on what is subsidiary, <s>sūtras</s> 3-6)
[Subsidiary status applies] to substance, qualifying attribute, and preparatory rite — [says] <s>Bādari</s>. / Jaim_3,1.3 /
Actions too — [says] <s>Jaimini</s>, because they serve the purpose of the fruit. / Jaim_3,1.4 /
And the fruit [is subsidiary], because it serves the person's purpose. / Jaim_3,1.5 /
And the person [is subsidiary], because of serving the purpose of the action. / Jaim_3,1.6 /

He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is it only substance, qualifying attribute, and preparatory rite that are subsidiary, or also the fruit,

children.translated_text: the person, and the action? The two positions are to be accepted according to the difference of views. // MJaiNy_3,1.5 //
<s>Bādari</s> says that subsidiary status, which is the property of being helpful, [applies] to substance and the like;

children.text:
sphyakapālādikaṃ dravyam, arūṇimādiko guṇaḥ, avaghātaprokṣaṇādikaḥ saṃskāraḥ |
eteṣu triṣveva śeṣatvam |
svargaḥ phalam, tatkāmī puruṣaḥ, darśapūrṇamāsau karma |
na hi phalādīnāṃ trayāṇāṃ śeṣatvamasti |
upakāritvasya śeṣatvalakṣaṇasya phalādiṣvabhāvāt - iti bādarermatam |
pārārthye lakṣaṇamabhipretya 'phalādayo 'pi śeṣāḥ' iti jaiminermatam |
tathā ca trīṇi sūtrāṇi paṭhyante- 'karmāṇyapi jaiminiḥ phalārthatvāt' 'phalaṃ ca puruṣārthatvāt' 'puruṣaśca karmārthatvāt' iti |
children.translated_text: Thus three <s>sūtras</s> are recited: '<s>karmāṇy api Jaiminiḥ phalārthatvāt</s>' (even the actions [are subordinate], says <s>Jaimini</s>, because they exist for the sake of fruit); '<s>phalaṃ ca puruṣārthatvāt</s>' (and the fruit [is subordinate], because it exists for the sake of the person); '<s>puruṣaś ca karmārthatvāt</s>' (and the person [is subordinate], because he exists for the sake of the action).
Therein, [<s>Bādari</s>'s definition of] rendering service (<s>upakāritva</s>) is over-extended,
because rendering service is observed even in the case of the master — who is the principal — as in the case of a pregnant maid-servant [who serves her master though he is principal].
Therefore, <s>Jaimini</s>'s view alone is the primary established conclusion. || MJaiNyC_3,1.5-6 ||

The wooden sword (<s>sphya</s>), potsherds (<s>kapāla</s>), and the like are substances; redness (<s>aruṇiman</s>) and the like are qualifying attributes (<s>guṇa</s>); pounding (<s>avaghāta</s>), sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>), and the like are preparatory rites (<s>saṃskāra</s>). Subordination (<s>śeṣatva</s>) pertains to these three alone. Heaven (<s>svarga</s>) is the fruit; the person desiring it is the agent (<s>puruṣa</s>); the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rites are the principal action (<s>karma</s>). Fruit and the other two [agent and action] do not have subordination. Because the defining characteristic of subordination — namely rendering service (<s>upakāritva</s>) — is absent in fruit and the like — this is <s>Bādari</s>'s view. Intending the defining characteristic to be [mere] existence for the sake of another (<s>pārārthya</s>), <s>Jaimini</s> holds that 'fruit and the rest are also subordinate.'
(In the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the fixed domain of the offering (<s>nirvapaṇa</s>) and the like, <s>sūtras</s> 7–10)
Their connection is with a [specific] purpose. / Jaim_3,1.7 /

children.text: vihitas tu sarvadharmaḥ syāt saṃyogato 'viśeṣāt prakaraṇāviśeṣāc ca / Jaim_3,1.8 /
children.translated_text: But that which is enjoined would apply to all <s>dharmas</s>, because of the connection, because of the absence of distinction, and because of the non-distinction of the context. / Jaim_3,1.8 /
Due to the loss of purpose, there would be no action. / Jaim_3,1.9 /

children.text: phalaṃ tu saha ceṣṭayā śabdārtho 'bhāvād viprayoge syāt / Jaim_3,1.10 /
children.translated_text: But the fruit, together with the effort, being the meaning of the word — in the absence [of such connection], there would be separation. / Jaim_3,1.10 /
He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.translated_text: that is not correct.
Because they are fixed by the scriptural accusative case, as in '<s>vrīhīn prokṣati</s>' (he sprinkles the rice), '<s>ājyam avekṣate</s>' (he inspects the ghee), and similar passages.
And scriptural text (<s>śruti</s>) is stronger than context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>).
Therefore, the attributes are fixed [in their respective substances]. || MJaiNyC_3,1.7-8 ||

The attributes of rice are pounding (<s>avaghāta</s>), sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>), and the like; the attributes of ghee are skimming (<s>utpavana</s>), inspection (<s>avekṣaṇa</s>), and the like; the attributes of <s>sāṃnāyya</s> are milking (<s>dohana</s>), straining (<s>atañcana</s>), and the like. All of these are connected with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa apūrva</s> (unseen merit) as being causes of the fruit. Because no intermediate <s>apūrva</s> exists — since when the fruit is accomplished by a single <s>apūrva</s>, there is no basis for postulating another <s>apūrva</s>. And since [these] attributes, being performed in connection with the fruit-<s>apūrva</s>, generate the fruit-<s>apūrva</s> regardless of which substance they are performed upon — intermixture would result. Having arrived at this position, we say: The six sacrifices — the <s>Āgneya</s> and the others — being momentary and perishable, occurring at different moments, cannot combine to generate the fruit-<s>apūrva</s>. Therefore, six intermediate <s>apūrvas</s> generated by the <s>Āgneya</s> and other sacrifices must be postulated. Among those, the <s>apūrva</s> generated by the sacrifice whose substance is the offering cake (<s>puroḍāśa</s>) is the motivator of the rice-attributes, because of proximity. But [the connection] with the fruit-<s>apūrva</s> is mediated by it. Similarly, the ghee-attributes and the <s>sāṃnāyya</s>-attributes each have a direct connection with the intermediate <s>apūrva</s> generated by the sacrifice of their respective substance. This being so, the preparatory rites motivated by each respective <s>apūrva</s> are fixed in the archetype-substances that are the means of producing that respective <s>apūrva</s>. Now, the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context is the assigner (<s>viniyojaka</s>) of the preparatory rites here. And that [context] is common to all archetype-substances — hence the intermixture remains as before. If it be said: 'Since the removal of husks (<s>tuṣavimoka</s>) is possible only in rice, it is confined to rice, not to ghee and <s>sāṃnāyya</s>. Similarly, melting (<s>vilāpana</s>) is confined to ghee alone. Milking and the like are confined to <s>sāṃnāyya</s> alone' — granted. Even when [these] attributes that serve visible purposes are fixed, the attributes with invisible purposes — such as sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>) and the like — would still be intermixed — if so it is argued,
(In the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the fixed status of the wooden sword (<s>sphya</s>) and the like by following their syntactic connection, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

Nor is the restatement of the sacrifice-implements entirely purposeless,
because it is useful for the injunction of procurement [of the implements], as in '<s>yajñāyudhāni saṃbharanti</s>' (they collect the sacrifice-implements).

children.translated_text: Therefore — just as the preparatory rites such as pounding and the like [are fixed], so too the substances such as the wooden sword, potsherds, and the like are fixed. || MJaiNyC_3,1.9-10 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, it is heard: '<s>sphyaś ca kapālāni cāgnihotrahavaṇī ca śūrpe ca kṛṣṇājinaṃ ca śamyā colkhalaṃ ca musalaṃ ca dṛṣac copalā caitāni vai daśa yajñāyudhāni</s>' (the wooden sword, the potsherds, the <s>Agnihotra</s> ladle, the winnowing baskets, the black antelope skin, the wooden pin, the mortar, the pestle, the grinding stone, and the upper mill-stone — these are indeed the ten sacrifice-implements). The word '<s>sphya</s>' denotes a sword-shaped piece of wood. Therein — even though the intermixture of the preparatory rites such as pounding and the like in the substances such as rice and the like has been refuted, the intermixture of the substances such as the wooden sword, potsherds, and the like in the ancillary actions such as splitting, cake-baking, and the like cannot be refuted — because the sacrifice-implement status that is heard is not contradicted [even] when any substance is used in any action. For mere non-fixedness does not remove sacrifice-instrumentality — having arrived at this position, we say: In the intermixture view, the sentences '<s>sphyenoddhanti</s>' (they split with the wooden sword), '<s>kapāleṣu śrapayati</s>' (he cooks in the potsherds), '<s>agnihotrahavaṇyā havīṃṣi nirvapati</s>' (he offers the oblations with the <s>Agnihotra</s> ladle), '<s>śūrpeṇa vivinakti</s>' (he winnows with the winnowing basket), '<s>kṛṣṇājinam adhastād ulūkhalasyāvastṛṇāti</s>' (he spreads the black antelope skin beneath the mortar), '<s>śamyayā dṛṣadam upadadhāti</s>' (he places the grinding stone with the wooden pin), '<s>ulūkhalamusalābhyām avahanti</s>' (they thresh with the mortar and pestle), '<s>dṛṣadupalābhyāṃ pinaṣṭi</s>' (he grinds with the grinding stone and upper mill-stone) — these sentences, which convey specific connections, would become purposeless. If it be said that even in the fixedness view, the sacrifice-implement sentence, which conveys a general connection, would be purposeless — no. Because it is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) of what is already established by the splitting-sentences and the like. Nor should the reverse be said — that the splitting-sentences and the like are themselves restatements —
(In the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the non-intermixed status of qualifying attributes such as redness (<s>āruṇya</s>) and the like, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: arthaikatve dravyaguṇayor aikakarmyān niyamaḥ syāt / Jaim_3,1.12 /
children.translated_text: When the purpose is one, the restriction of the substance and the qualifying attribute would result from their belonging to the same action. / Jaim_3,1.12 /

children.translated_text: It is not appropriate to disregard the one-year-old cow substance present in its own sentence and instead delimit with cloth and the like.

Therefore, for the substance and the attribute — both directly connected with the purchase — the subsequent connection through mutual delimitation is [established] through implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>).
This being so, the meaning resolves as: 'he purchases with a one-year-old cow possessing redness.'
Therefore — the redness-attribute pertains only to the one-year-old cow, which is the instrument of purchase. || MJaiNyC_3,1.11-12 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, it is heard: '<s>aruṇayā piṅgākṣyaikahāyanyā somaṃ krīṇāti</s>' (he purchases <s>Soma</s> with a reddish, tawny-eyed, one-year-old [cow]). Therein — the word '<s>aruṇā</s>' denotes the qualifying attribute of redness (<s>aruṇiman</s>). Even though used as referring to the substance possessing the attribute, it conveys the attribute — because of the principle 'the qualified is not cognized without the qualifier being grasped.' And the etymological derivation applies to the attribute alone, through agreement and difference (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>). And the instrumentality in the <s>Soma</s>-purchase (<s>somakraya</s>) of this redness-attribute is understood from the instrumental case (<s>tṛtīyā</s>). But that is untenable — because an incorporeal attribute cannot serve as the instrument of purchase, like an army-commander. Therefore, since the instrumental case-ending has no assigning capacity, the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) becomes the assigner here. And the context extends the redness to all the substances — cups (<s>graha</s>), ladles (<s>camasa</s>), and all other subsidiary substances. Nor should it be suspected that by this reasoning, the meanings of the words '<s>piṅgākṣī</s>' (tawny-eyed) and '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' (one-year-old) would also extend to all substances — because those words denote substances. '<s>Piṅgākṣī</s>' is a cow whose eyes are tawny-colored. Similarly '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' (one-year-old [cow]). Although both words denote a single cow, they are two words because of the difference in the characterizing attributes. And operating simultaneously, they enjoin a cow-substance qualified by both attributes as the instrument of purchase. One substance cannot impose itself on another substance. But the attribute of redness, being fit to serve as a qualifier in substances, is extended to them. The word-by-word construal is: '<s>aruṇayā</s>' is a separate sentence. Therein, by the instrumental case, all the contextual instrument-substances are restated, and the attribute is enjoined by the stem — 'all the instrument-substances of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> should be made reddish.' Therefore — the attribute is intermixed — having arrived at this position, we say: Although the attribute is incorporeal, it nevertheless delimits the cow-substance, just as '<s>ekahāyanī</s>' (one-year-old) and '<s>piṅgākṣī</s>' (tawny-eyed) do. And that substance is the instrument; through it, the attribute has a connection with the purchase. This being so, there will be no splitting of the sentence. Now, even without splitting of the sentence, secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) is unavoidable — because of accepting that the word denoting the attribute has the substance possessing the attribute as its referent. That is not correct. For it is the attribute itself whose instrumentality is stated by the instrumental case here. And since that [instrumentality] is not possible without the medium of a substance, the delimiting function [of the attribute with respect to a substance] is postulated through implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>). If it be said: then let the cup, ladle, and other substances also be delimited — no. Because those substances, not being instruments of purchase, would not establish the attribute's instrumentality in the purchase that is heard [in the text]. If it be said: since cloth and the like are instruments of purchase, as in '<s>vāsasā krīṇāti</s>' (he purchases with cloth) and '<s>ajayā krīṇāti</s>' (he purchases with a goat), let the delimitation apply to them — no. Because those are instruments of different purchases. For there, as in the <s>Agnihotra</s> where milk and curds are alternatives, the alternative substances of cloth and the like are not enjoined by restating [the same] purchase. Because the mere purchase that is restated is not enjoined elsewhere as it is in the <s>Agnihotra</s> [case]. Therefore, the injunctions of cloth and other substances are injunctions of distinct purchases.
(In the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the purification of cups — the principle of cup-unity — <s>sūtras</s> 13–15)
What is connected with unity is appropriate for one [cup], because of the scriptural connection. / Jaim_3,1.13 /

children.text: sarveṣāṃ vā lakṣaṇatvād aviśiṣṭaṃ hi lakṣaṇam / Jaim_3,1.14 /
children.translated_text: Or for all, because of being a defining characteristic; for a defining characteristic is non-specific. / Jaim_3,1.14 /

children.text: codite tu parārthatvād yathāśruti pratīyetā / Jaim_3,1.15 /
children.translated_text: But when enjoined, being for the sake of another, it should be understood according to the scripture. / Jaim_3,1.15 /
START MJaiNy 3,1.13-14
He composes the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'He purifies the cup' — is one cup to be purified, or all?
One, because of the singular number being the addressee; [it should be treated] with care, like [a number that is] to be adopted. // MJaiNy_3,1.13 //
Due to its being principal, and since the repetition of its attribute [does not apply], the singularity is irrelevant;
if that [singularity] were enjoined, there would be sentence-splitting; therefore, by the mention of the substance, all [cups] should be purified. // MJaiNy_3,1.14 //

children.text:
some śrūyate- 'daśāpavitreṇa grahaṃ saṃmārṣṭi' iti |
daśāpatritraṃ vāsaḥkhaṇḍaḥ |
tatra - yathā 'paśunā yajeta' ityaścopādeyapaśugatamekatvaṃ vivakṣitam, tadvadddeśyagrahagatamapyekatvaṃ vivakṣitavyam |
kiṃca grahaśabdasya jātivācitvena jāteḥ saṃskāyatve sati tadāśrayabhūte yasminkasminnapi dravye 'nuṣṭhitena saṃskāreṇa jātiḥ saṃskṛtā bhavati |
tasmāt - eka eva grahaḥ śodhanīyaḥ-iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- 'graham' iti dvitīyayā grahasyoddeśyatayā prayojanavattayā ca prādhānyaṃ gamyate |
grahaṃ prati guṇaḥ saṃmārgaḥ |
'pratipradhānaṃ ca guṇa āvartanīyaḥ' iti nyāyena yāvanto grahāḥ santi, te saṃmārjanīyāḥ |
evaṃ niścaye sati saṃmārjayitavyagraheyattāyā avubhutsitatvāduddeśyagatamekatvaṃ śrūyamāṇamapyavivakṣitam |
athocyeta - nedamuddeśyagatam, kiṃtu dvayaṃ vidheyam-iti |
tanna |
vākyabhedāpatteḥ |
'grahaṃ saṃsṛjyāt, taṃ caikam' ityevaṃ vidheyārthabhedādvākyabhedaḥ |
' paśunā yajeta' ityatra tu yāgaṃ prati guṇabhūtaḥ paśuḥ |
na hi 'pratiguṇaṃ pradhānasyā'vṛttiḥ' iti kaścinyāyo 'sti |
tata iyattāyā bubhutsitatvācchrūyamāṇamekatvaṃ vivakṣyata iti vaiṣamyam |
na ca jātiḥ saṃskāryā |

children.translated_text: because the universal has no parts.
Therefore, the word '<s>graha</s>' (cup), qualifying the universal, designates the substance [itself].
And regarding that [substance], the repetition has been stated.
Therefore — all the cups are to be purified. || MJaiNyC_3,1.13-14 ||

In the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] it is heard: 'He purifies the cup (<s>graha</s>) with a cloth of ten threads (<s>daśāpavitra</s>).' The <s>daśāpavitra</s> is a piece of cloth. Therein — just as in 'one should sacrifice with an animal,' the unity pertaining to the animal to be procured is intended, so too the unity pertaining to the cup to be designated should be intended. Moreover, since the word '<s>graha</s>' (cup) denotes a universal (<s>jāti</s>), and since the universal is the object of the preparatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>), the universal is considered purified when the preparatory rite is performed on any substance whatsoever that serves as the substratum thereof. Therefore — only one cup is to be purified — having arrived at this position, we say: By the accusative case in '<s>graham</s>' (the cup), the primacy of the cup as the designee (<s>uddeśya</s>) and as having a purpose is understood. The purification (<s>saṃmārga</s>) is a qualifying attribute (<s>guṇa</s>) with respect to the cup. By the principle 'a qualifying attribute is to be repeated for each principal,' as many cups as there are, all of them are to be purified. When this is determined, the unity pertaining to the designee, even though heard, is not intended, because the number of cups to be purified is [already] desired to be known. But if it be said — 'this [unity] does not pertain to the designee, but rather both [unity and purification] are to be newly enjoined' — no. Because that would result in a split of the sentence. Due to the difference in the content to be enjoined — 'purify the cup, and that [cup should be] one' — there would be a sentence-split. But in 'one should sacrifice with an animal,' the animal is a qualifying attribute with respect to the sacrifice. For there is no principle that 'the principal is to be repeated for each qualifying attribute.' Therefore, since the number is desired to be known, the unity that is heard is intended — this is the difference. Nor is the universal (<s>jāti</s>) the object of the preparatory rite,
(In the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the non-application of purification and the like to the <s>camasa</s> and the like, <s>sūtras</s> 16-17:)

children.text: saṃskārād vā guṇānām avyavasthā syāt / Jaim_3,1.16 /
children.translated_text: From the preparatory rite, or else, there would be indeterminacy of the qualifying attributes. / Jaim_3,1.16 /

children.text: vyavasthā vārthasya śrutisaṃyogāt tasya śabdapramāṇatvāt / Jaim_3,1.17 /
children.translated_text: Or there would be determinacy, because of the connection with scripture regarding the object, since [scripture] is the means of knowledge for it. / Jaim_3,1.17 /
START MJaiNy 3,1.15-16
He composes the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>—

children.text: camasādi ca saṃsṛjyānno vā tasyāsti mārjanam /
children.translated_text: Should the <s>camasa</s> and the like also be purified, or is there no purification for them?
Just as the unity [could be disregarded], so too the cup-hood (<s>grahatva</s>) could be disregarded. // MJaiNy_3,1.15 //
The reason for disregard here is non-obstruction; but there is no sentence-split [in this case];

children.text: camasādau na saṃmārgaḥ śrutyā tadviṣayārpaṇāt // MJaiNy_3,1.16 //
children.translated_text: therefore there is no purification for the <s>camasa</s> and the like, because scripture assigns its scope to [cups alone]. // MJaiNy_3,1.16 //

children.text:
'graham' ityatra pratyayārthabhūtamekatvaṃ yathā na vivakṣitam, tathā prātidikārthasya grahatvasyāpyavivakṣā saṃbhāvyate |
tato grahaśabdasya somapātropalakṣakatvādgrahāṇāmiva camasānāmapi saṃmārgeṇa somāvasekanirharaṇaprayojanasaṃbhavācyamasādayo 'pi mārjanīyāḥ- iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- ekatvaṃ vākyabhedena duṣṭatvādavivakṣitam |
aduṣṭaṃ tu grahatvaṃ kuto na vivakṣyeta |
tataḥ satyapi prayojane pramāṇābhāvāccamasādau nāsti saṃmārgaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, even though there is a purpose, due to the absence of a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), there is no purification for the <s>camasa</s> and the like.
Nor should that [purification] be postulated based on the need for a purpose.
Because the scripture about '<s>graha</s>' (cup) itself assigns its scope to that [i.e., cups alone].
Therefore, there is no purification [for <s>camasas</s>]. || MJaiNyC_3,1.15-16 ||

Just as in '<s>graham</s>' (the cup), the unity — which is the meaning of the suffix — was not intended, so too the disregard of cup-hood (<s>grahatva</s>) — the meaning of the stem — may be suspected. In that case, since the word '<s>graha</s>' would indicate <s>Soma</s> vessels in general, and since there is a purpose for the purification of <s>camasas</s> also — namely, the removal of <s>Soma</s> residue — the <s>camasas</s> and the like should also be purified — having arrived at this position, we say: The unity was not intended because it was vitiated by the sentence-split. But the cup-hood, being unvitiated, why should it not be intended?
(In the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the status of the seventeen-cubit [post] as a subsidiary of the animal, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
Because of purposelessness, [it pertains] to the subsidiaries of that [animal]. / Jaim_3,1.18 /
START MJaiNy 3,1.17-19
He composes the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>—
The sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) of the <s>Vājapeya</s> would be seventeen cubits (<s>aratni</s>) [tall];
is the measurement a [qualifying attribute] belonging to the substance, or a subsidiary of the <s>Vājapeya</s>, or rather of the animal? // MJaiNy_3,1.17 //
Because of the immediate succession [of words] and the context, it is a subsidiary of the rite; in the absence of that, [it is connected] with the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> vessel;
in the upward vessel (<s>ūrdhvapātra</s>) made of <s>Khadira</s> wood, [pertaining to] fire — it is connected and follows the rite. // MJaiNy_3,1.18 //
Through the medium of the post, it is a subsidiary of the animal; and through the medium of the animal, [it is a subsidiary] of the rite;

children.text: saumikatvādvājapeye yūpo nāsti paśuṃ vinā // MJaiNy_3,1.19 //
children.translated_text: since [the <s>Vājapeya</s>] is a <s>Soma</s> sacrifice, in the <s>Vājapeya</s> there is no post without an animal. // MJaiNy_3,1.19 //

children.text:
vājapeyaprakaraṇe śrūyate - ' saptadaśāratnirvājapeyasya yūpo bhavati' iti |
tatra - yūpadravyagataṃ saptadaśāratniśabdoditaṃ yadūrdhvamānaṃ tadvājapeyakarmaṇo 'ṅgam |
saptadaśāratniśabdavājapeyaśabdayorānantaryāt |
prakaraṇaṃ caivamanugṛhyate |
yadi karmaṇaḥ sākṣādūrdhvamānaṃ na saṃbhavet, tarhi vājapeyagataṃ khādiramūrdhve yatṣoḍaśipātraṃ tasminnada unmānaṃ prathamaṃ saṃbadhya taddvārā karmaṇānveti - iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- 'saptadaśāratniryūpaḥ' iti sāmānādhikaraṇyādyūpena sākṣātsaṃbadhyate |
tasya yūpasya paśvaṅgatvādunmānaṃ yūpadvārā paśoraṅgaṃ bhavati |
tasyāpi paśorvājapeyāṅgatvātpaśudvārā karmaṇo 'ṅgam |
yadyapi vājapeyayūpaśabdayorānantaryamasti, tathāpi vājapeyasya somayāgatayā sākṣādyūpasaṃbandhābhāvā-
tpaśuvyavadhānamabhyupeyam |
'vājapeyasya' iti ṣaṣṭhyāḥ saṃbandhamātravācitvena vyavahitasaṃbandhamapyasāvabhidhatte |
'devadattasya naptā' iti prayogāt |

children.translated_text: As for the immediate succession of the words 'seventeen cubits' and '<s>Vājapeya</s>,' and the context — both of these are not contradicted [by our view],
because even when [the measurement] is a subsidiary of the animal, it is ultimately accepted as a subsidiary of the <s>Vājapeya</s>.
Moreover — in the prima facie view, the word '<s>yūpa</s>' (post) would have to be used figuratively to denote the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> vessel.
But in the established conclusion, that defect does not arise. || MJaiNyC_3,1.17-19 ||

In the <s>Vājapeya</s> context it is heard: 'The sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) of the <s>Vājapeya</s> should be seventeen cubits [tall].' Therein — the upward measurement stated by the word 'seventeen cubits,' which pertains to the substance of the post, is a subsidiary of the <s>Vājapeya</s> rite. [This is so] because of the immediate succession of the words 'seventeen cubits' and '<s>Vājapeya</s>.' And the context supports this interpretation. If the upward measurement cannot be directly connected with the rite, then it first connects with the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> vessel — the upward vessel made of <s>Khadira</s> wood which belongs to the <s>Vājapeya</s> — and through that medium, connects with the rite — having arrived at this position, we say: By the co-referentiality in 'a post of seventeen cubits,' the [measurement] is directly connected with the post. Since that post is a subsidiary of the animal, the measurement, through the medium of the post, becomes a subsidiary of the animal. And since the animal too is a subsidiary of the <s>Vājapeya</s>, through the medium of the animal, it becomes a subsidiary of the rite. Even though there is immediate succession between the words '<s>Vājapeya</s>' and '<s>yūpa</s>' (post), nevertheless, since the <s>Vājapeya</s> is a <s>Soma</s> sacrifice and thus has no direct connection with the post, the mediation of the animal must be accepted. The genitive in '<s>vājapeyasya</s>' (of the <s>Vājapeya</s>), denoting mere relation, can also express a mediated relation, as in the usage '<s>devadattasya naptā</s>' (the grandson of <s>Devadatta</s>).
(In the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the <s>abhikramaṇa</s> and the like being subsidiaries of the <s>prayāja</s> only, <s>sūtras</s> 19-20:)

children.text: kartṛguṇe tu karmāsamavāyād vākyabhedaḥ syāt / Jaim_3,1.19 /
children.translated_text: But in the case of a qualifying attribute of the agent, since [the qualifying attribute] does not inhere in the rite, there would be a sentence-split. / Jaim_3,1.19 /

children.text: sākāṅkṣaṃ tv ekavākyaṃ syād asamāptaṃ hi pūrveṇa / Jaim_3,1.20 /
children.translated_text: But [the sentence] would be a single sentence when it has an expectancy, since it is incomplete by the earlier [part]. / Jaim_3,1.20 /
START MJaiNy 3,1.20-22
He composes the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>—
'He offers while stepping forward (<s>abhikrāmam</s>)' — is this connected with the agent of the entire [<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>],
or would it pertain only to the <s>prayāja</s> (preliminary offering), being connected with the agent of the whole? // MJaiNy_3,1.20 //
Since both the <s>prayāja</s> and the stepping-forward (<s>abhikramaṇa</s>) are actions,
and since there is mutual absence of connection between them — not so, because they are on equal footing. // MJaiNy_3,1.21 //
There is no fault because of the connection with the agent; and this reconciliation is fitting;
therefore, because of the proximity of the <s>prayāja</s>, [the stepping-forward] is connected with the agent of that alone. // MJaiNy_3,1.22 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ prayājasamīpe śrūyate- 'abhikrāmaṃ juhoti' iti |
tatra homakāle yadetadāhavanīyamabhitaḥ saṃcaraṇaṃ, tatkṛtsnadarśapūrṇamāsakartrā saṃbadhyate, na tu prayājamātrakartrā |
kutaḥ |
abhikramaṇasya kriyārūpasya kārakatvābhāvena prayāñakriyayā saṃbandhāsaṃbhavāt - iti cet |
maivam |

children.translated_text: Because, precisely since it is in the form of an action, a connection with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> action too is [equally] impossible.

children.text: athocyeta-abhikramaṇaṃ kartṛkārakeṇa sākṣātsaṃbadhyate, taddvārā kṛtsnadarśapūrṇamāsakarmaṇā saṃbadhyate- iti |
children.translated_text: But if it be said — 'the stepping-forward is directly connected with the agent-instrument (<s>kartṛkāraka</s>), and through that medium, is connected with the entire <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> rite' —
that very reconciliation applies equally well to the connection with the <s>prayāja</s>.
Therefore, by the force of proximity (<s>saṃnidhi</s>), it is connected with the agent of the <s>prayāja</s> [alone]. || MJaiNyC_3,1.20-22 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [sacrifice], near the <s>prayāja</s> (preliminary offering), it is heard: '<s>abhikrāmaṃ juhoti</s>' (he offers while stepping forward). Therein, this circumambulation around the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire at the time of the offering is connected with the agent of the entire <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, not merely with the agent of the <s>prayāja</s>. Why? Because the stepping-forward (<s>abhikramaṇa</s>), being in the form of an action, has no capacity to function as an instrument (<s>kāraka</s>), and therefore a connection with the <s>prayāja</s> action is impossible — if so it is argued, not so.
START MJaiNy 3,1.23-24
He composes this same <s>adhikaraṇa</s> according to the view of the <s>Vārtikakāra</s> (the author of the <s>Vārttika</s>)—
Or rather, since proximity has force, and there is a context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), therefore
when the stepping-forward is studied within the <s>Darśa</s> and other procedures, it would have subsidiary-status thereof. // MJaiNy_3,1.23 //
The sub-context (<s>avāntara-prakaraṇa</s>) [begins] from '<s>samidho yajati</s>' (he sacrifices the kindling-sticks);

since it is read within that [sub-context], [the stepping-forward] is a subsidiary of that [<s>prayāja</s>]; and through that medium, it is a subsidiary of the <s>Darśa</s> [sacrifice]. // MJaiNy_3,1.24 //

children.text:
asminnapi mate tāveva viṣayasaṃśayau |
pūrvottarapakṣahetumātramanyat |
prayājasaṃnidhito 'pi darśapūrṇamāsaprakaraṇasya prabalatvātprākaraṇikeṣu kṛtsneṣvapyabhikramaṇaṃ niviśate - iti pūrvaḥpakṣaḥ |
"samidho yajati"ityāraṃbhyā'mnātamavāntaraprayājaprakaraṇam |

children.translated_text: Within that [sub-context], the stepping-forward is transmitted.

children.text: tasya cābhikramaṇavidherubhayataḥ prayājaviṣayairvākyaiḥ saṃdṛṣṭatvādabhikramaṇaṃ prayājamātre niviśate - iti rāddhāntaḥ |
children.translated_text: And since that injunction of stepping-forward is seen surrounded on both sides by sentences pertaining to the <s>prayāja</s>, the stepping-forward applies to the <s>prayāja</s> alone — this is the established conclusion.
Even in this view, the main context (<s>mahāprakaraṇa</s>) is not contradicted,
because [the stepping-forward] applies to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> through the medium of the <s>prayāja</s>. || MJaiNyC_3,1.23-24 ||

In this view as well, the subject matter and the doubt are the very same. Only the reasoning for the prima facie and established views differs. Since the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context is stronger than the proximity of the <s>prayāja</s>, the stepping-forward applies to all things belonging to the context — this is the prima facie view. The sub-context of the <s>prayāja</s> begins with what is transmitted starting from '<s>samidho yajati</s>' (he sacrifices the kindling-sticks).
(In the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the subsidiary-status of the sacred thread (<s>upavīta</s>) with respect to the entire context, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: saṃdigdhe tu vyavāyād vākyabhedaḥ syāt / Jaim_3,1.21 /
children.translated_text: But when [the connection] is doubtful, due to the interruption (<s>vyavāya</s>), there would be a sentence-split. / Jaim_3,1.21 /
START MJaiNy 3,1.25-26
He composes the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s>—
'He puts on the sacred thread (<s>upavyayate</s>)' — does it have the status of a subsidiary of the <s>sāmidhenī</s> [hymns], or rather
a subsidiary of the <s>Darśa</s> [sacrifice]? This [depends on whether] the sub-context (<s>avāntara</s>) or the former [main context] applies here. // MJaiNy_3,1.25 //
By the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>), [the <s>nivid</s> hymns] that are subsidiaries of the fire (<s>Agni</s>) — [these are] the <s>mantras</s> called <s>nivit</s>;

since there is an interruption [by the <s>nivid</s> section], [the sacred thread] is a subsidiary of the <s>Darśa</s> [sacrifice] by the force of the main context (<s>mahāprakaraṇa</s>). // MJaiNy_3,1.26 //

tatra - pūrvanyāyena sāmidhenīprakaraṇasyāvāntarasyāṅgīkārātsāmidhenyaṅgamupavītam - iti cet |
na |
nividbrāhmaṇena sāmidhenīprakaraṇasya viccheditatvāt |
na ca - nividāmapi sāmidhenyaṅgatayā tatprakaraṇapāṭhādavicchedakatvam - iti vācyam |
liṅgena nividāmagnyaṅgatvāvagamāt |
