children.translated_text: because of the interruption by the optional <s>sāmidhenī</s> [hymns].
Nor should subsidiary-status with respect to the optional <s>sāmidhenī</s> [hymns] be suspected,
because the [main] context is stronger than proximity.

Therefore — here, since the principle of the <s>prayāja</s> [sub-context] does not apply, the sacred thread (<s>upavīta</s>) is a subsidiary of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> by the force of the main context (<s>mahāprakaraṇa</s>). || MJaiNyC_3,1.25-26 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context, in the <s>prapāṭhaka</s> [beginning with] '<s>viśvarūpo vai tvāṣṭraḥ</s>' — in the seventh and eighth <s>anuvākas</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [section] on the <s>sāmidhenī</s> [hymns] is transmitted. In the ninth — the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> on the <s>mantras</s> called <s>nivit</s>, [beginning with] '<s>agne mahāṃ asi brāhmaṇabhārata</s>' and the like. In the tenth — the optional <s>sāmidhenī</s> alternatives. But in the eleventh — the sacred thread (<s>upavīta</s>) is prescribed thus: '<s>nivītaṃ manuṣyāṇām, prācīnāvītaṃ pitṝṇām, upavītaṃ devānām, upavyayate devalakṣmameva tatkurute</s>' (the <s>nivīta</s> [manner of wearing] is for humans, the <s>prācīnāvīta</s> for the ancestors, the <s>upavīta</s> for the gods; by wearing the sacred thread, one produces the mark of the divine). Therein — by the previously [established] principle, if the <s>sāmidhenī</s> sub-context is accepted, then the sacred thread is a subsidiary of the <s>sāmidhenī</s> [hymns] — if so it is argued, no. Because the <s>sāmidhenī</s> context has been interrupted by the <s>nivid</s> <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. Nor should it be said that the <s>nivid</s> [hymns] too, being subsidiaries of the <s>sāmidhenī</s>, do not interrupt the <s>sāmidhenī</s> context by virtue of being read within it — because, by the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>), the <s>nivid</s> [hymns] are understood to be subsidiaries of <s>Agni</s> (the fire). Having addressed <s>Agni</s>, the fire that is the locus of the oblation, with the <s>nivid</s> sentences beginning '<s>mahān asi</s>' (you are great) and the like, the qualities of <s>Agni</s> are conveyed in order to generate his enthusiasm. For this very reason, the etymology is heard thus: '<s>nividbharnyavedayet, tannividāṃ nivittvam</s>' (the <s>nivid</s> should inform <s>Agni</s> well; that is the <s>nivid</s>-nature of the <s>nivids</s>). But if it be objected — 'By the etymology: "those <s>ṛcs</s> by which the fire is properly kindled are the <s>sāmidhenīs</s>," these [<s>nivids</s>] too are for the purpose of <s>Agni</s> through the medium of kindling, and hence [they are <s>sāmidhenī</s> subsidiaries]' — let that be so. Even so, that alone does not establish a mutual subsidiary-principal relationship between them. But if it be said — 'Let the <s>sāmidhenī</s> context be interrupted; then by the <s>nivid</s> context, the sacred thread would be a subsidiary of the <s>nivid</s>' — no. Because the <s>nivids</s> are not heard in the preceding and following <s>anuvākas</s>, and hence there is no [<s>nivid</s>] context. [If it be said] 'by proximity it would be a subsidiary thereof' — no,
(In the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the mutual non-connection of qualifying attributes, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: guṇānāṃ ca parārthattvād asambandhaḥ samatvāt syāt / Jaim_3,1.22 /
children.translated_text: And for the qualifying attributes, because of serving another's purpose, there would be non-connection, because of equality. / Jaim_3,1.22 /
START MJaiNy 3,1.27-28
He composes the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>—
A vessel made of <s>Vikaṅkata</s> [wood] and the like [is used] in the oblations of the <s>Pavamāna</s> [chant];
is it connected with the entire sacrifice by the context, or with the <s>Ādhāna</s> (fire-establishment) [oblations] here? // MJaiNy_3,1.27 //
Being purposeless there, it remains confined to the [<s>Ādhāna</s>] oblations alone as a subsidiary;
it would not pertain to the entire sacrifice due to equality with the <s>Ādhāna</s> oblations, [even though] by sentence [it might seem so]. // MJaiNy_3,1.28 //

children.text:
ādhānaprakaraṇe dārupātraṃ homārthe yajñārthe ca śrūyate -"tasmādvāraṇo yajñāvacaraḥ syānnatvetena juhuyāt, vaikaṅkato yajñāvacaraḥ syājjuhuyādevaitena"iti |
yajñāvacaro yajñapracārahetuḥ |
tatra - vāraṇavaikaṅkatādipātraṃ prakaraṇabalādādhāne prathamamanveti |
etena pātreṇā'dhāne prayojanābhāvādādhānāṅgeṣu pavamānahaviḥṣveva tatpātraṃ niviśate |
asti hi pavamānahaviṣāmādhānāṅgatvam |
tatprakaraṇe pāṭhāt |
'kṛttikāsvagnimādadhīta' ityasminprakaraṇe 'prajāpatirvācaḥ satyamapaśyat' ityasminnanuvāke 'trīṇi havīṃṣi nirvapati' ityādinā tāni vihitāni |
tato yathā saptadaśāratnitvaṃ vājapeye sākṣādasaṃbhavattadaṅgapaśoraṅge niviśate, tadvadidamapi -- iti prāpate, brūmaḥ- agnimuddiśyā'dhānaṃ yathā vihitaṃ, tathā pavamānahavīṃṣyapi |
'yadāhavanīye juhvati tena so 'svābhīṣṭaḥ prītaḥ' ityāhavanīyoddeśena pavamānahavirhomavidhānāt |
children.translated_text: Because the injunction of the <s>Pavamāna</s> oblation in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire is stated with reference to the <s>Āhavanīya</s>: '<s>yad āhavanīye juhvati tena so 'svābhīṣṭaḥ prītaḥ</s>' (when they offer in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, by that he [<s>Agni</s>] is pleased by his own share).
Therefore, the <s>Pavamāna</s> oblations, which are recorded as consecrations of <s>Agni</s>, do not have a mutual principal-subsidiary relationship with each other.

children.text: tathā sati prakaraṇasya pātraṃ prati viniyojakatvābhāvāt |
children.translated_text: This being so, the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) lacks the capacity to assign the vessel.

children.text: 'vaikaṅkato yajñāvacaraḥ' iti vākyena darśapūrṇamāsādisarvayajñeṣu tadviniyujyate || MJaiNyC_3,1.27-28 ||
children.translated_text: By the sentence '<s>vaikaṅkato yajñāvacaraḥ</s>' (the <s>vikaṅkata</s> [vessel] serves the sacrifice), the vessel is assigned to all sacrifices — <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the like. || MJaiNyC_3,1.27-28 ||

In the section on the establishment of sacred fires (<s>ādhāna</s>), a wooden vessel (<s>dārupātra</s>) is heard [as used] for oblation and for the sacrifice: '<s>tasmād vāraṇo yajñāvacaraḥ syān na tv etena juhuyāt, vaikaṅkato yajñāvacaraḥ syāj juhuyād eva etena</s>' (therefore the [vessel] made of <s>vāraṇa</s> wood would serve the sacrifice but one should not offer oblations with it; the [vessel] made of <s>vikaṅkata</s> wood would serve the sacrifice and one should indeed offer oblations with it).
'<s>Yajñāvacara</s>' means 'that which facilitates the conduct of the sacrifice.'
Therein — the vessel made of <s>vāraṇa</s>, <s>vikaṅkata</s>, and other [woods] first pertains to the establishment of fires (<s>ādhāna</s>) by the force of the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>).
Since there is no purpose for such a vessel in the [ceremony of] establishment itself, the vessel finds its place only in the <s>Pavamāna</s> oblations, which are ancillaries of the establishment.
For the <s>Pavamāna</s> oblations have the status of being ancillary to the establishment,
because they are prescribed in that context.
In the section '<s>kṛttikāsv agnim ādadhīta</s>' (one should establish the fire in the [constellation] <s>Kṛttikā</s>), in the <s>anuvāka</s> '<s>Prajāpatir vācaḥ satyam apaśyat</s>' (<s>Prajāpati</s> saw the truth of speech), they are prescribed by '<s>trīṇi havīṃṣi nirvapati</s>' (he prepares three oblations) and so on.
Therefore, just as the seventeen-<s>aratni</s> [length] in the <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifice, being impossible to apply directly, finds its place in the ancillary — the animal's limb — so too this [vessel] — having arrived at this position, we say: Just as the establishment of fire is ordained with reference to <s>Agni</s>, so too are the <s>Pavamāna</s> oblations.
(In the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the topic of the <s>Vārtraghna</s> [mantras], the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
And because of the mutual absence of meaningful connection. / Jaim_3,1.23 /
START MJaiNy 3,1.29-31
He composes the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: vārtraghnyau pūrṇamāse sto vṛdhanvatyau tu darśage /
children.translated_text: Are the two <s>Vārtraghna</s> [mantras] in the full-moon [sacrifice] and the two <s>Vṛdhanvatī</s> [mantras] in the new-moon [sacrifice]
subsidiary to the principal [sacrifices as stated], or is there a [different] determination? // MJaiNy_3,1.29 //
The four <s>mantras</s> too have been obtained in sequence for the two <s>ājyabhāga</s> (ghee-portion) offerings;
the sentence is stronger than the sequence — therefore these are subsidiary to the <s>Darśa</s> [new-moon] and the like. // MJaiNy_3,1.30 //
In the principal [sacrifice], neither <s>Soma</s> alone exists, nor [does the time-reference of] the two times [serve as] a container;
since determination is not obtained for the <s>Darśa</s> and the like, the determination is from the [explicit] sentence. // MJaiNy_3,1.31 //

children.text:

brūmaḥ- 'agnirvṛtrāṇi jaṅganat' ityāgneyī prathamā vārtraghnī, 'tvaṃ somāsi satpatiḥ' iti saumyā dvitīyā vārtraghnī |
'agniḥ pratnena janmanā' - ityāgneyī prathamā bṛdhanvatī, 'soma gīrbhiṣṭvā vayam' iti saumyā dvitīyā vṛdhanvatī |

kālasya tūpasarjanatvāttadvācitvaṃ yuktam |

children.translated_text: And even there, the determination — 'in the first <s>ājyabhāga</s> addressed to <s>Agni</s>, the <s>mantra</s> too is addressed to <s>Agni</s>;

children.text: saumye dvitīye saumyaḥ' ityeṣā vyavasthā liṅgenaiva labhyate |
children.translated_text: in the second [<s>ājyabhāga</s>] addressed to <s>Soma</s>, [the <s>mantra</s> is] addressed to <s>Soma</s>' — this determination is obtained by the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) alone.
Granted.

children.text: tathāpi 'vārtraghnīyugalaṃ paurṇamāsīkāle, vṛdhanvatīyugalamamāvāsyāyām' ityeṣā vyavasthā pūrvanaprāptā brāhmaṇavākyenābhidhīyate - iti na vaiyarthyam || MJaiNyC_3,1.29-31 ||
children.translated_text: Even so, the determination — 'the <s>Vārtraghna</s> pair at the full-moon time, the <s>Vṛdhanvatī</s> pair at the new-moon' — this, which was not previously obtained, is stated by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> sentence — hence there is no purposelessness. || MJaiNyC_3,1.29-31 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> section, it is heard: 'The two <s>Vārtraghna</s> [mantras] are recited at the full-moon, the two <s>Vṛdhanvatī</s> at the new-moon.'
Therein — this pair of <s>Vārtraghna</s> and pair of <s>Vṛdhanvatī</s> [mantras] are recited in the <s>Hautrakāṇḍa</s> (the chanter's section), in the sequence of the two <s>ājyabhāga</s> offerings, in the <s>anuvāka</s> '<s>agnir vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanat</s>' (may <s>Agni</s> slay the enemies).
But from the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> sentence cited above, the injunction of these [mantras] for the <s>Darśa</s> and <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s> sacrifices is understood.
Therein, since the sentence is stronger, these <s>mantras</s> are subsidiary to the <s>Darśa</s> and <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s> sacrifices, not to the <s>ājyabhāga</s> offerings — having arrived at this position,
we say: '<s>Agnir vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanat</s>' (may <s>Agni</s> slay the enemies) — this is the first <s>Vārtraghna</s>, addressed to <s>Agni</s>. '<s>Tvaṃ somāsi satpatiḥ</s>' (you, O <s>Soma</s>, are the lord of truth) — this is the second <s>Vārtraghna</s>, addressed to <s>Soma</s>.
'<s>Agniḥ pratnena janmanā</s>' (<s>Agni</s>, with his ancient birth) — this is the first <s>Vṛdhanvatī</s>, addressed to <s>Agni</s>. '<s>Soma gīrbhis tvā vayam</s>' (O <s>Soma</s>, with hymns we [praise] you) — this is the second <s>Vṛdhanvatī</s>, addressed to <s>Soma</s>.
Therein, in the two principal <s>Darśa</s> and <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s> sacrifices, since the <s>Āgneya puroḍāśa</s> (oblation to <s>Agni</s>) exists, the two <s>Āgneya</s> [mantras] may somehow serve as invocatory verses (<s>puronuvākyā</s>) through optional alternation.
But for the two <s>Saumya</s> (addressed to <s>Soma</s>) [mantras], that is not possible,
because <s>Soma</s> as a deity is absent [in these sacrifices].
For even in the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [sacrifice], <s>Soma</s> alone does not exist [as the sole deity].
Furthermore, the seventh-case endings in '<s>pūrṇamāse</s>' (at the full-moon) and '<s>amāvāsyāyām</s>' (at the new-moon) indicate a container (<s>ādhāra</s>).
If the words referred to the sacrifices, the container-meaning would not be possible, since the sacrifice is the principal [entity].
But since the time is subordinate, its being the referent is appropriate.
Furthermore, this <s>anuvāka</s> is recited immediately after the passage that anaphorically refers to the <s>prayāja</s> (pre-sacrifice) <s>mantras</s>.
And that sequence pertains to the <s>ājyabhāga</s> offerings, which are ancillaries,
not to the principal <s>Darśa</s> and <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s> sacrifices.
Therefore the group of four <s>mantras</s> is not subsidiary to the principal sacrifices, but rather to the <s>ājyabhāga</s> offerings.
Now — this has already been obtained by the sequence alone.
(In the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the ancillary status of hand-washing and the like to the entire ritual context — <s>sūtras</s> 24-25)
Succession is not an injunction [of ancillary status]. / Jaim_3,1.24 /
And because the sentences are complete [in themselves]. / Jaim_3,1.25 /
START MJaiNy 3,1.32-33
He composes the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'He washes both hands' and 'he spreads the <s>ulaparāji</s> [grass]' —
is the hand-washing an ancillary of the grass-spreading alone, or of the entire [ritual]? // MJaiNy_3,1.32 //
It would be an ancillary of that [grass-spreading] alone, because of the sequence-based authority;
but through the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), it is subsidiary to all performances. // MJaiNy_3,1.33 //

darśapūrṇamāsaprakaraṇe śrūyate - 'hastāvavanenikte, ' 'ulaparājiṃ stṛṇāti' iti |

maivam |
avanejanaṃ hastasaṃskāraḥ |
'saṃskṛtau ca hastau sarvānuṣṭhānayogyau' ityetādṛśaṃ sāmarthyo liṅgam |
prakaraṇaṃ ca darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ sphuṭam |
ataḥ prabalābhyāṃ liṅgaprakaraṇābhyāṃ kramabādhātsarvaśeṣo hastarśuddhaḥ |
ayaṃ nyāyo vāgyame 'pi draṣṭavyaḥ |
sa ca vāgyamo jyotiṣṭomaprakaraṇe śrutaḥ- 'muṣṭī karoti' 'vācaṃ yacchati' iti |

children.translated_text: Immediately after that, this is heard: '<s>dīkṣitam āvedayati</s>' (he announces the one who has been consecrated).

children.text: āvedanaprakāraścaivaṃ śrutaḥ- 'adīkṣiṣṭāyaṃ brāhmaṇa iti trirupāṃśvāha devebhya evainaṃ prāha, triruccairubhayebhya evainaṃ devamanuṣyebhyaḥ prāha' iti |
children.translated_text: And the manner of announcement is heard thus: '<s>adīkṣiṣṭāyaṃ brāhmaṇa iti trir upāṃśv āha devebhya evainaṃ prāha, trir uccair ubhayebhya evainaṃ devamanuṣyebhyaḥ prāha</s>' (he says thrice in a whisper 'this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has been consecrated' — thus he announces him to the gods; thrice aloud — thus he announces him to both gods and humans).

children.text: atra muṣṭīkaraṇavāṅniyamābhyāṃ hastajihvāgatacāpale nivārite sati manasa ekāgrasya sarvakarmastu yogyatvaṃ liṅgam |
children.translated_text: Here, when the restlessness of the hands and tongue is restrained by the making of fists and the control of speech, the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is the fitness of the concentrated mind for all ritual acts.
By that [mark], the sequence is overridden. || MJaiNyC_3,1.32-33 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> section, it is heard: '<s>hastāv avanenijkte</s>' (he washes both hands), '<s>ulaparājiṃ stṛṇāti</s>' (he spreads the <s>ulaparāji</s> grass).
The <s>ulaparāji</s> is a bundle of grass prepared for spreading on the sacrificial altar (<s>vedī</s>).
Therein — if [it be said that] since the hand-washing and grass-spreading sentences are recited in immediate succession, by the authority of sequence, the hand-washing is an ancillary of the grass-spreading alone — 
that is not so.
The hand-washing is a consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the hands.
The mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is the capacity [indicating] 'consecrated hands are fit for all performances.'
And the context of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> is clear.
Therefore, through the mark and the context, which are stronger [than sequence], the sequence is overridden, and the hand-washing is subsidiary to all [ritual acts].
This same principle should be seen in the case of speech-control (<s>vāgyama</s>) as well.
That speech-control is heard in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> section: '<s>muṣṭī karoti</s>' (he makes fists), '<s>vācaṃ yacchati</s>' (he restrains speech).
(In the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the ancillary status of the fourfold division and the like to the <s>Āgneya</s> [offering] alone — <s>sūtras</s> 26-27)

children.text: śeṣas tu guṇasaṃyuktaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ pratīyeta mithas teṣām asaṃbandhāt / Jaim_3,1.26 /
children.translated_text: But the remainder, being connected with the qualifying attribute, should be understood as common [to all], because of their mutual non-connection. / Jaim_3,1.26 /

children.text: vyavasthā vārthasaṃyogāl liṅgasyārthena saṃbandhāl lakṣaṇārthā guṇaśrutiḥ / Jaim_3,1.27 /
children.translated_text: Or there would be determination through the connection of the mark with the meaning; the hearing of the qualifying attribute is for the purpose of indication. / Jaim_3,1.27 /
START MJaiNy 3,1.34-36
He composes the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'The <s>Āgneya</s> sacrificial cake (<s>puroḍāśa</s>) is to be divided into four parts' — thus it is stated;
is the fourfold division subsidiary to all [offerings], or does it pertain to the <s>Āgneya</s> alone? // MJaiNy_3,1.34 //
It is appropriate that [the word '<s>Āgneya</s>'] serves as an indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) for [all offerings including] the <s>Āgneya</s>; hence it is subsidiary to all;
since the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> and <s>Aindrāgna</s> [offerings] also have <s>Āgneya</s>-ness [being connected with <s>Agni</s>]. // MJaiNy_3,1.35 //
The <s>Āgneya</s>-ness of those two is not primary, because they do not rely on <s>Agni</s> alone;
therefore, the fourfold division is established in the one [<s>Āgneya</s>] sacrificial cake alone. // MJaiNy_3,1.36 //

children.translated_text: that is not so.

children.text: nahi 'āgneyaḥ' ityayarṃ taddhataḥ saṃbandhamātre vihitaḥ, kiṃtu ddevatāsaṃbandhe |
children.translated_text: For this <s>taddhita</s> suffix [in '<s>āgneya</s>'] is not prescribed merely for connection in general, but specifically for connection with the deity.
And <s>Agni</s> alone is not the deity of the two-deity sacrificial cakes.

children.text: tato ddevataikadeśena kṛtsnadevatopalakṣaṇatvādāgneyatvaṃ tayorna mukhyamiti mukhya evā'gneye caturdhākaraṇaṃ vyavatiṣṭhate || MJaiNyC_3,1.34-36 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the <s>Āgneya</s>-ness of those two is not primary — because indicating the complete deity by [only] a part of it — the fourfold division is established for the <s>Āgneya</s> [offering] alone, whose [connection with <s>Agni</s> as deity] is primary. || MJaiNyC_3,1.34-36 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, it is heard: '<s>āgneyaṃ caturdhā karoti</s>' (he divides the <s>Āgneya</s> [offering] into four parts).
Therein — just as the <s>Āgneya</s>, so too the <s>Aindrāgna</s> and <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> sacrificial cakes, having a connection with <s>Agni</s>, are indicated by the word '<s>Āgneya</s>' — [therefore] the three cakes are included.
Thus it is subsidiary to all three — if this is the objection,

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīye jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistare tṛtīyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Mādhavīya Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s>.
Now the second <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s>.

children.text: arthābhidhānasāmarthyān mantreṣu śeṣabhāvaḥ syāt tasmād utpattisambandho 'rthena nityasaṃyogāt / Jaim_3,2.1 /
children.translated_text: Because of the capacity to express meaning, <s>mantras</s> would have a subsidiary status; therefore, the connection with the origination [-sentence] is because of the permanent association with the meaning. / Jaim_3,2.1 /
Because of being a consecrating agent, it would be [connected] with what is not [directly] enjoined. / Jaim_3,2.2 /

'<s>Barhir devasadanaṃ dāmi</s>' (I cut the sacred grass, the seat of the gods) — does the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) in this <s>mantra</s>

because the primary is understood first, the [<s>mantra</s>] is restricted to the primary [<s>barhis</s>]. // MJaiNy_3,2.2 //

children.text:
"barhirdevasadanaṃ dāmi' iti lavanaprakāśako mantra āmnātaḥ |

lavitavyaṃ ca barhirdvividham - mukhyaṃ gauṇaṃ ca |
mukhyaṃ - kuśakāśādidaśavidhadarbharūpam |
gauṇaṃ tu -tatsadṛśaṃ tṛṇāntaram |

children.translated_text: This being so, just like the primary, the word '<s>barhis</s>' refers to the secondary as well — hence the <s>mantra</s> is assigned to the cutting of both <s>darbha</s> grass and other grass — having arrived at this position,

children.text: brūmaḥ- mukhyasya śīghrapratītatvena mukhye mantraṃ viniyujya caritārtha liṅgaṃ vilambapratītatayā gauṇapratīkṣāṃ na karoti |
children.translated_text: we say: Since the primary is understood more quickly, the mark, having fulfilled its purpose by assigning the <s>mantra</s> to the primary, does not wait for the secondary, which is understood with delay.

children.text: tasmāt - mukhyasyaiva lavane mantro niyamyate || MJaiNyC_3,2.1-2 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — the <s>mantra</s> is restricted to the cutting of the primary [<s>barhis</s>] alone. || MJaiNyC_3,2.1-2 ||

The <s>mantra</s> '<s>barhir devasadanaṃ dāmi</s>' (I cut the sacred grass, the seat of the gods), which illuminates the cutting (<s>lavana</s>), is recited.
Therein — by the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) characterized by the capacity to illuminate the cutting, this <s>mantra</s> is assigned to the cutting-action.
The <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass) to be cut is of two kinds — primary and secondary.
The primary is the tenfold <s>darbha</s> grass in the form of <s>kuśa</s>, <s>kāśa</s>, and the like.
The secondary is some other grass similar to those.
The word '<s>barhis</s>' applies to the secondary through connection with a qualifying attribute, like the word '<s>agni</s>' in [the case of] a boy [called Agni].
(In the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (the <s>Aindrī</s> principle), on the assignment of the <s>Aindrī</s> [<s>ṛc</s>] to the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire — <s>sūtras</s> 3-4)

children.text: vacanāt tv ayathārtham aindrī syāt / Jaim_3,2.3 /

children.translated_text: Or the statement would be from the qualifying attribute as well, because the connection is not scripturally caused. / Jaim_3,2.4 /

children.text: prakāśye mukhya indre vā gauṇe mukhye 'stu pūrvavat // MJaiNy_3,2.3 //

Since one of the two has a secondary meaning, because the <s>mantra</s> itself is an anaphoric reference,
since there is secondary meaning, the <s>mantra</s> is assigned by scripture to the fire-worship (<s>agnyupasthāna</s>). // MJaiNy_3,2.4 //

children.translated_text: But the secondary <s>Indra</s> is the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire.
Because of his similarity to the primary <s>Indra</s> through the qualifying attribute of lordship or through being an instrument of sacrifice.

children.text: tatra pūrvānyāyena śīghrapratītyā mukhyendra mantreṇa prakāśite sati mantrabrāhmaṇayorvisaṃvādaṃ vārayituṃ gārhapatyaśabdena mukhyendro gārhapatyasamīpadeśo vā lakṣaṇīyaḥ- iti prāpte, brūmaḥ- indragāharpatyaśabdayoranyatasya gauṇatve 'vaśyaṃbhāvini sati brāhmaṇavākyasya vidhāyakatvādaprāptārthatvena vidhau lakṣaṇāyā anyāyyatvātprāptārthatvenānuvādako mantra evendraśabdena vahniṃ lakṣayiṣyati |
children.translated_text: Therein, by the preceding principle, when the primary Indra has been indicated through the mantra by virtue of quick apprehension, in order to prevent contradiction between the mantra and the Brāhmaṇa, the word 'Gārhapatya' should be taken figuratively to mean the primary Indra or the location near the Gārhapatya [fire] — having arrived at this position, we say: Since it is inevitable that one of the two words 'Indra' and 'Gārhapatya' must be taken in a secondary sense, and since the Brāhmaṇa sentence, being injunctive, conveys something not otherwise known and figurative interpretation in an injunction is improper, it is rather the mantra, being a restatement of what is already known, that will figuratively indicate <s>Agni</s> (fire) by the word '<s>Indra</s>'.

children.text: tato gārhapatyaprakāśane samarthameva mantram 'aindryā' iti tṛtīyāśrutirgārhapatyopasthāne viniyuṅkte || MJaiNyC_3,2.3-4 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, the mantra being fully capable of indicating the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire], the third-case ending (<s>tṛtīyā</s> vibhakti) in '<s>aindrī</s>' assigns it to the service of the <s>Gārhapatya</s>. || MJaiNyC_3,2.3-4 ||

In the <s>Agnicayana</s>, a certain <s>ṛc</s> addressed to <s>Indra</s> (<s>Aindrī</s>) is recited: '<s>niveśanaḥ saṃgamanaḥ</s>' (the settler, the assembler) and so on.
[It is called <s>Aindrī</s>] because in its latter half, '<s>indro na tasthau</s>' (<s>Indra</s> stood firm) is recited.
And the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage pertaining to that <s>mantra</s> is recited thus: '<s>niveśanaḥ saṃgamano vasūnām ity aindryā gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhate</s>' (with the <s>Aindrī</s> [<s>ṛc</s>] '<s>niveśanaḥ saṃgamanaḥ vasūnām</s>' one worships the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire).
By this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the <s>mantra</s> being assigned to the worship of the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire illuminates the primary <s>Indra</s> in its meaning.
And the primary <s>Indra</s> is the lord of heaven, the thousand-eyed one,
because the word '<s>Indra</s>' is conventionally established (<s>rūḍha</s>) in that sense.
(In the third [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the assignment of the invocation, <s>sūtras</s> 4–9) /
Similarly with regard to the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire] also — if so [it is argued]. / Jaim_3,2.5 /
No — the time-specification is [not needed] because it is already enjoined. / Jaim_3,2.6 /
Because of the absence of the subordinate [element]. / Jaim_3,2.7 /
And because of the mark (<s>liṅga</s>). / Jaim_3,2.8 /
And there would be a conflict with the injunction if [it were merely] instruction. / Jaim_3,2.9 /

He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Having addressed [the wife] with '<s>haviṣkṛdehī</s>' (O preparer of the oblation, come!), one should invoke while striking thrice;
the assignment may be in the striking or in the invocation along with the striking. // MJaiNy_3,2.5 //
Like the <s>Aindrī</s> [case], the invocation by the mantra is secondary; '<s>hanti</s>' (strikes) is purposeless otherwise;
the triplicity obtained through the recitation — this is figurative speech regarding '<s>hvayati</s>' (invokes). // MJaiNy_3,2.6 //
The triple repetition is to be enjoined, because it is not obtained as a permanent [rule];

children.text: hantinā lakṣyate kālaḥ prāpto 'sau hvayatistathā // MJaiNy_3,2.7 //
children.translated_text: '<s>hanti</s>' (strikes) indicates the time; that [time] is already established, and so too '<s>hvayati</s>' (invokes). // MJaiNy_3,2.7 //
In the assignment, there would be sentence-splitting; by the mark, [it is] subsidiary to the invocation;
the <s>Aindrī</s> principle does not apply here due to the absence of the [third-case] <s>śruti</s>; by the <s>Barhis</s> principle, the primary [meaning] prevails. // MJaiNy_3,2.8 //

children.translated_text: Nor does the <s>Aindrī</s> principle extend here,
because of the absence of the third-case <s>śruti</s> (Vedic testimony).

children.text: 'barhiddevasadanaṃ dāmi' ityatroktena tu nyāyena mukhya evā'hvāne liṅgena mantraviniyogaḥ, na tvavavātarūpe gauṇāhvāne |
children.translated_text: But by the principle stated in the context of '<s>barhiddevasadanaṃ dāmi</s>' (I place the <s>barhis</s>, the seat of the gods), the assignment of the mantra is by the mark to the primary invocation, not to the striking which is a secondary form of invocation.
Therefore — this mantra is subsidiary to the invocation. || MJaiNyC_3,2.5-8 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices), it is heard: '<s>haviṣkṛdehīti triravaghnannāhvayati</s>' (saying 'O preparer of the oblation, come!' he invokes while striking thrice). She who prepares the oblation (<s>havis</s>) for the gods is the <s>haviṣkṛt</s>. Addressing her, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> says 'come!' (<s>ehi</s>). And this mantra is explained by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> thus: '<s>haviṣkṛdehītyāha yā eva devānāṃ haviṣkṛtastānāhvayati</s>' (he says 'O preparer of the oblation, come!' — he thereby invokes those who are the preparers of the oblation for the gods). The meaning is: having recited this mantra, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> invokes while performing the striking three times. By this sentence, the mantra is assigned to the striking. But [the objection is:] [the mantra] is capable [of being assigned] to the invocation, not to the striking — if so [it is argued], no. Because it indicates the striking [as the occasion]. Just as in the previously cited <s>Aindrī</s> [case] the word '<s>Indra</s>' is secondary, so too the word '<s>ehi</s>' (come!), being within the mantra, will be secondary with respect to the striking. Otherwise, since both the mantra and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> would refer to the invocation, the word '<s>avaghnan</s>' (striking) that is heard would become purposeless. [If it is argued:] In the injunction of the mantra and of the triplicity with reference to the already-established striking, there would be sentence-splitting — if so, no. Because the triplicity, being already known, is merely restated. In a certain <s>śākhā</s> (Vedic recension), this mantra is recited three times in repetition in the <s>Mantrakāṇḍa</s>. The word '<s>āhvayati</s>' (invokes) is to be figuratively understood as referring to the striking, just like '<s>ehi</s>' (come!) — having arrived at this position, we say: The obtaining of the triple repetition as a permanent [rule] is not established by mere recitation alone. Because in some schools it is recited twice. In some, only once. Therefore, it is enjoined as if it were a permanent [rule]. Nor is the word '<s>avaghnan</s>' (striking) purposeless. Because it indicates the time. [If it is argued:] In the injunction of the time also, there would be sentence-splitting — if so, no. Because [the time] is already established. For the invocation does not occur at any time other than together with the striking. Therefore, the time is established by the nature of the action. The invocation too, being already established by the very capacity of the mantra, is not to be enjoined. For the recitation of the mantra '<s>ehi</s>' (come!) cannot be explained without the invocation. And the mantra-explanation has been cited. Therein, this sentence-meaning is established: 'The triple repetition of the invocation at the time of striking is to be performed.' For this very reason, in another <s>śākhā</s>, the repetition is clearly enjoined by restating the invocation: '<s>trirāhvayati triḥsatyā hi devāḥ</s>' (he invokes thrice, for the gods are true thrice). This being so, even in the assignment of the mantra there would be sentence-splitting. But by the mark (<s>liṅga</s>), it is assigned to the invocation, not to the striking.
(In the fourth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the assignment of mantras that indicate fire-carrying and the like, the <s>sūtra</s> is:) /
Similarly with the rising and the dismissal. / Jaim_3,2.10 /
START MJaiNy 3,2.9-11
He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
While rising, one should recite '<s>agnīdagnīn</s>' (O <s>Āgnīdh</s>, [carry forward] the fires) and the like; similarly,
while reciting '<s>kṛṇuta vratam</s>' (perform the vow), one releases the speech. // MJaiNy_3,2.9 //
Are the two mantras to be enjoined, or the time? The two mantras are to be assigned to the rising and the releasing;

children.text: viniyojyau na kālasya lakṣaṇā yujyate vidhau // MJaiNy_3,2.10 //
children.translated_text: figurative interpretation of the time is not appropriate in an injunction. // MJaiNy_3,2.10 //
Due to the non-connection of the meaning of the mantras therein, such an injunction is not possible;

children.text: agatyā lakṣaṇāpyastu tena kālo vidhīyate // MJaiNy_3,2.11 //
children.translated_text: even if figurative interpretation be accepted out of necessity, thereby the time is enjoined. // MJaiNy_3,2.11 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome samāmananti - 'uttiṣṭhannanvāhāgnīdagnīnvihara' iti |
tathā - 'vrataṃ kṛṇuteti vācaṃ visṛjati' iti |
tatra - āgnīdhraṃ saṃbodhyāgniviharaṇādipraiṣarūpo mantro 'nena vākyenotthānaśeṣatayā viniyujyate |
tathā- muṣṭiṃ kṛtvā niyamitavāco dīkṣitasya vāgvimoke 'vrataṃ kṛṇuta' iti mantro viniyujyate |
children.translated_text: Similarly — for the <s>dīkṣita</s> (consecrated person) who has formed a fist and restrained his speech, the mantra '<s>vrataṃ kṛṇuta</s>' (perform the vow) is assigned at the release of speech.
And here, unlike the word '<s>avaghāta</s>' (striking) mentioned earlier, the words '<s>utthāna</s>' (rising) and '<s>vimoka</s>' (release) do not indicate the time.

children.text: tatkālayoravaghātakālavadarthaprāptyabhāvena vidheyatve sati lakṣaṇāyā anyāyyatvāt - iti prāpte, brūmaḥ- agniviharaṇapraiṣe payaḥpānarūpavratasaṃpādanapraiṣe cānvitāvetau mantrau, na tūtthāne vāgvimoke ca |
children.translated_text: Since, unlike the time of striking, there is no establishment by the nature of the action for those respective times, and since when [they are] to be enjoined, figurative interpretation is improper — having arrived at this position, we say: The two mantras are connected with the directive for fire-carrying and the directive for accomplishing the vow in the form of milk-drinking, but not with the rising and the release of speech.

Therefore, since the assignment of the two, which are not meaningfully connected [with rising and speech-release], is impossible, accepting figurative interpretation even out of necessity, the time is enjoined. || MJaiNyC_3,2.9-11 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, they recite: '<s>uttiṣṭhannanvāhāgnīdagnīnvihara</s>' (while rising, he says: O <s>Āgnīdh</s>, carry forward the fires). Similarly: '<s>vrataṃ kṛṇuteti vācaṃ visṛjati</s>' (saying 'perform the vow,' he releases the speech). Therein — the mantra in the form of a directive (<s>praiṣa</s>) for fire-carrying addressed to the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> is assigned by this sentence as subsidiary to the rising.
(In the fifth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the subsidiarity of the <s>Sūktavāka</s> to the casting of the <s>Prastara</s> [the <s>Prastarapraharaṇa</s> principle], <s>sūtras</s> 11–14:) /
And in the <s>Sūktavāka</s>, the time-specification [applies], because it serves another's purpose. / Jaim_3,2.11 /

children.translated_text: The subsidiarity of the <s>Sūktavāka</s>, which reveals deities such as <s>Agni</s>, to the casting is understood from the third-case <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: yadi prakaraṇe 'gnyādayo devatā bhaveyuḥ, tadā tatprakāśanena dṛṣṭor'tho mantrasya labhyeta |
children.translated_text: If in the ritual context <s>Agni</s> and other deities are present, then by revealing them, the mantra obtains a visible purpose.

children.text: tato devatākalpanena taduddeśapūrvakasya prakṣepasya yāgatvaṃ sidhyati |
children.translated_text: Thereby, by positing the deities, the status of the casting as a sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) — being a throwing preceded by dedication to them — is established.
Therefore — there is indeed connection through the medium of the deity. || MJaiNyC_3,2.12-13 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices), it is recited: '<s>sūktavākena prastaraṃ praharati</s>' (he casts the <s>Prastara</s> with the <s>Sūktavāka</s>). The mantra beginning with '<s>idaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī bhadramabhūt</s>' (this auspicious [rite] has been accomplished, O Heaven and Earth) is the <s>Sūktavāka</s>. [It is so called] because in that mantra, <s>Agni</s> is addressed with '<s>tvaṃ sūktavāgasi</s>' (you are the one of good utterance). The <s>Prastara</s> is a handful of <s>darbha</s> grass; its casting (<s>praharaṇa</s>) is the throwing into the fire. Therein — the word '<s>sūktavākena</s>' (with the <s>Sūktavāka</s>) indicates the time. While the <s>Hotṛ</s> is reciting this mantra, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should cast the <s>Prastara</s> at the time of that recitation. But the mantra cannot be assigned here to the casting. Because, as with the previously mentioned directive-mantras, there is no connection here. What is recited in the mantra is: '<s>agniridaṃ havirajuṣatāvīvṛdhata maho jyāyo 'kṛta</s>' (<s>Agni</s> enjoyed this oblation, grew great, and created greater splendor) and the like. Its meaning is: '<s>Agni</s>, increased by the service of the sacrificial cake, created an abundance of radiance in that sacrificial session.' And that [meaning] cannot be connected with the casting of the <s>Prastara</s> — having arrived at this position, we say: By the third-case <s>śruti</s> in '<s>sūktavākena</s>' (with the <s>Sūktavāka</s>), the mantra is assigned to the casting. Nor is there a complete absence of connection. For this mantra brings to mind the gods such as <s>Agni</s> who were previously worshipped. And the casting of the <s>Prastara</s> is a consecration for the desired deities. Therefore, through the medium of the deity, there is a connection between the mantra and the casting, and thus the mantra is assigned. [If it be objected:] The casting is merely a throwing, not a throwing dedicated to a deity. Because the verbal root '<s>yaj</s>' (to sacrifice) is not heard. In that case, due to the absence of the naming of the deities, there would be no connection even through them — if so [it is argued], that is not correct. Because the deities do exist.
In the sixth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>] — the <s>sūtras</s> on the assignment of the <s>Sūktavākas</s> according to their meaning
Because of the instruction regarding the whole, the word 'all' applies to both [rites]. / Jaim_3,2.15 /
in the <s>Yoga</s> <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (the <s>Sūktavāka</s> principle):
Or [it is assigned] according to the meaning, because the consecration is subsidiary. / Jaim_3,2.16 /
Because of the verbal statement — if so [it is argued]. / Jaim_3,2.17 /
The word 'entire' applies to both because there is no division of the context. / Jaim_3,2.18 /

children.translated_text: The meaning is: at the time of the sacrifice, one recites the god who has been properly praised by the respective mantra.

children.text: ata eva brāhmaṇena vyākhyātam- 'agniridaṃ havirajuvatetyāha, yo āyākṣma devatāstā arīradhāmeti bāvaitadāha' iti |
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> explains: '<s>agniridaṃ havirajuṣatetyāha, yo āyākṣma devatāstā arīradhāmeti vāvaitadāha</s>' (he says '<s>Agni</s> enjoyed this oblation'; what he thereby says is 'the deities whom we have besought, them we have propitiated').
'<s>Arīradhāma</s>' means 'we have propitiated, we have pleased [them].'
Therefore, this [<s>Sūktavāka</s>] is assigned by dividing [it]. || MJaiNyC_3,2.14-15 ||

In the previously cited mantra, the designation <s>Sūktavāka</s> extends to the entire mantra. Because ritualists (<s>yājñikas</s>) use that word for the whole. Therefore, the entire [mantra] is subsidiary to the casting — if so [it is argued], no. Because the designation is overridden by the mark. In that mantra, the mention of the full-moon deities is seen in a certain portion: '<s>agnīṣomāvidaṃ havirajuṣetām</s>' (may <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> enjoy this oblation). But in another portion, the mention of the new-moon deities [is seen]: '<s>indrāgnī idaṃ havirajuṣetām</s>' (may <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> enjoy this oblation), '<s>indra idaṃ havirajuṣata</s>' (may <s>Indra</s> enjoy this oblation), '<s>mahendra idaṃ havirajuṣata</s>' (may <s>Mahendra</s> enjoy this oblation). <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Mahendra</s> are established in the new-moon [rite] as different persons [i.e., distinct deities]. This being so, by the mark of the mantra, each portion is established at its respective time according to its respective [deity]. And the word <s>Sūktavāka</s> is etymologically derived (<s>yaugika</s>) for each portion — '<s>sūktaṃ vakti</s>' (one who speaks the <s>sūkta</s>) being its derivation.
(In the seventh [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the subsidiarity of the <s>kāmya</s> [optional] <s>yājyā</s> and <s>anuvākyā</s> [verses] to the <s>kāmya</s> [rites] alone, the <s>sūtra</s> is:) /
Because of the mark, the sequence, and the designation, what is recited is connected with the optional (<s>kāmya</s>) [rite]. / Jaim_3,2.19 /
START MJaiNy 3,2.16-18
He composes the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The <s>Aindrāgna</s> and other optional (<s>kāmya</s>) <s>iṣṭis</s> — their <s>yājyā</s> [verses] are also recited in sequence;
in both sections (<s>kāṇḍas</s>), they are to be distributed according to the mark, or else there is a restriction. // MJaiNy_3,2.16 //
The mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is stronger than sequence (<s>krama</s>) and designation (<s>samākhyā</s>); by its force, those [<s>yājyā</s> and <s>anuvākyā</s> mantras]

children.text: akāmyāsvapi saṃcāryā yājyāḥ sarvatra kā kṣatiḥ // MJaiNy_3,2.17 //
children.translated_text: can be applied even in non-optional (<s>akāmya</s>) rites; what harm is there if they are applicable everywhere? // MJaiNy_3,2.17 //
From the designation, the connection with the <s>kāṇḍa</s> (section); in the sequence-based assignments, [the sequence]
requires only the deity [as input]; the capacity [of sequence and designation] pertains only to the optional (<s>kāmya</s>) rites. // MJaiNy_3,2.18 //

children.translated_text: '<s>idaṃ vām āsye haviḥ</s>' (this oblation is in your mouth) — this is one pair.
'<s>asme indrā bṛhaspatī</s>' (for us, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>) and the like — this is another.

children.text: tayoḥ prathamayugalasya krameṇa viniyoge 'pi dvitīyayugalaṃ liṅgenaiva viniyoktavyam |
children.translated_text: Even when the first pair is assigned by sequence, the second pair must be assigned by the mark alone.
Therefore — aided by sequence and designation, these <s>yājyā</s> [mantras] are restricted to the optional sacrifices alone. || MJaiNyC_3,2.16-18 ||

The optional sacrifices (<s>kāmyeṣṭi</s>) are recited in that <s>kāṇḍa</s> in sequence: '<s>aindrāgnam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped yasya sajātā vīyuḥ</s>' (one should offer an eleven-potsherd cake to <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s> for one whose kinsmen have turned away) and so on. '<s>Sajātāḥ</s>' means kinsmen; '<s>vīyuḥ</s>' means departed, i.e., turned hostile. In the <s>mantra</s> section, the <s>yājyā</s> and <s>anuvākyā</s> [mantras] are recited in sequence, beginning with '<s>indrāgnī rocanā</s>' and the like. Therein, the designation of the sacrificial specialists — 'this is the <s>kāṇḍa</s> (section) of <s>yājyā</s> and <s>anuvākyā</s> mantras for optional rites' — is understood. The assignment is made by sequence between the two — the sacrifice-<s>kāṇḍa</s> and the <s>mantra</s>-<s>kāṇḍa</s> — such that the first pair of <s>yājyā</s>-<s>anuvākyā</s> [mantras] in the <s>mantra</s> section corresponds to the first sacrifice in the sacrifice section, and so on. But the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s> [deity reference] in the <s>mantra</s> assigns those <s>yājyā</s>-<s>anuvākyā</s> mantras to the <s>Aindrāgna</s> sacrifice — whether optional or obligatory (<s>nitya</s>). And since the mark is stronger, they should be assigned everywhere — having arrived at this position, we say: Here, the mark cannot override the sequence and designation. Because [the mark] depends on [them]. The mark merely reveals the nature of the deity — <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>. But that alone does not establish the ancillary-principal relationship between the <s>mantra</s> and the rite. Therefore, by the force of the designation, when the connection between the <s>mantra</s>-<s>kāṇḍa</s> and the rite-<s>kāṇḍa</s> is understood, the general connection between <s>mantra</s> and rite is understood. The specific [assignment] — 'in this first rite, this first <s>mantra</s>' — is understood from the sequence. Now, if it be argued that the specific [assignment] — 'in the <s>Aindrāgna</s> sacrifice, the <s>Aindrāgna</s> <s>mantra</s>; in the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> sacrifice, the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>mantra</s>' — is understood by the mark alone, no — because when the mark is common [to multiple rites], the sequence must be relied upon. '<s>Aindrāgnam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped bhrātṛvyavān</s>' (one possessing a rival should offer an eleven-potsherd cake to <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>) — this is also a second <s>Aindrāgna</s> sacrifice. In the <s>mantra</s> section too, '<s>indrāgnī navatim</s>' and the like — another pair of <s>Aindrāgna yājyā</s>-<s>anuvākyā</s> mantras is recited. There, determination is not possible without sequence. Nor should it be said that since the matter is settled by sequence alone, the mark is without purpose — because in some cases, the mark alone is the establisher. The <s>Aindrā-Bārhaspatya</s> sacrifice is recited as unique: '<s>yaṃ kāmayeta rājanyam anayuddho jāyeta vṛtrāghnaṃś caret — iti tasmā enam aindrābārhaspatyaṃ caruṃ nirvaped</s>' (for whichever prince one desires — 'may he be born unconquered and go about slaying enemies' — for him one should offer the <s>Aindrā-Bārhaspatya caru</s>). The desire of the king and the priest regarding a prince about to be born is: 'may he be born without obstruction by any divine impediment in the mother's womb, and once born, may he go about slaying enemies.' This sacrifice is for the sake of that prince. In the <s>mantra</s> section, at the point corresponding to that sacrifice in sequence, two kinds of <s>yājyā</s>-<s>puronuvākyā</s> mantras having <s>Indra</s>-<s>Bṛhaspati</s> as deity are recited.
(In the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the assignment of archetype mantras in the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> adoration (<s>upasthāna</s>), <s>sūtras</s> 20–23)

He composes the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In the <s>Āgneya</s> [rite], for the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> [hall], the <s>Ṛk</s> verses having <s>Agni</s> as deity — are all of them

Due to the general statement with the word [<s>āgneyyā</s>], the adoration would be with all [such verses];
but since the injunction pertains to the specific [application], [it should be] with the archetype [verses] only — let this be accepted. // MJaiNy_3,2.20 //

'ko 'sau vyāpāraḥ' iti viśeṣabubhutsāyām 'āgnīdhropasyānarūpo 'yam, iti bodhayannayaṃ vidhirviśeṣamātre saṃkrāmatīti lāghavam |
children.translated_text: When the specific [function] is sought — 'what is that function?' — this injunction, by indicating 'it is in the form of the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> adoration,' pertains only to the specific [function] — this is the more parsimonious [interpretation].

children.text: aprakṛtānāṃ kratūpayuktavyāpārasādhanatvaṃ tadvyāpāraviśeṣaṣcetyubhayamanena bodhyata iti gauravam |
children.translated_text: For non-archetype [verses], both — the instrumentality for a ritual function of the sacrifice and the specific nature of that function — would have to be conveyed by this [injunction], which is burdensome.
Therefore, the adoration is with the archetype <s>Āgneya</s> [verses].

children.text: evam 'aindyā sado vaiṣṇavyā havirdhānam' ityatra sadohavirdhānanāmakayormaṇḍapayorupasthāne prakṛtānāmevaindrīṇāṃ vaṣṇaivīnāṃ ca prayoga iti draṣṭavyam || MJaiNyC_3,2.19-20 ||
children.translated_text: Similarly, in '<s>aindyā sado vaiṣṇavyā havirdhānam</s>' (the <s>Sadas</s> [hall is adorned] with <s>Aindra</s> [verses], the <s>Havirdhāna</s> with <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> [verses]), the application of only the archetype <s>Aindrī</s> and <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> verses for the adoration of the halls named <s>Sadas</s> and <s>Havirdhāna</s> should be understood. || MJaiNyC_3,2.19-20 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, it is heard: '<s>āgneyyāgnīdhram upatiṣṭhate</s>' (one adores the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> [hall] with an <s>Āgneya</s> [verse]). Therein — the adoration of the hall named <s>Āgnīdhra</s> is to be performed with any <s>Ṛk</s> verse from the <s>Daśatayī</s> (ten-hymn collection) that has a connection with <s>Agni</s>. Because the specific verse is not apprehended from the general statement '<s>āgneyī</s>' (belonging to <s>Agni</s>), where '<s>agnir devatā yasyā ṛcaḥ sāgneyī</s>' (that <s>Ṛk</s> whose deity is <s>Agni</s> is <s>āgneyī</s>) — if so it is argued, that is not correct. The fact that the <s>Āgneya</s> verses recited in the sacrificial context are means of accomplishing some ritual function pertaining to the sacrifice is understood from the context alone.
(In the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the assignment of <s>bhakṣa</s> (drinking) mantras according to the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) in the cup-drawing and the like, <s>sūtras</s> 24–25)
By means of the mark and the designation, the <s>anuvāka</s> (section) serves the purpose of the <s>bhakṣa</s> (drinking). / Jaim_3,2.24 /
Its withdrawal is through the form and the instruction, because the purpose is enjoined. / Jaim_3,2.25 /
He composes the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is this <s>anuvāka</s> [beginning with] '<s>bhakṣehi</s>' (drink!) to be used entirely in the drinking, or
is it to be divided and fixed in the cup-drawing and the like according to fitness? // MJaiNy_3,2.21 //
Since the cup-drawing and the like are not [separately] enjoined, let that entire [<s>anuvāka</s>] apply to the drinking;
but since they [cup-drawing etc.] are implied by the meaning, [the <s>anuvāka</s>] is divided according to the marks. // MJaiNy_3,2.22 //

children.translated_text: Nor is there an absence of human effort in digestion,
because proper sitting posture and the like serve the purpose of digestion.
'<s>Mandrābhibhūtiḥ</s>' (the gentle overpowerer) and so on, up to '<s>bhakṣayāmi</s>' (I drink) — [this portion] indicates the [actual] drinking.

children.text: tasmāt- liṅgena samākhyāṃ bādhitvā viniyogaḥ kartavyaḥ || MJaiNyC_3,2.21-22 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — the assignment should be made by overriding the designation through the mark. || MJaiNyC_3,2.21-22 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the drinking of the remaining <s>Soma</s> after offering is enjoined. Thus it is recited: '<s>abhiṣutyāhavanīye hutvā pratyañcaḥ paretya sadasi somaṃ bhakṣayanti</s>' (having pressed and offered in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, they return westward and drink <s>Soma</s> in the <s>Sadas</s> hall). In that drinking, there are four procedures: grasping (<s>grahaṇa</s>), inspecting (<s>avekṣaṇa</s>), swallowing (<s>nigaraṇa</s>), and proper digestion (<s>samyagjaraṇa</s>). And the <s>mantra</s> is recited in the <s>anuvāka</s> beginning with '<s>bhakṣehi</s>' (drink!). Therein, just as the drinking is directly enjoined, the grasping, inspecting, swallowing, and proper digestion are not [directly] enjoined. And a <s>mantra</s> cannot be assigned to what is not enjoined. The designation '<s>bhakṣānuvākaḥ</s>' (drinking-<s>anuvāka</s>) pertains only to the drinking. Therefore, the entire <s>anuvāka</s> should be assigned to the drinking alone — having arrived at this position, we say: Even though not [explicitly] enjoined, the grasping and the like are implied by the meaning (<s>arthākṣipta</s>) — because without them, drinking is impossible. Therefore, the <s>anuvāka</s> should be divided among them and assigned according to the marks (<s>liṅga</s>). Therein, from '<s>bhakṣehi</s>' (drink!) up to '<s>aśvinoḥ tvā bāhubhyāṃ sādhyāsam</s>' (may I accomplish you with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>) — [this portion] indicates the grasping. Because the summons '<s>ehi</s>' (come!) and 'may I receive you with the arms [of the <s>Aśvins</s>]' are observed [therein]. '<s>Nṛcakṣasaṃ tvā deva soma sucakṣā avakhyeṣam</s>' (O divine <s>Soma</s>, who art perceived by men, may I, being of good sight, behold you) — this portion indicates the inspecting. Because it states 'may I, being of good sight among men, behold you who are celebrated.' '<s>Hinva me gātrā</s>' (strengthen my limbs) and so on, up to '<s>mā me 'vāṅ nābhim atigāḥ</s>' (do not pass below my navel) — [this portion] indicates proper digestion. Because that [digestion] is understood through the delighting of the limbs and the prohibition against passing into the lower region. [If it be objected:] digestion is not implied by the meaning, since drinking is accomplished even without it — no. Because only drinking that extends to digestion is meaningful.
(In the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the unity of the <s>mantra</s> beginning with '<s>mandrābhibhūtiḥ</s>', the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: guṇābhidhānān mandrādir ekamantraḥ syāt tayor ekārthasaṃyogāt / Jaim_3,2.26 /
children.translated_text: Since it states a qualifying attribute, the [passage] beginning with '<s>mandrā</s>' would be a single <s>mantra</s>, because of the connection of both with a single meaning. / Jaim_3,2.26 /
START MJaiNy 3,2.23-24
He composes the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Are the two [passages] '<s>mandrā</s>' (the gentle) and '<s>vasumad</s>' (the wealthy) to be divided between satiation (<s>tarpaṇa</s>) and drinking (<s>bhakṣa</s>),
or should the entirety [be assigned] to the drinking that is accompanied by satiation? // MJaiNy_3,2.23 //
By the mark, there would be division; but no — satiation does not arise from [a source] other than drinking;
when the mark is inapplicable, by the sentence-complement, let the entirety apply to the drinking. // MJaiNy_3,2.24 //

children.text:
'mandrābhibhūtiḥ' - ityādiḥ 'juṣāṇā somasya tṛpyatu' ityanto bhāgo hṛṣṭāyā arucimabhibhavantyāḥ somaṃ sevamānāyā jihvāyāstṛptiṃ prakāśayati |
'vasumadgaṇasya'- ityādiḥ 'bhakṣayāmi' ityanto bhāgo bhakṣaṇaprakāśakaḥ |
tatra pūrvaballiṅgena vibhajya viniyogaḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
na khalu tṛptirbhakṣaṇādanyena vyāpāreṇa jāyate |
kiṃ tarhi-bhakṣaṇāmuniṣpādinī hi sā |
tathā sati kasminvyāpāre tṛptiprakāśako bhāgo viniyujyeta |

children.translated_text: Therefore, since assignment by the mark is impossible, the satiation-indicating portion will be the complement of the drinking-sentence.
And this portion is indeed useful there,
because by indicating drinking accompanied by satiation, it generates enthusiasm in the performer.
Therefore, the entire [passage] beginning with '<s>mandrā</s>' is assigned to the drinking. || MJaiNyC_3,2.23-24 ||

The portion from '<s>mandrābhibhūtiḥ</s>' (the gentle overpowerer) up to '<s>juṣāṇā somasya tṛpyatu</s>' (may the [tongue], enjoying, be satiated with <s>Soma</s>) indicates the satiation of the tongue that is delighted, that overcomes distaste, and that is savoring the <s>Soma</s>. The portion from '<s>vasumad gaṇasya</s>' (of the wealthy troop) up to '<s>bhakṣayāmi</s>' (I drink) indicates the drinking. Therein, [the two portions] should be divided and assigned by the force of the mark in the preceding [portion] — if so it is argued, that is not correct. Satiation does not arise from any procedure other than drinking. Rather, it is an effect inseparable from drinking. This being so, in which procedure would the satiation-indicating portion be assigned?
(In the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the assignment of mantras beginning with '<s>indrapītasya</s>' (drunk by <s>Indra</s>), <s>sūtras</s> 27–28)

Because of the specification by a particular mark (<s>liṅgaviśeṣa</s>), in rites of the same procedure, those that are non-<s>Aindra</s> (not relating to <s>Indra</s>) would lack <s>mantra</s>-status. / Jaim_3,2.27 /

children.text: yathādevataṃ vā tatprakṛtitvaṃ hi darśayati / Jaim_3,2.28 /
children.translated_text: Or [the assignment is] according to the deity, because [the mark] shows the archetype-nature of that [rite]. / Jaim_3,2.28 /
START MJaiNy 3,2.25-27
He composes the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is '<s>indrapītasya</s>' (drunk by <s>Indra</s>) a portion of the <s>bhakṣa</s> (drinking) <s>mantra</s> — [assigned] here only to the <s>Aindra</s> [cup]
alone, or to others as well — with substitution (<s>ūha</s>) — or to all, since it is heard without [specific] purpose? // MJaiNy_3,2.25 //
To the <s>Aindra</s> [cup] alone, because of [the mark's] applicability; for the drinking of the others, [it is performed] silently (<s>tūṣṇīm</s>);
or, with substitution in the others — even when the rite is one, substitution exists because of the difference in drinking [procedures]. // MJaiNy_3,2.26 //
Since the [<s>mantra</s>] states that in a certain pressing (<s>savana</s>) the <s>Soma</s> was drunk by <s>Indra</s>,
let the <s>mantra</s> be recited — without substitution — for all [cups] situated in that pressing. // MJaiNy_3,2.27 //

children.text:
bhakṣamantre kaścidaṃśaḥ 'indrapītasya' ityevaṃvidhaḥ śrūyate |
tatra- 'indreṇa pūtasya somasya śeṣaṃ bhakṣayāmi' ityartho bhavati |
tathā satyasya mantrasyendrapradānaśeṣabhakṣaṇa eva samarthatvāttatraivāyaṃ mantro viniyujyate, na tu maitrāvaruṇādiśeṣabhakṣaṇe |
tasmādamantrakameva tadbhakṣaṇam, ityekaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ |
'indrapītasya' iti padasyāsamarthatve 'pi 'mitrāvaruṇapītasya' ityeṣamūhe sati sāmarthye bhaviṣyati |
nanu-āgneyayāgasya prakṛtitvāttadvatasya 'agnaye juṣṭam' |
iti mantrasya vikṛtau saurye carau 'sūryāya juṣṭam' ityevamūhaḥ kriyate |
iha tu karmaikyānnohaḥ- iti cet |
na |
karmabheda iva bhakṣabhede 'pyūhituṃ śakyatvāt |
iti dvitīyaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ |
'indrapītasya' ityatra bahuvrīhirdraṣṭavyaḥ |
tatpurūṣatve 'samāsasya' (pā.sū. 6.1.123) iti sūtreṇāntodāttatvaprasaṅgāt |

children.translated_text: For this word is recorded with the initial syllable accented.
And the stem '<s>indra</s>' is inherently accented on the initial syllable.

children.text: tathā sati 'bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam'[pā.sū. 6.2.1] iti sūtreṇa pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaravidhānātsamastapadamapyādyudāttameva saṃpadyate |
children.translated_text: This being so, by the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam</s>' (<s>Pāṇini</s> 6.2.1), which prescribes that the prior member retains its original accent in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, the compound word also turns out to have the initial syllable accented.

children.text: 'indreṇa pītaḥ somo yasminsavane' iti vigrahātsavanaparatve sati 'aindrabhakṣaṇa eva' iti niyantumasamarthatvātsarvabhakṣaṇeṣvanūhenaivāyaṃ mantraḥ prayoktavya iti rāddhāntaḥ || MJaiNyC_3,2.25-27 ||
children.translated_text: With the analysis 'the pressing (<s>savana</s>) in which <s>Soma</s> was drunk by <s>Indra</s>,' when [the compound] refers to the pressing, it is unable to restrict [the <s>mantra</s>] to '<s>Aindra</s> drinking alone.' Therefore, this <s>mantra</s> should be employed through substitution (<s>ūha</s>) in all drinkings — this is the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>). || MJaiNyC_3,2.25-27 ||

In the drinking-mantra, a certain portion such as 'indrapītasya' (drunk by Indra) is heard. Therein, the meaning is: 'I drink the remainder of the Soma purified by Indra.' Since the mantra is applicable only to the drinking of the remainder given to Indra, the mantra is assigned there alone, and not to the drinking of the remainder of Maitrāvaruṇa and others. Therefore, that drinking [of the remainder of Maitrāvaruṇa etc.] is without mantra — this is the first <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view). Even if the word '<s>indrapītasya</s>' is inapplicable [to others], when substitution (<s>ūha</s>) is made as '<s>mitrāvaruṇapītasya</s>' (drunk by <s>Mitrāvaruṇa</s>), applicability will arise. [Objection:] Since the <s>Āgneya</s> sacrifice is the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>), its <s>mantra</s> '<s>agnaye juṣṭam</s>' (pleasing to <s>Agni</s>) is substituted in the modified (<s>vikṛti</s>) <s>Saurya</s> oblation as '<s>sūryāya juṣṭam</s>' (pleasing to <s>Sūrya</s>). But here, since the rite is one, there is no substitution — if so argued, no. Because substitution is possible in the difference of drinking [portions] just as in the difference of rites. This is the second <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>. In '<s>indrapītasya</s>', a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (possessive compound) should be recognized. Because if it were a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> (determinative compound), by the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>samāsasya</s>' (<s>Pāṇini</s> 6.1.123), the accent would fall on the final syllable.
(In the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the drinking of <s>Soma</s> that has been re-elevated (<s>abhyunnīta</s>), <s>sūtras</s> 29–31)
When [the <s>Soma</s>] has been re-elevated, it serves as an indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) for all [deities], because it pertains to two. / Jaim_3,2.29 /
Or, because of the removal of the prior [<s>Soma</s>], [it is] not an indicator. / Jaim_3,2.30 /
Or, the removal would be due to the drawing (<s>grahaṇa</s>). / Jaim_3,2.31 /
START MJaiNy 3,2.28-30
He composes the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
On the view of substitution (<s>ūha</s>), that which is to be substituted is examined in a set of five principles (<s>nyāyapañcaka</s>):
When [<s>Soma</s>] has been offered to <s>Indra</s>, then its remainder, situated in the cups of the <s>Hotraka</s> [priests] — // MJaiNy_3,2.28 //
Having re-elevated the <s>Soma</s>, offering it to the gods, it is then drunk together;

children.text: indro na lakṣyo lakṣyo vā na śeṣe 'nyārthatā yataḥ // MJaiNy_3,2.29 //
children.translated_text: Is <s>Indra</s> not to be indicated, or is he to be indicated? In the remainder, [he is not], because [the remainder serves] another's purpose. // MJaiNy_3,2.29 //

children.text: unnīta eva saṃbaddho na pūrvo devatāntaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Only the re-elevated [<s>Soma</s>] is connected, not the prior, with the other deities;

children.text: ata indrasya siddhyarthe lakṣyo 'sāvitaraiḥ saha // MJaiNy_3,2.30 //
children.translated_text: therefore, for establishing <s>Indra</s>'s [connection], he is to be indicated along with the others. // MJaiNy_3,2.30 //

pūrvādhikaraṇe yo 'yamūharūpo dvitīyaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ, tatprasaṃṅgātkṛtvācintārūpeṇa nyāyapañcakenohaviṣayaścintyate |
maitrāvaruṇabrāhmaṇācchaṃsipotrādaya ṛtvijo hotrakāḥ |
teṣāṃ ca santi camasāḥ |
pātraviśeṣasthitāḥ somarasāścamasāḥ |

children.translated_text: Therefore — since there is no connection with <s>Indra</s>, <s>Indra</s> should not be indicated — having arrived at this position,

children.text: brūmaḥ- mā bhūtsaṃkalpaḥ, tathāpyunnayanaṃ kariṣyamāṇaṃ maitrāvaruṇādiyāgārthameva |
children.translated_text: we say: let there be no [explicit] intention; nevertheless, the re-elevation that is about to be performed is indeed for the purpose of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> and other sacrifices.
But it is not possible for it to have the character of the <s>Indra</s> sacrifice that was previously performed.

children.text: tasmādunnīto mitrāvaruṇādisaṃbaddhaśeṣa indrasaṃbaddha evetyubhayabhakṣaṇe mitrāvaruṇādibhiḥ sahendro 'pyupalakṣaṇīyaḥ || MJaiNyC_3,2.28-30 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, the re-elevated remainder, being connected with <s>Mitrāvaruṇa</s> and others, is indeed also connected with <s>Indra</s> — thus in both drinkings, <s>Indra</s> too is to be indicated along with <s>Mitrāvaruṇa</s> and others. || MJaiNyC_3,2.28-30 ||

The second <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> in the form of substitution (<s>ūha</s>) from the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s> — taking occasion from that, the scope of substitution is examined through a set of five principles in the form of investigation. The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>, <s>Potṛ</s>, and others are <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests) called <s>Hotrakāḥ</s>. And they have cups (<s>camasāḥ</s>). <s>Soma</s> juices situated in special vessels are the cups. With those, oblations are to be made at the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> and <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> calls. Since the cups belong to <s>Indra</s>, at the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> call, <s>Indra</s> is offered to first. Then, after [offering] the remainder in the cup, having re-elevated additional <s>Soma</s>, the <s>Hotraka</s> [priests] offer to the other deities at the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> call. There, the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [priest] worships <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> with the <s>mantra</s> '<s>mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe</s>' (we invoke <s>Mitra</s>). The <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> worships <s>Indra</s> with the <s>mantra</s> '<s>indra tvā vṛṣabhaṃ vayam</s>' (O <s>Indra</s>, you the bull). The <s>Potṛ</s> worships the <s>Maruts</s> with the <s>mantra</s> '<s>maruto yasya hi kṣaye</s>' (the <s>Maruts</s>, in whose dwelling). Having thus offered, the <s>Soma</s> is drunk afterward. In that drinking, the <s>mantra</s> is to be substituted as '<s>mitrāvaruṇapītasya</s>' (drunk by <s>Mitrāvaruṇa</s>). At that time, <s>Indra</s> should not be indicated (<s>upalakṣaṇīya</s>) together with <s>Mitrāvaruṇa</s> as '<s>indramitrāvaruṇapītasya</s>.' Why? Because when the remainder of the [<s>Soma</s>] re-elevated after [the offering to] <s>Indra</s> serves the purpose of <s>Mitrāvaruṇa</s> and others, that remainder is devoid of connection with <s>Indra</s>. [Objection:] It is only the re-elevated [<s>Soma</s>] that serves another's purpose, not the prior — if so argued, no. Because at the time of re-elevation, there is no intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) that 'this is for the purpose of <s>Mitrāvaruṇa</s> and others.' But at the time of offering, [the Soma] is given to <s>Mitrāvaruṇa</s> and others together with the prior remainder.
(In the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the non-indication of <s>Indra</s> and others in the drinking of the <s>Pātnīvata</s> [cup], <s>sūtras</s> 32–33)
In the <s>Pātnīvata</s> [cup], as before. / Jaim_3,2.32 /
Or, since [the Soma] is drawn, the removed [Soma] would be [separate]. / Jaim_3,2.33 /
START MJaiNy 3,2.31-33
He composes the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The remainder of the two-deity [offerings] reaches the <s>Āditya</s>-vessel, [and then] the vessel called <s>Āgrayaṇa</s>;

children.text: sthālīṃ prāptastataḥ pātnīvatasya grahaṇe sati // MJaiNy_3,2.31 //
children.translated_text: from that vessel, when the <s>Pātnīvata</s> [cup] is drawn — // MJaiNy_3,2.31 //

children.text: tadbhakṣaṇe dvidevāḥ kiṃ sārdhe pātnīvatena te /
children.translated_text: In the drinking of that [cup], should the two-deity [gods] along with the <s>Pātnīvata</s> deity
be indicated, or not? By the previous principle, let there be indication. // MJaiNy_3,2.32 //
The <s>Pātnīvata</s> [cup], being different from the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s>, has no
expectation (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) toward the prior deities; only the lord of wives (<s>patnīvān</s>) is indicated. // MJaiNy_3,2.33 //

children.text:
aindravāyavādayo dvidevatyāḥ |
teṣāṃ śeṣa ādityasthālīmāgacchati, punarapi tasyāḥ sthālyā āgrayaṇasthālīmāgacchati |
tasyā āgrayaṇasthālyāḥ pātnīvato gṛhyate |
tasya pātnīvatasya bhakṣaṇa indravāyvādaya upalakṣaṇīyāḥ |
pūrvādhikaraṇe yathā mitrāvaruṇādibhiḥ sahendra upalakṣitaḥ, tadvat - iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- 'yadupāṃśu pātreṇa pātnīvatamāgrayaṇādgṛhṇāti' ityāgrayaṇapātrasyāpādānatvaśravaṇāttato niḥsṛtasomarasasya tatsaṃbandhe 'pete sati paścātpatnīvaddevatāyai grahaṇaṃ bhavati |

children.translated_text: This being so, the <s>Pātnīvata</s> [cup], being entirely distinct, has no expectation toward the prior deities.
But the re-elevated <s>Soma</s> is mixed with the <s>Aindra</s> (belonging to <s>Indra</s>) remainder.

children.text: tasya saṃsṛṣṭasya bhakṣaṇe maitrāvaruṇādīnāmivendrasyāpi saṃbandho nāpaitīti vaiṣamyam |
children.translated_text: In the drinking of that mixed [<s>Soma</s>], the connection of <s>Indra</s>, just like that of <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> and others, does not cease — thus there is a difference [between the two cases].
Therefore, in the drinking of the <s>Pātnīvata</s> [cup], <s>Indravāyu</s> and others are not to be indicated. || MJaiNyC_3,2.31-33 ||

The <s>Aindravāyava</s> and others have two deities. Their remainder reaches the <s>Āditya</s> vessel, and again from that vessel reaches the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> vessel. From that <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> vessel, the <s>Pātnīvata</s> [cup] is drawn. In the drinking of that <s>Pātnīvata</s>, <s>Indravāyu</s> and others should be indicated — just as in the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, <s>Indra</s> was indicated along with <s>Mitrāvaruṇa</s> and others — having arrived at this position, we say: From the Vedic statement '<s>yadupāṃśu pātreṇa pātnīvatamāgrayaṇādgṛhṇāti</s>' (he draws the <s>Pātnīvata</s> from the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> with the <s>Upāṃśu</s> vessel), since the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> vessel is heard as the source (<s>apādāna</s>), when the connection with the <s>Soma</s> juice that has issued from it has ceased, the drawing is subsequently for the deity <s>Patnīvat</s>.
(In the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the non-indication of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> in the drinking of the <s>Pātnīvata</s> remainder, <s>sūtras</s> 34–35)
One should indicate <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>. / Jaim_3,2.34 /
But because of inequality, it should not be so. / Jaim_3,2.35 /
START MJaiNy 3,2.34-35
He composes the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: saha patnīvatā tvaṣṭā tadgrahe lakṣyate na vā /
children.translated_text: Is <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> indicated along with the <s>Patnīvat</s> in the drawing of that [cup], or not?
Since it is said '<s>saha tvaṣṭrā pibet</s>' (let him drink with <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>), due to deity-status, he too is indicated. // MJaiNy_3,2.34 //
For <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, there would be mere co-presence (<s>sahatva</s>), not drinker-status (<s>pātṛtva</s>), because of the absence of [supporting] word;

children.text: codanāyā abhāvācca na devo 'to na lakṣyate // MJaiNy_3,2.35 //
children.translated_text: and because of the absence of an injunction (<s>codanā</s>), he is not a deity — therefore he is not to be indicated. // MJaiNy_3,2.35 //

children.text:
tasminneva pātnīvatagrahe śeṣabhakṣaṇamantre patnīvatā saha tvaṣṭāpyupalakṣaṇīyaḥ |
kutaḥ |
tvaṣṭurapi taddevatvāt |
tacca homamantrādavagatam |
'agnī 3 i patnībantsajūrdevena tvaṣṭrā somaṃ piba svāhā' ityasminmantre patnīvantamagniṃ plutāntena saṃbodhya'tvaṣṭrā devena saha piba' ityabhidhānātpātṛtvena patnīvata iva tvaṣṭustaddevatvam |
tataḥ- 'patnīvattvaṣṭṛpītasya' ityupalakṣaṇam-iti prāpte -
brūmaḥ- pānakāle sahāvasthānamātraṃ tvaṣṭuḥ 'sajūḥ' ityanena padena pratīyate, na tu pātṛtvam |
asaṃbodhitasya tvaṣṭuḥ 'piba' ityanena śabdena sāmānādhikaraṇyābhāvāt |
na ca pātṛsahabhāvamātreṇa pātṛtvam -
"sahaiva daśabhiḥ putrairbhāraṃ vahati gardagrī" |
ityatra putrāṇāṃ voḍhṛtvādarśanāt |
āstāṃ mantraḥ |

children.translated_text: [Objection:] <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> has deity-status by the force of the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) — if so argued,
no.
Because in '<s>pātnīvatamāgrayaṇādgṛhṇāti</s>' (he draws the <s>Pātnīvata</s> from the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s>), <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> is not apprehended.
Therefore — since [he has] no deity-status, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> is not to be indicated. || MJaiNyC_3,2.34-35 ||

In that very drawing of the <s>Pātnīvata</s> [cup], in the drinking-remainder <s>mantra</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> too should be indicated along with the <s>Patnīvat</s>. Why? Because <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> also has deity-status therein. And that is understood from the oblation <s>mantra</s>. In the <s>mantra</s> '<s>agnī3i patnīvantsa jūrdevena tvaṣṭrā somaṃ piba svāhā</s>' (O <s>Agni</s> lord of wives, with the protracted call, drink <s>Soma</s> with the god <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>), having addressed <s>Agni</s> bearing the epithet <s>Patnīvat</s> with the protracted vowel, the statement 'drink with the god <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>' establishes deity-status for <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> as a drinker, just like <s>Patnīvat</s>. Therefore — the indication should be '<s>patnīvattvaṣṭṛpītasya</s>' (drunk by <s>Patnīvat</s> and <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>) — having arrived at this position, we say: By the word '<s>sajūḥ</s>' (together), only the mere co-presence of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> at the time of drinking is understood, not drinker-status. Because there is no co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) between the unaddressed <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> and the word '<s>piba</s>' (drink). And mere co-presence with a drinker does not [confer] drinker-status — 'A she-donkey carries a load together with her ten foals' — here, carrier-status of the foals is not seen. Let the <s>mantra</s> be set aside.
(In the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the non-indication of the thirty [-three gods] in the drinking of the <s>Pātnīvata</s> remainder, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
And the thirty [-three], because of serving another's purpose. / Jaim_3,2.36 /
START MJaiNy 3,2.36-37
He composes the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The thirty-three gods bearing the epithet <s>Patnīvat</s> — [the mantra says] 'delight them!' —
Are they to be indicated, or not? Due to the deity-status from the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse), [they should be] indicated. // MJaiNy_3,2.36 //
Only <s>Agni</s> is delighted by the sacrificer; the others are [delighted] by the fire;
therefore, since only <s>Agni</s> has deity-status, the others are not to be indicated. // MJaiNy_3,2.37 //

children.text:
tasyaiva pātnīvatagrahasya yājyāyāmagniṃ saṃbodhya 'patnīvannāmadhāriṇastrayastriṃśaddevānmādaya' ityabhidhīyate - 'patnīvatastriṃśataṃ trīṃśca devānanuṣvadhamāvaha mādayasva' iti |
anuṣvadhamanupradānam |
atra hūyamānena somarasena mādanīyatvātrayastriṃśatāṃ taddevatvam |
attaste 'pi bhakṣaṇe lakṣaṇīyāḥ- iti cet |

children.translated_text: no.
Because only <s>Agni</s>, who is to be delighted by the sacrificer, has deity-status therein.

children.text: trayastriṃśaddevāstu vahninā mādyanta iti na teṣāmatra devatvam |
children.translated_text: The thirty-three gods are delighted by the fire [<s>Agni</s>], so they do not have deity-status here.
Therefore, they are not to be indicated. || MJaiNyC_3,2.36-37 ||

In the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse) of that very <s>Pātnīvata</s> cup-drawing, addressing <s>Agni</s>, it is stated: 'delight the thirty-three gods bearing the name <s>Patnīvat</s>' — '<s>patnīvatastriṃśataṃ trīṃśca devānanuṣvadhamāvaha mādayasva</s>' (O <s>Patnīvat</s>, bring the thirty and three gods with offerings, and be delighted). <s>Anuṣvadham</s> means offering. Here, since they are to be delighted by the <s>Soma</s> juice being offered, the thirty-three [gods] have deity-status. They too should be indicated in the drinking — if so argued,
(In the sixteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the non-indication of the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> deity in the drinking, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
And the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> [deity], as before. / Jaim_3,2.37 /
START MJaiNy 3,2.38-39
He composes the sixteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The deity of the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> mentioned in '<s>somasyāgne</s>' (O <s>Agni</s>, of <s>Soma</s>) —

children.text: lakṣyā na vā devatātvāllakṣyā triṃśadvilakṣaṇā // MJaiNy_3,2.38 //
children.translated_text: is [he] to be indicated, or not? Due to deity-status, he should be indicated — [but he is] different from the thirty [-three]. // MJaiNy_3,2.38 //
<s>Agni</s>, who is present in the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>), is indicated by the [mark of] non-dedication;
<s>Indra</s>, the intended [deity], is indicated — therefore, in the modified rite (<s>vikṛti</s>) too, it is likewise. // MJaiNy_3,2.39 //

children.text:
"somasyāgne vīhī |
tyanuyajati"iti śrūyate |
tatra-anuvaṣaṭkārasya māntravarṇiko 'gnirdevatā |
na ca trayastriṃśatāmiva vahneradevatātvam |
mantre vahniṃ saṃbodhya somapātṛtvāmidhānāt |
tasmāt-agnirlakṣaṇīyaḥ- iti cet |
na |
prakṛtāvalakṣitatvāt |
aindraśvamasaḥ prakṛtiḥ |
itare vikṛtirūpāḥ |
tathā hi-aindraśca somo gṛhyate mīyate ca |
tenaindroṣveva somaḥ, anaindreṣu soma eva nāstīti sarve somadharmā aindreṣveva |
anaindrā adharmakāḥ |
dharmatākāṅkṣāścodakena sadharmakā iti vikṛtitvam |
gṛhyamāṇasya mīyamānasya ca somasyaindratvam 'indrāya tvā vasumate' ityādigrahaṇamantrādavagamyate |
tasya prakṛtibhūtasyendracamasasya bhakṣaṇe 'gniranuvaṣaṭkāradevo nopalakṣitaḥ |
kutaḥ |

children.translated_text: Because of the absence of dedication to him at the time of drawing.
But <s>Indra</s>, being the intended [deity], is indicated.
Similarly, in the modified rite too, indication of only the intended deities is proper.
Therefore — <s>Agni</s> is not to be indicated. || MJaiNyC_3,2.38-39 ||

It is heard: '<s>somasyāgne vīhi tyanuyajati</s>' (he makes the secondary offering [saying] 'O <s>Agni</s>, of <s>Soma</s>, convey'). Therein, <s>Agni</s>, known from the Vedic word in the <s>mantra</s>, is the deity of the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s>. And his deity-status is not [negated] like that of the thirty-three — [for those], the fire [merely] delights them. In the <s>mantra</s>, having addressed the fire, the statement of <s>Soma</s>-drinking [is made]. Therefore — <s>Agni</s> should be indicated — if so argued, no. Because he is not indicated in the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>). The <s>Aindra</s> cup is the archetype. The others are modified forms (<s>vikṛti</s>). Thus — the <s>Aindra</s> <s>Soma</s> is drawn and measured. Therefore, the <s>Soma</s> exists only in the <s>Aindra</s> [cups]; in the non-<s>Aindra</s> [cups], there is no <s>Soma</s> at all — so all the properties of <s>Soma</s> [belong] to the <s>Aindra</s> [cups] alone. The non-<s>Aindra</s> [cups] lack these properties. Their expectation of properties and the injunction establishing them as having the same properties — this is the basis of [their] modified status. The <s>Aindra</s> character of the <s>Soma</s> being drawn and measured is understood from the drawing <s>mantra</s> '<s>indrāya tvā vasumate</s>' (to <s>Indra</s> the wealthy, you [I draw]). In the drinking of that archetypical <s>Indra</s> cup, <s>Agni</s>, the deity of the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s>, is not indicated. Why?
(In the seventeenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, of the form of investigation (<s>kṛtvācintā</s>), on the drinking without <s>mantra</s> for the non-<s>Aindra</s> [cups], the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
But the prohibition of the meter [applies] because of its universal applicability. / Jaim_3,2.38 /
START MJaiNy 3,2.40-41
He composes the seventeenth adhikaraṇa —
Having adopted the position that [the rites are] without mantra, and having set aside three alternative considerations (kṛtvācintā),

children.text: ūho 'sti no vā so 'styatra vikṛtau tasya saṃbhavāt // MJaiNy_3,2.40 //
children.translated_text: whether substitution (ūha) exists or not — it does exist here in the modified rite (vikṛti), because of its possibility. // MJaiNy_3,2.40 //
Because of the equal status of the injunction 'somena' (with Soma) in all cup-drawings (pradāna),
even in the absence of modification, there is no substitution; therefore the non-Aindra [cup-drinking] is without mantra. // MJaiNy_3,2.41 //

children.text:
uktābhyaḥ pañcamyaḥ kṛtvācintābhyaḥ pūrvasminnevādhikaraṇe yo 'yam 'anaindreṣvamantrakaṃ bhakṣaṇam' ityevaṃrūpaḥ prathamaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ, tameva manasi nidhāya punaḥ kṛtvācintānāṃ trayamabhidhīyate - anaindrapūktarītyā vikṛtitvenohasaṃbhavādaratyūhaḥ- iti cet |
na |
anaindraṇāṃ vikṛtitvāsaṃbhavāt |
'somena yajeta' ityutpattiśrutaḥ somaḥ karmaṇo 'ṅgam, na tu pradānaviśeṣasya kasyacidaṅgam |
sa eva somaḥ sarvapradāneṣvabhyasyata iti sarvāṇi samapradhānāni |

children.translated_text: Therefore, since the archetype-modification relationship (prakṛti-vikṛti-bhāva) does not hold between the Aindra and the non-Aindra [cups], there is no substitution here.
Let the mantra beginning with 'indrāya tvā vasumate' (unto Indra, the wealthy one, [I consecrate] you) be directed toward the Aindra [cup] by virtue of its indicatory mark (liṅga).
By this alone, the archetype-modification relationship is not established.
Therefore, since the stated mantra pertains to the Aindra [cup] by virtue of its mark, the drinking in the non-Aindra [cups] is without mantra. || MJaiNyC_3,2.40-41 ||

From the five [objections] stated previously, having set aside the post-factum considerations (kṛtvācintā) in the very same adhikaraṇa, the first pūrvapakṣa (prima facie view) of this form — 'in the non-Aindra [cups], the drinking is without mantra' — keeping that very [view] in mind, three post-factum considerations are now stated: In the non-Aindra [cups], since they have the nature of modified rites (vikṛti), substitution is possible, and therefore substitution [should be applied] — if so argued, no. Because the non-Aindra [cups] do not have the nature of being modified rites. The Soma, heard in the originating injunction 'somena yajeta' (one should sacrifice with Soma), is an accessory (aṅga) of the rite, and not an accessory of any particular cup-drawing.
