That very Soma is repeated in all cup-drawings, so all [cup-drawings] have equal principal status.
(In the eighteenth [adhikaraṇa], on the mantra-less nature of the Aindrāgna [cup-]drinking, sūtras 39–40)
But in the Aindrāgna [cup], it would [apply] because of the presence of the mark (liṅga). / Jaim_3,2.39 /
Or [there would be assignment] to one only, as [there would be] division from another deity. / Jaim_3,2.40 /
START MJaiNy 3,2.42-43
He composes the eighteenth adhikaraṇa —
Should the drinking of the Aindrāgna and the like be with mantra or without mantra?
In the Aindrāgna [cup], because of the possibility that it was drunk by Indra, [the drinking is] with mantra. // MJaiNy_3,2.42 //

children.text: na pānamaśarīrasya yuktaṃ dānaṃ tu miśragam /
children.translated_text: Drinking by one who has no body is not possible; but the offering is mixed [between two deities];
this mantra, however, is not fit for a mixed [deity]; therefore, this [drinking] is without mantra. // MJaiNy_3,2.43 //

children.text:
yadetat 'aindrāgnaṃ gṛhṇāti' iti vihitaṃ śeṣabhakṣaṇam, tatra- indrāgnibhyāṃ pītaḥ soma indreṇāpi pīto bhavati' iti leṅgenaiva viniyogātsamantrakaṃ bhakṣaṇam - iti cet |
maivam |
navamādhyāye vakṣyamāṇadevatādhikaraṇanyāyenāśarīrasyendrasya pānāsaṃbhavāt |
atha- patiśabdena dānaṃ vivakṣyeta, tadānīm 'indrāya dattaḥ somaḥ' iti mantrārtho bhavati |
children.translated_text: Now — if by the word 'pati' (lord), offering (dāna) is intended, then the meaning of the mantra would be 'Soma given to Indra.'

children.text: na cātra yajamāna indramuddiśya dadau, kiṃtvindrāgnī uddīśya |
children.translated_text: But here the sacrificer did not give [the Soma] designating Indra [alone]; rather, he gave it designating Indra and Agni [together].
Therefore, 'the offering pertains to the mixed [deity].

children.text: mantrastu na miśraviṣayaḥ' ityamantrakaṃ bhakṣaṇam || MJaiNyC_3,2.42-43 ||
children.translated_text: But the mantra does not pertain to the mixed [deity]' — therefore the drinking is without mantra. || MJaiNyC_3,2.42-43 ||

Regarding the residual drinking (śeṣa-bhakṣaṇa) enjoined as 'aindrāgnaṃ gṛhṇāti' (he grasps the Aindrāgna [cup]) — since the Soma drunk by Indra and Agni is also drunk by Indra [alone], the drinking would be with mantra due to assignment by the mark alone — if so argued, that is not correct. By the principle to be stated in the ninth chapter regarding the deity adhikaraṇa, drinking by Indra who has no body is impossible.
(In the nineteenth [adhikaraṇa], on the assignment of mantras [beginning with] 'gāyatracchandasaḥ' and the like, sūtras 41–43) /
And the meter [is assigned] like the deity. / Jaim_3,2.41 /
Or [it applies] to all, because of the absence of a single-metered [Soma]. / Jaim_3,2.42 /

children.text: sarveṣāṃ vaikamantryam aitiśāyanasya bhaktipāvanatvāt savanādhikāro hi / Jaim_3,2.43 /
children.translated_text: Or the single-mantra status of all [is established], because of Aitiśāyana's [view that] the qualification pertains to purification, for the entitlement belongs to the pressing (savana). / Jaim_3,2.43 /
START MJaiNy 3,2.44-46
He composes the nineteenth adhikaraṇa —
In the Aindra cup-drawing, should the mantra be accompanied by the Gāyatrī meter alone, or also by the others —

children.text: chandobhirapi yukte syādādyo mantre tathoktitaḥ // MJaiNy_3,2.44 //
children.translated_text: other meters? And should the first [meter be assigned] in the mantra, as it is stated? // MJaiNy_3,2.44 //
For both [interpretations], the bahuvrīhi [compound] is the same; but a single-metered [Soma] does not exist anywhere;
in the many-metered Aindra [cup] alone, this post-factum consideration (kṛtvācintā) is stated. // MJaiNy_3,2.45 //
The statement that [Soma] was drunk by Indra is for the purpose of the pressing (savana);

children.text: tena sarvapradāneṣu mantrapāṭho yathā sthitaḥ // MJaiNy_3,2.46 //
children.translated_text: therefore, in all cup-drawings, the recitation of the mantra remains as it stands. // MJaiNy_3,2.46 //

children.text:
tasminneva bhakṣamantre 'gāyatracchandasa indrapītasya' iti śrūyate |
'gāyatrameva chando yasya' iti mantrapade samāsābhidhānādekacchandoyukta aindre some bhakṣamantraḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
bahucchandoyukte 'pi bahuvrīheḥ samānatvāt |
evakāraṃ parityajya 'gāyatraṃ chando yasya' iti vigrahasaṃbhavāt |

children.translated_text: But a single-metered Soma does not exist anywhere.

children.text: tasmānnānāchandaske soma aindrapradāna eva mantraḥ, nānyatra |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the mantra [applies] to the Soma that is many-metered, specifically in the Aindra cup-drawing alone, and not elsewhere.
Thus the triad of post-factum considerations (kṛtvācintā) is concluded.

children.text: dvividhakṛtvācintodghāṭanā tu prāgeva siddhāntinā darśitā || MJaiNyC_3,2.44-46 ||
children.translated_text: The resolution (udghāṭanā) of the twofold post-factum consideration, however, was already shown by the siddhāntin (the proponent of the established view) previously. || MJaiNyC_3,2.44-46 ||

In that very drinking mantra, it is heard: 'gāyatracchandasa indrapītasya' (of [the Soma] drunk by Indra, having the Gāyatrī meter). Since the compound states 'gāyatram eva chandaḥ yasya' (that whose meter is Gāyatrī alone), the drinking mantra [applies to] the Aindra Soma which has a single meter — if so argued, that is not correct. Because the bahuvrīhi [compound] would be the same even for one accompanied by many meters. Setting aside the restrictive particle 'eva' (alone), the analysis 'gāyatraṃ chandaḥ yasya' (that whose meter is Gāyatrī) is possible.

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīye jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistare tṛtīyādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second pāda of the third adhyāya in the illustrious Mādhavīya Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara.
Now the third pāda of the third adhyāya. /
(In the first [adhikaraṇa], on the Veda-nature of loudness (uccaistva) and the like, sūtras 1–8) /
From the scripture (śruti), the entitlement would arise for [each] particular [mantra]. / Jaim_3,3.1 /
Or [it belongs to] the Veda, because of the observation of the general [principle]. / Jaim_3,3.2 /
And because of the mark (liṅga). / Jaim_3,3.3 /

children.text: dharmopadeśāc ca na hi dravyeṇa saṃbandhaḥ / Jaim_3,3.4 /
children.translated_text: And because of the teaching of dharma — for there is no connection with a material substance. / Jaim_3,3.4 /
And the designation 'Trayīvidyā' (threefold knowledge) [confirms this], for one who knows that [knows the Veda]. / Jaim_3,3.5 /
If [it be argued that] in the case of deviation of [individual] instances, [one should proceed] according to what is heard — / Jaim_3,3.6 /
[That is] not [so], because of [its] establishment in all [cases]. / Jaim_3,3.7 /
Because of the connection with the Veda, [it] is not overridden by the context. / Jaim_3,3.8 /
START MJaiNy 3,3.1-3
He composes the first adhikaraṇa of the third pāda —
Loudness (uccaistva) is to be performed [with Ṛk and Sāman], since they are born of Sāman; low voice (upāṃśu) [is to be performed] with Yajus — these

children.text: mantrāṇāṃ vātha vedānāṃ dharmā mantragatā yataḥ // MJaiNy_3,3.1 //
children.translated_text: are properties of the [individual] mantras, or of the Vedas [as a whole] — since they inhere in the mantras. // MJaiNy_3,3.1 //
In the statement of the injunction, the words Ṛk and the like denote the mantras;
'The Ṛgveda arose from Agni' — this opening passage speaks of the Vedas. // MJaiNy_3,3.2 //
Because no contradiction has arisen [between them], and because [the injunction] can be brought into harmony with that [opening passage],

children.text: nayane sati vākyena dharmāṇāṃ vedagāmitā // MJaiNy_3,3.3 //
children.translated_text: when the leading [of the injunctive words] by the sentence [makes them refer to the Vedas], the properties [such as loudness] pertain to the Vedas. // MJaiNy_3,3.3 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate- 'uccaiṛcā kriyate |
upāṃśu yajuṣā |
uccaiḥ sāmnā' iti |
tatra vidhivākye mantravācināmṛgādiśabdānāṃ prayogānmantradharmā uccaistvādayaḥ |
tathā sati yajurvedotpannā adhvaryuṇā prayujyamānā apyṛca uccaireva paṭhitavyāḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
asaṃjātavirodhitvena prabalamupakramamanusṛtya tadvaśenopasaṃhārasya naitavyatvāt |
upakrame hi vedaśabdaḥ śrutaḥ- 'trayo vedā asṛjyanta |
agneṛgvedaḥ |
vāyoryajurvedaḥ |
ādityātsāmavedaḥ' iti |
ata upakramagatavedānusāreṇa vidhyuddeśagatānāmapyṛgādiśabdānāṃ vedaparatve satyṛco 'pi yajurvedotpannā upāṃśu paṭhanīyāḥ |
nanu- upakramo 'trārthavādatvāddurbalaḥ |
upasaṃhāro vidhyuddeśatvātprabalaḥ- iti cet |
bāḍham |
labdhātmano hi vidhyuddeśasya prābalyam |

children.translated_text: But here, the opening passage is the first to generate understanding.
At that time, since [the injunctive statement] has not yet established its meaning, [the opening passage] does not override it.
Subsequently, for the unity of the sentence, [the injunctive statement] will acquire its meaning only in conformity with that [opening passage].
Thus, from the force of the sentence-unity of the opening passage and the concluding statement, the determination is: this is an assignment by sentence. || MJaiNyC_3,1.1-3 ||

In the Jyotiṣṭoma, it is heard: 'uccai ṛcā kriyate (the Ṛk is performed aloud), upāṃśu yajuṣā (in a low voice with Yajus), uccaiḥ sāmnā (aloud with Sāman).' Therein, since the words Ṛk and the like in the injunctive sentence denote the [individual] mantras, loudness and the like are properties of the mantras. This being so, even Ṛk verses that originated in the Yajurveda and are employed by the Adhvaryu should be recited aloud — if so argued, that is not correct. Because the opening passage, being free from [any] arisen contradiction, is more authoritative, and the conclusion (upasaṃhāra) is to be led in conformity with it. For in the opening passage, the word 'Veda' is heard: 'trayo vedā asṛjyanta (the three Vedas were created), agner ṛgvedaḥ (the Ṛgveda from Agni), vāyor yajurvedaḥ (the Yajurveda from Vāyu), ādityāt sāmavedaḥ (the Sāmaveda from Āditya).' Therefore, following the Veda-reference in the opening passage, even the words Ṛk and the like in the injunctive statement should be taken as referring to the Vedas, so that even Ṛk verses originating in the Yajurveda should be recited in a low voice. Now — if it be objected: the opening passage is weak because it is an arthavāda (laudatory passage), while the concluding injunction is strong because it is part of the injunctive statement — that is true. For the injunctive statement has strength [only] when it has [already] established its meaning.
(In the second [adhikaraṇa], on the low-voiced nature of singing in the Ādhāna [rite], the sūtra is:) /

When there is a conflict between the subsidiary (guṇa) and the principal (mukhya), because [the subsidiary] serves the purpose of that [principal], [the subsidiary] is connected with the Veda through the principal. / Jaim_3,3.9 /
START MJaiNy 3,3.4-6
He composes the second adhikaraṇa —
The Ādhāna (fire-establishment) belongs to the Yajurveda; a Sāman is its accessory — therein, should
the singing be aloud or in a low voice? Aloud, because of the immediate apprehension [of the Sāmaveda connection]. // MJaiNy_3,3.4 //
The assignment by origination is [apparently] strong, as it follows [the Veda of origin];
but the subsidiary should conform to the principal; therefore, the singing is in a low voice. // MJaiNy_3,3.5 //
Here, the Ādhāna has principal status, or the singing has subsidiary status;
alternatively, the assignment has principal status, while the origination has subsidiary status. // MJaiNy_3,3.6 //

children.text:
ādhāne vāmadevyādisāmānyaṅgatvena vihitāni |
tatra- yadyapyetāni yajurvedagatasyā'dhānasyāṅgāni, tathāpi sāmavede teṣāmutpannatvāt, utpatteśca śīghrabuddhihetutvātsāmavedadharmeṇa geyāni - iti cet |
na |
viniyogasya prabalatvāt |
sa ca yajurvede śrutaḥ- 'ya evaṃ vidvānvāmadevyaṃ gāyati' iti |
guṇena hi mukhyasyānusaraṇaṃ nyāyyam |
ko guṇaḥ, kiṃ mukhyam- iti cet |
atrāṅgitvādādhānaṃ mukhyam, sāmagānamaṅgatvena guṇaḥ |
tathā sāti 'dharmaḥ śiraḥ' - ityādaya ādhānāṅgabhūtā mantrā yathopāṃśu paṭhyante, tathā sāmānyapyādhānānusāreṇopāṃśu geyāni |
children.translated_text: This being so, just as the mantras that are accessories of the Ādhāna, such as 'dharmaḥ śiraḥ' and the like, are recited in a low voice, similarly the Sāmans too should be sung in a low voice, following the Ādhāna.
Alternatively, the assignment is the principal, because it is the injunction that impels performance (anuṣṭhāpaka-vidhi).
The originating injunction is the subsidiary, because it is not of that [directly impelling] nature.
Therefore — here, following the Veda of assignment, they should be sung in a low voice. || MJaiNyC_3,1.4-6 ||

In the Ādhāna (fire-establishment), Sāmans such as the Vāmadevya are enjoined as accessories. Therein — even though these are accessories of the Ādhāna belonging to the Yajurveda, since they originated in the Sāmaveda, and since origination quickly brings understanding, they should be sung according to the Sāmaveda convention — if so argued, no. Because the assignment is more authoritative. And that [assignment] is heard in the Yajurveda: 'ya evaṃ vidvān vāmadevyaṃ gāyati' (he who, knowing thus, sings the Vāmadevya). For it is proper that the subsidiary follow the principal. What is the subsidiary and what is the principal? — if asked: Here, the Ādhāna is the principal because it is the aṅgin (possessor of accessories), and the Sāman-singing is the subsidiary because it is an accessory (aṅga).
(In the third [adhikaraṇa], on the Yājurvedika nature of the Jyotiṣṭoma, the sūtra is:) /
Because of the preponderance [of Yajus], and because both [Vedas] contain the scriptural statement. / Jaim_3,3.10 /
START MJaiNy 3,3.7-8
He composes the third adhikaraṇa —
The Jyotiṣṭoma exists in both the Yajurveda and the Sāmaveda — therein, should
loudness or low voice [prevail]? Due to the absence of a [decisive] reason, there is no determination. // MJaiNy_3,3.7 //
Since the substance (dravya) and the deity are comprehended in the Yajurveda, the injunction belongs there;
by virtue of that, since the pitch (svara) is determined [by the Yajurveda], the performance should be in a low voice. // MJaiNy_3,3.8 //
The sentence 'jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajeta' (one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma) is recited in both Vedas.

children.text: tatra-'ko vidhiḥ, kaśca guṇavidhānāyānuvādaḥ, iti jijñāsāyāṃ niyāmakahetorapratimānāt 'etasya vedasya dharmo 'nuṣṭheyaḥ' ityanirṇayaḥ- iti cet |
children.translated_text: Therein — when the inquiry arises 'which is the injunction and which is the restatement (anuvāda) for the purpose of subsidiary prescriptions' — since there is no discriminating factor, the non-determination that 'the dharma of this [particular] Veda should be followed' — if so argued,
no.

children.text: somadravyasya, indravāyvādidevatāyāśca yajurvede 'dhigatatvādaṅgabāhulyaśravaṇācca tatraiva vidhiḥ, iti - upāṃśuprayogaḥ || MJaiNyC_3,1.7-8 ||
children.translated_text: Since the substance (dravya) Soma and the deities Indra, Vāyu and the like are comprehended in the Yajurveda, and because of the preponderance of accessory scriptural passages therein, the injunction belongs there — hence the performance is in a low voice. || MJaiNyC_3,1.7-8 ||
(In the fourth [adhikaraṇa], on the capacity of the context (prakaraṇa) to assign [ritual elements], the sūtra is:)
That which is unconnected [is assigned] by the context, because [it] seeks [to know] the manner of performance. / Jaim_3,3.11 /
START MJaiNy 3,3.9-10
He composes the fourth adhikaraṇa —

children.text: na kratvaṅgaṃ prayājādi kratvaṅgaṃ vā na cāṅgatā /
children.translated_text: The preliminary offerings (prayāja) and the like are not accessories of the sacrifice; or they are accessories — but then [the sacrifice] would not have the status of accessory
of the [preparatory] procedure, since it is without measure (pramāṇa), or because of the self-sufficiency of the sentences. // MJaiNy_3,3.9 //
The preliminary offerings (prayāja) and the like have an expectation regarding the result [of the sacrifice]; and even as to the manner [of performance], [they depend] on the sacrifice;
therefore the contextual recitation [assigns them]; hence they have the mutual relationship of accessory and principal. // MJaiNy_3,3.10 //

children.text:
sārdhapādadvaye viniyojakatvenoktāni yāni śrutiliṅgavākyāni, tebhyo 'tiriktaṃ prakaraṇanāmakaṃ kiṃcitpramāṇaṃ na vede paśyāmaḥ |
nahi padatatsāmarthyānvayairasaṃtṛṣṭaḥ kaścidvedabhāgaḥ kenacidāmnāyate |
ekavākyatāmāpanno vākyasamūhaḥ prakaraṇama-iti cet |
na |
vākyayoḥ satoḥ paścādekatākyatāyā abhāvāt |
na hi 'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta' 'samidho yajati' ityanayorvākyayoḥ parasparākāṅkṣāsti, yena vākyaikavākyatā kalpyeta |
tasmāt - na prayājādīnāṃ darśapūrṇamāsāṅgatvam- iti prāpte, -

children.translated_text: we say: The preliminary offerings (prayāja) and the like are causes of the result, because they are in the form of human activity, like service and the like.
The Darśapūrṇamāsa rites are to be assisted by the implements (upakaraṇa), because they are instrumental, like a lamp assisting the eye.

children.text: tathā sati 'kiṃ prayājādeḥ phalam, kiṃvā darśapūrṇamāsayorupakaraṇam' ityākāṅkṣāyāṃ saṃpannavākyaikavākyatārūpaṃ prakaraṇam |
children.translated_text: This being so, when the expectation arises — 'What is the fruit of the <s>prayāja</s> (preliminary offering) and the like, or are they subsidiary to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices)?' — the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), which has the form of syntactic unity with the completed sentence, [resolves this].
And through that [context], the subsidiary nature (<s>aṅgatva</s>) of the <s>prayāja</s>s and the like is understood. || MJaiNyC_3,1.9-10 ||

In the half-pāda and a half dealing with assignment, the sentences of scripture, mark, and sentence were stated. We do not find in the Veda any means of valid knowledge called 'context' (prakaraṇa) beyond those. For no part of the Veda, remaining unsatisfied by word, capacity, and syntactic connection, is recited together with any [other part]. A collection of sentences that has attained sentence-unity is a 'context' — if so argued, no. Because when two sentences exist, there is no sentence-unity afterward. For between the two sentences 'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta' (one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the Darśapūrṇamāsa) and 'samidho yajati' (he sacrifices with the kindling sticks), there is no mutual expectation, on the basis of which sentence-unity could be constructed. Therefore — the preliminary offerings and the like are not accessories of the Darśapūrṇamāsa — having arrived at this position,
(In the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the capacity of sequence (<s>krama</s>) to assign [ritual elements], the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
And sequence [is an assigning factor], because of the commonality of place. / Jaim_3,3.12 /
START MJaiNy 3,3.11-14
He composes the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The <s>mantra</s> called '<s>dabdhiḥ</s>' — is it a subsidiary of the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> (quiet offering) or not?
Because of [the mark's] generality, [and] due to the absence of a valid means of knowledge, there is non-subsidiarity (<s>anaṅgatā</s>). // MJaiNy_3,3.11 //
Here, the sequential recitation (<s>āmnāna</s>) of <s>mantras</s> and ritual acts is observed in order;
sequence, as in the original procedure (<s>prakriyā</s>), is a valid means of knowledge; hence from enumeration (<s>yathāsaṃkhya</s>), subsidiarity is [established]. // MJaiNy_3,3.12 //
Sequence is the co-location (<s>samānadeśatva</s>) — [derived] from textual position and from meaning; from textual position,
there is enumeration (<s>yathāsaṃkhya</s>) and proximity (<s>saṃnidhi</s>); enumeration is illustrated [as follows]. // MJaiNy_3,3.13 //
'<s>Śundhadhvam</s>' (be purified) — this is a subsidiary of the <s>sāṃnāyya</s> (mixed-milk offering) vessel, according to the view based on proximity;
the animal-rite rules, by similarity of purpose, would pertain to the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [sacrifice]. // MJaiNy_3,3.14 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoryājamāne - mantrakāṇḍe kaścinmantra āmnāyate-'dabdhirasyadabdho bhūyāsam, amuṃ dabheyam' iti |
asya mantrasyopāṃśuyājāṅgatāyāṃ śrutivākye na vidyete |
brāhmaṇe viniyogamanāmnāyārthavivaraṇasyaivā'bhnānāt |
'etayā vai dabdhyā devā asurānadabhnuvan |
tayaiva bhrātṛvyaṃ dabhnoti' iti brāhmaṇam |
dabdhirdhātukamāyudham |
āgneyāgnīṣomīyayorapyaniṣṭanivārakatvālliṅgaṃ sādhāraṇam |
prakaraṇaṃ ca trayāṇāmekameva |
tato mānābhāvādayaṃ mantro nopāṃśuyājāṅgam - iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- ādhvaryave kāṇḍa āgneyopāṃśuyājāgnīṣomīyakarmāṇi krameṇā'mnātāni |
yājamāne ca kāṇḍe tadviṣayā mantrāḥ krameṇā'mnātāḥ- 'agnerahaṃ devayajyayānnādo bhūyāsam', 'dabdhirasyadabdho bhūyāsamamuṃ dabheyam','agniṣomayārehaṃ devayajyayā vṛtrahā bhūyāsam' iti |
tatra yathā vākyadvayānusaṃdhāna saṃpannaṃ prakaraṇaṃ pṛthakpramāṇam, tathā prakaraṇadvayānusaṃdhānasaṃpannaḥ kramaḥ kuto na mānaṃ syāt |
na cāsya prakaraṇe 'ntarbhāvaḥ |
dvayorvākyayoriva prakaraṇayorekavākyatvābhāvāt |
tasmātkramapramāṇena madhyavartina upāṃśuyājasya madhyavartī mantro 'ṅgam |
'samānadeśatvaṃ kramaḥ' iti kramasya svarūpam |
tacca dvividham- pāṭhakṛtamarthakṛtaṃ ca |
tatra pāṭhakṛtamapi dvividham- yathāsaṃkhyaṃ saṃnidhiśceti |
tayorādyasya dabdhimantra udāharaṇam |
"śundhadhvaṃ daivyāya karmaṇe"-ityayaṃ mantraḥ śodhanīyeṣu vastuṣu sādhāraṇobhāsate |
children.translated_text: '<s>Śundhadhvaṃ daivyāya karmaṇe</s>' (purify yourselves for the divine rite) — this <s>mantra</s> appears to be common to [all] objects that require purification.

children.text: tatra sāṃnāyyapātrāṇi kumbhīśākhāpavitrādīnyanantareṣu 'mātariśvanaḥ'- ityādimantreṣvavabhāsanta iti saṃnidhinā tatpātraprokṣaṇe 'śundhadhvam' iti mantro viniyujyate |
children.translated_text: Therein, the <s>sāṃnāyya</s> vessels — <s>kumbhī</s> (pot), <s>śākhā</s> (branch), <s>pavitra</s> (strainer) and the like — appear in the immediately following <s>mantras</s> beginning with '<s>mātariśvanaḥ</s>'; therefore, by proximity (<s>saṃnidhi</s>), the <s>mantra</s> '<s>śundhadhvam</s>' is assigned to the sprinkling of those vessels.
The animal-rite rules (<s>paśudharmāḥ</s>) are subsidiary to the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [sacrifice], due to similarity in performance.
Thus, the three-fold nature of sequence should be understood. || MJaiNyC_3,1.11-14 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices), in the section concerning the sacrificer — a certain <s>mantra</s> is recited in the <s>Mantrakāṇḍa</s>: '<s>dabdhir asya dabdho bhūyāsam, amuṃ dabheyam</s>' (may I be the overpowering of this [adversary], may I overpower him). For the subsidiarity of this <s>mantra</s> to the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> (quiet offering), no Vedic injunctive statement (<s>śruti</s>) exists. In the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, only the explanation of the meaning is recited, not the assignment. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> states: 'By this overpowering (<s>dabdhi</s>) indeed, the gods overpowered the demons; by that very [power] one overpowers one's rival.' <s>Dabdhi</s> is a weapon made of materials. The mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is common [to all three], since the <s>Āgneya</s> and <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [offerings] also have the capacity to avert the undesired. And the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) of the three is one and the same. Therefore, due to the absence of a valid means of knowledge, this <s>mantra</s> is not a subsidiary of the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> — having arrived at this position, we say: In the section on the <s>Adhvaryu</s> [priest's duties], the <s>Āgneya</s>, <s>upāṃśuyāja</s>, and <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> rites are recited in sequence. And in the section concerning the sacrificer, the <s>mantras</s> pertaining to those [rites] are recited in sequence: '<s>agner ahaṃ devayajyayānnnādo bhūyāsam</s>' (through the divine worship of <s>Agni</s>, may I become an eater of food), '<s>dabdhir asya dabdho bhūyāsam amuṃ dabheyam</s>' (may I be the overpowering of this one, may I overpower him), '<s>agniṣomayā rehaṃ devayajyayā vṛtrahā bhūyāsam</s>' (through the divine worship of <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, may I become a slayer of obstacles). Therein, just as context — established through the correlation of two sentences — is an independent means of knowledge, so too, why should sequence — established through the correlation of two contexts — not be a valid means? Nor can this [sequence] be subsumed under context. Because, just as two sentences do not form a single syntactic unit, so too two contexts [do not]. Therefore, by the authority of sequence, the <s>mantra</s> that stands in the middle is a subsidiary of the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s>, which stands in the middle. 'Co-location (<s>samānadeśatva</s>) is sequence' — this is the essential nature of sequence. And it is of two kinds: based on textual position (<s>pāṭhakṛta</s>) and based on meaning (<s>arthakṛta</s>). Of these, that based on textual position is also of two kinds: enumeration (<s>yathāsaṃkhya</s>) and proximity (<s>saṃnidhi</s>). Of those, the <s>dabdhi</s>-<s>mantra</s> is an illustration of the first [enumeration].
(In the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the capacity of designation (<s>samākhyā</s>) to assign [ritual elements], the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
And designation likewise [is an assigning factor], because [the element] serves the purpose of that [which is designated]. / Jaim_3,3.13 /
START MJaiNy 3,3.15-16
He composes the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The ritual duties stated in the three <s>Vedas</s>, [each] associated with three [classes of] priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>) —
whether [the association is] indeterminate or determinate — the determination [cannot be established] without proper examination. // MJaiNy_3,3.15 //
The designation as '<s>hautra</s>' (pertaining to the <s>Hotṛ</s>) and the like is itself indicative of the determination;
being unobstructed and [operating] like other [means of knowledge], it therefore serves as the assigning factor here. // MJaiNy_3,3.16 //

children.text:
yājyāpuronuvākyaṃpāṭhādayo dharmā ṛgvede proktāḥ |
dohananirvāpādayo yajurvede |
ājyastotrapṛṣṭhastotrādayaḥ sāmavede |
tatra 'asyaivaite dharmāḥ' iti niyāmakasya durnirūpatvādyena kenāpyṛtvijā yaḥ ko 'pi dharmaicchayāsaṃgacchate- iti cet |

children.translated_text: that is not correct.

The determination is conveyed by the designation: '<s>hautra</s>' (pertaining to the <s>Hotṛ</s>), '<s>ādhvaryava</s>' (pertaining to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>), '<s>audgātra</s>' (pertaining to the <s>Udgātṛ</s>).
Nor do we perceive any factor that would invalidate the designation.

Therefore, since neither of the two causes of invalidity — non-indicativeness and being overridden — is present, the ritual duties are determined by designation as a valid means of knowledge, just like the five-fold [group of] <s>śruti</s> (direct statement), <s>liṅga</s> (mark), and the rest. || MJaiNyC_3,1.15-16 ||

The ritual duties such as <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse), <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse), and <s>pāṭha</s> (recitation) are stated in the <s>Ṛgveda</s>. The duties such as milking (<s>dohana</s>), placing [the offering] (<s>nirvāpa</s>), and the like are in the <s>Yajurveda</s>. The <s>ājya-stotra</s>, <s>pṛṣṭha-stotra</s>, and the like are in the <s>Sāmaveda</s>. Therein, since the determinant 'these duties belong to this [particular priest]' is difficult to ascertain — if it is argued that any priest may undertake whatever duty he desires,
(In <s>adhikaraṇas</s> [7-12], on the relative strength of the earlier among <s>śruti</s> and the rest, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

When <s>śruti</s> (direct statement), <s>liṅga</s> (mark), <s>vākya</s> (sentence), <s>prakaraṇa</s> (context), <s>sthāna</s> (position), and <s>samākhyā</s> (designation) co-occur, each later one is weaker, due to remoteness from the [intended] meaning. / Jaim_3,3.14 /
START MJaiNy 3,3.17-19
He composes the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (on the superior strength of <s>śruti</s>) —
'Let the <s>Aindrī</s> [verse] be employed for the adoration of <s>Agni</s> (fire)' — [this leads to] an alternative between <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>,

children.text: samuccayo vote śakra evāgniḥ kevalo 'thavā // MJaiNy_3,3.17 //
children.translated_text: or a combination of both, or [the adoration is] of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) alone, or of <s>Agni</s> alone. // MJaiNy_3,3.17 //
There would be an alternative, based on <s>śruti</s> and <s>liṅga</s>; by secondary application of the subsidiary, a combination;

children.text: śratiḥ śaktyanusāreti śakra eko 'tra liṅgataḥ // MJaiNy_3,3.18 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śruti</s> follows [actual] capacity — therefore <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) alone [is established] here, by the mark. // MJaiNy_3,3.18 //
The capacity stated is <s>śruti</s>; <s>śruti</s> acts swiftly; the mark is an inferential indicator dependent on capacity;

children.text: nairākāṅkṣyātmake bodhe śrutyāgnau kevale sthitiḥ // MJaiNy_3,3.19 //
children.translated_text: since <s>śruti</s> produces cognition that leaves nothing to be desired, the conclusion rests on <s>Agni</s> alone [as the object of adoration]. // MJaiNy_3,3.19 //

children.text:
'aindyā gārhapatyamupatiṣṭhate' iti śrūyate |
'kadācana starīrasi nendra saścasi dāśuṣe' ityasāvṛgaindrī |
tatrendrasya prakāśanāt |
'bho indra, kadācidapi ghātako na bhavasi |
kiṃtvāhutiṃ dattavate yajamānāya prīyase' ityarthaḥ |
tatra-indraprakāśanasāmarthyarūpālliṅgānmantrasyendraviṣayakriyā sādhanatvaṃ gamyate |
yadyasau mantra indrapradhānakakriyāyāḥ sādhako na bhavet, tadānīmanena mantreṇendraprakāśanaṃ vyarthe syāt |
tasmāt 'etanmantrakaraṇakakriyāṃ pratīndraḥ pradhānam' ityetādṛśabuddhyīṃ- tpādanaṃ liṅgaviniyogaḥ |
'kāsau kriyā' iti viśeṣajijñāsāyām 'aindyopatiṣṭhate' ityanenāviruddhapada- dvayarūpeṇa vākyenopasthānakriyāyāṃ paryavasānaṃ kriyate |
tathāsati 'aindramantreṇendramupatiṣṭheta' ityayamarthaḥ paryavasyati |
tathā 'gārhapatyam' iti dvitīyāntapadarūpayā śrutyā gārhapatyasya prādhānyaṃ gamyate |
tacca guṇabhūtāṃ yatkiṃcitkaraṇakakriyāmantareṇa na saṃbhavati |
tataḥ 'tādṛśīṃ kāṃcitkriyāṃ prati gārhyatyaḥ pradhānam' ityetādṛśabuddhyīṃtpādanaṃ śrutiviniyogaḥ |
'aindyā, upatiṣṭhate' iti padadvayena mantraviśeṣakriyāviśeṣayoḥ paryavasānaṃ bhavati |
tathā sati 'aindreṇa mantreṇa gārhapatyamupatiṣṭhate' ityartho bhavati |
tadevaṃ śrutiliṅgayorvirodhe sati pramāṇatvāviśeṣādbrīhiyavavadvikalpaḥ- ityekaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ |
indragārhapatyayoḥ pradhānatvāviśeṣadupasthānasya ca guṇatvāt 'pratipradhānaṃ guṇaḥ' iti nyāyenopasthānāvṛtyā śrutiliṅgayoḥ samuccayaḥ- iti dvitīyaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ |
śrutirviniyuñjānā vastusāmathyamanukṛtyaiva viniyuṅkte |
anyathā 'vahninā siñcet' 'vāriṇā dahet' ityapi viniyujyeta |
tata upajīvyatvena liṅgasya prabalatvādindra eva mantreṇopastheyaḥ- iti tṛtīyaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ |
aindramantrasya gārhapatye mukhyavṛttyā śaktyabhāve 'pi gauṇavṛttyā śaktirastīti 'niveśanaḥ'- ityasminnudāharaṇe pūrvameva darśitam |
tathā sati sāmarthyābhāvakṛtapratibandhābhāvānnirvighnā śrutiḥ śīghraṃ viniyuṅkte, liṅgaṃ tu vilambate |
mantrapadānyādau svābhidheyamarthe pratipādayanti |
tata ūrdhva mantrasya sāmarthye nirūpyate |
paścātsāmarthyavaśātsādhanatvavācinī prādhānyavācinī ca śrutiḥ kalpate |
sā ca śrutiḥ 'mantreṇendramupatiṣṭheta' iti viniyuṅkte |
tathā sati pratyakṣaśrutau svābhidheyapratipādanaviniyogayo rmadhyavartinau sāmarthyanirūpaṇa- śrutikalpanavyāpārau na sta iti prābalyāttayā liṅgaṃ bādhyate |
na ca - pratyakṣaśrutiviniyogavelāyāmalabdhātmakatvenāprāptaṃ liṅgaṃ kathaṃ bādhyeta- iti śaṅkanīyam |
children.translated_text: Nor should it be objected that — at the time when the directly perceived <s>śruti</s> makes its assignment, the mark, not yet having attained its own nature, has not [even] arrived, so how can it be overridden?
Because what is meant here as 'overriding' is precisely the obstruction of [the mark's] future arrival.

children.text: śrutyā viniyuktasya mantrasya punarviniyogākāṅkṣāyā anudayātkathaṃ viniyojakaṃ liṅgaṃ prāpsyati |
children.translated_text: Since, after the <s>mantra</s> has been assigned by <s>śruti</s>, the expectation of a further assignment does not arise, how will the mark, as an assigning factor, [ever] come into operation?

children.text: tasmāt - gārhapatyopasthāne mantraḥ pratyakṣaśrutyā viniyujyate || MJaiNyC_3,1.18-19 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — the <s>mantra</s> is assigned to the adoration of the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire] by directly perceived <s>śruti</s>. || MJaiNyC_3,1.18-19 ||

It is heard: '<s>aindyā gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhate</s>' (one adores the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire] with an <s>Aindrī</s> [verse]). '<s>Kadācana starīr asi na indra saś casi dāśuṣe</s>' — this is the <s>Aindrī Ṛk</s>. Therein, <s>Indra</s> is made manifest. The meaning is: 'O <s>Indra</s>, you are never a destroyer; rather, you are well-disposed toward the one who offers oblations.' Therein — from the mark, which is the capacity to illuminate <s>Indra</s>, the instrumentality of the <s>mantra</s> for a rite concerning <s>Indra</s> is understood. If that <s>mantra</s> were not an instrument for a rite having <s>Indra</s> as its principal [deity], then the illumination of <s>Indra</s> by this <s>mantra</s> would be purposeless. Therefore, the generation of such a cognition — 'with respect to the rite that has this <s>mantra</s> as its instrument, <s>Indra</s> is the principal [deity]' — this is assignment by the mark (<s>liṅga-viniyoga</s>). When the specific [rite] is sought — 'What is that rite?' — through the sentence formed by the two uncontradicted words '<s>aindyā upatiṣṭhate</s>,' the conclusion is reached that it is the rite of adoration (<s>upasthāna</s>). This being so, the meaning arrives at: 'One should adore <s>Indra</s> with the <s>Aindrī mantra</s>.' Similarly, through the <s>śruti</s> in the form of the accusative-ending word '<s>gārhapatyam</s>,' the principalness of the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire] is understood. And that [principalness] is impossible without some subsidiary instrumental rite. Hence, the generation of such a cognition — 'with respect to some such rite, the <s>Gārhapatya</s> is the principal [entity]' — this is assignment by <s>śruti</s> (<s>śruti-viniyoga</s>). Through the two words '<s>aindyā</s>' and '<s>upatiṣṭhate</s>,' the conclusion is reached regarding a specific <s>mantra</s> and a specific rite. This being so, the meaning becomes: 'One adores the <s>Gārhapatya</s> with the <s>Aindrī mantra</s>.' Thus, when there is a conflict between <s>śruti</s> and <s>liṅga</s>, the first prima facie view is: since there is no difference in their validity as means of knowledge, there should be an alternative, like [the choice between] barley and rice. The second prima facie view is: since <s>Indra</s> and <s>Gārhapatya</s> are equally principal and the adoration is subsidiary, by the maxim 'the subsidiary [is repeated] for each principal,' through the repetition of adoration, <s>śruti</s> and <s>liṅga</s> are combined. The third prima facie view is: <s>śruti</s>, when making an assignment, does so only by following the actual capacity of the thing; otherwise, even '<s>vahninā siñcet</s>' (one should sprinkle with fire) and '<s>vāriṇā dahet</s>' (one should burn with water) would be [valid] assignments. Therefore, since the mark is stronger by virtue of being that upon which [<s>śruti</s>] depends, <s>Indra</s> alone is to be adored with the <s>mantra</s>. [The conclusion is:] Even when the <s>Aindrī mantra</s> lacks primary applicability to the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, it has the capacity through secondary application (<s>gauṇavṛtti</s>) — as was already shown in the example '<s>niveśanaḥ</s>' (dwelling). This being so, since there is no obstruction caused by the absence of capacity, <s>śruti</s> makes its assignment swiftly and without hindrance, while the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is delayed. The words of the <s>mantra</s> first convey their own denoted meaning. Only thereafter is the <s>mantra</s>'s capacity ascertained. Subsequently, through that capacity, <s>śruti</s> in the form of an instrumentality-indicating and principality-indicating statement is formulated. And that <s>śruti</s> assigns: 'One should adore <s>Indra</s> with the <s>mantra</s>.' This being so, since in the interval between the direct perception of <s>śruti</s> and its assignment through conveying its own denoted meaning, the two operations of ascertaining capacity and formulating <s>śruti</s> do not exist, by virtue of its [directness and] strength, the mark is overridden by <s>śruti</s>.
START MJaiNy 3,3.20-22
He composes the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (on the superior strength of the mark over sentence and the rest) —

children.text: syonaṃ ta iti pūrvārdha tasminsīdeti cottaram /
children.translated_text: '<s>Syonaṃ te</s>' (may it be pleasant for you) — this is the first half; '<s>tasmin sīda</s>' (sit upon that) — this is the latter half;

children.text: sadane sādane cāyaṃ sarvai vār'dhe vyavasthite // MJaiNy_3,3.20 //
children.translated_text: and this [<s>mantra</s>] pertains to [both] the spreading [of the seat] (<s>sadana</s>) and the sitting down (<s>sādana</s>), being established in each half. // MJaiNy_3,3.20 //
If, due to the word '<s>tat</s>' (that), there is syntactic unity [of the two halves], the first [half] would [apply] to the <s>śruti</s> [i.e., the direct statement regarding sitting];
since the mark is more proximate, when the sentence is overridden, the determination [stands by the mark]. // MJaiNy_3,3.21 //
This illustration is for [the case where] the sentence is overridden, not for [the case of] the <s>Aindrī</s> [verse] —
because after being overridden, purposelessness [of the overridden factor] would lead to the absurd consequence of invalidity. // MJaiNy_3,3.22 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate- 'syonaṃ te sadanaṃ kṛṇomi ghṛtasya dhārayā supevaṃ kalpayāmi |
tasminsīdāmṛte pratitiṣṭha vrīhīṇāṃ megha sumanasyamānaḥ' iti |
'bhoḥ puroḍāśa, tava samīcīnaṃ sthānaṃ karomi |
tacca sthānaṃ ghṛtasya dhārayā suṣṭhu sevituṃ yogyaṃ kalpayāmi |
bho vrīhisārabhūta, tvaṃ samāhitamanaskastasminsamīcīne sthāna upaviśa |
tatra sthiro bhava' ityarthaḥ |
tatra-'tasmin' ityanena tacchabdena prakṛtavācinā pūrvottarārdhayorekavākyatve sati mantradvayābhāvātsarvo 'pyayaṃ mantraḥ sthānakaraṇe 'ṅgaṃ syāt |
mantraviniyojikā śrutirevaṃ kalpanīyā- 'sarveṇānena mantreṇa sthānaṃ kartavyam' iti |
tathā 'sarveṇa mantreṇa puroḍāśaḥ sthāpanīyaḥ, ityapi kalpanīyā |
sadanāṅgatvavatpratiṣṭhāpanāṅgatvasyāpi tadvākyabodhitatvāt |
tathā sati sadanasthāpanayorasya mantrasya vikalpaḥ samuccayo vā nijecchayā bhaviṣyati- iti prāpte,-
brūmaḥ- yadetatpūrvottarārdhayoḥ parasparānvayena saṃpannamekaṃ vākyam, tadetaduttarādhasya sadanakaraṇe śaktimakalpayitvā kṛtsnaṃ mantraṃ sadane viniyoktuṃ nārhati |
tathā pūrvārdhasya sthāpane śaktimakalpayitvā na tatra prabhavati |
ato liṅgakalpanavyavadhānena vākyaṃ śrutiṃ prati viprakṛṣyate |
pratyakṣaṃ tu liṅgadvayaṃ saṃnikṛṣyate |
tathā sati liṅgena vākyabādhādarthadvayamubhayorvyavasthitam |
nanu-'aindyā gārhapatyam |
ityatrāpi padadvayānvayarūpasya vākyasya viniyojakatvapratīterliṅgavākyavirodhāya tadevodāhniyatām- iti cet |
children.translated_text: here too, since the sentence — which has the form of a syntactic connection of two words — is recognized as the assigning authority, let that very [example] be cited as [illustrating] the conflict between mark and sentence — if so it is objected,
no.

children.text: tatra liṅgena vākye bādhite satyekaikapadasyārthapratyāyakatvābhāvena śrutikṛtaviniyogasyāpyasiddheraprāmāṇyamevodāhṛtasya prasajyeta |
children.translated_text: There, when the sentence is overridden by the mark, since each individual word would lack the capacity to convey meaning [independently], even the assignment based on <s>śruti</s> would be unestablished, and invalidity alone would result for the cited [example].

children.text: iha tu mahāvākye bādhite 'pyavāntaravākyayorarthapratītau liṅgaviniyogaḥ sidhyatītyetadevodāharaṇam || MJaiNyC_3,1.20-22 ||
children.translated_text: But here, even when the major sentence is overridden, since the meaning is cognized from the subordinate sentences, the assignment through the mark succeeds — and this is precisely the [appropriate] illustration. || MJaiNyC_3,1.20-22 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices), it is heard: '<s>syonaṃ te sadanaṃ kṛṇomi ghṛtasya dhārayā supevaṃ kalpayāmi | tasminsīdāmṛte pratitiṣṭha vrīhīṇāṃ megha sumanasyamānaḥ</s>' — 'O <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake), I make your seat comfortable; I prepare it to be well served with a stream of ghee. O essence of rice, being cheerful-minded, sit upon that proper seat; be firm there' — this is the meaning. Therein, by the word '<s>tasmin</s>' (in that), which is a pronoun referring to what was previously mentioned, when the two halves [of the verse] form a single sentence, there would be no two [separate] <s>mantras</s>, and this entire <s>mantra</s> would be an accessory to the preparation of the seat. The <s>śruti</s> that assigns the <s>mantra</s> should be construed thus: 'with this entire <s>mantra</s>, the seat is to be prepared.' Likewise, it should also be construed: 'with the entire <s>mantra</s>, the <s>puroḍāśa</s> is to be placed.' Because the accessory-nature with respect to placing (<s>pratiṣṭhāpana</s>) is also conveyed by that very sentence, just like the accessory-nature with respect to the seat. In that case, the optional alternation or cumulative application of this <s>mantra</s> for the seat-preparation and the placing would occur according to one's own wish — having arrived at this position, we say: This single sentence that is formed by the mutual syntactic connection of the two halves — without postulating the capacity of the latter half for seat-preparation, it is not proper to assign the entire <s>mantra</s> to the seat-preparation. Likewise, without postulating the capacity of the former half for the placing, it cannot be effective there. Therefore, the sentence is distanced from the <s>śruti</s> by the intervention of postulating the mark (<s>liṅga</s>). But the two marks are brought into proximity directly. This being so, since the sentence is overridden by the mark, the two meanings are settled in both [halves] respectively. Now — '<s>aindyā gārhapatyam</s>' (the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire is adorned] with <s>Aindrī</s> [verse]) —
START MJaiNy 3,3.23-24
He composes the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (on the strength of the sentence over context and the like) —
From the statement '<s>agnīṣomāv idaṃ havyam ajuṣetām</s>' (may <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> enjoy this oblation),
is the remainder beginning with '<s>idam</s>' (this) a <s>sarvaśeṣa</s> (accessory to all) or not? // MJaiNy_3,3.23 //
One might think so from the procedure; but no — the procedure is separated by three [intervening steps];
the sentence is separated by [only] two, therefore it is stronger than the context. // MJaiNy_3,3.24 //

children.text:
sūktavāke śrūyate- 'agniṣomāvidaṃ havirajuṣetām, avīvṛdhetām, mahojyāyo 'krātām |
indrāgnī idaṃ havirajuṣetām, avīvṛghetām, 'maho jyāyo 'krātām' iti |
tatra-devatāvācakamagnīṣomādipadaṃ paurṇamāsyādikāle yathādevataṃ vibhajya prayoktavyam- iti pūrvapāde nirṇītam |
yattu 'idaṃ haviḥ'- ityādikamavaśiṣṭaṃ padajātaṃ, tadagnīṣomamantragatamapyamāvāsyāyāmagnīṣomapadaparityāgena paṭhanīyam |
evam- indrāgnimantragatamapi paurṇamāsyāmindrāgnipadaparityāgena paṭhanīyam |
tathā satyeṣāṃ mantrabhāgāṇāṃ sarvaśeṣatvabodhako darśapūrṇamāsaprakaraṇapāṭho 'nugṛhyate- iti prāpte, brūmaḥ- agnīṣomamantraśeṣasyendrāgnipadānvayāśravaṇāt |
prakaraṇena prathame tadanvayarūpaṃ vākyaṃ kalpanīyam |
tena ca vākyenendrādiprakāśanasāmarthyarūpaṃ liṅgaṃ kalpyate |
tacca liṅgam 'anena mantrabhāgeṇendrāgniviṣayakriyānuṣṭheyā' iti viniyojikāṃ tṛtīyāśrutiṃ kalpayati |
children.translated_text: And that mark postulates a third <s>śruti</s> as the assigning authority: 'with this <s>mantra</s>-portion, the rite pertaining to <s>Indrāgni</s> is to be performed.'
Therefore, between the context-based assignment [and the direct assignment], there is a separation by three [intervening postulations].
But the sentence in the form of the syntactic connection with the <s>Agnīṣoma</s> word — since it is directly heard — is separated only by the mark and the <s>śruti</s>.
Therefore, since the context is overridden by the sentence, that remainder is established as belonging to that [original <s>mantra</s>] alone. || MJaiNyC_3,1.23-24 ||

In the <s>Sūktavāka</s> (hymn-recitation), it is heard: '<s>agniṣomāv idaṃ havir ajuṣetām, avīvṛdhetām, maho jyāyo 'krātām | indrāgnī idaṃ havir ajuṣetām, avīvṛdhetām, maho jyāyo 'krātām</s>' (May <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> enjoy this oblation, may they be magnified, may they produce great eminence; may <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> enjoy this oblation, may they be magnified, may they produce great eminence). Therein — the word denoting the deities, such as <s>agnīṣomā</s>, is to be distributed according to the deities and employed at the appropriate times such as the full-moon day — this was determined in the earlier section. But the remaining group of words beginning with '<s>idaṃ haviḥ</s>' (this oblation) — even though occurring in the <s>Agnīṣoma</s> <s>mantra</s>, on the new-moon day it is to be recited with the omission of the <s>Agnīṣoma</s> word. Likewise, that which occurs in the <s>Indrāgni</s> <s>mantra</s> is to be recited on the full-moon day with the omission of the <s>Indrāgni</s> word. This being so, the reading in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context — which conveys the <s>sarvaśeṣatva</s> (accessory-to-all status) of these <s>mantra</s>-portions — is supported. Having arrived at this position, we say: Because the remainder of the <s>Agnīṣoma</s> <s>mantra</s> is not heard in syntactic connection with the <s>Indrāgni</s> word — by the context, a sentence in the form of such syntactic connection must first be postulated. And by that sentence, a mark in the form of the capacity to indicate <s>Indra</s> and the like is postulated.
START MJaiNy 3,3.25-26
He composes the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (on the strength of context over sequence and the like) —
In the <s>Rājasūya</s>, in the sacrifice called <s>Abhiṣecya</s> (coronation), the <s>devanā</s> (dice-playing) and the like —
are they accessories of that [<s>Abhiṣecya</s> alone], or do they serve all purposes? They are accessories of that [<s>Abhiṣecya</s>], because of its proximity. // MJaiNy_3,3.25 //
Because of the continuity of the nature of the <s>Rājasūya</s>, they would be accessories to all;
the postulated expectancy of the <s>Abhiṣecya</s> — the context (<s>prakriyā</s>) is stronger than that. // MJaiNy_3,3.26 //

children.text:
rājasūye paśviṣṭhisomayāgā bahavaḥ pradhānabhūtāḥ |
tatrābhiṣecanīyākhyaḥ kaścitsomayāgaḥ |
tasya saṃnidhau devanādayaḥ śrūyante-'akṣairdīvyati |
rājanyaṃ jināti |
śaunaḥśepamākhyāpayati' iti |
jināti jayati |
bahvṛcabrāhmaṇe samāmnātaṃ śunaḥ śepaviṣayamupākhyānaṃ śaunaḥśepam |
tatra saṃnidhibalāddevanādayo 'bhiṣecanīyāṅgam- iti cet |
maivam |
rājasūyasya kathaṃbhāvākāṅkṣāyāmanuvṛttāyāṃ vihitā devanādayaḥ prakaraṇena rājasūyaśeṣāḥ |
rājasūyaśca bahuyāgātmaka iti tatratyasarvayāgaśeṣatvam |
na cābhiṣecanīyasya kācidākāṅkṣā devanādiṣvasti |
jyotiṣṭomavikṛtitvenātidiṣṭaiḥ prākṛtāṅgaireva tadākāṅkṣānivṛtteḥ |

children.translated_text: If it is argued that the need arises by the force of the proximate injunction —

children.text: ata evā'kāṅkṣārūpamavāntaraprakaraṇamādau parikalpya taddvārā vākyaliṅgaśrutīkalpanayā saṃnidhirviprakṛṣyate |
children.translated_text: precisely for this reason, by first postulating a sub-context in the form of the expectancy [of the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s>], and through that, by postulating sentence, mark, and <s>śruti</s>, the proximity is distanced.

children.text: rājasūyākāṅkṣārūpaṃ tu mahāprakaraṇaṃ kḷptatvādekaryā kakṣayā saṃnikṛṣyate |
children.translated_text: But the greater context in the form of the <s>Rājasūya</s> expectancy — being already postulated — is brought into proximity by one step fewer.
Therefore, since proximity is overridden by the context, the <s>devanā</s> and the like are accessories of all [rites in the <s>Rājasūya</s>]. || MJaiNyC_3,1.25-26 ||

In the <s>Rājasūya</s>, the animal sacrifices (<s>paśviṣṭi</s>) and <s>Soma</s> sacrifices are the many principal [rites]. Among them, there is a certain <s>Soma</s> sacrifice called <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> (coronation). In its proximity, the <s>devanā</s> (dice-playing) and the like are heard: '<s>akṣair dīvyati</s>' (he plays with dice), '<s>rājanyaṃ jināti</s>' (he defeats the nobleman), '<s>śaunaḥśepam ākhyāpayati</s>' (he narrates the story of <s>Śunaḥśepa</s>). '<s>Jināti</s>' means 'conquers.' The story relating to <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> recorded in the <s>Bahvṛca Brāhmaṇa</s> is the <s>Śaunaḥśepa</s> [narrative]. Therein, by the force of proximity, the <s>devanā</s> and the like would be accessories of the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> — if so it is argued, that is not correct. When the expectation of the nature of the <s>Rājasūya</s> continues, the <s>devanā</s> and the like, being enjoined by the context, are accessories of the <s>Rājasūya</s>. And since the <s>Rājasūya</s> consists of many sacrifices, they are accessories of all the sacrifices therein. Nor does the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> have any [independent] need for the <s>devanā</s> and the like — because its need is fulfilled by the archetype-accessories already assigned to it, since it is a modification (<s>vikṛti</s>) of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.
START MJaiNy 3,3.27-28
He composes the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (on the strength of sequence over designation) —
Is the <s>mantra</s> '<s>śundhadhvam</s>' (purify yourselves) an accessory to the purification of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> implements,
or to the purification of the <s>sānnāyya</s> (curdled milk) vessels? Let the first [alternative hold] by designation (<s>samākhyā</s>). // MJaiNy_3,3.27 //
In '<s>pauroḍāśika</s>' — by the base-word (<s>prakṛti</s>) or by the suffix (<s>taddhita</s>),

since the proximity [to the <s>puroḍāśa</s> vessels] must be postulated from the fact that it is not stated [explicitly], the latter [alternative holds] by sequence (<s>krama</s>), since [that proximity] is already established. // MJaiNy_3,3.28 //

children.text:
'śudhadhvaṃ daivyāya karmaṇe' ityayaṃ mantraḥ 'pauroḍāśikam' iti yājñikaiḥsamākhyāte kāṇḍe paṭhitatvātsamākhyayā puroḍāśakāṇḍoktānāmulūkhalajuhvādīnāmapi śodhane 'ṅgam- iti cet |
maivam |
'pauroḍāśikam' iti samākhyāyāṃ prakṛtiḥ puroḍāśamātramabhidhatte |
taddhitapratyayaśca kāṇḍam |
na caitāvatā kṛtsnapuroḍāśapātrāṇāṃ mantrasaṃnidhiḥ pratyakṣo bhavati, kiṃtvarthāpattyā kalpyate |
yadyuktasaṃnidhirna syāt, tadā mantrapratipādakagranthasya pauroḍāśikasamākhyā na syāt |
na hyagnyasaṃnihitānām 'iṣe tvā-' dimantrāṇāmāgneyakāṇḍasamākhyā bhavati |
saṃnihitānāṃ tu 'yuñjānaḥ prathamaṃ manaḥ'- ityādimantrāṇāṃ bhavatyeṣā samākhyā |
tasmāt- kāṇḍasamākhyayā saṃnidhiṃ parikalpya tatsaṃnidhyanyathānupapattyā parasparākāṅkṣārūpaṃ kṛtsnaṃ pātraprakaraṇaṃ kalpayitvā taddvārā vākyaliṅgaśrutīḥ kalpayitvā tayā śrutyā viniyoga iti samākhyāyā viprakarṣaḥ |
sāṃnāyyapātrāṇāṃ śodhane mantrasaṃnidhistu pratyakṣaḥ |
idhmābarhiḥ saṃpādanasya muṣṭinirvāpasya cāntarālaṃ sāṃnāyyapātrāṇāṃ deśa uktaḥ |
children.translated_text: The place of the <s>sānnāyya</s> vessels is stated in the interval between the preparation of the fuel-sticks and the <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass) and the hand-sowing (<s>muṣṭinirvāpa</s>).
And the <s>mantra</s> is recited in the middle <s>anuvāka</s> (section) between the <s>anuvākas</s> relating to fuel-sticks and <s>barhis</s> and the sowing.

children.text: tena ca pratyakṣasaṃnidhinā prakaraṇādīnāṃ caturṇāmeva kalpanātsaṃnidhiḥ saṃnikṛṣyate |
children.translated_text: And through this direct proximity, since only four [postulations] — namely the context and the like — need be made, the proximity is brought closer.

children.text: tasmāt- krameṇa samākhyāṃ bādhitvā 'sāṃnāyyapātraśodhanaśeṣo mantraḥ' ityayaṃ caramaḥ pakṣo 'bhyupeyaḥ || MJaiNyC_3,1.27-28 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, overriding the designation by the sequence, the final position — that the <s>mantra</s> is an accessory to the purification of the <s>sānnāyya</s> vessels — should be accepted. || MJaiNyC_3,1.27-28 ||

This <s>mantra</s> '<s>śundhadhvaṃ daivyāya karmaṇe</s>' (purify yourselves for the divine rite), since it is recited in the section designated by the ritualists as '<s>pauroḍāśika</s>' (pertaining to the <s>puroḍāśa</s>), would by that designation be an accessory also to the purification of the mortar (<s>ulūkhala</s>), ladle (<s>juhū</s>), and other implements mentioned in the <s>puroḍāśa</s> section — if so it is argued, that is not correct. In the designation '<s>pauroḍāśika</s>', the base-word denotes only the <s>puroḍāśa</s> itself. And the <s>taddhita</s> suffix denotes the section (<s>kāṇḍa</s>). But by this much alone, the proximity of the <s>mantra</s> to all the <s>puroḍāśa</s> vessels is not directly evident; rather, it must be postulated through implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>). If the stated proximity did not exist, then the designation '<s>pauroḍāśika</s>' for the text expounding the <s>mantra</s> would not apply. For <s>mantras</s> like '<s>iṣe tvā</s>' that are not proximate to <s>Agni</s> do not receive the designation '<s>Āgneya-kāṇḍa</s>.' But for <s>mantras</s> such as '<s>yuñjānaḥ prathamaṃ manaḥ</s>' that are proximate [to <s>Agni</s>], this designation does apply. Therefore, by postulating proximity through the section-designation, and by the impossibility of that proximity being otherwise [explained], postulating a sub-context in the form of the mutual expectancy of all vessels, and through that postulating sentence, mark, and <s>śruti</s> — by that <s>śruti</s> the assignment [is made] — this is the remoteness of the designation. But the proximity of the <s>mantra</s> to the purification of the <s>sānnāyya</s> vessels is directly evident.
START MJaiNy 3,3.29-30
He composes the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (on the capacity for being overridden) —

children.text: bādho na yukto yukto vā prāptyaprāptyorna yujyate /
children.translated_text: Overriding is not justified, or is it justified? It is not appropriate based on [the dichotomy of] apprehension and non-apprehension;

children.text: apravṛttaṃ prasaktaṃ yaddhiyā tasyāstu bādhyatā // MJaiNy_3,3.29 //
children.translated_text: that which has not [fully] proceeded but is cognized by the intellect — let that be subject to being overridden. // MJaiNy_3,3.29 //
The overriding of what is established by a valid means of knowledge — this is what is [discussed] in the tenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>];
but the overriding of what is established through error — therefore [here we discuss] the overriding of what is not [truly] established. // MJaiNy_3,3.30 //

children.text:
prāptasya pravṛttirastīti na tannivāraṇaṃ śakyam |
aprāptasya bādhaviṣayatvenāvasthānameva nāsti |
tasmāt-na yukto bādhaḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
buddhyāviṣayīkṛtasya vārayituṃ śakyatvāt |
na caitadatyantaṃ pravṛttam |
anuṣṭhānarūpaphalaparyavasānābhāvāt |
nāpyatyantamapravṛttam |

children.translated_text: because the cognition thereof has arisen.
Therefore, neither of the stated defects applies.

In the tenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], the meaning comprehended through a valid means of knowledge (<s>codaka-pramāṇa</s>) is overridden — this is the overriding of what is [truly] established (<s>prāpta-bādha</s>).

But here, what is comprehended through subsequent pseudo-valid means that contradict the earlier valid means — this is the overriding of what is not [truly] established (<s>aprāpta-bādha</s>). || MJaiNyC_3,1.29-30 ||

That which has been apprehended has [already] proceeded to activity, so it is not possible to prevent it. That which has not been apprehended has no standing as a subject of overriding at all. Therefore, overriding is not justified — if so it is argued, that is not correct. Because that which has been grasped by the intellect can be prevented. And this has not fully proceeded — because it has not reached its culmination in the form of actual performance. Nor is it entirely unproceeded —
(In the thirteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> on the <s>Ahīna</s>-nature of the twelve-day <s>Upasad</s> [worship] (the <s>Ahīna</s> principle), <s>sūtras</s> 15–16:)
Or it is an <s>Ahīna</s> [sacrifice], from the context, [and the term is] secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>). / Jaim_3,3.15 /

children.text: asaṃyogāt tu mukhyasya tasmād apakṛṣyeta / Jaim_3,3.16 /
children.translated_text: But since there is no connection with the primary [meaning], it should be withdrawn from that. / Jaim_3,3.16 /
START MJaiNy 3,3.31-33
He composes the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: tistra eva hi sāhne syurahīne dvādaśetyataḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Sāhna</s> (one-day sacrifice), there would be only three [<s>Upasads</s>]; in the <s>Ahīna</s>, twelve — therefore,
would the twelve-[fold number] apply to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, or to the sequence of days (<s>ahargaṇa</s>)? // MJaiNy_3,3.31 //
Let the first [alternative hold] from the context; the <s>Ahīna</s>-nature is not contradicted;
since [the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>] is the archetype, it is not deficient (<s>hīna</s>) in anything — therefore let there be an option here. // MJaiNy_3,3.32 //
The designation <s>Ahīna</s>, which is different from [the derivation based on] <s>Sāhna</s>, is a conventional term (<s>rūḍhi</s>) [applying] to the sequence of days;
by the genitive <s>śruti</s>, the twelve-fold [number] should be withdrawn from the context. // MJaiNy_3,3.33 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭomaprakaraṇe śrūyate-'tistra eva sāhnasyopasado dvādaśāhīnasya' iti |
ekenāhnā niṣpādyatvātsāhno jyotiṣṭomaḥ |
dīkṣādivasādūrdhve somābhiṣavadivasātpūrva kartavyā homā upasadaḥ |
tāsāṃ dvādaśatvaṃ prakaraṇabalājjyotiṣṭome niviśate |
ahīnaśabdaśca tasminneva kalpate |
jyotiṣṭomasya nikhilasomayāgaprakṛtitvena sarveṣāmaṅgānāṃ tatropadeśe sati tadupadeśavikalavikṛtīnāmiva hīnatvābhāvāt |
ato dvādaśatvatritvayorvikalpaḥ- iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- āvṛttasomayāgarūpo dvirātratrirātrādirahargaṇaḥ |
tasminnahīnaśabdo rūḍhaḥ |
yaugikatve tu 'na hīnaḥ' iti vigṛhya samāse kṛte satyayajñādiśabdabadādyudāttaḥ syāt |
madhyodāttastvāmnāyate |

children.translated_text: And convention (<s>rūḍhi</s>), since it is independent of etymological analysis, is the cause of quick cognition.

Therefore, this designation <s>Ahīna</s>, being different from the <s>Sāhna</s>-denoting word for <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, denotes the <s>ahargaṇa</s> (day-sequence) which is different from the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.
In that day-sequence (<s>ahargaṇa</s>), the twelve-fold number stated by the genitive <s>śruti</s> is established.
For the accomplishment of that, this [twelve-fold number] should be withdrawn from the context. || MJaiNyC_3,1.31-33 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> context, it is heard: '<s>tisra eva sāhnasyopasado dvādaśāhīnasya</s>' (there are exactly three <s>Upasads</s> for a <s>Sāhna</s> [sacrifice], and twelve for an <s>Ahīna</s>). The <s>Sāhna</s> is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, because it is accomplished in a single day. The <s>Upasads</s> are the oblations to be performed after the day of consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) and before the day of the <s>Soma</s> pressing (<s>abhiṣava</s>). Their twelve-fold number, by the force of the context, applies to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. And the word <s>Ahīna</s> is fitting for that very [<s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>] — since the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, being the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>) of all <s>Soma</s> sacrifices, when all accessories are taught therein, is not deficient (<s>hīna</s>) in any [accessory], unlike the modifications (<s>vikṛtis</s>) that are incomplete in their instructions. Therefore, there would be an option between twelve and three — having arrived at this position, we say: The <s>ahargaṇa</s> (sequence of days), which is a repeated <s>Soma</s> sacrifice in the form of a two-day, three-day [series] and so on, is a day-sequence. The word <s>Ahīna</s> is conventional (<s>rūḍha</s>) in [referring to] that. If it were etymological (<s>yaugika</s>), then by analyzing it as '<s>na hīnaḥ</s>' (not deficient) in a compound, it should have initial accent (<s>yudātta</s>) like the word <s>ayajña</s> and the like. But it is recorded with middle accent (<s>madhyodātta</s>).
(In the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the augmentation of the <s>pratipat</s> [introductory verse] in the <s>Kulāya</s> and the like, <s>sūtras</s> 17-19:)
Or [the <s>pratipat</s>] is connected with duality and plurality, because of the injunction regarding that. / Jaim_3,3.17 /
If it be said that [the duality etc.] is purpose-based, then by the alternative — / Jaim_3,3.18 /
No, because of the single connection with the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>). / Jaim_3,3.19 /
START MJaiNy 3,3.34-36
He composes the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: yuvaṃ hīti dvayoḥ kartrorbahūnāṃ caita ityamūm /
children.translated_text: '<s>Yuvāṃ hi</s>' (you two indeed) — for two performers; and '<s>eta</s>' (these) — for many [performers];
should this be the <s>pratipat</s> [introductory verse] in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, or in the day-sequence (<s>sāhargaṇa</s>)? // MJaiNy_3,3.34 //
When one [sacrificer] is unable, [the sacrifice is performed] by two or indeed by many;
since it is to be performed as part of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, it should apply in the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>) itself. // MJaiNy_3,3.35 //
The plurality of the sacrificer is directly heard in the modifications (<s>vikṛtis</s>);
by augmenting the <s>pratipat</s>, let it be applied to the <s>Kulāya</s> and the like. // MJaiNy_3,3.36 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate- 'yuvaṃ hi sthaḥ svarpatī'- iti dvayoryajamānayoḥ pratipadaṃ kuryāt |
ete asṛgramindavaḥ'- iti bahubhyo yajamānebhyaḥ' iti |
stotrasyopakrame paṭhanīyāmṛcaṃ pratipacchabdo 'bhidhatte |
sā codāhṛtā pratipatprakaraṇājjyotiṣṭome niviśate |
na ca tatra yajamāsadvitvabahutvayorasaṃbhavaḥ |
ekasya yajamānasya dravyalābhādinā tadaśaktau nityakarmaṇaḥ parityāgāsaṃbhavena dvābhyāṃ bahubhirvā tasyāvaśyakartavyatvāt- iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- yajamānadvitvaṃ kulāyanāmake yajñe sākṣādāmnātam-'etena rājapurohitau sāyujyakāmau yajeyātām' iti |
yajamānabahutvaṃ satreṣvāmnātam- 'caturviṃśatiparamāḥ sattramāsīran' iti |
tato dviśabdabahuśabdarūpābhyāṃ śrutibhyāṃ prakaraṇaṃ bādhitvā kulāyādiṣu yathoktapratipadorutkarṣaḥ kartavyaḥ |
na cāśaktāvapi yajamānadvitvabahutve saṃbhavataḥ |

children.translated_text: Because, when another person is appointed as a substitute for one who is unable, that [substitute] does not [himself] possess the status of sacrificer.
It will be stated: 'There is no substitute for the sacrificer.'

children.text: yadyanyaḥ puruṣaḥ svayameva pravartate tadānīṃ svakīyameva prayogaṃ kuryāt, natvaśaktasya sāhāyyamācaret |
children.translated_text: If another person undertakes [the sacrifice] on his own initiative, then he would perform his own rite — he would not render assistance to the one who is unable.

children.text: tasmāt- śrūyamāṇasya yajamānaikatvasya kālādivadanupādeyāṅgatvena tyaktumaśakyatvānna jyotiṣṭome yajamānasya dvitvabahutve saṃbhavataḥ || MJaiNyC_3,1.34-36 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — since the unity of the sacrificer, as heard [in the texts], cannot be discarded, being an essential accessory like the time and the like, the duality and plurality of the sacrificer are not possible in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. || MJaiNyC_3,1.34-36 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: '<s>yuvāṃ hi sthaḥ svarpatī</s>' (you two are indeed lords of heaven) — the <s>pratipat</s> should be performed for two sacrificers. '<s>Ete asṛgram indavaḥ</s>' (these <s>Soma</s> drops have flowed forth) — [this is] for many sacrificers. The word <s>pratipat</s> denotes the <s>Ṛk</s> verse to be recited at the commencement of the <s>stotra</s> (praise chant). And the <s>pratipat</s> so stated applies to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> by the force of the context. Nor is the duality and plurality of sacrificers impossible therein. Since a permanent rite (<s>nityakarma</s>) cannot be abandoned, when one sacrificer is unable [to perform] due to lack of materials and the like, it must necessarily be performed by two or many — having arrived at this position, we say: The duality of sacrificers is directly enjoined in the sacrifice called <s>Kulāya</s>: '<s>etena rājapurohitau sāyujyakāmau yajeyātām</s>' (by this [sacrifice], the king and the royal priest, desiring union, should sacrifice). The plurality of sacrificers is enjoined in <s>Sattra</s> [sacrifices]: '<s>caturviṃśati paramāḥ sattram āsīran</s>' (twenty-four at most should sit for the <s>Sattra</s>). Therefore, overriding the context by the <s>śrutis</s> in the form of the words for duality and plurality, the augmentation of the stated <s>pratipat</s> should be made in the <s>Kulāya</s> and the like. Nor can the duality and plurality of sacrificers occur even when [one is] unable.
(In the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the non-augmentation of the <s>jāghanī</s> [hindquarter], <s>sūtras</s> 20-23:)
And the hindquarter (<s>jāghanī</s>), because of being a part. / Jaim_3,3.20 /
Or the injunction [applies], because it is unprecedented. / Jaim_3,3.21 /
[It is] a part — if so it is argued — / Jaim_3,3.22 /
No, because the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>) is not established by [independent] scriptural injunction. / Jaim_3,3.23 /
START MJaiNy 3,3.37-38
He composes the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The <s>jāghanī</s> (hindquarter) is used in the <s>saṃyāja</s> (joint offering) of wives — is this for the <s>paśu</s> (animal sacrifice) as well?

children.text: darśādau tatpaśau yuktaṃ jāghanyāḥ samavāyataḥ // MJaiNy_3,3.37 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and animal sacrifice, it is appropriate [to assign it to both], because of co-occurrence with the <s>jāghanī</s>. // MJaiNy_3,3.37 //

children.text: jāghanī nāma bhāgo 'sau darśādau samavaiti hi /
children.translated_text: That part called <s>jāghanī</s> co-occurs indeed with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>;
it should not be augmented, nor should a new consecration be made — because of the instrumentality indicated by the instrumental case. // MJaiNy_3,3.38 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsaprakaraṇe śrūyate-'jāghanyā patnīḥ saṃyājayanti' iti |
jāghanī paśoḥ puccham |
patnīśabdo 'trā'huticatuṣṭayātmakasya karmaṇo nāmadheyaikadeśaḥ |
ata eva śrūyate-'pañca prayājā ijyante, catvāraḥ patnīsaṃyājāḥ' iti |
tatra tṛtīyāhutau devapatnīnāṃ devatātvāttaddvārā karmanāmnaḥ patnīsaṃyājaśabdasya pravṛttiḥ |
tatra jāghanīmuddiśya patnīsaṃyājasaṃskāro vidhīyate |
jāghanī ca paśau samavetā na tu darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ |
ataḥ prakaraṇādutkṛṣya paśau niveśanam- iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- jāghanīśabdena paśorbhāmo 'bhidhīyate |
sa ca darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ paśuyāgatvābhāve 'pi krayādinā saṃpādayituṃ śakyate |
children.translated_text: And that [haunch], even though the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> does not have the character of an animal sacrifice, can be procured through purchase and the like.

children.text: na cātra paśau vidyamānāyāṃ jāghanyāṃ patnīsaṃyājaiḥ saṃskāryatvam |
children.translated_text: Nor is the <s>jāghanī</s>, when present in the animal [sacrifice], subject to being consecrated by the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s>.
Because the instrumentality [of the <s>jāghanī</s>] is understood from the instrumental case [ending].
Therefore — there is no augmentation from the context. || MJaiNyC_3,1.37-38 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context, it is heard: '<s>jāghanyā patnīḥ saṃyājayanti</s>' (with the hindquarter, they perform the <s>saṃyāja</s> [joint offerings] of the wives). The <s>jāghanī</s> is the tail of the animal. The word <s>patnī</s> (wives) here is a part of the name of the ritual consisting of four oblations. Hence it is heard: '<s>pañca prayājā ijyante, catvāraḥ patnīsaṃyājāḥ</s>' (five <s>prayājas</s> are offered, [and] four <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s>). Therein, in the third oblation, because the divine wives (<s>devapatnīs</s>) are the deities, through them the ritual name <s>patnīsaṃyāja</s> is applied. Therein, the consecration of the <s>patnīsaṃyāja</s> is enjoined with reference to the <s>jāghanī</s>. And the <s>jāghanī</s> co-occurs with the animal [sacrifice], not with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. Therefore, augmenting from the context, it should be placed in the animal sacrifice — having arrived at this position, we say: By the word <s>jāghanī</s>, the haunch of an animal is denoted.
(In the sixteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the placement of the <s>saṃtardana</s> (tightening) in the concluding rite, <s>sūtras</s> 24-31:)
The <s>saṃtardana</s> (tightening) should be in the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>), like the purchase-price (<s>krayaṇa</s>), since there is no loss of purpose. / Jaim_3,3.24 /
Or there is augmentation, because of the apprehension of a specific [meaning]. / Jaim_3,3.25 /
Or [the specificity pertains] to the performer, because [the name] is caused by that. / Jaim_3,3.26 /
Or [it should apply] to the sacrifice, because of the fitness [indicated] by the <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage). / Jaim_3,3.27 /
And the concluding rites (<s>saṃsthās</s>) [should be treated] like the performer, since there is no distinction in the purpose of sustaining. / Jaim_3,3.28 /
Or in the <s>Ukthya</s> and the like, because the purpose [of the term 'long'] is present there. / Jaim_3,3.29 /
If it be said that, due to the lack of distinction, the praise (<s>stuti</s>) is purposeless — / Jaim_3,3.30 /
[That praise] would apply, because of [its] non-permanence. / Jaim_3,3.31 /
START MJaiNy 3,3.39-40
He composes the sixteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
One should tighten (<s>saṃtardana</s>) in the long <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] — is that in the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>) or in the modification (<s>vikṛti</s>)?

children.text: dīrghasya soma ityukte prakṛtāvastu tardanam // MJaiNy_3,3.39 //
children.translated_text: Since 'of the long one, the <s>Soma</s>' is stated, the tightening should be in the archetype. // MJaiNy_3,3.39 //
Since the co-ordinate compound (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) is stronger than the genitive [construction],
the augmentation [applies] to the <s>Ukthya</s> concluding rite and the like, which possess length, since other [interpretations] are overridden. // MJaiNy_3,3.40 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate- 'dīrghasome saṃtṛdyeddhṛtyai' iti |
somayāgaviśeṣo dīrghasomaḥ |
tasminsomābhiṣavādhārayoradhiṣavaṇaphalakayoḥ saṃtardanaṃ kāryam |
anyonyaviyogena śaithilyaṃ mā bhūditi dṛḍhasaṃśleṣaḥ saṃtardanam |
tadetatprakaraṇabalātprakṛtau niviśate |
na ca tatra dīrghasomatvānupapattiḥ |
'dīrghasya somaḥ' ityevaṃ dīrghaśabdasya yajamānaviśeṣaṇatvenāpyupapatteḥ- iti prāpte-
brūmaḥ- 'ṣaṣṭhīsamāsātkarmadhārayo balīyān' iti (niṣādasthapatyadhikaraṇe) vakṣyate |
tathā sati dīrghatvaṃ somasya dharmaḥ, na tu yajamānasya |
nanvevamapi prakṛtibhūtasya somasyeṣṭipaśvapekṣayā dīrghatvamastyeva - iti cet |
na |
somaśabdenaiva tadavagatau dīrghaśabdasya vaiyarthyāt |
na hīṣṭipaśvapekṣayā hrasvaḥ kaścitsomo 'sti, yasya vyāvṛttaye dīrghaśabdaḥ prayujyeta |
tasmātprakṛtirūpaṃ hrasvaṃ soyaṃ vyāvartayitumayaṃ dīrghaśabdaḥ |
vikṛtiṣūkthyādiṣu grahādhikyāddīrghatvam |
dvirātrādiṣu cā'vṛttyā dīrghatvam |

children.translated_text: Therefore, overriding the context by the sentence, the placement [of the tightening] is in the modifications.
And in the archetype, the word <s>dīrgha</s> is overridden, as already stated.

children.text: saṃtardanabādhaśca sākṣācchrūyate- 'hanū vā ete yajñasya yadadhiṣavaṇe na saṃtṛṇatti, asaṃtṛṣṇe hi han' iti |
children.translated_text: And the overriding of [the non-application of] the tightening [in the archetype] is directly heard: '<s>hanū vā ete yajñasya yad adhiṣavaṇe na saṃtṛṇatti, asaṃtṛṣṇe hi han</s>' (these [pressing-boards] are indeed the jaws of the sacrifice; when one does not tighten [them], [the sacrifice] is indeed impaired).
Therefore — there is no placement in the archetype. || MJaiNyC_3,1.39-40 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: '<s>dīrghasome saṃtṛdyed dhṛtyai</s>' (one should tighten [the pressing-boards] in the long <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice], for the sake of sustaining). The <s>Dīrghasoma</s> is a particular type of <s>Soma</s> sacrifice. In that [sacrifice], the tightening — the firm joining to prevent loosening caused by mutual separation — is to be performed on the two pressing-boards (<s>adhiṣavaṇa-phalaka</s>). This [tightening], by the force of the context, applies to the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>). Nor is there any impossibility of the <s>Dīrghasoma</s>-nature [in the archetype]. Because the word <s>dīrgha</s> (long) can also be construed as qualifying the sacrificer — '<s>dīrghasya somaḥ</s>' (the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] of the tall one) — having arrived at this position, we say: It will be stated (in the <s>Niṣāda-sthapati-adhikaraṇa</s>): 'A co-ordinate compound (<s>karmadhāraya</s>) is stronger than a genitive compound (<s>ṣaṣṭhī-samāsa</s>).' This being so, the length (<s>dīrghatva</s>) is an attribute of the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice], not of the sacrificer. But even so — if it is argued that the archetype <s>Soma</s> sacrifice itself possesses length relative to the <s>Iṣṭi</s> (simple offering) and the <s>Paśu</s> (animal sacrifice) — no. Because if that [length] were known from the word <s>Soma</s> alone, the word <s>dīrgha</s> would be purposeless. For there is no <s>Soma</s> sacrifice that is 'short' relative to the <s>Iṣṭi</s> and <s>Paśu</s>, from which the word <s>dīrgha</s> would serve to distinguish [the present one]. Therefore, this word <s>dīrgha</s> distinguishes [it] from the archetype-form, which is 'short.' In the modifications (<s>vikṛtis</s>) — the <s>Ukthya</s> and the like — the length arises from the excess of cups (<s>graha</s>). And in the two-day (<s>Dvirātra</s>) and other [sacrifices], the length arises from repetition.
(In the seventeenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the prohibition of the <s>Pravargya</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 32-33:)
That which is connected with number should apply to the sacrifice, from the context. / Jaim_3,3.32 /

children.text: naimittikaṃ vā kartṛsaṃyogāl liṅgasya tannimittatvāt / Jaim_3,3.33 /
children.translated_text: Or [it is] occasional (<s>naimittika</s>), because of the connection with the performer, since the mark is caused by that. / Jaim_3,3.33 /
START MJaiNy 3,3.41-41
He composes the seventeenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
One should not perform the <s>Pravargya</s> at the first sacrifice — does the prohibition apply to the sacrifice [itself], or [only] when it has been [previously] performed?

children.text: pratiṣedhaḥ kratau yukta uktā hyasyā'dyayajñatā // MJaiNy_3,3.41 //
children.translated_text: The prohibition is appropriate with respect to the sacrifice, for its first-sacrifice-nature has been stated. // MJaiNy_3,3.41 //
From the sentence 'he performs the <s>Pravargya</s> before the <s>Upasads</s>,' the injunction pertains to the sacrifice;
the prohibition [applies] only in certain [cases], because of the priority of the first performance. // MJaiNy_3,3.42 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome pravargyākhyaṃ karma prakṛtya śrūyate- 'na prathamayajñe pravṛñjyāt' iti |
so 'yaṃ pratiṣedho jyotiṣṭomakratau draṣṭavyaḥ' na tu tadīyaprathamaprayoge |
kutaḥ |
'evavāva prathamo' yajño yajñānāṃ yajjyotiṣṭomaḥ' iti tasya prathamayajñatvāmidhānāt- iti cet maivam |
'purastādupasadāṃ pravargye pravṛṇakti' iti vākyena ktatau pravargyasya vihitatvāt |
na ca vidhiniṣedhavākyayoḥ samānabalatvādanirṇayaḥ |
niṣedhavākye prathamaśabdena niṣedhasya prayogaparatvanirṇayāt |
prathamadvitīyādiśabdāḥ kriyāyā āvṛttau mukhyāḥ, tatsaṃbandhādvastuṣūpacaryante |
prathamamadhyetavyatvātprathamaṃ kāṇḍam, tadanantaramadhyetavyatvāddvitīyaṃ kāṇḍam |
evam- ādāvutpannatvātprathamaḥ putraḥ, tadanantaramutpannatvāddvitīyaḥ |
tathā sati prayogakriyāyā āvṛttiviśeṣe prathamaśabdo mukhyaḥ |
tadāvṛttiviṣayatayā yajñe lākṣaṇikaḥ |
tvatpakṣe 'pi kratau mukhyo yajñaśabdaḥ, prayoge lākṣaṇikaḥ syāt- iti cet |
bāḍham |
tathāpyasaṃjātavirodhinilākṣaṇikatvakalpanādvaramuttara pade tatkalpanam |
tasmājjyotiṣṭomasya prathamaprayoge pravargyaniṣedhaḥ |
nanu-saptasaṃsthāyuktasya jyotiṣṭomasya prathamasaṃsthārūpo 'gniṣṭomaḥ, tatrāyaṃ niṣedhaḥ paryavasyati |
vidhiśca tatra śrūyate- agniṣṭome pravṛṇakti' iti |
children.translated_text: And an injunction is also heard therein: '<s>agniṣṭome pravṛṇakti</s>' (one performs [the <s>Pravargya</s>] in the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>).
If so, then let there be a resolution of the injunction and the prohibition through difference of qualified persons (<s>adhikārin</s>).

children.text: tathā hi śrūyate- 'kāmaṃ tu yo 'nūcānaḥ syāt, tasya pravañjyāt' iti |
children.translated_text: For it is heard: '<s>kāmaṃ tu yo 'nūcānaḥ syāt, tasya pravṛñjyāt</s>' (but for one who is learned [in the <s>Vedas</s>], one may perform the <s>Pravargya</s>).
Therefore — this prohibition applies only to the first performance of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> when the performer is someone other than the <s>anūcāna</s> (learned one). || MJaiNyC_3,1.41-42 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, with reference to the rite called <s>Pravargya</s>, it is heard: '<s>na prathamayajñe pravṛñjyāt</s>' (one should not perform the <s>Pravargya</s> at the first sacrifice). This prohibition should be understood as applying to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice [itself], not to its first performance [by a given sacrificer]. Why? Because it is stated that 'the first of sacrifices is indeed the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>' — if so it is argued, that is not correct. Because the <s>Pravargya</s> is enjoined in the sacrifice by the sentence: '<s>purastād upasadāṃ pravargye pravṛṇakti</s>' (he performs the <s>Pravargya</s> before the <s>Upasads</s>). Nor is there irresolution due to equal force of the injunctive and prohibitive sentences. Because in the prohibitive sentence, the word <s>prathama</s> (first) determines that the prohibition pertains to [a specific] performance. The words <s>prathama</s> (first), <s>dvitīya</s> (second), and the like are primary [in meaning] with reference to the repetition of an action, and are used figuratively with respect to things by association with that [action]. The first <s>kāṇḍa</s> [is called so] because it is to be studied first, the second <s>kāṇḍa</s> because it is to be studied next thereafter. Similarly — the first son [is called so] because he is born at the beginning, the second because he is born next thereafter. This being so, the word <s>prathama</s> is primary with reference to a particular repetition of the performance-action. With respect to the sacrifice, which is the object of that repetition, it is figurative (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>). If it is argued that in your position too, the word <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice) is primary with respect to the rite, while with respect to the performance it would be figurative — indeed so. Nevertheless, it is better to posit the figurative usage in the latter word [rather than the former], since figurative usage in [the word] with which no conflict has yet arisen [should be preferred]. Therefore, the prohibition of the <s>Pravargya</s> applies to the first performance of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. But — if the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, which has seven concluding forms (<s>saṃsthā</s>), has the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> as its first concluding form, then this prohibition culminates there [in the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>].
(In the eighteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the assignment of the <s>Pauṣṇa</s> grinding in the modification, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: pauṣṇaṃ peṣaṇaṃ vikṛtau pratīyetācodanāt prakṛtau / Jaim_3,3.34 /
children.translated_text: The <s>Pauṣṇa</s> (relating to <s>Pūṣan</s>) grinding should be understood in the modification, since there is no injunction [for it] in the archetype. / Jaim_3,3.34 /
START MJaiNy 3,3.43-44
He composes the eighteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
