<s>Pūṣan</s> has ground offerings as his share — is this in the archetype or in the modification?
From the context of the <s>Iṣṭi</s> (simple offering), it is appropriate that it be in the archetype. // MJaiNy_3,3.43 //
Like the <s>saṃtardana</s> and the like, from the sentence [it applies] to the modification, since <s>Pūṣan</s> is possible [there];
the restatement of what is already established is for the purpose of [stating] something additional. // MJaiNy_3,3.44 //
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context it is heard: '<s>tasmāt pūṣā prapiṣṭabhāgo 'dantako hi</s>' (therefore <s>Pūṣan</s> has ground [offerings] as his share, for he is toothless).
Therein — the ground-food-share nature of the toothless <s>Pūṣan</s> is already established, like the <s>saṃtardana</s>, the <s>pratipat</s>, and the like.
Nevertheless, in the subsequent

children.text: dhikaraṇe tasminneva viṣaye viśeṣaṃ vaktumiha prastūyate || MJaiNyC_3,1.43-44 ||
children.translated_text: <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, with regard to that very topic, [the discussion] is introduced here in order to state a specific point. || MJaiNyC_3,1.43-44 ||
(In the nineteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the placement of the <s>Pauṣṇa</s> grinding exclusively in the <s>caru</s> [rice cake offering], <s>sūtras</s> 35-38:)
That [grinding] serves all purposes, due to the absence of distinction. / Jaim_3,3.35 /

children.text: carau vārthoktaṃ puroḍāśe 'rthavipratiṣedhāt paśau na syāt / Jaim_3,3.36 /
children.translated_text: Or [it applies] to the <s>caru</s> (rice cake), [since] the purpose stated [there applies]; in the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake offering), because of the contradiction of purpose, [it does] not [apply]; in the animal [sacrifice], it should not [apply]. / Jaim_3,3.36 /
If it be said [it does not apply] to the <s>caru</s> as well — / Jaim_3,3.37 /
No, because [the <s>caru</s> is so called] due to being [an object of] cooking. / Jaim_3,3.38 /
START MJaiNy 3,3.45-46
He composes the nineteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the grinding [applicable] to the <s>caru</s> (rice cake), the <s>paśu</s> (animal), and the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake)? Or is the grinding exclusively for the <s>caru</s>?
Since no distinction is perceived, it is enjoined for all of them. // MJaiNy_3,3.45 //
[It is] not [applicable] to the <s>puroḍāśa</s>, since it is already accomplished [there], due to the destruction of the heart and other forms [through grinding];

children.text: na paśau pāriśeṣyeṇa carāveva hi peṣaṇam // MJaiNy_3,3.46 //
children.translated_text: not to the animal [sacrifice]; by elimination (<s>pāriśeṣya</s>), the grinding applies exclusively to the <s>caru</s>. // MJaiNy_3,3.46 //
'<s>pauṣṇaṃ śyāmam ālam etānnakāmaḥ</s>' — this is the injunction of the animal [sacrifice].
'<s>paśum ālabhya puroḍāśaṃ nirvapati</s>' — by this injunctive [text], a <s>puroḍāśa</s> is obtained in the <s>Pauṣṇa</s> animal sacrifice.

children.text: tatra- 'yaddevatyaḥ paśustaddevatyaḥ puroḍāśaḥ' iti nyāyena puroḍāśasya pūṣā devatā |
children.translated_text: Therein, by the principle '<s>yad devatyaḥ paśus tad devatyaḥ puroḍāśaḥ</s>' (the <s>puroḍāśa</s> has the same deity as the animal), <s>Pūṣan</s> is the deity of the <s>puroḍāśa</s>.

children.text: tatra pūrvoktaṃ peṣaṇaṃ viṣayīkṛtyocyamānāḥ saṃśayapūrvottarapakṣā vispaṣṭāḥ || MJaiNyC_3,1.45-46 ||
children.translated_text: Therein, taking the grinding mentioned earlier as the subject, the doubt, the prior position, and the final position being stated are clear. || MJaiNyC_3,1.45-46 ||
'<s>pauṣṇaṃ carum anunirvapet</s>' — thus a <s>caru</s> (rice-oblation) is enjoined.
(In the twentieth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the assignment of the <s>Pauṣṇa</s> grinding in a single-deity [sacrifice], <s>sūtras</s> 39–46:)
Because of the connection with one [deity], in a single [deity sacrifice]. / Jaim_3,3.39 /
And because of a conflict of properties (<s>dharma</s>). / Jaim_3,3.40 /

children.text: api vā sadvitīye syād devatānimittatvāt / Jaim_3,3.41 /
children.translated_text: Or rather, it would be in one accompanied by a second [deity], because it is occasioned by the deity. / Jaim_3,3.41 /
And because the mark is observed. / Jaim_3,3.42 /

children.text: vacanāt sarvapeṣaṇaṃ taṃ prati śāstravatvād arthābhāvād vicarāv apeṣaṇaṃ bhavati / Jaim_3,3.43 /
children.translated_text: Because of the statement, all the grinding is for that [deity]; since it has the character of a <s>śāstra</s> (injunction), in the case of absence of purpose, there would be no grinding in a subsidiary [context]. / Jaim_3,3.43 /

children.text: ekasmin vārthadharmatvād aindrāgnav adubhayor na syād acoditatvāt / Jaim_3,3.44 /
children.translated_text: Or in one [deity sacrifice], because the property belongs to the meaning; in the <s>Aindrāgna</s> (relating to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>), it would not apply to both, because it is not enjoined. / Jaim_3,3.44 /
The non-chewing [of <s>Pūṣan</s>'s share] is merely a reason [for grinding]. / Jaim_3,3.45 /
The statement [of the <s>śruti</s>] is supreme. / Jaim_3,3.46 /
START MJaiNy 3,3.47-48
He composes the twentieth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Even in a two-deity [sacrifice], should one grind, or [only] in one with <s>Pūṣan</s> alone as deity?
Even in a two-deity [sacrifice], because <s>Pūṣan</s>, who partakes of ground [offerings], is present, [one should grind]. // MJaiNy_3,3.47 //
The deity, being without fruit [independently], cannot cause the grinding;

children.text: yāgasya tattve bhāgokterna yāgāntaragāmi tat // MJaiNy_3,3.48 //
children.translated_text: when the sacrifice remains the same, the share-holder [deity] does not transfer [the grinding] to another sacrifice. // MJaiNy_3,3.48 //

children.text:
rājasūye śrūyate- 'saumāpauṣṇaṃ caruṃ nirvapati, aindrāpauṣṇaṃ carum' iti |
tatra dvidevake 'pi carau piṣṭabhājaḥ pūṣṇaḥ sattvāttatpeṣaṇaṃ pūṣārthe kartavyam- iti cet |
tatra vaktavyam- kiṃ peṣaṇasya devatā prayojikā, kiṃvā yāgaḥ |
nā'dyaḥ |
yāgamantareṇa kevaladevatā phalajanakatvābhāvena peṣaṇaṃ prayoktuṃ na prabhavati |
pauṣṇasya yāgasya peṣaṇaprayojakatve tu tatpeṣaṇaṃ dvidevake yāgāntare gantuṃ nārhati |
- 'pūṣā prapiṣṭabhāgaḥ' ityatra yāgau na śrutaḥ- iti cet |
maivam |

children.translated_text: Because, by the impossibility of otherwise explaining the word '<s>bhāga</s>' (share), a sacrifice must be postulated.
For the partaking of ground material is not established without deity-status.
And when deity-status is established, since both the material and the deity are obtained, a sacrifice is postulated.

children.text: tasmāt- ekadevakrayāgasya peṣaṇaprayojakatvāt, na dvidevakayāge peṣaṇamasti || MJaiNyC_3,1.47-48 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the single-deity sacrifice is what causes the grinding, there is no grinding in a two-deity sacrifice. || MJaiNyC_3,1.47-48 ||

In the <s>Rājasūya</s>, it is heard: '<s>saumāpauṣṇaṃ caruṃ nirvapati, aindrāpauṣṇaṃ carum</s>' (he offers a <s>caru</s> to <s>Soma</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s>, a <s>caru</s> to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s>). Therein, even in a two-deity <s>caru</s>, since <s>Pūṣan</s>, who partakes of ground [offerings], is present, the grinding should be performed for the purpose of <s>Pūṣan</s> — if so it is argued, in response we must ask: Is it the deity that causes the grinding, or the sacrifice? Not the first — because the deity alone, without a sacrifice, is incapable of producing fruit and therefore cannot cause the grinding. And if the <s>Pauṣṇa</s> sacrifice is what causes the grinding, then that grinding cannot transfer to another sacrifice with two deities. [If it is argued:] 'In the statement <s>Pūṣā prapiṣṭabhāgaḥ</s> (Pūṣan partakes of ground offerings), no sacrifice is mentioned' — that is not correct.

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīye jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistare tṛtīyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Jaiminīya Nyāyamālā Vistara</s> of the illustrious <s>Mādhava</s>.
Now the fourth <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s>.
(In the first [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>arthavāda</s>-nature of <s>nivīta</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 1–9:)

children.text: nivītām iti manuṣyadharmaḥ śabdasya tatpradhānatvāt / Jaim_3,4.1 /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nivītam</s>' — this is a human custom (<s>manuṣyadharma</s>), because the word primarily denotes that. / Jaim_3,4.1 /
Or it is a description (<s>apadeśa</s>) of a [well-known] thing, because of the existence of its reality. / Jaim_3,4.2 /
But it would be an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>), because of its novelty (<s>apūrvatva</s>). / Jaim_3,4.3 /
That would likely be a property of the rite (<s>karmadharma</s>). / Jaim_3,4.4 /
Because it is a sentence-complement (<s>vākyaśeṣa</s>). / Jaim_3,4.5 /

children.text: tatprakaraṇe yat tat saṃyuktam avipratiṣedhāt / Jaim_3,4.6 /
children.translated_text: That which is connected in that context — [is not contradictory], because of the absence of conflict. / Jaim_3,4.6 /

children.text: tatpradhāne vā tulyavat prasaṃkhyānād itarasya tadarthatvāt / Jaim_3,4.7 /
children.translated_text: Or, when that [context] is primary, by equal enumeration, the other [statement] serves its purpose. / Jaim_3,4.7 /
Or it is an <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage), because of the context. / Jaim_3,4.8 /
And because of forming a single sentence with the injunction. / Jaim_3,4.9 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.1-2
He composes the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the fourth <s>pāda</s> —
Is <s>nivīta</s> an injunction for human beings, or is the expression laudatory (<s>arthavāda</s>)?
Because of novelty (<s>apūrvatva</s>), [it is] an injunction from the context, or [it is] an injunction pertaining to the rite itself. // MJaiNy_3,4.1 //
<s>Nivīta</s> is already obtained among mortals, because it is generally observed in practice;
due to forming a single sentence with the injunction of <s>upavīta</s>, it is an <s>arthavāda</s>. // MJaiNy_3,4.2 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsaprakaraṇe śrūyate-'nivītaṃ manuṣyāṇām |
prācīnāpītaṃ pitṝṇām |
upavītaṃ devānām |
upavyayate devalakṣmameva tatkurute' iti |
tatra- nivītasya pūrve mānāntareṇāprāhatvā- dvidheyatvamabhyupetavyam |
tacca nivītaṃ 'manuṣyāṇām' iti ṣaṣṭhyā puruṣārthatvena vidhīyate- ityekaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ |
asminpakṣe manuṣyasaṃbandho dvividhaḥ- suvarṇadhāraṇavatsarvapuruṣasyabandhaḥ, ityekaḥ prakāraḥ |
'upavītaprācīnāvītayoḥ kratupraveśarahitayoḥ svatantradaivikapaitṛkakarmaṇorapi darśanāttatsāhacaryeṇa svatantra ācāryātithyādimanuṣyaviṣaye karmaṇi nivītam' ityaparaḥ prakāraḥ |
prakaraṇabalātprayājādivadyāgadharṣaḥ- iti dvitīyaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ |
asminpakṣe manuṣyagrahaṇaṃ kartṛsaṃbandhānuvādaḥ |
'ṣaṣṭhīśrutiprakaraṇayoravirodhādubhayāvalambanena kratusaṃbandhimanuṣyadharmaḥ' iti pakṣāntaramudeti |
tacca dvividham-'lohitoṣṇīpādivadṛtvigdharmaḥ, ityekaḥ prakāraḥ |
'kratāveva yanmanuṣyapradhānaṃ karmānvāhāryadānādi, taddharmatve satyupavītasāhacaryamapyanugṛhyate' ityaparaḥ |
sarvathāpi nivītaṃ nārthavādaḥ- iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- atra pratīyamānaṃ nivītādikaṃ vāsoviṣayam, na tu trivṛtsūtraviṣayam |
'ajinaṃ vāso vā dakṣiṇata upavīya' ityanena sadṛśatvāt |
vastrasya ca nivītaṃ saukaryāya prāptam |
cīnāvītopavītayoravaśyamekamekasminpārśve vastramadhaḥ patet |
ataḥ prāpter'the 'manuṣyāṇām' iti ṣaṣṭhīśrutirna vidhāyikā |
na ca prakaraṇātkratvaṅgatvena vidhiḥ |
vākyabhedaprasaṅgāt |
upavītaṃ tāvadvidhīyate |

children.translated_text: because otherwise the praise '<s>devalakṣmam eva tat kurute</s>' (he assumes the very mark of the gods) would be purposeless, leading to the undesirable consequence of futility.

And in the injunction of that <s>upavīta</s>, when it is possible to form a single sentence with <s>nivīta</s> and <s>prācīnāvīta</s> as <s>arthavāda</s>, a separate injunction [for them] is improper.

children.text: navīta prācīnāvīte manuṣyapitṛviṣayavattvāddaivike karmaṇyayogye, upavītaṃ tu yogyam- iti vyatireka- mukheṇa stāvakaṃ nivītam |
children.translated_text: Since <s>nivīta</s> and <s>prācīnāvīta</s> — being applicable to the human and ancestral domains respectively — are unsuitable for divine rites, while <s>upavīta</s> is suitable, the <s>nivīta</s> [passage], by way of [showing] the distinction, is laudatory.
Therefore, it is an <s>arthavāda</s>. || MJaiNyC_3,1.1-2 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context, it is heard: '<s>nivītaṃ manuṣyāṇām | prācīnāvītaṃ pitṝṇām | upavītaṃ devānām | upavyayate devalakṣmam eva tat kurute</s>' (the <s>nivīta</s> [wearing of the sacred thread around the neck] is for humans; the <s>prācīnāvīta</s> [wearing over the right shoulder] is for the ancestors; the <s>upavīta</s> [wearing over the left shoulder] is for the gods; by wearing the <s>upavīta</s>, one assumes the mark of the gods). Therein — since the <s>nivīta</s> is not previously known through another means of knowledge, its injunctive nature must be accepted. And this <s>nivīta</s> is enjoined by the genitive '<s>manuṣyāṇām</s>' as serving a human purpose — this is the first <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prior position). In this position, the connection with humans is of two kinds: first, it is a connection applicable to all persons, like wearing gold; second, 'since <s>upavīta</s> and <s>prācīnāvīta</s>, being excluded from non-ritual contexts, are observed in independent divine and ancestral rites, by association with them, the <s>nivīta</s> is for independent human-related rites such as serving the teacher and guests' — this is the other kind. By the force of context, like the <s>prayājas</s> (preliminary offerings), it is a property of the sacrifice — this is the second <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>. In this position, the mention of '<s>manuṣya</s>' is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) of the connection with the agent. 'Since there is no conflict between the genitive <s>śruti</s> and the context, relying on both, it is a human property connected with the sacrifice' — thus another position arises. And this is of two kinds: 'like the <s>lohitoṣṇīṣa</s> (red turban) and the like, it is a property of the officiating priest' — this is one kind. 'When the human-oriented rite within the sacrifice — such as the <s>anvāhārya</s> (supplementary offering) and gifts — is its domain, then the association with <s>upavīta</s> is also supported' — this is the other kind. In any case, <s>nivīta</s> is not an <s>arthavāda</s> — having arrived at this position, we say: What is understood here — <s>nivīta</s> and the like — pertains to the garment (<s>vāsas</s>), not to the triple-stranded cord (<s>trivṛt-sūtra</s>). Because of the similarity with '<s>ajinaṃ vāso vā dakṣiṇata upavīya</s>' (wearing a hide or garment on the right side). And the <s>nivīta</s> wearing of the garment is already obtained for the sake of convenience. For in the <s>prācīnāvīta</s> and <s>upavīta</s> [modes], inevitably one side of the garment hangs down on one flank. Therefore, since [<s>nivīta</s>] is already obtained, the genitive <s>śruti</s> '<s>manuṣyāṇām</s>' is not injunctive. Nor is there an injunction by the context as an accessory of the sacrifice — because that would entail a break in the sentence-unity. As for <s>upavīta</s>, that is indeed enjoined —
(In the second [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the accessory-nature of <s>upavīta</s> to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 10–11:)
<s>Upavīta</s>, because of the observation of the mark (<s>liṅga</s>), would be a universal property (<s>sarvadharma</s>). / Jaim_3,4.10 /

children.text: na vā prakaraṇāt tasya darśanam / Jaim_3,4.11 /
children.translated_text: Or not — because of the context, the observation [of the mark] pertains to that [context alone]. / Jaim_3,4.11 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.3-4
He composes the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is '<s>upavyayate</s>' (he wears the <s>upavīta</s>) for all purposes, or for the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> alone?
It would be for all purposes — even in the <s>Agnihotra</s>, because of the mark [stating] '<s>upavītī</s>' (wearing the <s>upavīta</s>). // MJaiNy_3,4.3 //
It is for the <s>Darśa</s> (new-moon) and other purposes, from the context; the mark would have a different explanation;
this [mark] is recited in praise of the milking of the <s>Agnihotra</s> for the deceased. // MJaiNy_3,4.4 //

children.text:
'yajñopavītī hi devebhyo dohayati' ityevamagnihotre yajñopavītasya siddhavadanuvādena liṅgena sarvakarmārthamupavītam- iti cet |
na |

children.translated_text: Because the mark can be explained otherwise.
The <s>Agnihotra</s> for the deceased (<s>mṛtāgnihotra</s>) — on that day, the milking is done by another person.

children.text: tatra 'prācīnāvītī dohayet' iti vidhāya tasya stutaye 'yajñepavītī'- ityādyanūditam |
children.translated_text: There, having enjoined '<s>prācīnāvītī dohayet</s>' (he should milk wearing the <s>prācīnāvīta</s>), for the praise of that [injunction], '<s>yajñopavītī</s>' and so on is restated.
Therefore, since overriding by a mere semblance of a mark (<s>liṅgābhāsa</s>) is impossible, from the context, <s>upavīta</s> is an accessory of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. || MJaiNyC_3,1.3-4 ||

'<s>Yajñopavītī hi devebhyo dohayati</s>' (for he milks for the gods wearing the <s>yajñopavīta</s>) — by this mark in the <s>Agnihotra</s>, the <s>upavīta</s> being restated as already established, it would serve all rites — if so it is argued, no.
(In the third [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the injunctive nature of <s>upavīta</s>, the <s>sūtra</s>:)
Or it would be an injunction, because of novelty (<s>apūrvatva</s>). / Jaim_3,4.12 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.5
He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In the wearing of the <s>upavīta</s> — is it a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) or an injunction? The first [alternative holds] because it is known from <s>Smṛti</s>;
but no — because of novelty, it is enjoined for the sacrifice by the optative (<s>leṭ</s>) [verbal ending]. // MJaiNy_3,4.5 //

children.text: 'nityodakī nityayajñopavītī' iti smṛtyā prāptasya 'upadhyayate' ityavamanuvādaḥ- iti cat |
children.translated_text: '<s>Nityodakī nityayajñopavītī</s>' (one should always have water and always wear the sacred thread) — by this <s>Smṛti</s>, since [<s>upavīta</s>] is already obtained, '<s>upavyayate</s>' is merely a restatement — if so it is argued,
that is not correct.

children.text: puruṣārthasya prāptāvapi kratvarthasya prāptyabhāvātpañcamalakāreṇa darśapūrṇamāsāṅgatayā vidhīyate || MJaiNyC_3,1.5 ||
children.translated_text: Even though [<s>upavīta</s>] is obtained as a personal duty (<s>puruṣārtha</s>), since it is not obtained as a duty of the sacrifice (<s>kratvārtha</s>), it is enjoined by the optative ending (<s>pañcama-lakāra</s>) as an accessory of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. || MJaiNyC_3,1.5 ||
(In the fourth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>anuvāda</s>-nature of <s>upavīta</s> and northward-pointing, <s>sūtras</s> 13–14:)
And the northward-pointing [of the <s>darbha</s> grass is also an injunction], because of novelty. / Jaim_3,4.13 /
Or the observation [of the mark] pertains to what already exists. / Jaim_3,4.14 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.6-7
He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: upavītī hi devebhyaḥ purodañco dvayaṃ vidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He [milks] wearing the <s>upavīta</s> for the gods, and the <s>darbhas</s> [are placed] facing forward' — are both injunctions,
or restatements? Since they are not otherwise obtained, what is novel is being enjoined. // MJaiNy_3,4.6 //
From the two words '<s>hi</s>' and '<s>yat</s>', they are restatements; from the <s>Smṛti</s>-based wearing of <s>upavīta</s>, both
are already obtained; [and the statements about] southward-pointing [of <s>darbhas</s>] and <s>prācīnāvīta</s> are praise [of those enjoined practices]. // MJaiNy_3,4.7 //

children.text:
pretāgnihotre śrūyate- 'prācīnāvītī dohayedyajñopavītī hi devebhyo dohayati' iti |
'ye purodañco darbhāḥ, tāndakṣiṇāgrānstṛṇīyāt' iti |
tatra- mṛtasyāgnihotre dohane prācīnāvītam, darbhāstaraṇe dakṣiṇāgratvaṃ ca yathā vidhīyate, tathā maraṇātpūrve jīvato 'gnihotre dohanāṅgamupavītam, darbhāstaraṇāṅgamuttarāgratvaṃ vidhātavyam |
'deṣebhyo yajñopavītī dohayet' 'maraṇātpurā ye darbhāsta udañcaḥ kāryāḥ' iti vacanavyaktiḥ |
nahyetadubhayamanyataḥ prāptam |
tasmāt- apūrvārtho vidhīyatām- iti cet |
maivam |
hiśabdena yacchabdena cobhayatrānuvādatvapratīteḥ |

children.translated_text: And there is indeed a [prior] obtaining of both.

children.text: 'agravantyudagagrāṇi'- iti smṛtyā sarvasmindaivike karmaṇi prāptamuttarāgratvamanūdya vidheyaṃ dakṣiṇāgratvaṃ stūyate |
children.translated_text: By the <s>Smṛti</s> '<s>agravanty udagagrāṇi</s>' (the tips [of the <s>darbhas</s>] should face north), the northward-pointing, which is already obtained for all divine rites, is restated, and the enjoined southward-pointing is praised [by contrast].

children.text: tathā- darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ 'upavyayate' ityanena vidhinā prāptaṃ daivikamupavītamanūdya vidheyaṃ prācīnāvītaṃ stūyate |
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, by the injunction '<s>upavyayate</s>', the divine <s>upavīta</s> — which is already obtained — is restated, and the enjoined <s>prācīnāvīta</s> is praised [by contrast].
Therefore, they are restatements (<s>anuvāda</s>). || MJaiNyC_3,1.67 ||

In the <s>Agnihotra</s> for the deceased (<s>pretāgnihotra</s>), it is heard: '<s>prācīnāvītī dohayed yajñopavītī hi devebhyo dohayati</s>' (he should milk wearing the <s>prācīnāvīta</s>; for, wearing the <s>yajñopavīta</s>, he milks for the gods). And: '<s>ye purodañco darbhāḥ, tān dakṣiṇāgrān stṛṇīyāt</s>' (the <s>darbha</s> grasses that [normally] face forward — one should spread them with tips pointing south). Therein — just as in the <s>Agnihotra</s> for the deceased, the <s>prācīnāvīta</s> for milking and the southward-pointing of the <s>darbhas</s> for spreading are enjoined, so too, in the <s>Agnihotra</s> for the living, the <s>upavīta</s> as an accessory of milking and the northward-pointing as an accessory of <s>darbha</s>-spreading should be enjoined. The expression of the statement would be: 'he should milk for the gods wearing the <s>yajñopavīta</s>' and 'the <s>darbhas</s> before death should be placed facing north.' For neither of these two is obtained from any other source. Therefore, let them be enjoined as conveying something novel — if so it is argued, that is not correct. Because from the words '<s>hi</s>' (for) and '<s>yat</s>' (that which), in both cases, the sense of restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) is understood.
(In the fifth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the injunctive nature of holding the fuel-stick [upward], the <s>sūtra</s>:)
But the holding [of the fuel-stick upward] is an injunction, because of novelty. / Jaim_3,4.15 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.8-9
He composes the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'He holds [the fuel-stick] above, for [he holds it thus] for the gods' — is this praise (<s>saṃstava</s>),

children.text: vidhirvā'dyo dhṛteḥ pitrye proktāyāḥ pūrvavatstutiḥ // MJaiNy_3,4.8 //
children.translated_text: or is it an injunction? The first [alternative]: since the holding [is already stated] in the ancestral [rite], as before, it is praise. // MJaiNy_3,4.8 //
The upward holding of the fuel-stick is already obtained; it is not obtained from any other source;
therefore, by setting aside the word '<s>hi</s>', what is novel is being enjoined. // MJaiNy_3,4.9 //

children.text:
pretāgnihotra evaṃ śrūyate-'adhastātsamidhaṃ dhārayannanudravet, upari hi devebhyo dhārayati' iti |
atra- 'pitryaṃ havirhotuṃ haste dhārayanyadā mantraṃ paṭhati, tadānīṃ strugdaṇḍasyādhastātsamidhaṃ dhārayet- iti yadvidhīyate, tadetaddaivikenoparidhāraṇena stūyate |

children.translated_text: Because, from the word '<s>hi</s>', the sense of restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) is understood, just as in the preceding <s>adhikaraṇa</s> — if so it is argued,
that is not correct.
Because in the divine oblation, the holding of the fuel-stick above the ladle-handle must be enjoined as conveying something novel.
The word '<s>hi</s>', which would indicate restatement, being inapplicable [here], should be disregarded. || MJaiNyC_3,1.8-9 ||

In the <s>Agnihotra</s> for the deceased (<s>pretāgnihotra</s>), it is thus heard: '<s>adhastāt samidhaṃ dhārayan anudravet, upari hi devebhyo dhārayati</s>' (holding the fuel-stick below, one should run after [the fire]; for, he holds it above for the gods). Herein — 'when, while holding in the hand the ancestral oblation to be offered, one recites the <s>mantra</s>, at that time one should hold the fuel-stick below the ladle-handle' — what is thus enjoined is praised by [the contrast with] the upward holding for divine [rites].
(In the sixth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>arthavāda</s>-nature of the directional division, the <s>sūtra</s>:)
And the directional division is likewise, because the connection serves as a reason for the meaning. / Jaim_3,4.16 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.10-11
He composes the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'Humans divided the western direction' — is this an injunction,
Or, the ancient precedent (<s>purākalpa</s>) here is laudatory (<s>stutyartha</s>) and merits an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>). // MJaiNy_3,4.10 //
From the Vedic statement about the <s>prācīnavaṃśa</s> (eastward-beamed [shed]), since [the passage about] the directions forms a single sentence with the injunction,
this division of directions is a laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>), like [the case of] the sacred thread (<s>upavīta</s>) [and] the <s>nivīta</s> [mode of wearing it]. // MJaiNy_3,4.11 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate-'prācīnavaṃśaṃ karoti |
devamanuṣyā diśo vyabhajantaprācīṃ devāḥ, dakṣiṇāṃ pitaraḥ, pratīcīṃ manuṣyāḥ, udīcīṃ rudrāḥ, yatprācīnavaṃśaṃ karoti devalokameva tadyajamāna upāvartate' iti |
tatra- devādīnāṃ karmānadhikārānna tatra vidhiśaṅkā |
'manuṣyāḥ pratīcīṃ vibhajoyuḥ' ityevaṃ vidhiḥ syāt |
kutaḥ |
purākalparūpeṇārthavādena stūyamānatvāt |
pūrvapuruṣācaritatvābhidhānaṃ purākalpaḥ |
'vyabhajanta' ityanena bhūtārthavācinā tadabhidhīyate |

children.translated_text: Therefore — it is an injunction — this is the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view).

children.text: yasya maṇḍapaviśeṣasyoparivaṃśāḥ prāgagrā bhavanti sa prācīnavaṃśaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>prācīnavaṃśa</s> is a particular type of pavilion (<s>maṇḍapa</s>) whose upper beams (<s>vaṃśas</s>) have their tips pointing eastward.
Since [the direction passage] is understood to form a single sentence with the injunction of that [<s>prācīnavaṃśa</s>], it is a laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>).
In the evening <s>Āptyā</s> [rite] and the like, the western [direction] is obtained. || MJaiNyC_3,4.10-11 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, it is heard: 'He makes [the shed] with eastward beams (<s>prācīnavaṃśa</s>). The gods and men divided the directions — the east [belonged to] the gods, the south to the ancestors (<s>pitṛs</s>), the west to men, the north to the <s>Rudras</s>. That he makes [the shed] with eastward beams — thereby the sacrificer turns toward the world of the gods.' Therein — since gods and others are not eligible for ritual action, there is no suspicion of an injunction regarding them. [But one might think:] 'Men should divide the west' — thus there would be an injunction. Why? Because [the passage] is praised through a laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>) in the form of an ancient precedent (<s>purākalpa</s>). The narration of what was done by ancient people is a <s>purākalpa</s>. That is expressed by the past-tense word '<s>vyabhajanta</s>' (they divided).
(In the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the restatement-nature of [passages about] the cut [<s>barhis</s>], the full [vessel], and the like, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
In [the text about] the joint (<s>paruṣi</s>), the cut (<s>dita</s>), the full (<s>pūrṇa</s>), the ghee (<s>ghṛta</s>), and the well-cooked (<s>vidagdha</s>) — likewise. / Jaim_3,4.17 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.12-13
He composes the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In [the text about] the joint (<s>paruṣi</s>), by the statement 'that which is cut (<s>chinna</s>),' [it praises] the [pulling of] the sacred grass (<s>barhis</s>) with roots;

children.text: ghṛtaṃ daivaṃ mastu pitryamityuktyā navanītakam // MJaiNy_3,4.12 //
children.translated_text: by the statement 'ghee is divine, <s>mastu</s> (whey) belongs to the ancestors,' [it praises] fresh butter (<s>navanīta</s>). // MJaiNy_3,4.12 //

children.text: yo vidagdhaḥ sa ityuktyā puroḍāśasya pakvatām /
children.translated_text: By the statement 'that which is well-cooked is [for the gods],' [it praises] the proper cooking of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice-cake);

children.text: stauti pūrvottarau pakṣau yojanīyau nivītavat // MJaiNy_3,4.13 //
children.translated_text: the former and latter views should be construed like [the case of] the <s>nivīta</s> [mode]. // MJaiNy_3,4.13 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ piṇḍapitṛyajñe śrūyate- 'yatparuṣi ditaṃ taddevānām, yadantarā tanmanuṣyāṇām, yatsamūlaṃ tatpitṝṇām, samūlaṃ barhirbhavati vyāvṛtyai' iti |
paruḥ parva |
ditaṃ khaṇḍitam |
tathā jyotiṣṭome dīkṣārthābhyaṅge śrūyate- 'ghṛtaṃ devānāṃ, mastu pitṝṇām, niṣpakvaṃ manuṣyāṇām, tadvā etatsarvadevatyaṃ yannavanītam, yannavanītanābhyaṅkte sarvā eva devatāḥ prīṇāti' iti |
mastu dadhibhavaṃ maṇḍam |
niṣpakvaṃ śirasiprakṣeptumīṣadvilīnaṃ navanītaṃ takraṃ vā |
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ puroḍāśaśrapaṇe śrūyate-"yo vidagdhaḥ sa naiṛtaḥ, yo 'śṛtaḥ sa raudraḥ, yaḥ śataḥ sa daivaḥ, tasmādavidahatā śrapayitavyaḥ sa daivatvāya'' iti |
vidagdho 'tyantapakvaḥ |
aśṛto 'pakvaḥ |
tatra - varhiṣi samūlacchedasya, abhyaṅge navanītasya puroḍāśe yathocitapākasya ca vidheyatayā sarvamavaśiṣṭaṃ stāvakam |
nivītavicārasyaivāyaṃ prapañcaḥ |
evam 'yatpūrṇe tanmanuṣyāṇām' ityatrāpi draṣṭavyam |
tacca cāturmāsyeṣu mahāpitṛyajñe 'pitṛbhyo 'gniṣvāttebhyo 'bhivānyā gordugdhe mantham'ityatra vatsarahitāyā abhidānīśabdābhidheyāyā dhenvā dugdhe piṣṭaṃ prakṣipya kriyamāṇe manthane śrūyate- 'yatpūrṇe tanmanuṣyāṇāmupari, ardho devānām , ardhaḥ pitṛṇāma, ardha upamanthati, artho hi pitṝṇām' iti |
tatra pātrasyādhobhāgarūpeṇār dhena parimite dugdhe manthanasya kartavyatvātsor'dho vidhīyate |
sa ca pūrṇādivākyena stūyate || MJaiNyC_3,4.12 || 13 ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>Piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> (ancestral oblation) of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices), it is heard: 'That which [is cut] at the joint (<s>paruṣi</s>) belongs to the gods; that which [is cut] in between belongs to men; that which [is pulled] with roots belongs to the ancestors (<s>pitṛs</s>). The sacred grass (<s>barhis</s>) is [pulled] with roots, for the sake of distinction.' <s>Paru</s> means a joint. <s>Dita</s> means cut. Similarly, in the anointing for the purpose of consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, it is heard: 'Ghee belongs to the gods, <s>mastu</s> (whey) to the ancestors, the uncooked to men. That which is fresh butter (<s>navanīta</s>) belongs to all deities. When one anoints with fresh butter, one pleases all the deities.' <s>Mastu</s> is the thin liquid from curd. The uncooked (<s>niṣpakva</s>) is fresh butter or buttermilk slightly melted for pouring on the head. In the cooking of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice-cake) in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, it is heard: 'That which is over-cooked belongs to <s>Nirṛti</s>; that which is uncooked belongs to <s>Rudra</s>; that which is [properly] cooked belongs to the gods. Therefore, one should cook it without burning — for the sake of divine status.' <s>Vidagdha</s> means excessively cooked. <s>Aśṛta</s> means uncooked. Therein — since the pulling of the <s>barhis</s> with roots, the use of fresh butter for anointing, and the proper cooking of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> are the things to be enjoined, all the rest is laudatory (<s>stāvaka</s>). This is merely an elaboration of the same <s>nivīta</s> discussion. Similarly, in '<s>yatpūrṇe tanmanuṣyāṇām</s>' (that which is in the full [vessel] belongs to men), the same should be understood. And that [passage] is heard in the <s>Mahāpitṛyajña</s> (great ancestral sacrifice) among the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (four-monthly) rites, in connection with '<s>pitṛbhyo'gniṣvāttebhyo'bhivānyā gordugdhe mantham</s>' (he prepares a <s>mantha</s> [barley drink] with milk from a cow that has lost its calf, for the fire-consuming ancestors): 'That which is in the full [vessel] belongs to men above; the half belongs to the gods; the half to the ancestors. He churns with a half, for a half [portion] indeed belongs to the ancestors.' Therein, since the churning is to be done with [only] half the milk measured as the lower portion of the vessel, the half-[portion] is enjoined. And that is praised by the sentence about the full [vessel] and so forth. || MJaiNyC_3,4.12 || 13 ||
(In the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the prohibition of speaking untruth is a property of the sacrifice (<s>kratu</s>), the <s>sūtras</s> are:)

children.text: akarma kratusaṃyuktaṃ saṃyogān nityānuvādaḥ syāt / Jaim_3,4.18 /
children.translated_text: Not being a [specific] action, [the prohibition] being connected with the sacrifice — because of [its] connection, it would be a restatement of what is already established (<s>anuvāda</s>). / Jaim_3,4.18 /
Or, it is an injunction, because of a different connection. / Jaim_3,4.19 /

START MJaiNy 3,4.14-16
He composes the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The [prohibition] 'one should not speak untruth' — is it an injunction, or a restatement as a person's duty (<s>puṃdharma</s>)?

children.text: sakratau puṃsi śuddhevā kratau yadvā vidhiḥ kratau // MJaiNy_3,4.14 //
children.translated_text: Is it a person's duty in the context of the sacrifice, or is [it] a duty of the sacrifice itself? Or is the injunction in [relation to] the sacrifice? // MJaiNy_3,4.14 //
Since untruth-speaking pertains to the person's purpose, its prohibition is likewise [person-related];

the <s>smārta</s> (traditional) [prohibition] is a restatement, since [it applies to] both person and sacrifice, due to the absence of [separate] Vedic procedure (<s>śruti-prakriyā</s>). // MJaiNy_3,4.15 //
In the verbal form (<s>ākhyāta</s>), the person is not [directly] denoted; [the prohibition] applies to the sacrifice alone, like the <s>prayāja</s> (preliminary offering);
since the connection [here] is different from the <s>smārta</s> truth-speaking rule, [this] is an injunction in [relation to] the sacrifice. // MJaiNy_3,4.16 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsaprakaraṇe śrūyate- 'nānṛtaṃ vadet' iti |
tatra-puruṣadharmatvenāyaṃ pratiṣedho vidhīyate |
kutaḥ |
pratiyogino 'nṛtavadanasya puruṣadharmatayā tanniṣedhasyāpi puruṣadharmatvenaiva vidhātavyatvāt |
'vadet' ityākhyātaṃ tāvatkartṛvācakam |
tenā'khyātena kartṛḥ pratīyamānatvāt |
puruṣasyā'khyātapratyayavācyatve sati prakṛtyarthasya vadanasya puruṣadharmatvaṃ yuktam |
'prakṛtipratyayau pratyayārthe saha brūtaḥ, tayostu pratyayaḥ prādhānyena' iti śābdikairuddhoṣaṇāt |
vadanasya puruṣadharmatve tanniṣedhasyāpi puruṣadharmatvaṃ yuktam |
anyathā bhinnaviṣayatve bādhakatvaṃ na syāt |
tasmātpurūṣavācakākhyātaśrutyā prakaraṇaṃ bādhitvā puruṣārtho 'yaṃ pratiṣedho vidhīyate |
astyeva smārtaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ- iti cet |
tarhi tasyaitacchrutivākyaṃ mūlamastu |
tasmāt- puruṣārthaḥ- ityekaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ |
ākhyātaśruteḥ prakaraṇasya cāvirodhāya kratuyuktapuruṣadharmo 'stu |
nahyetadvākyaṃ smṛtermūlam |
bhinnaviṣayatvāt |
smṛtiścopanayanamārabhyā'maraṇaṃ puruṣasyānṛtaṃ pratiṣedhati |
tanmadhyapatitatvātkratāvapi smārto niṣedhaḥ prāpta eva |
tata ubhayārtho 'pyayaṃ pratiṣedho na vidhīyate, kiṃtvanūdyate- iti dvitīyaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ |
ākhyātena bhāvanābhidhīyate |
kartā tu tadavinābhūtor'thātpratīyate |
ataḥ śrutyabhāvātkevalena prakaraṇena prayājādivadārādupakārakaḥ kratāveva niviśate |
na ca tatrāpi vidhīyate, kiṃtu sārvatrikasya niṣedhasya kratāvapi prāptatvādanūdyate- iti tṛtīyaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ |
'satyameva vadet, natvanṛtam' iti yo 'yaṃ smārtāniyamarūpaḥ puruṣārthaḥ saṃyogaḥ, tasmādayamanyaḥ kratvarthaḥ saṃyogaḥ |
ato 'prāptatvādvidhīyate |
etadvyatikrame kratoreva vaiguṇyam, na tu puruṣasya pratyavāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: When this [rule] is transgressed, there is a deficiency of the sacrifice alone, not a fault (<s>pratyavāya</s>) of the person.
Therefore, the expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) here pertains to the sacrifice.

children.text: puruṣārthaniyamātikrame tu puruṣasyaiva pratyavāyo na kratorvaiguṇyam |
children.translated_text: But when the person-related rule is transgressed, the fault is the person's alone, not a deficiency of the sacrifice.

children.text: tatra smārte prāyaścitam- iti viśeṣaḥ || MJaiNyC_3,4.14-16 ||
children.translated_text: In that case, the expiation follows the <s>smārta</s> [tradition] — this is the distinction. || MJaiNyC_3,4.14-16 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context, it is heard: '<s>nānṛtaṃ vadet</s>' (one should not speak untruth). Therein — this prohibition is enjoined as a person's duty (<s>puruṣadharma</s>). Why? Because, since the counter-correlate — speaking untruth — is a person's property, its prohibition too must be enjoined as a person's property. The verbal ending (<s>ākhyāta</s>) '<s>vadet</s>' (one should speak) denotes the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>). Because the agent is understood through that verbal ending. When the person is denoted by the verbal suffix, it is fitting that the speaking — the meaning of the verbal base (<s>prakṛti</s>) — is a person's duty. As the grammarians declare: 'The base and the suffix together denote the meaning of the suffix; but between them, the suffix has predominance.' When speaking is a person's duty, it is fitting that its prohibition too is a person's duty. Otherwise, if they had different domains, there would be no overriding capacity. Therefore, by the Vedic statement (<s>śruti</s>) in the form of the person-denoting verbal ending, overriding the context, this prohibition is enjoined as person-related. [Objection:] There already exists a <s>smārta</s> (traditional) prohibition — if so, then let this Vedic sentence be its source. Therefore — it is person-related — this is the first <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>. To reconcile the verbal-ending <s>śruti</s> and the context without conflict, let it be a duty of a person engaged in the sacrifice. For this sentence is not the source of the <s>smṛti</s> [prohibition]. Because they have different domains. The <s>smṛti</s> prohibits untruth for a person from the investiture (<s>upanayana</s>) until death. Since [the sacrificial prohibition] falls within that [period], the <s>smārta</s> prohibition is already applicable in the sacrifice as well. Therefore, this prohibition, whether person-related or sacrifice-related, is not [newly] enjoined, but merely restated (<s>anūdyate</s>) — this is the second <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>. The verbal form (<s>ākhyāta</s>) denotes the productive activity (<s>bhāvanā</s>). But the agent is understood from the meaning, as inseparable from it. Therefore, in the absence of [direct] Vedic statement (<s>śruti</s>), by the context alone, like the <s>prayāja</s> (preliminary offering) which indirectly assists, [the prohibition] is situated in the sacrifice alone. And even there it is not [newly] enjoined, but since the universal prohibition is already applicable in the sacrifice too, it is merely restated — this is the third <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>. The <s>smārta</s> connection, which is person-related in the form of the rule 'one should speak only truth, not untruth' — this connection [here] is different from that, being sacrifice-related. Therefore, since it is not already established, it is [newly] enjoined.
(In the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the assignment of the duties of one who is yawning (<s>jañjabhyamāna</s>) in the context, <s>sūtras</s> 20–22)
Like [the case of] the <s>Ahīna</s> [sacrifice], [the duty pertains to] the person, because it serves that [person's] purpose. / Jaim_3,4.20 /

children.text: prakaraṇaviśeṣād vā tadyuktasya saṃskāro dravyavat / Jaim_3,4.21 /
children.translated_text: Or, because of a specific context, it is a consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the one connected with that [sacrifice], like a [ritual] substance. / Jaim_3,4.21 /
It should be withdrawn by virtue of the designation. / Jaim_3,4.22 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.17
He composes the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The <s>mantra</s>-recitation of one who is yawning (<s>jañjabhyamāna</s>) — is it a person's duty or a duty of the sacrifice?
From the sentence, the first; by the ritual procedure (<s>prakriyā</s>), which is not contradicted, the second. // MJaiNy_3,4.17 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsaprakaraṇe śrūyate-'prāṇo vai dakṣaḥ |
apānaḥ kratuḥ |
tasmājjañjanyamāno brūyāt- mayi dakṣakratū-iti, prāṇāpānāvevā'smanyadhatta' iti |
gātravināmena vidāritamukhaḥ puruṣo jañjabhyamānaḥ |
tasya vākyānmantroktiḥ pratīyate |

children.translated_text: And a sentence is stronger than the context.
Therefore — it is solely a person's duty — if so argued,
that is not so.

children.text: kratāvapi jañjabhyamānapuruṣasaṃbhavena vākyaprakaraṇayorvirodhābhāve satyubhābhyāṃ kratuyuktapuruṣasaṃskāratvāvagamāt || MJaiNyC_3,4.17 ||
children.translated_text: Because, since a yawning person can [also] occur within the sacrifice, there being no conflict between the sentence and the context, from both [taken together], it is understood as a consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the person engaged in the sacrifice. || MJaiNyC_3,4.17 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context, it is heard: '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is <s>Dakṣa</s>. <s>Apāna</s> is <s>Kratu</s>. Therefore, one who is yawning should say: "May <s>Dakṣa</s> and <s>Kratu</s> be in me" — thus he establishes <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> in himself.' One who is yawning (<s>jañjabhyamāna</s>) is a person whose mouth is opened wide through contortion of the limbs. From the sentence, the <s>mantra</s>-recitation is understood [as pertaining to him].
And [the rule about] the yoke-pin (<s>śamyā</s>), because of the all-encompassing offering (<s>sarvaparidāna</s>). / Jaim_3,4.23 /
(In the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] despising [a Brahmin] and the like serve the person's purpose, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
START MJaiNy 3,4.18-19
He composes the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The [prohibition] 'one should not despise a Brahmin' — is it sacrifice-related, or person-related?
Like the previous <s>mantra</s> [case], it is sacrifice-related, because of the proximity of the sacrifice that has a result (<s>phala</s>). // MJaiNy_3,4.18 //
The avoidance of torment (<s>yātanā</s>) befits being the fruit of the prohibition;
this being a prohibition, due to its person-relatedness, it should be withdrawn from the [sacrificial] procedure. // MJaiNy_3,4.19 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsaprakaraṇe śrūyate- 'yo brāhmaṇāyāvagurettaṃ śatena yātayet |
tasmādbrāhmaṇāya nāvagureta' iti |
tatra- yathā pūrvādhikaraṇe mantrapāṭhasya phalarahitasya phalavati kratāvaṅgatvaṃ prakaraṇenāvagamyate, evamatrāpi brāhmaṇāvajñāniṣedhasya kratvaṅgatvam- iti cet |
na |
vaiṣamyāt |
pūrvatra hi - ātmani māṇāpānadhāraṇaṃ mantroccāraṇaphalaṃ na saṃbhavati |
children.translated_text: For in the previous case, the fruit of the <s>mantra</s>-recitation — the maintenance of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> in oneself — is not possible [as an independent fruit],
because that [maintenance of breath] is already accomplished [naturally].
But here, since the [text] mentions torment for a hundred years as [the consequence of] despising, the avoidance of torment is appropriate as the fruit of the prohibition.

children.text: tasmāt- niṣedhasya kevalapuruṣārthatayā prakaraṇā dutkarṣo yuktaḥ || MJaiNyC_3,4.18-19 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the prohibition is purely person-related, its withdrawal from the context is justified. || MJaiNyC_3,4.18-19 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context, it is heard: 'He who despises (<s>avaguret</s>) a Brahmin — him he should torment for a hundred [years]. Therefore, one should not despise a Brahmin.' Therein — just as in the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the <s>mantra</s>-recitation — which is devoid of [independent] fruit — is understood from the context as an accessory of the sacrifice that has fruit, similarly here too, the prohibition of despising a Brahmin would be an accessory of the sacrifice — if so argued, no. Because of the dissimilarity.
(In the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the prohibition of conversing with one wearing soiled garments, <s>sūtras</s> 24–25)
Before the conclusion (<s>aparodha</s>), [the prohibition concerns] one with soiled garments (<s>malavadvāsas</s>). / Jaim_3,4.24 /
And because of the prohibition regarding food. / Jaim_3,4.25 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.20
He composes the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'One should not converse with one wearing soiled garments (<s>malavadvāsas</s>)' — this too, as before,
would be person-related, because conversing [with such a person] has no relevance anywhere in the sacrifice. // MJaiNy_3,4.20 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsaprakaraṇe śrūyate- 'malavadvāsattā na saṃvedata' iti |
-asya niṣedhasya prakaraṇā tkratvaṅgatvam- iti cet |

children.translated_text: that is not so.
Because there would be the fallacy of prohibiting what is [already] inapplicable.

children.text: yasya vratye 'hani patnvanālambhukā bhavati, tāmaparudhya yajeta' iti rajasvalāyā niḥsāraṇena kratau tatsaṃvādasyāprasaktiḥ |
children.translated_text: When the wife becomes impure (<s>anālambhukā</s>) on the day of the observance (<s>vratya</s>), one should sacrifice after removing her — thus, by the exclusion of the menstruating woman, conversing with her has no relevance in the sacrifice.
Therefore, this being purely person-related, its withdrawal from the context [is justified]. || MJaiNyC_3,4.20 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context, it is heard: 'One wearing soiled garments — one should not converse with [such a person].' — This prohibition, from the context, would be an accessory of the sacrifice — if so argued,
(In the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] wearing gold and the like are person-related duties, <s>sūtras</s> 26–30)

children.text: aprakaraṇe tu taddharmas tato viśeṣāt / Jaim_3,4.26 /
children.translated_text: But when there is no [specific] context, [the rule] has the property of that [sacrifice], because of the specification from that [context]. / Jaim_3,4.26 /
But since it is not a [ritual] substance, it would be a subsidiary (<s>śeṣa</s>). / Jaim_3,4.27 /
Because of connection with the Veda. / Jaim_3,4.28 /
And because of connection with the [ritual] substance. / Jaim_3,4.29 /

children.text: syād vāsya saṃyogavat phalena saṃbandhas tasmāt karmaitiśāyanaḥ / Jaim_3,4.30 /
children.translated_text: Or, like [the case of] connection, its relation with the fruit [is possible] — therefore it is [related to] the rite — [this is the view of] <s>Aitiśāyana</s>. / Jaim_3,4.30 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.21-23
He composes the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the wearing of gold an accessory of the sacrifice like [wearing] colored [garments] by the wife, or
is the consecration (<s>saṃskṛti</s>) of the gold [the relevant point] here, or the color, or is it person-related? // MJaiNy_3,4.21 //
Since it is Vedic, from the [sacrifice-]context, it would be an accessory of the rite with respect to the agent (<s>karmakāraka</s>);
since the consecration and the color are predominant, let the [other aspect] be a secondary attribute, for the sake of economy of injunctions (<s>vidhilāghava</s>). // MJaiNy_3,4.22 //
Since [it is] heard without being inaugurated [by a specific context], the connection with the sacrifice is not fixed;

children.text: ataḥ pumarthatā svargaḥ kalpyo 'nyadvāstu rātrivat // MJaiNy_3,4.23 //
children.translated_text: therefore, it is person-related; heaven (<s>svarga</s>) should be postulated [as its fruit]; or let it be otherwise, like [the case of the] night [ritual]. // MJaiNy_3,4.23 //

children.text:
anārabhya śrūyate- 'tasmātsuvarṇe hiraṇyaṃ bhāryam |
suvarṇa eva bhavati |
duvarṇo 'sya bhrātṛvyo bhavati' iti |
tatra-yadetacchobhanavarṇopetahiraṇyadhāraṇaṃ tasya vaidikakriyārūpatvena kratusmārakatvātkratvaṅgaṃ dhāraṇam- ityekaḥ pakṣaḥ |
kratvaṅgatve 'pi nā'rādupakārakam, kiṃtu kratṛgataṃ hiraṇyaṃ dhāraṇena saṃskriyate |
'bhāryam' ityatra ṇyatpratyayasya karmaṇi vihitatvena karmakārakasya hiraṇyasya prādhānyāvagamāt - iti dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ |
varṇaviśiṣṭadhāraṇavidhāne gauravāddhāraṇasahitaṃ hiraṇyamanūdya śobhanavarṇamātraṃ vidheyam- iti tṛtīyaḥ pakṣaḥ |
tredhāpi- kratvartho vidhiḥ, na tu puruṣārthaḥ- iti prāpte-
brūmaḥ- yaddhikratuprakaraṇe śrutam, tasyāsti niyamena kratusmārakatvam |
idaṃ tvanārabhyādhītam |
na cātra hiraṇyaṃ juhvādivatkratāvavyabhicaritam, yena kratusmṛtirniyamyeta |
nanu saṃskāryatvānyathānupapattyā kratupraveśaḥ syāt |
nahi dhāraṇena saṃskṛtasya hiraṇyasya laukikaḥ kaścidupayogo 'sti- iti cet |
na |
kratāvapyupayogābhāvāt |
- kratūpayogo 'pi kalpyate- iti cet |
na |
'kratūpayogitvena saṃskāryatvam, tena ca kratūpayogaḥ' ityanyonyāśrayatvāt |
ataḥ kratau niyantumaśakyatvātpuruṣārthamidaṃ dhāraṇam |

children.translated_text: Nor is there an absence of fruit here,
because by the principle of the <s>Viśvajit</s> [sacrifice], heaven (<s>svarga</s>) can be postulated [as the fruit].

children.text: athavā rātrisanne yathā vākyaśeṣeṇārthavādena śrutā pratiṣṭhā kalatvena kalpitā tathātrāpi 'suvarṇa eva bhavati, durrvaṇo 'sya bhrātṛvyaḥ' ityarthavādagataṃ phalamastu |
children.translated_text: Alternatively, just as in the <s>Rātrisanna</s> [rite], the <s>pratiṣṭhā</s> (firm standing) heard through the sentence-complement in the <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage) is postulated as the fruit, so here too let the fruit stated in the <s>arthavāda</s> — '<s>suvarṇa eva bhavati, durvarṇo 'sya bhrātṛvyaḥ</s>' (one becomes of good color, his rival becomes of bad color) — stand as the fruit.
Therefore — the injunction of wearing [gold] serves the individual's purpose. || MJaiNyC_3,4.21-23 ||

It is heard without being initiated [into any particular rite]: '<s>tasmātsuvarṇe hiraṇyaṃ bhāryam</s> | <s>suvarṇa eva bhavati</s> | <s>durvarṇo 'sya bhrātṛvyo bhavati</s>' (Therefore, gold of good color is to be worn. One becomes of good color. His rival becomes of bad color). Therein — one view is that wearing gold possessing beautiful color, being in the form of a Vedic act and hence a reminder of the sacrifice, is an accessory of the sacrifice (<s>kratvāṅga</s>). The second view is that even if it is an accessory of the sacrifice, it does not serve the sacrifice from afar; rather, the gold belonging to the sacrificer is consecrated by the wearing. Because in '<s>bhāryam</s>' (to be worn), the <s>ṇyat</s> suffix being prescribed for the object (<s>karman</s>), the primacy of gold as the object-factor is understood. The third view is that in the injunction of wearing [gold] qualified by [a particular] color, since there is cumbersomeness, the gold together with its wearing is merely restated, and only the beautiful color is what is to be enjoined. In all three views — the injunction serves the sacrifice's purpose, not the individual's purpose — having arrived at this position, we say: What is heard in the context of a sacrifice does necessarily remind one of the sacrifice. But this is recited without being initiated [into a specific rite] (<s>anārabhyādhīta</s>). And here gold is not invariably connected to the sacrifice like the <s>juhū</s> (ladle) and such, by which the remembrance of the sacrifice would be fixed. But — the entry into the sacrifice would follow from the impossibility of explaining the consecration otherwise. For there is no worldly use of gold that has been consecrated by wearing — if so [it is argued], no. Because there is no use even in the sacrifice. [If it is argued:] The use in sacrifice can also be postulated — no. Because there would be mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>): 'being fit for sacrifice is the reason for consecration, and through that comes the use in sacrifice.' Therefore, since [the wearing of gold] cannot be restricted to the sacrifice, this wearing serves the individual's purpose.
(In the thirteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the subsidiarity of the <s>Jaya</s> and other [oblations] to Vedic rites, <s>sūtras</s> 31–33)
The remaining [oblations], being in the [Vedic] context, [serve] all rites without distinction. / Jaim_3,4.31 /
But the oblations are to be distinguished, because of the connection with fire and the <s>Āhavanīya</s>. / Jaim_3,4.32 /
And the remainder [is established] from the designation. / Jaim_3,4.33 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.24-25
He composes the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In whichever rite one desires prosperity, the <s>Jaya</s> oblation serves the totality of purposes therein;
or it is a remainder of all Vedic [rites] alone, because of the absence of a restricting [factor]. // MJaiNy_3,4.24 //

children.text: homa āhavanīye syātkṛṣyādiṣu na so 'sti hi /
children.translated_text: The oblation would be in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire]; but in ploughing and the like, that [fire] does not exist;
therefore, even though recited without being initiated [into a specific rite], these <s>Jaya</s> [oblations] belong to Vedic [rites] alone. // MJaiNy_3,4.25 //

children.text:
anārabhya śrūyate- 'yena karmaṇertset |
tatra jayāṃ juhuyāt |
rāṣṭrabhṛto juhoti |
abhyātānāñjuhoti' iti |
īrtsedṛddhimicchet |
'cittaṃ ca svāhā' ityādayo jayāḥ 'ṛtāṣāḍ' ityādayo rāṣṭrabhṛtaḥ |
'agnirbhūtānām'- ityādayo 'bhyātānāḥ |
tatra- vaidikakarmaṇeva laukikakṛṣyādikarmaṇāpyṛddheriṣyamāṇatvāt, saṃkoce kāraṇāmāvājjayādihomaḥ sarvaśeṣaḥ- iti cet |
children.translated_text: Therein — since prosperity is desired both in Vedic rites and in worldly activities like ploughing, and since there is no reason for restriction, the <s>Jaya</s> and other oblations serve all purposes as a remainder — if so [it is argued],
that is not correct.

children.text: 'yadāhavanīye juhvati tena so 'syābhīṣṭaḥ prītaḥ' iti vākyena homamuddiśyā' havanīyavidhānāt |
children.translated_text: Because the sentence '<s>yadāhavanīye juhvati tena so 'syābhīṣṭaḥ prītaḥ</s>' (when they offer in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, thereby that [deity] of his, being desired, is pleased) enjoins the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire] with reference to the oblation.
Since that [<s>Āhavanīya</s> fire] is absent in ploughing and the like, the <s>Jaya</s> and other oblations belong to Vedic [rites] alone. || MJaiNyC_3,4.24-25 ||

It is heard without being initiated [into any particular rite]: '<s>yena karmaṇertset</s> | <s>tatra jayāṃ juhuyāt</s> | <s>rāṣṭrabhṛto juhoti</s> | <s>abhyātānāñjuhoti</s>' (In whichever rite one desires prosperity, there one should offer the <s>Jaya</s> oblations. One offers the <s>Rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> oblations. One offers the <s>Abhyātāna</s> oblations). '<s>Īrtset</s>' means 'desires prosperity' (<s>ṛddhim icchet</s>). '<s>cittaṃ ca svāhā</s>' and the like are the <s>Jaya</s> [oblations]. '<s>ṛtāṣāḍ</s>' and the like are the <s>Rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> [oblations]. '<s>agnirbhūtānām</s>' and the like are the <s>Abhyātāna</s> [oblations].
(In the fourteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on whether the <s>iṣṭi</s> is to be performed upon the Vedic acceptance of a horse, <s>sūtras</s> 34–35)

children.text: doṣāt tv iṣṭir laukike syāc chāstrād dhi vaidika na doṣaḥ syāt / Jaim_3,4.34 /
children.translated_text: But because of the defect, an <s>iṣṭi</s> would apply to the worldly [gift], for the Vedic [gift], being from scripture, would have no defect. / Jaim_3,4.34 /

children.text: arthavādo vānupapātat tasmād yajñe pratīyeta / Jaim_3,4.35 /
children.translated_text: Or [the scripture] is an <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage), because [the worldly defect] is untenable; therefore, it should be understood as [applying] to the sacrifice. / Jaim_3,4.35 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.26-28
He composes the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The <s>iṣṭi</s> for the acceptance of a horse — it will be stated that '<s>pratigraha</s>' (acceptance) means giving;

children.text: dānadvaye laukike vā vaidike vā bhavediyam // MJaiNy_3,4.26 //
children.translated_text: in which of the two givings — worldly or Vedic — would this [<s>iṣṭi</s>] apply? // MJaiNy_3,4.26 //
Since there is no distinction between the two, either [would apply]; or, since [the <s>Smṛti</s> states] 'one should not give a horse with a mane' (<s>na kesariṇo dadāti</s>),
because of the worldly prohibition, this would be an expiatory rite (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) in that [worldly] context. // MJaiNy_3,4.27 //
The causation of dropsy (<s>jalodara</s>) is not established anywhere in worldly [context];

children.text: vaidike tu śrutaṃ tasmāttatprāyaścittaye 'tra sā // MJaiNy_3,4.28 //
children.translated_text: but in the Vedic [context] it is heard; therefore, this [<s>iṣṭi</s>] is for the expiation of that [defect]. // MJaiNy_3,4.28 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate-'yāvato 'śvānpratigṛhṇīyāttāvato vāruṇāścatuṣkapālānnirvapet' iti |
tatra 'pratigrahaśabdo dānaparaḥ' ityanantarameva vakṣyate |
tatra-viśeṣāśravaṇāllaukikavaidikadānayorubhayo rapyasāviṣṭiḥ- ityekaḥ pakṣaḥ |
'na ketariṇo dadāti' iti smṛtyā mitradāyādādibhyaḥ prītyā kriyamāṇaṃ lokikamaśvadānaṃ niṣiddham |
tadanuṣṭhāne prāyaścittarūpeyāmiṣṭiḥ- iti dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ |
'varuṇo vā etaṃ gṛhṇāti yo 'śvaṃ pratigṛhṇāti' ityaśvadāne jalodakhyādhirūpo dṛṣṭadoṣo varuṇagrahavākyenocyate |
na ca laukikasyāśvadānasya taddhetutvaṃ pramitam |

children.translated_text: But the hearing of the defect pertains to Vedic [giving], concerning a future birth.
Therefore, the <s>iṣṭi</s> with respect to Vedic giving is the expiation.
For there does exist Vedic horse-giving,
because of the hearing '<s>vaḍavā dakṣiṇā</s>' (a mare is the sacrificial fee) and the like. || MJaiNyC_3,4.26-28 ||

This is recited: '<s>yāvato 'śvānpratigṛhṇīyāttāvato vāruṇāścatuṣkapālānnirvapet</s>' (for as many horses as one accepts, one should prepare that many four-kapāla cakes for <s>Varuṇa</s>). Therein, 'the word <s>pratigraha</s> (acceptance) means giving' — this will be stated shortly after. Therein — one view is that since no distinction is heard, this <s>iṣṭi</s> applies to both worldly and Vedic giving. The second view is that the <s>Smṛti</s> '<s>na kesariṇo dadāti</s>' (one should not give a horse with a mane) prohibits the worldly giving of a horse made to friends, heirs, and others out of affection. When that is transgressed, this <s>iṣṭi</s> is in the form of an expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>). [The correct view:] The sentence about <s>Varuṇa</s>'s seizing — '<s>varuṇo vā etaṃ gṛhṇāti yo 'śvaṃ pratigṛhṇāti</s>' (Verily, <s>Varuṇa</s> seizes him who gives a horse) — states the visible defect of dropsy (<s>jalodara</s>) that afflicts [the giver] through <s>Varuṇa</s>'s seizing. And the causation of that [dropsy] by worldly horse-giving is not established [by any evidence].
(In the fifteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on whether the <s>Vāruṇī</s> <s>iṣṭi</s> is for the giver, <s>sūtras</s> 36–37)
And [it is] not enjoined [for the receiver], because of the difference in the rite. / Jaim_3,4.36 /
That [<s>iṣṭi</s>] would be for the officiating priest, by the mark. / Jaim_3,4.37 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.29-30
He composes the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
For as many horses as one accepts, that many <s>iṣṭis</s> [are to be performed];
would this be for the receiver or the giver? Let the first [alternative hold] according to the rule. // MJaiNy_3,4.29 //
From the <s>arthavāda</s> that does not contradict [the established meaning], the <s>iṣṭi</s> is heard as belonging to the giver, <s>Prajāpati</s>;

children.text: iṣṭiḥ śrutā tato dāturṇijarthe 'pi vidhiṃ nayet // MJaiNy_3,4.30 //
children.translated_text: therefore, even though the injunctive word refers to [the receiver], it should be construed as pertaining to the giver. // MJaiNy_3,4.30 //

children.text:
pūrvodāhṛte vākye 'pratigṛhṇīyāt' iti vidhipadaśravaṇātpratigrahīturiṣṭiḥ- iti cet |
na |
upakramarūpeṇārthavādena dātustadiṣṭipratīteḥ |
upakramaścaivaṃ śrūyate- 'prajāpativaruṇāyāśvamanayat, sa svāṃ devatāmārchat |
sa paryadīryata, sa etaṃ vāruṇaṃ catuṣkapālamapaśyat, taṃ niravapat, tato vai sa varuṇapāśādamucyata' iti |

children.translated_text: '<s>Anayat</s>' [means] he gave.

children.text: sa ca dātā prajāpatiḥ svakīyāṃ varuṇadevatāṃ jalodararogapradāṃ prāptavāna |
children.translated_text: And he — the giver <s>Prajāpati</s> — obtained his own deity <s>Varuṇa</s>, who inflicts the disease of dropsy.

children.text: tena ca rogeṇa grastaḥ sa prajāpatirvidīrṇo bhūtvā rogaparihārāyeṣṭiṃ kṛtvā rogādamucyata, ityatra- dāturiṣṭiḥ- ityavagamyate |
children.translated_text: And seized by that disease, <s>Prajāpati</s>, being afflicted, performed the <s>iṣṭi</s> for the removal of the disease and was freed from the disease — from this, it is understood that the <s>iṣṭi</s> belongs to the giver.

In accordance with the introduction that does not contradict [the established meaning], even the non-injunctive word in the injunction should be explained as having the causative meaning implied in '<s>pratigrāhayet</s>' (one should cause to accept). || MJaiNyC_3,4.29-30 ||

In the previously cited sentence, since the injunctive word '<s>pratigṛhṇīyāt</s>' (one should accept) is heard, the <s>iṣṭi</s> would be for the receiver — if so [it is argued], no. Because the <s>arthavāda</s> in the form of the introduction indicates that the <s>iṣṭi</s> belongs to the giver. And the introduction is heard thus: '<s>prajāpativaruṇāyāśvamanayat, sa svāṃ devatāmārchat</s> | <s>sa paryadīryata, sa etaṃ vāruṇaṃ catuṣkapālamapaśyat, taṃ niravapat, tato vai sa varuṇapāśādamucyata</s>' (<s>Prajāpati</s> brought a horse to <s>Varuṇa</s>. He approached his own deity. He was afflicted. He saw this four-<s>kapāla</s> cake for <s>Varuṇa</s>. He prepared it. Thereby he was freed from the noose of <s>Varuṇa</s>).
(In the sixteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the Vedic <s>Soma</s>-drinking mishap, <s>sūtras</s> 38–39)
And the drinking-mishap, similarly. / Jaim_3,4.38 /

children.text: doṣāt tu vaidike syād arthād dhi laukike na doṣaḥ syāt / Jaim_3,4.39 /
children.translated_text: But because of the defect, it would apply to the Vedic [context], for in the worldly [context], being purposeful, there would be no defect. / Jaim_3,4.39 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.31-32
He composes the sixteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The <s>caru</s> (oblation-cake) for one who vomits <s>Soma</s> — in the worldly or the Vedic [context]? The loss of senses;
the visible defect is in the worldly [context]; therefore, the <s>caru</s> is prescribed for [worldly] vomiting. // MJaiNy_3,4.31 //

children.text: adoṣo vamanāyaiva loke pānaṃ śrutau punaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the worldly [context], vomiting itself is without defect; but in the <s>Śruti</s>,
[<s>Soma</s> is drunk] for digestion; therefore, the <s>caru</s> would be for the pacification of the defect of vomiting [the ritually drunk <s>Soma</s>]. // MJaiNy_3,4.32 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate- 'saumendraṃ caruṃ nirvapecchyāmākaṃ somavāminaḥ'' iti |
tatra-laukike somavamane vihito 'yaṃ caruḥ |
kutaḥ |
'vi vā eṣa indriyeṇa vīryeṇa vyṛdhyave yaḥ somaṃ vamati' iti dṛṣṭadoṣamupanyasya tacchāntaye caruvidhānāt - iti cet |

children.translated_text: that is not correct.

children.text: loke dhātusāmyārthino vamanāyaiva somasya pāne sati vamanasya doṣahetusvābhāvāt |
children.translated_text: Because in the worldly [context], when <s>Soma</s> is drunk for the purpose of balancing the bodily humors (<s>dhātusāmya</s>), the vomiting is intentional and not inherently defective.

children.text: vede tu 'hinva me gātrā harivaḥ' ityanena mantreṇa jarayituṃ somaḥ pīyate |
children.translated_text: But in the Vedic [context], <s>Soma</s> is drunk to be digested, with the <s>mantra</s> '<s>hinva me gātrā harivaḥ</s>' (strengthen my limbs, O <s>Hari</s>).
There, this <s>caru</s> serves as expiation for [the mishap of] vomiting. || MJaiNyC_3,4.31-32 ||

This is recited: '<s>saumendraṃ caruṃ nirvapecchyāmākaṃ somavāminaḥ</s>' (one should prepare a <s>Saumendra</s> [i.e., dedicated to <s>Soma</s> and <s>Indra</s>] <s>caru</s> of <s>śyāmāka</s> grain for one who vomits <s>Soma</s>). Therein — this <s>caru</s> is prescribed for worldly <s>Soma</s>-vomiting. Why? Because having presented the visible defect — '<s>vi vā eṣa indriyeṇa vīryeṇa vyṛdhyate yaḥ somaṃ vamati</s>' (he who vomits <s>Soma</s> is verily deprived of sense-faculty and vigor) — the <s>caru</s> is prescribed for its pacification — if so [it is argued],
(In the seventeenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on whether the <s>Saumendra</s> <s>caru</s> pertains to the drinking-mishap of the sacrificer, <s>sūtras</s> 40–42)
That [applies] everywhere, without distinction. / Jaim_3,4.40 /
Or [it applies] to the patron (<s>svāmin</s>), because it serves his purpose. / Jaim_3,4.41 /
And because of the evidence of the mark. / Jaim_3,4.42 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.33
He composes the seventeenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Even when the priests vomit, [does] this [<s>caru</s> apply], or only for the sacrificer? By the exclusion
of the specific [reference], the first [view would hold]; but no — it is determined as [applying] to the sacrificer alone. // MJaiNy_3,4.33 //

children.text:
'īdṛśasya somasya vamane caruḥ' iti viśeṣasyābhāvādṛtvijāṃ yajamānasya ca vamane sarvatrāsau caruḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
'yo vamati sa nirvapati' iti nirvapturvamanaṃ carunimittam |
children.translated_text: 'He who vomits, he prepares [the <s>caru</s>]' — the vomiting of the preparer (<s>nirvaptṛ</s>) is the occasion for the <s>caru</s>.
And the preparer is the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>).
Because if the priests were the preparers, there would be the undesirable consequence of [them being treated as] a different class of eligible persons.
Therefore — the injunction of the <s>caru</s> applies only when the sacrificer vomits. || MJaiNyC_3,4.33 ||

Since there is no specification such as 'for the vomiting of such-and-such <s>Soma</s>,' the <s>caru</s> applies everywhere — both when the priests and the sacrificer vomit — if so [it is argued], that is not correct.
(In the eighteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on whether the cut portion (<s>avadāna</s>) of the <s>Āgneya</s> eight-<s>kapāla</s> <s>caru</s> is to be offered, <s>sūtras</s> 43–47)
The entire oblation (<s>havis</s>) is to be given, because it serves that [deity's] purpose. / Jaim_3,4.43 /
But because of the cutting (<s>avadāna</s>), the remainder would exist. / Jaim_3,4.44 /
Or [the cutting is] a means, because it serves that [offering's] purpose. / Jaim_3,4.45 /

children.text: kṛtatvāt tu karmaṇaḥ sakṛt syād dravyasya guṇabhūtatvāt / Jaim_3,4.46 /
children.translated_text: But since the rite is [already] accomplished, it would be done once, because the substance is subordinate. / Jaim_3,4.46 /
And because the remainder is observed. / Jaim_3,4.47 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.34
He composes the eighteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In the sacrifice, should one offer the entire oblation (<s>havis</s>), or is some portion left over?
Since it serves the deity's purpose, one should offer all; but [only] the cut portion is left over after two cuttings. // MJaiNy_3,4.34 //

children.text:
'āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaḥ' ityatra kṛtsno 'pi puroḍāśo 'gnaye tyaktavyaḥ |
taddhitena kṛtsnasyāgnidevatāsaṃbandhāvagateḥ |
tyāgamantareṇaitadanupapattiḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
'dvirhaviṣo 'vadyati' ityavadānadvayaṃ śrūyate |
avadeyaṃ cāṅguṣṭhaparvamāvam |
tathā ca kalpasūtrakāraḥ- 'āgneyasya puroḍāśasya madhyādaṅguṣṭhaparvamātramavadānaṃ tiraścīnamavadyati' iti |
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>Kalpasūtrakāra</s> [states]: '<s>āgneyasya puroḍāśasya madhyādaṅguṣṭhaparvamātramavadānaṃ tiraścīnamavadyati</s>' (from the middle of the <s>Āgneya</s> sacrificial cake, he cuts crosswise a portion the size of a thumb-joint).
Therefore, having cut two portions the size of a thumb-joint each from the oblation, [only those] are to be offered.
The rest is to be left as remainder.
And the connection with the deity is served even through a portion. || MJaiNyC_3,4.34 ||

In '<s>āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaḥ</s>' (the eight-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] for <s>Agni</s>), the entire sacrificial cake (<s>puroḍāśa</s>) is to be offered to <s>Agni</s>. Because by the <s>taddhita</s> suffix, the connection of the whole with <s>Agni</s> as deity is understood. Without offering, this [connection] cannot be explained — if so [it is argued], that is not correct. '<s>Dvirhaviṣo 'vadyati</s>' (he cuts twice from the oblation) — a twofold cutting is heard. And the portion to be cut is the size of a thumb-joint.

children.text: aprayojakatvād ekasmāt kriyerañ śeṣasya guṇabhūtatvāt / Jaim_3,4.48 /
children.translated_text: Since [giving] from one would be non-productive, the offering should be made from [the one], because the remainder is subordinate. / Jaim_3,4.48 /
And because [the remainder] has been consecrated. / Jaim_3,4.49 /

children.text: sarvebhyo vā kāraṇāviśeṣāt saṃskārasya tadarthatvāt / Jaim_3,4.50 /
children.translated_text: Or from all [oblations], because there is no distinction in the reason, and the consecration serves that [common] purpose. / Jaim_3,4.50 /
And because the mark is observed. / Jaim_3,4.51 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.35
He composes the nineteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
For the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, from one remainder or from all? Since a single [cutting] has been done,
the scriptural purpose is accomplished from all [remainders]; [the cutting] should be done from all, because of the equality of consecration. // MJaiNy_3,4.35 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate- 'śeṣātsviṣṭakṛte samavadyati' iti |
tatra-āgneyādīnāṃ trayāṇāṃ haviṣāṃ madhye yasya kasyacidekasya haviṣaḥ śeṣādavadātavyam |
tāvataiva śāstrārthānuṣṭhānasiddhaḥ- iti cet |

children.translated_text: that is not correct.
This cutting is made to consecrate the used oblation.
And the consecration is the same for all the oblations.
Therefore — the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering for proper completion) should be performed from [the remainders of] all the oblations (<s>haviḥśeṣa</s>). || MJaiNyC_3,4.35 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices), it is heard: '<s>śeṣātsviṣṭakṛte samavadyati</s>' (from the remainder, he cuts equally for the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>). Therein — from among the three oblations, the <s>Āgneya</s> and the others, the cutting should be from the remainder of any one single oblation. By that alone the scriptural purpose is accomplished — if so [it is argued],
(In the twentieth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the performance of the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> from the first remainder, <s>sūtras</s> 52–53)
If from one [remainder] only, then [the choice is] according to wish, because there is no distinction. / Jaim_3,4.52 /
Or from the principal [offering], because of its temporal priority. / Jaim_3,4.53 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.36
He composes the twentieth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
If from one [remainder] only, then there is no fixed rule (<s>niyati</s>) regarding the principal, or there is;
since there is no authority (<s>śruti</s>) [establishing a rule], there is no reason for departing from the principal [offering]. // MJaiNy_3,4.36 //

children.text: 'ekasmādeva haviḥśeṣātsviṣṭakṛt' iti yaḥ pūrvādhikaraṇe pūrvapakṣaḥ, tasminpakṣe niyāmakasyāśrutatvāt-
children.translated_text: Regarding the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) in the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s> — 'the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> [is to be performed] from just one oblation-remainder' — on that view, since no restrictive rule is heard,
it would follow that [it may be performed] from the remainder of any oblation whatsoever — having arrived at this position,

children.text: brūmaḥ- prathamātikrame mānābhāvātprathamahaviḥśeṣeṇaiva saṃskārāsiddhāvitaratra prāptyabhāvādasti niyatiḥ || MJaiNyC_3,4.36 ||
children.translated_text: we say: Since there is no authority for departing from the first [offering], and since the consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is not established without the remainder of the first oblation, and since there is no possibility of obtaining [the consecration] from any other [remainder], there is indeed a fixed rule. || MJaiNyC_3,4.36 ||
(In the twenty-first [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the purpose of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> distribution being for eating (<s>bhakṣa</s>), <s>sūtras</s> 54–57)
Since eating (<s>bhakṣa</s>) is not heard, the word 'giving' (<s>dāna</s>) [denotes] a purchase (<s>parikraya</s>). / Jaim_3,4.54 /
And because of the praise associated with that [giving]. / Jaim_3,4.55 /
Or [the distribution is] for the purpose of eating, because of the equal status of the substance (<s>dravya</s>). / Jaim_3,4.56 /
The praise of giving is [explained] by the express teaching (<s>vyādeśa</s>). / Jaim_3,4.57 /
START MJaiNy 3,4.37-38
He composes the twenty-first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: idaṃ brahmaṇa ityaktiḥ krayārthā bhakṣaṇāya vā /
children.translated_text: The statement 'this is for the <s>Brahman</s> [priest]' — is it for the purpose of purchasing, or for eating?
Since eating is not heard, [it is] for purchasing; therefore, let it be used by them as they wish. // MJaiNy_3,4.37 //
Since the entirety [of the offering] is already ordained for the deity, there is no ownership [by the sacrificer];

children.text: śeṣasya pratipattyarthe bhakṣaṇaṃ tatra yujyate // MJaiNy_3,4.38 //
children.translated_text: the eating of the remainder for the purpose of reception (<s>pratipatti</s>) — that is fitting. // MJaiNy_3,4.38 //

children.text:
caturdhākṛtapuroḍāśasya bhāgānyajamāna evaṃ nirdiśet- 'idaṃ brahmaṇaḥ, idaṃ hotuḥ, idamadhvaryoḥ, idamagnīdhaḥ, iti |
so 'yaṃ nirdeśa na bhakṣaṇārthaḥ |
bhakṣaṇasyāśrutatvāt |
tato bhṛtidānena tānṛtvijaḥ parikretumayaṃ nirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ |
krayaśca tadaṅgīkārānusāreṇa svalpenāpyupapadyate |
tasmātsvakīyā bhāgāstairicchayopayoktuṃ śakyāḥ- iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- 'agneya juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi' iti kṛtsnasya haviṣo devatārthe saṃkalpitatvena tatra yajamānasya svāmitvābhāvānna yuktaḥ parikrayaḥ |
children.translated_text: we say: Since by [the utterance] '<s>agneya juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi</s>' (I offer what is pleasing to <s>Agni</s>) the entire oblation is dedicated for the deity, the sacrificer has no ownership over it, so the purchase is not justified.
But eating is justified, because it serves the purpose of reception (<s>pratipatti</s>).
Whatever use of the remainder there may be — that is the reception.

children.text: puroḍāśasya bhakṣaṇāhatvādbhakṣaṇena karmakarāṇāmṛtsāhajananācca bhakṣaṇārtho 'yaṃ nirdeśo yujyate || MJaiNyC_3,4.37-38 ||
children.translated_text: Since the <s>puroḍāśa</s> is suited for eating, and since eating generates enthusiasm among the officiating priests — this designation for the purpose of eating is justified. || MJaiNyC_3,4.37-38 ||

The sacrificer should designate the portions of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial rice cake) divided into four parts thus: 'this is for the <s>Brahman</s> [priest], this is for the <s>Hotṛ</s>, this is for the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, this is for the <s>Agnīdh</s>.' This designation is not for the purpose of eating, since eating is not heard [in the injunction]. Therefore, this designation was made to purchase those priests with payment (<s>bhṛti-dāna</s>). And the purchase is possible even with a small [amount], in accordance with their acceptance. Therefore, [those] portions belonging to them may be used by them as they wish — having arrived at this position,

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīye jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistare tṛtīyādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the illustrious <s>Mādhavīya Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s>.
Now the fifth <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s>. /
(In the first [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the non-performance of the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and other remainder-rites by means of [the remainder from] the <s>Pravargya</s> and the like, <s>sūtras</s> 1–12)
And from the clarified butter (<s>ājya</s>), because of the connection with all [offerings]. / Jaim_3,5.1 /
And because of [its being] the cause. / Jaim_3,5.2 /
Since in one [offering the word] '<s>samavatta</s>' (poured together) is heard. / Jaim_3,5.3 /
And since in the clarified butter the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> is observed, this [remainder] has a purpose [already]. / Jaim_3,5.4 /

children.text: aśeṣatvāt tu naivaṃ syāt sarvādānād aśeṣatā / Jaim_3,5.5 /
children.translated_text: But [this] would not be so, because of its not being a remainder — since all is offered, there is no remainder. / Jaim_3,5.5 /
Because of [its] common nature, [it] would not [apply to] the <s>Dhruvā</s> [ladle]. / Jaim_3,5.6 /

children.text: aktatvāc ca juhvāṃ tasya ca homasaṃyogāt / Jaim_3,5.7 /
children.translated_text: And because [the <s>Dhruvā</s>] is not anointed, and [it pertains to] the <s>Juhū</s> [ladle], and because of [the <s>Juhū</s>'s] connection with the oblation. / Jaim_3,5.7 /
If [it be argued] that it is like the <s>Camasa</s> (drinking cup) — / Jaim_3,5.8 /

children.text: na codanāvirodhād dhaviḥ prakalpanāc ca / Jaim_3,5.9 /
children.translated_text: No, because of [the principle of] non-contradiction with the injunction, and because of the establishment of the oblation. / Jaim_3,5.9 /
Since the entitlement has [already] arisen, the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) [is used] when [the remainder] exists. / Jaim_3,5.10 /
Beyond [this], because of the specific class (<s>jātiviśeṣa</s>). / Jaim_3,5.11 /
The last [remainder] is for the purpose of the <s>Areka</s> (non-emptying). / Jaim_3,5.12 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.1-2
He composes the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the fifth <s>pāda</s> —
Does the remainder-rite take place with the substance of the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s> (low-voiced offering), or not?
It does, because it is obtained by the statement 'from all the oblations.' // MJaiNy_3,5.1 //
But the remainder of the stated clarified butter substance is for the purpose of sub-spreading (<s>upastāraṇa</s>) and the like;

children.text: ato na pratipattyarhaḥ śeṣakārye tataḥ katham // MJaiNy_3,5.2 //
children.translated_text: therefore it is not fit for reception — so how can there be a remainder-rite [with it]? // MJaiNy_3,5.2 //

children.text:
dhrauvādājyājupāṃśuyājārthamavadāne kṛte taccheṣeṇa dhrauveṇa dravyeṇa sviṣṭakṛdādikaṃ śeṣakārya kartavyam |
kutaḥ |
'tadyatsarvebhyo havirbhyaḥ samavadyati' iti vākyena prāpitatvāt- iti cet |
maivam |

children.translated_text: For [only] the remainder of a substance whose purpose has been fulfilled merits reception, as it awaits utilization.
But the clarified butter in the <s>Dhruvā</s> [ladle] has not fulfilled its purpose,
because the sub-spreading (<s>upastāraṇa</s>) and other [functions] that are to be performed with it still exist.

children.text: tasmāt - na tena śeṣakārye bhavati || MJaiNyC_3,5.1-2 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — the remainder-rite does not take place with that [substance]. || MJaiNyC_3,5.1-2 ||

After the portion has been taken from the <s>Dhruvā</s> [ladle] containing clarified butter for the purpose of the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s>, the remainder-rite — the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and the like — should be performed with the remainder, that is, with the substance in the <s>Dhruvā</s> [ladle]. Why? Because it is obtained by the statement '<s>tadyatsarvebhyo havirbhyaḥ samavadyati</s>' (that which is poured together from all the oblations) — if so argued, that is not correct.
(In the second [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the non-performance of the remainder-rites in the <s>Sākaṃprasthāyya</s> sacrifice, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: sākaṃprasthāyye sviṣṭakṛd iḍaṃ ca tadvat / Jaim_3,5.13 /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Sākaṃprasthāyya</s> [sacrifice], the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and the <s>Iḍā</s> [offerings] are likewise [absent]. / Jaim_3,5.13 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.3-4
He composes the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
When advancing together with the pots (<s>kumbhī</s>) — does the remainder-rite exist or not?
As in the archetype, by taking a portion with the <s>Juhū</s> [ladle], the remainder-rite is appropriate. // MJaiNy_3,5.3 //
Since the remainder in the pots is not established in the <s>Sākaṃprasthāyya</s> rite,
the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and <s>Iḍā</s> should not be performed, because the ladles are given to the <s>Agnīdh</s>. // MJaiNy_3,5.4 //

children.text:
'sākaṃprasthāyīyena yajeta paśukāmaḥ' iti vihite karmaṇi śrūyate- 'saha kumbhībhirabhikrāmannāha' iti |
