tatra catasṛbhirdadhipayaḥkumbhībhiḥ sahā'havanīyadeśe 'bhikramaṇa mātraṃ śrutam |
na tu tatra kumbhībhirhomaḥ śrutaḥ |
tathā satyasya karmaṇaḥ sāṃnāyyavikṛttitvājjuhvā kumbhībhyo 'vadāya hotavyam |
hutaśeṣeṇa ca sviṣṭakṛdādikaṃ sāṃnāyyaśeṣeṇaiva kartavyam- iti prāpte, -

children.translated_text: we say: Here, the remainder in the pots is not established,
because, unlike in the <s>Sānnāyya</s>, there is no taking of a portion from them with the <s>Juhū</s> [ladle].

children.text: 'agnīdhe strucau pradāya saha kumbhībhirabhikrāman' ityuktyā juhūpabhṛtoḥ prattatvādabhikramaṇasya homārthatvācca kumbhībhireva dadhipayasorhome sati kumbhīmātrāmavaśiṣyate, na tu haviḥśeṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Since by the statement '<s>agnīdhe strucau pradāya saha kumbhībhir abhikrāman</s>' (having given the ladles to the <s>Agnīdh</s>, advancing together with the pots), the <s>Juhū</s> and <s>Upabhṛt</s> [ladles] have been given away, and since the advancing is for the purpose of offering, when the oblation of curd and milk is made with the pots alone, only [the dregs in] the pots remain, but there is no oblation-remainder.
Therefore, how can there be a remainder-rite? || MJaiNyC_3,5.3-4 ||

In the rite enjoined as '<s>sākaṃprasthāyīyena yajeta paśukāmaḥ</s>' (one desiring cattle should sacrifice with the <s>Sākaṃprasthāyya</s>), it is heard: '<s>saha kumbhībhir abhikrāmann āha</s>' (advancing together with the pots, he recites). Therein, only advancing toward the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire with four pots of curd and milk is heard, but the oblation with the pots is not heard there. This being so, since this rite is a modification (<s>vikṛti</s>) of the <s>Sānnāyya</s>, the portion should be taken from the pots with the <s>Juhū</s> [ladle] and offered. And the remainder-rite — the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and the like — should be performed with the remainder of the <s>Sānnāyya</s> itself — having arrived at this position,
(In the third [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the non-performance of remainder-rites in the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> sacrifice, <s>sūtras</s> 14–15)
And in the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> [sacrifice], in the cup-drawings (<s>graha</s>). / Jaim_3,5.14 /
And the statement regarding the remainder is likewise [applicable]. / Jaim_3,5.15 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.5
He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: sautrāmaṇyāṃ grahe sviṣṭakṛdādyasti na vāsti tat /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> [sacrifice], does the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and the like exist in the cup-drawing, or not?
Because of the [existence of a] remainder, [it exists]; but no — because the liquor (<s>surā</s>) and milk are used elsewhere. // MJaiNy_3,5.5 //

children.text:
sautrāmaṇināmake yāge śrūyate - 'payograhāḥ surāgrahāśca gṛhyante' iti |
tatra prakṛtigata somadyaheṣviva śeṣakārye sviṣṭakṛdādikamasti |
na cātra pūrvavaccheṣābhāvaḥ |
'ucchinaṣṭi, na sarve juhoti' ityavaśeṣayitavyatvaśravaṇāt- iti cet |
maivam |
avaśiṣṭasyānyatropayogaśravaṇāt |
'brāhmaṇaṃ parikrīṇīyāduccheṣaṇasya pātāram' iti śrūyate |
'yadi brāhmaṇaṃ na vindeta, valmīkavapāyāmavanayet' iti ca |
children.translated_text: 'If he does not find a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he should pour [the remainder] on an anthill' — thus it is stated.
And '<s>śatātṛṇāyām avaneyat</s>' (he should pour [it] in a hundred-perforated [vessel])' — thus it is stated.
A pot with a hundred holes is the '<s>śatātṛṇā</s>' (hundred-perforated vessel).
Therefore — the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and the like do not exist [in this sacrifice]. || MJaiNyC_3,5.5 ||

In the sacrifice called <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>, it is heard: '<s>payograhāḥ surāgrahāś ca gṛhyante</s>' (milk cup-drawings and liquor cup-drawings are taken). Therein, as in the <s>Soma</s> days of the archetype, the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> and the like exist as remainder-rites. Nor is there an absence of remainder as in the previous [case], since it is heard that [a portion] must be left over: '<s>ucchinaṣṭi, na sarve juhoti</s>' (he leaves some over, he does not offer all) — if so argued, that is not correct. Because it is heard that the remainder is used elsewhere. It is heard: '<s>brāhmaṇaṃ parikrīṇīyād uccheṣaṇasya pātāram</s>' (one should purchase a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> to be the drinker of the leftovers).
(In the fourth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the single performance of the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, <s>Iḍā</s>, and the like in the <s>Sarvapṛṣṭha</s> sacrifice, <s>sūtras</s> 16–17)
When the substance is one, since the rites differ, [the remainder-rites] would be performed for each rite separately. / Jaim_3,5.16 /

children.text: avibhāgāc ca śeṣasya sarvān pratyaviśiṣṭatvāt / Jaim_3,5.17 /
children.translated_text: But because the remainder is undivided, being equal with respect to all [rites]. / Jaim_3,5.17 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.6-7
He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The <s>Indras</s>, differentiated by [the <s>Sāmans</s>] <s>Rathantara</s> and the like — their

children.text: puroḍāśastatra śeṣakārye kiṃ bhidyate na vā // MJaiNy_3,5.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>puroḍāśa</s> is not differentiated; therein, is the remainder-rite differentiated or not? // MJaiNy_3,5.6 //
It is differentiated, because of the difference of the rites, since the <s>Auddalaka</s> [authorities] state [them] separately;
since the remainder is equal with respect to all, the remainder-rite should be [performed] once only. // MJaiNy_3,5.7 //

children.text:
'ya indriyakāmo vīryakāmaḥ syāt, tametayā sarvapṛṣṭhayā yājayet' iti vihitāyāmiṣṭau ṣaḍindrā evaṃ śrūyante- 'indrāya rāthaṃtarāya, indrāya bārhatāya, indrāya vairājāya, indrāyaśākvarāya, indrāya raivatāya' iti |
tatra svarūpeṇaiko 'pīndraḥ pṛṣṭhastotreṣu ṣaṭsu vihitānāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ rathaṃtarādi sāmnāṃ saṃbandhena viśeṣyamāṇaḥ ṣoṭhā bhidyate |
tāsāṃ sarvāsāmindradevatānāmeka eva puroḍāśo vidhīyate- 'dvādaśakapālaḥ puroḍāśo bhavati |
vaiśvadevatvāya' iti |
tasmiṃśca puroḍāśe proktadevatābhyaḥ pṛthakpṛthakpradānāya bahubhyaḥ pradeśebhyo 'vadānaṃ śrūyate- 'samantaṃ paryavadyati' iti |
tatra devatābhedena pradānabhedena ca karmaṇāṃ bhede sati pṛthagatideśātsviṣṭakṛdiḍādi śeṣakārye ṣaṭkṛtvaḥ pṛthakkartavyam - iti cet |
children.translated_text: Therein, since the rites differ due to the difference of deities and the difference of offerings, and because of the separate instruction, the remainder-rite — <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, <s>Iḍā</s>, and the like — should be performed six times separately — if so argued,
that is not correct.
Because, since the remainder is one, and the reception thereof [is one], differentiation is impossible.
Therefore — it should be performed only once. || MJaiNyC_3,5.6-7 ||

In the sacrifice enjoined as '<s>ya indriyakāmo vīryakāmaḥ syāt, tam etayā sarvapṛṣṭhayā yājayet</s>' (whoever desires power and strength, him one should cause to sacrifice with this <s>Sarvapṛṣṭha</s> [offering]), six <s>Indras</s> are heard thus: '<s>Indrāya Rāthaṃtarāya</s> (to <s>Indra</s> of the <s>Rathantara</s>), <s>Indrāya Bārhatāya</s> (to <s>Indra</s> of the <s>Bṛhat</s>), <s>Indrāya Vairājāya</s> (to <s>Indra</s> of the <s>Vairāja</s>), <s>Indrāya Śākvarāya</s> (to <s>Indra</s> of the <s>Śākvara</s>), <s>Indrāya Raivatāya</s> (to <s>Indra</s> of the <s>Raivata</s>).' Therein, although <s>Indra</s> is one in his own form, he is differentiated sixfold through association with the six <s>Sāmans</s> — <s>Rathantara</s> and the like — enjoined in the six <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants (<s>stotras</s>). For all those <s>Indra</s>-deities, a single <s>puroḍāśa</s> is enjoined: '<s>dvādaśakapālaḥ puroḍāśo bhavati, vaiśvadevatvāya</s>' (the <s>puroḍāśa</s> is on twelve potsherds, for the sake of universality). And in that <s>puroḍāśa</s>, it is heard that portions are taken from many places for separate offering to the stated deities: '<s>samantaṃ paryavadyati</s>' (he takes portions from all around).
(In the fifth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the twice-eating of the remainder in the <s>Aindravāyava</s> cup-drawing, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: aindravāyave tu vacanāt pratikarma bhakṣaḥ syāt / Jaim_3,5.18 /
children.translated_text: But in the <s>Aindravāyava</s> [cup], because of the express statement, the eating (<s>bhakṣa</s>) would be for each rite [separately]. / Jaim_3,5.18 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.8
He composes the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The remainder of the <s>Aindravāyava</s> [cup] — is the eating once or more than once?
When once-only is obtained by the preceding principle, the eating is twice, because of the express statement. // MJaiNy_3,5.8 //

children.text: jyotiṣṭome yo 'yamaindravāyavagrahaḥ' tatra saṃskāryasya somasyaikatvātsakṛdeva śeṣakāryam- iti cet |
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, regarding the <s>Aindravāyava</s> cup-drawing — since the <s>Soma</s> to be consecrated is one, the remainder-rite should be only once — if so argued,
that is not correct.

children.text: 'dviraindravāyavasya bhakṣayati, dvirhyetasya vaṣaṭkaroti' iti vacanādvirbhakṣaṇam || MJaiNyC_3,5.8 ||
children.translated_text: Because of the express statement '<s>dvir aindravāyavasya bhakṣayati, dvir hy etasya vaṣaṭkaroti</s>' (he eats twice from the <s>Aindravāyava</s>, for he utters the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call twice for it), the eating is twice. || MJaiNyC_3,5.8 ||
(In the sixth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the remainder-eating in <s>Soma</s> sacrifices, <s>sūtras</s> 19–21)
In <s>Soma</s> [sacrifices], since [eating] is not stated, there is no eating (<s>bhakṣa</s>). / Jaim_3,5.19 /
Or it would [exist], because of the observation of a different purpose. / Jaim_3,5.20 /

children.text: vacanāni tv apūrvatvāt tasmād yathopadeśaṃ syuḥ / Jaim_3,5.21 /
children.translated_text: But the statements [are valid] because of their originating force (<s>apūrvatva</s>); therefore they would be as instructed. / Jaim_3,5.21 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.9
He composes the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: someṣvabhakṣo bhakṣo vā na bhakṣo grahahomataḥ /
children.translated_text: In <s>Soma</s> [sacrifices], is there no eating, or is there eating? No eating, because the entire cup-drawing is offered;
but because of the limited offering, there is a remainder — the eating thereof [exists] by the force of the originating statement (<s>apūrva-vacana</s>). // MJaiNy_3,5.9 //

children.text:
somayāgeṣu śeṣabhakṣo nāsti, 'yadgrahāñjuhoti' iti kṛtsnagraheṇā'huti śravaṇātkumbhīṣviva śeṣābhāvāt- iti cet |
maivam |

children.translated_text: The remainder is established by the specific statement '<s>alpaṃ juhoti</s>' (he offers a small [portion]).
And its eating is understood from statements that convey an originating purpose (<s>apūrvārtha</s>).

children.text: 'āśvinaṃ bhakṣayanti' dviraindravāyavasya bhakṣayanti' 'sadasi bhakṣayanti' ityādīni vacanānyapūrvārtha pratipādayanti |
children.translated_text: The statements '<s>āśvinaṃ bhakṣayanti</s>' (they eat the <s>Āśvina</s> [cup]), '<s>dvir aindravāyavasya bhakṣayanti</s>' (they eat twice from the <s>Aindravāyava</s>), '<s>sadasi bhakṣayanti</s>' (they eat in the <s>Sadas</s> hall)' and the like convey an originating purpose.
Therefore, since eating is enjoined, there is eating in <s>Soma</s> sacrifices. || MJaiNyC_3,5.9 ||

In <s>Soma</s> sacrifices, there is no remainder-eating, because it is heard that the entire cup-drawing is offered: '<s>yad grahāñ juhoti</s>' (when he offers the cup-drawings) — and since there is no remainder, just as in the [case of the] pots — if so argued, that is not correct.
(In the seventh [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the remainder-eating of the <s>Camasa</s> holders, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
In the <s>Camasas</s> (drinking cups), because of the designation, since the connection arises from that [designation]. / Jaim_3,5.22 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.10
He composes the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Does [the <s>Soma</s> in] the <s>Camasa</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s> proceed [for eating], or is there no eating?
[There is] no eating, because [it is] not stated; but because of the designation '<s>Camasa</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s>' — that [eating exists]. // MJaiNy_3,5.10 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate- 'praitu hotuśrvamasaḥ, pra brahmaṇaḥ, prodvātṝṇāṃ, pra yajamānasya, prayantu sadasyānām' iti |
tatra- vacanāmāvādabhakṣaḥ- iti cet |

children.translated_text: that is not correct.
Because the drinking is understood through the word <s>camasa</s> (cup) which is apprehended by the designation (<s>samākhyā</s>).
For the etymological derivation of that [word] is: '<s>camvate</s>' — '<s>Soma</s> is drunk in this particular vessel.'
Therefore — the drinking from that [cup] does exist. || MJaiNyC_3,5.10 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: '<s>praitu hotuś camasaḥ, pra brahmaṇaḥ, prod vātṝṇāṃ, pra yajamānasya, prayantu sadasyānām</s>' (let the cup of the <s>Hotṛ</s> go forth, [let that] of the <s>Brahman</s> [go forth], [let that] of the <s>Udvātṛs</s> [go forth], [let that] of the sacrificer [go forth], let those of the <s>Sadasyāḥ</s> go forth). Therein — from the statement, the cup-drinking (<s>camasa-bhakṣa</s>) [is established] — if so it is argued,
(In the eighth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the drinking of the <s>Udvātṛs</s> together with the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 23-26:)
There is one cup for the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, because of the textual connection. / Jaim_3,5.23 /
Or [it belongs to] all, because of the connection with all. / Jaim_3,5.24 /
Or [to] those who perform the <s>Stotra</s> (chant), because of their connection and the plural expression. / Jaim_3,5.25 /

children.text: sarve tu vedasaṃyogāt kāraṇād ekadeśe syāt / Jaim_3,5.26 /
children.translated_text: But all [should drink], because of the Vedic connection; [this is] because the cause [applies to] a part [as well]. / Jaim_3,5.26 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.11-13
He composes the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'Of the <s>Udvātṛs</s>' — should only one, the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, drink [from that cup],
or should all the <s>Sāmavedic</s> chanters also [drink], who are mentioned along with the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s>? // MJaiNy_3,5.11 //
Those [chanters] associated with him — or all, from the word '<s>Udgātṛ</s>';
from the plural [number], by connection with the chanting, the third [view holds], when the conventional meaning (<s>rūḍhi</s>) is overridden. // MJaiNy_3,5.12 //
When [the term is construed] by etymological derivation (<s>yoga</s>) with the designation, by the <s>daṇḍi</s>-maxim the last [view] here is the one [accepted] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>;
or the third [view] is explicitly stated [by the <s>Vārtikakāra</s>], since the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s> does not have a seat in the <s>Sadas</s> [hall]. // MJaiNy_3,5.13 //

children.text:
pūrvodāhṛtavākye 'prodvātṝṇām' ityatraikasyaiva bhakṣaḥ |
udvīthaśabdābhidheyāyāḥ sāmabhakteru- dgātaryudgātṛprātipadikasya rūḍhatvāt - ityekaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ |
'udgātṝṇām' ityasya bahutvasyaikasmi nnasaṃbhavādudgātropalakṣitāḥ ṣoḍaśartvijaḥ sarve 'pi bhakṣayeyuḥ- iti dvitīyaḥ |
udgīthaprastāvaprati hārāntāmabhāgānudvātṛprastotṛpratihartāraḥ prayogakāle gāyanti |
'udutkarṣeṇa gāyanti' iti yogenodvātārastrayo bhakṣayeyuḥ- iti tṛtīyaḥ pakṣaḥ |
'rūḍhiryogamapaharati' iti nyāyādeka evodgātā |
tena ca bahuvacanopapattaye pratyāsannā upalakṣyante |

children.translated_text: And there is proximity for the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s> as well, just as for the <s>Prastotṛ</s> and <s>Pratihartṛ</s>.

Because the designation <s>audgātra</s> (pertaining to the <s>Udgātṛ</s>) applies also to his [the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s>'s] ritual function in the form of the <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s> invocation, since he is a student of the <s>Sāmaveda</s>.

children.text: tasmāt- 'subrahmaṇyena sahitāścatvāraḥ sāmagā bhakṣayeyuḥ'- ityayamantyaḥ pakṣo bhāṣyakārasyābhimataḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore — 'the four <s>Sāmavedic</s> chanters together with the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s> should drink' — this is the final view accepted by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (<s>Śabara</s>).

children.text: vārtikakārastu - sadaso bhakṣaṇasthānatvātsubrahmaṇyasya sadasyapraveśāttena virahitā avaśiṣṭāḥ sāmagā bhakṣayanti- iti tṛtīyaṃ pakṣamaṅgīcakāra || MJaiNyC_3,5.11-13 ||
children.translated_text: But the <s>Vārtikakāra</s> (<s>Kumārila</s>) accepted the third view — that, since the <s>Sadas</s> [hall] is the place for drinking and the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s> does not enter the <s>Sadas</s>, the remaining <s>Sāmavedic</s> chanters without him should drink. || MJaiNyC_3,5.11-13 ||

In the previously cited sentence, '<s>prod vātṝṇām</s>' (of the <s>Udvātṛs</s>) — [there is debate about who drinks from] one cup alone. [Option 1:] Only the <s>Udgātṛ</s> [drinks], because the base-word <s>udgātṛ</s>, being a conventional term (<s>rūḍha</s>) for the <s>Sāmic</s> portion called <s>Udvītha</s>, [refers to him alone] — this is the first prima facie view. [Option 2:] Since the plural '<s>udgātṝṇām</s>' cannot apply to a single person, all sixteen priests indicated by [the designation] <s>Udgātṛ</s> should drink — this is the second [view]. [Option 3:] The <s>Udgātṛ</s>, <s>Prastotṛ</s>, and <s>Pratihartṛ</s> sing the portions of the <s>Udgītha</s>, <s>Prastāva</s>, and <s>Pratihāra</s> during the performance. Since '<s>Udvātṛs</s>' [etymologically means] 'those who sing with elevation (<s>utkarṣa</s>),' the three <s>Udvātṛs</s> should drink by etymological derivation (<s>yoga</s>) — this is the third view. By the maxim 'convention overrides etymology (<s>rūḍhi</s> overrides <s>yoga</s>),' only the <s>Udgātṛ</s> alone [should drink]. And to account for the plural number, those who are proximate [to him] are included by indication.
(In the ninth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>Soma</s>-drinking of the <s>Grāvastut</s> also, <s>sūtras</s> 27-30:)
The <s>Grāvastut</s> has no [<s>Soma</s>-]drinking, because he is not named [among the cup-holders]. / Jaim_3,5.27 /
Or [the drinking applies] at the <s>Hāriyojana</s> [libation], because of the connection with all. / Jaim_3,5.28 /
Or [only] for the cup-holders, because of proximity. / Jaim_3,5.29 /

children.text: sarveṣāṃ tu vidhitvāt tadarthā camasiśrutiḥ / Jaim_3,5.30 /
children.translated_text: But for all, because it is an injunction; the mention of cup-holders serves that purpose. / Jaim_3,5.30 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.14-15
He composes the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the <s>Hāriyojana</s> drinking only for the cup-holders (<s>camasins</s>),
or for all? The former [have priority], because of the proximity [of their mention] in the preceding sentence. // MJaiNy_3,5.14 //
All indeed desire [to drink] — [this is understood] from the <s>Hāriyojana</s> sentence;
even the <s>Grāvastut</s> has [a right to] drinking; being a cup-holder is not the [sole] cause. // MJaiNy_3,5.15 //

children.text:
'harirasi hāriyojanaḥ' ityanena mantreṇa gṛhyamāṇo graho hāriyojanaḥ |
hotṛbrahmādaya ścamasimaḥ |
yastu caturṇo hotṝṇāṃ madhye caturtho grāvastunnāmake 'sti, nāsau camasī |
tatra camasināmeva hāriyojanabhakṣaṇam |
kutaḥ-"yathācamasamanyāṃścamasāṃścamasino bhakṣayanti, athaitasya hāriyojanasya sarva eva lipsante' ityatra pūrvavākye camasināṃ saṃnihitvenottaravākye sarvaśabdena teṣāmevābhidhātavyatvāt |
ato nāsti grāvastutastatra bhakṣaḥ- iti prāpte-
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>Grāvastut</s> has no drinking therein — having arrived at this position,

children.text: brūmaḥ- athaśabdenaivakāreṇa ca camasimātraśaṅkāmapodya vākyena vihitasya sarvamakṣaṇasya saṃnidhimātreṇa saṃkocāyogādasti grāvastuto 'pi bhakṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: we say: By the words '<s>atha</s>' (now, then) and '<s>eva</s>' (indeed), the doubt that it applies only to cup-holders is dispelled; since the drinking enjoined by the sentence for all cannot be restricted by mere proximity alone, the <s>Grāvastut</s> also has [a right to] drinking.

children.text: tasmāt- camasitvaṃ na bhakṣaṇe kāraṇam || MJaiNyC_3,5.14-15 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — being a cup-holder (<s>camasi</s>) is not the cause of [the right to] drinking. || MJaiNyC_3,5.14-15 ||

The cup (<s>graha</s>) drawn with the <s>mantra</s> '<s>harir asi hāriyojanaḥ</s>' (you are <s>Hari</s>, the <s>Hāriyojana</s>) is the <s>Hāriyojana</s>. The <s>Hotṛ</s>, <s>Brahman</s>, and the others are cup-holders (<s>camasins</s>). But the fourth among the four <s>Hotṛs</s>, called <s>Grāvastut</s>, is not a cup-holder. Therein, only the cup-holders should drink from the <s>Hāriyojana</s>. Why? Because in the text '<s>yathā camasam anyāṃś camasāṃś camasino bhakṣayanti, athaitasya hāriyojanasya sarva eva lipsante</s>' (just as the cup-holders drink from other cups, each from his own cup, so all indeed desire [to drink from] this <s>Hāriyojana</s>), since the cup-holders are mentioned in proximity in the preceding sentence, the word <s>sarva</s> (all) in the latter sentence should denote them alone.
(In the tenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (exclamation) being a cause for drinking, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
And one should drink on account of the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation). / Jaim_3,5.31 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.16-17
He composes the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the first drinking of the one who utters the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> an injunction of [mere] priority,
or would it apply to the drinking connected with that — [i.e.,] to drinking caused by the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>? // MJaiNy_3,5.16 //
The first [interpretation] — [mere] priority — is not [correct], because the compound cannot be resolved [that way];
the injunction is of the qualified [drinking]; therefore the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> is also a cause [of drinking]. // MJaiNy_3,5.17 //

children.text:
'vaṣaṭkartuḥ prathamabhakṣaḥ' ityevaṃ śrūyate |
vaṣaṭkartā hotā |
tasya bhakṣaṇaṃ samākhyāyā prāptam |
prāthamyaṃ tvaprāptamiti tadevātra vidhiyate - iti cet |
children.translated_text: But the priority [of his drinking] is not yet obtained, so only that is being enjoined here — if so it is argued,
that is not correct.

children.text: 'prathamabhakṣaḥ' ityasya samastapadatvena 'yo bhakṣaḥ, sa prathamaḥ' ityeyaṃ vicchidyānve tumayogyatvātprāthampaviśiṣṭabhakṣaṇamatra vidhīyate |
children.translated_text: Since '<s>prathamabhakṣaḥ</s>' (first-drinking) is a compound word, the analysis 'that drinking which is first' — this splitting — is unsuitable; therefore, what is being enjoined here is drinking qualified by priority.
In that drinking, the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> is the cause. || MJaiNyC_3,5.16-17 ||

It is thus heard: '<s>vaṣaṭkartuḥ prathamabhakṣaḥ</s>' (the first drinking belongs to the one who utters the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>). The one who utters the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> is the <s>Hotṛ</s>. His [right to] drinking is already obtained from the designation (<s>samākhyā</s>).
(In the eleventh [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the oblation and pressing also being causes of drinking, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
And [one should drink] on account of the oblation (<s>homa</s>) and the pressing (<s>abhiṣava</s>). / Jaim_3,5.32 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.18-19
He composes the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Are the designation, the sentence, and the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> alone the causes of drinking,
or are the pressing and the oblation as well? Let the first [be accepted] by the stated reasoning. // MJaiNy_3,5.18 //
In the <s>Havirdhāna</s> [shed], having pressed with the stones, and then having offered in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire], one should drink in the <s>Sadas</s> [hall] —

children.text: iti śrutatvatastau ca bhakṣahetū yathettare // MJaiNy_3,5.19 //
children.translated_text: since this is heard, those two [pressing and oblation] are also causes of drinking, just like the others. // MJaiNy_3,5.19 //

children.text:
'praitu hotuścamasaḥ' ityatra samākhyā bhakṣahetuḥ |
hāriyojane vākyam |
'vaṣaṭkartuḥ prathamabhakṣaḥ' ityatra vaṣaṭkāraḥ |
ityevamuktatvātraya eva bhakṣahetavaḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
'havirdhāne grāvabhirabhiṣutyā'havanīye hutvā pratyañcaḥ paretya sadasi bhakṣānbhakṣayanti' iti śrūyate |
uttaravedyāḥ pratīcīne sadasaḥ prācīne maṇḍale 'miṣavaḥ |

children.translated_text: The oblation takes place on the <s>Uttaravedi</s>.
The drinking takes place in the <s>Sadas</s>.

Therein — since the pressing and the oblation, being already obtained by another statement, are not themselves being enjoined, they are mentioned as causes (<s>nimitta</s>) and the drinking is [then] enjoined.
Therefore — like the designation and the rest, these two also have the status of being causes of drinking. || MJaiNyC_3,5.18-19 ||

In '<s>praitu hotuś camasaḥ</s>' (let the cup of the <s>Hotṛ</s> go forth), the designation is the cause of drinking. In the <s>Hāriyojana</s> [case], the sentence [is the cause]. In '<s>vaṣaṭkartuḥ prathamabhakṣaḥ</s>' (the first drinking belongs to the one who utters the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>), the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> [is the cause]. Since thus only three have been stated, these three alone are the causes of drinking — if so it is argued, that is not correct. It is heard: '<s>havirdhāne grāvabhir abhiṣutyāhavanīye hutvā pratyañcaḥ paretya sadasi bhakṣān bhakṣayanti</s>' (having pressed with the stones in the <s>Havirdhāna</s> [shed], having offered in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire], they return westward and drink the <s>Soma</s> draughts in the <s>Sadas</s> [hall]). The pressings take place in the area to the west of the <s>Uttaravedi</s>, in the eastern enclosure of the <s>Sadas</s>.
(In the twelfth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>Soma</s>-drinking of the one who utters the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> and the like from the cup, <s>sūtras</s> 33-35:)
Because of the direct instruction regarding the cups, [the drinking] is unspecified for the remainder. / Jaim_3,5.33 /

children.text: syād vā kāraṇabhāvād anirdeśaś camasānāṃ kartus tadvacanatvāt / Jaim_3,5.34 /
children.translated_text: Or there would be no specification of cups because of the causal nature; [the non-specification relates to] the performer, because the statement pertains to him. / Jaim_3,5.34 /
And because of [its] not being seen as different in the cup [context]. / Jaim_3,5.35 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.20-21
He composes the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: hetusaṃghe vikalpaḥ kiṃ bādho vātha samuccayaḥ /
children.translated_text: When multiple causes co-occur, is there an alternative (<s>vikalpa</s>), overriding (<s>bādha</s>), or combination (<s>samuccaya</s>)?
An alternative, because of [their] equal [strength]; let those that have [independent] scope be overridden by the designation. // MJaiNy_3,5.20 //
What is established by textual statement should not be overridden; here, in drinking, by differentiation,

children.text: siddhevikalpo no yuktaḥ svīkāryo 'taḥ samuccayaḥ // MJaiNy_3,5.21 //
children.translated_text: an alternative in what is already established is not appropriate; therefore, combination should be accepted. // MJaiNy_3,5.21 //

children.text:
'praitu hotuścamasaḥ, pra brahmaṇaḥ'- ityatra cimasiṣu samākhyā bhakṣaṇe hetuḥ |
'vaṣaṭkartuḥ prathamabhakṣaḥ' ityatra vaṣaṭkāro hoturbhakṣahetuḥ |
'havirdhāne grāvamirabhaṣutyā'havanīye hutvā sadasi bhakṣayanti' ityatrābhiṣavasahito homo 'dhvaryorbhakṣahetuḥ |
tatra camasavaṣaṭkārayoḥ saṃgho hotari prāptaḥ |
camasābhiṣavasaṃgho 'dhvaryau prāptaḥ |
tatra hetudvayasya samānabalatvādvikalpe satyanyatara nimittakṛtamevaṃ bhakṣaṇam- ityādyaḥ pakṣaḥ |
vaṣaṭkārādihetoścamasetaragrahe sāvakāśatvānniravakāśayā camasisamākhyayā tadbādhe sati camasiṣu pākṣikamapi vaṣaṭkārādi hetukaṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ nāsti- iti dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ |
'vaṣaṭkartuḥ' ityādivākyasya prabalatvātsamākhyayā bādho na yuktaḥ |
miravakāśatayā sāpi prabalā- iti cet |
tarhi pramāṇadvayena pṛthagbhakṣaṇe vihite samuccayo 'bhyupeyaḥ, na ca vrīhiyavavadvikalpaḥ |

children.translated_text: Because in that [barley-and-rice case], the visible purpose — the production of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake) — is single.
But here, the drinking pertaining to the unseen purpose (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) is [governed by] restriction.
And that unseen [merit] is of two kinds, in accordance with [each] statement.
Therefore, there is combination. || MJaiNyC_3,5.20-21 ||

In '<s>praitu hotuś camasaḥ, pra brahmaṇaḥ</s>' — here, regarding the cups, the designation is the cause of drinking. In '<s>vaṣaṭkartuḥ prathamabhakṣaḥ</s>' — here, the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> is the cause of the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s drinking. In '<s>havirdhāne grāvabhir abhiṣutyāhavanīye hutvā sadasi bhakṣayanti</s>' — here, the oblation combined with the pressing is the cause of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s drinking. Therein, the co-occurrence of cup and <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> applies to the <s>Hotṛ</s>. The co-occurrence of cup and pressing applies to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. Therein, the first view is: since the two causes are of equal strength, when there is an alternative, the drinking on each occasion is produced by only one of the causes. The second view is: since the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> and other causes have [independent] scope in [cases involving] cups other than the <s>camasī</s>, the cup-designation (<s>camasī-samākhyā</s>), being without independent scope, overrides them; thus, even the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>-based drinking that would otherwise [apply] in the cups does not exist. [The conclusion is:] Since the statements like '<s>vaṣaṭkartuḥ</s>' are more authoritative, overriding by the designation is not appropriate. If it be argued that the designation too is authoritative, having no [independent] scope [of its own] — then, since drinking is separately enjoined by two valid means of knowledge, a combination should be accepted, not an alternative as [in the case of] barley and rice.
(In the thirteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the first drinking of the <s>Hotṛ</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 36-39:)

children.text: ekapātre kramād adhvaryuḥ pūrvo bhakṣayet / Jaim_3,5.36 /
children.translated_text: When [the <s>Soma</s> is] in a single vessel, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should drink first, by sequence. / Jaim_3,5.36 /
Or the <s>Hotṛ</s>, because of the <s>mantra</s> wording. / Jaim_3,5.37 /
And because of the [explicit] statement. / Jaim_3,5.38 /
And because of the order of [causal] priority. / Jaim_3,5.39 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.22-23
He composes the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
When [the <s>Soma</s> is] in one vessel, should the <s>Adhvaryu</s> drink first, [since he] handles [the vessel] earlier?
Because the vessel rests in his hand, his first drinking [would follow]. // MJaiNy_3,5.22 //

children.text: pāhi hoteva naḥ pūrvamiti mantreṇa pūrvatā /
children.translated_text: 'Drink for us first, like the <s>Hotṛ</s>' — by this <s>mantra</s>, the priority [belongs to the <s>Hotṛ</s>];
and because [it is] stated for the one who utters the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>; a statement is not overridden by mere reasoning. // MJaiNy_3,5.23 //

children.text:
ekasminpātre vahanāṃ kvacidvihitaṃ bhakṣaṇam- tatra- adhvaryuḥ prathamaṃ bhakṣayetpātrasaṃnidhānāt - iti cet |
maivam |
liṅgavākyābhyāṃ hotuḥ prathamamakṣāvagamāt |
'hoteva naḥ prathamaḥ pāhi' iti ṛtvijo 'dhvaryu saṃbodhyaivaṃ prārthayante- 'yathā hotāsmattaḥ pūrve bhakṣayitvā śeṣapradānenāsmānpālitavān, tathā tvamapi vāhi' iti |
tadetaddhotuḥ prathamabhakṣe liṅgam |

children.translated_text: And the sentence is thus recited: '<s>vaṣaṭkartuḥ prathamabhakṣaḥ</s>' (the first drinking belongs to the one who utters the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>).
Therein, the priority is also established from the injunction of the qualified [drinking].

children.text: na caitadvacanaṃ pātrasaṃnidhirūpeṇa nyāyamātreṇa bādhituṃ śakyam |
children.translated_text: Nor can this statement be overridden by the mere reasoning based on the proximity of the vessel.
Therefore — the <s>Hotṛ</s> should drink first. || MJaiNyC_3,5.22-23 ||

When drinking is enjoined for multiple [priests] from a single vessel — therein, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should drink first because of the proximity of the vessel [to him] — if so it is argued, that is not correct. Because from the mark and the sentence, the first drinking of the <s>Hotṛ</s> is understood. The priests address the <s>Adhvaryu</s> thus: '<s>hotā iva naḥ prathamaḥ pāhi</s>' (drink for us first, like the <s>Hotṛ</s>) — they entreat him: 'Just as the <s>Hotṛ</s>, having drunk before us and giving us the remainder, has protected us, so you too should drink.' This is the mark indicating the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s first drinking.
Drinking is with prior permission, because of the [explicit] statement. / Jaim_3,5.40 /
(In the fourteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on drinking being preceded by permission, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
START MJaiNy 3,5.24
He composes the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the drinking not preceded by permission, or is it so preceded? The latter, here, by parsimony (<s>lāghava</s>);
the first [view is]: since what has not been invited should not be drunk — from this statement, the latter [is correct]. // MJaiNy_3,5.24 //
If both — the permission and the drinking — [are required] to be performed, then from the burden [of two acts], drinking alone [would suffice] — if so it is argued,
that is not correct.

children.text: 'tasmātsomāṃ nānupahūtena peyaḥ' iti vacanenānujñāyā āvaśyakatvāt || MJaiNyC_3,5.24 ||
children.translated_text: Because from the statement '<s>tasmāt somaṃ nānupahūtena peyaḥ</s>' (therefore <s>Soma</s> should not be drunk without being invited), the indispensability of permission [is established]. || MJaiNyC_3,5.24 ||
(In the fifteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on granting permission through a Vedic utterance, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
One should grant permission to the one [who is] invited, with [the words] '<s>upahvayasva</s>' (invite!), because of the mark. / Jaim_3,5.41 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.25
He composes the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: kimanujñā laukikoktyā vedoktyā vā yathā tathā /
children.translated_text: Is the permission [given] through a worldly utterance, or through a Vedic utterance? Either way,
since there is no distinction, [it could be either]; but from the mark of the invitation-<s>mantra</s>, it should be Vedic. // MJaiNy_3,5.25 //

children.text: 'upahūta upahvayasya'- ityayaṃ mantro liṅgena mantramanujñāyāṃ viniyuṅkte |
children.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> '<s>upahūta upahvayasva</s>' (O invoked one, summon!) assigns [its parts] to the invitation (<s>mantrānujñā</s>) by means of the mark.
Therefore, the permission is expressed through Vedic utterance. || MJaiNyC_3,5.25 ||
(In the sixteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the response through a Vedic sentence, the <s>sūtra</s>:)
Therein, from the meaning, a response [is given]. / Jaim_3,5.42 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.26-27
He composes the sixteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is '<s>upahvayasva</s>' (summon!) and '<s>upahūtaḥ</s>' (invoked) an undivided whole for both [the summoning and the permission],
or is it to be divided between the permission (<s>anujñā</s>) and the act of granting permission (<s>anujñāpana</s>)? // MJaiNy_3,5.26 //
Since there is no basis for division, it would be undivided — if so it is argued, [then] by the mark,
'<s>upahvayasva</s>' (summon!) [is assigned] to the granting of permission, and the other [part '<s>upahūtaḥ</s>'] likewise to the permission. // MJaiNy_3,5.27 //

children.text: 'upahūta upahūvayasva' ityasminmantre madhyamapuruṣekavacanānto bhāgaḥ paścātpaṭhito 'pi praścasamatvātprathamabhāvinyanujñāpane samarthaḥ |
children.translated_text: In this <s>mantra</s> '<s>upahūta upahvayasva</s>', the portion ending in the second-person singular, though recited later, is equal to [what comes] before in terms of sequence-fitness, and hence is capable of [being assigned to] the granting of permission, which occurs first.
And the portion ending in the first-person singular, though recited first, being equal to what follows, is capable of [being assigned to] the permission, which occurs afterwards.
Therefore, it is divided and assigned by means of the mark. || MJaiNyC_3,5.26-27 ||
(In the seventeenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the granting of permission for those sharing a single vessel, the <s>sūtra</s>:)
That [granting of permission applies] to those sharing a single vessel, because of their conjunction. / Jaim_3,5.43 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.28
He composes the seventeenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the summoning (<s>upahvāna</s>) for all [drinkers] without exception, or [only] for those sharing a single vessel?
The first [alternative], because of an unseen purpose; the latter, because of the greater [relevance of the] seen [purpose]. // MJaiNy_3,5.28 //

children.text:
anujñāpanasyādṛṣṭaṃ prayojanam |
tacca vibhinnapātreṣvapi samānam- iti cet |

children.translated_text: no.
Because a seen (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>) purpose exists.
In a commonly shared substance, when someone takes a greater share, an offense occurs.
Therefore, the granting of permission — which is motivated by the avoidance of [the dispute over] having less or more — applies only to those sharing a single vessel. || MJaiNyC_3,5.28 ||
The purpose of granting permission is unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>). And that [unseen purpose] is the same even for those with separate vessels — if so it is argued,
(In the eighteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the existence of the drinking right (<s>bhakṣa</s>) for the self-sacrificing [<s>yajamāna</s>], <s>sūtras</s> 44–45:)
The drinking right (<s>bhakṣa</s>), removed along with the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse), [is transferred] like the <s>pravara</s> (selection). / Jaim_3,5.44 /
Or it belongs to the sacrificer, because of the arrival of the cause. / Jaim_3,5.45 /
The <s>pravara</s> does not depart, because it has [already] commenced. / Jaim_3,5.46 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.29-30
He composes the eighteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
When the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s <s>yājyā</s> is removed [and given to the <s>yajamāna</s>], is there also no <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial call) and drinking for [the <s>Hotṛ</s>]?
The removal [applies], or there is no departure — because of the distinction [between the two]. // MJaiNy_3,5.29 //
The sacrifice must be performed by the <s>yajamāna</s> himself; the <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) cannot proceed without the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>;
since the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> accompanies the <s>yājyā</s>, the drinking also departs with it. // MJaiNy_3,5.30 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭoma ṛtuyājanāmakeṣu yāgeṣvāmnāyate-"yajamānasya yājyā so 'bhipreṣyati- hotaretadyaja- iti, svayaṃ vāṃ niṣadya yajati"iti |
hautre kāṇḍe samāmnātā yājyāḥ samākhyayā hotuḥ prāptāḥ |
tāsu kācidyājyā hoturapanīya yajamānasya vidhīyate |
tato yajamānaḥ svecchayā hotāraṃ vā preṣyati, svayaṃ vā yājyāṃ paṭhati |
tatra tvapāṭhapakṣe yājyā hoturapanīyate, na tu vaṣaṭkārabhakṣāvapanīyete |
tayoryājyāyāmanantarbhāvāt |
ato hotā vaṣaṭkaroti bhakṣayati ca iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- 'svayaṃ vā niṣadya yajati' iti pakṣasvīkārādyajamānena svayaṃ yāgaḥ kartavyaḥ |
sa ca yāgo vaṣaṭkāramantareṇa na saṃbhavati |
'yājyāyā adhi vaṣaṭkaroti' iti tadvidhānāt |
nanu- yajamāno yājyāṃ paṭhatu, hotā vaṣaṭkarotu- iti cet |

children.translated_text: that is not correct.

Because from the prohibition of breathing [between the <s>yājyā</s> and the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>] in '<s>anavānaṃ yajati</s>' (he offers without a breath), it is understood that both must have a single agent.
Therefore, the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> departs from the <s>Hotṛ</s> along with the <s>yājyā</s>.

children.text: tadapāye vaṣaṭkāranimitto bhakṣaśca hoturapetya yajamāne niviśate || MJaiNyC_3,5.29-30 ||
children.translated_text: And upon the departure of that [<s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>], the drinking — which is occasioned by the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> — also departs from the <s>Hotṛ</s> and is established in the <s>yajamāna</s>. || MJaiNyC_3,5.29-30 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, in the sacrifices called <s>Ṛtuyājana</s> (seasonal offerings), it is recorded: '<s>yajamānasya yājyā so 'bhipreṣyati — hotaretadyaja — iti, svayaṃ vā niṣadya yajati</s>' (the <s>yājyā</s> belongs to the <s>yajamāna</s>; he either directs [the <s>Hotṛ</s>] — 'O <s>Hotṛ</s>, offer this' — or, sitting down himself, offers). The <s>yājyās</s> recorded in the <s>Hautra</s> section (<s>kāṇḍa</s>) are obtained for the <s>Hotṛ</s> by designation (<s>samākhyā</s>). Among them, a certain <s>yājyā</s> is removed from the <s>Hotṛ</s> and assigned to the <s>yajamāna</s>. Then the <s>yajamāna</s>, at his own will, either directs the <s>Hotṛ</s> or himself recites the <s>yājyā</s>. Now, in the case where [the <s>yajamāna</s>] does not recite, the <s>yājyā</s> is removed from the <s>Hotṛ</s>, but the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial call) and the drinking (<s>bhakṣa</s>) are not removed — because they are not included within the <s>yājyā</s>. Therefore, the <s>Hotṛ</s> would [still] perform the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> and the drinking — having arrived at this position, we say: From the acceptance of the alternative 'or, sitting down himself, he offers (<s>svayaṃ vā niṣadya yajati</s>),' the <s>yajamāna</s> himself must perform the sacrifice. And that sacrifice is not possible without the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> — because of the injunction '<s>yājyāyā adhi vaṣaṭkaroti</s>' (he utters the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> over the <s>yājyā</s>). Now, [one might say:] let the <s>yajamāna</s> recite the <s>yājyā</s> and the <s>Hotṛ</s> utter the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> — if so it is argued,
(In the nineteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>phalacamasa</s> (fruit-cup) being a modification of the offering, <s>sūtras</s> 47–51:)
The <s>phalacamasa</s> (fruit-cup) is an occasional (<s>naimittika</s>) modification of the drinking (<s>bhakṣa</s>), because of the connection with the <s>śruti</s>. / Jaim_3,5.47 /
Or it is a modification of the offering (<s>ijyā</s>), because the consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) serves that purpose. / Jaim_3,5.48 /
Because of the oblation (<s>homa</s>). / Jaim_3,5.49 /
And because of being simultaneous with the [other] cups (<s>camasas</s>). / Jaim_3,5.50 /
And because of the observation of the mark. / Jaim_3,5.51 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.31-33
He composes the nineteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The ground fruit of the <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree, as a substitute for <s>Soma</s>, for <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s> —
should it modify the drinking alone, or the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice as well? // MJaiNy_3,5.31 //
The sentence is commenced and concluded with the intention of drinking;

children.text: bhakṣaṃ yacchediti tato vikāro bhakṣamātragaḥ // MJaiNy_3,5.32 //
children.translated_text: '<s>bhakṣaṃ yacchet</s>' (one should give the drink) — therefore the modification pertains to the drinking alone. // MJaiNy_3,5.32 //
Because it is heard '<s>phalākhya-camasena asau yajet</s>' (one should offer with the cup called <s>phala</s> [fruit-cup]),

children.text: ijyāyāṃ ca vikāro 'sti yāgārthā bhakṣasaṃskṛtiḥ // MJaiNy_3,5.33 //
children.translated_text: the modification applies to the offering (<s>ijyā</s>) as well; the consecration of the drink is for the purpose of the sacrifice. // MJaiNy_3,5.33 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate- 'yadi rājanyaṃ vaiśyaṃ vā yājayet, sa yadi somaṃ bibhakṣayipet, nyagrodhastibhinīrāhṛtya tāḥ saṃpiṣya dadhanyunmṛjya tamasyai bhakṣaṃ prayacchet, na somam' iti |
stibhinyo mukulāni |
tatra- upakramopasaṃhārayorbhakṣaviṣayatvādbhakṣamātre somaḥ piṣṭena vikriyate - iti cet |
maivam |
'yadānyāścamasāñjuhvati, athaitasya darbhataruṇakenoṣahatya juhoti' iti śrutam |
tatra phalacamasarūpeṇa yathoktapiṣṭena yāgamaṅgīkṛtya taruṇakaguṇo vidhīyate |
children.translated_text: Therein, accepting the sacrifice in the form of the fruit-cup with the aforementioned ground [substance], the quality of young <s>darbha</s> shoots is enjoined.
Moreover, the drink (<s>bhakṣa</s>) is the consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the desired material.
And that [consecration] is impossible without a sacrifice.
Therefore, the modification applies to the offering as well. || MJaiNyC_3,5.31-33 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, it is heard: '<s>yadi rājanyaṃ vaiśyaṃ vā yājayet, sa yadi somaṃ bibhakṣayiṣet, nyagrodha-stibhinīr āhṛtya tāḥ saṃpiṣya dadhnā unmṛjya tam asyai bhakṣaṃ prayacchet, na somam</s>' (if one would sacrifice for a <s>Kṣatriya</s> or <s>Vaiśya</s>, and if he wishes to give him the drink, one should bring the buds (<s>stibhinī</s>) of the <s>nyagrodha</s> tree, grind them, wash them with curds, and give him this as the drink — not <s>Soma</s>). '<s>Stibhinīs</s>' are buds. Therein, since the beginning and conclusion [of the passage] pertain to the drinking, <s>Soma</s> is modified by the ground [substance] only in the drinking — if so it is argued, that is not correct. Because it is heard: '<s>yadā anyāś camasāñ juhvati, athaitasya darbha-taruṇakena uṣahatya juhoti</s>' (when they offer the other cups, then for this one he offers by stirring with young <s>darbha</s> shoots).
(In the twentieth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on [only] <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> approaching the <s>Kṣatriya</s> cups, <s>sūtras</s> 52–53:)
Among those who approach [the cups], because of the general [rule]. / Jaim_3,5.52 /
Or by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, because of the identity of expression. / Jaim_3,5.53 /
START MJaiNy 3,5.34-35
He composes the twentieth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In the <s>Rājasūya</s>, in a certain [sacrifice], the cup of the sacrificer is to be drunk by ten persons —

children.text: makṣyaḥ kiṃ tatra rājanyā bhakṣakā brāhmaṇā uta // MJaiNy_3,5.34 //
children.translated_text: should those [ten] be <s>Kṣatriyas</s> as the drinkers, or <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>? // MJaiNy_3,5.34 //
The first [alternative], because of the indication [that they are of the same caste]; the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, [being] a hundred and ten by count of one caste,
drink the cups first — by this statement, the <s>Kṣatriya</s> vessel also goes to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. // MJaiNy_3,5.35 //

children.text:
rājasūye daśapeyanāmake yāge śrūyate- 'daśa daśaikaikaṃ camasamanuprasarpanti' iti |
tatra yajamānasya rājanyasya yaścamasaḥ, so 'yaṃ rājanyaireva daśabhirbhakṣaṇīyaḥ |
kutaḥ |
'daśa' iti saṃkhyāyā jātyekatvapratibhānāt |
tathā hi - daśapoyasya jyotiṣṭomavikṛtvātprākṛtaṃ dharmajātaṃ codakena prāptam |
prakṛtau ca - yajamānacamasasya bhinnajātibhirbhakṣaṇaṃ nāsti, ityatrāpi tathaiva praptam |
yadi- atra 'daśa' iti viśeṣo vidhīyate, tarhi prākṛtaṃ bhakṣasaṃkhyāmātraṃ nivartatām, natvekajātitvam |
children.translated_text: If the specific rule 'ten' is being enjoined here, then only the archetype rule regarding the number of drinkers should be set aside, but not the class-unity.

children.text: tasmāt- rājanyo yajamāno 'nyai rājanyairnavabhiḥ saha bhakṣayet- iti prāpte,- brūmaḥ- prakṛtitaḥ prāpteṣu daśasu camaseṣu bhakṣaṇāyāmuprasarpatāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ 'daśa, daśa, iti vīpsayā praticamasaṃ daśasaṃkhyāṃ vidhāyārthasiddhāṃ śatasaṃkhyāmanūdya saṃkhyeyānāṃ sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇyaṃ vidhīyate -'ṅgha śataṃ brāhmaṇāḥ pibanti' iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>Kṣatriya</s> <s>yajamāna</s> should drink with nine other <s>Kṣatriyas</s> — having arrived at this position, we say: Among the ten cups obtained from the archetype, the number of persons approaching each cup for drinking — by the repetitive use '<s>daśa daśa</s>' (ten, ten), [which] enjoins the number ten per cup, and by restating the hundred-count that is accomplished by implication — the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> status of all those to be counted is enjoined: '<s>aṅgha śataṃ brāhmaṇāḥ pibanti</s>' (indeed, a hundred <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> drink).

children.text: tathā sati- yajamānasyāpi rājanyasya yatra camasabhakṣo nāsti, tatra kuto 'nye rājanyā bhakṣayeyuḥ |
children.translated_text: This being so — even for the <s>yajamāna</s> who is a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, where there is no cup-drinking [for him], how would other <s>Kṣatriyas</s> drink?
Therefore, only <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are the drinkers. || MJaiNyC_3,5.34-35 ||

In the <s>Rājasūya</s>, in the sacrifice called <s>Daśapeya</s> (ten-drinks), it is heard: '<s>daśa daśa ekaikaṃ camasam anuprasarpanti</s>' (ten by ten approach each cup). Therein, the cup of the <s>yajamāna</s> who is a <s>Kṣatriya</s> — this cup should be drunk by ten <s>Kṣatriyas</s> only. Why? Because the number 'ten' evokes the notion of class-unity (<s>jātyekatva</s>). For thus — since the <s>Daśapeya</s> is a modification of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the entire class of archetype rules is obtained through the injunctive [texts]. And in the archetype, the <s>yajamāna</s>'s cup is not drunk by those of a different class — and so here too, this is likewise obtained.

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīye jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistare tṛtīyādhyāyasya pañcamaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Jaiminīya Nyāyamālā Vistara</s> of the illustrious <s>Mādhava</s>.
Now the sixth <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s>.
(In the first [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the archetype-reaching [scope] of injunctions regarding <s>khadira</s>-wood and the like for the ladle (<s>sruva</s>) and other [implements], <s>sūtras</s> 1–8:)
It is for all purposes, because it is not in [any specific] context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>). / Jaim_3,6.1 /
Or [it applies] to the archetype, because it is not stated [elsewhere]. / Jaim_3,6.2 /
But excluding that [archetype], when [the rule] is obtained by the statement [itself]. / Jaim_3,6.3 /
Because of observation — if so it is argued. / Jaim_3,6.4 /
No, because of the singleness of purpose of the injunction. / Jaim_3,6.5 /
If [it is argued that it pertains to] origination. / Jaim_3,6.6 /
No, because of equality [between archetype and modification]. / Jaim_3,6.7 /
But because the injunction is complete in its meaning, and because of the conflict with the primary [sense], it serves the archetype's purpose. / Jaim_3,6.8 /
START MJaiNy 3,6.1-2
He composes the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the sixth <s>pāda</s> —

children.text: prakṛtau vikṛtau vā syādyasya parṇetyasau vidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Does the injunction '<s>yasya parṇa</s>' (whose [ladle is made of] <s>Parṇa</s> [palāśa] wood) apply to the archetype, the modification, or both?
Or [it applies] to the archetype alone — equally from the statement, it [would apply] to both. // MJaiNy_3,6.1 //
The injunction of <s>Parṇa</s>-wood, being dependent on the <s>juhū</s> (ladle), applies only to the archetype;
since [the ladle] is obtained in both by the injunctive [text], what would an [additional] injunction accomplish in the modification? // MJaiNy_3,6.2 //

children.text:
anārabhya śrūyate- 'yasya parṇamayī jūhūrbhavati, na sa pāpaṃ ślokaṃ śṛṇoti' iti |
tatra- avyabhicaritakratusaṃbandhavatīṃ juhūmāśritya taddhetuḥ parṇavṛkṣo vākyena vidhīyate- 'yā juhūḥ sā parṇamayī' iti |
vākyaṃ ca prakṛtivikṛtyostulyameva pravartate |
ubhayatrā'śrayabhūtāyā juhvāḥ satvāt |
tasmāt- prakṛtivikṛtyorūmayorapyayaṃ vidhiḥ- iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- kimayaṃ vidhirvikṛtau codakātpūrve niviśate, paścādvā |
nā'dyaḥ |

children.translated_text: because the <s>juhū</s>, which is the basis, is impossible without the injunctive [text] [of the modification].

children.text: dvitīye tu parṇatvamapi juhvā sahaiva codakenātidiśyate |
children.translated_text: And in the second [case], the <s>Parṇa</s>-nature is also transferred (<s>atidiṣyate</s>) to [the modification] along with the <s>juhū</s> by the very injunctive [text].
Therefore, since a separate injunction would be purposeless, this injunction applies only to the archetype.

children.text: evaṃ 'yasya svādiraḥ strubo bhavati' ityudāharaṇīyam || MJaiNyC_3,6.1-2 ||
children.translated_text: Similarly, '<s>yasya svādirah struvo bhavati</s>' (he whose <s>sruva</s> ladle is of <s>svādira</s> wood) should be cited as an example. || MJaiNyC_3,6.1-2 ||

Without reference [to any specific context], it is heard: '<s>yasya parṇamayī juhūr bhavati, na sa pāpaṃ ślokaṃ śṛṇoti</s>' (he whose <s>juhū</s> ladle is made of <s>Parṇa</s> wood does not hear ill repute). Therein — based on the <s>juhū</s>, which has an invariable connection with the sacrifice, the <s>Parṇa</s> tree is enjoined by the sentence as the material: 'the <s>juhū</s> should be made of <s>Parṇa</s> wood.' And the sentence applies equally to both the archetype and the modification — because the <s>juhū</s>, which is the basis [of the injunction], exists in both. Therefore, this injunction applies to both the archetype and the modification — having arrived at this position, we say: Does this injunction apply to the modification before [it applies through] the injunctive [text], or after? Not the first —
(In the second [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the modification-reaching [scope] of the seventeen-count of the <s>sāmidhenī</s> verses, the <s>sūtra</s>:)

children.text: prakaraṇaviśeṣāt tu vikṛtau virodhi syāt / Jaim_3,6.9 /
children.translated_text: But because of the specific context, it would apply in the modification, being conflicting [with the archetype]. / Jaim_3,6.9 /
START MJaiNy 3,6.3-4
He composes the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The seventeen <s>sāmidhenī</s> [verses] — [do they apply] in the archetype or in the modification?
As before, in the archetype; this is optionally varied with the fifteen-count. // MJaiNy_3,6.3 //
The seventeen-count would apply in the modification; in the archetype, by the force of the context,
since [the count] is blocked by the fifteen-count, there being no [further] need, it ceases. // MJaiNy_3,6.4 //

children.text:
anārabhya śrūyate- 'saptadaśa sāmidhenīranubrūyāt' iti |
'pravo vājā abhidyava' - ityādyā agnisamindhanārthā ṛcaḥ sāmidhenyaḥ |
tāsāṃ sāptadaśyaṃ pūrvabhyāyena prakṛtigatam |
yadi prakṛtau 'pañcadaśa sāmidhenīranvāha' iti vidhiḥ syāt, tarhi pāñcadaśyasāptadaśye vikalpeyātām- iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- vikṛtāveva sāptadaśyaṃ niviśate |
prakṛtau pāñcadaśyenāvaruddhānāṃ sāmidhenīnāṃ saṃkhyākāṅkṣāyā abhāvāt |
na ca - prāñcadaśyasāptadaśyavākyayoḥ samānabalatvādavarodhā bhāvaḥ- iti śaṅkanīyam |

children.translated_text: because the fifteen-count has a greater [degree of] support from the context.
Therefore, the seventeen-count is established in modifications such as the <s>Mitravinda</s> ritual (<s>adhvara-kalpa</s>) and the like.
And the previous reasoning [of the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s>] does not apply here,
because there is no fault in a separate injunction, since the seventeen-count is not obtained through the injunctive [text of the modification]. || MJaiNyC_3,6.3-4 ||

Without reference [to any specific context], it is heard: '<s>saptadaśa sāmidhenīr anubrūyāt</s>' (one should recite seventeen <s>sāmidhenī</s> verses). The <s>Ṛk</s> verses beginning with '<s>pravo vājā abhidyavaḥ</s>' are the <s>sāmidhenīs</s>, which serve the purpose of kindling the fire (<s>agni-samidhana</s>). Their seventeen-count, by the previous reasoning, pertains to the archetype. If there were an injunction '<s>pañcadaśa sāmidhenīr anvāha</s>' (one recites fifteen <s>sāmidhenīs</s>) in the archetype, then the fifteen-count and seventeen-count would be optional alternatives — having arrived at this position, we say: The seventeen-count applies only to the modification. Because in the archetype, there is no need (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) for a number of <s>sāmidhenīs</s>, since [their number] is blocked by the fifteen-count. Nor should one suspect that the blocking does not hold because the sentences [enjoining] fifteen and seventeen have equal force —
(In the third [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the archetype-reaching [scope] of the occasional seventeen-count, the <s>sūtra</s>:)

children.text: naimittikaṃ tu prakṛtau tadvikāraḥ saṃyogaviśeṣāt / Jaim_3,6.10 /
children.translated_text: But the occasional [seventeen-count applies] to the archetype; that [occasional count] is a modification [of the archetype], because of the specific connection. / Jaim_3,6.10 /
START MJaiNy 3,6.5-6
He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The seventeen-count for the <s>Vaiśya</s> — [does it apply] in the modification or in the archetype?
As before, [the objection is:] if [it would remain in the archetype], no — because of the restriction [of the permanent rule] by the statement of the occasional [rule]. // MJaiNy_3,6.5 //
The <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) cited [the example]: 'One desiring [cattle] should draw [water] with a cow-milking [vessel]';
let that also [be considered], since the principle is the same here. // MJaiNy_3,6.6 //

children.text:
'saptadaśānubrūyādvaiśyasya' iti vihitaṃ vaiśyanimittaṃ sāptadaśyaṃ pūrvanyāyena vikṛtigatam- iti cet |
maivam |
naimittikenānena vacanena prakṛtigatasya nityasya pāñcadaśyasya vaiśyavyatirikta viṣayatayā saṃkocanīyatvāt |
nityaṃ sāmānyarūpatayā sāvakāśatvena ca durbalam |
naimittikaṃ tu viśeṣarūpatvaniravakāśatvābhyāṃ prabalam |

children.translated_text: Therefore — the seventeen-fold [chant] occasioned by the <s>Vaiśya</s> remains in the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>).
Here, the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> cited another [example]: 'He should draw water with a ladle (<s>camasa</s>); [or] with a cow-milking [vessel] for one desiring cattle.'
Therein — since [the use of] the ladle is confined to the archetype, the cow-milking [vessel] would [transfer to] the modified rite — this is the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>.

children.text: kāmanānimittakena godohanena nityasya camasasya niṣkāmaviṣayatayā saṃkocanīyatvātprakṛtāveva godohanam- iti rāddhāntaḥ || MJaiNyC_3,6.5-6 ||
children.translated_text: Since the permanent [rule about] the ladle must be restricted to the domain of those not desiring [cattle] by the cow-milking [vessel] which is occasioned by desire, the cow-milking [vessel] remains in the archetype alone — this is the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>). || MJaiNyC_3,6.5-6 ||

The seventeen-fold [chant] (<s>sāptadaśya</s>) occasioned by the <s>Vaiśya</s>, which is enjoined as 'he should recite seventeen [verses] for the <s>Vaiśya</s>,' would by the previous principle transfer to the modified rite (<s>vikṛti</s>) — if so argued, that is not so. Because the permanent fifteen-fold [chant] (<s>pāñcadaśya</s>) situated in the archetype must be restricted to a domain excluding the <s>Vaiśya</s> by this occasional statement. The permanent [rule], being general in form and having [other] scope, is weak. But the occasional [rule], being specific in form and without [other] scope, is strong.
(In the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the fire-establishment (<s>ādhāna</s>) is not an accessory of the <s>Pavamāna</s> <s>iṣṭis</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 11–13)
The fire-establishment (<s>agnyādheya</s>) is for the purpose of the <s>iṣṭis</s> (offerings), from the context. / Jaim_3,6.11 /
Or not, because those [<s>iṣṭis</s>] serve the purpose of that [fire]. / Jaim_3,6.12 /
And because of the observation of the mark. / Jaim_3,6.13 /
START MJaiNy 3,6.7-8
He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Would the fire-establishment (<s>ādhāna</s>) be an accessory of the <s>Pavamāna</s> and other <s>iṣṭis</s>, or not?
Since the fires are subsidiaries of the <s>iṣṭis</s>, [the <s>ādhāna</s>] through them would be an accessory of those [<s>iṣṭis</s>]. // MJaiNy_3,6.7 //
But since the <s>ādhāna</s> (fire-establishment) is taught without being inaugurated [by any sacrifice], it is not an accessory of anything;
since the <s>iṣṭis</s> are for the purpose of the fires, the <s>iṣṭi</s> is equivalent to the fire, and the fires belong to the <s>Agnihotra</s>. // MJaiNy_3,6.8 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate- 'agnaye pavamānāyāṣṭādaśakapālaṃ nirvapat, agnaye pāvakāya, agnaye śucaye' iti |
'vasante brāhmaṇo 'gnīnādadhīta' iti ca |
tatra- ādhānaṃ pavamānādīṣṭīnāmaṅgaṃ bhavet |
kutaḥ |
darśapūrṇamāsavikṛtiṣu pavamānādīṣṭiṣu codakaprāptānāmāhavamanīyādyagnīnāmiṣṭyaṅgatve satyagnidvārā tatsaṃskārarūpasyā'dhānasyāpi tadaṅgatāyā anivāryatvāt - iti cet |
maivam |
na hyetadādhānaṃ kasyacitkratoḥ prakaraṇe paṭhitam |
kiṃtu - anārabhyādhītam |
ato na kasyāpyetadaṅgam, kiṃtvādhānavadiṣṭīnāmapyagnisaṃskārārthatvātparasparaṃ nāstyaṅgāṅgibhāvaśaṅkā |
nanu- pavamāneṣṭhyaṅgatvābhāve 'gnisaṃskāravaiyarthyādagnidvārā tadaṅgatvaṃ yuktam- iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] In the absence of being an accessory of the <s>Pavamāna</s> <s>iṣṭi</s>, the consecration of the fire would be purposeless — therefore, through the fire, it is appropriate [for the <s>ādhāna</s>] to be an accessory thereof — if so argued,
no.
Because the assignment of the consecrated fires to subsequent rites like the <s>Agnihotra</s> and others is understood from their respective Vedic statements.
Therefore — the <s>ādhāna</s> is not an accessory. || MJaiNyC_3,6.7-8 ||

This is taught in the Veda: 'He should prepare an eighteen-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] for <s>Agni Pavamāna</s>, for <s>Agni Pāvaka</s>, for <s>Agni Śuci</s>.' And: 'In spring, a Brahmin should establish his fires.' Therein — the fire-establishment (<s>ādhāna</s>) would be an accessory of the <s>Pavamāna</s> and other <s>iṣṭis</s>. Why? Because when the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other fires — which are obtained through the injunction (<s>codaka</s>) for the <s>Pavamāna</s> and other <s>iṣṭis</s>, which are modifications of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> — become accessories of the <s>iṣṭis</s>, it is unavoidable that the <s>ādhāna</s>, which is the consecration of those fires, also becomes an accessory thereof — if so argued, that is not so. For this <s>ādhāna</s> is not recited in the context of any sacrifice. Rather — it is taught without being inaugurated [by any specific rite]. Therefore, it is not an accessory of anything. Since both the <s>ādhāna</s> and the <s>iṣṭis</s> serve the purpose of consecrating the fires, there is no suspicion of an accessory-principal relationship between them.
(In the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the <s>ādhāna</s> serves all purposes, <s>sūtras</s> 14–15)
For the purpose of [establishing] the archetype thereof, like other <s>anārabhyādhīta</s> (statements taught without inauguration). / Jaim_3,6.14 /
Or [it is] for all purposes, because the <s>ādhāna</s> has its own [appropriate] time. / Jaim_3,6.15 /
START MJaiNy 3,6.9-10
He composes the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: ādhānaṃ kiṃ prakṛtyarthe vahnimātreṇa vā yutam /
children.translated_text: Does the <s>ādhāna</s> serve the purpose of the archetype alone, or is it connected with any fire whatsoever?
Like the <s>parṇa</s> (palāśa-wood) [for the ladle], this is situated in the archetype through the channel of the consecrated fire. // MJaiNy_3,6.9 //
If [the fire] had merely a worldly form, [the <s>ādhāna</s>] would be purposeless — hence the connection with the sacrifice;
let the <s>parṇa</s> [wood] for the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other [ladles] be independent with respect to the Vedically prescribed [form]. // MJaiNy_3,6.10 //

children.text:
anārabhyādhītaṃ parṇamayītvaṃ yathā juhūpranāḍyā prakṛtau niviṣṭam, tathaivāgnipranāḍyā tatsaṃskārarūpamādhānaṃ prakṛtau niviśate- iti cet |
maivam |
vaiṣamyāt |
dvividho hi juhvā ākāraḥ- laukikaḥ śāstrīyaśca |
aratnimātradairghya hasamukhatvatvagbilatvādirūpo dṛśyamāno laukikaḥ |
apūrvīyatvākārastu śāstrīyaḥ |
tayorapūrvīyatvaṃ kratupraveśamantareṇa nāsti |
tatra yadi laukikākāramātre paryavasyati, tadā parṇamayītvaṃ viphalaṃ bhavet |
kāṣṭhāntareṇāpi tadākārasya susaṃpādatvāt |
aco 'pūrvīyatvāya parṇaḥ kratau praviṣṭaḥ |
āhavanīyādīnāṃ tveka eva śāstrīyākāraḥ |

children.translated_text: And that is produced only by the <s>ādhāna</s> through the power of the injunction, not otherwise.

children.text: tasmādādhānasya kratupraveśaṃ vinaiva śāstrīvāhavanīyādyākārasaṃpādanasamartha tvādagnihotreṇa tatsaṃyujyate |
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the <s>ādhāna</s> is capable of producing the Vedically prescribed form of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other [fires] without entering the sacrifice, it is connected with the <s>Agnihotra</s>.
This being so, unlike the <s>parṇa</s> [wood case], without entering the archetype, having produced the fires, [the <s>ādhāna</s>] stands independently with its own purpose.

children.text: tato laukikopāyasaṃpāditasuvarṇavrīhyādivadādhānasaṃpāditānāṃ svatantrāṇā mevā'havanīyādyagnīnāṃ paścādvākyaiḥ kratuṣu viniyogo 'stu || MJaiNyC_3,6.9-10 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as gold, rice, and the like acquired by worldly means [are independently used], let the independently established <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other fires produced by the <s>ādhāna</s> be assigned to the sacrifices afterward through [their respective] Vedic statements. || MJaiNyC_3,6.9-10 ||

Just as the <s>parṇa</s>-wood quality [of the ladle], taught without inauguration (<s>anārabhyādhīta</s>), is situated in the archetype through the channel of the ladle (<s>juhū</s>), similarly the <s>ādhāna</s>, being the consecration of the fire, would be situated in the archetype through the channel of the fire — if so argued, that is not so. Because of the dissimilarity. For the ladle has two aspects of form — worldly and Vedically prescribed (<s>śāstrīya</s>). The visible form — being of one <s>aratni</s> (cubit) in length, having an opening like a face, having a hole for the skin [wrapping] — this is the worldly [aspect]. But the aspect of producing an unprecedented [ritual effect] (<s>apūrvīyatva</s>) is the Vedically prescribed [aspect]. Of these two, the unprecedented character does not exist without entering the sacrifice. Therein, if [the <s>parṇa</s> quality] culminates in mere worldly form, then the <s>parṇa</s>-wood quality would be purposeless — because that form can be easily achieved with other woods as well. Therefore, for the sake of unprecedented character, the <s>parṇa</s> [wood] enters the sacrifice. But for the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other [fires], there is only one aspect — the Vedically prescribed.
(In the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the <s>Pavamāna</s> <s>iṣṭis</s> are to be performed with unconsecrated fire, <s>sūtras</s> 16–17)

children.text: tāsām agniḥ prakṛtitaḥ prayājavat syāt / Jaim_3,6.16 /
children.translated_text: Their fire [would come] from the archetype, like the <s>prayāja</s> (preliminary offering). / Jaim_3,6.16 /
Or not, because those [<s>iṣṭis</s>] serve the purpose of that [fire]. / Jaim_3,6.17 /
START MJaiNy 3,6.11-12
He composes the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Are the <s>Pavamāna</s> <s>iṣṭis</s> to be performed with consecrated fire, or are those <s>iṣṭis</s> [performable] without [consecrated fire]?
They should be performed with fire consecrated thereby, in accordance with the injunction (<s>codaka</s>). // MJaiNy_3,6.11 //

children.text: codakaḥ pavamāneṣṭau na tāṃ prāpayituṃ prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: The injunction (<s>codaka</s>) is unable to bring the <s>Pavamāna</s> <s>iṣṭi</s> to [fruition],
because of the non-accessory status of the <s>iṣṭi</s>, and because the <s>iṣṭi</s> [would not be] accomplished with unconsecrated [fire]. // MJaiNy_3,6.12 //

children.text:
pāvamānādīṣṭibhirāhavanīyādyagnayaḥ saṃskriyante |
saṃskṛteṣvagniṣvagnihotradarśapūrṇamāsādi kratavaḥpravartante |
tathā sati- vimatāḥ pavamāneṣṭayastābhiriṣṭibhiḥ saṃskṛte bahnau kartavyāḥ, iṣṭitvāt, itareṣṭivat |
codako 'pyevaṃ |
satyanugṛhīto bhavati |
etābhiriṣṭibhiḥ saṃskṛte bahnau prakṛtyanuṣṭhānāt- iti prāpte-
brūmaḥ- yadyapi pavamāneṣṭirvikṛtiḥ, tathāpi codako na tasyāṃ pavamāneṣṭau pavamāneṣṭi matideṣṭuṃ prabhavati |
children.translated_text: we say: even though the <s>Pavamāna</s> <s>iṣṭi</s> is a modification (<s>vikṛti</s>), the injunction cannot enjoin the <s>Pavamāna</s> <s>iṣṭi</s> as requiring the <s>Pavamāna</s> <s>iṣṭi</s> [as its own prerequisite].
Because the <s>Pavamāna</s> <s>iṣṭi</s> is not an accessory in the archetype, like the <s>prayāja</s> (preliminary offering).

children.text: kiṃca- 'etasyāḥ pavamāneṣṭeḥ saṃskṛtāgnisiddhyartha pavamāneṣṭyantarāṅgīkāre tatrāpi tathā' ityanavasthāyāmiṣṭireva na sidhyet |
children.translated_text: Moreover — if for the sake of accomplishing [this] <s>Pavamāna</s> <s>iṣṭi</s> with consecrated fire, another <s>Pavamāna</s> <s>iṣṭi</s> were accepted as its accessory, [and] the same [reasoning applied] there too — in this infinite regress, the <s>iṣṭi</s> itself would never be accomplished.

children.text: tasmāt- tābhiriṣṭibhirasaṃskṛte vahnau pavamāneṣṭayaḥ kartavyāḥ || MJaiNyC_3,6.11-12 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — the <s>Pavamāna</s> <s>iṣṭis</s> are to be performed with fire not consecrated by those <s>iṣṭis</s>. || MJaiNyC_3,6.11-12 ||

The <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other fires are consecrated by the <s>Pāvamāna</s> and other <s>iṣṭis</s>. When the fires are consecrated, the <s>Agnihotra</s>, <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, and other rites proceed. This being so — the <s>Pavamāna</s> <s>iṣṭis</s> in question should be performed with fire consecrated by those [very] <s>iṣṭis</s>, because they are <s>iṣṭis</s>, like other <s>iṣṭis</s>. The injunction (<s>codaka</s>) too supports this — [it is] confirmed by the performance according to the archetype — having arrived at this position,
(In the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the <s>upākaraṇa</s> and other [rites] have the properties of the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [animal sacrifice], <s>sūtras</s> 18–27)
The animal-sacrifice procedure is the same for all, because there is no distinction in the context. / Jaim_3,6.18 /
And because of the position (<s>sthāna</s>) of the first [animal sacrifice]. / Jaim_3,6.19 /

children.text: śvas tv ekeṣāṃ tatra prākśrutir guṇārthā / Jaim_3,6.20 /
children.translated_text: But for some, the prior Vedic statement there is for the purpose of a [secondary] attribute. / Jaim_3,6.20 /
If it be said that it is a time-injunction for what is distinguished thereby — / Jaim_3,6.21 /
No, because [the time-injunction] pertains to only one part. / Jaim_3,6.22 /
If [one argues] by the meaning — / Jaim_3,6.23 /
No, because of the conflict with the Vedic statement. / Jaim_3,6.24 /

children.text: sthānāt tu pūrvasya saṃskārasya tadarthatvāt / Jaim_3,6.25 /
children.translated_text: But because of the position of the first consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>), since it serves the purpose of that [first sacrifice]. / Jaim_3,6.25 /
And because of the observation of the mark. / Jaim_3,6.26 /
Or, [the Vedic statement would be] without injunctive force, because of [its serving] the purpose of a [secondary] attribute. / Jaim_3,6.27 /
START MJaiNy 3,6.13-15
He composes the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Are the principal rites such as the <s>upākaraṇa</s> (inaugural touching) regarding the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>, <s>Savanīya</s>, and <s>Anubandhya</s> animals

children.text: upākaraṇamukhyāstu dharmāḥ sādhāraṇa na vā // MJaiNy_3,6.13 //
children.translated_text: common [to all three], or not? // MJaiNy_3,6.13 //
Since they are recited in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> context, these [rites] are common;
if the animal-sacrifice properties are not adopted, they would be purposeless in the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice. // MJaiNy_3,6.14 //
Their property of belonging to the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [sacrifice] is established from the position (<s>sthāna</s>);

children.text: dvayoritarayoḥ paśrvoḥ prāpyante codakena te // MJaiNy_3,6.15 //
children.translated_text: for the other two animals, [these properties] are obtained through the injunction (<s>codaka</s>). // MJaiNy_3,6.15 //

children.text:
agnīṣomīyaḥ, savanīyaḥ, anubandhyaśca, ityete trayaḥ paśavo jyotiṣṭomaprakaraṇe samāmnātāḥ |
paśudharmāścopākaraṇaparyagnikaraṇādayastatrā'mnātāḥ |
'prajāpaterjāyamānāḥ' 'imaṃ paśum'- ityābhyāmṛgbhyāṃ paśorupasparśanamupākaraṇam |
darbhajvālayā triḥ pradakṣiṇīkaraṇaṃ paryagnikaraṇam |
ta ete dharmāstriṣvapi paśuṣu sādhāraṇyena vidhīyante |
trayāṇāmapi jyotiṣṭomaprakaraṇapāṭhasāmyāt |
nanu jyotiṣṭhomasya prakaraṇe paṭhitānetāndharmānsa eva grahīṣyati, na tu paśavaḥ- iti cet |
na |
tasya somayāgatvāt |
somo hyabhiṣavādīndharmānākā ṅkṣati, na tu yūpaniyojanaviśasanādīn |
tasmāt- aṅginyanarthakāḥ santo 'ṅgeṣu niviśamānā aviśeṣatastriṣvapi paśuṣvavatiṣṭhante- iti prāpte-
brūmaḥ- astyatra viśeṣaḥ saṃnidhilakṣaṇaḥ |
sautyanāmakādahnaḥ prācīna aupavasathyanāmake 'hni dhiṣṇyanirmāṇādūrdhvamete dharmā āmnātāḥ |

children.translated_text: The <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [animal sacrifice] also has that very same position [in time].

children.text: savanīyastu sautye 'hani śrūyate- 'āśvinaṃ grahaṃ gṛhītvā trivṛtā yūpaṃ parivīyā'gneyaṃ savanīyaṃ paśumupākaroti' iti |
children.translated_text: But the <s>Savanīya</s> is heard [as occurring] on the <s>Sautya</s> day — 'Having drawn the <s>Āśvina</s> cup, having wound [the rope] around the sacrificial post with a three-fold [winding], he inaugurates the <s>Āgneya Savanīya</s> animal.'
And the <s>Anubandhya</s> is taught at the end of the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath).

children.text: tataḥ saṃnidhinā te dharmā agnīṣomīye saṃbadhyante, savanīyānubandhyayostu codakādatidiśyante || MJaiNyC_3,6.13-15 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, by proximity, those properties are connected with the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>, and for the <s>Savanīya</s> and the <s>Anubandhya</s>, they are extended through the injunction (<s>codaka</s>). || MJaiNyC_3,6.13-15 ||

The <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>, the <s>Savanīya</s>, and the <s>Anubandhya</s> — these three animals are taught in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> context. And the animal-sacrifice properties such as the <s>upākaraṇa</s> (inaugural touching) and the <s>paryagnikaraṇa</s> (circumambulation with fire) are taught therein. The <s>upākaraṇa</s> is the touching of the animal with the two <s>Ṛk</s> verses '<s>prajāpaterjāyamānāḥ</s>' and '<s>imaṃ paśum</s>.' The <s>paryagnikaraṇa</s> is the three-fold clockwise circumambulation with a <s>darbha</s>-grass flame. These properties are enjoined as common to all three animals — because all three are equally recited in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> context. [Objection:] The <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> itself will adopt these properties recited in its context, not the animals — if so argued, no. Because [the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>] is a <s>Soma</s> sacrifice. For <s>Soma</s> requires properties like pressing (<s>abhiṣava</s>) and the like, not yoke-fastening, slaughtering, and the like. Therefore — being purposeless in the principal rite, [these properties], entering the accessories, remain in all three animals without distinction — having arrived at this position, we say: there is indeed a distinction here based on proximity (<s>saṃnidhi</s>). These properties are taught after the construction of the <s>dhiṣṇya</s> (fire-hearths), on the day called <s>Aupavasathya</s> (preparatory), which precedes the day called <s>Sautya</s> (pressing day).
(In the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the branch-cutting and other [rites] are properties of both milkings, <s>sūtras</s> 28–29)

children.text: dohayoḥ kālabhedād asaṃyuktaṃ śṛtaṃ syāt / Jaim_3,6.28 /
children.translated_text: Because of the temporal difference of the two milkings, the cooked [milk] would not be connected. / Jaim_3,6.28 /
Or, because of the division of the context, the time-instruction is for what is connected with that [context]. / Jaim_3,6.29 /
START MJaiNy 3,6.16-17
He composes the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The properties of the milking, such as branch-cutting and the like, are established in the evening [milking];

children.text: prātaśca santi vā sāyaṃ sthānātte pūrvavatsthitāḥ // MJaiNy_3,6.16 //
children.translated_text: do they exist in the morning [milking] as well, or, being established in the evening by position, are they [confined there] as before? // MJaiNy_3,6.16 //
The obstacle of purposelessness that [applied] before does not exist here;
therefore, since the context is stronger, they apply to the morning milking as well. // MJaiNy_3,6.17 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsaṃprakaraṇe - palāśaśākhāchedanam, tayā śākhayā vatsāpākaraṇam, ityādayo dohadharmāḥ samāmnātāḥ |
dohau ca dvau vidyete-amāvāsyāyāṃ rātrāveko dohaḥ |
pratipadi prātaraparo dohaḥ |
tatra pūrvanyāyena prāthamike sāyaṃdohe prathamaśrutāste dharmā vyavatiṣṭhante- iti cet |
maivam |

children.translated_text: Because of the dissimilarity.
For in the previous case, the properties such as slaughtering and the like have no applicability to <s>Soma</s>, so the context is obstructed by purposelessness.
But here, there is no such obstacle of purposelessness.

children.text: tataḥ prakaraṇena sthānaṃ bādhitvā dvayordohayoste dharmā abhyupeyāḥ || MJaiNyC_3,6.16-17 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, overriding the position by the context, those properties should be accepted for both milkings. || MJaiNyC_3,6.16-17 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context, the milking properties — cutting of a <s>palāśa</s> branch, driving away the calf with that branch, and the like — are taught. And there are two milkings — one milking on the night of the new moon, and another milking in the morning of the first day [of the new fortnight]. Therein, by the previous principle, those properties would be established in the first-heard evening milking — if so argued, that is not so.
(In the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the <s>sādana</s> (placing) and other [rites] are properties of [all] three pressings, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
Likewise, the teaching of the cup [properties] in the other pressings. / Jaim_3,6.30 /
START MJaiNy 3,6.18
He composes the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The cup-properties such as <s>sādana</s> (placing) and the like — do they belong to the morning pressing alone,
or to all three? The first [alternative holds] from the established position; the latter, as before. // MJaiNy_3,6.18 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome prātaḥsavane santyaindravāyavādayo grahāḥ, mādhyaṃdine savane marutvatīyādayaḥ, tṛtīyasavana ādityādayaḥ |
tatra sādanasaṃmārgādayo dharmāḥ prātaḥsavanīyagrahasaṃnidhāvāmnāyante - 'upopte 'nye grahāḥ sādyante, anupopte dhruvaḥ' iti |
'daśāpavitreṇa grahaṃ saṃmārṣṭi' iti ca |
dhruvavyatiriktānāṃ grahāṇāmadhastānmṛttikopaveśanaṃ kṛtvā tatra sādanam, dhruvasya tu na tathā |
pūrvādhikaraṇe śāśāharaṇādayaḥ pradhānayordadhipayasorrdhamāḥ samāmnātāḥ |

tacca dadhi pūrvodyuḥ sāyaṃdohamantareṇa na sidhyatīti tatsiddhyarthe kevalaṃ sāyaṃ duhyate, na tu sāyaṃdohasyāsādhāraṇa tvena dharmaiḥ sahaikasmindeśe pāṭho 'stīti sthānaṃ na niścitam, iha tu tanniścitamiti prātaḥsavana eva te dharmā iti cet |
children.translated_text: And that curd is not obtained without the previous day's evening milking; therefore, purely for its accomplishment, there is an evening milking — but since no recitation of the properties specific to the evening milking is found together [with it] in one place, the location is not fixed. But here [in the case of the cup-drawings], the location is fixed — therefore, those properties belong to the morning pressing alone — if so [it is argued],
that is not correct.

children.text: sādanādīnāṃ vākyena grahadharmatvaṃ, prakaraṇena jyotiṣṭomadharmatvaṃ cāvagamyate |
children.translated_text: The property of belonging to the cup-drawings for the settling and the like is understood from the sentence, and the property of belonging to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is understood from the context.

children.text: tasminniścitamapi sthānaṃ vākyaprakaraṇābhyāṃ bādhitvā triṣu sabaneṣu sādanādayo 'vatiṣṭhante || MJaiNyC_3,6.18 ||
children.translated_text: Even though the location is fixed therein, overriding it by the sentence and the context, the settling and the like apply to all three pressings. || MJaiNyC_3,6.18 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, at the morning pressing (<s>prātaḥsavana</s>) there are the <s>Aindravāyava</s> and other cup-drawings (<s>grahas</s>); at the midday pressing (<s>mādhyaṃdina savana</s>), the <s>Marutvatīya</s> and others; at the third pressing, the <s>Āditya</s> and others. Therein, the properties such as settling (<s>sādana</s>), wiping (<s>saṃmārga</s>), and the like are recited in proximity to the morning-pressing cup-drawings: '<s>upopte 'nye grahāḥ sādyante, anupopte dhruvaḥ</s>' (the other cup-drawings are settled on what is spread [with earth]; the <s>Dhruva</s> cup is [settled] on what is not spread). And '<s>daśāpavitreṇa grahaṃ saṃmārṣṭi</s>' (he wipes the cup-drawing with a ten-[strand] purifier). For the cup-drawings other than the <s>Dhruva</s>, settling is done after placing earth below; for the <s>Dhruva</s>, it is not so. In the preceding <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the properties such as the drawing of the <s>śāśa</s> and the like were recited as belonging to the two principal [substances], curds and milk.
(In the tenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the universality of the rope's triple-twisting and other properties for all animal [sacrifices], the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
And the rope (<s>raśanā</s>), because of the observation of the mark. / Jaim_3,6.31 /
He composes the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
START MJaiNy 3,6.19-18*
The wrapping with the rope and the like — in one [animal sacrifice] only, or in all?
