In the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [animal sacrifice] alone, by sequence; but by the mark, the latter [view holds: in all]. // MJaiNyC_3,6.18* //

children.text:
agnīṣomīyapaśusaṃnidhau raśanayā yūpasya veṣṭanam, raśanāyāstrivṛttvaṃ darbhamayatvaṃ ca, ityādayo dharmā āmnātāḥ- 'parivyayati, ūrgvai raśanā' iti, 'triṣṛdbhavati' iti, 'darbhamayī bhaviti' iti ca |
tatra yeyaṃ raśanā, ye ca veṣṭanādayaḥ, te sarve saṃnidheravāntaraprakaraṇā dvāgnīṣomīya eva syuḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
savanīyapaśāvapi tatsadbhāvo liṅgādavagamyate |
'trivṛtā yūpaṃ parinīyā'gneyaṃ savanīyaṃ paśumupākaroti' iti trivṛttvaparivyāṇayoḥ siddhavadanuvādoliṅgam |
children.translated_text: '<s>Trivṛtā yūpaṃ parinīyā'gneyaṃ savanīyaṃ paśumupākaroti</s>' (having wrapped the sacrificial post with the triple-twisted [rope], he commences the <s>Āgneya Savanīya</s> animal [sacrifice]) — the restatement of the triple-twisting and the wrapping as if already established is the mark.

children.text: kiṃca tṛtīyāśrutyā vākyena ca parivyāṇasya yūpadharmatā, na tu paśudharmatā |
children.translated_text: Moreover, by the third-case <s>śruti</s> and by the sentence, the wrapping is a property of the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>), not of the animal.

children.text: yūpaśca trayāṇāṃ paśūnāṃ tantram, iti vakṣyate |
children.translated_text: And the sacrificial post is the common element (<s>tantra</s>) of [all] three animals — this will be stated later.

children.text: tasmāt- sarveṣu paśudhvete dharmāḥ syuḥ || MJaiNyC_3,1.18* ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — these properties should apply to all animal [sacrifices]. || MJaiNyC_3,1.18* ||

In proximity to the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal [sacrifice], the properties are recited — the wrapping of the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) with the rope (<s>raśanā</s>), the triple-twisting of the rope, its being made of <s>darbha</s> grass, and so on: '<s>parivyayati, ūrgvai raśanā</s>' (he wraps around; the rope is vigor), '<s>trivṛdbhavati</s>' (it is triple-twisted), '<s>darbhamayī bhavati</s>' (it is made of <s>darbha</s>). Therein, this rope and the wrapping and other [properties] — all being recited in the sub-context of the proximity [to the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>] — would belong only to the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [sacrifice] — if so [it is argued], that is not correct. Because their presence in the <s>Savanīya</s> (pressing-day) animal [sacrifice] also is understood from the mark.
(In the eleventh [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>Aṃśu</s> and <s>Ādābhya</s> [cups] also possessing the properties of settling and the like, <s>sūtras</s> 32–34)

children.text: ārāc chiṣṭam asaṃyuktam itaraiḥ saṃnidhānāt / Jaim_3,6.32 /
children.translated_text: What is taught from afar (<s>ārāt</s>) is not connected with the others, because of proximity [to its own context]. / Jaim_3,6.32 /

children.text: saṃyuktaṃ vā tadarthatvāc cheṣasya tannimittatvāt / Jaim_3,6.33 /
children.translated_text: Or it is connected, because it serves that [common] purpose, and the remainder depends on that. / Jaim_3,6.33 /
It would be determined from the specific indication. / Jaim_3,6.34 /
START MJaiNy 3,6.19
He composes the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Do the cup-drawing properties exist in the <s>Aṃśu</s> and <s>Ādābhya</s> [cups that are] recited without being initiated [into the context], or not?
They do exist, by the context; or, by the sentence and so on, the latter [view holds]. // MJaiNy_3,6.19 //

children.text:
anārabhya dvau grahau śrutau- 'aṃśuṃ gṛhṇāti' iti, 'adābhyaṃ gṛhṇāti' iti ca |
tayoḥ sādanasaṃmārgādayo grahadharmā na vidyante |
kutaḥ |
ārabhyādhīteṣvaindravāyavādiṣveva prakaraṇena vyavasthāpitatvāt - iti cet |
maivam |
'grahāḥ sādyante' ityādivākyena grahadharmatvāvagame tayorapi grahayoranivārya tvāt |
children.translated_text: Because when the sentence '<s>grahāḥ sādyante</s>' (the cup-drawings are settled) and the like establishes [settling etc.] as properties of cup-drawings, those two cup-drawings also cannot be excluded.
And the <s>Aindravāyava</s> and others are not the contextual principal (<s>prakaraṇin</s>).
For the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is the contextual principal.
Therefore, those [settling and other] properties do exist in those two [cup-drawings]. || MJaiNyC_3,6.19 ||

Two cup-drawings are heard without being initiated [into the main context]: '<s>aṃśuṃ gṛhṇāti</s>' (he draws the <s>Aṃśu</s> [cup]) and '<s>adābhyaṃ gṛhṇāti</s>' (he draws the <s>Ādābhya</s> [cup]). For those two, the cup-drawing properties of settling, wiping, and the like do not exist. Why? Because they are established by the context only for the <s>Aindravāyava</s> and other [cups] that are recited within the initiated [context] — if so [it is argued], that is not correct.
(In the twelfth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the subsidiarity of the <s>Citriṇī</s> and other bricks to the fire-altar, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
An accessory of the fire-altar, [even] outside the context — similarly. / Jaim_3,6.35 /
START MJaiNy 3,6.20-21
He composes the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The properties of the bricks — intactness (<s>akhaṇḍa</s>) and the like — are they not applicable to the <s>Citriṇī</s> and other [bricks]?

children.text: santi vā vākyamapyatrānārabhyoktaṃ tato na te // MJaiNy_3,6.20 //
children.translated_text: Or do they exist? The sentence here too is recited without being initiated [into the context]; therefore they do not [apply]. // MJaiNy_3,6.20 //
Because of the connection with the <s>apūrva</s> (novelty) of what is contextually established, even from such a sentence [recited outside the context],
intactness and the like, serving the fire-altar's purpose, do exist in the <s>Citriṇī</s> and other [bricks]. // MJaiNy_3,6.21 //

children.text:
anārabhya śrūyate- 'citriṇīrupadadhāti' iti |
agniprakaraṇe ceṣṭakānāṃ dharmāḥ śrutāḥ- 'akhaṇḍāmakṛṣṇāṃ kuryāt' iti |
pūrvatra- aṃśvadābhyayorutpattivākyasyānārabhyādhītatve 'pi viniyojakavākyaṃ prakaraṇādhītam |
citriṇyādināmakānāṃ tviṣṭakāviśeṣāṇāṃ viniyojakaṃ vākyamapyanārabhyāghītam |
tacca cityantare tāścitriṇīrviniyuṅkte |
akhaṇḍatvādidharmāstu ṣaṇṇāṃ citīnāṃ madhye prathamacitāvāmnātāḥ |
tasmāt- te citriṇyādiṣu nocitāḥ- iti prāpte, -
children.translated_text: Therefore — they are not applicable to the <s>Citriṇī</s> and others — having arrived at this position,

children.text: brūmaḥ- yadyapyutpattiviniyojakavākyayoranyatarasyāpi prakaraṇapāṭho nāsti, tathāpi 'ya evaṃ vidvānagniṃ cinute' iti prakṛtaṃ yadetadagnyapūrve tatsaṃbandhitvenaivacitriṇyādayo 'pyaprakaraṇa paṭhitenāpi vākyena viniyujyante |
children.translated_text: we say: Even though neither the origination nor the assignment sentence is recited in the context, nevertheless, since the fire-altar — which is the contextual subject introduced by '<s>ya evaṃ vidvānagniṃ cinute</s>' (he who, knowing thus, constructs the fire-altar) — is connected with the <s>apūrva</s> (originating novelty) of that, the <s>Citriṇī</s> and other [bricks] too are assigned by the sentence, even though recited outside the context.
And the properties of intactness and the like are properties of the bricks that serve as means for [constructing] the fire-altar, not properties of the first layer.

children.text: tasmāt- agnisādhanabhūtāsu citriṇyādīṣṭakāsvapi te santi || MJaiNyC_3,6.20-21 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — those [properties] exist also in the <s>Citriṇī</s> and other bricks that serve as means for the fire-altar. || MJaiNyC_3,6.20-21 ||

It is heard without being initiated [into the context]: '<s>citriṇīrupadadhāti</s>' (he places the <s>Citriṇī</s> [bricks]). And in the fire-altar context, the properties of the bricks are heard: '<s>akhaṇḍāmakṛṣṇāṃ kuryāt</s>' (one should make [the brick] unbroken and not black). In the previous [case], even though the origination-sentence of the <s>Aṃśu</s> and <s>Ādābhya</s> [cups] was recited without being initiated [into the context], the assignment-sentence was recited within the context. But for the <s>Citriṇī</s> and other specific bricks, even the assignment-sentence is recited without being initiated [into the context]. And that [sentence] assigns those <s>Citriṇī</s> [bricks] in a different layer of the fire-altar. The properties of intactness and the like, however, are recited in the first layer among the six layers.
(In the thirteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the pressing (<s>abhiṣava</s>) and the like being properties of <s>Soma</s> alone, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
The occasional [substance], being unequal, would have a different procedure. / Jaim_3,6.36 /
START MJaiNy 3,6.22-23
He composes the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: vidhayo 'bhiṣavādyāḥ syuḥ phalākhye camase na vā /
children.translated_text: Do the injunctions of pressing (<s>abhiṣava</s>) and the like apply to the <s>Phalacamasa</s> (fig-pulp cup) or not?
Since the occasional is equal to the permanent, that injunction [does apply]. // MJaiNy_3,6.22 //
The consecrations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) that have achieved their purpose in the permanent [substance] — in the subsequently arising occasional [substance],

children.text: na vidheyāḥ kiṃtu tatra prāpyantāmatideśataḥ // MJaiNy_3,6.23 //
children.translated_text: [they are] not to be enjoined; rather, they are obtained therein by transfer (<s>atideśa</s>). // MJaiNy_3,6.23 //

children.text:
nyagrodhamukularūpasya phalasya piṣṭaṃ camyate yatra sa phalacamasaḥ |
sa ca naimittikaḥ |
rājanyavaiśyau nimittīkṛtya vihitatvāt |
somastu nityaḥ |
upādhikramamapyanupajīvyaiva 'somena yajeta' iti vihitatvāt |
tasya ca nitvasya somasya yathā yāgasādhanatvam, tathā phalacamasasyāpi tadasti |
tasmāt 'somamabhipuṇoti' 'somaṃ krīṇāti' ityādayo yāgadravya saṃskāravidhayaḥ soma iva phalacamase 'pi pravartante- iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- nityā abhikvādisaṃskārā nityaṃ somaṃ saṃskārya labdhvā caritārthāḥ santo nānyaṃ saṃskāryamapekṣante |
phalacamasastu soyavikāratvātpaścādbhāvī |
tato nirapekṣāḥ saṃskāravidhayo na tatra pravartante |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the consecration-injunctions, being without [further] expectation, do not apply therein.
But this does not mean the consecrations are absent.
They are established by the enjoining [authority] (<s>codaka</s>).
Therefore — the injunctions pertain to <s>Soma</s> alone. || MJaiNyC_3,6.22-23 ||

The <s>Phalacamasa</s> is [a cup] in which the paste of fruit in the form of banyan buds (<s>nyagrodhamukula</s>) is placed. And it is occasional (<s>naimittika</s>). Because it is enjoined with the <s>Rājanya</s> (nobleman) and the <s>Vaiśya</s> (merchant) as the occasion. But <s>Soma</s> is permanent (<s>nitya</s>). Because it is enjoined as '<s>somena yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>) without depending on any limiting condition. And just as the permanent <s>Soma</s> serves as the sacrificial substance, so too does the <s>Phalacamasa</s>. Therefore, the injunctions of consecration for the sacrificial substance — '<s>somamabhiṣuṇoti</s>' (he presses the <s>Soma</s>), '<s>somaṃ krīṇāti</s>' (he purchases the <s>Soma</s>) and the like — apply to the <s>Phalacamasa</s> just as to <s>Soma</s> — having arrived at this position, we say: The permanent consecrations of pressing and the like, having consecrated the permanent <s>Soma</s> and fulfilled their purpose, do not require another substance to consecrate. But the <s>Phalacamasa</s>, being a modification of <s>Soma</s>, arises subsequently.
(In the fourteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the performance of the properties of the original even in substitutes, <s>sūtras</s> 37–39)
And the substitute, similarly. / Jaim_3,6.37 /
Similarly, because the purpose is one. / Jaim_3,6.38 /
And because [the substitute] is not characterized by scripture [as different]. / Jaim_3,6.39 /
START MJaiNy 3,6.24
He composes the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
For the substitute such as <s>nīvāra</s> (wild rice) — is the injunction unequal, or equal?
First [there would be] inequality; [but there is] equality, because of the form — since <s>vrīhi</s>-nature [applies]. // MJaiNy_3,6.24 //

children.text:
'vrīhibhiryajeta' iti vihitānāṃ vrīhīṇāmasaṃbhave nībārāḥ pratinidhitvena svīkāryā iti vakṣyate |
tatra pūrvanyāyenāvaghātādividhayo vrīhiṣu kṛtārthāḥ paścādbhāvini nīvārādau na pravartante- iti cet |

children.translated_text: that is not correct.
For the word '<s>vrīhi</s>' denotes a substance possessing either a specific species or a specific form.

children.text: nīvāreṣu jātito vrīhiśabdārthatvābhāve 'pyākārato vrīhiśabdārthatvena 'vrīhīnavahanti' iti vidhiḥ pravartate |
children.translated_text: In the <s>nīvāra</s> grains, even though the species-based meaning of the word '<s>vrīhi</s>' is absent, the injunction '<s>vrīhīnavahanti</s>' (they bring <s>vrīhi</s>) applies because of the form-based meaning of the word '<s>vrīhi</s>'.

children.text: yathā vrīhijātāveva samīcīnānāṃ vrīhīṇāmabhāve jalavahnyādyupaghātena sāravikaleṣvapi vidhiḥ, tathā jātivikaleṣvapi brīhiṣu mukhyaikadeśarūpatvādvidhirastu || MJaiNyC_3,6.24 ||
children.translated_text: Just as, even in the <s>vrīhi</s> species itself, when proper <s>vrīhi</s> grains are unavailable, the injunction applies even to those deficient in essence due to damage by water, fire, and the like, so too in the case of grains deficient in species, let the injunction apply because they partially share the form of the primary [substance]. || MJaiNyC_3,6.24 ||

It will be stated that when the <s>vrīhi</s> (rice) grains enjoined in '<s>vrīhibhiryajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice with rice) are unavailable, <s>nīvāra</s> (wild rice) is to be accepted as a substitute. Therein, by the preceding principle, the injunctions of threshing (<s>avaghāta</s>) and the like, having achieved their purpose in the <s>vrīhi</s> [rice], do not apply to the subsequently arising <s>nīvāra</s> and such — if so [it is argued],
(In the fifteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the performance of properties of the original even in scripturally [indicated] substitutes, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
The <s>śruti</s> regarding the subordinate [element] serves the purpose of restriction (<s>niyama</s>). / Jaim_3,6.40 /
START MJaiNy 3,6.25
He composes the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the pressing of <s>Pūtīka</s> [plants as a <s>Soma</s> substitute] unequal, or equal? Because of the equality with <s>Soma</s>,
it is not [equal] because of being occasional; [but it is] equal because of being a substitute. // MJaiNy_3,6.25 //

children.text:
'yadi somaṃ na vindeta, pūti(tī) kānabhiṣuṇuyāt' iti śrūyate |
tatra somābhāvaṃ nimittīkṛtya pūtīkalatākhaṇḍānāṃ vihitatvātphalacamasavannaimittikatvena somābhiṣavakrayādividhiḥ pūtīkeṣu na tulyaḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
nīvārabatpratinidhitvāt |
nanu- pratinidhitve svayamevopāditsitatvādvidhirnāpekṣitaḥ |
ata eva nīvāreṣu vidhirna śrutaḥ- iti cet |
children.translated_text: For this very reason, no injunction is heard regarding the <s>nīvāra</s> — if so [it is argued],
no.
Because the injunction serves the purpose of restriction (<s>niyama</s>) — this will be stated in the sixth [<s>adhyāya</s>].
Therefore — the injunctions of pressing, purchasing, and the like are equal for <s>Soma</s> and <s>Pūtīka</s>. || MJaiNyC_3,6.25 ||

It is heard: '<s>yadi somaṃ na vindeta, pūtīkānabhiṣuṇuyāt</s>' (if one does not find <s>Soma</s>, one should press <s>Pūtīka</s> [plants]). Therein, since the <s>Pūtīka</s> creeper-segments are enjoined with the absence of <s>Soma</s> as the occasion, like the <s>Phalacamasa</s>, the injunctions of pressing, purchasing, and the like for <s>Soma</s> would not apply equally to the <s>Pūtīka</s> because of its being occasional — if so [it is argued], that is not correct. Because, like the <s>nīvāra</s> (wild rice), it is a substitute. But — in the case of a substitute, since it is itself desired to be accepted [in place of the original], no injunction is needed.
(In the sixteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the subsidiarity of the consecration-day (<s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s>) and other properties to the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 41–47)
The conclusions (<s>saṃsthās</s>) have the same procedure, because there is no distinction of context. / Jaim_3,6.41 /
And the designation, similarly. / Jaim_3,6.42 /

children.text: vikārās tu kāmasaṃyoge nityasya samatvāt / Jaim_3,6.43 /
children.translated_text: But the modifications (<s>vikāras</s>) [exist only] when there is connection with desire, because of the equality with the permanent. / Jaim_3,6.43 /

children.text: api vā dviruktatvāt prakṛter bhaviṣyantīti / Jaim_3,6.44 /
children.translated_text: Or, because of the double recitation, they will belong to the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>). / Jaim_3,6.44 /
But because of the verbal statement, there is a combination (<s>samuccaya</s>). / Jaim_3,6.45 /
And because of the prohibition of the former marks. / Jaim_3,6.46 /
The designation applies to one, because of the specific subordinate [element]. / Jaim_3,6.47 /
START MJaiNy 3,6.26-27
He composes the sixteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In the <s>Ukthya</s> and other [sacrifices], is the injunction of accessories such as the consecration-day (<s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s>) the same, or not?
Because of being in the same context and because of having [their own] fruit, there is equality. // MJaiNy_3,6.26 //
The <s>Ukthya</s> and others, being connected with desire, are modifications (<s>vikāras</s>); therefore, the procedure
is [established] in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> that has the nature of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, and that injunction is in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> alone. // MJaiNy_3,6.27 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭomaḥ- svayameko 'pi samāptibhedādbhidyate |
yajñāyajñiyastotreṇa samāptau 'agniṣṭomaḥ' ityucyate |
tasmādapi stotrādūrdhvamukthyastotreṇa samāptau 'ukthyaḥ' ityucyate |
evaṃ ṣoḍaśyādayo 'pi |
tādṛśasya saptasaṃsthāvato jyotiṣṭomasya prakaraṇe dīkṣaṇīyeṣṭiprāyaṇīyeṣṭyādīnāmaṅgānāṃ vidhirāmnātaḥ |
sa ca vidhirjyotiṣṭomasya prathamasaṃsthāviśeṣe 'gniṣṭome yathā pravṛttaḥ, tathaivokthyādiṣvapi pravartate |
kutaḥ |
prakaraṇasaṃbandhasya samānatvāt |
kiṃca- yathāgniṣṭomaḥ phalatvādaṅgavidhibhiḥ saṃyujyate, evamukthyādayo 'pi |
teṣāṃ ca phalamevamāmnāyate-'paśukāma ukthyaṃ gṛhṇīyāt' 'ṣoḍaśinā vīryakāmaḥ stuvīta' 'atirātreṇa prajākāmaṃ yājayet' iti |
tasmāt - saptasvapi saṃsthāsu samāno 'ṅgavidhiḥ- iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- yadetadukthyādīnāṃ phalamudāhṛtam, tattu teṣāṃ vikāratvaṃ gamayati |
'kāmyo guṇaḥ śrūyamāṇo nityamartha vikṛtya niviśate' iti nyāyādyathā godohanaguṇo nityaṃ camasasādhanakamapāṃ praṇayanaṃ vikṛtya niviśate,evamukthyaguṇo nityāmagniṣṭomasya saṃsthāṃ vikṛtya saṃsthāntaratvaṃ gamayati |
tato 'gniṣṭomasya guṇavikārā ukthyādaya iti na sarvasaṃsthāsādhāraṇaṃ prakaraṇam, kiṃtu - agniṣṭomasyai vāsādhāraṇama |
nanu- 'jyotiṣṭomena yajeta' ityuktatvājjyotiṣṭomasyedaṃ prakaraṇam, na tvagniṣṭomasaṃsthāyāḥ- iti cet |
bāḍham |
asā jyotiṣṭomo na kadācidapyagniṣṭomaṃ vyabhicarati |
ukthyādīnāmapyantarbhāvitāgniṣṭomakatvāt |

children.translated_text: But it does deviate from the Ukthya and the rest,
because the Jyotiṣṭoma-nature is possible even without them, in the Agniṣṭoma-form alone.

children.text: ato 'gniṣṭomasaṃsthasya jyotiṣṭomasyedaṃ prakaraṇaṃ sattatraiva dīkṣaṇīyādyaṅgavidhiṃ niveśayati |
children.translated_text: Therefore, this context — being of the Jyotiṣṭoma that has the Agniṣṭoma as its conclusion — establishes the accessory-injunctions of the Dīkṣaṇīya and the like therein alone.
In the Ukthya and the rest, the accessories are extended by the injunctive force (codaka). || MJaiNyC_3,6.26-27 ||

The Jyotiṣṭoma — though one in itself, is divided by differences in conclusion (samāpti). When concluded with the Yajñāyajñiya stotra, it is called 'Agniṣṭoma.' When concluded with the Ukthya stotra beyond that stotra, it is called 'Ukthya.' Similarly the Ṣoḍaśī and the rest. In the context (prakaraṇa) of the Jyotiṣṭoma possessing seven such forms (saptasaṃsthā), the injunction of accessories such as the Dīkṣaṇīyeṣṭi (consecration-offering), Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi (setting-forth offering) and the like is recited. And that injunction, just as it operates in the Agniṣṭoma — the first particular form of the Jyotiṣṭoma — operates equally in the Ukthya and the rest. Why? Because the connection with the context is the same. Moreover — just as the Agniṣṭoma, being the fruit-bearer, is conjoined with the accessory-injunctions, so too are the Ukthya and the rest. And their fruit is recited thus: 'paśukāma ukthyaṃ gṛhṇīyāt' (one desiring cattle should take the Ukthya [cup]), 'ṣoḍaśinā vīryakāmaḥ stuvīta' (one desiring strength should praise with the Ṣoḍaśin), 'atirātreṇa prajākāmaṃ yājayet' (one should cause the one desiring offspring to sacrifice with the Atirātra). Therefore — the accessory-injunction is common to all seven forms — having arrived at this position, we say: The fruit that has been cited for the Ukthya and the rest — that in fact indicates their nature as modifications (vikāra). By the principle 'kāmyo guṇaḥ śrūyamāṇo nityam artha vikṛtya niviśate' (an optional attribute, when heard, modifies a regular [rite] and establishes itself) — just as the subsidiary of cow-milking modifies the regular means of water-drawing with a camasa-cup, similarly the Ukthya subsidiary modifies the regular conclusion of the Agniṣṭoma and establishes a different conclusion. Therefore, the Ukthya and the rest are subsidiary-modifications of the Agniṣṭoma — hence the context is not common to all forms, but rather exclusive to the Agniṣṭoma alone. If it be argued: since it is stated 'jyotiṣṭomena yajeta' (one should sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma), this context belongs to the Jyotiṣṭoma, not to the Agniṣṭoma-form — that is true. But the Jyotiṣṭoma never deviates from the Agniṣṭoma, because the Ukthya and the rest also contain the Agniṣṭoma within them.

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīye jauminīyanyāyamālāvistare tṛtīyādhyāyasya ṣaṣṭha pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth pāda of the third adhyāya in the illustrious Mādhavīya Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara.
Now the seventh pāda of the third adhyāya. /
(In the first [adhikaraṇa], on whether the barhis (sacred grass) and the like are accessories of both the Darśapūrṇamāsa [as a whole] and its subordinate rites, sūtras 1–5)
Because of the specific context, that which is unconnected [belongs] to the principal [offering]. / Jaim_3,7.1 /
Or [it belongs] to all, because the subsidiarity is not restricted to that alone. / Jaim_3,7.2 /
If [it be argued that] even from afar [the connection obtains] — / Jaim_3,7.3 /
No, for that sentence is [meant] for that purpose. / Jaim_3,7.4 /
And because of the observation of the mark (liṅga). / Jaim_3,7.5 /
He composes the first adhikaraṇa of the seventh pāda —
START MJaiNy 3,7.1-2
Are the altar (vedī) and the like accessories only of the principal [offering], or also of the subsidiary [offerings] such as the preliminary offerings (prayāja)?
That sentence, being connected with the preparatory procedure, is indicative of accessory-status to the principal alone. // MJaiNy_3,7.1 //
Even the altar and the like, being accessories of the principal, also serve as accessories in the preliminary offerings and the like;
because the preliminary offerings serve the purpose of the principal, [and] because of the intervening [position] of their own originating [injunctions]. // MJaiNy_3,7.2 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate- 'vedyāṃ havīṃṣyāsādayati' 'barhiṣi havīṃṣyāsādayati' iti |
tathā taddharmāḥ śrūyante- 'vediṃ khanati' 'barhirlunāti' ityādayaḥ |
mukhyahavīṃṣyāgneyapuroḍāśādīni, amukhyahavīṃṣi tu prayājādyarthāni |
tatra-svasvadharmasahitāni vedyādīni prakaraṇabalānmukhyahaviṣā mevāṅgāni- 'vedyāṃ havīṃṣyāsādayati' iti vākyātsarvahaviraṅgatā- iti cet |
na |
prakaraṇena vākyasya saṃkocanīyatvāt |
yadi vākyaṃ prakaraṇanairapekṣyeṇa svatantraṃ syāt, tadā sādanamātraparyavasānena yāgābhāve vaiyarthya syāt |
saumikahīvaṣāmapyetadvedyāsādanaṃ prasajyeta |

children.translated_text: Therefore — the altar and the like are accessories of the principal oblation — having arrived at this position,

we say: Let the altar and the like serve as accessories of the oblations that are means of accomplishing the originating purpose (apūrva) relevant [to the sacrifice], thereby avoiding purposelessness and unwarranted extension.

The oblations of the preliminary offerings (prayāja) and the like are also means of accomplishing the principal originating purpose through their own intermediate originating purposes — hence the accessory-status of the altar and the like to them is also justified.

children.text: evaṃ sati vākyasyātyantasaṃkoco na bhaviṣyati || MJaiNyC_3,7.1-2 ||
children.translated_text: This being so, the sentence will not be excessively restricted. || MJaiNyC_3,7.1-2 ||

In the Darśapūrṇamāsa [sacrifices], it is heard: 'vedyāṃ havīṃṣy āsādayati' (he places the oblations on the altar), 'barhiṣi havīṃṣy āsādayati' (he places the oblations on the sacred grass). Similarly, their properties are heard: 'vediṃ khanati' (he digs the altar), 'barhir lunāti' (he cuts the sacred grass), and the like. The principal oblations are the Āgneya puroḍāśa and the like; the non-principal oblations are those for the preliminary offerings (prayāja) and the like. Therein — the altar and the like, together with their respective properties, are accessories only of the principal oblation, by the force of the context. By the sentence 'vedyāṃ havīṃṣy āsādayati' (he places the oblations on the altar), they would be accessories of all oblations — if so argued, no. Because the sentence is to be restricted by the context. If the sentence were independent, disregarding the context, then — being confined merely to the placing — it would be purposeless in the absence of a sacrifice. The placing of even Soma oblations on the altar would be entailed.
(In the second [adhikaraṇa], on the consecrations of the sacrificer being for the purpose of the principal [rite], the sūtra is:)
But because of the connection with the fruit, that which is connected with the owner (svāmin) belongs to the principal [rite]. / Jaim_3,7.6 /
He composes the second adhikaraṇa —
Does the benefit of tonsure (vapana) and the like serve both — the principal and the accessory [rites], or
only the principal? Let it be for both, since it pertains to the agent in his entirety. // MJaiNy_3,7.3 //
The scriptural consecration is appropriate for the principal [rite], the enjoyer of the fruit;

children.text: vināpi saṃsakṛtiṃ dṛṣṭaṃ kartṛtvaṃ tatra nāsti saḥ // MJaiNy_3,7.4 //
children.translated_text: even without consecration, agency is observed [in other cases] — therefore [the consecration] does not [serve] there. // MJaiNy_3,7.4 //

jyotiṣṭome keśaśmaśruvapanapayovratādayo yajamānasaṃskārā āmnātāḥ |
grahaiḥ somahomo jyotiṣṭome mukhyaḥ |
agnīṣomīyapaśvādikamaṅgam |
tatra-dvayormukhyāṅgayorete vapanādaya upakurvanti |
kutaḥ |
kartṛdharmatvāt |
yajamāno hi kartṛtayā vapanādibhiḥ saṃskriyate |
kartṛtvaṃ ca yathā mukhyaṃ prati tasya vidyate, tathāṅgaṃ pratyapyasti |
tasmāt-ubhayorupakāraḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
dvau hi yajamānasyā'kārau- kriyākartṛtvam, phalabhoktṛtvaṃ ceti |
tayoradṛṣṭaḥ phalabhogaḥ, kriyāniṣpattiśca dṛṣṭā |
tathā sati- vapanādikṛtopakāratyāpyadṛṣṭatvādbhoktṛśeṣā vapanādayaḥ phalabhogasādhane mukhya eva paryavasyanti |
vapanādisaṃskārarahitairapyṛtvigbhiḥ kṛṣīvalādibhiśca kriyā niṣpādyamānā dṛśyate |

children.translated_text: Therefore — this scriptural consecration, being unseen in nature and belonging to this sacrificer who is the enjoyer of the unseen fruit — is appropriate only for the principal rite, not for the accessories.

children.text: nātra pūrvavadvākyamasti, yena paramparāphalasādhaneṣvaṅgeṣu vapanādyupakāraḥ śaṅkayeta |
children.translated_text: Here there is no sentence as in the previous [case], by which one might suspect that the tonsure and the like benefit the accessories that are indirect means to the fruit.
And the context belongs to the principal [rite] alone, not to the accessories.
Therefore — there is no benefit [of the consecrations] in them [i.e., the accessories]. || MJaiNyC_3,7.3-4 ||

In the Jyotiṣṭoma, the consecrations of the sacrificer — tonsure (keśaśmaśru-vapana), milk-vow (payovrata), and the like — are recorded. In the Jyotiṣṭoma, the Soma offering with the cup-drawings (graha) is the principal [rite]; the animal sacrifice to Agnīṣomīya and the like is the accessory (aṅga). Therein — these tonsure and the like benefit both, the principal and the accessory. Why? Because they are properties of the agent. For the sacrificer is consecrated by tonsure and the like in the capacity of being the agent. And just as he has agency with respect to the principal [rite], so too with respect to the accessory. Therefore — the benefit is for both — if so argued, that is not correct. For the sacrificer has two aspects: being the agent of the ritual action, and being the enjoyer of the fruit. Of these, the enjoyment of the fruit is unseen (adṛṣṭa), and the accomplishment of the action is seen (dṛṣṭa). This being so — since the benefit produced by tonsure and the like is also unseen, the tonsure and the like are subservient to the fruit-enjoyer and culminate in the principal [rite] alone, which is the means of fruit-enjoyment. Even without the consecrations of tonsure and the like, the officiating priests (ṛtvij), laborers (kṛṣīvala), and the like are observed to accomplish the ritual action. Therefore, in that aspect of agency, the benefit produced by tonsure and the like does not exist.
(In the third [adhikaraṇa], on whether the Soma altar (vedī) and the like serve the accessory, the principal, or both, sūtras 7/9)
And because of the connection with the desire to perform (cikīrṣā). / Jaim_3,7.7 /

children.text: tadyukte tu phalaśrutis tasmāt sarvacikīrṣā syāt / Jaim_3,7.9 /
children.translated_text: But in that which is connected [with the desire], the statement of the fruit [is heard]; therefore the desire [extends] to all. / Jaim_3,7.9 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.5-6
He composes the third adhikaraṇa —
Is the Soma altar (saumikī vedī) for the principal alone, for both, or for the principal [only]?
For the principal — because the principal [rite] is the object of the desire to perform, and because the altar's construction is possible [only] for that. // MJaiNy_3,7.5 //
Because [the principal together with its accessories] is the cause of the full result (pauṣkalya), the accessory too is the object of the desire to perform;
therefore, like the principal, the altar also benefits the accessories. // MJaiNy_3,7.6 //

asyāyamarthaḥ- śrūyamāṇenānena dairdhyapramāṇena tiryakpramāṇadvayena ca pramite bhūbhāge phalahetusomayāgaṃ kartu śakṣyāmahe' iti niścitya tathaiva kuryāta- iti |
seyaṃ cikīrṣā mukhyaviṣayā |

aṅgānāṃ tu paśūnāmiṣṭīnāṃ ca sadohavirdhānādi maṇṭapanirapekṣāṇāṃ yathoktaparimāṇamantareṇāpyanuṣṭhātuṃ śakyatvātsa upanyāsastatra nirarthakaḥ |
somasya tvanuṣṭhānaṃ yathoktavedyāmeva saṃbhavati, natvanyatra |
tasmāt- sā vedirmukhyasyaivopakaroti- iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- 'iyati śakṣyāmahe' ityatra sāṅgapradhānānuṣṭhāne śaktiruktā |
tādṛśasyaiva phalaṃ prati puṣkalahetutvāt |
ato mukhyāṅgayościkīrṣāyāstulyatvādvedirubhayārthā |

children.translated_text: Nor should the analogy with the tonsure and the like be suspected here,
because the absence of visible utility was stated in that [case].
But here — the placing of the oblations and the like constitutes visible utility.

children.text: sa ca mukhyāṅgayoḥ sama ityubhayārthatvam || MJaiNyC_3,7.6 ||
children.translated_text: And that is equal for both the principal and the accessory — hence the altar serves both purposes. || MJaiNyC_3,7.6 ||

The Darśa altar (dārśikī vedī) being placed in the center, the pavilion with the front-beam (prācīnavaṃśa) is situated [around it]. Beyond that, in the eastern direction, there is a particular area of ground sufficient for the Sadas hall, the Havirdhāna (oblation-shed), and the like. Together with those — the Sadas and the rest — it is called the 'Soma altar' (saumikī vedī). This [altar] serves the principal Soma sacrifice alone, not the non-principal accessories like the Agnīṣomīya [animal sacrifice] and the like. Why? Because the principal is the object of the desire to perform (cikīrṣā). Nor should it be said that the accessories too are objects of the desire to perform — because the nature of the desire to perform is expressed by the Veda itself. For it is thus heard: 'ṣaṭtriṃśat prakramā prācī, caturviṃśatir agreṇa, triṃśaj jaghanena, iyati śakṣyāmahe' (thirty-six paces in length, twenty-four in front, thirty behind — in this much [space] we shall be able [to perform]). The meaning of this is: Having determined that 'in the area of ground measured by this stated length and two transverse measurements, we shall be able to perform the Soma sacrifice that is the means of the fruit,' one should do so accordingly. This desire to perform pertains to the principal [rite] — because of the mention of measurement and capacity in 'iyati śakṣyāmahe' (in this much we shall be able). But the accessories — the animal sacrifices and the subsidiary offerings — being independent of the Sadas, Havirdhāna, and other pavilions, can be performed even without the stated measurement, so that mention is purposeless there. But the performance of the Soma [sacrifice] is possible only on the altar as described, and not elsewhere. Therefore — the altar serves the principal alone — having arrived at this position, we say: In 'iyati śakṣyāmahe' (in this much we shall be able), the capacity for performance of the principal together with its accessories is stated — because only such [complete performance] is the full cause (puṣkala-hetu) of the fruit. Therefore, since the desire to perform is equal for both the principal and the accessories, the altar serves both purposes.
(In the fourth [adhikaraṇa], on whether the touching (abhimarśana) [mantra] serves the accessory, the principal, or both, sūtra 8/10)
Similarly, by the designation (abhidhāna). / Jaim_3,7.8 /
Since the designation pertains to the subsidiary, the designation [extends] to all. / Jaim_3,7.10 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.7-8
He composes the fourth adhikaraṇa —
Should the Caturhotṛ [mantra] touch [only] the Paurṇamāsī [oblation]? In the touching of the clarified butter and other [oblations],

children.text: mantro mukhya utāṅge 'pi mukhye tadvāciśabdataḥ // MJaiNy_3,7.7 //
children.translated_text: is this mantra [applied] only to the principal or also to the accessory? To the principal, because of the word denoting that [principal oblation]. // MJaiNy_3,7.7 //
Since the word denotes the rite [as a whole] and touching of the rite [itself] is excluded,
when the case-ending is taken in a transferred sense, the mantra [serves] both — the oblations of the principal and the accessory. // MJaiNy_3,7.8 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate- 'caturhotrā paurṇamāsīmabhimṛśet, pañcahotrābhāvāsyām' iti |
pṛthivī hotā'- ityādiko mantraścaturhotā |
tasminmantre yajñāṅgānāṃ caturṇā śrutatvāt |
athavā- tasya mantrasyābhimānitvenā'tmabhūtaḥ kaścitpuruṣaḥ prajāpatinā caturthāramāmantritaḥ pratvuttaramuvāceti sa puruṣaścaturhūtaḥ |
tadīyanāmnā mantro 'pi 'caturhūtaḥ' ityucyate |
'pūjyānāṃ pratyakṣanāmagrahaṇamayuktam' ityabhiprāyeṇa hūtaśabdasthāne hotṛśabdaḥ paṭhyate |
ayamarthaḥ sarvo 'pi taittirīyabrāhmaṇe śrūyate-
"ātmannātmannityāmantrayata |
tasmai caturhūtaḥ pratyaśṛṇot |
sa caturhūto 'bhavat |
caturhūto ha vai nāmaiṣaḥ |
taṃ vā etaṃ caturhūtaṃ santaṃ 'caturhotā' ityācakṣate parokṣeṇa |
parokṣapriyā iva hi devaḥ"iti |
'agnirhotā'- ityādiko mantraḥ pañcahotā |
tatrāpyuktaprakāro draṣṭavyaḥ |
- atra-yo 'yamājyādihaviṣa upasparśanārtho mantraḥ, asau mukhya eva haviṣi niviśate |

children.translated_text: because the words Paurṇamāsī and Amāvāsyā refer to the principal oblation — having arrived at this position,

children.text: brūmaḥ- paurṇamāsyabhāvāsyaśabdau karmavācinau, na tu havirvācinau |
children.translated_text: we say: The words Paurṇamāsī and Amāvāsyā denote the rite [as a whole], not the oblation.
And touching of the rite [itself] is not possible.

children.text: atha kālavivakṣāyāṃ vibhaktivyatyayena saptamyartho vyākhyāyeta, tadā kālasaṃbandhasya mukhyāṅga yorubhayostulyatvādubhayavidhahavirupasparśane mantro viniyujyate || MJaiNyC_3,7.7-8 ||
children.translated_text: Now, if the intention is to refer to the time [of the rite], and the case-ending is explained as a transferred locative (saptamī), then — since the temporal connection is equal for both the principal and the accessory oblations — the mantra is applied to the touching of both types of oblations. || MJaiNyC_3,7.7-8 ||

In the Darśapūrṇamāsa [sacrifices], it is heard: 'caturhotrā paurṇamāsīm abhimṛśet, pañcahotrā amāvāsyām' (one should touch the full-moon [oblation] with the Caturhotrā [mantra] and the new-moon [oblation] with the Pañcahotrā). The mantra 'Pṛthivī hotā' (the Earth is the Hotṛ priest) and the like constitutes the Caturhotrā — because four ritual accessories (aṅgas) are mentioned in that mantra. Alternatively — a certain person, who is the spiritual embodiment (abhimānin) of that mantra, was addressed by Prajāpati as the fourth invitee, and he answered in reply — that person is the 'Caturhūta' (the four-times-invoked). By his name, the mantra too is called 'Caturhūta.' With the intention that 'it is improper to use the actual name of venerable beings,' the word 'Hotṛ' is read in place of the word 'Hūta.' All this meaning is heard in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa: 'ātmann ātmann ity āmantrayata | tasmai caturhūtaḥ pratyaśṛṇot | sa caturhūto 'bhavat | caturhūto ha vai nāmaiṣaḥ | taṃ vā etaṃ caturhūtaṃ santaṃ caturhotā ityācakṣate parokṣeṇa | parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ' (He called out 'Self! Self!' To him the Caturhūta responded. He became the Caturhūta. His name indeed is Caturhūta. That very Caturhūta they designate indirectly as Caturhotā — for the gods, as it were, are fond of the indirect). The mantra 'Agnir hotā' (Agni is the Hotṛ) and the like is the Pañcahotā — therein too the same explanation should be understood. Here — this mantra for the purpose of touching the clarified butter and other oblations applies to the principal oblation alone,
(In the fifth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) and the sacrificial fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) serving the purpose of the principal [rite], <s>sūtras</s> 11-12:)
But the consecration-fee (<s>dīkṣādakṣiṇā</s>) [serves the purpose] of the principal [rite], because of the [explicit] statement. / Jaim_3,7.11 /
And because of the observed cessation [of the fee when the principal is absent]. / Jaim_3,7.12 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.9-10
He composes the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) with a staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>), and the fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) of twelve hundred —
do these serve both purposes, or [only] the principal? Since the expression 'of the <s>Soma</s>' is possible [for both readings]. // MJaiNy_3,7.9 //
[It is] not [for] both the principal and the accessories — [for] that would be a travesty of indirect connection (<s>pāramparyaviḍambanā</s>);

children.text: vacanasya na yuktātaḥ pradhānārthamidaṃ sthitam // MJaiNy_3,7.10 //
children.translated_text: the statement does not support [that]; therefore, it is established that this serves the purpose of the principal [rite]. // MJaiNy_3,7.10 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome dīkṣādakṣiṇaṃ śrūyate- 'daṇḍena dakṣiyati' iti, 'tasya dvādaśaśataṃ dakṣiṇā' iti ca |
tatra dīkṣā mukhyāṅgayorupakaroti, tathā dakṣiṇāpi |
na ca - dīkṣā somasya, dakṣiṇā somasya' iti vākye ṣaṣṭhyā mukhyasaṃbandha evāvagamyate, na tvaṅgasaṃbandhaḥ- iti vācyam |
dīkṣādakṣiṇe somanaiva sākṣātsaṃbadhnītām, sa somaḥ punaraṅgaiḥ saṃbaddhaiti paramparayā dīkṣādakṣiṇayoraṅgairapi saṃbandho 'sti |
tasmāt- ubhayārthe dīkṣādikam- iti prāpte,-

children.translated_text: we say: The meaning conveyed by the genitive is only the direct, unmediated connection.
Only when that [direct connection] is impossible is the indirect successive connection somehow accepted.
But here, since that [direct connection] is possible, the indirect [connection] is not appropriate.
Therefore — the consecration and the like serve the purpose of the principal [rite]. || MJaiNyC_3,7.9-10 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the consecration-fee (<s>dīkṣādakṣiṇā</s>) is heard: '<s>daṇḍena dakṣiṇayati</s>' (he gives the fee with a staff) and '<s>tasya dvādaśaśataṃ dakṣiṇā</s>' (the fee for that is twelve hundred). Therein, the consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) serves both the principal and the accessories, and likewise the fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>). Nor should it be argued that — in the sentences '<s>dīkṣā somasya</s>' (the consecration of the <s>Soma</s>) and '<s>dakṣiṇā somasya</s>' (the fee of the <s>Soma</s>) — the genitive conveys only the connection with the principal, not with the accessories. [For:] the consecration and fee are directly connected only with the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice]; and that <s>Soma</s> is in turn connected with the accessories; thus, through indirect succession, there is a connection of the consecration and fee with the accessories as well. Therefore — the consecration and the like serve both purposes — having arrived at this position,
(In the sixth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>vedi</s> (altar) not being a subsidiary of the <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post), <s>sūtras</s> 13-14:)
Similarly, the <s>vedi</s> (altar) [is subsidiary] to the <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post). / Jaim_3,7.13 /
Or [the <s>vedi</s> merely indicates] the place, because of the syntactic unity with the remainder. / Jaim_3,7.14 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.11-12
He composes the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'He measures within the <s>vedi</s>' — is half [the <s>yūpa</s>] a subsidiary of the <s>yūpa</s>, or does it indicate
the place? [If] the <s>vedi</s>-portion is a subsidiary of the <s>yūpa</s>, this is what is under discussion. // MJaiNy_3,7.11 //
'Half outside the <s>vedi</s>' — this sentence would be split if that [subsidiary-nature] were enjoined;
for the <s>yūpa</s> being measured, the [<s>vedi</s>] merely indicates the extent of the place. // MJaiNy_3,7.12 //

children.text:
agnīṣomīyapaśau 'yūpaṃ minoti' iti prakṛtya śrūyate- 'ardhamantarvedi minoti, ardha bahirvedi' iti |
'yūpaṃ sthāpayituṃ kiyadvistāravānavaṭo 'pekṣitaḥ' iti bubhutsāyāṃ tannirṇayāya yūpamūlasya sthaulyamaṅgulyādibhirmātavyam |
tasya ca pīyamānasya yūpasya vedyabhyantarabhāgo 'laṅgatvenaṃ vidhīyate- iti cet |

children.translated_text: that is not correct.

children.text: yathā saṃskṛto vedyabhyantarabhāgaḥ 'ardhamantarvedi' ityanena vākyena vidhīyate, tadvada saṃskṛto bahirbhāgo 'bahirvedi'- ityanena vākyena vidhātavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as the consecrated inner portion of the <s>vedi</s> is enjoined by the sentence '<s>ardham antarvedi</s>' (half within the <s>vedi</s>), similarly the unconsecrated outer portion should be enjoined by the sentence '<s>bahirvedi</s>' (outside the <s>vedi</s>).
Then the sentence would be split.

children.text: yadā tu vederabhyantarabāhyabhāgābhyāmupalakṣito 'saṃskṛto' laukikadeśa evātra yūpāṅgatvena vidhīyate, na tu saṃskṛtavedibhāgaḥ || MJaiNyC_3,7.11-12 ||
children.translated_text: But when the unconsecrated, ordinary place indicated by the inner and outer portions of the <s>vedi</s> is what is enjoined here as subsidiary to the <s>yūpa</s> — then it is not the consecrated <s>vedi</s>-portion [that is subsidiary]. || MJaiNyC_3,7.11-12 ||

In the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal sacrifice, it is heard with reference to the <s>yūpa</s>: '<s>yūpaṃ minoti</s>' (he measures the <s>yūpa</s>) — and: '<s>ardham antarvedi minoti, ardhaṃ bahirvedi</s>' (he measures half within the <s>vedi</s>, half outside the <s>vedi</s>). When the question arises — 'How wide a pit is required for erecting the <s>yūpa</s>?' — to determine that, the girth of the base of the <s>yūpa</s> must be measured with fingers and the like. And the inner portion of the <s>vedi</s> that belongs to the <s>yūpa</s> being measured is enjoined as a subsidiary — if so it is argued,
(In the seventh [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>Havirdhāna</s> not being a subsidiary of the <s>Sāmidhenī</s> [verses], <s>sūtras</s> 15-17:)

children.text: sāmidhenīs tad anvāhur iti havir dhānayor vacanāt sāmidhenīnām / Jaim_3,7.15 /
children.translated_text: 'They recite the <s>Sāmidhenīs</s> accompanying that' — the <s>Havirdhāna</s> is [a subsidiary] of the <s>Sāmidhenīs</s>, because of the statement. / Jaim_3,7.15 /

children.text: deśamātraṃ vā pratyakṣaṃ hy arthakarma somasya / Jaim_3,7.16 /
children.translated_text: Or [the <s>Havirdhāna</s> merely indicates] the place, because the purpose-serving action pertaining to the <s>Soma</s> is directly perceived. / Jaim_3,7.16 /
And the designation likewise [indicates the place]. / Jaim_3,7.17 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.13-14
He composes the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Standing in the <s>Havirdhāna</s> [shed], one should recite the <s>Sāmidhenīs</s> — is the subsidiarity here
of the <s>Havirdhāna</s> to those [<s>Sāmidhenīs</s>]? Or is the <s>Havirdhāna</s> portion [merely] indicative of the place? // MJaiNy_3,7.13 //
By the sentence, there would be subsidiarity; but no — in the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>), the place [for the <s>Sāmidhenīs</s>] is already obtained as west of the fire;

children.text: deśaḥ prāpto lāghavena lakṣyaḥ śakaṭasaṃnidhiḥ // MJaiNy_3,7.14 //
children.translated_text: by parsimony, the proximity to the cart [<s>Havirdhāna</s>] is merely indicated [as the place]. // MJaiNy_3,7.14 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate- 'uta yatsunvanti sāmidhenīstadanvāhuḥ' - iti |
havirdhānamaṇḍapagatayor dakṣiṇottarabhāgāvasthitayorhavirdhānanāmakayoḥ śakaṭayormadhye dakṣiṇaṃ śakaṭamatra yattacchabdābhyā mabhidhīyate |
tasya samīpe somasyābhiṣavaḥ |
'uta' ityayaṃ śabdo 'thabdārthe vartate |
'atha yasminhavirdhāne somamabhiṣuṇvanti, tasminsāmidhenīranubrūyuḥ' |
aiha dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasya sāmidhenīṣvaṅgatvaṃ pratīyate |
na cātra pūrvavadvākyabhedadoṣaḥ śaṅkyaḥ |
akavākyatāyāḥ spaṣṭaṃ pratibhāsāt- iti prāpte-
brūmaḥ- sāmidhenīnāmiṣṭyaṅgatayā darśapūrṇamāsāvatra prakṛtiḥ |
prakṛtau cā'havanīyāgneḥ paścimo deśaḥ sāmidhenīnāṃ sthānam |
ihottaravederāhavanīyatvāttadapekṣayā havirdhānasya paścimadeśāvasthānāt |
sa deśaścodakena prāptaḥ- iti na deśasya sāmidhenyaṅgatvaṃ vidhātavyam |
kiṃtu dakṣiṇottarahavirdhānasamīpa deśayoraniyamena prāptau- dakṣiṇasyaiva havirdhānasya samīpadeśaḥ- iti niyantuṃ havirdhānena saṃnidhirlakṣyate |
children.translated_text: Rather, when [the place is] obtained indeterminately with respect to the vicinity of either the southern or northern <s>Havirdhāna</s> cart — the proximity is indicated by the <s>Havirdhāna</s> [reference] in order to restrict [it] to the vicinity of the southern <s>Havirdhāna</s> alone.
This being so, there is parsimony, since only a restriction is being enjoined.

children.text: tvatpakṣe tvabhiṣavopalakṣitasya dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasyā tyantamaprāptaṃ sāmidhenyaṅgatvaṃ vidhīyata iti gauravam |
children.translated_text: In your view, however, the subsidiarity of the southern <s>Havirdhāna</s> — identified by [its proximity to] the pressing — to the <s>Sāmidhenīs</s>, which is entirely unobtained, is being enjoined — which is burdensome.
Therefore, [the <s>Havirdhāna</s> reference is merely] an indication of the place. || MJaiNyC_3,7.13-14 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: '<s>uta yat sunvanti sāmidhenīs tad anvāhuḥ</s>' (and when they press [the <s>Soma</s>], they thereupon recite the <s>Sāmidhenīs</s>). The word '<s>tat</s>' (that) refers to the southern cart of the two carts called <s>Havirdhāna</s>, which are placed respectively in the southern and northern parts within the <s>Havirdhāna</s> pavilion. Near that [southern cart] is the pressing of <s>Soma</s>. The word '<s>uta</s>' has the meaning of '<s>atha</s>' (then). [The meaning is:] 'Then, in that <s>Havirdhāna</s> [shed] where they press the <s>Soma</s>, they should recite the <s>Sāmidhenīs</s>.' Here, the subsidiarity of the southern <s>Havirdhāna</s> [cart] to the <s>Sāmidhenīs</s> is understood. Nor should the defect of sentence-splitting, as in the previous [case], be apprehended here. Because the syntactic unity [of the sentence] is clearly apparent — having arrived at this position, we say: The <s>Sāmidhenīs</s>, being accessories of the <s>Iṣṭi</s> (simple offering), have the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> as their archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>). And in the archetype, the place west of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire is the location for the <s>Sāmidhenīs</s>. Here [in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>], since the <s>Uttaravedi</s> serves as the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, the <s>Havirdhāna</s> is positioned to the west relative to it. That place is already obtained by reasoning alone — so the subsidiarity of the place to the <s>Sāmidhenīs</s> need not be enjoined.
(In the eighth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the performance of accessories through another [agent], <s>sūtras</s> 18-20:)

children.text: śāstraphalaṃ prayoktari tallakṣaṇatvāt tasmāt svayaṃ prayoge syāt / Jaim_3,7.18 /
children.translated_text: The fruit of the scriptural [injunction belongs to] the performer, because it is characterized by him; therefore, in the [actual] performance, it should be [done] by himself. / Jaim_3,7.18 /

children.text: utsarge tu pradhānatvāc cheṣakārī pradhānasya tasmād anyaḥ svayaṃ vā syāt / Jaim_3,7.19 /
children.translated_text: But in the general rule, since the principal [rite] is primary, the performer of the remainder [does it for] the principal; therefore, another [person] or [the sacrificer] himself may [perform it]. / Jaim_3,7.19 /

children.text: anyo vā syāt parikrayāmnānād vipratiṣedhāt pratyag ātmani / Jaim_3,7.20 /
children.translated_text: Or another [may perform it], because the hiring is stated; due to the contradiction, [the rule applies] to oneself. / Jaim_3,7.20 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.15-16
He composes the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: yajamānena kartavyaṃ nikhilaṃ tyāga eva vā /
children.translated_text: Should everything be done by the sacrificer himself, or [should he perform] only the offering (<s>tyāga</s>)?
From the <s>śruti</s> that the fruit goes to the performer, complete agency [by the sacrificer] is appropriate. // MJaiNy_3,7.15 //
Even the one who causes [the action] has agency; if not, the hiring [of priests] would be futile;
since [the action] is to be accomplished by him [through delegation], only the offering [is his direct act]; the priests have agency elsewhere. // MJaiNy_3,7.16 //

children.text:
'svargakāmo yajeta' iti svargabhokturyāgakartuśca sāmānādhikaraṇyādekatvaṃ gamyate |
pāṇiniśca 'svaritañitaḥ kartrabhiprāye krimāphale'[pā.sū.1.3.72 ]iti sūtreṇa kriyāphalasya kartṛgāmitve satyātmanepadaṃ vidadhāti |
ataḥ sāṅgakarmānuṣṭhānamantareṇa phalāsaṃbhavānnikhilaṃ yajamānena kartavyam- iti prāpte-
brūmaḥ- nikhilānuṣṭhānābhāve 'pi prayojakatayā yajamānasya sarvakartṛtvamasti |
'ṣahūbhirhalaiḥ karṣati' ityatra tathādarśanāt |
yadi svenaiva sarvamanuṣṭhīyeta, tadānīmṛtviṇāṃ parikrayo vṛthā syāt |
children.translated_text: If everything were performed by oneself alone, then the hiring of priests (<s>ṛtvijs</s>) would be futile.
Therefore — only the offering (<s>tyāga</s>) is to be performed by the sacrificer.
Elsewhere, the hired priests perform the principal [rite] together with its accessories.

children.text: tathā sati sākṣātparamparayā ca sarvakartṛtvasya yajamāne saṃbhavāttasya phalaṃ na virudhyate || MJaiNyC_3,7.15-16 ||
children.translated_text: This being so, since the complete agency of the sacrificer is possible both directly and indirectly, his [attainment of] the fruit is not contradicted. || MJaiNyC_3,7.15-16 ||

'<s>Svargakāmo yajeta</s>' (one desiring heaven should sacrifice) — from the co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) of the enjoyer of heaven and the performer of the sacrifice, their identity is understood. And <s>Pāṇini</s>, by the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>svaritañitaḥ kartrabhiprāye kriyāphale</s>' [Pā.Sū. 1.3.72], prescribes the <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) when the fruit of the action goes to the agent. Therefore, since the fruit is impossible without the performance of the entire rite with its accessories, everything should be done by the sacrificer himself — having arrived at this position, we say: Even without performing everything himself, the sacrificer has complete agency by virtue of being the causer (<s>prayojaka</s>). Because this is observed in [expressions like] '<s>ṣaḍbhir halaiḥ karṣati</s>' (he ploughs with six ploughs) [where the agent delegates].
(In the ninth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the restriction of the specific number of hired priests, <s>sūtras</s> 21-24:)
Therein, from the purpose, the number of agents would be [determined]; there is no restriction, due to the absence of specification. / Jaim_3,7.21 /

children.text: api vā śrutibhedāt pratināmadheyaṃ syuḥ / Jaim_3,7.22 /
children.translated_text: Or, because of the difference in <s>śruti</s> [statements], there would be [a priest] for each name-designation. / Jaim_3,7.22 /
If it be said that one [priest performs] different ritual acts — / Jaim_3,7.23 /
No, because [the number is determined] at the point of origination. / Jaim_3,7.24 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.17
He composes the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: na krītakartṛsaṃkhyāyā niyamo 'satyasti vā na hi /
children.translated_text: Is there no restriction on the number of hired performers, or is there? No, there is not;

children.text: aviśeṣādasti yāvatkārya tāvanta eva hi // MJaiNy_3,7.17 //
children.translated_text: due to the absence of specification, there should be exactly as many as the tasks [require]. // MJaiNy_3,7.17 //

children.text:
ye yajamānena krītāḥ kartāra ṛtvijaḥ, teṣāṃ saṃkhyāviśeṣo yadyapi na śrutaḥ |
tathāpi kāryānusāreṇa so 'vagantavyaḥ |

te ca kāryaviśeṣāḥ kartṛsaṃyuktā evaṃ śrūyante- 'puro 'dhvaryurvibhajati, pratiprasthātā manthinaṃ juhoti, neṣṭhā patnīmudānayati, unnetā camasānunnayati, prastotā prastauti, udgātodgāyati, pratihartā pratiharati, subrahmaṇyaḥ subrahmaṇyāmāhvayati, hotā prātaranuvākamanubrūte, maitrāvarūṇaḥ preṣyati, acchāvāko yajati, grāvastudgrāvastotrīyamanvāha' iti |
children.translated_text: nevertheless, it should be understood in accordance with the tasks. And those specific tasks, connected with agents, are heard thus: '<s>puro 'dhvaryur vibhajati</s>' (the <s>Adhvaryu</s> distributes the [<s>Soma</s>] cakes), '<s>pratiprasthātā mathinaṃ juhoti</s>' (the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s> offers the <s>Manthina</s>), '<s>neṣṭā patnīm udānayati</s>' (the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> leads the wife), '<s>unnetā camasān unnayati</s>' (the <s>Unnetṛ</s> raises the cups), '<s>prastotā prastauti</s>' (the <s>Prastotṛ</s> begins the chant), '<s>udgātodgāyati</s>' (the <s>Udgātṛ</s> sings the <s>Udgītha</s>), '<s>pratihartā pratiharati</s>' (the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> responds), '<s>subrahmaṇyaḥ subrahmaṇyām āhvayati</s>' (the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s> makes the <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s> invocation), '<s>hotā prātaranuvākam anubrūte</s>' (the <s>Hotṛ</s> recites the morning litany), '<s>maitrāvaruṇaḥ preṣyati</s>' (the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> gives directions), '<s>acchāvāko yajati</s>' (the <s>Acchāvāka</s> sacrifices), '<s>grāvastud grāvastotrīyam anvāha</s>' (the <s>Grāvastut</s> recites the stone-praise hymn).
Similarly, the tasks of the four — <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>, <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, and <s>Potṛ</s> — should also be cited.
Therefore —

children.text: yāvanti karyāṇi tāvanta ṛtvijo varītavyāḥ || MJaiNyC_3,7.17 ||
children.translated_text: as many tasks as there are, that many priests should be selected. || MJaiNyC_3,7.17 ||
Although the specific number of those performers — the priests (<s>ṛtvijs</s>) — hired by the sacrificer is not heard [explicitly],
(In the tenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the distinctness of the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
And the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> (cup-<s>Adhvaryus</s>) [are distinct] from them, because of the [separate] designation. / Jaim_3,7.25 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.18
He composes the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Are the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> not distinct from the [other] priests, or are they distinct? The first [view holds];

children.text: yaugikyā saṃjñayā maivaṃ ṣaṣṭhyā tebhyo vibhedanāt // MJaiNy_3,7.18 //
children.translated_text: by the etymological derivation (<s>yaugikī saṃjñā</s>) [they would not be distinct]; but no — because the genitive [in the text] differentiates them from those [other priests]. // MJaiNy_3,7.18 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate- 'camasādhvaryūnvṛṇīte' iti |
ye pūrvatra kāryānusāreṇādhvaryupramukhā ṛtvija uktāḥ, tebhyo na vyatiriktāścamasādhvaryavaḥ |
kutaḥ |
yaugikasaṃjñayā tadabhedapratīteḥ |
ta(ya)thā devadatta eva pacikriyāyogātpācako bhavati, tathādhvaryupramukhā eva camasayogāccamasādhvaryavaḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
madhyataḥkāriṇāṃ camasādhvaryavaḥ, hotrakāṇāṃ, camasādhvaryava iti apaṭhyā bhedāvabhāsāt |
children.translated_text: Because in the readings '<s>madhyataḥkāriṇāṃ camasādhvaryavaḥ</s>' (the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> of the <s>Madhyataḥkārins</s>) and '<s>hotrakāṇāṃ camasādhvaryavaḥ</s>' (the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> of the <s>Hotrakas</s>), the distinctness is apparent.
The <s>Madhyataḥkārins</s> are the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, the <s>Hotṛ</s>, and the like.
The <s>Hotrakas</s> are the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s>, the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, and the like.
Therefore, [the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> are] distinct from the [main] priests. || MJaiNyC_3,7.18 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: '<s>camasādhvaryūn vṛṇīte</s>' (he selects the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>). The <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> are not distinct from the priests headed by the <s>Adhvaryu</s> that were mentioned earlier in accordance with the tasks. Why? Because by the etymological designation, their non-difference is understood. Just as <s>Devadatta</s> himself becomes a 'cook' (<s>pācaka</s>) by virtue of his connection with the act of cooking, so too the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and the others themselves become '<s>Camasādhvaryus</s>' by virtue of their connection with the cups — if so it is argued, that is not correct.
(In the eleventh [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the restriction of the plurality of the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
But [plurality obtains] at the point of origination, because of the plural expression. / Jaim_3,7.26 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.19
He composes the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'He selects them' — does the plural [not] obtain, or does it? [It would] not, as in the singularity of the cup;
if [it is argued] no — not so, because of the dissimilarity here; at the point of origination, the plural is heard. // MJaiNy_3,7.19 //

children.text:
'camasādhvaryūnvṛṇīta' iti yadbahutvaṃ śrutam, tanna vivakṣitam |
grahaikatvavaduddeśyagatatvāt- iti cet |
maivam |

children.translated_text: Because of the dissimilarity with the cup.
'<s>Grahaṃ saṃmārṣṭi</s>' (he wipes the cup) — this is not the origination-sentence for the cups.
But for the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>, this [sentence '<s>camasādhvaryūn vṛṇīte</s>'] is indeed the origination-sentence.
Therefore, since they are to be employed [in the sacrifice], the plurality contained in that [sentence] is intended. || MJaiNyC_3,7.19 ||

The plurality heard in '<s>camasādhvaryūn vṛṇīte</s>' (he selects the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>) is not intended — because it pertains to the referent, as in the singularity of the cup — if so it is argued, that is not correct.
(In the twelfth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the restriction of the number of <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> to ten, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
The number ten, because of the observation of the mark. / Jaim_3,7.27 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.20
He composes the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is there a definite number for them or not? Not [directly], due to the absence of a restricting [statement];
but since the cups are ten, the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> are [also] ten. // MJaiNy_3,7.20 //
The meaning is clear. || MJaiNyC_3,7.20 ||
(In the thirteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the non-distinctness of the <s>Śamitṛ</s> (animal slaughterer), <s>sūtras</s> 28-29:)
And the <s>Śamitṛ</s> [is distinct], because of the difference in name. / Jaim_3,7.28 /
Or [he is not distinct], from the context, because he is not connected with a [separate] origination. / Jaim_3,7.29 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.21
He composes the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the <s>Śamitṛ</s> distinct from those [priests] or not? He is distinct, because of the difference in designation;
he is not distinct, because there is no [separate] selection (<s>varaṇa</s>); the difference in designation is merely etymological. // MJaiNy_3,7.21 //

children.text:
'śamitāra upeta na yajñam' ityasminmantre śrutāyāḥ śamitṛsaṃjñāyāḥ pṛthaktyāduktebhyo 'nyaḥ śamitā- iti cet |
maivam |

children.translated_text: Because there is no separate selection (<s>varaṇa</s>) [of such a person].
The difference in designation is explained by the association with the killing (<s>saṃjñapana</s>) of the animal.

children.text: yadyapyayaṃ mantro 'dhvaryu kāṇḍe paṭhitaḥ, tathāpyadhvaryoḥ parāvṛttiśravaṇādadhvaryupuruṣāḥ pratiprasthātrādayaḥ śamitāraḥ |
children.translated_text: Even though this <s>mantra</s> is recited in the <s>Adhvaryu</s> section, nevertheless, because the withdrawal of the <s>Adhvaryu</s> [from the killing] is heard, the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s assistants — the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s> and the like — are the slaughterers.

children.text: ata eva śrūyate- 'parāvartate 'dhvaryuḥ paśoḥ saṃjñapyamānāt' iti || MJaiNyC_3,7.21 ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason it is heard: '<s>parāvartate 'dhvaryuḥ paśoḥ saṃjñapyamānāt</s>' (the <s>Adhvaryu</s> turns away from the animal being killed). || MJaiNyC_3,7.21 ||

In the <s>mantra</s> '<s>śamitāra upeta na yajñam</s>' (O slaughterers, approach the sacrifice), the designation <s>śamitṛ</s> (slaughterer) is heard, and because of its distinctness, the slaughterer would be someone other than those already mentioned — if so it is argued, that is not correct.
(In the fourteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the non-distinctness of the <s>upaga</s> [accompanists], the <s>sūtra</s>:)
And the <s>upagas</s> (accompanists), because of the observation of the mark. / Jaim_3,7.30 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.22
He composes the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: anye syurupagātāra uditebhyo na vā yathā /
children.translated_text: Would the <s>upagātṛs</s> (accompanists) be persons different from those already mentioned, or not?
As in worldly [practice], so here too [they would be different]; but no — from the mark, because '<s>nādhvaryuḥ</s>' (not the <s>Adhvaryu</s>) [is stated]. // MJaiNy_3,7.22 //

children.text: yathā loke mukhyebhyo gāyakanāyakādibhyo 'nye pārśvasthā upagātāraḥ, tathātrāpi- iti cet |
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, the accompanists (<s>upagātṛs</s>) — who stand beside — are different from the principal singers, leaders, and the like, so too here — if so it is argued,
that is not correct.

children.text: yadyuktebhyaḥ puruṣebhya upagātāro 'nye bhaveyuḥ, tadānīmadhvaryoḥ prasaktyabhāvāt 'nādhvaryurupagāyet' iti pratiṣedho 'narthakaḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: If the accompanists were different from the [already] mentioned persons, then since there would be no occasion for the <s>Adhvaryu</s> [to be involved in singing], the prohibition '<s>nādhvaryur upagāyet</s>' (the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should not sing along) would be purposeless.
Therefore, the difference in designation among those already mentioned is merely etymological (<s>yaugika</s>). || MJaiNyC_3,7.22 ||
(In the fifteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the distinctness of the <s>Soma</s> seller, the <s>sūtra</s>:)
But the seller is someone else, because [selling] is not enjoined as a ritual act. / Jaim_3,7.31 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.23
He composes the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the <s>Soma</s> seller one among these [priests], or not — because the selection [of sellers] is excluded?

children.text: ekaḥ kratvarthatā nāsti vikrayasyeti bhidyate // MJaiNy_3,7.23 //
children.translated_text: He is a separate person; the selling has no ritual purpose — therefore he is distinct. // MJaiNy_3,7.23 //

children.text: kraya eva jyotiṣṭomāṅgatvena śrutaḥ, na vikrayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Only the purchase (<s>kraya</s>) is heard as an accessory of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, not the selling (<s>vikraya</s>).
And the priests (<s>ṛtvijs</s>) do not perform what is not enjoined.
Therefore, the seller is someone else. || MJaiNyC_3,7.23 ||
(In the sixteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the non-universal scope of the designation '<s>ṛtvik</s>', <s>sūtras</s> 32–35:)
Because of the ritual action (<s>karmakārya</s>), all would have the status of <s>ṛtvik</s> (priest), because there is no distinction. / Jaim_3,7.32 /
Or not, because of the restrictive enumeration (<s>parisaṃkhyāna</s>). / Jaim_3,7.33 /
If [it is argued that the enumeration is] by alternatives (<s>pakṣa</s>). / Jaim_3,7.34 /
Not all have the [ritual] qualification (<s>adhikāra</s>). / Jaim_3,7.35 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.24-25
He composes the sixteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the designation '<s>ṛtvik</s>' common to all [ritual participants], or to some [only]?

children.text: ṛtau yajanametiṣāṃ tulyamityasti nāma tat // MJaiNy_3,7.24 //
children.translated_text: The sacrificing (<s>yajana</s>) at the proper season (<s>ṛtu</s>) is equal for these [all] — so they all have that designation. // MJaiNy_3,7.24 //
In the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice, there would be seven, or ten — by such enumeration,

children.text: na sarveṣāṃ samaṃ nāma keṣāṃcidyogarūḍhitaḥ // MJaiNy_3,7.25 //
children.translated_text: the designation is not common to all; for some [only], because of both etymology and convention (<s>yoga-rūḍhi</s>). // MJaiNy_3,7.25 //

children.text:
ṛtvikśabdasya pravṛttinimittamṛtau yajanama |
tacca brahmādiṣviva canasādhvaryupvapyasti |
tasmāt- sarveṣāmṛtvignāma samānam- iti cet |

children.translated_text: that is not correct.
Because of the conflict with the <s>śruti</s> on enumeration.
It is heard: '<s>saumyasyādhvarasya yajñakratoḥ saptadaśa rtvijaḥ</s>' (the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice has seventeen priests).

Therefore, not transgressing the etymological derivation but also relying on the conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>) established by the <s>śāstra</s>, it should be understood that this designation applies only to some. || MJaiNyC_3,7.24-25 ||

The etymological basis for the word '<s>ṛtvik</s>' is 'sacrificing at the proper season' (<s>ṛtau yajanam</s>). And this [etymological meaning] exists even in the <s>Camasādhvaryu</s> (cup-bearing assistants), just as in the <s>Brahman</s> and other [principal priests]. Therefore, the designation '<s>ṛtvik</s>' is common to all — if so it is argued,

(In the seventeenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on [only] the <s>Brahman</s> and the other [principal priests] mentioned in the <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration) and <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee) passages being the seventeen priests, <s>sūtras</s> 36–37:)
The restriction is through the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (priestly fees), because of the connection with the <s>śruti</s>. / Jaim_3,7.36 /

children.text: uktvā ca yajamānatvaṃ teṣāṃ dīkṣāvidhānāt / Jaim_3,7.37 /
children.translated_text: And having stated [their] sacrificer-status, [the restriction follows] from the injunction of their consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>). / Jaim_3,7.37 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.26
He composes the seventeenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Even among those enumerated, are some restricted or not, without distinction?

children.text: ādyo na dakṣiṇādāne dīkṣāyāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ // MJaiNy_3,7.26 //
children.translated_text: The first [alternative, i.e. no restriction] — but no, because of the specific [mention] in the giving of <s>dakṣiṇā</s> and in the <s>dīkṣā</s>. // MJaiNy_3,7.26 //

children.text:
ye saptadaśa saṃkhyātāḥ, te brahmādiṣu camasādhvaryuṣu ca ye kecidicchayā grahītavyāḥ |
viśeṣasyāśravaṇāt- iti cet |
maivam |
dakṣiṇāvākye dīkṣāvākye ca viśeṣaśravaṇāt |
'ṛtvigbhyo dakṣiṇāṃ dadāti' ityuktvā tadviśeṣaḥ śrūyate- 'agnīdhe dadāti' ' brahmaṇe dadāti' ityādinā |
dīkṣāvākyaṃ ca tatra prakaraṇe 'ye yajamānāsta ṛtvijaḥ' ityuktvānantarameva māmnādyate- 'adhvaryurgṛhapatiṃ dīkṣayitvā brahmāṇaṃ dīkṣayati, tata udvātāram, tato hotāram, tatastaṃ pratiprasthātā dīkṣayitvārdhino dīkṣayati brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaṃ brahmaṇaḥ, prastotāramudgātuḥ, maitrāvaruṇaṃ hotuḥ |
tatastaṃ neṣṭā dīkṣayitvā tṛtīyino dīkṣayati- agnīdhaṃ brahmaṇaḥ, pratihartāramudgātuḥ, acchāvākaṃ hotuḥ |
tatastamunnetā dīkṣayitvā pādino dīkṣayati- potāraṃ brahmaṇaḥ, subrahmaṇyamudgātuḥ, grāvastutaṃ hotuḥ |
tatastamanyo brāhmaṇo dīkṣayati' iti asyāyamarthaḥ- 'adhvaryuryajurvedaproktaṃ karoti, tasya puruṣāstrayaḥ-brāhmaṇācchaṃsī, agnīt, potā ceti |
udgātodgānaṃ karoti, tasya puruṣāstrayaḥ - prastotā, pratihartā, subrahmaṇyaśceti |
hotā śaṃsanaṃ karoti, tasya puruṣāstrayaḥ- maitrāvaruṇaḥ acchāvākaḥ, grāvastuditi |
caturṣu vargeṣu ye prathamāste dakṣiṇāṃ saṃpūrṇā prāpnuvanti |
ye dvitīyāste tadardha prāpnuvanti- ityardhinaḥ |
ye tṛtīyāste tṛtīyāṃśaṃ prāpnuvanti- iti tṛtīyinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who are third receive a third portion — hence they are called <s>tṛtīyins</s> (third-share holders).

children.text: ye caturthāste caturthamaṃśaṃ prāpnuvanti- iti pādinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who are fourth receive a fourth portion — hence they are called <s>pādins</s> (quarter-share holders).

children.text: tāmetānuktakrameṇa sa sa puruṣaḥ saṃskaroti' iti |
children.translated_text: Each person consecrates [those below him] in the stated order.'

children.text: atra - dīkṣāvākye nirdiṣṭā adhvaryuprabhṛtaya ṛtvijaḥ ṣoḍaśa, na tu camasādhvaryavaḥ- iti niyamo draṣṭavyaḥ || MJaiNyC_3,7.26 ||
children.translated_text: Herein — the restriction should be seen that the priests specified in the <s>dīkṣā</s> passage are the sixteen beginning with the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, and not the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>. || MJaiNyC_3,7.26 ||

Those seventeen who are enumerated — they should be taken at will from among the <s>Brahman</s> and others, and the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> — because no specification is heard — if so it is argued, that is not correct. Because specification is heard in the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> passage and the <s>dīkṣā</s> passage. Having stated 'he gives the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> to the priests,' the specification is heard: 'he gives to the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>,' 'he gives to the <s>Brahman</s>,' and so on. And the <s>dīkṣā</s> passage — therein, in that context, having stated 'those who sacrifice are the priests (<s>ṛtvijas</s>),' immediately thereafter it is recorded: 'the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, having consecrated the householder (<s>gṛhapati</s>), consecrates the <s>Brahman</s>; then the <s>Udvātṛ</s>; then the <s>Hotṛ</s>. Then the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s>, having consecrated that one, consecrates the <s>ardhins</s> (half-share holders): the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> for the <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Prastotṛ</s> for the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> for the <s>Hotṛ</s>. Then the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>, having consecrated that one, consecrates the <s>tṛtīyins</s> (third-share holders): the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> for the <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> for the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, the <s>Acchāvāka</s> for the <s>Hotṛ</s>. Then the <s>Unnetṛ</s>, having consecrated that one, consecrates the <s>pādins</s> (quarter-share holders): the <s>Potṛ</s> for the <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s> for the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, the <s>Grāvastut</s> for the <s>Hotṛ</s>. Then another <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> consecrates that one.' The meaning of this is: 'The <s>Adhvaryu</s> performs what is prescribed by the <s>Yajurveda</s>; his assistants are three — the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>, the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, and the <s>Potṛ</s>. The <s>Udgātṛ</s> performs the chanting; his assistants are three — the <s>Prastotṛ</s>, the <s>Pratihartṛ</s>, and the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s>. The <s>Hotṛ</s> performs the recitation; his assistants are three — the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, the <s>Acchāvāka</s>, and the <s>Grāvastut</s>. In each of the four groups, those who are first receive the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> in full. Those who are second receive half — hence they are called <s>ardhins</s> (half-share holders).
(In the eighteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>yajamāna</s> being the seventeenth [along with the sixteen] priests, the <s>sūtra</s>:)
They are seventeen with the patron (<s>svāmin</s>), because of the commonality of the ritual action. / Jaim_3,7.38 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.27
He composes the eighteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Does the seventeenth [status] belong to the <s>sadasya</s> (assessor) or to the <s>yajamāna</s> (patron)?

children.text: sadasye kurute kiṃcinnāsau svāmini tattvataḥ // MJaiNy_3,7.27 //
children.translated_text: It belongs to the <s>sadasya</s>, because he is selected (<s>vṛta</s>); he does something [ritually]; the <s>yajamāna</s> is not truly [an <s>ṛtvik</s>]. // MJaiNy_3,7.27 //

children.text:
adhvaryubrahmādiṣu ṣoḍaśasu vyavasthiteṣu saptadaśasaṃkhyāpūrakaḥ kaścidṛtvigavaikṣitaḥ |
so 'tra sadasyo bhaviṣyati |
sadasyavasthitaḥ sadasyaḥ |
na ca tasya varaṇābhāvaḥ |
keṣāṃcicchākhāyāṃ tadvaraṇasyā'mnātatvāt |
tataḥ sāptadaśyaṃ sadasye paryavasitam- iti cet |
maivam |
asau sadasyaḥ kiṃcidapi na karoti |

children.translated_text: Because there is no injunction '<s>sadasya idaṃ kuryāt</s>' (the <s>sadasya</s> should do this).
And without action, the word '<s>ṛtvik</s>' — whose basis is the occasioning of sacrifice (<s>ṛtu-yajana</s>) — cannot apply to him.
But the <s>yajamāna</s> does perform the renunciation (<s>tyāga</s>) [of the offering], so [the designation] is appropriate for him.
Therefore, the seventeen-count is properly [completed] by the <s>yajamāna</s>. || MJaiNyC_3,7.27 ||

When the sixteen priests beginning with the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and <s>Brahman</s> have been settled, some priest completing the seventeen-count is sought. He would be the <s>sadasya</s> (assessor) — the one stationed in the <s>sadas</s> (assembly hall). Nor is there an absence of selection for him — because in some Vedic recensions, his selection is recorded. Therefore, the seventeen-count is fulfilled in the <s>sadasya</s> — if so it is argued, that is not correct. That <s>sadasya</s> does not do anything at all.

children.text: (ekonaviṃśe- ādhvaryavādiṣvadhvaryvādīnāṃ kartṛtāniyamādhikaraṇe, (viṃśe- agneḥ prakṛtivikṛtisarvārthatādhikaraṇe, ca sūtrāṇi 39 - Jaim_3,7.42)
children.translated_text: (In the nineteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the restriction of the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and others as agents of the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> and other [rites], and in the twentieth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the archetype-modification-universal scope of the fires, <s>sūtras</s> 39–42:)

children.text: te sarvārthāḥ prayuktatvād agnayaś ca svakālatvāt / Jaim_3,7.39 /
children.translated_text: They serve all purposes, because they are employed; and the fires also, because of their belonging to the proper time. / Jaim_3,7.39 /

children.text: tatsaṃyogāt karmaṇo vyavasthā syāt saṃyogasyārthavattvāt / Jaim_3,7.40 /
children.translated_text: The restriction of the ritual action would be from the connection with that [specific agent], because the connection is purposeful. / Jaim_3,7.40 /
The specification thereof is by the instruction and the designation (<s>samākhyā</s>). / Jaim_3,7.41 /
And similarly, because of the observation of the mark. / Jaim_3,7.42 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.28
He composes the nineteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: na kārya niyataṃ teṣāṃ niyataṃ vāgrimo yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Is the work (<s>kārya</s>) of these [priests] not restricted, or is it restricted? The first [alternative], since

children.text: śaktāḥ kena kimityatra niyatiḥ syātsamākhyayā // MJaiNy_3,7.28 //
children.translated_text: all are capable [of performing any task] — how would restriction arise here? It would arise by designation. // MJaiNy_3,7.28 //

children.text:
teṣāmadhvaryuprabhṛtīnāṃ kārya na niyatam |
yataḥ sarve sarvatra śaktāḥ |
prakaraṇaṃ ca sarvasādhāraṇatvānna niyāmakam- iti cet-

children.translated_text: that is not correct.
Because the designation (<s>samākhyā</s>) is a restricting factor.
The ritual action for which the designation '<s>ādhvaryavam</s>' (belonging to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>) [exists] — that action belongs to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>.
Similarly in other cases as well. || MJaiNyC_3,7.28 ||

The work of these — the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and the others — is not restricted. Because all are capable in every [task]. And the context, being common to all, is not a restricting factor — if so it is argued,
(In the twentieth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the archetype-modification-universal scope of the fires — a portion of the stated <s>sūtra</s>:)
And the fires [serve all purposes], because of their belonging to the proper time. // MJaiNyC_3,7.31 //
He composes the twentieth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
START MJaiNy 3,7.29
Does the fire serve only the archetype, or all [sacrifices]? Let the first [hold], as with the <s>Parṇa</s> [wood];
the <s>Parṇa</s> reasoning applies to what is transferred (<s>atidiṣṭa</s>); but for what is [directly] instructed (<s>upadiṣṭa</s>), it is universal. // MJaiNy_3,7.29 //

children.text:
yathā 'yasya parṇamayī juhūrbhavati na sa pāpaṃ ślokaṃ śṛṇoti' ityasau parṇavidhiḥ prakṛtyarthaḥ |
evamādhānasyāpyanārabhyā dhītatvādāhita āhavanīyādyagniḥ prakṛtyarthaḥ- iti cet-
maivam |
vaiṣamyāt |
parṇavākyātparṇatāyā yāvatkratupraveśe juhūrdvāram |
sā ca juhūḥ prakṛtāveva vihitā vikṛtiṣu sarvatrātidiśyate |
āhavanīyādyagnestu kraptupradeśe dvāraṃ homaḥ |
sa ca kvacitprakṛtāveva vihitaḥ sanvikṛtāvatidiśyate |
tadyathāprayāṇanāriṣṭhādihomāḥ |
tādṛśe viṣaye 'yadāhavanīye juhvati' iti vākyenāgniḥ prakṛtāveva vidhīyate |
vikṛtau tu homena sahātidiśyate |
tasmāsatra parṇanyāyaḥ |

children.translated_text: But when the oblation is [directly] instructed (<s>upadiśyate</s>) in the modification,
for example, the <s>Āmana-homa</s> (vessel-oblation) in the <s>iṣṭi</s> called <s>Sāṃgrahaṇī</s>,

children.text: tatra dvārarabhūtasya homasya vikṛtāvupadiśyamānatayā dvāriṇo 'pi prakṛtāviva vikṛtāvapi vākyena vidhirdhārayitumaśakyaḥ |
children.translated_text: there, since the oblation — which is the gateway — is directly instructed in the modification, it is impossible to maintain that the fire (which enters through the gateway) is enjoined by the sentence only in the archetype, as in [the case of the archetype].
Therefore, the fire serves all purposes. || MJaiNyC_3,7.29 ||

Just as the <s>Parṇa</s> injunction — '<s>yasya parṇamayī juhūr bhavati na sa pāpaṃ ślokaṃ śṛṇoti</s>' (he whose <s>juhū</s> ladle is of <s>Parṇa</s> wood does not hear ill repute) — serves the archetype's purpose, so too the establishment of fire (<s>ādhāna</s>), being stated without reference [to any specific context], and the established <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other fires should serve only the archetype's purpose — if so it is argued, that is not correct. Because of the dissimilarity. For the <s>Parṇa</s> passage, the gateway to entry into all sacrifices is the <s>juhū</s> ladle. And that <s>juhū</s> is enjoined only in the archetype, and is transferred (<s>atidiśyate</s>) to all modifications everywhere. But for the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other fires, the gateway to entry into the sacrifice is the oblation (<s>homa</s>). And that [oblation] is sometimes enjoined only in the archetype and transferred to modifications — such as the oblations of the <s>prayāṇa</s>, <s>nāriṣṭha</s>, and the like. In such cases, the sentence '<s>yad āhavanīye juhvati</s>' (when they offer in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>) enjoins the fire only for the archetype. And in modifications, it is transferred along with the oblation. Therefore, here the <s>Parṇa</s> reasoning applies.
(In the twenty-first [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the overriding of designation, <s>sūtras</s> 43–45:)
The direction (<s>praiṣa</s>) and the recitation (<s>anuvacana</s>) belong to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, because of the instruction. / Jaim_3,7.43 /
Or the <s>Hotṛ</s> has the right to the <s>puro'nuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse), because of the proximity to the direction. / Jaim_3,7.44 /
And from the observation [of the <s>Hotṛ</s>] in the morning <s>anuvāka</s>. / Jaim_3,7.45 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.30-31
