He composes the twenty-first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> directs (<s>preṣyati</s>) and also recites (<s>anu cāha</s>) — this overrides
the designation of <s>Hautra</s> (belonging to the <s>Hotṛ</s>) and the like — does this [apply] everywhere, or [only] in some cases? // MJaiNy_3,7.30 //
The first [i.e. everywhere], because of the statement; but no — because of the observation of togetherness in the statement,

children.text: praiṣānuvacane yatra sahite tatra bādhanam // MJaiNy_3,7.31 //
children.translated_text: where the direction and the recitation are stated together, there alone the overriding [applies]. // MJaiNy_3,7.31 //

children.text:
agnīṣomīyapaśau śrūyate- 'maitrāvaruṇaḥ preṣyati cānu cā'ha' iti |
tadetadvākyaṃ praiṣānuvacanayormaitrāvaruṇakartṛkatāṃ vidadhāti |
tena ca vākyena samākhyā bādhyate |
'agnaye samidhyamānāyānubrūhi' 'yūpāyājyamānāyānubrūhi' ityādipraiṣāṇāmadhvaryu kartṛkatvadarśanāt- 'ādhvaryavāḥ praiṣāḥ' ityasti yājñikānāṃ samākhyā |
tathā |
'pravo bājā abhidyavaḥ'- 'añjanti tvāmadhvare devayantaḥ' ityādyanuvacanānāṃ hotṛkartṛkatvadarśanāt |
'anuvacanāni hautrāṇi'- iti yājñikasamākhyā |
praiṣānuvacane ca dvividhe- samaste vyaste ca |
pūrvodāhṛte vyaste |
'hotāpakṣadagniṃ samidham'- ityādyanuvacanamantrasyānte 'hotaryaja' iti praiṣa āmnātaḥ |
ete praiṣānuvacane samaste |
teṣu ca vyastasamastapraiṣānuvacaneṣu sarvatra prabalena vākyena samākhyāṃ bādhitvā hotṛkartṛkatvamadhvaryukartṛkatvaṃ ca parityajya maitrāvaruṇakartṛkatvamevābhyupayem- iti prāpte-
children.translated_text: In all those separate and combined directions and recitations, should we accept, by the stronger statement overriding the designation, that the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> is the agent — setting aside the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s and <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s agency in all cases? — having arrived at this position,

children.text: abhidhīyate- 'preṣyati cānu cā'ha' iti cakāradvayena praiṣānuvacanayoḥ samuccayo vākye 'sminnupalabhyate |
children.translated_text: It is stated: by the two <s>ca</s>-particles in '<s>preṣyati cānu cāha</s>' (and he directs and he responds), the combination of the <s>praiṣa</s> (directive) and the <s>anuvacana</s> (response) is perceived in this sentence.
Therefore, the overriding of the designation applies only to the combined [pair].
But for the separate [praiṣa and anuvacana], the agent-status of the <s>Hotṛ</s> and the like according to the designation should be accepted. || MJaiNyC_3,7.30-31 ||

In the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal sacrifice, it is heard: '<s>maitrāvaruṇaḥ preṣyati cānu cāha</s>' (the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> directs and also recites). This statement enjoins the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> as the agent of both the direction (<s>praiṣa</s>) and the recitation (<s>anuvacana</s>). And by this statement, the designation is overridden. Since the agency of the <s>Adhvaryu</s> is observed in directions such as '<s>agnaye samidhyamānāyānubrūhi</s>' (recite for <s>Agni</s> being kindled), '<s>yūpāya ājyamānāya anubrūhi</s>' (recite for the sacrificial post being anointed), there exists the ritualists' designation '<s>ādhvaryavāḥ praiṣāḥ</s>' (the directions belong to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>). Likewise, since the agency of the <s>Hotṛ</s> is observed in recitations such as '<s>pravo vājā abhidyavaḥ</s>' (forth, O prizes, heavenward) and '<s>añjanti tvām adhvare devayantaḥ</s>' (the god-seekers anoint you in the sacrifice), there exists the ritualists' designation '<s>anuvacanāni hautrāṇi</s>' (the recitations belong to the <s>Hotṛ</s>). And the directions and recitations are of two kinds: combined (<s>samasta</s>) and separate (<s>vyasta</s>). The earlier examples are of the separate kind. When the recitation <s>mantra</s> '<s>hotā pakṣad agniṃ samidham</s>' concludes with the direction '<s>hotar yaja</s>' (O <s>Hotṛ</s>, offer) — these are combined directions and recitations.
The cups [are offered] by the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>, because of the designation (<s>samākhyā</s>). / Jaim_3,7.46 /
(In the twenty-second <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the <s>Adhvaryu</s> or the <s>Camasādhvaryu</s> performs the cup-oblation, <s>sūtras</s> 46–49)
Or [by] the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, because it follows that principle. / Jaim_3,7.47 /
And because in [the matter of] the cup, a different [agent] is seen. / Jaim_3,7.48 /
They [the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>] would be recognized when [the <s>Adhvaryu</s>] is unable. / Jaim_3,7.49 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.32-33
He composes the twenty-second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Does the <s>Camasādhvaryu</s> offer the oblation with the cups, or the <s>Adhvaryu</s> himself?
The first, because of the specific designation; but no — because of the [general] designation '<s>Adhvaryu</s>.' // MJaiNy_3,7.32 //
Since the specific [designation] does not depend [on the general], while the other [<s>Camasādhvaryu</s>] depends on that [general designation];
the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should offer when able; when he is unable, then the other [<s>Camasādhvaryu</s>] may [do so]. // MJaiNy_3,7.33 //

children.text:
'camasādhvaryuḥ' ityevaṃvidhasaṃjñāviśeṣāccamasādhvaryava eva camasairjuhuyuḥ - iti cet |
maivam |
adhvaryusaṃjñāyā nirapekṣatvena prabalatvāt |
kevalādhvaryau camasādhvaryuṣu cānugato 'dhvaryuśabdaḥ sāmānyarūpaḥ |
camasaśabdastu camasādhvaryuṣveveti viśeṣarūpaḥ |
taṃ ca viśeṣamanapekṣyaivādhvaryuśabda ṛtviksaṃjñārūpeṇa vartituṃ prabhavati |
children.translated_text: And the word '<s>adhvaryu</s>' is capable of functioning as a priestly designation independent of that specific [qualifier].
But the word '<s>camasa</s>' becomes a designation for persons only by depending on the general word '<s>adhvaryu</s>'.

children.text: tathā sati 'ādhvaryavo homaḥ' ityanayāṃ nirapekṣayāṃ prabalayā samākhyayādhvaryureva satyāṃ śaktau camasairjuhuyāt |
children.translated_text: This being so, by the independent and stronger designation '<s>ādhvaryava</s>' (pertaining to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>) in '<s>ādhvaryavo homaḥ</s>' (the oblation belongs to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>), the <s>Adhvaryu</s> himself should offer with the cups when he is able.
When he is occasionally unable due to being occupied with the cup-oblation, the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> should offer. || MJaiNyC_3,7.32-33 ||

The <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> alone should offer with the cups, because of the specific designation '<s>Camasādhvaryu</s>' — if so argued, that is not so. Because the designation '<s>Adhvaryu</s>' is stronger due to its independence. The word '<s>adhvaryu</s>' in its general sense applies both to the chief <s>Adhvaryu</s> and to the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s>. But the word '<s>camasa</s>' applies only to the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> — hence it is specific in form.
(In the twenty-third <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the multiple agents in the <s>Śyena</s> and <s>Vājapeya</s> [sacrifices], <s>sūtras</s> 50–51)
Because of the Vedic instruction, as before, when [the rite] belongs to a different Veda, they should be according to the instruction. / Jaim_3,7.50 /

children.text: tadguṇād vā svadharmaḥ syād adhikārasāmarthyāt sahāṅgair avyaktaḥ śeṣe / Jaim_3,7.51 /
children.translated_text: Or, because of its being a secondary attribute of that [archetype], one's own properties would apply — from the capacity of the eligibility, together with the accessories, [but] unexpressed in the remainder. / Jaim_3,7.51 /
START MJaiNy 3,7.34-35
He composes the twenty-third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The <s>Śyena</s> [sacrifice], mentioned in the <s>Udgātṛ</s>'s (<s>Sāmaveda</s>) text, and the <s>Vājapeya</s>, in the <s>Yajurveda</s> —
should [the <s>Śyena</s>] be performed by the <s>Udgātṛ</s> and [the <s>Vājapeya</s>] by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, or should the first follow the archetype? // MJaiNy_3,7.34 //
Because the injunction (<s>codaka</s>) precedes the designation, which [arises from] a specific designation,
the agents, as in the archetype, are established in their respective functions. // MJaiNy_3,7.35 //

children.text:
śyenayāgaḥ sāmavede samāmnāta iti tatratyāḥ sarve padārthā udgātrānuṣṭheyāḥ, bahiṣpavamānājyapṛṣṭhādistotreṣvivodgātratva samākhyāyāḥ śyone 'pi samatvāt |
tathā- yajurvede samāmnāto vājapeyaḥ sarvo 'pyadhvaryuṇaivānuṣṭheyaḥ |
samākhyāvaśāt- iti prāpte-
brūmaḥ- śyenavājapeyau hi jyotiṣṭomavikārau |

children.translated_text: Therein, the injunction (<s>codaka</s>) assigns the various elements to their respective persons for performance.

After the accessories are extended [from the archetype], the procedure-statement (<s>prayogavacana</s>) comes into operation to prescribe the performance of the principal [rite] together with [its] accessories.
But the designation, which depends on the procedure-statement, is extremely subordinate.

children.text: tataḥ prabalacodakavaśātprakṛtāviva nānāvidhāḥ kartāraḥ svasvadharmeṣu vyavatiṣṭhante || MJaiNyC_3,7.34-35 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, by the force of the stronger injunction, as in the archetype, the various agents are established in their respective functions. || MJaiNyC_3,7.34-35 ||

The <s>Śyena</s> sacrifice is taught in the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, so all its elements should be performed by the <s>Udgātṛ</s> — since the designation '<s>Udgātṛ</s>' applies equally to the <s>Śyena</s> as to the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s>, <s>Ājyapṛṣṭha</s>, and other <s>stotras</s>. Similarly, the <s>Vājapeya</s>, taught in the <s>Yajurveda</s>, should be performed entirely by the <s>Adhvaryu</s> alone — by force of the designation. Having arrived at this position, we say: the <s>Śyena</s> and the <s>Vājapeya</s> are modifications (<s>vikāra</s>) of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīya jaiminīyanyāyamālavistare tṛtīyādhyāyasya saptamaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the seventh <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the glorious <s>Mādhavīya Jaiminīya Nyāyamālā Vistara</s>.
Now the eighth <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s>.
(In the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the purchase [of priests] is the sacrificer's action, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
The purchase is the owner's (<s>svāmin</s>'s) action, because the ritual serves the purpose of that [owner]. / Jaim_3,8.1 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.1-2
He composes the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> in the eighth <s>pāda</s> —
The purchase through <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (priestly gifts) and the like — does it belong to the <s>ṛtvij</s> (priest) or to the owner (<s>svāmin</s>)?
From the designation, the purchase would belong to the <s>ṛtvij</s>; how [could it be] otherwise? // MJaiNy_3,8.1 //
Since before the purchase, the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, <s>Hotṛ</s>, and others do not [yet] exist,
the agency of purchasing belongs to the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>), not to the <s>ṛtvij</s>. // MJaiNy_3,8.2 //

children.text:
dakṣiṇādānena karmakarāḥ parikretavyāḥ |
tatra havistyāgavyatiriktaṃ sarvamārtvivyam- iti nirṇītam |
dakṣiṇā ca dvādaśaśatarūpādhvaryuveda udgātṛvede ca samāmnātai |

children.translated_text: The supplementary <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (<s>anvāhārya</s>) [is taught] in the <s>Adhvaryu Veda</s>.
Therefore, by the designation, the purchasing agency belongs to the <s>ṛtvij</s> (priest) — if so argued,
that is not so.

children.text: ṛtvijāṃ parikrayaṇottarakālīnānāṃ tatkartṛtvāsaṃbhavena yajamānasyaiva tatkartṛtvāt || MJaiNyC_3,8.1-2 ||
children.translated_text: Since the <s>ṛtvijs</s> come into existence only after the purchase, they cannot be its agents; therefore, the purchasing agency belongs to the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>) alone. || MJaiNyC_3,8.1-2 ||

The ritual workers are to be purchased through the giving of <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (priestly gifts). Therein, it has been established that all priestly service except the offering of the oblation substance is encompassed [by this purchase]. The <s>dakṣiṇā</s> in the form of twelve hundred [cows] is taught in the <s>Adhvaryu Veda</s> (<s>Yajurveda</s>) and in the <s>Udgātṛ Veda</s> (<s>Sāmaveda</s>).
(In the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the giving of boons is the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s action, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
From the [Vedic] statement, it would belong to the others. / Jaim_3,8.2 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.3
He composes the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Does the giving of boons in [connection with] the sacrificial bricks (<s>iṣṭakā</s>) belong to the owner (<s>svāmin</s>) or to the <s>ṛtvij</s>?
Like the previous [case], it belongs to the owner; but no — from the [Vedic] statement, it belongs to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. // MJaiNy_3,8.3 //
'He who should place this brick — he should give three boons' — the giving of three [boons] by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, who places [the bricks], is based on the Vedic statement (<s>vācanika</s>).
Indeed, there is no excessive burden on the [Vedic] statement. || MJaiNyC_3,8.3 ||
(In the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the consecrations such as shaving and the like belong to the sacrificer, <s>sūtras</s> 3–8)

children.text: saṃskārās tu puruṣasāmarthye yathāvedaṃ karmavadvyavatiṣṭheran / Jaim_3,8.3 /
children.translated_text: The consecrations (<s>saṃskāras</s>), when within the person's capacity, should be established according to the [respective] Veda, like rites. / Jaim_3,8.3 /
But they belong to the sacrificer (<s>yājamāna</s>), because that [sacrificer] is the principal, like a rite. / Jaim_3,8.4 /
And because of the designation. / Jaim_3,8.5 /
The statement of that [consecration] is as a secondary element (<s>guṇa</s>). / Jaim_3,8.6 /
And because of [its] being [the object] with respect to the injunction. / Jaim_3,8.7 /
Because of inequality, the procedures would be different. / Jaim_3,8.8 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.4-5
He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The consecrations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) such as shaving and the like — do they belong to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> or to the owner (<s>svāmin</s>)?
To the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, because of his competence therein and because they are stated in his Veda. // MJaiNy_3,8.4 //
By obtaining eligibility through the consecrations, [the sacrificer] hires the <s>ṛtvijs</s> to perform his work;

children.text: krīṇātyataḥ kriyā teṣāṃ saṃskriyā yajamānagā // MJaiNy_3,8.5 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the [other] ritual actions belong to them [the <s>ṛtvijs</s>], but the consecrations are directed toward the sacrificer. // MJaiNy_3,8.5 //

children.text:
'āpa undantu jīvase' ityādyāḥ saṃskāramantrāḥ |
tadvidhayaścādhvaryuvede samāmnātāḥ- 'keśaśmaśru vapate','nakhāni nikṛntate' iti |
śaktaścādhvaryurvapanādau |
tasmāt- tasyādhvaryoste vapanādisaṃskārāḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
vapanādisaṃskārā yajamānagatamālinyamapanīya yāgayogyatāmutpādayituṃ kriyante |
tathā ca brāhmaṇam- 'keśaśmaśru vapate |
mṛtā vā eṣā tvagamedhyā yatkeśaśmaśru |
mutāmeva tvacamamedhyāmapahatya yajñiyo bhūtvā medhamupaiti' iti |
nahyadhvayuvapanena yajamānagatā mṛtā tvagapaiti |
yogyasya hi karmādhikāra sati paścātprayāsarūpeṣu vyāpāreṣu svayamaśaktaḥ sankarmakarānṛtvijaḥ parikrīṇāti |
loke 'pi rogiṇaḥ svāmina auṣadhādyānayana eva bhṛtyo jīvitadānena parikrīyate |

children.translated_text: But it is not the servant who takes the medicine.
Therefore — other ritual actions belong to the <s>ṛtvijs</s>, but the consecrations belong to the sacrificer.
However, in some cases,
from the [Vedic] statement, the consecration may belong to the <s>ṛtvijs</s> as well. || MJaiNyC_3,8.4-5 ||

The consecration <s>mantras</s> are '<s>āpa undantu jīvase</s>' (O waters, wet [him] for life) and the like. Their injunctions are taught in the <s>Adhvaryu Veda</s> — 'he shaves the hair and beard,' 'he trims the nails.' And the <s>Adhvaryu</s> is competent in shaving and the like. Therefore — those consecrations such as shaving belong to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> — if so argued, that is not so. The consecrations such as shaving are performed to remove the impurity inherent in the sacrificer and to produce eligibility for the sacrifice. Thus the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text states]: 'He shaves the hair and beard. This skin from which hair and beard [grow] is indeed dead and impure. Having removed this dead, impure skin, he becomes fit for sacrifice and attains the sacrificial victim.' For indeed, by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s shaving, the dead skin inherent in the sacrificer does not depart. For it is the eligible [person himself who] — having [first] obtained the right to the sacrifice — subsequently hires the <s>ṛtvij</s> priests as ritual workers for the laborious procedures, being himself unable [to perform them]. In the world too, when a sick master [seeks treatment], the servant is hired with the grant of livelihood only for bringing the medicine and the like.
(In the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] austerity (<s>tapas</s>) belongs to the sacrificer, <s>sūtras</s> 9–11)
And austerity (<s>tapas</s>), because it achieves the fruit, like [in] the world. / Jaim_3,8.9 /
And the sentence-complement is likewise. / Jaim_3,8.10 /
From the [Vedic] statement, it would belong to the others. / Jaim_3,8.11 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.5*-6
He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The [injunction] 'he does not eat for two days' — this austerity (<s>tapas</s>) — to which of the two does it belong?
Since it is painful, and since it is a consecration of the enjoyer [of the fruit], the austerity befits the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. // MJaiNy_3,8.5* //
As a consecration that destroys the sin which obstructs the fruit,
from the mark, the austerity belongs to the owner (<s>svāmin</s>), like other consecrations. // MJaiNy_3,8.6 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭhome- 'dvyahaṃ nāśnāti' 'tryahaṃ nāśnāti'ityādinoktaṃ tapo 'ghvaryoryuktam |
tasya duḥkhātmakatvena parikrītapuruṣaiḥ kartumucitatvāt |
duḥkhatvādeva phalabhoktṛsaṃskāratvābhāvādyajamānasya na yuktam- iti cet |
maivam |
bhāvinaḥ sukharūpasya phalasya pratibandhakaṃ duḥkhajanakaṃ yatpāpaṃ tasya nāśakatvena duḥkharūpasyāpi tapasaḥ svāmisaṃskāratvasaṃbhavāt |
asminnarthe vākyaśeṣagataṃ liṅgaṃ kalpasūtrakāreṇaivamudāhṛtam- 'yadā vai dīkṣitaḥ kṛśo bhavati, atha medhyo bhavati |
yadāsminnantarna kiṃcana bhavati, atha medhyo bhavati |
yadāsya kṛṣṇaṃ cakṣuṣornaśyati, atha medhyo bhavati |
yadāsya tvacāsthi saṃdhīyate, atha medhyo bhavati |
pītvā dīkṣate, kṛśo yajate |
yadasyāṅgānāṃ mīyate juhotyeva taditi vijñāyate' iti |
children.translated_text: When [the substance of] his limbs diminishes — that itself is [considered] the offering' — thus it is understood.

children.text: na hi duḥkharūpaṃ tapo vinā duḥkhapradaṃ pāpaṃ naśyati |
children.translated_text: For without the painful austerity, the sin that produces suffering does not perish.
Just as without lancing, poisonous wounds do not heal — so it is.
Therefore — like the consecrations of shaving and the like, the austerity too belongs to the sacrificer alone. || MJaiNyC_3,8.5-6 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the austerity described as 'he does not eat for two days,' 'he does not eat for three days,' and so on — would befit the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. Because, being painful in nature, it is appropriate to be performed by hired persons. Because of its painful nature, it is not appropriate for the sacrificer, since it is not a consecration of the enjoyer of the fruit — if so argued, that is not so. Because even though the austerity is painful in nature, its being a consecration of the owner is possible — as the destroyer of the sin which is pain-producing and which obstructs the future fruit that is of the nature of happiness. On this point, the mark found in the sentence-complement has been cited by the <s>Kalpasūtra</s> author thus: 'When the consecrated one becomes emaciated, then he becomes fit for sacrifice. When nothing remains inside him, then he becomes fit for sacrifice. When the dark [color] disappears from his eyes, then he becomes fit for sacrifice. When his skin adheres to [his] bones, then he becomes fit for sacrifice. Having drunk [Soma], he is consecrated; emaciated, he sacrifices.
(In the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the red turban and the like are duties of all <s>ṛtvijs</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: guṇatvāc ca vedena na vyavasthā syāt / Jaim_3,8.12 /
children.translated_text: And because of the secondary nature, there should be no distinction based on the Veda. / Jaim_3,8.12 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.7-8
He composes the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The consecrations such as wearing a gold necklace and the like — from the [Vedic] statement, they are considered

children.text: ṛtvijāṃ te yathākhyānaṃ kartavyā nikhilairuta // MJaiNy_3,8.7 //
children.translated_text: to belong to the <s>ṛtvijs</s>; should they be performed according to the designation, or by all? // MJaiNy_3,8.7 //
The first [alternative holds] by the force of the designation; but no — from the recitation in the proximity of all;
because each principal [<s>ṛtvij</s>] is the locus for the repetition of the secondary [attribute], they should be performed by all. // MJaiNy_3,8.8 //

children.text:
vājapeye śrūyate- 'hiraṇyamālina ṛtvijaḥ pracaranti' iti |
śyene śrūyate- 'lohitoṣṇīṣā lohitavasanā nivītā ṛtvijaḥ pracaranti' iti |
yadyapi hiraṇyamālitvādīnāṃ saṃskāratvādyajamānaviṣayatvaṃ pūrvanyāyena prāptam, tathāpi vacanādaya mṛtviksaṃskāraḥ |
tatra hiraṇyamālitvaṃ yajurvedoktatvādadhvaryūṇāmeva, lohitoṣṇīṣādikaṃ sāmavedoktatvādudgātṝṇāmeva iti samākhyāvaśādabhyupeyam- iti cet |
children.translated_text: Therein, the wearing of gold necklaces, being stated in the <s>Yajurveda</s>, belongs to the <s>Adhvaryus</s> alone; the red turban and the like, being stated in the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, belongs to the <s>Udgātṛs</s> alone — this should be accepted by force of the designation — if so argued,
that is not so.

children.text: 'hiraṇyamālina ṛtvijaḥ pracaranti' iti sarveṣāmṛtvijāṃ saṃnidhau paṭhyamāno hiraṇyamālitvasaṃskāraḥ saṃnidhinā samākhyāṃ bādhitvā sarvairapyṛtvigbhiḥ saṃbadhyate |
children.translated_text: The consecration of wearing a gold necklace, being recited in the proximity of all <s>ṛtvijs</s> in '<s>hiraṇyamālina ṛtvijaḥ pracaranti</s>' (the <s>ṛtvijs</s> perform wearing gold necklaces), overrides the designation by proximity and is connected with all the <s>ṛtvijs</s>.

children.text: kiṃca- saṃrakāryatvādṛtvijāṃ prādhānye sati pratipradhānaṃ guṇāvṛttyā sarveṣāmapyṛtvijāṃ hiraṇyamālitvādisaṃskāro 'bhyupatevyaḥ || MJaiNyC_3,8.7-8 ||
children.translated_text: Moreover — since the <s>ṛtvijs</s> are [all] equally principal [performers], when each principal is the locus [for the attribute], through the repetition of the secondary [attribute] (<s>guṇāvṛtti</s>), the consecration of wearing gold necklaces and the like should be accepted for all the <s>ṛtvijs</s>. || MJaiNyC_3,8.7-8 ||

In the <s>Vājapeya</s>, it is heard: 'The <s>ṛtvijs</s> perform wearing gold necklaces.' In the <s>Śyena</s>, it is heard: 'The <s>ṛtvijs</s> perform wearing red turbans, red garments, in the <s>nivīta</s> mode.' Even though, by the previous principle, the consecration-nature of wearing gold necklaces and the like would make them pertain to the sacrificer, nevertheless, from the [Vedic] statement, they are consecrations of the <s>ṛtvijs</s>.
(In the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the desire for rain belongs to the sacrificer, <s>sūtras</s> 13–14)
Likewise, the desire [ritual], because of connection with the purpose. / Jaim_3,8.13 /
From the designation, it would belong to the others. / Jaim_3,8.14 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.9-10
He composes the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The desire [expressed as] 'one desiring rain should build the <s>sadas</s> (hall) low' — this wish-ritual —
does it belong to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> or to the owner? The first, from the sentence; the mother [Veda] declares it so. // MJaiNy_3,8.9 //
From the <s>parasmaipada</s> (active voice ending), the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s activity is understood as serving another's purpose;
therefore, overriding the sentence, like [the case of] austerity, let that [desire-ritual] belong to the owner. // MJaiNy_3,8.10 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭhome śrūyate- 'yadi kāmayeta- varṣukaḥ parjanyaḥ syāt- iti nīcaiḥ sado minuyāt' iti |
-yathā purastātpaścāccāvasthitau havirdhānaprācīnavaṃśāvuccaiḥ, tathā sado noccaṃ, kiṃtu nīcaiḥ kāryam- ityarthaḥ |
atra- vṛṣṭikāmanādhvaryoryuktā |
'yaḥ kāmayet, sa minuyāt' iti vākyena kāmayitṛmātrorekatvāvagamāt |
mātṛtvaṃ cādhvaryorityabivādam |
tasmāt- sa kāmayitā- iti cet |
maivam |
'minuyāt' iti parasmaipadenādhvaryuvyāpāraphalasya paragāmitā pratīyate |
tato vṛṣṭilakṣaṇaphalasya yajamānagāmitvātparasmaipadaśrutyā vākyaṃ bādhitvā kāmasya yajamānakartṛkatvaṃ draṣṭavyam |
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the fruit in the form of rain goes to the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>), overriding the sentence by the <s>parasmaipada</s> <s>śruti</s>, the desire should be understood as having the sacrificer as its agent.

children.text: - 'yajamānakāmitāṃ vṛṣṭiṃ parjanyaḥ saṃpādayatu' ityeva yo 'dhvaryuḥ kāmayate, sa nīcairminuyāt, iti vākyaṃ vyākhyeyam |
children.translated_text: The sentence should be explained thus: 'Whichever <s>Adhvaryu</s> desires that <s>Parjanya</s> should produce the rain desired by the sacrificer, he should construct [the <s>Sadas</s>] low.'

children.text: - 'evaṃvidudvātā'tmane vā yajamānāya vā yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate, tamāgāyati' iti ṛtvijo 'pi kāmaḥ- iti cet |
children.translated_text: [If it is argued:] '<s>evaṃvidudgātā'tmane vā yajamānāya vā yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate, tamāgāyati</s>' (the <s>Udgātṛ</s> who knows thus chants for whatever desire he desires, whether for himself or for the sacrificer) — from this, the priest also has a desire — if so,
then, in that meditation on the <s>Udgītha</s>, by the verbal statement, let the priest also have the fruit. || MJaiNyC_3,8.9-10 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, it is heard: '<s>yadi kāmayeta — varṣukaḥ parjanyaḥ syāt — iti nīcaiḥ sado minuyāt</s>' (if one desires that <s>Parjanya</s> [the rain-god] should be rainy, one should construct the <s>Sadas</s> [hall] low). The meaning is: unlike the <s>Havirdhāna</s> and the <s>Prācīnavaṃśa</s> [halls] situated in front and behind which are high, the <s>Sadas</s> should not be high, but should be made low. Therein — [the desire for rain] is appropriate for the <s>Adhvaryu</s> who desires rain. Because the sentence '<s>yaḥ kāmayet, sa minuyāt</s>' (whoever desires, he should construct) conveys the oneness of the desirer alone. And the <s>Adhvaryu</s> is the performer (<s>mātṛ</s>) — this is stated without dispute. Therefore — he is the desirer — if so [it is argued], that is not correct. By the <s>parasmaipada</s> (active voice) in '<s>minuyāt</s>' (he should construct), it is understood that the fruit of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s activity goes to another.
(In the seventh [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the mantras beginning with '<s>āyurdā</s>' (giver of life) belonging to the sacrificer, <s>sūtras</s> 15–16)
And the mantras that are operative instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>) — similarly. / Jaim_3,8.15 /
And because of the observation in disjunction. / Jaim_3,8.16 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.11
He composes the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The mantra-statement '<s>āyurdā</s>' (giver of life) — to whom [does it pertain]? To the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, by designation;
when that is overridden, by the mark, the [fruit] goes to the patron — this is the established view. // MJaiNy_3,8.11 //

children.text: tasyaitasya mantrasya pāṭho 'dhvaryoryajamānasya vā -ityayaṃ saṃśayaḥ 'kasya' ityanena padena sūcitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whether the recitation of this mantra belongs to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> or to the sacrificer — this doubt is indicated by the word 'to whom' (<s>kasya</s>).

children.text: asminmantre 'āyurme dehi' iti phalasya svātmasaṃbandhaḥ pratīyate |
children.translated_text: In this mantra, the connection of the fruit with oneself is understood through '<s>āyurme dehi</s>' (give me life).
And that is appropriate for the sacrificer, not for the <s>Adhvaryu</s>.
Therefore — like the desire [discussed earlier], the mantra too belongs to the sacrificer. || MJaiNyC_3,8.11 ||
This is recited: '<s>āyurdā agne 'syāyurme dehi</s>' (O <s>Agni</s>, giver of life, give me life).
(In the eighth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on a doubly-recited [mantra] being used by both, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
In those that are doubly recited, both [recite], because of the meaningfulness of the double recitation. / Jaim_3,8.17 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.12
He composes the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: vājasya metyamuṃ brūyādeko dvau vā kṛtārthataḥ /
children.translated_text: Should one person or two recite this [mantra] '<s>vājasya me</s>' (of vigor, for me)? Since one achieves the purpose,
[it would be] one; but because of recitation in both sections (<s>kāṇḍas</s>), both the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and the patron [should recite]. // MJaiNy_3,8.12 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ- 'vājasya mā prasavena' ityayaṃ mantro 'dhvaryukāṇḍe yajamānakāṇḍe cā'mnātaḥ |
tatraikena paṭhite sati mantrasya caritārthatvāditarastaṃ na paṭhet- iti cet |
maivam |
kāṇḍāntarapāṭhavaiyarythaprasaṅgāt |

children.translated_text: Therefore, both should recite it.
There is a difference in intention between the two reciters.
The <s>Adhvaryu</s> thinks: 'I shall perform the meaning revealed by this mantra.'
The sacrificer [thinks]: 'I shall not be negligent herein.' || MJaiNyC_3,8.12 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices), this mantra '<s>vājasya mā prasavena</s>' (by the impulse of vigor, for me) is recited in the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s section and in the sacrificer's section. Therein, when one has recited it, the mantra having served its purpose, the other should not recite it — if so [it is argued], that is not correct. Because the recitation in the other section would become purposeless.
(In the ninth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the fact that only one who is knowledgeable should be made to recite, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: jñāte ca vācanaṃ na hy avidvān vihito 'sti / Jaim_3,8.18 /
children.translated_text: And the prompting to recite (<s>vācana</s>) is to one who knows, for an ignorant person is not prescribed. / Jaim_3,8.18 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.13
He composes the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: vācayetsvāminaṃ jñājñau vācamīyau jña eva vā /
children.translated_text: Should one prompt the patron to recite — both the knowledgeable and the ignorant, or only the knowledgeable?
Since there is no distinction, both; [but] because of the patronship of the knowledgeable one, one should prompt him [alone] to recite. // MJaiNy_3,8.13 //

children.text:
vājapeye śrūyate-'kḷptīryajamānaṃ vācayati' iti |
'āryuyajñena kalpatām' ityādayo mantrāḥ kḷptayaḥ |
tatra- mantratadarthābhijñamanabhijñaṃ cobhāvapi vācayet |
'vidvāsaṃ vācayet' ityevaṃ viśeṣasyāśravaṇāt |
anabhijñaṃ tadaiva śikṣayitvāpi vācayituṃ śakyatvāt- iti cet |
children.translated_text: Because even one who is not knowledgeable can be taught at that very time and then prompted to recite — if so [it is argued],
that is not correct.
Because by the force of the injunction of Vedic study (<s>adhyayana</s>), only one who has studied the <s>Veda</s> and understood its meaning is a [proper] sacrificer.
Therefore — one should prompt only the knowledgeable to recite. || MJaiNyC_3,8.13 ||

In the <s>Vājapeya</s> [sacrifice], it is heard: '<s>kḷptīryajamānaṃ vācayati</s>' (he prompts the sacrificer to recite the <s>Kḷpti</s> [mantras]). '<s>āryuyajñena kalpatām</s>' (may [this] be accomplished by the noble sacrifice) and the like are the <s>Kḷpti</s> mantras. Therein — one should prompt both the one who knows the mantra and its meaning and the one who does not know — to recite. Because no specific [requirement] such as 'one should prompt a learned person to recite' is heard.
(In the tenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the twelve pairs [of actions] belonging to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 19–20)

children.text: yājamāne samākhyānāt karmāṇi yājamānaṃ syuḥ / Jaim_3,8.19 /
children.translated_text: In the sacrificer's [section], from the designation, the rites would belong to the sacrificer. / Jaim_3,8.19 /

children.text: adhvaryur vā tadartho hi nyāyapūrve samākhyānam / Jaim_3,8.20 /
children.translated_text: Or [they belong to] the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, for that serves his purpose; the designation is in the domain of the principle (<s>nyāya</s>). / Jaim_3,8.20 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.14-15
He composes the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'One releases the calf and likewise puts the pot on [the fire]' —
these twelve pairs of actions — do they belong to the patron or to the other [the <s>Adhvaryu</s>]? // MJaiNy_3,8.14 //
The first [view: the patron], because of the recitation in the patron's section; by the purposefulness of hiring,
let the latter [view] hold — from the recitation in the main section; herein, the enumeration as pairs alone is stated. // MJaiNy_3,8.15 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoryājamāne kāṇḍe śrūyate- 'dvādaśa dvaṃdvāni darśapūrṇamāsayostāni saṃpādyāni- ityāhuḥ- vatsaṃ copāvasṛjati, ukhāṃ cādhiśrayati' ayaṃ ca hanti, dṛṣadau ca samāhanti' ityādi |
tatra- palāśaśākhayā vatsāpākaraṇamekaṃ karma, dohanena saṃpāditaṃ kṣīraṃ dhārayituṃ piṭharasthāpanamaparaṃ karma, tadetadubhavamekaṃ dvaṃdvam |
tathā vrīhīṇāmavaghātaḥ, dṛṣadupalayoḥ pāṣāṇāntareṇa samāghātaḥ, ityetadubhayaṃ dvitīyaṃ dvaṃdvam |
evaṃ dvādaśa karmadvaṃdvānyanuṣṭheyānyāmnātāni |
teṣāṃ yājamāne kāṇḍe paṭhitatvātsamākhyayā yajamānena tānyanuṣṭheyāni- iti prāpte-
brūmaḥ- yajamānasya yāni kāryāṇi, tānyanuṣṭhātumeva parikrītā ṛtvijaḥ |
kiṃca- yajurvede yājamānamidamavāntara kāṇḍam, mahākāṇḍaṃ tvādhvaryavameva |
tatraivaite vatsāpākaraṇādayo dharmā āmnātāḥ |

children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> alone should perform them.

children.text: yājamāne tu kāṇḍe na yevāmanuṣṭhānaprakāraścoditaḥ, kiṃtu parigaṇanayā dvaṃdvatāsaṃpādanamātramāmnātam |
children.translated_text: And in the sacrificer's section, the manner of performance is not enjoined at all; rather, only the enumeration as pairs is recited.

children.text: tena yajamānastāmānupūrvī manasi nidhāyādhvaryoranuṣṭhāne pramādarāhityamanusaṃdhātuṃ prabhavati |
children.translated_text: By that, the sacrificer, bearing that sequence in mind, is able to ensure the absence of negligence in the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s performance.
Therefore, the performance belongs to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> alone. || MJaiNyC_3,8.14-15 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices), in the sacrificer's section, it is heard: 'There are twelve pairs in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>; they are to be accomplished' — thus they say — 'he releases the calf and puts the pot on [the fire]; he threshes and strikes the two grinding stones' and so on. Therein — driving away the calf with a <s>palāśa</s> (leaf) branch is one action; placing the pot (<s>piṭhara</s>) to hold the milk produced by milking is another action; these two together form one pair. Similarly, the threshing of the rice grains and the striking together of the two grinding stones with another stone — these two form the second pair. Thus twelve pairs of actions are recited as to be performed. Since they are recited in the sacrificer's section, by the designation, the sacrificer should perform them — having arrived at this position, we say: The priests are hired precisely to perform those tasks that are the sacrificer's duties. Moreover — this sacrificer's section is a sub-section within the <s>Yajurveda</s>; but the main section is the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s section itself. And it is there that these properties such as calf-driving and the like are recited.
(In the eleventh [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on whether the <s>Hotṛ</s> performs the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s operative acts, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: vipratiṣedhe karaṇaḥ samavāyaviśeṣād itaram anyas teṣāṃ yato viśeṣaḥ syāt / Jaim_3,8.21 /
children.translated_text: In the case of conflict, the operative agent [performs], because of the specific connection; the other [performs] the rest — for them, [the specific connection determines] from which the specification arises. / Jaim_3,8.21 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.16-17
He composes the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
He who is [both] the <s>Hotṛ</s> and the <s>Adhvaryu</s> — performing the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s [act],

children.text: hautraṃ kuryānna vā tyāgahetvamāvātkaroti tat // MJaiNy_3,8.16 //
children.translated_text: should he perform the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s [act] or not? There is no reason to abandon it, so he should perform it. // MJaiNy_3,8.16 //
One <s>Hotṛ</s> cannot perform two acts simultaneously;
let him abandon the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s [act] obtained from the enjoining authority, and perform the verbally prescribed [<s>Adhvaryu</s>'s] act. // MJaiNy_3,8.17 //

children.text:
agnīṣomīyavaśau 'parivīrasi' ityanena karaṇamantreṇādhvaryuryūpasya raśanayā pariṣyāṇaṃ karoti |
tadānīṃ kriyamāṇaṃ tatparivyaṇaṃ hotā 'yuvā suvāsāḥ'- ityanena mantreṇānuvadati |
tadetadubhayaṃ codakaparamparayā kuṇḍapāyināmayane prāptam |
tatrādhvaryorhotuśca samāsa āmnātaḥ- 'yo hotā so 'dhvaryuḥ' iti |
hotāramanūṣṭhā dhvaryutvavidhānādadhvaryukārye hotrānuṣṭheyam |
tataḥ 'parivīrasi' ityanena karaṇamantreṇa hotā yūpaparivyāṇaṃ kurvīta |
tadānīṃ svasya codakataḥ prāptaṃ hautramapi hotā na tyajet |
nahi tyāgahetuṃ kaṃcinniṣedhaṃ paśyāmaḥ |
tasmātkriyamāṇaṃ tatparivyāṇaṃ 'yuvā struṣāsāḥ' ityanena mantreṇa hotānuvadet- iti prāpte-
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>Hotṛ</s> should recite along with the mantra '<s>yuvā suvāsāḥ</s>' (the young one, well-clothed) as the wrapping is being performed — having arrived at this position,

children.text: brūmaḥ- dvayoradhvaryuhotrorucitaṃ karmadvayameko hotā yugapatkartu na śaknoti |
children.translated_text: we say: One <s>Hotṛ</s> cannot simultaneously perform two acts — [one each] appropriate to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and the <s>Hotṛ</s>.

children.text: tato 'nyatarasyāvaśyaṃbhāvini tyāge codakataḥ prāptaṃ hautrameva tyajet |
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the abandonment of one is inevitable, he should abandon precisely the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s [act] that is obtained from the enjoining authority.

children.text: ādvayava tu 'yo hotā so 'dhvaryuḥ' ityanena prāpitatvādanuṣṭheyam || MJaiNyC_3,8.16-17 ||
children.translated_text: But the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s [act], being obtained through '<s>yo hotā so 'dhvaryuḥ</s>' (whoever is the <s>Hotṛ</s>, he is the <s>Adhvaryu</s>), should be performed. || MJaiNyC_3,8.16-17 ||

In the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal [sacrifice], the <s>Adhvaryu</s> performs the wrapping of the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) with the rope using the operative mantra (<s>karaṇamantra</s>) '<s>parivīrasi</s>' (you are the encloser). At that time, the <s>Hotṛ</s> recites along with the mantra '<s>yuvā suvāsāḥ</s>' (the young one, well-clothed). Both of these are obtained through the chain of enjoining authority in the <s>Kuṇḍapāyin</s> journey. Therein, the identity of the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and the <s>Hotṛ</s> is recited: '<s>yo hotā so 'dhvaryuḥ</s>' (whoever is the <s>Hotṛ</s>, he is the <s>Adhvaryu</s>). Since the <s>Adhvaryu</s>-status is enjoined after the <s>Hotṛ</s>-status, the <s>Hotṛ</s> should perform the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s task. Then, the <s>Hotṛ</s> should perform the wrapping of the sacrificial post with the operative mantra '<s>parivīrasi</s>' (you are the encloser). At the same time, the <s>Hotṛ</s> should not abandon his own <s>Hotṛ</s>'s task obtained from the enjoining authority. For we see no prohibition that would be a reason for abandoning it.
(In the twelfth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the sprinkling-water placement and the like not being the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s [task], the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
And in the directives (<s>praiṣas</s>), because the authority belongs to another. / Jaim_3,8.22 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.18
He composes the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Should the <s>Adhvaryu</s> perform the placement of the sprinkling water, or another [priest]?
By the designation, the first [the <s>Adhvaryu</s>]; [but] since '<s>sādaya</s>' (place!) is a directive [to another], the other [priest], by the mark. // MJaiNy_3,8.18 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ- prokṣaṇīnāṃ kenacitpātreṇa vedyāmātādanaṃ śrutam |
tadetadyajurvedoktatvādādhvaryam- iti cet |
maivam |
praiṣamantravirodhaprasaṅgāt |
'prokṣaṇīrāsādaya |

children.translated_text: '<s>Idmāvarhirupatādava</s>' (Bring the fuel-sticks and sacred grass!).
'<s>Agnīdagnīnvihara</s>' (O <s>Āgnīdh</s>, carry forward the fires!).

children.text: varhiḥ stṛṇīhi' ityādiṣvādhvaryaveṣu praiṣamantreṣu śrūyamāṇamāgnīṃprasaṃbodhanaṃ madhyamapuruṣaścānyena tadanuṣṭhāne satyupapadyate |
children.translated_text: '<s>Varhiḥ stṛṇīhi</s>' (Spread the sacred grass!)' — in these directive-mantras belonging to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, the addressing of the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> and the second-person [verb form] are explained only when another person performs [the act].
Therefore — it is not the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s [task]. || MJaiNyC_3,8.18 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices), the placement of the sprinkling waters with some vessel on the altar (<s>vedi</s>) is heard. This, being stated in the <s>Yajurveda</s>, would be the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s [task] — if so [it is argued], that is not correct. Because there would be a conflict with the directive-mantras. '<s>Prokṣaṇīrāsādaya</s>' (Place the sprinkling waters!).
(In the thirteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the directive-mantras belonging to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 23–24)
But the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, because of the observation [of the mark]. / Jaim_3,8.23 /
Or secondary, because of the commonality of the rite. / Jaim_3,8.24 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.19
He composes the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Does the <s>Adhvaryu</s> direct [the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>] as a messenger, or is the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> [the speaker] — without contradiction?
Because of the contradiction with the designation, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> [directs], since he accomplishes the purpose through the directive. // MJaiNy_3,8.19 //

children.text:
yathā prokṣaṇīrāgnīdhra āsādayati, tathā praiṣamantramapyāgnīdhra eva paṭhatu |
virodhābhāvāt - iti cet |
maivam |

children.translated_text: Because of the contradiction with the designation '<s>Ādhvaryava</s>' (belonging to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>), and with the addressing and second-person [forms] cited earlier.

children.text: na ca - prokṣaṇyāsādanādīnāma dhvaryukartṛkatvābhāve 'pi samākhyāvirodhastadavasthaḥ- iti vācyam |
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that — even in the absence of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s agency for the placement of sprinkling water and the like, the contradiction with the designation remains the same.
Because even in the capacity of instigator-agent through the directive, there is no contradiction [with the designation].
Therefore — the directive-mantra belongs to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> alone. || MJaiNyC_3,8.19 ||
Just as the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> places the sprinkling waters, let the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> also recite the directive-mantra. Because there is no contradiction — if so [it is argued], that is not correct.
(In the fourteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the fruit of the operative mantras being attributable to the patron (the <s>varcas</s> principle), <s>sūtras</s> 25–27)
The priest [receives] the fruit in operative [mantras], because of the purposefulness. / Jaim_3,8.25 /
Or [it belongs to] the patron, because it serves his purpose. / Jaim_3,8.26 /
And because the mark is observed. / Jaim_3,8.27 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.20
He composes the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: mamāgna iti kasyātra phalaṃ liṅgena vaktṛgam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Mamāgne</s>' (for me, O <s>Agni</s>) — to whom does the fruit belong here? By the mark, to the reciter;

children.text: śrutyā svāmini na krīte liṅgaṃ tatropacaryatām // MJaiNy_3,8.20 //
children.translated_text: by the <s>śruti</s>, to the patron — [since the priest is] hired, let the mark be figuratively construed [as referring to the patron]. // MJaiNy_3,8.20 //

children.text:
'mamāgne varco vihaveṣvastu' ityayamāhavanīyasyānvādhāne karaṇabhūto mantro 'dhva- |
rpuṇā paṭhyate |
'viśiṣṭaṃ havanaṃ yeṣāṃ yajñānāṃ te vihavāsteṣu varcastejasopalakṣitaṃ yatphalaṃ tanmamāstu' ityanena liṅgena mantramuccārayituradhvaryostatphalam- iti cet |
maivam |
'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta' ityātmanepadaśrutyā sāṅgapradhānaphalasya yajamānagāmitvaṃ pratīyate |

children.translated_text: And it is not proper that the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, who is hired [for a fee], should have a connection with a fruit beyond the sacrificial fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>).
Therefore — that mark, being in conflict with the <s>śruti</s> and the principle (<s>nyāya</s>), should be figuratively construed as pertaining to the sacrificer.
The figurative construal is thus: 'May that brilliance belong to my sacrificer.'

children.text: tasmāt- yajamānena pāṭhyeṣu 'āyurdā agne 'syāyurme dehi' ityādiṣu kriyamāṇānuvādiṣu pratyagāśīrmantreṣu śrutaṃ phalaṃ yathā yājamānam, tathaivādhvaryuṇā pāṭhyeṣu karaṇamantreṣu śrutamapi phalaṃ yājamānameva || MJaiNyC_3,8.20 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — just as in the mantras recited by the sacrificer — namely the self-blessing (pratyag-āśīr) mantras such as 'āyurdā agne asy āyur me dehi' (O Agni, you are the giver of life, give me life) recited while performing the reiteration (anuvāda) — the fruit heard therein belongs to the sacrificer, similarly even the fruit heard in the instrument-mantras (karaṇa-mantra) recited by the Adhvaryu also belongs to the sacrificer alone. || MJaiNyC_3,8.20 ||

'<s>Mamāgne varco vihaveṣvastu</s>' (O <s>Agni</s>, may brilliance be mine in the offerings) — this operative mantra at the re-establishment of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire] is recited by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. '<s>Vihava</s>' means distinguished offerings; the fruit indicated by <s>varcas</s> (brilliance/radiance) in those [offerings] is mine — by this mark, the fruit would belong to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> who utters the mantra — if so [it is argued], that is not correct. By the <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle-voice) <s>śruti</s> in '<s>darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta</s>' (one who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>), it is understood that the fruit of the principal along with its accessories goes to the sacrificer.
(In the fifteenth [adhikaraṇa], on the rite-related fruit in instrument-mantras being a property of the officiating priest, the sūtra is:)

children.text: karmārthaṃ tu phalaṃ teṣāṃ svāminaṃ pratyarthavattvāt / Jaim_3,8.28 /
children.translated_text: But the fruit of those [mantras] pertains to the rite; it [accrues] to the owner [i.e., the sacrificer], because [the mantra] has a purpose [for the rite]. / Jaim_3,8.28 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.21
He composes the fifteenth adhikaraṇa —
'May I not be scorched (mā mā saṃtāptam)' — to which owner does this [mantra apply]? As before [to the sacrificer]?
But [it applies] to the Adhvaryu, because of the utility of [the Adhvaryu's well-being for] the owner's rite. // MJaiNy_3,8.21 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayorāghārahomārthamājyapūrṇau strukstruvau gṛhītvā nābhisamīpe hastena dhārayate |
tatrāyaṃ karaṇamantro 'dhvaryuṇā paṭhyate - 'agnāviṣṇū mā vāmavakramivaṃ vijihāthāṃ mā mā saṃtāptaṃ lokaṃ me lokakṛtau kuṇutam' iti |
'bho strukstruvarūpāvagnāviṣṇū yuvāṃ nābhideśe dhārayannahamadhvaryurmā vāmavakramiṣaṃ yuvayoratikramaṃ na kṛtavānasmi |
yuvāṃ ca matto viyuktau mā bhavatam |
tato māṃ dehadhāriṇaṃ mā saṃtāptaṃ mama dehe saṃtāpaṃ jvarādirūpaṃ mā kurutam |
sthānakṛtau yuvāmāghārahomāya sthānaṃ kurutam' ityarthaḥ |
tatra pūrvoktavarconyāyena saṃtāpābhāvo 'pi yajamānasyaiva, na tvadhvaryoḥ- iti cet |
children.translated_text: Therein, by the principle of the splendor (varcas) stated previously, the absence of scorching too belongs to the sacrificer alone, not to the Adhvaryu — if so argued,
that is not correct.
When the Adhvaryu is unscorched, the rite of the owner (sacrificer) is completed without obstacle.

children.text: tasmāt - adhvayurgato 'pi saṃtāpābhāvo yajamānasyaiva phalam - iti nātra macchabdasyopacāraḥ || MJaiNyC_3,8.21 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — even though the absence of scorching pertains to the Adhvaryu, the fruit belongs to the sacrificer alone — hence there is no figurative usage (upacāra) of the first-person pronoun ('me') here. || MJaiNyC_3,8.21 ||

In the Darśapūrṇamāsa [sacrifices], having grasped the ladles (sruk and sruva) filled with clarified butter for the purpose of the Āghāra (sprinkling) offering, [the Adhvaryu] holds them with his hand near the navel. There the Adhvaryu recites this instrument-mantra: 'agnāviṣṇū mā vām avakramivaṃ vijihāthāṃ mā mā saṃtāptaṃ lokaṃ me lokakṛtau kuṇutam' (O Agni and Viṣṇu, may I not transgress you, may you not be separated from me, may you not scorch me, you who create [my] world, create [my] world). The meaning is: 'O Agni and Viṣṇu, who are in the form of the ladles, I the Adhvaryu, holding you at the navel region, have not transgressed you — I have committed no offense against you. And may you two not be separated from me. Therefore, do not scorch me who am embodied — do not cause burning in the form of fever and the like in my body. You who create a place — create a place for the Āghāra offering.'
(In the sixteenth [adhikaraṇa], on the dual-applicability of [the mantra] 'bhadram' (may it be auspicious), the sūtra is:)
And because of the designation (vyapadeśa). / Jaim_3,8.29 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.22
He composes the sixteenth adhikaraṇa —
'Bhadraṃ tan nau saha' (may that auspiciousness be ours together) — to which owner does this [mantra] apply?
Because of the dual number (dvitva) heard, it [applies] to both — the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer. // MJaiNy_3,8.22 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome havirdhānamaṇḍape somābhiṣavādhārayoḥ phalakayoradhastāccatasṛṣvāgneyyādividikṣu catvāra uparavanāmakā gartā aratnimātrakhātā adhobhāge parasparaṃ militā ūrdhvabhāge parasparaṃ prādeśamātravyavahitā vartante |
teṣvekasminnuparave yajamāno dakṣiṇahastaṃ prasārayati, tathaivādhvaryuranyasminsvahastaṃ prasāryādhastādyajamānahastaṃ gṛhṇāti |
tadā yajamānaḥ 'kimatra' ityanena mantreṇa phalaṃ pṛcchati |
adhvaryuśca 'bhadram-' ityanena mantreṇottaraṃ brūte |
tato yajamānaḥ 'tannau saha - ' ityanena mantreṇa tatphalaṃ svakīyatvena svī karoti |

children.translated_text: Therefore — that [fruit] belongs to the sacrificer alone —
if so argued,
that is not correct.

children.text: 'nau' ityanena dvivacanena, 'saha' ityanena cobhayagāmitayaiva svīkārāt || MJaiNyC_3,8.22 ||
children.translated_text: Because by the dual pronoun 'nau' (of us two) and by the word 'saha' (together), the appropriation itself is made as belonging to both [the sacrificer and the Adhvaryu together]. || MJaiNyC_3,8.22 ||

In the Jyotiṣṭoma, in the Havirdhāna pavilion, beneath the two boards for pressing the Soma (abhiṣava), there are four pits called 'uparava' in the four intermediate directions beginning with the southeastern, dug to the depth of a forearm, meeting each other at the bottom and separated from each other by a span at the top. In one of these pits (uparava), the sacrificer extends his right hand; similarly, the Adhvaryu, extending his own hand in another [pit], grasps the hand of the sacrificer from below. Then the sacrificer, with the mantra 'kim atra' (what is here?), asks about the fruit. And the Adhvaryu, with the mantra 'bhadram' (auspiciousness), gives the reply. Then the sacrificer, with the mantra 'tan nau saha' (may that be ours together), appropriates that fruit as belonging to himself.
(In the seventeenth [adhikaraṇa], on whether substance-consecrations (dravyasaṃskāra) serve all rites [including accessories and principal], sūtras 30–31)
The substance-consecration [applies] to all rites, because there is no distinction in the context. / Jaim_3,8.30 /
But by the specific instruction, in the modified rite (vikṛti), that which is novel (apūrva) has no entitlement. / Jaim_3,8.31 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.23-24
He composes the seventeenth adhikaraṇa —
The properties [of consecration] situated in the archetype (prakṛti) — do they extend to the modified rite (vikṛti) through transference (atideśa)
in their entirety, or only specifically? The former, because the specific [application] cannot be determined. // MJaiNy_3,8.23 //
Only the properties that produce the [same] function in the archetype would [apply] in the modified rite, not others;

children.text: yūpāvaṭāstṛtiḥ kārya na hi prākṛtabarhiṣaḥ // MJaiNy_3,8.24 //
children.translated_text: the spreading with the sacrificial-post-pit (yūpāvaṭa) grass is to be performed, but not with the archetypal sacred grass (barhis). // MJaiNy_3,8.24 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayorvedidharmā barhirrdhamāśca havirāsādanādayo 'ṅgapradhānārthā iti pūrvatra nirṇītam |
te ca dharmā vikṛtāvatiddiśyamānā niyāmakābhāvātsarve 'pyatidiśyantām- iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- kāryamatra niyāmakam |
prakṛtau hi havirāsādanaṃ vedikāryam |
tacca vikṛtāvapi prāpyamāṇaṃ svasiddhayekhananādīnvedidharmānprāpayati |

children.translated_text: But the function of spreading the sacrificial-post-pit (yūpāvaṭa) does not exist in the archetype,
because there is no sacrificial-post-pit in the Darśapūrṇamāsa [sacrifices].

children.text: tarcca''staraṇakārye vikṛtau vidhīyamānamapyaprākṛtakāryatayā prākṛtāllaṃvanādīnvarhiḥ saṃskārānna prāpayanti |
children.translated_text: And that [spreading function], even though enjoined in the modified rite as a function of the sacrificial-post-pit, — since it is not an archetypal function — does not bring about the sacred-grass consecrations from the archetype, such as the cutting and the like.

children.text: tasmātprakṛtigatāḥ kāryakṛddharmā eva vikṛtau prāpyante || MJaiNyC_3,8.23-24 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, only the function-producing properties from the archetype are obtained in the modified rite. || MJaiNyC_3,8.23-24 ||

It was previously determined that the properties of the altar (vedī) and the properties of the sacred grass (barhis) — such as the placing of oblations (havirāsādana) and the like — serve both the accessories and the principal in the Darśapūrṇamāsa [sacrifices]. And when those properties are transferred to the modified rite, since there is no restrictive factor, let all of them be transferred — having arrived at this position, we say: The function (kārya) is the restrictive factor here. For in the archetype, the placing of the oblation is a function of the altar. And that [function], when obtained in the modified rite too, brings about the altar-properties such as digging and the like for its own accomplishment.
(In the eighteenth [adhikaraṇa], on the purifying-strainer (pavitra) being made from the eating-grass (paribhojanīya-barhis), the sūtra is:)

children.text: virodhe ca śrutiviśeṣād avyaktaḥ śeṣe / Jaim_3,8.32 /
children.translated_text: And in the case of conflict, because of the specific scriptural statement, [the rule] is unexpressed for the remainder. / Jaim_3,8.32 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.25
He composes the eighteenth adhikaraṇa —
Is that sacred grass (barhis) for the purpose of the purifying-strainer (pavitra), or not? The first [view], because of its possibility;

children.text: saṃskṛtaṃ staraṇe kṣīṇaṃ pavitraṃ tvanyato bhavet // MJaiNy_3,8.25 //
children.translated_text: but the consecrated [grass] is exhausted in the spreading, so the strainer should be made from another [grass]. // MJaiNy_3,8.25 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayorāmananti- 'samāvapracchinnāgnau darmau prādeśamātrau pavitre karoti' iti |
tatra- yadetadvedistaraṇārtha lavanasaṃskṛtaṃ barhiḥ, tena pavitrasaṃbhavādāstaraṇavatpavitramapi barhipaḥ kāryam - iti cet |

children.translated_text: that is not correct.

children.text: āstaraṇa eva saṃskṛtasya sarvasya barhiṣa upakṣīṇatvāt |
children.translated_text: Because all the consecrated sacred grass is exhausted in the spreading alone.

children.text: na hi 'vediṃ stṛṇāti' iti vihitasya staraṇasyākasmādbarhirekadeśe saṃkoco yuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: For it is not appropriate to suddenly restrict to one portion of the sacred grass the spreading enjoined by 'vediṃ stṛṇāti' (he spreads the altar).

children.text: tasmāt- yathā yūpāvaṭamasaṃskṛtena barhiṣā stṛṇāti, tathā pavitraniṣpattirapi śāstrīyalavanādisaṃskārarahitaiḥ paribhojanīyanāmakairdarbheḥ saṃpādanīyā || MJaiNyC_3,8.25 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — just as one spreads the sacrificial-post-pit with unconsecrated sacred grass, similarly the production of the purifying-strainer too should be accomplished with darbha grasses called 'paribhojanīya' (eating-grasses), which lack the scriptural consecrations of cutting and the like. || MJaiNyC_3,8.25 ||

In the Darśapūrṇamāsa [sacrifices], it is recorded: 'samāvapracchinnāgnau darmau prādeśamātrau pavitre karoti' (when the fire that had been cut off is re-established, he makes two darbha grass blades, each a span in length, into a purifying-strainer). Therein — since the sacred grass that has been consecrated by cutting for the purpose of altar-spreading can also produce the strainer, the strainer too should be made from the sacred grass, just like the spreading — if so argued,
(In the nineteenth [adhikaraṇa], on the depositing (nidhāna) of the archetypal puroḍāśa and the like, the sūtra is:)
But the removal of a portion [is made from the existing substance], because of the connection with what is present. / Jaim_3,8.33 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.26-27
He composes the nineteenth adhikaraṇa —
A fragment (śakala) of the puroḍāśa is to be deposited in the Aindravāyava vessel;
should a new puroḍāśa [be made], or the one from the pressing (savanīya)? // MJaiNy_3,8.26 //
Since the completed [puroḍāśa] serves the purpose of sacrifice, prepare a new one and perform that rite;
with the pressing-puroḍāśa, since [its fragment] is to be consecrated, [the rite is to be performed] by the second [alternative, i.e., using the existing one]. // MJaiNy_3,8.27 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate - 'puroḍāśaśakalamaindravāyavasya pātre nidadhāti' iti |
tatra- stravanīyapuroḍāśasya śakalaṃ yadyapi niṣpannam, tathāpi tasya yajamārthatvena saṃskṛtabarhirbadupakṣayānnūtanaṃ kaṃcitpuroḍāśaṃ saṃpādya tadīyaśaphalasyaindravāyavapātraprakṣepakriyā kartavyā - iti cet |
maivam |
savanīyapuroḍāśaśakalenaitannidhānaṃ kartavyam |
kutaḥ |
saṃskāryatvāt |
'śakalaṃ nidadhāti' iti dvitīyayā saṃskāryatvaṃ gamyate |

children.translated_text: For the consecration is in the form of the reception (pratipatti) of what is desired and prescribed.
And here, not the entire [puroḍāśa] serves the purpose of sacrifice,
because a portion of the puroḍāśa has been set aside as the remainder of the portion taken.

children.text: yathātra pūrvasiddhapuroḍāśaśakalam, tathā'dhānā āścinapātre' 'payasyāṃ maitrāvaruṇapātre' ityatrāpi pūrvaśeṣasyaiva prakṣepaḥ || MJaiNyC_3,8.26-27 ||
children.translated_text: Just as the fragment of the previously completed puroḍāśa [is used] here, so too in 'ādhānā āścinipātre' (in the vessel of the Āścini [cup-drawing] of the Ādhāna) and 'payasyāṃ maitrāvaruṇapātre' (in the Maitrāvaruṇa vessel in the milk [rite]), the casting is of the previously remaining [substance] itself. || MJaiNyC_3,8.26-27 ||

In the Jyotiṣṭoma, it is heard: 'puroḍāśaśakalam aindravāyavasya pātre nidadhāti' (he deposits a fragment of the puroḍāśa in the vessel of the Aindravāyava [cup]). Therein — although a fragment of the pressing-puroḍāśa (savanīya-puroḍāśa) has been produced, since it has been consecrated for the purpose of sacrifice with consecrated sacred grass and the like [which are now] exhausted, one should prepare some new puroḍāśa and the rite of casting its fragment into the Aindravāyava vessel should be performed — if so argued, that is not correct. This depositing should be done with the fragment of the pressing-puroḍāśa itself. Why? Because [the fragment] is to be consecrated (saṃskārya). By the accusative case in 'śakalaṃ nidadhāti' (he deposits the fragment), the status of being the object of consecration is understood.
(In the twentieth [adhikaraṇa], on the property of low-voiced performance (upāṃśutva) of the Tāmya-iṣṭi cakes belonging to the principal [rite], sūtras 34–35)
In the modified rite (vikṛti), the remainder serves all purposes, because of [the vikṛti's] archetypal nature. / Jaim_3,8.34 /
Or [it serves] the principal only, because [the property] is not enjoined for the accessory. / Jaim_3,8.35 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.28-29
He composes the twentieth adhikaraṇa —
Optional (kāmya) [rites] are to be performed in a low voice (upāṃśu); does this [apply] to both the accessory and the principal,

children.text: pradhāna eva vā nātra viśeṣoktirato dvayoḥ // MJaiNy_3,8.28 //
children.translated_text: or to the principal only? There is no specific statement here, so [it should apply] to both. // MJaiNy_3,8.28 //
Since only the principal [rites] are optional (kāmya), the incitement (paricodanā) pertains to them alone;
since the accessories do not have that [optional] character, the low-voiced nature pertains to the principal [rite]. // MJaiNy_3,8.29 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate - 'yajñātharvaṇaṃ vai kāmyā iṣṭayaḥ, tā upāṃśu ṣaṣṭavyāḥ' iti |
atharvavedoktakarmavadyajñeṣu kāmyā iṣṭayo gomyāḥ |
tasmāttāsāmupāṃśutvaṃ yuktamityarthaḥ |
yathā vedidharmāṇāṃ barhirrdhamāṇāṃ cāṅgapradhānayoḥ samāno vidhiḥ, tathopāṃśutvasyāpi |
nahyatra kaścidviśeṣa āmnātaḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
kāmyatvasyaivātra viśeṣaniyāmekatvāt |

children.translated_text: But the accessories do not have the character of being optional.
Because those [accessories], which bring about the fullness (pauṣkalya) of the instrument, have no direct connection with the fruit.
Therefore — the low-voiced performance [applies] only to the principal [rite], which is the direct means to the fruit.
But in the accessories, the pitch-mode (dhvani-viśeṣa) follows the respective Veda [to which they belong]. || MJaiNyC_3,8.28-29 ||

It is recorded: 'yajñātharvaṇaṃ vai kāmyā iṣṭayaḥ, tā upāṃśu yaṣṭavyāḥ' (the optional rites are verily like the Atharvavedic rites; they should be performed in a low voice). Like the rites taught in the Atharvaveda, the optional rites (kāmya iṣṭi) in sacrifices are to be concealed. Therefore their low-voiced performance is appropriate — this is the meaning. Just as the properties of the altar and the properties of the sacred grass are common to both the accessories and the principal, so too should the low-voiced performance be. For no distinction is recorded here — if so argued, that is not correct. Because the character of being optional (kāmyatva) itself is the specific restrictive factor here.
(In the twenty-first [adhikaraṇa], on the fresh-butter (navanīta) clarified butter of the Śyena accessories, sūtras 36–38)
Because of the non-distinction of proximity, when [the normal clarified butter] is impossible, [the fresh-butter quality applies] to the accessories thereof. / Jaim_3,8.36 /
If [it be argued that] even in the Ādhāna [rite] it is the same — / Jaim_3,8.37 /
No, because [the Ādhāna] is not the context [of the Śyena], and because the accessory does not have that [Śyena] as its cause. / Jaim_3,8.38 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.30-31
He composes the twenty-first adhikaraṇa —

children.text: navanītaṃ śyena ājyaṃ mukhye 'ṅge vāstu mukhyagam /
children.translated_text: In the Śyena [sacrifice], the fresh-butter (navanīta) clarified butter — does [it apply] to the principal [rite], or to the accessory? To the principal;
the clarified butter [is] to be enjoined [as] not previously obtained, [being] fresh butter kept in a leather bag. // MJaiNy_3,8.30 //
The principal [Śyena] is a modification (vikāra) of the Soma [sacrifice]; in the accessory, the clarified butter is obtained by the injunctive force (codaka);
by restating the leather-bag storage, the quality of fresh-butter is the [subject of the] injunction. // MJaiNy_3,8.31 //

children.text: dṛtau ciraṃ saṃgṛhītaṃ navanītaṃ yasyā'jyasya prakṛtidravyaṃ tadetadīdṛśamājyaṃ mānāntareṇa pūrvamaprāptatvātpradhānakarmaṇi vidheyam- iti cet |
children.translated_text: The clarified butter whose raw material is fresh butter stored for a long time in a leather bag — this particular kind of clarified butter, not previously obtained by any other means of knowledge, should be enjoined for the principal rite — if so argued,
that is not correct.
Because the principal Śyena, being a modification of the Soma sacrifice, has no requirement for clarified butter.

children.text: aṅgeṣviṣṭiviśeṣeṣu codakaprāptasyā'jyasya prakṛtidravyatvena yathoktanavanītaguṇo vidhīyate || MJaiNyC_3,8.30-31 ||
children.translated_text: In the accessories, which are specific subsidiary offerings (iṣṭi), the quality of fresh butter as stated is enjoined for the clarified butter that is obtained through the injunctive force as the raw material. || MJaiNyC_3,8.30-31 ||
In the Śyena [sacrifice], it is heard: 'dṛtinavanītam ājyaṃ bhavati' (the clarified butter is [made from] fresh butter kept in a leather bag).
(In the twenty-second [adhikaraṇa], on the fresh-butter clarified butter [applying to] all Śyena accessories, sūtras 39–41)
Or [it applies] only to those at the time [of the pressing], because of the observation of the mark (liṅga). / Jaim_3,8.39 /
Or to all, because there is no distinction. / Jaim_3,8.40 /
The observation of the mark [occurs] in what is stated by the principle (nyāya). / Jaim_3,8.41 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.32
He composes the twenty-second adhikaraṇa —
Is the [fresh-butter] quality enjoined [only] in the accessories occurring at the time of the pressing (sutyā), or in all?
The first, because [the statement] is specific to the accessories; by the sentence, it extends to all accessories. // MJaiNy_3,8.32 //

children.text:
yo 'yaṃ śyenasyāṅgeṣu dṛtinavanītatvaguṇo vihitaḥ so 'yaṃ sutyākālīneṣveva savanīyapaśutatpuroḍāśarūpeṣvaṅgeṣu, na tu kālāntaravartidīkṣaṇīyādyaṅgeṣu |
vimato guṇaḥ sutyākālīnāṅgamātragaḥ, śyenavaiśeṣikatvāt, paśusāhityavat |
yathā 'saha paśūnālabhate' iti vihitaṃ paśusāhityaṃ śyena eva viśeṣatvenocyamānaṃ sutyākālīneṣveva savanīyapaśuṣvavasthitam, tathā - navanītamapi- iti prāpte -
children.translated_text: Just as the simultaneity of the animals enjoined by 'saha paśūn ālabhate' (he seizes the animals simultaneously), being stated specifically in the Śyena, pertains only to the pressing-time animals (savanīya-paśu), similarly the fresh-butter [quality] — having arrived at this position,

we say: By the sentence 'yad ājyaṃ tad dṛtinavanītam' (whatever clarified butter there is, that is [made from] fresh butter kept in a leather bag), which conveys that it pertains to the clarified butter of all accessories, the inference [that it is limited] is overridden by the [broader] statement.
Therefore — that fresh-butter [quality applies] in all the accessories. || MJaiNyC_3,8.32 ||

This quality of fresh-butter (dṛtinavanītatva) enjoined in the accessories of the Śyena — it [applies] only to the accessories occurring at the time of the pressing, namely the pressing-animal-sacrifice (savanīya-paśu) and its puroḍāśa and the like, not to the accessories of other times such as the Dīkṣaṇīya and the like. The quality in question pertains only to the accessories occurring at the pressing-time, because it is specific to the Śyena, like the simultaneity of the animals (paśusāhitya).
(In the twenty-third [adhikaraṇa], on the meat-nature of the pressing [offerings], sūtras 42–44)
But the flesh [should apply] to the <s>Savanīya</s> [offerings], because of the non-distinction of the injunction. / Jaim_3,8.42 /
If it be said that the apportioning, in the absence of proximity, is not justified — / Jaim_3,8.43 /
It would be [justified], from the mark of the archetype, like the <s>Vairāja</s> [<s>Sāman</s>]. / Jaim_3,8.44 /
START MJaiNy 3,8.33-34
He composes the twenty-third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In the <s>Śākyāyana</s> [sacrifice], the <s>puroḍāśas</s> (cakes) are '<s>tarasā</s>' (quick/raw) — does the flesh-nature [apply] everywhere,

children.text: sarvatra savanīye vā sarvatra navanītavat // MJaiNy_3,8.33 //
children.translated_text: or only to the <s>Savanīya</s> [offerings]? Everywhere, like butter. // MJaiNy_3,8.33 //
'<s>Tarasāḥ</s>' and '<s>savanīyāḥ</s>' — their proximity is heard;
the flesh-nature of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> is therefore restricted to those [<s>Savanīyas</s>] alone. // MJaiNy_3,8.34 //

children.text:
ṣaṭtriṃśatsu saṃvatsareṣvanuṣṭheyaṃ śākyāyanam |
tatra śrūyate - saṃsthito 'hani gṛhapatirmṛgayāṃ yāti, sa yānmṛgānhanti, teṣāṃ tarasāḥ savamīyāḥ puroḍāśā bhavanti' iti |
tatra- yathā navanītaṃ sarveṣvaṅgeṣu niviṣṭam, tathā māṃsatvamapi sarveṣu puroḍāśeṣu niviśate - iti cet |
maivam |
tadā hi 'ye puroḍāśāste tarasāḥ' iti vacanavyaktau vyavahitānvayaḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: For then, in the rendering of the statement 'those <s>puroḍāśas</s> which are <s>tarasā</s>,' there would be a discontinuous syntactic connection.
Because the word <s>savanīya</s> intervenes between the words <s>tarasā</s> and <s>puroḍāśa</s>.

children.text: iha tu 'tarasāḥ savanīyāḥ' ityanayoḥ saṃnidhiḥ śrūyate |
children.translated_text: But here, the proximity of '<s>tarasāḥ</s>' and '<s>savanīyāḥ</s>' is [directly] heard.

children.text: tathā sati 'ye savanīyāste tarasāḥ' ityanena saṃnidhyanugṛhītena vākyena māṃsatvaṃ savanīyapuroḍāśeṣveva niyamyate || MJaiNyC_3,8.33-34 ||
children.translated_text: This being so, by the sentence supported by this proximity — 'those that are <s>savanīya</s>, those are <s>tarasā</s>' — the flesh-nature is restricted to the <s>Savanīya puroḍāśas</s> alone. || MJaiNyC_3,8.33-34 ||

The <s>Śākyāyana</s> [sacrifice] is to be performed over thirty-six years. Therein it is heard: '<s>saṃsthito 'hani gṛhapatir mṛgayāṃ yāti, sa yān mṛgān hanti, teṣāṃ tarasāḥ savanīyāḥ puroḍāśā bhavanti</s>' (on the day of the concluding rite, the householder goes hunting; the animals he kills — their [flesh makes] the quick <s>Savanīya puroḍāśas</s>). Therein — just as butter pervades all accessories, so too the flesh-nature should pervade all <s>puroḍāśas</s> — if so it is argued, that is not correct.
Thus ends the eighth <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the illustrious <s>Mādhavīya Jaiminīya-Nyāyamālā-Vistara</s>.
And this third <s>adhyāya</s> is concluded.
Now begins the first <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s>.
START MJaiNy 4,1.1
When the subsidiary-principal relationship is established, what is the object of employment and what is the employing agent?
Since this expectation arises, he speaks [the fourth <s>adhyāya</s>] as the answer to the fourth [inquiry]. // MJaiNy_4,1.1 //

children.text: anena tṛtīya- caturthayoradhyāyayoḥ pūrvottarabhāva upapāditaḥ || MJaiNyC_4,1.1 ||
children.translated_text: By this, the sequential relationship between the third and fourth <s>adhyāyas</s> is established. || MJaiNyC_4,1.1 ||
(In the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the formal statement of purpose, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
Now, therefore, [there should be] an inquiry into what serves the purpose of the sacrifice (<s>kratvārtha</s>) and what serves the purpose of the person (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). / Jaim_4,1.1 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.2-3
He composes the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the first <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> —

children.text: cintā na kāryā kāryā vā kratvarthapuruṣārthayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Should there be an inquiry into <s>kratvārtha</s> (sacrifice-purpose) and <s>puruṣārtha</s> (person-purpose), or not?
[If] fruitless, it should not be undertaken; [but since it is] productive, let this [inquiry] be conducted. // MJaiNy_4,1.2 //
Sometimes through this very inquiry, sometimes by the force of the fruit-injunction,
sometimes directly — in this <s>adhyāya</s>, the productive application is stated in many ways. // MJaiNy_4,1.3 //

children.text: 'kratvartho 'yam, puruṣārtho 'yam' iti vivekasya prayojanaṃ kimapi na paśyāmaḥ |
tasmāt- kākadantavicāravadayaṃ vicāra upekṣaṇīyaḥ- iti cet |
children.translated_text: Therefore — this inquiry should be disregarded, like the inquiry into the teeth of a crow — if so it is argued,
that is not correct.
Because through this inquiry, the productive application [of ritual elements] can be ascertained.

children.text: sākṣādvā paramparayā vā prayuktinirṇayopayuktaṃ sarvamiha cintanīyam || MJaiNyC_4,1.2-3 ||
children.translated_text: Everything that is useful for determining the productive application — whether directly or indirectly — is to be investigated here. || MJaiNyC_4,1.2-3 ||
We do not perceive any purpose in the distinction 'this serves the sacrifice, this serves the person.'
(In the second [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the definition of <s>kratvārtha</s> and <s>puruṣārtha</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: yasmin prītiḥ puruṣasya tasya lipsārthalakṣaṇāvibhaktatvāt / Jaim_4,1.2 /
children.translated_text: That in which the person takes pleasure — the defining characteristic of [<s>puruṣārtha</s>] is the desire for that purpose, because of the indivisibility [of the two]. / Jaim_4,1.2 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.4
He composes the first topic (<s>varṇaka</s>) of the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is there a defining characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) of <s>kratvārtha</s> and the like, or is there not? There is not, because of the impossibility of determination;
that which is for the sacrifice — that is <s>kratvārtha</s> — this is its determination. // MJaiNy_4,1.4 //

children.text:
'kratāvanuṣṭheyaḥ kratvarthaḥ' ityukte godohanādāvativyāptiḥ |
'puruṣeṇārthyamānaḥ puruṣārthaḥ' ityukte prayājādīnāmapyanuṣṭheyatayā puruṣeṇārthyamānatvādativyāptiḥ |
tasmāt- tayoradruṣṭaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ durnirūpama- iti cet |
maivam |
ṛtusvarūpapauṣkalyāyaiva yo vidhīyate sa kratvarthaḥ |
prayājādayastādṛśāḥ |
nahi prayājādimiḥ puruṣasya kaścitprītiviśeṣa utpadyate, yenaite puruṣārthā bhaveyuḥ |
darśapūrṇamāsakratustu taiḥ prayājādibhiḥ phalajananasāmarthyalakṣaṇaṃ pauṣkalyaṃ prāpnoti |
tasmāt- te kratvarthāḥ |
puruṣaprītaye vidhīyamānaḥ puruṣārthaḥ |
darśapūrṇamāsādayo godohanādayaśca tādṛśāḥ |
na hi darśapūrṇamāsābhyā kasyacitkratoḥ pauṣkasyaṃ bhavati |

children.translated_text: Because only three are sacrifices [of that kind].
Nor is cow-milking <s>kratvārtha</s>.
Because even without it, the completeness of the sacrifice is achieved through the cup (<s>camasa</s>).
Therefore — the defining characteristic of both is well-determined. || MJaiNyC_4,1.4 ||

If <s>kratvārtha</s> is defined as 'that which is to be performed in the sacrifice,' there is over-extension to cow-milking and the like. If <s>puruṣārtha</s> is defined as 'that which is desired by the person,' there is over-extension, since the <s>prayājas</s> and the like, being objects of desire by the person insofar as they must be performed, [would also qualify]. Therefore — the unseen defining characteristic of both is impossible to determine — if so it is argued, that is not correct. That which is enjoined solely for the completeness of the sacrifice's own nature is <s>kratvārtha</s>. The <s>prayājas</s> and the like are of this kind. For no particular pleasure arises in the person from the <s>prayājas</s> and the like, such that they would be <s>puruṣārtha</s>. But the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> sacrifice, through those <s>prayājas</s> and the like, attains the completeness characterized by the capacity to generate fruit. Therefore, they are <s>kratvārtha</s>. That which is enjoined for the pleasure of the person is <s>puruṣārtha</s>. The <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the like, and cow-milking and the like, are of this kind. For the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> does not bring completeness to any [other] sacrifice.
START MJaiNy 4,1.5
He composes the second topic (<s>varṇaka</s>) —
Is the fruit (<s>phala</s>) to be enjoined, or not? The first [view]: because it is a component of the <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force), like the others;

children.text: na bhāvyāṃśo vidheyaḥ syādrāgāttatra pravartanāt // MJaiNy_4,1.5 //
children.translated_text: the component of the <s>bhāvanā</s> should not be enjoined, because the person's engagement with it arises from natural desire (<s>rāga</s>). // MJaiNy_4,1.5 //

children.text: 'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta' iti svargaḥ phalatvena śrūyate |
tatra-vimataṃ phalaṃ vidheyam, bhāvanāṃśatvāt, karaṇavat, itikartavyatāvacca - iti cet |
children.translated_text: Therein — the fruit is the object of doubt, it should be enjoined, because it is a component of the <s>bhāvanā</s>, like the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), and like the procedure (<s>itikartavyatā</s>) — if so it is argued,
that is not correct.
For injunction (<s>vidhāna</s>) is the impelling of one who has not [yet] engaged.

children.text: phalaṃ tu puruṣaḥ saundarya jāmansvayaṃ rāgādeva pravṛttaḥ- iti vyarthastatra vidhiḥ || MJaiNyC_4,1.5 ||
children.translated_text: But the person, due to the natural attractiveness [of the fruit], is already engaged toward the fruit through innate desire — so an injunction regarding it would be purposeless. || MJaiNyC_4,1.5 ||
In '<s>darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta</s>' (one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the new- and full-moon offerings), heaven is heard as the fruit.
START MJaiNy 4,1.6
He composes the third topic (<s>varṇaka</s>) —
Does cow-milking (<s>godohana</s>) serve both purposes or not? The first [view]: it serves both, because both aspects are apparent;

children.text: anyathāpi kratoḥ siddhiḥkevalaṃ puruṣāya tat // MJaiNy_4,1.6 //
children.translated_text: [but] even otherwise, the sacrifice is accomplished; [cow-milking] is solely for the person. // MJaiNy_4,1.6 //

children.text: tatra- godohanasya kratvarthatvaṃ puruṣārthatvaṃ ca, ityākāradvayamasti paśuphalajanamena puruṣaprītirbhāti, apāṃ praṇayanena kratupauṣkalyamapi bhāti- iti cet |
children.translated_text: Therein — cow-milking has both <s>kratvārtha</s>-nature and <s>puruṣārtha</s>-nature — two aspects are present: through the generation of the fruit of cattle, the person's pleasure is apparent; through the carrying of water, the completeness of the sacrifice is also apparent — if so it is argued,
that is not correct.
Even without cow-milking, [the sacrifice can] lack the [cattle-]fruit — this establishes <s>puruṣārtha</s>-nature.

children.text: kratustu tadabhāve 'pi camasena sidhyatīti na kratvarthatā || MJaiNyC_4,1.6 ||
children.translated_text: But the sacrifice is accomplished even without it, through the cup — so there is no <s>kratvārtha</s>-nature. || MJaiNyC_4,1.6 ||
In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> it is heard: '<s>camasenāpaḥ praṇayed godohanena paśukāmasya</s>' (one should carry water with the cup, [but] with cow-milking for one desiring cattle).
START MJaiNy 4,1.7
He composes the fourth topic (<s>varṇaka</s>) —
Is the acquisition of wealth (<s>dravyārjana</s>) <s>kratvārtha</s> (for the sacrifice) or <s>puruṣārtha</s> (for the person)? In the sacrifice, this —
because of the restriction [of means], it is <s>puruṣārtha</s>; [but if] seen [as] <s>kratvārtha</s>, the purpose would require it. // MJaiNy_4,1.7 //

children.text:
brāhmaṇasya dravyārjane pratigrahayājanādhyāpanānyeva niyatāni tatra tatra śrutāni, rājanyasya jayādikam, vaiśyasya kṛṣyādikam, śūdrasya sevādikam |
tacca yadetaddravyasaṃpādanaṃ tadetatkratvartham |
kutaḥ |
arjanopāyānāṃ niyatatvāt |
puruṣaprītestu yena kenāpi dravyeṇa siddhatvādarjanopāyaniyamastatra nirarthakaḥ |
kratau tu niyamāpūrva paramāpūrvāpayogīti sārthako niyamaḥ- iti prāpte |
brūmaḥ- dravyārjane rāgaḥ pravartako dṛṣṭa iti na vidhirapekṣyate |
phalaṃ ca kṣunnivṛttyādirūpaṃ dṛṣṭameva |
ata eva smaryate-
'ṣaṇṇāṃ tu karmaṇāmasya trīṇi karmāṇi jīvikā |
yājanādhyāpane caiva viśuddhācca pratigrahaḥ || ita |

children.translated_text: But if [wealth-acquisition] were <s>kratvārtha</s>, then due to the absence of livelihood, the sacrifice itself would not be accomplished.

When <s>puruṣārtha</s>-nature is [accepted], since the sacrifice, by virtue of producing pleasure pertaining to the next world — like food and the like that produce pleasure in this world — is included among <s>puruṣārthas</s>, the <s>kratvārtha</s>-nature is also incidentally accomplished.
And the restriction of means is explained by the intention to [avoid] transgressions in other means.
Therefore — the acquisition of wealth is <s>puruṣārtha</s>. || MJaiNyC_4,1.7 ||
