For the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, in the acquisition of wealth, only accepting gifts (<s>pratigraha</s>), performing sacrifices for others (<s>yājana</s>), and teaching (<s>adhyāpana</s>) are heard as restricted [means] in the respective [texts]; for the <s>Kṣatriya</s>, conquest and the like; for the <s>Vaiśya</s>, agriculture and the like; for the <s>Śūdra</s>, service and the like. And this acquisition of wealth is <s>kratvārtha</s>. Why? Because the means of acquisition are restricted. Since the person's pleasure can be accomplished by any means whatsoever, the restriction of the means of acquisition would be purposeless in that case. But in the sacrifice, the restriction is meaningful, as it produces an unprecedented <s>apūrva</s> (transcendental merit) — having arrived at this position, we say: In the acquisition of wealth, natural desire (<s>rāga</s>) is seen as the motivating force, so no injunction is needed. And the fruit — in the form of the alleviation of hunger and the like — is directly visible. Hence it is recorded in <s>Smṛti</s>: '<s>ṣaṇṇāṃ tu karmaṇām asya trīṇi karmāṇi jīvikā / yājanādhyāpane caiva viśuddhāc ca pratigrahaḥ</s>' (of his six duties, three are his livelihood: performing sacrifices [for others], teaching, and accepting gifts from the pure).
(In the third [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>puruṣārtha</s>-nature of the vows of <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 3-6:)

children.text: tadutsarge karmāṇi puruṣārthāya śāstrasyānatiśaṅkyatvān na ca dravyaṃ cikīrṣyate tenārthenābhisambandhāt kriyāyāṃ puruṣaśrutiḥ / Jaim_4,1.3 /
children.translated_text: In that general rule, the ritual acts are for the purpose of the person, since the scripture is not to be doubted; nor is [mere] material [substance] intended — because of the connection with the purpose [of the person]; the mention of the person is in [connection with] the action. / Jaim_4,1.3 /

children.text: aviśeṣāt tu śāstrasya yathāśruti phalāni syuḥ / Jaim_4,1.4 /
children.translated_text: But due to the non-distinction of scripture, the fruits should be as directly stated. / Jaim_4,1.4 /

children.text: api vā kāraṇāgrahaṇe tadartham arthasyānabhisaṃbandhāt / Jaim_4,1.5 /
children.translated_text: Or, when the cause is not apprehended, [the restriction] serves that purpose, because of the non-connection with the [sacrifice's] purpose. / Jaim_4,1.5 /
And similarly in worldly matters. / Jaim_4,1.6 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.8-9
He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'One should not look at the rising sun' — is this <s>kratvārtha</s>, or not? The first [view holds]:,
since the fruit should not be postulated [unnecessarily], what is [already] obtained in the sacrifice is being prohibited. // MJaiNy_4,1.8 //
When, through the expression '<s>vrata</s>' (vow), there is an exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>), the resolve not to look is the [prescribed practice] here;
it is not the same as a sacrifice-accessory — [it is] <s>puruṣārtha</s>, for the removal of sin. // MJaiNy_4,1.9 //

children.text:
anārabhya śrūyate- 'nekṣetodyantamādityaṃ nāstaṃ yantaṃ kadācana' iti |
atra nañpadamabhidhāvṛttyā pratiṣedhaṃ brūte, na tu paryudāsam |
pratiṣedhaśca prāptipūrvakaḥ |
prāptiśca vaidikasya nipedhasya vaidikī pratyāsannā |
tathā sati kratau yatrā'dityekṣaṇaṃ vihitam, tatrāyaṃ niṣedha udayāstamayoddeśena pravartate |
evaṃ ca sati phalaṃ na kalpanīyam |
paryudāsamāśritya puruṣārthatvāṅgīkāre 'dhikārasiddhaye phalaṃ kalpanīyaṃ syāt |
tasmāt- kratvartho niṣedhaḥ- iti prāpte-
brūmaḥ- 'tasya vratam' ityupaktamya 'nekṣetodyantamādityam' ityāmnātatvādanīkṣaṇarūpaṃ kiṃcidanuṣṭheyam |
tacca paryudāsatve satyavakalpate |
īkṣaṇasyābhāvaḥ pratiṣedhapakṣe nañarthaḥ |
paryudāsapakṣe tvīkṣaṇāditaraḥ saṃkalpo nañpadena lakṣyate |
sa ca saṃkalpo 'trānuṣṭheyavratatvena vidhīyate |
yadyapīkṣaṇāditare bahavo vyāpārā anuṣṭhānayogyāḥ santi, tathāpi kāyikavācikavyāpāraviśeṣasyāpratīyamānatvāt, mānasavyāpārasyāvarjanīyatvācca saṃkalpa eva pariśiṣyate |
saṃkalpanīyaścārthaḥ pratyāsattyā dhātvarthaniṣedhaḥ |
tathā sati'udyantam, astaṃ yantaṃ cā'dityaṃ nekṣiṣye' ityevaṃrūpaḥ saṃkalpo 'trānuṣṭheyatvena vidhīyate |
na ca tasya saṃkalpasya kratvaṅgatvam |
tadbodhakaśrutiliṅgādipramāṇābhāvāt |

children.translated_text: Nor is there an absence of valid means of knowledge for <s>puruṣārtha</s>-nature.

children.text: 'etāvatā hainasā mukto bhavati' ityanena vākyenekṣituḥ puruṣasya pratyavāyasaṃbandhamupanyasya tatpratyavāyanivāraṇaphalakasyānīkṣaṇasaṃkalpasya vidhānena puruṣārthatvāvagamāt |
children.translated_text: Because, by the sentence '<s>etāvatā hainasā mukto bhavati</s>' (by this much, one is freed from sin), the connection of sin with the person who looks is presented, and by the enjoining of the resolve not to look — which has the fruit of averting that sin — the <s>puruṣārtha</s>-nature is understood.
But if <s>kratvāṅga</s>-nature (sacrifice-accessory-nature) were intended, the opposing argument in the form of sacrifice-incompleteness would have to be presented.
Therefore — the resolve not to look and the other vows of <s>Prajāpati</s> are <s>puruṣārthas</s>. || MJaiNyC_4,1.8-9 ||

It is heard without a specific [ritual] context: '<s>nekṣetodyantam ādityaṃ nāstaṃ yantaṃ kadācana</s>' (one should never look at the rising sun nor at the setting one). Here, the negative particle (<s>nañ</s>) conveys a prohibition through its denotative function, not an exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>). And a prohibition presupposes a prior obtaining (<s>prāpti</s>). And the most proximate obtaining for a Vedic prohibition is a Vedic [injunction]. This being so, the prohibition operates with reference to the rising and setting [sun] precisely where the looking at the sun is enjoined in a sacrifice. In this case, no fruit need be postulated. If, by resorting to exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>), <s>puruṣārtha</s>-nature were accepted, then a fruit would have to be postulated to establish the qualified person (<s>adhikāra</s>). Therefore — the prohibition is <s>kratvārtha</s> — having arrived at this position, we say: Because it is recited after the introductory words '<s>tasya vratam</s>' (his vow), something in the form of non-looking is to be practiced. And that is possible only when there is exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>). In the case of prohibition, the meaning of the negative particle is the absence of looking. But in the case of exclusion, what is indicated by the negative particle is a resolve (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) that is other than looking. And that resolve is what is enjoined here as the vow to be practiced. Although there are many activities other than looking that could be practiced, since no specific bodily or verbal activity is apprehended, and since mental activity is inescapable, the resolve alone remains by elimination. And the object to be resolved upon, by proximity, is the negation of the action denoted by the verbal root. This being so, the resolve of the form 'I shall not look at the rising or setting sun' is what is enjoined here as something to be practiced. And that resolve is not a sacrifice-accessory (<s>kratvāṅga</s>). Because there is no valid means of knowledge — such as <s>śruti</s> or <s>liṅga</s> — that would indicate it as such.
(In the fourth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the restatement-nature (<s>anuvāda</s>) of the sacrificial implements (<s>yajñāyudha</s>), <s>sūtras</s> 7-10:)
The materials (<s>dravyas</s>), without distinction, would be given [to the priests], since [otherwise they would be] purposeless. / Jaim_4,1.7 /

children.text: svena tvarthena sambandho dravyāṇāṃ pṛthagarthatvāt tasmād yathāśruti syuḥ / Jaim_4,1.8 /
children.translated_text: But the materials have a connection with their own purpose, since [each] material has a separate purpose; therefore, they should be [assigned] as directly stated. / Jaim_4,1.8 /
And they are cited in the explanatory passages (<s>arthakathā</s>). / Jaim_4,1.9 /
And because of the observation of the mark. / Jaim_4,1.10 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.10-11
He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'Ten sacrificial implements (<s>yajñāyudha</s>)' — is this an injunction of their being <s>havis</s> (oblation material), or not?
The first [view]: since [the <s>puroḍāśa</s>-nature is] not [otherwise] obtained, in the <s>puroḍāśa</s> [context], combination or alternative [would apply]. // MJaiNy_4,1.10 //
Together with the origination-instruction, an alternative and the like are not appropriate;
'He digs with the <s>sphya</s>' (wooden sword) — since [its use] is already obtained, this is restated here as praise (<s>saṃstava</s>). // MJaiNy_4,1.11 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ- 'sphyaśca kapālāni ca-' ityādyupakramya 'etāni vai daśayajñāyudhāni' ityāmnātam |
tāni cātra haviṣṭvena vidhīyante |
kutaḥ |
mānāntarairaprāptatvenāpūrvārthatvāt |
yadi tatra puroḍāśo havirbhavat, tadā tena sahaiteṣāṃ samuccayo vikalpo vāstu- iti prāpte, |
brūmaḥ- 'āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaḥ' ityutpattiśiṣṭena puroḍāśena saha paścācchiṣṭānāmāyudhānāṃ vikalpaḥ samuccayo vā na saṃbhavati |
children.translated_text: we say: The optional alternation or cumulative application of the subsequently taught implements (<s>āyudhas</s>) with the <s>puroḍāśa</s> — which is taught as the oblation by the origination-injunction '<s>āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaḥ</s>' (an eight-potsherd [cake] for <s>Agni</s>) — is not possible.
The status of being implements (<s>āyudhatva</s>) means being means of accomplishing the sacrifice.

children.text: tacca 'sphyenoddhanti, kapāleṣu śrapayati' ityādiśāstrasiddhamevātrānūdya 'yajñāyudhāni saṃbharati' ityeṣa saṃbharaṇavidhiḥ stūyate |
children.translated_text: And that [instrumentality] — already established by injunctive texts such as '<s>sphyena uddhanti</s>' (he digs with the wooden sword), '<s>kapāleṣu śrapayati</s>' (he cooks on the potsherds) — is merely restated here, and the collection-injunction '<s>yajñāyudhāni saṃbharati</s>' (he collects the sacrificial implements) is praised.
Therefore, they do not have the status of oblations. || MJaiNyC_4,1.10-11 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, beginning with '<s>sphyaś ca kapālāni ca</s>' (the wooden sword and the potsherds) and so on, it is recorded: '<s>etāni vai daśa yajñāyudhāni</s>' (these are indeed the ten sacrificial implements). And these are being enjoined here as having the status of oblations (<s>havis</s>). Why? Because they are novel, not being obtained through other means of knowledge. If the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake) were the oblation there, then there would be either a cumulative application or an optional alternation of these [implements] with it — having arrived at this position,
(In the fifth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the singularity of the animal, <s>sūtras</s> 11–16:)
Therein, the singularity [of the animal] is not an accessory of the sacrifice, because the meaning is subordinate [to the substance]. / Jaim_4,1.11 /
And because both are heard in a single [statement]. / Jaim_4,1.12 /
If [it is argued that] it is understood [as an accessory]. / Jaim_4,1.13 /
What is not expressed by words has no authority — as before. / Jaim_4,1.14 /

children.text: śabdavat tūpalabhyate tadāgame hi taddṛśyate tasya jñānaṃ hi yathānyeṣām / Jaim_4,1.15 /
children.translated_text: But [the singularity] is grasped as if expressed by words, for it is seen when the [word] arrives; and its cognition is like that of others. / Jaim_4,1.15 /
And similarly, because of the observation of the mark. / Jaim_4,1.16 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.12-13
He composes the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In '<s>paśur ālabhya</s>' (having seized an animal), does the singularity of the animal have the status of an accessory of the sacrifice?

children.text: nāstyasti vā'dyaḥ svapade śrutyā paśvaṅgatāgateḥ // MJaiNy_4,1.12 //
children.translated_text: It does not; or it does — the first [alternative], because singularity comes to the animal through the <s>śruti</s> in its own word. // MJaiNy_4,1.12 //
First, by the suffix (<s>pratyaya</s>) expressing [number], in the nearest <s>kāraka</s> (grammatical case-relation),

children.text: yogaḥ kratau paśau ceti krame yāgāṅgatocitā // MJaiNy_4,1.13 //
children.translated_text: the connection is [first] with the sacrifice [or] with the animal — in [the proper] sequence, the accessory-status to the sacrifice is appropriate. // MJaiNy_4,1.13 //

children.text:
'agnīṣomīyaṃ paśumālabheta' ityatra paśorekatvaṃ yajanāṅgaṃ na bhavati |
tasya śrutyā paśusaṃbandhāvagamāt |
'paśum' ityetasminneva pade paśutadekatvayoḥ śravaṇātpadāntaranairapekṣyeṇa parasparasaṃbandho 'vagamyate |
yāgastu 'ālabheta' ityanena padāntareṇopāttaḥ |
tatra vākyena saṃbandhāvagatiḥ |
vākyācca śrutirbalīyasī |
tata ekatvasya yāgāṅgatvābhāvāddvābhyāṃ bahubhirvā yāgo 'nuṣṭhātuṃ śakyate- iti prāpte, brūmaḥ- 'paśum' iti padaṃ yadyapyekam, tathāpi prakṛtyā paśurmirdiṣṭaḥ |
pratyayena kārakatvam, ekatvaṃ ca, ityubhayaṃ nirdiṣṭam |
tata ekatvasyā'sannatare kārake prathamaṃ saṃbandho bhavati |
kārakatvaṃ nāma kriyāhetutvam |
tathā sati kārakadvārā kriyāyāmapi saṃbandhaḥ pratyayenaivāvagataḥ |
kriyāviśeṣaśca saṃnihitapadāntaropātto yāga iti yajanāṅgatvamekatvasya sidhyati |
children.translated_text: And the specific action — the sacrifice, which is expressed by the adjacent word — is such that the accessory-status of singularity to the sacrifice is established.

children.text: taccaikatvaṃ svayamamūrtatayā yāgakriyāṃ niṣpādayitumasamartha sattatra samarthe paśudravyaṃ paścādavacchinatti |
children.translated_text: And that singularity, being itself formless (<s>amūrta</s>), is incapable of accomplishing the sacrificial action; being so incapable, it subsequently delimits the animal substance, which is [itself] capable.

children.text: tata ekatvasya yāgāṅgatvānna dvābhyāṃ tribhirvā yāgasiddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, since singularity is an accessory of the sacrifice, the sacrifice is not accomplished with two or three [animals].

children.text: evam- 'anaḍvāhau yunakti' 'vasantāya kapiñjalānālabhate' ityatra dvitvabahutvayorvivakṣitatvaṃ draṣṭavyam || MJaiNyC_4,1.12-13 ||
children.translated_text: Similarly, in '<s>anaḍvāhau yunakti</s>' (he yokes two bulls) and '<s>vasantāya kapiñjalān ālabhate</s>' (he seizes francolin partridges for spring), the intended expression of duality and plurality respectively should be noted. || MJaiNyC_4,1.12-13 ||

In '<s>agnīṣomīyaṃ paśum ālabheta</s>' (one should seize an animal sacred to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>), the singularity of the animal is not an accessory of the sacrifice. Because the connection with the animal is understood from the <s>śruti</s> itself. Since both the animal-nature and its singularity are heard in this very word '<s>paśum</s>', the mutual connection [between animal and singularity] is understood independently of any other word. But the sacrifice is expressed by another word '<s>ālabheta</s>' (one should seize). There, the connection is understood through the sentence [as a whole]. And the <s>śruti</s> (direct word-meaning) is stronger than the sentence. Therefore, since singularity is not an accessory of the sacrifice, the sacrifice can be performed with two or many [animals] — having arrived at this position, we say: Although '<s>paśum</s>' is a single word, nevertheless the base (<s>prakṛti</s>) denotes the animal, and the suffix (<s>pratyaya</s>) denotes both the case-relation (<s>kārakatva</s>) and the singularity. Therefore, the singularity first connects with the nearer case-relation. And case-relation means being a cause of action. This being so, through the case-relation, the connection with the action is also understood by the very suffix.
(In the sixth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the intended expression of the grammatical gender of the animal, the <s>sūtra</s>:)
And the mark is similarly [intended]. / Jaim_4,1.17 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.14
He composes the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the masculine gender not intended to be expressed, or is it intended? — because of the uselessness of its expression;
the first [alternative]; but because of the dependence on [actual] performance, like number, the gender should be taken as intended. // MJaiNy_4,1.14 //

children.text:
'paśumālabheta' ityatra paśupade puṃliṅgamavivakṣitam |
kutaḥ |
śabdārthavicāre 'nuṣṭhānavicāre ca tadupayogādarśanāt |
aliṅge 'pi vṛkṣapadārthe puṃliṅgo vṛkṣaśabdaḥ prayujyate |
tathā puṃvyaktāvapi strīliṅgo makṣikāśabdaḥ prayuktaḥ |
tato na liṅgasya śabdārthatvena vivakṣāsti |
anuṣṭhānamapi puṃvyaktistrīvyaktyoḥ samānam |
ekatvāvacchinnapaśutve vaiṣamyābhāvāt |
tasmāt- avivakṣitaṃ liṅgam- iti prāpte,-
brūmaḥ- yathā paśutvajātiḥ, yathā vā -tadekatvam, vṛddhavyavahāre 'nvayavyatirekābhyāmananyathāsiddhābhyāṃ śabdārthaḥ, tathā liṅgasyāpi kutaḥ śabdārthatā na syāt |
vṛkṣamakṣikāśabdayostu na vayamarthataḥ sādhutāṃ brūmaḥ, kiṃtvabhiyuktaprayogamātrabalena sādhutvam |

children.translated_text: Nor is there equality in performance.
Because of the existence of a specific [difference] in a non-male animal.

children.text: 'vākta āpyāyatām' ityādibhirmantraistattadavayavānāmāpyāyamanakāle 'meḍhraṃ tu ādhyāyatām' iti mantreṇa tadavayavasyā'pyāyanaśravaṇāt |
children.translated_text: In the <s>mantras</s> '<s>vāk ta āpyāyatām</s>' (may your speech be nourished) and so on, at the time of nourishing the respective limbs, the hearing of the nourishment of that [specific] limb by the <s>mantra</s> '<s>meḍhraṃ tu āpyāyatām</s>' (may your penis be nourished) [shows that a male is required].
Therefore, like singularity, the masculine gender too is intended to be expressed. || MJaiNyC_4,1.14 ||

In '<s>paśum ālabheta</s>' (one should seize an animal), the masculine gender in the word '<s>paśu</s>' is not intended to be expressed. Why? Because its usefulness is not seen in either the analysis of word-meaning or the analysis of performance. Even in the case of the word '<s>vṛkṣa</s>' (tree), which is masculine, the referent is without gender. Likewise, in the case of the word '<s>makṣikā</s>' (bee), which is feminine, even a male individual [is denoted]. Therefore, the gender is not part of the word-meaning and is not intentionally expressed. Performance too is the same for male and female individuals — because there is no difference when [the animal] is delimited by singularity and animal-nature. Therefore, gender is not intended to be expressed — having arrived at this position, we say: Just as the genus 'animal-nature' (<s>paśutva-jāti</s>) and its singularity are the word-meaning — ascertained through agreement and difference (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) in the usage of the learned, which cannot be otherwise explained — why should gender not similarly be the word-meaning? As for the words '<s>vṛkṣa</s>' and '<s>makṣikā</s>', we do not claim their correctness on the basis of meaning, but only on the strength of the usage of the learned.
(In the seventh [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the unseen purpose of dependent [ritual elements], <s>sūtras</s> 18–20:)
In dependent [elements], without distinction, the state of being (<s>bhāva</s>) would be understood as the purpose. / Jaim_4,1.18 /

children.text: codanāyāṃ tv anārambho vibhaktatvān na hy anyena vidhīyate / Jaim_4,1.19 /
children.translated_text: But [that state is] not commenced in the injunction, because they are separately [enjoined]; for they are not enjoined by another [injunction]. / Jaim_4,1.19 /

children.text: syād vā dravyacikīrṣāyāṃ bhāvo 'rthe ca guṇabhūtatvāśrayād viguṇībhāvaḥ / Jaim_4,1.20 /
children.translated_text: Or perhaps, when the substance is desired to be accomplished, the state of being is subordinate in purpose; and from the deficiency of the support, [the whole] becomes deficient. / Jaim_4,1.20 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.15-16
He composes the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is [the substance] exhausted in the consecration for the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, or is it also useful for the unseen [result]?
Since the purpose is one, [being exhausted] in one rite is appropriate — therefore [it would be] exhausted. // MJaiNy_4,1.15 //
By the <s>mantra</s>, the consecration of the deity; by the casting [of the substance], the consecration of the material;
from the renunciation (<s>tyāga</s>), the unseen [merit] is produced, and that [unseen merit] accrues to the principal [sacrifice]. // MJaiNy_4,1.16 //

children.text:
yo 'yaṃ sviṣṭakṛdyāgaḥ so 'yamupayuktahaviḥsaṃskāraḥ- ityavivādam |
tatra saṃskārasya dṛṣṭaprayojanatvenāvaśyaṃbhāve sati tāvataivopakṣīṇaḥ sviṣṭakṛdyāgo nāpūrvasyopakaroti |
na hyekasminkarmaṇi prayojanadvayaṃ yuktam- iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- karmaṇa ekatve 'pyaṃśabhedātprayojanabhedo na virudhyate |
mantrapāṭhaḥ, dravyaprakṣepaḥ, devatoddeśena tyāgaśca, iti trayoṃ'śāḥ |
children.translated_text: The recitation of the <s>mantra</s>, the casting of the substance, and the renunciation dedicated to the deity — these are the three aspects.
Therein, by the renunciation, a subordinate unseen [merit] (<s>avāntarāpūrva</s>) is produced — which is useful for the ultimate unseen [result] (<s>paramāpūrva</s>).
Therefore, the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> serves both purposes.
Similarly, the final preliminary offering (<s>antya-prayāja</s>) and the animal <s>puroḍāśa</s> should also be cited as examples. || MJaiNyC_4,1.15-16 ||

This <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> sacrifice is a consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the oblation that has been used — this is undisputed. Now, since the consecration necessarily exists as having a visible purpose, the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> sacrifice, being exhausted by just that much, does not contribute to the unseen [merit]. For it is not appropriate that a single ritual action have two purposes — having arrived at this position, we say: Even though the action is one, since there are different aspects, the difference of purposes is not contradicted.
(In the eighth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the thesis of the inquiry into causal connection (<s>prayukti</s>), the <s>sūtra</s>:)
From the equality or inequality of purpose in substances and actions. / Jaim_4,1.21 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.17
He composes the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the accessory-nature the topic of inquiry in the subsequent text, or something else?
It is the accessory-nature, from the means of knowledge; but not that alone here — because the fruit called causal connection (<s>prayukti</s>) is discussed. // MJaiNy_4,1.17 //

children.text:
vakṣyamāṇeṣvadhikaraṇeṣu śeṣatvameva cintāviṣayaḥ |
yathā - atīteṣvadhikaraṇeṣu kratuśeṣo 'yam, puruṣaśeṣo 'yam, iti cintitam, tadvat |
kutaḥ |
uparitanagranthena tatra tatra parṇādīnāṃ śeṣatvavicārasya bhāsamānatvāt- iti cet |
children.translated_text: Because in the subsequent text, the inquiry into the accessory-nature of <s>Parṇa</s> [wood] and the like is apparent in each case — if so it is argued,
that is not correct.

children.text: śeṣatvasya yatprayuktirūpaṃ phalaṃ tadeva prādhānyena vicāryate |
children.translated_text: The fruit of the accessory-nature — which is the causal connection (<s>prayukti</s>) — that alone is primarily discussed.

children.text: śeṣatvaṃ tu tadupayogitveneti na tadvicāraḥ pradhānabhūtaḥ || MJaiNyC_4,1.17 ||
children.translated_text: The accessory-nature itself serves as an auxiliary to that [discussion], so the inquiry into accessory-nature is not the primary [topic]. || MJaiNyC_4,1.17 ||

In the <s>adhikaraṇas</s> to follow, the accessory-nature (<s>śeṣatva</s>) alone is the subject of inquiry. Just as in the past <s>adhikaraṇas</s>, it was inquired: 'this is an accessory of the sacrifice,' 'this is an accessory of the person' — similarly. Why?
(In the ninth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the causal role of <s>āmikṣā</s> (curd-whey), in the <s>Vājina</s> principle, <s>sūtras</s> 22–24:)
Since they are produced together, all would be equal. / Jaim_4,1.22 /
Or <s>āmikṣā</s> would be the principal, because of the production from the mixture of flavors. / Jaim_4,1.23 /
And because of the praise in the primary word. / Jaim_4,1.24 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.18-19
He composes the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Are both <s>āmikṣā</s> (curd-whey) and <s>vājina</s> (strengthening substance) the causal agents, since the bringing of curds [produces both]?
Or is the <s>āmikṣā</s> alone [the cause]? The capacity of both is equal, therefore [one might think both are]. // MJaiNy_4,1.18 //
The <s>āmikṣā</s> is just milk here — from the word [used for it], from the <s>mantra</s>, from the flavor;
the single [<s>āmikṣā</s>] is the causal agent by virtue of its primacy, and the <s>vājina</s> is a by-product. // MJaiNy_4,1.19 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate- 'tapte payasi dadhyānayati sā vaiśvadevyāmikṣā vājibhyo vājinam' iti |
tatra-payasi dadhiprakṣepādāmikṣādravyaṃ yathā niṣpadyate, tathā vājinadravyamapi' iti dadhyānayanasya janakatvasāmarthyamubhayadravyaviṣayaṃ tulyameva |
tasmāt- ubhayamapi prayojakam- iti prāpte,-
brūmaḥ- 'na dravyāntaramāmikṣā, kiṃ tu paya eva' iti tacchabdādibhiravagamyate |
'yasminpayasi dadhiprakṣepaḥ, sā'mikṣā' iti tacchabdena payaḥ parāmṛśyate |

children.translated_text: In the invitatory verse (<s>puronuvākyā</s>) of the <s>āmikṣā</s> sacrifice, it is thus recorded: '<s>junantāṃ yujyaṃ payaḥ</s>' (may they yoke the yokeable milk).

children.text: payorasaśca madhura āmikṣāyāmanuvartate, na tu vājine |
children.translated_text: And the sweet flavor of milk continues in the <s>āmikṣā</s>, but not in the <s>vājina</s>.

children.text: tataḥ- prādhānyena payaso vanībhāvāvasthāṃ janayituṃ dadhyānītam- ityāmikṣaiva prayojikā |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the curds are brought primarily to produce the state of curdling in the milk — so the <s>āmikṣā</s> alone is the causal agent.

children.text: anuniṣpādyeva vājinam, na tu prayojakam || MJaiNyC_4,1.18-19 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>vājina</s> is merely a by-product (<s>anuniṣpādya</s>), not a causal agent. || MJaiNyC_4,1.18-19 ||

This is recorded: '<s>tapte payasi dadhy ānayati sā vaiśvadevyāmikṣā vājibhyo vājinam</s>' (he brings curds into heated milk — that is the <s>āmikṣā</s> sacred to the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, and the <s>vājina</s> for the <s>vājins</s>). Therein, just as by the addition of curds into milk the <s>āmikṣā</s> substance is produced, so too the <s>vājina</s> substance is produced — and thus the capacity of the curds-bringing to generate [both] is equal for both substances. Therefore, both are causal agents — having arrived at this position, we say: 'The <s>āmikṣā</s> is not a different substance, but just the milk itself' — this is understood from the pronoun '<s>sā</s>' (that) and the like. By the pronoun '<s>sā</s>', the milk into which the curds are added is referred to as the <s>āmikṣā</s>.
(In the tenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the non-causal role of bringing the cow for the foot-rite, the <s>sūtra</s>:)
The foot-rite (<s>padakarman</s>) is not the causal agent of the bringing [of the cow], because the bringing serves another's purpose. / Jaim_4,1.25 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.20-21
He composes the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the foot-rite the causal agent of the bringing of the <s>Soma</s>-purchasing cow?
Or not — the first [alternative]; like the axle-anointing (<s>akṣāñjana</s>), because of [its] proximity to the purchase. // MJaiNy_4,1.20 //
By the instrumental case, the cow serves the purchase; through that, the bringing [of the cow] also [serves the purchase];
since it serves that purpose, [the foot-rite] is occasioned by that [bringing] — but the foot-rite is not the causal agent [of the bringing]. // MJaiNy_4,1.21 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome somakraya āghnāyate- 'ekahāyanyā krīṇāti' iti |
sevamekahāyanī gauryadā somaṃ kretumānīyate, tadādhvaryustasyāḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nugacchati |
tadapyāmnātam- 'ṣaṭpadānyanuniṣkrāmati' iti |
tataḥ saptame pade hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya hutvā tatpadagataṃ rajo gṛhṇīyāt |
etadapi śrūyate- 'saptamaṃ padamadhvaryurañjalinā gṛhṇāti' iti |
tadetadrajaḥ saṃgṛhya havirdhānayoḥ śakaṭayorakṣe tena rajasāṃ saṃyuktamañjanaṃ prakṣipet |
etadapi śrutam-'yajñaṃ vā etatsaṃbharanti yatsomakrayaṇyai padam' iti prastutya 'yarhi havirdhāne prācī pravartayeyuḥ, tarhi tenākṣamupāñjyāt' iti |
tatra yathā krayaḥ saṃnikṛṣṭaḥ, tathaiva padakarmāpyakṣāñjanaṃ saṃnikṛṣṭam |
athocyeta-
dadhyānayanamāmikṣayā yathā saṃyuktam, na tathākṣāñjanaṃ somakrayaṇyānayanena saṃyuktam- iti |
tanna |
kraye 'pi tadasaṃyogasya tulyatvāt |
atha- asaṃyukto 'pi krayo gavānayanena niṣpadyate |
- tarhyakṣāñjanamapi tena niṣpadyate- iti samānatvāt |
krayavatpadakarmāpi somakrayaṇyānayanasya prayojakam- iti prāpte,-
brūmaḥ- 'ekahāyanyā krīṇāti' iti tṛtīyāśrutyā goḥ krayārthatā gamyate |
children.translated_text: we say: By the instrumental <s>śruti</s> '<s>ekahāyanyā krīṇāti</s>' (he purchases with a one-year-old cow), it is understood that the cow serves the purchase.

children.text: godvārā tadānayanamapi krayārthameveti kraya evā'nayane prayojakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Through the cow, the bringing too serves the purchase alone — so the purchase alone is the causal agent of the bringing.

children.text: na ca padakarmārthatvaṃ gorvā tadānayanasya vā kvacicchrutam |
children.translated_text: And nowhere is it heard that the cow or its bringing serves the purpose of the foot-rite.
Therefore, the [foot-rite] is not the causal agent [of the bringing]. || MJaiNyC_4,1.20-21 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, in the <s>Soma</s> purchase, it is recorded: '<s>ekahāyanyā krīṇāti</s>' (he purchases with a one-year-old cow). Now, when this one-year-old cow is brought to purchase the <s>Soma</s>, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> follows behind her. This too is recorded: '<s>ṣaṭ padāny anuniṣkrāmati</s>' (he steps out following for six paces). Then, at the seventh step, having placed gold [on the ground] and having offered, he should collect the dust from that footstep. This too is heard: '<s>saptamaṃ padam adhvaryur añjalinā gṛhṇāti</s>' (the <s>Adhvaryu</s> collects the seventh footstep with his cupped hands). Having collected that dust, he should throw it, mixed with ointment, onto the axle of the two <s>Havirdhāna</s> carts. This too is heard: '<s>yajñaṃ vā etat saṃbharanti yat somakrayaṇyai padam</s>' (they indeed collect the sacrifice when [they collect] the footstep of the <s>Soma</s>-purchasing cow), introducing [the topic], then '<s>yarhi havirdhāne prācī pravartayeyuḥ, tarhi tena akṣam upāñjyāt</s>' (when they would roll the <s>Havirdhāna</s> [carts] eastward, then one should anoint the axle with that). Therein, just as the purchase is proximate [to the bringing], so too the foot-rite — the axle-anointing — is proximate. Now if it were argued: the curds-bringing was connected with the <s>āmikṣā</s>, but the axle-anointing is not similarly connected with the bringing of the <s>Soma</s>-purchasing cow — that is not so. Because the same lack of connection exists with the purchase as well. Now — even though unconnected, the purchase is accomplished through the bringing of the cow. Then the axle-anointing too is accomplished through that [bringing] — by parity of reasoning. Like the purchase, the foot-rite too would be the causal agent of the bringing of the <s>Soma</s>-purchasing cow — having arrived at this position,
(In the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the non-employment of the <s>kapālas</s> (potsherds) for scattering husks, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: arthābhidhānakarma ca bhaviṣyatā saṃyogasya tannimittatvāt tadartho hi vidhīyate / Jaim_4,1.26 /
children.translated_text: And the action stated as meaningful [is connected] with the future [use], because of the connection being occasioned by that — for it is enjoined for that purpose. / Jaim_4,1.26 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.22-23
He composes the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Are both the cooking and the scattering of husks occasions for the employment of the <s>kapāla</s> (potsherd),
or is the cooking alone [the occasion]? The first, because the instrumental case indicates [the kapāla's] purpose for scattering. // MJaiNy_4,1.22 //
By the name '<s>puroḍāśakapāla</s>' (rice-cake potsherd), the purpose would be for cooking;

children.text: prayuktasya prayuktirno tasya vāpe prasañjanam // MJaiNy_4,1.23 //
children.translated_text: that which is already employed [for cooking] need not be [separately] employed — its involvement in scattering follows incidentally. // MJaiNy_4,1.23 //

children.text:
'kapāleṣu śrapayati' iti śrapaṇaṃ puroḍāśasya śrutam |
tathā- 'puroḍāśakapālena tuṣānupavapati' iti kapāle tuṣadhāraṇaṃ śrutam |
te ca tuṣāḥ sakapālāḥ 'rakṣasāṃ bhāgo 'si' iti mantreṇa naiṛtyāṃ diśyavasthāpanīyāḥ |
tatra śrapaṇaṃ yathā kapālasaṃpādasya prayojakam, tathā tuṣavāpo 'pi prayojakaḥ |
'ekahāyamyā' iti tṛtīyayaikahāyanīnayanasya yathā krayārthatvāvagamaḥ tathā 'kapālena' iti tṛtīyayā kapālasya tuṣavāpārthatvāvagamāt-
iti cet |
maivam |
nātra kapālamātrasya tuṣopavāpasādhanatvaṃ śrutam |
kiṃ tarhi yatkapālaṃ puroḍāśaśrapaṇāyopāttamāsāditaṃ ca, tasya kapālasya sādhanatvam |
etacca 'puroḍāśakapālena' iti saviśeṣaṇanāmnā tadvidhānādavagamyate |
tathā sati pratham śrapaṇena kapālaṃ prayujyane |
children.translated_text: This being so, the potsherd is first employed by the cooking.

children.text: na ca prayuktasya punastuṣavāpena prayuktiḥ saṃbhavati |
children.translated_text: And it is not possible for what is already employed to be [separately] employed again by the husk-scattering.

children.text: tasmāt- śrapaṇenaiva prayuktaṃ kapālaṃ tuṣopavāpe 'pi prasaṅgātsidhyati |
children.translated_text: Therefore — the potsherd, already employed by the cooking, is incidentally available for the husk-scattering as well.
Precisely this kind of accessory status is conveyed by the instrumental-case Vedic statement. || MJaiNyC_4,1.22-23 ||

It is heard: '<s>kapāleṣu śrapayati</s>' (he cooks on the potsherds) — the cooking of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice-cake) on potsherds. Similarly: '<s>puroḍāśakapālena tuṣānupavapati</s>' (he scatters the husks with the rice-cake potsherd) — the holding of husks on the potsherd is heard. And those husks, together with the potsherd, are to be placed in the south-western direction with the <s>mantra</s> '<s>rakṣasāṃ bhāgo'si</s>' (you are the portion of the <s>rakṣases</s>). Therein, just as the cooking is an occasion for employing the potsherd, so too is the scattering of husks an occasion. Just as the instrumental case in '<s>ekahāyamyā</s>' (with a one-year-old [cow]) conveys that the one-year-old cow serves the purpose of purchase, similarly the instrumental case in '<s>kapālena</s>' (with the potsherd) conveys that the potsherd serves the purpose of husk-scattering — if so argued, that is not so. Here, it is not heard that the mere potsherd is the instrument for scattering husks. Rather, it is the potsherd that has been taken up and used for cooking the <s>puroḍāśa</s> — that potsherd is the instrument. And this is understood from the qualified name '<s>puroḍāśakapālena</s>' (with the rice-cake potsherd), which enjoins [it] with a qualifier.
(In the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the non-employment of dung and blood as [independent] occasions for the animal [sacrifice], the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
Since there is no [independent] slaughtering [for them], the dung and blood have no ritual-action status in the animal [sacrifice]. / Jaim_4,1.27 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.24-25
He composes the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Are the heart and the like, and the dung and the like, both occasions for the slaughtering of the animal,
or is only the heart and the like [the occasion]? The first [alternative holds] because of equal status as belonging to the archetype. // MJaiNy_4,1.24 //
Or, since the oblation substance (<s>havis</s>) is not exhausted, only the heart and the like, which have the nature of oblation,
serve as occasions — not the others [dung and blood], because they are not of that nature. // MJaiNy_4,1.25 //

children.text:
agnīṣomīyapaśau śrutam-"hṛdayasyāgre 'vadyati, atha jihvāyāḥ, atha vakṣasaḥ,"iti |
tathānyadapi śrutam- 'śakṛtsaṃpravidhyati' 'lohitaṃ nirasyati' iti |
tatra hṛdayādīnāṃ śakṛdādīnāṃ ca prakaraṇapāṭhasāmyātpaśusādhyatvasāmyāñca hṛdayādivacchakṛdādikamapi paśvālambhasya prayojakam- iti cet |
maivam |

children.translated_text: For the animal sacrifice serves the purpose of obtaining the oblation substance (<s>havis</s>).
And the status of oblation substance — due to fitness for being eaten — belongs only to the heart and the like, not to the unfit dung and blood.
Therefore — only the heart and the like serve as occasions [for slaughtering].
The piercing of the dung and the casting out of the blood — both of these are merely [acts of] disposing of the remainder. || MJaiNyC_4,1.24-25 ||

In the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal sacrifice, it is heard: 'He first cuts from the heart, then from the tongue, then from the chest.' And another [text] is also heard: '<s>śakṛtsaṃpravidhyati</s>' (he pierces the dung), '<s>lohitaṃ nirasyati</s>' (he casts out the blood). Therein, since the heart and the like and the dung and the like are equally recited in the context, and are equally accomplished through the animal, the dung and the like, just like the heart and the like, would also be occasions for slaughtering the animal — if so argued, that is not so.
(In the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the <s>puroḍāśa</s> [rice-cake] is not [independently] employed by the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> [offering], <s>sūtras</s> 28–32)
And the partial substance, at the time of production, because of its connection with what already exists. / Jaim_4,1.28 /

children.text: nirdeśāt tasyānyad arthād iti cet / Jaim_4,1.29 /
children.translated_text: If [it be argued that] from the statement, that [Sviṣṭakṛt] is for a different purpose — / Jaim_4,1.29 /
No, because of the proximity of [it being a] remainder. / Jaim_4,1.30 /
Because of the effect of the rite. / Jaim_4,1.31 /
And because of the observation of the mark. / Jaim_4,1.32 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.26-27
He composes the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering for the well-made) an occasion for employing the northern half of the <s>puroḍāśa</s>,

children.text: yadvā prayuktopajīvī syādādyaḥ svasya siddhaye // MJaiNy_4,1.26 //
children.translated_text: or does it, being already employed, subsist [on the existing puroḍāśa]? The first [alternative holds] for the sake of its own accomplishment. // MJaiNy_4,1.26 //
When the word '<s>uttarārdha</s>' (northern/upper half) has an expectation toward what is [already] present [in the context],
let this [Sviṣṭakṛt] operate by subsisting on the <s>puroḍāśa</s> that serves the purpose of <s>Agni</s> and other [deities]. // MJaiNy_4,1.27 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate- 'uttarārdhātsviṣṭakṛte samavadyati' iti |
so 'yaṃ sviṣṭakṛdyāgaḥ kasyacinnūtanasya taduttarārdhasya ca prayojakaḥ |
tadubhayābhāve svasiddhyabhāvāt- iti cet |
maivam |

children.translated_text: The word '<s>uttara</s>' (upper) and the word '<s>ardha</s>' (half) — being a pronoun and a part-denoting [word] respectively — require some antecedent entity that has parts.
The <s>puroḍāśa</s> intended for the deities <s>Agni</s> and others is the antecedent entity that has parts.
Therefore — by subsisting on that very [puroḍāśa], the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> sacrifice proceeds.
It is not [an independent] occasion for anything new. || MJaiNyC_4,1.26-27 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, it is heard: '<s>uttarārdhātsviṣṭakṛte samavadyati</s>' (he cuts from the upper half for the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>). This <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> sacrifice would be an [independent] occasion for some new [substance] and for its upper half — since without both, its own accomplishment would be impossible — if so argued, that is not so.
(In the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on the non-performance of remainder-holding and its vessel in the basting (<s>abhighāraṇa</s>), <s>sūtras</s> 33–39)

children.text: abhighāraṇe viprakarṣād anuyājavat pātrabhedaḥ syāt / Jaim_4,1.33 /
children.translated_text: In the basting (<s>abhighāraṇa</s>), because of the separation, there would be a vessel-distinction, like [the case of] the <s>anuyāja</s> (after-offering). / Jaim_4,1.33 /

children.text: na vāpātratvād apātratvaṃ tv ekadeśatvāt / Jaim_4,1.34 /
children.translated_text: Or, there would be no [separate] vessel, since [the ladle] is not [itself] a vessel; but [the remainder] would be part [of the same vessel]. / Jaim_4,1.34 /
And because of being the cause for simultaneous employment. / Jaim_4,1.35 /
And because the absence [of a separate vessel] is observed. / Jaim_4,1.36 /
When [the substance] exists, [one makes] a statement along with [it]. / Jaim_4,1.37 /
If [it be argued that] it does not [apply] to that — / Jaim_4,1.38 /
It would [apply], because of its being primary. / Jaim_4,1.39 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.28-29
He composes the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Having basted the [oblation substances] of the <s>prayājas</s> (preliminary offerings) — as for the remainder of the ghee (<s>havis</s>) here,
should the remainder-holding and its vessel be performed, or not? // MJaiNy_4,1.28 //

children.text: nānyathā tena te kārye na kārye pratipattitaḥ /
children.translated_text: They need not [be performed], since without them the [basting] is accomplished; and they are not to be performed, from the [nature of the] disposal;
and there is no purpose at all in the pouring out, since the <s>Prājāpatya</s> omental membrane does not [require it]. // MJaiNy_4,1.29 //

children.text:
prakṛtau śrutam- 'prayājaśeṣeṇa havīṃṣyabhidhārayati' iti |
tadetadvikṛtāvatidiṣṭam |
vikṛtayaśca vājapeyagatāḥ paśavaḥ |
te ca dvividhāḥ- kratupaśavaḥ prājāpatyapaśavaśceti |
'āgneyaṃ paśumālabhate' ityādinā vihitāḥ kratupaśavaḥ |
itare tu 'saptadaśa prājāpatyānpaśūnālabhate' iti vihitāḥ |
ete cobhayavidhāḥ paśavaḥ prātaḥsavane sahaivopakramyante |
tataḥ sarveṣāmarthe sakṛdeva prayājā anuṣṭhīyante |
tatra kratupaśūnāṃ prātaḥsavana evā'labdhavyatvāttadīyahaviṣāṃ prayājaśeṣeṇābhidhāraṇaṃ nirvighnameva sidhyati |
prājāpatyapaśūnāṃ paryagnikaraṇaparyantameva tadānīmanuṣṭhānam |
ālambhastu mādhyaṃdine savane, tatkālaviśeṣasya 'brahmasāmnyālabhate' iti vidhānāt |
teṣāṃ ca prājāpatyādīnāṃ haviṣāmabhidhāraṇārtha prātaḥkālīnaḥ prayājaśeṣo dhārayitavyaḥ |
na cātra juhvāṃ taddhāraṇaṃ saṃbhavati |
kratupaśvanuṣṭhāne juhvāyā vyāpṛtatvāt |
ataḥ pātrāntaraṃ saṃtādya tasminnayaṃ śeṣo dhārayitavyaḥ |
anyathā prājāpatyahaviṣāṃ prayājaśeṣeṇābhidhāraṇātsiddhiḥ |
tasmāt- śeṣadhāraṇatatpātre saṃpādanīye- iti prāpte-
brūmaḥ- te ubhe na kartavye |
kutaḥ |
abhidhāraṇasya śeṣapratipattirūpatvena haviḥsaṃskārakatvābhāvatt |
na hi dṛṣṭe pratipādane satyadṛṣṭārthaḥ saṃskāro yuktaḥ |
dṛṣṭaṃ ca juhvā riktīkaraṇam |
anyathā prayājaśeṣopetāyāṃ juhvāmājyabhāgārthatayā gṛhyamāṇaṃ saṃkīryeta |
tato riktīkaraṇarūpapapratipattyarthameva prakṛtau śeṣeṇābhidhāraṇam |
astu vā tatra haviḥsaṃskāro 'pi tathāpi prājāpatyavapāyāmabhidhāraṇaṃ vyartham |
rūkṣatvanivāraṇāya hyabhidhāryate |
na ca prājāpatyavapāyā rūkṣatāsti |
brahmasāmnaivatadrūkṣatāyā nivāritatvāt |
ata eva- śrūyate- 'śamyā vā etarhi vapā yarhyanabhidhṛtā |

children.translated_text: <s>Brahma</s> indeed is the <s>Brahmasāman</s>; when he slaughters at the <s>Brahmasāman</s>,
thereby [the omental membranes] are no longer rough, thereby they are basted.'
'<s>Śamyā</s>' means 'rough' — this is the meaning.
Therefore — the remainder-holding and its vessel need not be performed. || MJaiNyC_4,1.28-29 ||

In the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>), it is heard: '<s>prayājaśeṣeṇa havīṃṣyabhidhārayati</s>' (he bastes the oblation substances with the remainder of the <s>prayāja</s> [ghee]). This is extended (<s>atidiṣṭa</s>) to the modification (<s>vikṛti</s>). And the modifications are the animals belonging to the <s>Vājapeya</s>. These are of two kinds: ritual animals (<s>kratupaśus</s>) and <s>Prājāpatya</s> animals. The ritual animals are enjoined by '<s>āgneyaṃ paśumālabhate</s>' (he slaughters the <s>Āgneya</s> animal) and the like. The others are enjoined by '<s>saptadaśa prājāpatyānpaśūnālabhate</s>' (he slaughters seventeen <s>Prājāpatya</s> animals). Both kinds of animals are commenced together at the morning pressing. Therefore, the <s>prayājas</s> are performed only once for the sake of all. Therein, since the ritual animals must be slaughtered at the morning pressing itself, the basting of their oblation substances with the <s>prayāja</s>-remainder proceeds without obstacle. But for the <s>Prājāpatya</s> animals, only the procedures up to circumambulation with fire (<s>paryagnikaraṇa</s>) are performed at that time. The slaughtering, however, [occurs] at the midday pressing, because of the injunction '<s>brahmasāmnyālabhate</s>' (he slaughters at the <s>Brahmasāman</s> [chant]) specifying that particular time. And for the purpose of basting the oblation substances of those <s>Prājāpatya</s> animals, the morning <s>prayāja</s>-remainder must be retained. But its retention in the <s>juhū</s> (offering ladle) is not possible here, because the <s>juhū</s> is occupied with the ritual-animal procedure. Therefore, another vessel must be prepared, and this remainder should be held therein. Otherwise, the basting of the <s>Prājāpatya</s> oblation substances with the <s>prayāja</s>-remainder would succeed. Therefore — the remainder-holding and its vessel must be arranged — having arrived at this position, we say: both of those need not be done. Why? Because the basting (<s>abhidhāraṇa</s>) has the nature of disposing of the remainder, and does not serve to consecrate the oblation substance. For when a visible purpose for the disposal exists, a consecration with an invisible purpose is not appropriate. And the visible [purpose] is the emptying of the <s>juhū</s>. Otherwise, the ghee taken for the <s>ājyabhāga</s> (ghee-portion offering) into the <s>juhū</s> still containing the <s>prayāja</s>-remainder would become mixed. Therefore, the basting with the remainder in the archetype is solely for the purpose of disposal in the form of emptying [the ladle]. Even if there is also a consecration of the oblation substance there, nevertheless, the basting of the <s>Prājāpatya</s> omental membrane is purposeless. For [the substance] is basted in order to remove dryness. But there is no dryness in the <s>Prājāpatya</s> omental membrane — because its dryness has already been removed by the <s>Brahmasāman</s> [chant] itself. Hence — it is heard: 'Verily, the omental membrane is now rough (<s>śamyā</s>) when it is unbasted.
(In the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the bringing-together (<s>samānayana</s>) is an occasion for the <s>ājya</s> (ghee) properties, <s>sūtras</s> 40–41)

children.text: samānayanaṃ tu mukhyaṃ syāl liṅgadarśanāt / Jaim_4,1.40 /
children.translated_text: The bringing-together (<s>samānayana</s>) would be primary, because of the observation of the mark. / Jaim_4,1.40 /
For in the [Vedic] statement, the reason is incapable [of establishing it]. / Jaim_4,1.41 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.30-32
He composes the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
For the oblation of the fourth <s>prayāja</s> (preliminary offering), the ghee from the <s>upabhṛt</s> (secondary ladle) —
he brings [it] into the <s>juhū</s> — this <s>upabhṛt</s> [ghee] should not occasion the employment [of the bringing]. // MJaiNy_4,1.30 //
Or it should occasion it — the bringing serves the purpose of all the <s>prayājas</s> and the like;
since in the Vedic statement, the <s>upabhṛt</s> and the <s>juhū</s> [ghees] alternate in the <s>ājya</s> [offerings] — // MJaiNy_4,1.31 //

children.text: na prayojakatā maivaṃ niyatārtha tu jauhavam /
children.translated_text: No, [the bringing] is not an [independent] occasion — that is not so — the <s>juhū</s> [ghee] has a fixed purpose;

children.text: atihāyeḍa ityukte caturthe sā prayojayet // MJaiNy_4,1.32 //
children.translated_text: when it is said '<s>atihāyeḍaḥ</s>' (passing beyond the <s>Iḍā</s> [-hymn]), in the fourth [<s>prayāja</s>], that [bringing] occasions the employment. // MJaiNy_4,1.32 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate-'atihāyeḍo barhiḥ pratisamānayati juhvāmaupabhṛtam' iti |
asyāyamarthaḥ- 'pañcāmāṃ prayājānāṃ madhye tṛtīyaḥ prayāja iṭ śabdena bahuvacanāntenābhidhīyate |
taṃ tṛtīyaṃ prayojamatikramya barhirnāmakaṃ caturtha prayājaṃ hotumupabhṛtsaṃjñakāyāṃ struci sthitaṃ ghṛtaṃ juhvāmānetavyam' iti |
tadetadānayanamupabhṛtyājyagrahaṇasya na prayojakam |
tathā hi- juhūpabhṛddhruvāsu tisṛṣu strukṣvājyagrahaṇaprakārastadviniyogaścaivamāmnāyate- caturjuhvāṃ gṛhṇāti, aṣṭāvupabhṛti, ' 'catughruvāyāṃ,' yajjuhvāṃ gṛhṇāti, prayājebhyastat' ' yadupabhṛti prayājāmuyājebhyastat' 'sarvasmai vā etadyajñāya gṛhyate yaddhruvāyāmājyam' iti |
tatra- jauhavaṃ kevalaprayājārtham |
aupabhṛtaṃ tu prayājānuyājārthāmiti prayājeṣu jauhavamaupabhṛtaṃ ca vikalpate |
tathā sati yadā jauhavena prayājā ijyante tadānīmaupabhṛtasyā'nayanameva māsti, kuta ānayanasya prayojakatvam |
yadā tvaupabhṛtena prayājahomaḥ, tadānīmaupabhṛtasyardha pañcaprayājārtham, itaradanuyājārtham |
tayoḥ prayājasādhanamartha prathamaprayājakāla eva juhvāmānītamiti na tasya caturthaprayājaṃ prati samānayanaṃ vidhīyate |
yattvanuyājārthamitaradardhamupabhṛtyavaśiṣṭam, tanmadhye kiṃciccaturthaprayājaṃ prati samānetavyam |
tattvanuyājaireva prayuktamiti na tasyā'nayanaṃ prayojakam- iti prāpte-
brūmaḥ- 'yajjauhavaṃ tatprayājatritayārtham, yattvaupabhṛtaṃ tadavaśiṣṭaprayājadvayārthamanuyājārtha ca'- ityevaṃ vākyadvayasya vyavasthāyāṃ saṃbhavantyāmaṣṭadoṣagrasto vikalpo nā'śrayituṃ śakyaḥ |

yadā jauhavasvīkāraḥ, tadānīmaupabhṛtavākyasya prāptaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ parityajyeta, aprāptamaprāmāṇyaṃ svī kriyeta, punarapi kadācidaupabhṛtasvīkāre tyaktaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ svīkriyeta, svīkṛtamaprāmāṇyaṃ parityajyeta, ityaupabhṛtavākye catvāro doṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: When the <s>juhū</s>-[ghee] is accepted [as the sole source for all prayājas], the established validity of the <s>upabhṛt</s>-statement would be abandoned, and its unestablished invalidity would be accepted; and when the <s>upabhṛt</s>-[ghee] is accepted again [at another time], the abandoned validity would be re-accepted, and the accepted invalidity would be abandoned — thus there are four defects in the <s>upabhṛt</s>-statement.
Similarly, four [defects arise] in the <s>juhū</s>-statement — thus eight defects [in total].
And the aforesaid reconciliation is determined from the sentence '<s>atihāyeḍaḥ</s>' (passing beyond the <s>Iḍā</s>).

children.text: tathā satyaupabhṛtasyānuyājā yathā prayojakāḥ, tathaiva caturthapañcamaprayājaniṣpādakamānayanamapi prayojakameva || MJaiNyC_4,1.30-32 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, just as the after-offerings (<s>anuyājas</s>) of the <s>Upabhṛt</s> [ladle] are instigators, so too the bringing [of ghee] that accomplishes the fourth and fifth fore-offerings (<s>prayājas</s>) is itself an instigator. || MJaiNyC_4,1.30-32 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, it is heard: '<s>atihāyeḍo barhiḥ pratisamānayati juhvāmaupabhṛtam</s>' (passing beyond the <s>Iḍā</s>-[hymn], for the <s>Barhis</s> [<s>prayāja</s>], he brings the <s>upabhṛt</s> [ghee] into the <s>juhū</s>). Its meaning is: Among the five <s>prayājas</s>, the third <s>prayāja</s> is denoted by the word '<s>iḍ</s>' in the plural. Passing beyond that third <s>prayāja</s>, for the fourth <s>prayāja</s> called <s>Barhis</s>, the ghee situated in the ladle called <s>upabhṛt</s> is to be brought into the <s>juhū</s>. This bringing does not serve as an [independent] occasion for taking <s>ājya</s> from the <s>upabhṛt</s>. For the manner of taking <s>ājya</s> and its assignment in the three ladles — <s>juhū</s>, <s>upabhṛt</s>, and <s>dhruvā</s> — is taught thus: 'He takes four [portions] in the <s>juhū</s>, eight in the <s>upabhṛt</s>, four in the <s>dhruvā</s>.' 'That which he takes in the <s>juhū</s> is for the <s>prayājas</s>.' 'That which [he takes] in the <s>upabhṛt</s> is for the <s>prayājas</s> and <s>anuyājas</s>.' 'The <s>ājya</s> that is taken in the <s>dhruvā</s> — that is for the entire sacrifice.' Therein — the <s>juhū</s>-[ghee] (<s>jauhava</s>) is solely for the <s>prayājas</s>. But the <s>upabhṛt</s>-[ghee] (<s>aupabhṛta</s>) is for both <s>prayājas</s> and <s>anuyājas</s> — so there is an option between the <s>juhū</s>-ghee and the <s>upabhṛt</s>-ghee in the <s>prayājas</s>. This being so, when the <s>prayājas</s> are offered with the <s>juhū</s>-ghee, there should be no bringing at all of the <s>upabhṛt</s>-ghee — how then could the bringing be an [independent] occasion? When, however, the <s>prayāja</s>-oblation is with the <s>upabhṛt</s>-ghee, then half of the <s>upabhṛt</s> [ghee] serves the five <s>prayājas</s>, and the other half serves the <s>anuyājas</s>. Of those, the portion for the <s>prayājas</s> is brought into the <s>juhū</s> at the very time of the first <s>prayāja</s> — so the bringing is not enjoined with respect to the fourth <s>prayāja</s>. And the other half remaining in the <s>upabhṛt</s> for the <s>anuyājas</s> — from it, some [portion] is to be brought for the fourth <s>prayāja</s>. But that is already employed by the <s>anuyājas</s>, so the bringing is not an [independent] occasion — having arrived at this position, we say: when the two statements can be reconciled — 'the <s>juhū</s>-ghee is for the three <s>prayājas</s>, and the <s>upabhṛt</s>-ghee is for the remaining two <s>prayājas</s> and the <s>anuyājas</s>' — the option that is afflicted with the eightfold defect cannot be resorted to.
(In the sixteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>Aupabhṛta</s> and <s>Jauhava</s> [ghee portions] serving specific purposes in sequence, <s>sūtras</s> 42–45)
Therein, the origination would be undivided. / Jaim_4,1.42 /
The <s>Jauhava</s> [portion] there is for the purpose of prohibiting the after-offering. / Jaim_4,1.43 /
The <s>Aupabhṛta</s> [portion] likewise — if so [it is argued]. / Jaim_4,1.44 /
It would be a permanent restatement, from the prohibition of the <s>Juhū</s> [ladle]. / Jaim_4,1.45 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.33-34
He composes the sixteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The ghee in the <s>Juhū</s>, <s>Upabhṛt</s>, and <s>Dhruva</s> [ladles] — does it serve all purposes, or is there a fixed distribution?
It would serve all purposes, since there is no distinction; the <s>Jauhava</s> is for the fore-offerings. // MJaiNy_4,1.33 //
The <s>Aupabhṛta</s> portion would be for the fore-offerings and after-offerings;
the <s>Dhruva</s> [portion] is for the fire[-related rites] — this distribution is established by verbal statements. // MJaiNy_4,1.34 //

children.text: 'caturjuhvāṃ gṛhṇāti' ityādiṣu grahaṇavākyeṣu 'etadartham' iti viśeṣaniyāmakasyāśravaṇātpātratrayagatamājyaṃ sarvārtham- iti cet |
children.translated_text: In the drawing-statements such as '<s>caturjuhvāṃ gṛhṇāti</s>' (he draws four [portions] into the <s>Juhū</s> [ladle]) and the like, since no specific qualifier such as 'for this purpose' is heard, the ghee in the three vessels serves all purposes — if so [it is argued],
that is not correct.

Because the distribution is understood from statements such as '<s>yajjuhvāṃ gṛhṇāti prayājebhyastat</s>' (what is drawn into the <s>Juhū</s> is for the fore-offerings) and the like. || MJaiNyC_4,1.33-34 ||
(In the seventeenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the non-performance of the two-four drawing in the <s>Upabhṛt</s> [ladle], <s>sūtras</s> 46–48)
That [drawing] has the number eight, because of the <s>śruti</s>. / Jaim_4,1.46 /
And from the support of the <s>Jauhava</s> [portion]. / Jaim_4,1.47 /

children.text: dvayos tu hetusāmarthayaṃ śravaṇaṃ ca samānayane / Jaim_4,1.48 /
children.translated_text: But for both, the reasoning has force, and the <s>śruti</s> [states] a bringing-together. / Jaim_4,1.48 /
START MJaiNy 4,1.35-36
He composes the seventeenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'Eight in the <s>Upabhṛt</s>' — herein, is the injunction for a single drawing of eight,
or for two drawings of four? The first, because the <s>śruti</s> of 'eight' is primary. // MJaiNy_4,1.35 //
The four-fold drawing is an accessory of the offering; being fruitful, it is not overridden;
hence the four-and-two [i.e., two sets of four] is what is indicated; the eightness is for the bringing together. // MJaiNy_4,1.36 //

children.text:
grahaṇavākye 'caturjuhvāṃ gṛhṇāti' ityatra yathā catuḥsaṃkhyāviśiṣṭamekaṃ havirgrahaṇaṃ vihitam, tathaiva 'aṣṭāvupabhṛti' ityatrāpyaṣṭasaṃkhyāviśiṣṭamekaṃ havigrahaṇaṃ vidhātavyam' na tu caturgṛhītadvayam |
tathā satyaṣṭaśrutermukhyatvāvagamāt |
aṣṭasaṃkhyāvayavabhūtayordvayoścatuḥsaṃkhyayorvidhāne satyaṣṭaśabdasyāvayavalakṣaṇā prasajyeta- iti prāpte-
brūmaḥ- prasajyatāṃ nāma lakṣaṇa |
mukhyārthasvīkāre homavākyavirodhāpatteḥ |
'caturgṛhītaṃ juhroti' ityanārabhya śrutaṃ vākyaṃ homamātroddeśena caturgṛhītaṃ vidadhāti |
yadyapyetatsarvahomaviṣayatayā sāmānyarūpam, aupabhṛtaṃ tu prayājānuyājaviṣayatayā viśeṣarūpam, tathāpi homasya phalavattvena prādhānyāt, grahaṇasya homārthatvenopasarjanatvāt, pradhānānusāreṇa caturgṛhītameva yuktam, na tūpasarjanānusāreṇāṣṭagṛhītam |
tasmāt- upabhṛti caturgṛhītadvayaṃ vidhīyate |
tatraikaṃ caturgṛhītaṃ haviścaturthapañcamaprayājārtham |
aparaṃ tvanuyājārtham |
nanvevaṃ tarhi caturgṛhītasyaiva haviṣṭvāt 'caturupabhṛti' ityeva vidhātavyam, na tu 'aṣṭāvupabhṛti' iti vidhiryuktaḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
tathā satyanuyājārtha dvitīyaṃ caturgṛhītaṃ na sidhyet |
atha tadapi vākyāntareṇa vidhīyate, tadānīmupabhṛtaḥ prathamena caturgṛhītenāvaruddhatvāddvitīyasmai pātrāntaramanviṣyeta |
children.translated_text: If that too were enjoined by a separate statement, then since the <s>Upabhṛt</s> is occupied by the first four-fold drawing, a different vessel would need to be sought for the second.

children.text: yadi 'upabhṛti' ityeva dvitīyamapi caturgṛhītaṃ vidhīyate, tadā caturgṛhītadvayasya pṛthagevānuṣṭhānādupabhṛtyekaprayatnenā'nayanaṃ na sidhyet |
children.translated_text: If the second four-fold drawing were also enjoined simply as 'in the <s>Upabhṛt</s>,' then since the two four-fold drawings would be performed separately, the bringing of [both to] the <s>Upabhṛt</s> in a single effort would not be established.
Therefore, the expression '<s>aṣṭāvupabhṛti</s>' (eight in the <s>Upabhṛt</s>) is used for the purpose of bringing both together to the nearby ground.

children.text: tasmātsāhityārthamaṣṭaśabdaprayoge 'pi iviṣṭvasiddhaye caturgṛhīte atra vidhīyete || MJaiNyC_4,1.35-36 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, although the word 'eight' is used for the purpose of togetherness, two four-fold drawings are what is enjoined here for the establishment of the specific [purpose]. || MJaiNyC_4,1.35-36 ||

In the drawing-statement '<s>caturjuhvāṃ gṛhṇāti</s>' (he draws four into the <s>Juhū</s>), just as one drawing of ghee qualified by the number four is enjoined, so too in '<s>aṣṭāvupabhṛti</s>' (eight in the <s>Upabhṛt</s>), one drawing of ghee qualified by the number eight should be enjoined — not two drawings of four. This being so, the primary meaning of the <s>śruti</s> of 'eight' would be understood. If two sets of four were enjoined, then the word 'eight' would have a figurative meaning as denoting its component parts — having arrived at this position, we say: Let that figurative meaning arise. Because accepting the primary meaning would lead to a conflict with the offering-statement. The statement '<s>caturgṛhītaṃ juhoti</s>' (he offers a four-fold drawing), heard without being initiated [into a specific rite], enjoins the four-fold drawing with reference to offering in general. Although this is general in its scope pertaining to all offerings, while the <s>Aupabhṛta</s> is specific in pertaining to the fore-offerings and after-offerings, nevertheless, since the offering is principal because of its fruitfulness, and the drawing is subordinate because it serves the offering, the four-fold drawing following the principal is appropriate — not the eight-fold drawing following the subordinate. Therefore — two four-fold drawings are enjoined in the <s>Upabhṛt</s>. Therein, one four-fold drawing of ghee is for the fourth and fifth fore-offerings. The other is for the after-offerings. [If it is objected:] If so, since the four-fold drawing alone constitutes the oblation, it should be enjoined simply as '<s>caturupabhṛti</s>' (four in the <s>Upabhṛt</s>), and not '<s>aṣṭāvupabhṛti</s>' (eight in the <s>Upabhṛt</s>) — if so [it is argued], that is not correct. If so, the second four-fold drawing for the after-offerings would not be established.

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīye jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistare caturthādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> in the illustrious <s>Mādhavīya Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s>.
Now begins the second <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s>. /
(In the first [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the non-productivity of the cutting and the like of the <s>svaru</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 1–6)
But the <s>svaru</s> (wood-chip) is the product of many [actions], because [the word] denotes the action performed upon itself. / Jaim_4,2.1 /
And there is doubt, because of [the possibility of] a different species. / Jaim_4,2.2 /
Or it is a part of that [post], because [the post] is the cause of the <s>svaru</s>-ness. / Jaim_4,2.3 /
And because of the <s>śruti</s> of '<s>śakala</s>' (splinter). / Jaim_4,2.4 /
And for each sacrificial post, because of the observation. / Jaim_4,2.5 /
The word '<s>karoti</s>' (makes) refers to taking. / Jaim_4,2.6 /
START MJaiNy 4,2.1-2
In the second <s>pāda</s>, he composes the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'<s>Svaruṃ kuruta</s>' (make the <s>svaru</s>) — herein, does the <s>svaru</s> instigate a cutting separate from the sacrificial post,
or not? The first [view]: because of the injunction of a specific [product]. // MJaiNy_4,2.1 //
The first chip (<s>yūpakhaṇḍa</s>) from the sacrificial post — in the injunction of the specific designation '<s>svaru</s>-ness',

children.text: vihite lāghavaṃ tasmādanuniṣpanna eva saḥ // MJaiNy_4,2.2 //
children.translated_text: [there is] economy; therefore, it is a natural by-product. // MJaiNy_4,2.2 //

children.text:
agnīṣomīyapaśau śrūyate- 'yūpasya svaruṃ karoti' iti |
tatra yūpo yathā chedanasya prayojakaḥ, tathā svarurapi cchedanaṃ prayojayati |
kutaḥ- 'karoti' ityanena viśiṣṭavidhipratīteḥ |
karotidhātorhi bhāvanā mukhyor'thaḥ |
tatra yūpaśabdopalakṣitaḥ svādiravṛkṣaḥ karaṇam |
chedanādiritikartavyatā, 'chimnena vṛkṣeṇa svarurutpādanīyaḥ' iti viśiṣṭavidhiḥ |
utpannasya svarorviniyoga evamāmnātaḥ- 'svaruṇā paśumanakti' iti |

children.translated_text: Therefore — the <s>svaru</s> instigates the cutting — having arrived at this position,

children.text: brūmaḥ- 'chidyamānasya yūpasya yaḥ prathamaṃ pattitaḥ śakalaḥ sa svaruḥ' iti svarutvanāmamātravidhau lāghavādyūpavatsvarurnacchedanasya prayojakaḥ |
children.translated_text: we say: '<s>The first chip that falls when the sacrificial post is being cut — that is the <s>svaru</s></s>' — in the economy of merely enjoining the designation '<s>svaru</s>-ness,' like the sacrificial post, the <s>svaru</s> does not instigate the cutting.
Rather, it naturally arises as a by-product during the cutting instigated by the sacrificial post. || MJaiNyC_4,2.1-2 ||

In the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal [sacrifice], it is heard: '<s>yūpasya svaruṃ karoti</s>' (he makes the <s>svaru</s> of the sacrificial post). Therein, just as the sacrificial post instigates the cutting [of the tree], so too the <s>svaru</s> instigates [a separate] cutting. Why? Because the injunction of a specific [product] is understood from '<s>karoti</s>' (makes). For the primary meaning of the root '<s>kṛ</s>' (to do/make) is 'bringing about' (<s>bhāvanā</s>). Therein, the <s>svādi</s> tree indicated by the word '<s>yūpa</s>' (sacrificial post) is the material (<s>karaṇa</s>). The cutting and the like constitute the procedure (<s>itikartavyatā</s>). 'The <s>svaru</s> is to be produced from a tree that has been cut' — this is the specific injunction. And the application of the produced <s>svaru</s> is recited thus: '<s>svaruṇā paśumanakti</s>' (with the <s>svaru</s>, he anoints the animal).
(In the second [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the branch being brought, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
In [the case of] the branch, because that is principal. / Jaim_4,2.7 /
START MJaiNy 4,2.3
He composes the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'He brings the eastward [one]' — herein, is the direction or the branch [what is to be brought]? With the directional <s>śrutis</s>,

children.text: āhāryatvaṃ diśo nāsti śākhā tenopalakṣyate // MJaiNy_4,2.3 //
children.translated_text: the direction cannot be brought; therefore, the branch is what is indicated. // MJaiNy_4,2.3 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ 'yatpalāśaśākhayā vatsānavākaroti' iti palāśaśākhāṃ prakṛtya śrūyate- 'yatprācīmāharet, devalokamabhijayet' iti |
tatra prācīśabdasya digvācitvāddigāharaṇaṃ vidhīyata iti cet |

children.translated_text: that is not correct.
Because it is impossible [to bring a direction].
Therefore, the eastward branch of the tree is what is indicated here.
This being so, there is a benefit to the contextually established [branch]. || MJaiNyC_4,2.3 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices), having taken up the <s>palāśa</s> (leaf) branch — '<s>yatpalāśaśākhayā vatsānavākaroti</s>' (when he drives away the calves with the <s>palāśa</s> branch) — it is heard: '<s>yatprācīmāharet, devalokamabhijayet</s>' (if he were to bring the eastward [one], he would conquer the divine world). Therein, since the word '<s>prācī</s>' (eastward) denotes a direction, a bringing of the direction is enjoined — if so [it is argued],
(In the third [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on whether the cutting is instigated by the branch, <s>sūtras</s> 8–9)

children.text: śākhāyāṃ tatpradhānatvād upaveṣeṇa vibhāgaḥ syād vaiṣamyaṃ tat / Jaim_4,2.8 /
children.translated_text: In the branch, because that is principal, the division would be by the placement (<s>upaveṣa</s>); that [involves] inequality. / Jaim_4,2.8 /
And because of the loss of the <s>śruti</s>. / Jaim_4,2.9 /
START MJaiNy 4,2.4-6
He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: śākhāṃ chittvopaveṣaṃ ca mūle kurvīta śākhayā /
children.translated_text: Having cut the branch, one should make the placement (<s>upaveṣa</s>) at the base; with the branch
one should drive away the calves; with the placement, one should place the potsherds. // MJaiNy_4,2.4 //
Are both [the branch and the placement] instigators of the cutting, or is the calf-driving alone [the instigator]?
The first [view], because of the division between tip and base in their assignment here. // MJaiNy_4,2.5 //
'He makes the placement' — [this statement] is expectant [of completion] and is completed from the base for another's purpose;
therefore, it is a natural by-product; hence, the latter [view] is appropriate. // MJaiNy_4,2.6 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate- 'mūlataḥ śākhāṃ parivāsyopaveṣaṃ karoti' iti |
yeyaṃ palāśaśākhāṃ chittvā vakṣādāhṛtā, tāṃ punaśchittvā mūlabhāgaḥ prādeśaparimita upaveṣaḥ kāryaḥ |
tayoragramūlayoḥ śākhābhāgayoḥ pṛthagviniyoga āmnātaḥ- 'śākhayā vatsānapākaroti |
upaveṣeṇa kapālānyupadadhāti' iti |
tadidaṃ kāryadvayaṃ vṛkṣacchedena samāhṛtayā śākhayā niṣpadyate |
tasmāt- ubhayamapi cchedanāharaṇādeḥ prayojakam- iti cet |
maivam |
'upaveṣaṃ karoti' ityukte 'kena dravyeṇa ityākāṅkṣāyāṃ 'mūlataḥ' iti vaktavyam |
punarapi 'kasya mūlam' ityākāṅkṣāyāṃ 'vatsāpākaraṇārtha chinnāyāḥ palāśaśākhāyā mūlam' ityākāṅkṣā pūraṇīyā |
tasmācchedane vatsāpākaraṇameva prayojakam |
upaveṣastvanuniṣpādī |
nanu-ādyacchedane tathāstu, dvitīyacchedanasyopaveṣaḥ prayojakaḥ |
parivāsanasaṃpannena mūlenopaveṣakartavyatāvidhānāt |
anyathā 'parivāsyopaveṣaṃ karoti' iti samānakartṛtvapūrvakālatvavācino sthappratyayasyānupapatteḥ, iti cet |
maivam |
parivāsanasyopaveṣasaṃbandho vākyena pratīyate |
śākhāsaṃbandhastu 'śākhām' iti dvitīyāśrutyā |
pūrvacchinnāyā api śākhāyāḥ punarmūlāpādānakacaśchedo 'pekṣitaḥ |
anyathā samūlāṃ śākhāṃ hastenodyamya vatsāpākaraṇaṃ duḥśakaṃ syāt |
ata eva 'mūlataḥ' ityapādāne pañcamau śrutā |
tathā sati prathamacchedanāpādānabhūto vṛkṣo 'saṃskṛtatvādyathā laukikaḥ, tathā dvitīyacchedanāpādānabhūtaṃ mūlamapi laukikakāṣṭham |
children.translated_text: This being so, just as the tree, being the source from which the first cutting proceeds, is unconsecrated and hence worldly, so too the base, being the source from which the second cutting proceeds, is worldly wood.

children.text: avaśyamaṅgāreṣu kapālopadhāne kasyacitkāṣṭhasyopādānamarthātprāptaṃ tadevātra 'upaveṣaṃ karoti' ityanūdyate |
children.translated_text: The procurement of some piece of wood for placing the potsherds on embers is necessarily obtained by implication — that very thing is restated here as 'he makes the placement.'

children.text: śākhāṃ parivāsya parityakte mūle saṃnihite sati kapālopadhānārtha kāṣṭhāntarānveṣaṇaprayāso na kartavyaḥ- iti vākyārthaḥ |
children.translated_text: The sentence-meaning is: when, after paring the branch, the discarded base lies nearby, one need not seek another piece of wood for placing the potsherds.

children.text: evaṃ ca sati dohanarahitāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ vatsāpākaraṇārthāyāḥ śākhāyā abhāvādupaveṣāya śākhāchedo na kartavyaḥ || MJaiNyC_4,2.4-6 ||
children.translated_text: And this being so, on the full-moon day when there is no milking and hence no branch needed for calf-driving, one should not cut a branch for the purpose of the placement. || MJaiNyC_4,2.4-6 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, it is heard: '<s>mūlataḥ śākhāṃ parivāsyopaveṣaṃ karoti</s>' (having pared away the branch from the base, he makes the placement). This <s>palāśa</s> branch that has been cut and brought from the tree — cutting it again, a base-portion measuring one <s>prādeśa</s> (span) is to be made as the placement (<s>upaveṣa</s>). Of the two — the tip-portion and the base-portion of the branch — separate assignments are recited: '<s>śākhayā vatsānapākaroti</s>' (with the branch, he drives away the calves), '<s>upaveṣeṇa kapālānyupadadhāti</s>' (with the placement, he places the potsherds). These two tasks are accomplished by the branch collected through the cutting of the tree. Therefore — both are instigators of the cutting and the bringing — if so [it is argued], that is not correct. When it is said 'he makes the placement (<s>upaveṣa</s>),' the expectancy 'from what material?' is to be answered as 'from the base.' And again, the expectancy 'the base of what?' is to be filled with 'the base of the <s>palāśa</s> branch that was cut for the purpose of calf-driving.' Therefore, in the cutting, the calf-driving alone is the instigator. But the placement is a natural by-product. [If it is argued:] Let the first cutting be so; but the second cutting — the placement instigates it. Because the injunction states that the placement is to be made from the base that has been pared. Otherwise, the <s>śatr</s>-suffix in '<s>parivāsyopaveṣaṃ karoti</s>' (having pared, he makes the placement), which denotes same-agent-prior-action, would not be explained — if so [it is argued], that is not correct. The connection of paring with the placement is understood from the sentence. But the connection with the branch is from the accusative (<s>dvitīyā</s>) <s>śruti</s> '<s>śākhām</s>' (the branch). Even of the previously cut branch, a further cutting to separate the base is required. Otherwise, lifting the branch with its base by hand to drive away the calves would be difficult. For this very reason, the ablative (<s>pañcamī</s>) is heard in '<s>mūlataḥ</s>' (from the base).
(In the fourth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the casting of the branch being a disposal act (<s>pratipattikarma</s>), <s>sūtras</s> 10–13)

children.text: haraṇe tu juhotir yogasāmānyād dravyāṇāṃ cārthaśeṣatvāt / Jaim_4,2.10 /
children.translated_text: In the casting, 'offering' [is meant], because of the general connection, and because the substances serve a residual purpose. / Jaim_4,2.10 /
Or it is a disposal (<s>pratipatti</s>), because the word is primarily [directed] to that. / Jaim_4,2.11 /
Even with respect to the meaning — if so [it is argued]. / Jaim_4,2.12 /

children.text: na tasyānadhikārād arthasya ca kṛtatvāt / Jaim_4,2.13 /
children.translated_text: Not so, because [it has] no eligibility, and the purpose has been fulfilled. / Jaim_4,2.13 /
START MJaiNy 4,2.7-9
He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
He casts the <s>Prastara</s> together with the branch — is this casting
a purposeful ritual act (<s>arthakarma</s>) for the branch, or is disposal (<s>pratipatti</s>) appropriate? // MJaiNy_4,2.7 //
The sacrifice is enjoined for the <s>Prastara</s>; because of the companionship of the branch,
if it thereby becomes a purposeful ritual act, the casting would instigate [bringing] the branch. // MJaiNy_4,2.8 //
The verb '<s>harati</s>' (casts) is not a word denoting sacrifice; therefore, it would be a disposal;

children.text: paurṇamāsyāṃ tato naiva hṛtiḥ śākhāṃ prayojayet // MJaiNy_4,2.9 //
children.translated_text: hence, on the full-moon day, the casting does not instigate [bringing] the branch. // MJaiNy_4,2.9 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate- 'saha śākhayā prastaraṃ praharati' iti |
tatra śākhāpraharaṇamarthakarma |
kutaḥ |
prahṛtiśabdena yāgasyābhidhānāt |
etacca 'sūktavākena prastaraṃ praharati' ityetadvākyamudāhṛtya vicāritam |
prastarapraharaṇasya yāgatve tatsāhacaryācchākhāpraharaṇamapi yāga evetyarthakarma syāt |
arthāya kratusāphalyaprayojanāya kriyamāṇamarthakarma |
tataḥ praharaṇena paurṇamāsyāmapi palāśaśākhā prayujyate- iti prāpte, brūmaḥ- 'sūktavākena prastaraṃ praharati' ityatra haratidhātoryāgavācitvaṃ noktam |
kiṃtu māntravarṇikadevatāmupalabhya dravyadevatābhyāṃ yāgaḥ kalpitaḥ |
śākhāpraharaṇe tu nāsti devatā |
tato yāgasya kalpayitumaśakyatayā haratidhāturatra svavācyārthaparityāgamevā'caṣṭe |
tathā sati vatsāpākaraṇa upayuktāyāḥ palāśaśākhāyā upayogāntarābhāvādyāgadeśe 'vakāśalābhāya yatra kvāpyavasyaṃ parityāge prāpte śāstreṇā'havanīya eva tyāgo niyamyate |
anena ca śāstrīyatyāgena śākhāyāḥ pratipattirbhavati |

children.translated_text: Reception (pratipatti) is a consecration (saṃskāra) that constitutes a visible purpose.

children.text: yathā rājñā carvitasya trāmbūlasya sauvarṇe patadgrahe prakṣepaḥ, tadvat |
children.translated_text: Just as the remains of betel chewed by a king are placed in a golden receptacle — so it is in this case.
Therefore, the casting is a reception-rite (pratipattikarma).

children.text: tene ca tadabhāve 'pi kratuvaikalyābhāvāt, paurṇamāsyāṃ svasiddhihetubhūtāṃ śākhāṃ na prayojayati || MJaiNyC_4,2.7-9 ||
children.translated_text: And since, in the absence of that [casting], there is no deficiency in the sacrifice, [the branch] is not employed on the full-moon day, which lacks the branch that is the cause of its own completion. || MJaiNyC_4,2.7-9 ||

In the Darśapūrṇamāsa [sacrifices], it is heard: 'saha śākhayā prastaraṃ praharati' (he casts the prastara-grass together with the branch). Therein, the casting of the branch is a purpose-serving rite (arthakarma). Why? Because the word 'praharati' (casts) denotes sacrifice. This was discussed by citing the sentence 'sūktavākena prastaraṃ praharati' (he casts the prastara-grass with the Sūktavāka [mantra]). Since the casting of the prastara-grass is a sacrifice, by virtue of association with it, the casting of the branch too would be a sacrifice — hence it would be a purpose-serving rite. An arthakarma is that which is performed for a purpose, namely for the efficacy of the sacrifice. Therefore, by the casting, the palāśa branch would also be employed on the full-moon day — having arrived at this position, we say: In 'sūktavākena prastaraṃ praharati,' it was not stated that the root 'hṛ' (to carry/cast) denotes sacrifice. Rather, having apprehended the deity from the mantra-text (māntravārṇika), the sacrifice was construed from the substance and the deity [together]. But in the casting of the branch, there is no deity. Therefore, since the sacrifice cannot be construed, the root 'hṛ' here indicates the abandonment of its own denoted meaning [i.e., it means merely 'to cast away']. This being so, since the palāśa branch — having been used in the removal of the calves — has no other use, it would inevitably have to be discarded somewhere. When its abandonment at the sacrificial site is obtained, the scripture restricts the abandonment to the Āhavanīya fire alone. And by this scriptural abandonment, the reception (pratipatti) of the branch is accomplished.
(In the fifth [adhikaraṇa], on the reception-rite nature of the carrying-away (ninayana), sūtras 14–15)

children.text: utpattyasaṃyogāt praṇītānām ājyavad vibhāgaḥ syāt / Jaim_4,2.14 /
children.translated_text: Since the carried-forth (praṇīta) [waters] have no connection with the originating [injunction], like the clarified butter, there would be a division. / Jaim_4,2.14 /

children.text: saṃyavanārthānāṃ vā pratipattir itarāsāṃ tatpradhānatvāt / Jaim_4,2.15 /
children.translated_text: Or, for those [waters] that serve the purpose of mixing (saṃyavana), reception (pratipatti) of the other [waters] — because they have that [mixing] as their principal purpose. / Jaim_4,2.15 /
START MJaiNy 4,2.10-11
He composes the fifth adhikaraṇa —
With the carried-forth (praṇīta) waters, he mixes [the oblations] and carries [them] to the altar — what [is the purpose]?

children.text: apāṃ dve prāpake kiṃvā haviḥsaṃyavanaṃ tathā // MJaiNy_4,2.10 //
children.translated_text: Are there two purposes of the waters, or [only] the mixing with the oblation, likewise? // MJaiNy_4,2.10 //
From the statement 'apaḥ praṇayati' (he carries forth the waters), since there is equality, the waters serve both purposes;
by scripture, those [waters] are for the purpose of mixing; the carrying-away (ninīti) is a reception [rite]. // MJaiNy_4,2.11 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ śrūyate- 'apaḥ praṇayati' iti |
camasena pātreṇa praṇītānāṃ tāsāmapāṃ |
prayojanamevaṃ śrūyate- 'praṇītābhirhavīṃṣi saṃyauti' iti, 'antarvedi praṇītā bhinayati' iti ca |
havīṃṣi puroḍāśārthāni piṣṭhāni |
tatra haviḥsaṃyavanaṃ vedyāṃ ninayanaṃ cetyatadubhayamapāṃ praṇayanasya prayojakam |
kutaḥ |
'apaḥ vrajayati' ityasya pramayanotpattivākyasyobhayatra samānatvāt |
na hyasminvākye saṃyavanasya kaścidviśeṣasaṃbandhaḥ pratīyate- iti cet |
children.translated_text: For in this sentence, no special connection with the mixing is perceived — if so argued,
that is not correct.

children.text: viniyogavākye 'praṇītābhiḥ' iti tṛtīyāśrutyā saṃyavanasādhanatvāvagamāt, saṃyavanameva prayojakam |
children.translated_text: Because from the instrumental case (tṛtīyā) in the assignment-sentence 'praṇītābhiḥ' (with the praṇīta waters), the instrumentality for mixing is understood — hence the mixing alone is the motivating purpose.

children.text: ninayanavākye tu 'praṇītāḥ' ityanayā dvitīyayā saṃskāryatvāvagamānninayanaṃ pratipattirūpaḥ saṃskāra iti na praṇayanasya prayojakam || MJaiNyC_4,2.10-11 ||
children.translated_text: But in the carrying-away sentence, from the accusative case (dvitīyā) in 'praṇītāḥ' (the praṇīta waters), the status of being the object of consecration is understood — hence the carrying-away is a consecration in the form of reception, and is not a motivating purpose of carrying forth. || MJaiNyC_4,2.10-11 ||

In the Darśapūrṇamāsa [sacrifices], it is heard: 'apaḥ praṇayati' (he carries forth the waters). Of those waters carried forth in a camasa vessel, the purpose is thus heard: 'praṇītābhir havīṃṣi saṃyauti' (with the carried-forth [waters] he mixes the oblations) and 'antarvedi praṇītā niṇayati' (he carries the praṇīta [waters] inside the altar). The 'oblations' are the flour for the puroḍāśa. Therein, the mixing with the oblation and the carrying to the altar — both are the purposes of carrying forth the waters. Why? Because the originating sentence 'apaḥ praṇayati' (he carries forth the waters) is the same for both.
(In the sixth [adhikaraṇa], on the purpose-serving nature (arthakarmatā) of the giving of the staff (daṇḍadāna), sūtras 16–18)
Like the casting (prāsana), the giving of the staff to the Maitrāvaruṇa [priest], because [the staff's purpose] has been fulfilled. / Jaim_4,2.16 /
