Or it is a purpose-serving rite (arthakarma), because of the connection with the agent, like the garland (sraj). / Jaim_4,2.17 /
And because [it is] observed [to be used] in one connected with the rite. / Jaim_4,2.18 /
START MJaiNy 4,2.12-13
He composes the sixth adhikaraṇa —
Is the giving of the staff in the Maitrāvaruṇa [rite] a reception-rite (pratipatti),
or a purpose-serving rite (arthakarma)? The first, because [the staff's] purpose is fulfilled in the holding. // MJaiNy_4,2.12 //
From the consecration of what has been used and is to be used [further],
the staff is needed for standing and reciting the invitations (praiṣa) and repetitions (anuvacana) — it is a purpose-serving rite. // MJaiNy_4,2.13 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate- 'krīte some maitrāvaruṇāya daṇḍaṃ prayacchati' iti |
tadetaddaṇḍadānaṃ pratipattikarma |
kutaḥ |
daṇḍasya yajamānadhāraṇena kṛtakṛtyatvāt |
yajamāno hyadhvaryuṇā dīkṣāsiddhayartha dattaṃ daṇḍamāsomakrayāddhārayati |
ata evā'mnātam- 'daṇḍena dīkṣayati' iti, 'yaddīkṣitāya daṇḍaṃ prayacchati' iti ca |
tasmādupayuktasya daṇḍasya dānaṃ pratipattiḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
daṇḍe bhaviṣyadupayogasyāpi sadbhāvāt |
yadā maitrāvaruṇaḥ sthitvā praiṣānanuvadati, tadānīmavalambanāya daṇḍo 'pekṣitaḥ |
ata evā'mnātam- 'daṇḍīpraiṣānanvāha' iti |
tathā sati pratipattikarmarūpādupayuktasaṃskārādarthakarmarūpa upayokṣyamāṇasaṃskāraḥ praśastaḥ |

children.translated_text: For everywhere, the purpose of consecration is to put [the thing] to use.

children.text: upayukte tu pratipattirūpasya saṃskārasyākṣaramātraparyavasāyitvena kārye paryavasānābhāvādapraśastatvam |
children.translated_text: But in the case of reception, since the consecration in the form of reception culminates merely in the word [of the injunction] and does not culminate in an actual purpose, it is less preferable.
Therefore — the giving of the staff is a purpose-serving rite for the consecration of the Maitrāvaruṇa [priest].

children.text: tathā sati nirūḍhapaśāvasatyapi dīkṣite daṇḍasaṃpādanasyaitaddānaṃ prayojakam || MJaiNyC_4,2.12-13 ||
children.translated_text: This being so, this giving is the motivation for acquiring a staff for the consecrated one even when a firm one (nirūḍha-paśāva) does not exist. || MJaiNyC_4,2.12-13 ||

In the Jyotiṣṭoma, it is heard: 'krīte some maitrāvaruṇāya daṇḍaṃ prayacchati' (when the Soma is purchased, he gives the staff to the Maitrāvaruṇa [priest]). This giving of the staff is a reception-rite (pratipattikarma). Why? Because the staff has fulfilled its purpose through the sacrificer's holding of it. For the sacrificer holds the staff given by the Adhvaryu for the accomplishment of the consecration (dīkṣā) from [the time of consecration] until the purchase of the Soma. Hence it is recorded: 'daṇḍena dīkṣayati' (he consecrates with the staff) and 'yad dīkṣitāya daṇḍaṃ prayacchati' (when he gives the staff to the consecrated one). Therefore, the giving of the used staff is a reception — if so argued, that is not correct. Because a future use of the staff also exists. When the Maitrāvaruṇa [priest] stands and recites the invitations (praiṣa) and repetitions, the staff is needed at that time for support. Hence it is recorded: 'daṇḍī praiṣān anvāha' (holding the staff, he recites the invitations). This being so, the consecration in the form of utilization — which is a purpose-serving rite — is superior to the consecration in the form of reception of what has been used.
(In the seventh [adhikaraṇa], on the reception-rite nature of the casting (prāsana), the sūtra is:)

children.text: utpattau yena saṃyuktaṃ tadarthaṃ tat, śrutihetutvāt tasyārthāntaragamane śeṣatvāt pratipattiḥ syāt / Jaim_4,2.19 /
children.translated_text: That which is connected at the origination with that [purpose] — is for that purpose, because scripture is the cause thereof; when it goes to another purpose, because of being a remainder, there would be reception (pratipatti). / Jaim_4,2.19 /
START MJaiNy 4,2.14
He composes the seventh adhikaraṇa —

children.text: cātvāle kṛṣṇaśṛṅgasya prāso yaḥ sor'thakarma vā /
children.translated_text: The casting (prāsana) of the black horn into the pit (cātvāla) — is it a purpose-serving rite,
or a reception? The first, because of its purposefulness; the last [alternative] — let the last [hold], because of [its prior] use. // MJaiNy_4,2.14 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate- 'prattāsu dakṣiṇāsu cātvāle kṛṣṇaviṣāṇāṃ prāsyati' iti |
yajamānena dasā dakṣiṇā ṛtvigbhiryadā nītāḥ, tadā yajamānaḥ svahaste dhṛtaṃ kṛṣṇamṛgasya śṛṅgaṃ cātvālanāmake garte parityajet |
so 'yaṃ parityāgor'thakarma |
kutaḥ |
saprayojanatvāt |
pratipattitayāpūrvābhāvena nirarthakaḥ syāt |
ato 'pūrvalābhāyārthakarmatvam- iti cet |
maivam |
'kṛṣṇaviṣāṇayā kāṇḍūyate' iti tṛtīyāśrutyā yajamānaśiraḥkaṇḍūtāvupayuktasya viṣāṇasya pratipaśyapekṣatvāt |
children.translated_text: Because, by the instrumental case heard in 'kṛṣṇaviṣāṇayā kāṇḍūyate' (he scratches with the black horn), the horn — having been used for the scratching of the sacrificer's head — awaits reception.
Nor is there a complete absence of apūrva in reception,

children.text: 'cātvāla eva prāsanam' ityevaṃvidhasya niyamasya vaidhatvena prāsanakriyāprayuktāpūrvābhāve 'pi niyamāpūrvasadbhāvāt |
children.translated_text: because even when the apūrva generated by the casting-act is absent, there exists the apūrva of the restrictive rule — since the restrictive rule 'the casting is in the cātvāla alone' has the nature of an injunction.
Therefore — the casting is a reception-rite. || MJaiNyC_4,2.14 ||

In the Jyotiṣṭoma, it is heard: 'prattāsu dakṣiṇāsu cātvāle kṛṣṇaviṣāṇāṃ prāsyati' (when the fees have been given, he casts the black horn into the pit called cātvāla). When the sacrificial fees have been taken away by the priests, then the sacrificer should cast the horn of the black antelope held in his hand into the pit called cātvāla. This casting is a purpose-serving rite (arthakarma). Why? Because it has a purpose. As a reception (pratipatti), it would be purposeless due to the absence of an unprecedented effect (apūrva). Therefore, for the sake of obtaining an apūrva, it is a purpose-serving rite — if so argued, that is not correct.
(In the eighth [adhikaraṇa], on the reception-rite nature of the going to the Avabhṛtha [bath], sūtras 20–22)
And in the Soma [sacrifice], because [the vessels'] purpose has been fulfilled. / Jaim_4,2.20 /
Or it is a purpose-serving rite, because of the connection with the designation (abhidhāna). / Jaim_4,2.21 /
Or it is reception — because [it follows] that principle; the scripture regarding the Avabhṛtha [bath] is for [indicating] the place. / Jaim_4,2.22 /
START MJaiNy 4,2.15-16
He composes the eighth adhikaraṇa —
The carrying of the Soma-stained vessel to the Avabhṛtha [bathing site] — what [is its nature]?

children.text: sādhanaṃ pratipattirvā yanti tenetyataḥ śruteḥ // MJaiNy_4,2.15 //
children.translated_text: Is it an instrument (sādhana), or a reception? Because of the scripture 'they go with that,' [it is an instrument]. // MJaiNy_4,2.15 //
Instrumentality is obtained [by that view]; but not so — because of the puroḍāśa being the oblation,
and because the vessel has no connection with that [oblation], the casting [of the vessel] is for reception. // MJaiNy_4,2.16 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate- 'caturgṛhītaṃ vā etadyajñasya yadṛjīṣam, yadgrāvāṇaḥ, yadaudumvarī, yadadhiṣavaṇaphalake, tasmādyatkiṃcitsomaliptaṃ draṣyam, tenāvabhṛdyaṃ yanti' iti |
niṣpīḍitasya somasya nīraso bhāga ṛjīṣam |
tadetadṛjīṣagrāvādikaṃ somābhiṣavādau somena lipyate |
tasya lipsasya sarvasyāvabhṛthasādhanatvamabhyupeyam |
kutaḥ |
'tenāvamṛthaṃ yanti' iti tṛtīyāśrutyāvabhṛthasādhanatvāvagamāt |
tasmātsomaliptaṃ dravyamavabhṛdye haviṣṭvena nīyate- iti cet |
maivam |
'vāruṇenakapālenāvabhṛthamavayanti' ityanenotpattivākyaśiṣṭhapuroḍāśahaviṣāvaruddhi'vabhṛthe somaliptapātrasya haviṣṭvena saṃbandhāsaṃbhavāt |
tathā satyavabhṛthaśabdena tadartha deśaṃ lakṣayitvā tasmindeśe somaliptasya pātrasya nayanamatra vidhīyate |
children.translated_text: This being so, by the word 'Avabhṛtha' indicating the place designated for it, the carrying of the Soma-stained vessel to that place is what is enjoined here.
And that carrying is for the purpose of reception.
Because the vessel has been previously used.
Therefore — this is a reception-rite. || MJaiNyC_4,2.15-16 ||

In the Jyotiṣṭoma, it is heard: 'caturgṛhītaṃ vā etad yajñasya yad ṛjīṣam, yad grāvāṇaḥ, yad audumvarī, yad adhiṣavaṇaphalake, tasmād yat kiṃcit somaliptaṃ draṣyam, tenāvabhṛdyaṃ yanti' (these are the four things held [dear] by the sacrifice: the residue (ṛjīṣa), the pressing stones (grāvan), the Audumvarī [post], and the pressing boards — therefore, whatever Soma-stained [thing] is visible, with that they go to the Avabhṛtha [bath]). The residue (ṛjīṣa) is the juice-less portion of the pressed Soma. This residue, the pressing stones, and the like become stained with Soma during the Soma-pressing and so forth. The instrumentality of all these Soma-stained [things] for the Avabhṛtha should be accepted. Why? Because from the instrumental case in 'tenāvabhṛthaṃ yanti' (with that they go to the Avabhṛtha), the instrumentality for the Avabhṛtha is understood. Therefore, the Soma-stained substance is carried to the Avabhṛtha as oblation-material (haviṣṭva) — if so argued, that is not correct. Since the Avabhṛtha — confined by the originating sentence 'vāruṇena kapālenāvabhṛtham avayanti' (they approach the Avabhṛtha with the Vāruṇa potsherd offering) to the puroḍāśa as oblation — cannot have the Soma-stained vessel connected to it as oblation-material.
(In the ninth [adhikaraṇa], on the restrictive-rule nature (niyamārthatā) of injunctions regarding agent, place, and time, sūtras 23–24)
The [injunctions regarding] agent, place, and time — their non-injunctive [nature obtains] because, in actual performance, [they are] always co-present. / Jaim_4,2.23 /
Or the scripture serves a restrictive-rule purpose (niyamārtha). / Jaim_4,2.24 /
START MJaiNy 4,2.17-18
He composes the ninth adhikaraṇa —
'One should sacrifice on level ground' — is this a restatement (anuvāda) of place and the like, or an injunction?
The first [view], because in actual performance, [level ground] is already obtained. // MJaiNy_4,2.17 //
Whether on level ground or uneven — to eliminate this optionality,
a restrictive rule (niyama) is enjoined here, by the incidental inclusion of the non-obtained element. // MJaiNy_4,2.18 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate- 'same darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeta', 'prācīnapravaṇe vaiśvadevena yajeta' 'paurṇamāsyāṃ paurṇamāsyā yajeta' 'amāvāsyāyāmamāvāsyayā yajeta' 'paśubandhasya yajñakratoḥ ṣaḍṛtvijaḥ' 'darśapūrṇamāsayoryajñakratvoścatvāra ṛtvijaḥ' 'cāturmāsyānāṃ yajñakratūnāṃ pañcartvijaḥ' 'agnihotrasya yajñakratoreka ṛtvik' 'saumyasyādhvarasya yajñakratoḥsaptadarśītvajaḥ' 'somena yajeta' iti |
kratuśabde mānasa upāsane 'pi vartate |
'sa kratuṃ kurkṣīta manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīraḥ' ityatra kratuśabdena dhyānavidhānāt |
tadvyāvṛttaye 'yajñakratoḥ' iti viśeṣyate |
tatra deśakālakartṛdravyāṇi na vidhīyante, kiṃtvanuśrūyante |
kutaḥ |
prāptatvāt |
na hi deśādibhirvinā prayogaḥ saṃbhavati |
ator'thāpattyā tatprāptiḥ- iti cet |

children.translated_text: that is not correct.
The obtaining of level ground and the like through implication is merely optionality,
because uneven ground and the like are also possible.

children.text: tato yasminpakṣe prāptirnāsti tasminpakṣe samadeśādayo vidhīyante || MJaiNyC_4,2.17-18 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the [alternative] where the obtaining does not exist, level ground and the like are enjoined [as restrictive rules]. || MJaiNyC_4,2.17-18 ||

This is recorded: 'same darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeta' (one should sacrifice with the new- and full-moon [offerings] on level ground), 'prācīnapravaṇe vaiśvadevena yajeta' (one should sacrifice with the Vaiśvadeva [offering] on a slope facing east), 'paurṇamāsyāṃ paurṇamāsyā yajeta' (one should sacrifice on the full-moon day with the full-moon offering), 'amāvāsyāyām amāvāsyayā yajeta' (one should sacrifice on the new-moon day with the new-moon offering), 'paśubandhasya yajñakratoḥ ṣaḍ ṛtvijaḥ' (for the animal-binding sacrifice, six priests), 'darśapūrṇamāsayor yajñakratvoś catvāra ṛtvijaḥ' (for the new- and full-moon sacrifices, four priests), 'cāturmāsyānāṃ yajñakratūnāṃ pañcartvijaḥ' (for the seasonal sacrifices, five priests), 'agnihotrasya yajñakratoreka ṛtvik' (for the Agnihotra sacrifice, one priest), 'saumyasyādhvarasya yajñakratoḥ saptadaśa ṛtvijaḥ' (for the Soma sacrifice, seventeen priests), 'somena yajeta' (one should sacrifice with Soma). The word 'kratu' also applies to mental meditation. Because in 'sa kratuṃ kurvīta, manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīraḥ' (he should perform the kratu, [the self is] mind-made, with prāṇa as body), meditation is enjoined by the word 'kratu.' To exclude that, it is qualified as 'yajñakratu' (sacrificial kratu). Therein, place, time, agent, and substance are not being enjoined but merely restated (anuśrūyante). Why? Because they are already obtained. For performance is not possible without place and the like, hence they are obtained by implication (arthāpatti) — if so argued,
(In the tenth [adhikaraṇa], on the restrictive-rule nature of the injunction of substance-qualities, the sūtra is:)
Similarly, the scriptural statement of a quality in substances, because of the connection with the origination. / Jaim_4,2.25 /
START MJaiNy 4,2.19
He composes the tenth adhikaraṇa —
'A white [animal] should be seized [for Vāyu]' — is this a restatement (anuvāda) of whiteness, or an injunction? The first;
since whiteness is [already] obtained through the substance, it is restricted as before. // MJaiNy_4,2.19 //
This is recorded: 'vāyavyaṃ śvaitam ālabheta bhūtikāmaḥ' (one desiring prosperity should seize a white [animal] for Vāyu).

children.text: tatra śvaityaguṇasya dravyanirapekṣasya kriyānvayābhāvāddravyasahitasya tadanvaye dravyanirapekṣasya kriyānvayābhāvāddravyasahitasya tadanvaye dravyavidhinaivā'varjanīyatayā tatprāpteranuvādaḥ śvaityasya- iti cet |
children.translated_text: Therein — since the quality of whiteness, being independent of the substance, has no connection with the action [directly], and since in its connection [with the action] it requires the substance, it is inevitably included through the substance-injunction itself — hence the whiteness is a restatement — if so argued,
That is not correct.
Because, by the previous reasoning, in order to preclude the optional nature [of the alternative], the restrictive injunction (<s>niyamavidhi</s>) is accepted. || MJaiNyC_4,2.19 ||
And in the preparatory process (<s>saṃskāra</s>), because the principal [rite] is predominant [therein]. / Jaim_4,2.26 /
(In the eleventh [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the restrictive-injunction-nature of the enjoinment of the husking (<s>avaghāta</s>) and other preparatory processes, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)
START MJaiNy 4,2.20
He composes the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In husking (<s>avaghāta</s>) also, there is a restriction — as in [the case of] place and the like; by that,
it is employed by the principal [rite]; the connection [is established] from the statement of the procedure (<s>prakriyā</s>). // MJaiNy_4,2.20 //

children.text: yathā deśakālakartṛdravyāṇāṃ pakṣe prāptau niyamo vihitaḥ, evamavaghāto 'pi taṇḍulaniṣpattyartha lokataḥ prāpte 'pi pākṣikanakhavidalanādivyāvṛttaye niyamyate |

children.translated_text: And when the husking is [thus] enjoined, it is employed by the principal [rite] — the <s>Āgneya</s> and other offerings.
Nor should it be argued that it is not employed due to the absence of connection [with the principal].
Because the connection is established by [the husking] being recited in the context of the principal offering.

children.text: tasmāt- avaghātādayo vidhīyante pradhānena prayujyante ca || MJaiNyC_4,2.20 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — the husking and the like are enjoined [as restrictions] and are employed by the principal [rite]. || MJaiNyC_4,2.20 ||

Just as in the case of place, time, performer, and material, a restriction is enjoined when an alternative is [otherwise] available, similarly, husking (<s>avaghāta</s>) — even though already available from ordinary practice for the purpose of producing rice grains — is restricted in order to exclude the alternative methods such as splitting with fingernails and the like.
(In the twelfth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on determining the nature of <s>yāga</s> (offering) and <s>homa</s> (oblation), <s>sūtras</s> 27-28:)

The [word] '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices), in the injunction, [denotes] the aggregate of material (<s>dravya</s>), deity (<s>devatā</s>), and action (<s>kriyā</s>), because of the purposefulness [arising only] in the aggregate. / Jaim_4,2.27 /

children.text: tadukte śravaṇāj juhotir āsecanādhikaḥ syāt / Jaim_4,2.28 /
children.translated_text: Since, when that [<s>yāga</s>] is stated, '<s>juhoti</s>' (he offers) is [also] heard, [<s>homa</s>] would be [<s>yāga</s>] with the addition of pouring. / Jaim_4,2.28 /
START MJaiNy 4,2.21-23
He composes the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Are the natures of <s>yāga</s> (offering), <s>homa</s> (oblation), and <s>dāna</s> (gift) indeterminable or determinable?

children.text: tyāgādādyo yajistyāgaḥ prakṣepo homa iṣyate // MJaiNy_4,2.21 //
children.translated_text: From [the element of] relinquishment (<s>tyāga</s>), the first [view holds]; '<s>yaj</s>' (to sacrifice) means relinquishment; the casting [into fire] is <s>homa</s> — this is accepted. // MJaiNy_4,2.21 //
The expectation of the word <s>yāga</s> is satisfied by relinquishment alone;
since the injunction of <s>homa</s> is subsequent to <s>yāga</s>, [<s>homa</s>] culminates in the casting [into fire]. // MJaiNy_4,2.22 //

children.text: svīyaṃ dravyaṃ parityajya parakīyaṃ yathā bhavet /
children.translated_text: Having relinquished one's own property so that it becomes another's,

children.text: tathā saṃpādanaṃ dānaṃ tyāge 'pyeṣāmiyaṃ bhidā // MJaiNy_4,2.23 //
children.translated_text: such effecting is <s>dāna</s> (gift); in [the element of] relinquishment as well, this is the distinction among these [three]. // MJaiNy_4,2.23 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate- 'somena yajeta' agnihotraṃ juhoti' 'hiraṇyamātreyāya dadāti' iti |
tatra yāga-homa-dāna-śabdānāmarthā na nirūpayituṃ śakyante |
triṣvapi dravyatyāgasya sadbhāvāt |
tato vidheyānāmarthānāṃ pradhānabhūtānāmanirṇayāt, itaratra vidhyanuvādavivekaḥ pūrvokto vyarthaḥ- iti cet |
maivam |
devatāmuddiśya dravyatyāgo yāgaḥ |
tyaktasya vahnau prakṣepo homaḥ |
svakīyadravyasya svatvanivṛttipūrvakaṃ parasvatvāpādanaṃ dānam |

children.translated_text: Thus, these terms are well-determined.

children.text: 'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta' itivihitasya yāgasyopari 'caturavattaṃ juhoti' iti homasya vidhānāt 'tyāgamātrātmako yāgaḥ, prakṣepādhiko homaḥ' ityavagamyate |
children.translated_text: Since the injunction of <s>homa</s> — '<s>caturavattaṃ juhoti</s>' (he offers four cuttings) — is made subsequent to the enjoined <s>yāga</s> in '<s>darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta</s>' (one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the new- and full-moon offerings), it is understood that '<s>yāga</s> is [constituted by] mere relinquishment (<s>tyāga</s>), and <s>homa</s> is [<s>yāga</s>] with the addition of casting [into fire].'

children.text: yatra tu yajatyādipadaṃ na śrutam, kiṃtu 'āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaḥ' ityetāvadave śrutam, tatrāpyuddeśyāyā devatāyāstvajanīyadravyasya ca śrutatvāduddeśatvāgarūpo yāgo 'thasiddhaḥ |
children.translated_text: But where the word '<s>yajati</s>' and the like is not heard — where only '<s>āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaḥ</s>' (the <s>Āgneya</s> [offering] on eight potsherds) is heard — even there, since the deity to whom [the offering is] directed and the material to be relinquished are heard, the <s>yāga</s>, whose nature is directing [the offering] to the designated [deity], is automatically established.

children.text: tasmāt- pradhānavidheyānāṃ yāgādīnāṃ sunirūpitatvādvidhiviveko na vyarthaḥ || MJaiNyC_4,2.21-23 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — since <s>yāga</s> and the like, which are the principal objects of injunction, are well-determined, the distinction of injunction [and restatement] is not pointless. || MJaiNyC_4,2.21-23 ||

This is recited: '<s>somena yajeta</s>' (he should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>), '<s>agnihotraṃ juhoti</s>' (he offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>), '<s>hiraṇyam ātreyāya dadāti</s>' (he gives gold to the descendant of <s>Atri</s>). Therein, the meanings of the words <s>yāga</s>, <s>homa</s>, and <s>dāna</s> cannot be determined. Because in all three, the relinquishment of material is present. Therefore, since the principal meanings that are to be enjoined are undetermined, the previously stated distinction between injunction and restatement regarding the other [elements] would be pointless — if so it is argued, that is not correct. The relinquishment of material directed toward a deity is <s>yāga</s> (offering). The casting of the relinquished [material] into fire is <s>homa</s> (oblation). Effecting the transfer of ownership of one's own material — preceded by the cessation of one's own ownership — to another is <s>dāna</s> (gift).
(In the thirteenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass) being common to the <s>Ātithya</s> and other [rites], <s>sūtras</s> 29-30:)

children.text: vidheḥ karmāpavargitvād arthāntare vidhipradeśaḥ syāt / Jaim_4,2.29 /
children.translated_text: Since the injunction terminates with the [particular] ritual action, there would be a [separate] injunctive reference for a different purpose. / Jaim_4,2.29 /

children.text: api votpattisaṃyogād arthasaṃbandho 'viśiṣṭānāṃ prayogaikatvahetuḥ syāt / Jaim_4,2.30 /
children.translated_text: Or, because of the connection at origination, the connection with the purpose [is such that] it would be the cause of a single employment for the non-differentiated [elements]. / Jaim_4,2.30 /
START MJaiNy 4,2.24-25
He composes the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass) used in the <s>Ātithya</s> (hospitality offering) — is this an extension (<s>atideśa</s>) to the <s>Upasads</s>,
or an injunction of commonality? The first [view holds]: because [the <s>barhis</s>] specific to [the <s>Ātithya</s>] is transferred [to the other rites]. // MJaiNy_4,2.24 //
Since the <s>barhis</s> appears unified by the <s>śruti</s>, the figurative interpretation required for extension is not [needed];
this <s>barhis</s> is employed for the <s>Ātithya</s>, the <s>Upasads</s>, and [the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>]. // MJaiNy_4,2.25 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate- 'yadātithyāyāṃ barhiḥ, tadupasadām, tadagnīṣomīyasya ca' iti |
krītaṃ somaṃ śakaṭe 'vasthāpyaprācīnavaṃśaṃ pratyānayane 'bhimukho yāmiṣṭiṃ nirvapati seyamātithyā |
tata ūrdhva triṣu dineṣvanuṣṭhīyamānā upasadaḥ |
aupavasathye dine 'nuṣṭheyo 'gnīṣobhīyaḥ |
tatra- ātithyeṣṭau vihitaṃ yadbarhiḥ, tadyadi tasyā iṣṭerācchidyopasatsu vidhīyeta, tadānīmātithyāyāṃ vidhānamanarthakaṃ syāt |
yadi ca tatropayuktamitaratra vidhīyeta, tadā viniyuktaviniyogarūpo virodhaḥ syāt |
tasmāt- ātithyābarhiṣo ye dharmā aśvabālatvādayaḥ, te dharmā upasatsūpasaṃhriyante- ityatideśaparaṃ vākyam- iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- barhiḥ śabdasya dharmātideśatve lakṣaṇā prasajyeta |

children.translated_text: But from the <s>śruti</s>, the unity of the <s>barhis</s> used in the <s>Ātithya</s>, <s>Upasads</s>, and <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> is directly apparent.
Therefore, commonality is what should be enjoined here.

children.text: ātithyārtha yadbarhirupādīyate tanna kevalamātithyārtham, kiṃtūpasadarthamagnīṣomīyārtha copādeyamiti vidhivākyasyārthaḥ |
children.translated_text: The meaning of the injunctive sentence is: the <s>barhis</s> procured for the <s>Ātithya</s> is not for the <s>Ātithya</s> alone, but should also be employed for the <s>Upasads</s> and the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s>.
Therefore — all three — the <s>Ātithya</s>, the <s>Upasads</s>, and the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> — are the employing agents of this <s>barhis</s>. || MJaiNyC_4,2.24-25 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> it is heard: '<s>yad ātithyāyāṃ barhiḥ, tad upasadām, tad agnīṣomīyasya ca</s>' (the <s>barhis</s> [used] in the <s>Ātithya</s> [is also used] for the <s>Upasads</s>, and for the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> as well). The <s>Ātithya</s> is the <s>Iṣṭi</s> (offering) performed when, having placed the purchased <s>Soma</s> on the cart, one faces toward the <s>Prācīnavaṃśa</s> [shed] and offers the bringing-[of-<s>Soma</s>] offering. Thereafter, the <s>Upasads</s> are performed over three days. The <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [animal sacrifice] is performed on the day before the pressing (<s>aupavasathya</s>). Therein — if the <s>barhis</s> enjoined in the <s>Ātithya Iṣṭi</s> were detached from that <s>Iṣṭi</s> and enjoined in the <s>Upasads</s>, then its enjoinment in the <s>Ātithya</s> would be purposeless. And if what has been utilized there [in the <s>Ātithya</s>] were enjoined elsewhere, then there would be the contradiction of reassigning what has already been assigned. Therefore — the qualities of the <s>Ātithya</s>'s <s>barhis</s>, such as [having the texture of] horse-tail and the like, are transferred to the <s>Upasads</s> — the sentence is about extension (<s>atideśa</s>) — having arrived at this position, we say: If the word <s>barhis</s> were taken as an extension of qualities, a figurative interpretation would be entailed.

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīye jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistare caturtādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> in the illustrious <s>Mādhavīya Jaiminīya-Nyāyamālā-Vistara</s>.
Now begins the third <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s>.
(In the first [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>kratvārtha</s>-nature (sacrifice-serving-nature) of material-preparation rites, <s>sūtras</s> 1-3:)

children.text: dravyasaṃskārakarmasu parārthatvāt phalaśrutir arthavādaḥ syāt / Jaim_4,3.1 /
children.translated_text: In rites that prepare the materials, since they serve another's purpose, the statement of fruit would be <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage). / Jaim_4,3.1 /
And from the origination, because the principal [rite] is predominant therein. / Jaim_4,3.2 /
But the fruit [applies] when that [principal rite] is predominant. / Jaim_4,3.3 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.1-2
He composes the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> of the third <s>pāda</s> —
Because the <s>juhū</s> (offering ladle) is made of <s>Palāśa</s> wood, [the person] does not hear reproach; by the anointing,

children.text: vairidṛgvṛñjanaṃ, varma prayājaiḥ, puruṣāya kim // MJaiNy_4,3.1 //
children.translated_text: he overcomes the rival's [evil] eye; the <s>prayājas</s> [serve as] armor — are these for the person? // MJaiNy_4,3.1 //

children.text: kratave vāgrimo mānātphalasya na hi sādhyatā /
children.translated_text: Or for the sacrifice? The first [view]: since a valid means [establishes the fruit for the person]; but the fruit cannot be [independently] accomplished;

children.text: vibhāti kratave tasmādarthavādaḥ phalaṃ bhavet // MJaiNy_4,3.2 //
children.translated_text: it is apparent [that they are] for the sacrifice; therefore, the fruit[-statement] would be <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory). // MJaiNy_4,3.2 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate- 'yasya parṇamayī juhūrbhavati na sa pāpaṃ ślokaṃ śṛṇoti' 'yadāṅkte cakṣureva bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte' 'yatprayājānuyājā ijyante varma vā etadyajñasya kriyate, varma yajamānasya bhrātṛvyābhibhūtyai' iti |
tatra- yajjuhūprakṛtibhūtaṃ parṇadravyam, yaścāñjanena cakṣuṣaḥ saṃskāraḥ, yacca prayājānuyājarūpaṃ varma tacci dvayaṃ puruṣārthatvena vidhīyate |
kutaḥ |
pāpaślokaśravaṇādirāhityādeḥ puruṣasaṃbandhiphalasya pratibhānāt- iti cet |
maivam |
phalaṃ hi sādhyaṃ bhavati |
na cātra sādhyatā pratibhāsate |
'na śṛṇoti vṛṅkte, varma kriyate, iti vartamānatvanirdeśāt |

children.translated_text: Therefore, these are injunctions that are <s>kratvārtha</s> (for the sacrifice).
Therein, the <s>Palāśa</s>-nature [of the ladle], although studied without a [specific ritual] context, is connected with the sacrifice by the sentence.

children.text: saṃskāravarmaṇostu prakaraṇena kratvarthānāṃ tu kratuniṣpādanavyatirekeṇa phalākāṅkṣāyā abhāvādvartamānanirdeśasva vipariṇāmaṃ kṛtvāpi phalaṃ kalpayituṃ na śakyam |
children.translated_text: But for the preparatory process and the armor, since rites that are <s>kratvārtha</s> have no expectation of fruit beyond the accomplishment of the sacrifice, even by transforming the present-tense indication [into future sense], a fruit cannot be postulated.
Therefore — the freedom from hearing reproach and the like, which create the false impression of [independent] fruitfulness, are <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passages). || MJaiNyC_4,3.1-2 ||

This is recited: '<s>yasya parṇamayī juhūr bhavati na sa pāpaṃ ślokaṃ śṛṇoti</s>' (he whose <s>juhū</s> ladle is made of <s>Palāśa</s> wood does not hear reproach), '<s>yad āṅkte cakṣur eva bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte</s>' (when he anoints [the eyes], he indeed overcomes the rival's eye), '<s>yat prayājānuyājā ijyante varma vā etad yajñasya kriyate, varma yajamānasya bhrātṛvyābhibhūtyai</s>' (when the <s>prayājas</s> and <s>anuyājas</s> are offered, this armor of the sacrifice is made, armor for the sacrificer to overcome the rival). Therein — the <s>Palāśa</s> wood that is the material of the <s>juhū</s>, the preparatory process (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the eye through anointing, and the armor in the form of the <s>prayājas</s> and <s>anuyājas</s> — these are enjoined as <s>puruṣārtha</s>. Why? Because the fruit connected with the person — such as freedom from hearing reproach — is apparent — if so it is argued, that is not correct. For a fruit must be something to be accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>). But here, the character of being accomplishable is not apparent. Because [the texts] state [the fruit] in the present tense: 'does not hear,' 'overcomes,' 'is made.'
(In the second [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the non-permanent-purpose-nature of occasional (<s>naimittika</s>) [rites], the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: naimittike vikāratvāt kratupradhānam anyat syāt / Jaim_4,3.4 /
children.translated_text: In an occasional [rite], since it is a modification (<s>vikāra</s>), another [material] with the sacrifice as principal would [apply]. / Jaim_4,3.4 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.3-4
He composes the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Should one who desires [cattle] carry [water] in an earthen [vessel]? In the permanent [rite] also this, or something else?
Since there is expectation and proximity, the earthen [vessel applies] in the permanent [rite] too. // MJaiNy_4,3.3 //
Because of being for an optional purpose (<s>kāmārtha</s>), it is unsuitable [for the permanent rite]; and since
the expectation is removed by what is enjoined in general, the other [vessel] would serve the permanent purpose. // MJaiNy_4,3.4 //

children.text:
'apaḥ praṇayati' iti praṇayanasya nityapyoge 'pi mṛnmayapātrameva sādhanam |
kṛtaḥ |
nitye 'pi pātratvā'phaṅkṣitatvāt |
na ca lokasidhdaṃ kiṃcitpātramupādīyate-iti vācyam |
aupte karmaṇyatyantamaśrutācchrutasya saṃnihitatvāt- iti prāpte-
brūmaḥ- kāmārtha mṛnmayamāmnātam |
tacca sati kāme yogyam |
na hi pākṣikaṃ kāmaṃ nimittīkṛtya pravṛttaṃ nityasya yogyaṃ bhavati |
pātrākāṅkṣā tu sāmānyato vihitena nivartate |
'apaḥ praṇayati'iti hi pātraviśeṣamanupanyasya vihitam |
vañcānyathānuparpannaṃ tatpātraṃ kiṃcitsāmānyena kalpayati |
tasmānnityaprayoge tatkāmyaṃ mṛnmartha nānveti, kiṃtvitaratpātraṃ yatkiṃcidupādeyam |
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the permanent employment, the optional (<s>kāmya</s>) earthen [vessel] does not apply; rather, any other vessel whatsoever should be employed.

children.text: -'camasenāpaḥ praṇayet iti nitye pātraṃ vidhīyate-iti vidhīyate |
children.translated_text: '<s>Camasenāpaḥ praṇayet</s>' (one should carry water with the cup) — [by this statement,] a vessel is enjoined for the permanent [rite].
If so it is argued —
then, let the deliberation [on this point] be [considered as] having been completed. || MJaiNyC_4,3.3-4 ||

In '<s>apaḥ praṇayati</s>' (he carries water) — even though the carrying is employed in the permanent [rite], the instrument is the earthen vessel alone. Why? Because in the permanent [rite] too, a vessel is expected. Nor should it be said that some vessel known from ordinary life is to be taken — because in a purely scriptural rite, what is heard [in the texts] takes proximity over what is entirely unheard — having arrived at this position, we say: The earthen [vessel] is recited [in connection with] a desired purpose (<s>kāmārtha</s>). And that is suitable [only] when the desire is present. For what is undertaken on the basis of an optional desire is not suitable for a permanent [rite]. But the expectation of a vessel is removed by what is enjoined in general [terms]. For '<s>apaḥ praṇayati</s>' (he carries water) is enjoined without specifying a particular vessel. And [the expectation of] that vessel — which is not otherwise established — is postulated by general [reasoning] as any [suitable vessel].
(In the third [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the principle of connection-distinctness (<s>saṃyogapṛthaktva</s>), and on curd and the like serving both permanent and occasional purposes, <s>sūtras</s> 5-7:)
But when a single [substance] serves both [purposes], there is distinctness of connection. / Jaim_4,3.5 /
If it be said [that it is] a remainder (<s>śeṣa</s>) — / Jaim_4,3.6 /
No, because of the distinctness of purpose. / Jaim_4,3.7 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.5
He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
With curd, for one desiring [strong] senses — but in the permanent [rite], should it be something else, or that very curd?
Something else, by the previous [reasoning]; but no — because of the distinctness of the connection. // MJaiNy_4,3.5 //

children.text:
agnihotre śrūyate- 'dadhnendriyakāmasya juhuyāt' iti |
tatra- dadhnaḥ kānyatvānnitye 'gnihotre pūrvanyāyena taddadhi na prayoktavyam |
kiṃtvanyadeva kiṃciddravyam- iti cet |
maivam |

children.translated_text: Because in the other sentence '<s>dadhnā juhoti</s>' (he offers with curd), the connection with the optional desire is set aside and curd is enjoined in connection with the permanent offering.

children.text: tasmāt- ekasyāpi dadhno vākyadvayena nityatvaṃ kāmyatvaṃ cāviruddham |
children.translated_text: Therefore — even for a single [substance such as] curd, the permanence and the optional nature, [being established] by two [different] sentences, are not contradictory.
Similarly, in the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal sacrifice — '<s>khādire badhnāti</s>' (he ties [the animal] to a <s>Khadira</s> [post]) and '<s>khādiraṃ vīryakāmasya yūpaṃ
kurvīta</s>' (one desiring strength should make the sacrificial post of <s>Khadira</s> wood) — should be cited as an example. || MJaiNyC_4,3.5 ||

In the <s>Agnihotra</s> it is heard: '<s>dadhnā indriyakāmasya juhuyāt</s>' (one should offer with curd for one desiring [strong] senses). Therein — since the curd serves an optional purpose (<s>kāmyārtha</s>), in the permanent <s>Agnihotra</s>, by the previous reasoning, that very curd should not be used; rather, some other material [should be used] — if so it is argued, that is not correct.
(In the fourth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the sacrifice-serving-nature (<s>kratudharma</s>) of the milk-vow and the like, <s>sūtras</s> 8-9:)

children.text: dravyāṇāṃ tu kriyārthānāṃ saṃskāraḥ kratudharmaḥ syāt / Jaim_4,3.8 /
children.translated_text: But for materials that serve the purpose of the action, the preparatory process (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is a property of the sacrifice. / Jaim_4,3.8 /
It should stand separately [from the person]. / Jaim_4,3.9 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.6
He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'The milk-vow (<s>payovrata</s>) is for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' — is this for the person, or for the sacrifice?
The first [view]: because of its connection with the person; but no — because of fruitlessness [for the person], it is a remainder of the sacrifice (<s>kratuśeṣa</s>). // MJaiNy_4,3.6 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome dīkṣitasyānnabhojanābhāve vratamāmnāyate- 'payo vrataṃ brāhmaṇatva, yavāgū rājanyasya, āmikṣā vaiśyasya' iti |
tatra- brāhmaṇādipuruṣasaṃyogādetadvrataṃ puruṣārtham- iti cet-

children.translated_text: that is not correct.
Because, unlike [in the case of] senses, strength, and the like, no fruit is stated here.
But the <s>kratuśeṣa</s>-nature (remainder-of-sacrifice-nature) is understood from the context.
The persons — <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the like — are mentioned as occasioning factors (<s>nimitta</s>) for the determination of specific materials. || MJaiNyC_4,3.6 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, in the absence of [regular] food for the consecrated person (<s>dīkṣita</s>), a vow is recited: '<s>payo vrataṃ brāhmaṇasya, yavāgū rājanyasya, āmikṣā vaiśyasya</s>' (milk is the vow-diet of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, gruel that of the <s>Kṣatriya</s>, curdled milk that of the <s>Vaiśya</s>). Therein — since this vow is connected with persons such as the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the like, it is <s>puruṣārtha</s> — if so it is argued,
(In the fifth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], within the <s>Viśvajit</s> principle, on the fruitfulness of the <s>Viśvajit</s> and similar [sacrifices], <s>sūtras</s> 10-12:)

children.text: codanāyāṃ phalāśruteḥ karmamātraṃ vidhīyeta na hy aśabdaṃ pratīyate / Jaim_4,3.10 /
children.translated_text: When in the injunction no fruit is heard, only the ritual action is being enjoined; for what is not expressed by words cannot be understood. / Jaim_4,3.10 /

children.text: api vāmnānasāmarthyāc codanārthena gamyeta, ārthānāṃ hy arthavattvena vacanāni pratīyante, arthato hy asamarthānām ānantarye 'py asaṃbandhas tasmāc chrutyekadeśaḥ / Jaim_4,3.11 /
children.translated_text: Or, by the capacity of the recorded [text], it may be understood through the injunctive meaning — for the statements of meaningful [passages] are understood as having purpose; but for those that are meaningless in substance, even when adjacent, there is no connection — therefore it is a portion of the <s>śruti</s>. / Jaim_4,3.11 /
And the sentence-meaning is like the meaning of a qualifier. / Jaim_4,3.12 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.7
He composes the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Does the <s>Viśvajit</s> sacrifice have no fruit, or does it have one? Not [the former], because of the non-hearing [of fruit];

children.text: bhāvyāpekṣādvidheḥ kalpyaṃ phalaṃ paṃsaḥ pravṛttaye // MJaiNy_4,3.7 //
children.translated_text: since the injunction requires an object (<s>bhāvya</s>), a fruit must be postulated — for the sake of [motivating] activity. // MJaiNy_4,3.7 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate- 'viśvajitā yajeta' iti |
tatra- phalasyāśrutatvānnāsti viśvajidyāge phalam- iti cet |
maivam |
phalasya kalpanīyatvāt |
'viśvajinnāmnā yāgena kuryāt' ityuktā bhāvanā bhāvyamapekṣate |
'kiṃ kuryāt' ityāṅkākṣāyā anivṛtteḥ |

children.translated_text: Therefore, to complete the sentence, some fruit must necessarily be supplied.

children.text: adhyāhṛte ca tatkāminaḥ puruṣasyātra pravṛttyā yāgāmuṣṭhānaṃ sidhyati |
children.translated_text: And when it is supplied, the performance of the sacrifice is accomplished through the activity of a person who desires that [fruit] — giving him the ritual qualification.
Otherwise, due to the absence of ritual qualification, the injunction regarding performance would be purposeless.
Therefore, a fruit must be postulated. || MJaiNyC_4,3.7 ||

This is recorded: '<s>viśvajitā yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice with the <s>Viśvajit</s>). Therein — since no fruit is heard, the <s>Viśvajit</s> sacrifice has no fruit — if so it is argued, that is not correct. Because a fruit must be postulated. The <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force) expressed in 'one should perform with a sacrifice named <s>Viśvajit</s>' requires an object (<s>bhāvya</s>) — because the expectation 'what should one produce?' is not fulfilled [without it].
(In the sixth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], subsumed under the <s>Viśvajit</s> principle, on the <s>Viśvajit</s> and the like having a single fruit, <s>sūtras</s> 13–14:)
That [fruit] serves all purposes, because of the absence of specification. / Jaim_4,3.13 /
Or it is one, because the injunction is one. / Jaim_4,3.14 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.8
He composes the sixth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Should all [types of] fruit be postulated, or a single one? Let it be all, because of the absence of specification;
since the expectation is fulfilled by one alone, multiple [fruits] should not be postulated. // MJaiNy_4,3.8 //
Why?
Because there is no reason to specify 'this alone is its fruit' — if so it is argued,
that is not correct.
Because parsimony (<s>lāghava</s>) itself is the reason for specification. || MJaiNyC_4,3.8 ||
In that <s>Viśvajit</s>, cattle, sons, vigor, sense-faculties, and all such should be postulated as the fruit.
(In the seventh [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], subsumed under the <s>Viśvajit</s> principle, on the <s>Viśvajit</s> and the like having heaven as their fruit, <s>sūtras</s> 15–16:)

children.text: sa svargaḥ syāt sarvān pratyaviśiṣṭatvāt / Jaim_4,3.15 /
children.translated_text: That [fruit] would be heaven, because it is not distinguished for all [persons]. / Jaim_4,3.15 /
And because of the [optative verbal] suffix. / Jaim_4,3.16 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.9
He composes the seventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the single [fruit] just anything, or is it fixed? There is nothing to fix it;
therefore, the first [alternative — it is fixed]: since it is desired by all persons, that [fruit] is heaven itself. // MJaiNy_4,3.9 //

children.text: viśvajiti kalpyamānaṃ yadekaṃ phalaṃ tat 'inameva' iti niyāmakaṃ nāsti |
children.translated_text: The single fruit that is to be postulated for the <s>Viśvajit</s> — there is nothing to fix [it as] 'this one alone.'

children.text: tasmādicchayā kenacitkasmiṃścitphale kalpyamāner'thātsarvaphalatve gauravameva syāt- iti cet |
children.translated_text: Therefore, when it can be postulated by anyone's wish in any fruit, postulating all fruits would simply lead to the burden [of multiplicity] — if so it is argued,
that is not correct.

children.text: svargasya paśvādiphalavadduḥkhamiśritatvābhāvāt, niratiśayasukhatvācca sarvapuruṣāṇāmiṣṭatvātsvarga eva viśvajitaḥ phalam || MJaiNyC_4,3.9 ||
children.translated_text: Because heaven, unlike fruits such as cattle, is not mixed with suffering, and because it is unsurpassed happiness, it is desired by all persons — therefore heaven alone is the fruit of the <s>Viśvajit</s>. || MJaiNyC_4,3.9 ||
(In the eighth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], in the <s>Rātrisatra</s> principle, on the <s>Rātrisatra</s> having as its fruit what is [stated] in the laudatory passage, <s>sūtras</s> 17–19:)
In the sacrifice, the fruit-[statement] is a laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>) [serving the sacrifice] like an accessory — [so says] <s>Kārṣṇājini</s>. / Jaim_4,3.17 /

children.text: phalamātreyo nirdeśād aśrutau hy anumānaṃ syāt / Jaim_4,3.18 /
children.translated_text: The fruit [is as stated] — [so says] <s>Ātreya</s> — because of the indication; for when [a fruit] is not heard, inference would [apply]. / Jaim_4,3.18 /
In accessories, it is praise, because they serve another's purpose. / Jaim_4,3.19 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.10
He composes the eighth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the <s>Rātrisatra</s> for heaven, or for establishment (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>)? The first [alternative, i.e. heaven], here;
as before [in the <s>Viśvajit</s>] it would [be heaven]; but establishment is [directly] heard — therefore it is better than what is unheard. // MJaiNy_4,3.10 //

children.text:
satrakāṇḍe pratyekaṃ śrūyate- 'pratitiṣṭhanti ha vā ete, ya etā rātrīrupayanti' iti, 'brahmavarcasvino 'nnādā bhavanti, ya etā upayanti' iti ca |
dvādaśāhādūrdhvabhāvinastrayodaśarātracaturdaśarātrādayaḥ sarve satraviśeṣāḥ |
trayodaśasaṃkhāyākārātrayo yasminsatraviśeṣe so 'yaṃ trayodaśarātrāḥ, iti samudāyaprādhānyenaikavacanāntatayā prāyeṇa nirdeśo bhavati |
kvacittu samudādhināṃ rātriśabdenā'mnāyate |
tadyathā- 'ta etā viśatiṃ rātrīrapaśyat' iti tādṛśe rātrisatre viśvajinnyāyena svargaḥ phalatvena kalpanīyaḥ- iti prāpte-
children.translated_text: For example: '<s>ta etā viṃśatiṃ rātrīr apaśyat</s>' (he perceived these twenty nights) — in such a <s>Rātrisatra</s>, heaven should be postulated as the fruit by the <s>Viśvajit</s> principle — having arrived at this position,

children.text: brūmaḥ- asya rātrisatravidheḥ stāvaker'thavāde pratiṣṭhā śrutā |
children.translated_text: we say: In the laudatory passage (<s>stāvaka arthavāda</s>) of this <s>Rātrisatra</s> injunction, 'establishment' (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) is heard.
And that [establishment], in this sentence, is more proximate than heaven, which is completely unheard [in this context].

children.text: tasmāt- 'pratiṣṭhākāmo rātrisatraṃ kuryāt' ityevaṃ pratiṣṭhaiva phalatvena kalpanīyā || MJaiNyC_4,3.10 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, 'one who desires establishment should perform the <s>Rātrisatra</s>' — thus, establishment alone should be postulated as the fruit. || MJaiNyC_4,3.10 ||

In the <s>Satra</s> section, it is heard individually: '<s>pratitiṣṭhanti ha vā ete, ya etā rātrīr upayanti</s>' (they indeed become established, those who perform these nights), and '<s>brahmavarcasvino 'nnādā bhavanti, ya etā upayanti</s>' (they become possessors of Brahmanical splendor and food-eaters, those who perform these). All the <s>satra</s> varieties from thirteen nights, fourteen nights, and so on, which follow after the twelve-day [<s>satra</s>], are special <s>satras</s>. The <s>satra</s> variety consisting of thirteen nights in number is a 'thirteen-night [<s>satra</s>]' — and it is generally referred to in the singular, with primacy given to the aggregate. But sometimes the aggregate [of nights] is referred to by the word '<s>rātri</s>' (night).
(In the ninth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on optional (<s>kāmya</s>) rites having the stated desired fruit, <s>sūtras</s> 20–24:)

children.text: kāmye karmaṇi nityaḥ svargo yathā yajñāṅge kratvarthaḥ / Jaim_4,3.20 /
children.translated_text: In an optional rite, heaven is invariable, just as the sacrifice's purpose [is invariable] in an accessory of the rite. / Jaim_4,3.20 /
And when the occasion (<s>kāraṇa</s>) has passed, because of the restriction. / Jaim_4,3.21 /
Or the [stated] desire is impelled by connection with that [rite]. / Jaim_4,3.22 /
In accessories, because it is a qualifying attribute. / Jaim_4,3.23 /
And when the occasion has passed, the restriction is for that purpose. / Jaim_4,3.24 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.11
He composes the ninth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Are both the heard and unheard [fruits present]? In the <s>Saurya</s> (solar) [rite], a single heard [fruit] suffices for the activity of all;
the first [alternative — both]; but no — because the expectation of fruit is fulfilled by the heard [fruit] alone. // MJaiNy_4,3.11 //

children.text:
'saurya caruṃ rnivapedbrahmavarcasakāmaḥ' ityatra brahmavarcasaṃ phalaṃ śrutam |
svargo 'śrutaṃ phalam |
tadubhayamapyabhyupeyam |
tathā sati svargasya sarvairapekṣyamāṇatvātsarveṣāṃ tatra pravṛttirlabhyeta- iti cet |
children.translated_text: This being so, since heaven is desired by all, the activity of all [persons] in that [rite] would be obtained — if so it is argued,
that is not correct.

children.text: śrutena brahmavarcasaphalenaiva nirākāṅkṣe vidhivākye viśvajinnyāyena svargaphalakalpānāyā asaṃbhavāt |
children.translated_text: Because when the injunctive sentence is free from expectation through the heard fruit of Brahmanical splendor alone, the postulation of heaven as a fruit by the <s>Viśvajit</s> principle is impossible.
Therefore, only the heard fruit [applies]. || MJaiNyC_4,3.11 ||

In '<s>saurya caruṃ nirvapedbrahmavarcasakāmaḥ</s>' (one desiring Brahmanical splendor should offer a <s>caru</s> for <s>Sūrya</s>), the Brahmanical splendor (<s>brahmavarcasa</s>) is the heard fruit. Heaven is the unheard fruit. Both should be accepted.
(In the tenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], subsumed under the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> principle, on the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the like serving all desires, <s>sūtras</s> 25–26:)
It serves all desires, because of the desires [stated for] the accessories, from the context. / Jaim_4,3.25 /
Or [the statements are] indication of fruit, because of the connection with the primary word. / Jaim_4,3.26 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.12-13
He composes the tenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Does the <s>Darśa</s> (new-moon) and the like serve all desires, or is the [statement about] fruit an injunction or a restatement?
The desire stated in the accessories and sub-accessories — because of the absence of an injunction, it is [merely] restated. // MJaiNy_4,3.12 //
Relying on the established result of the origination-injunction, and in the postulation of injunctive force,
by conveying the connection with the fruit, this would be an injunction regarding the fruit. // MJaiNy_4,3.13 //

children.text:
idamāmnīyate- 'ekasmai vā anyā iṣṭayaḥ kāmāyā'hriyante, sarvebhyo darśapūrṇamāsau' iti |
'ekasmai vā anye yajñakratavaḥ kāmāyā'hriyante, sarvebhyo jyotiṣṭomaḥ' iti |
tatra- 'sarvebhyaḥ' ityanena vākyena darśapūrṇamāsayorna phale vidhiḥ |
vidhāyakasya liṅṅāderbhāvanāvācina ākhyātasya cābhāvāt |
anuvādastu bhaviṣyati |
sarvakāmānāṃ prāptatvāt |
na ca- 'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta' iti vidhānātsvarga eva prāpto na tu kāmāntaram- iti vācyam |
aṅgopāṅgakāmānāmapi prāptatvāt |
sāmidhenyo darśapūrṇamāsayoraṅgam |
tatra kāmāḥ śrṛyante- 'ekaviṃśatimanubrūyātpratiṣṭhākāmasya, caturviṃśatimanubrūyādbrahmavarcasakāmasya' iti |
tathā sāṃnāyyayāgasya dohanamaṅgam |
tatsādhanaṃ vatsāpākaraṇamupāṅgam |
tatra palāśaśākhāharaṇe kāma āmnātaḥ- 'yaḥ kāmayeta- paśumānsyāt- iti, bahuparṇā tasmai bahuśākhāmāharet |

children.translated_text: It makes him possessor of cattle.'

children.text: ta ete sarve kāmā anūdyante- iti prāpte, brūmaḥ- mā bhūtāmasminvākye vidhibhāvane |
children.translated_text: All these desires are [merely] restated — having arrived at this position, we say: Even if there is no injunctive force in this sentence,

children.text: tathāpyutpattivākyasiddhite āśritya tādarthyavācinyā caturthyā phalasaṃyogo bodhyate |
children.translated_text: nonetheless, relying on the established result of the origination-sentence, the connection with the fruit is conveyed by the dative case expressing purpose.
Therefore, this is an injunction regarding the fruit. || MJaiNyC_4,3.12-13 ||

This is recorded: '<s>ekasmai vā anyā iṣṭayaḥ kāmāyāhriyante, sarvebhyo darśapūrṇamāsau</s>' (other <s>iṣṭis</s> are performed for a single desire, [but] the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> for all [desires]). '<s>Ekasmai vā anye yajñakratavaḥ kāmāyāhriyante, sarvebhyo jyotiṣṭomaḥ</s>' (other sacrificial rites are performed for a single desire, [but] the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> for all [desires]). Therein — by the sentence '<s>sarvebhyaḥ</s>' (for all), there is no injunction of fruit for the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> — because the injunctive optative or other [verb forms] of the <s>bhāvanā</s>-expressing kind are absent. But it would be a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) — because all desires are already obtained. Nor should one say that since heaven alone is obtained from the injunction '<s>darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta</s>' (one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>), no other desire is obtained — because the desires [stated for] the accessories and sub-accessories are also obtained. The <s>sāmidhenīs</s> are an accessory of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. Therein, desires are heard: '<s>ekaviṃśatim anubrūyāt pratiṣṭhākāmasya</s>' (one should recite twenty-one for one desiring establishment), '<s>caturviṃśatim anubrūyād brahmavarcasakāmasya</s>' (one should recite twenty-four for one desiring Brahmanical splendor). Likewise, milking is an accessory of the <s>sānnāyya</s> sacrifice. The removal of the calf — which is the means for that [milking] — is a sub-accessory. Therein, a desire is recorded for the bringing of the <s>palāśa</s> branch: '<s>yaḥ kāmayeta — paśumān syāt — iti, bahuparṇā tasmai bahuśākhām āharet</s>' (one who desires — may I have cattle — for him, one should bring a many-branched [branch] from a many-leaved [<s>palāśa</s> tree]).

children.text: (ekādaśe darśapūrṇamāsanyāyāntargate darśapūrṇamāsādīnāṃ pratiphalaṃ pṛthaganuṣṭhānādhikaraṇe, yogasiddhinyāye ca sūtre 27-28)
children.translated_text: (In the eleventh [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], subsumed under the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> principle, on the separate performance of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the like for each fruit, the <s>yogasiddhi</s> [principle of individual accomplishment], <s>sūtras</s> 27–28:)
Therein, all [fruits are accomplished together], because of the absence of specification. / Jaim_4,3.27 /
Or individual accomplishment (<s>yogasiddhi</s>), because the meaning is not connected with origination [simultaneously]. / Jaim_4,3.28 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.14-15
He composes the eleventh <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
The <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> too serves all purposes; all [fruits arise] from a single performance,
or [should it] give [fruits] from separate performances? The first [alternative], because of the absence of specification for a single [performance]. // MJaiNy_4,3.14 //
Each independent fruit has its own means of accomplishment;

children.text: coditaṃ tena kāmāste paryāyeṇa bhavantyamī // MJaiNy_4,3.15 //
children.translated_text: enjoined [as such], those desires are [fulfilled] in turns. // MJaiNy_4,3.15 //

children.text:
yathā darśapūrṇamāsau sarvakāmārthau, tathā jyotiṣṭomaśca sarvakāmārtha iti pūrvādhikaraṇenaiva siddham |
tatrobhayatra kāmā naimittikāḥ |
jyotiṣṭomādisvarūpaṃ nicittam |
tacca sarveṣu kāmeṣvaviśiṣṭam |
na hi nimittasādhāraṇye sati naimittikānāṃ paryāyo bhavati |
vahnisāmīpye sati dāhaprakāśayoḥ paryāyādarśanāt |
tasmājyotiṣṭome sakṛdanuṣṭhite satyekaṃ phalaṃ yathā niṣpadyate, tathā phalāntarāṇāmapi vārayitumaśakyatvādyugapatsarvaphalasiddhiḥ- iti prāpte-
brūmaḥ- nahi jyotiṣṭoyaṃ nimittīkṛtya kāmā vidhīyante |
kāmānāmananuṣṭheyatvāt |
kiṃ tarhi- puruṣasya svata eva prāptānkāmānuddiśya tatsādhanatvenaiva jyotiṣṭomo vidhīyate |
yadyapi 'sarvebhyaḥ kāmebhyaḥ' iti svargapaśvādiphalānāmekenaiva śabdenoddiśyamānatvātsāhityaṃ pratibhāti, tathāpi na tadasyi |
uddeśyagatatvena sāhityasyāvivakṣitatvāt |
na ca śabdataḥ sāhityaniyamābhāve 'pyekakarmaphalatvādarthataḥ sāhityam- iti vācyam |
svargapaśvādīnāṃ parasparanirapekṣāṇāmeva phalatvāt |
tasmādekaikasya phalasya sādhanatvena karma codyate |
ata eva 'sarvebhyaḥ' iti nirdeśopapattiḥ |
anyathā hi sāhityaniyamānmilitamidamekameva phalaṃ saṃpannamiti sarvaśabdo nopapadyate |
tasmādyadā yatphalaṃ kāmyam, tadā tatsiddhye jyotiṣṭomaḥ prayoktavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, when a particular fruit is desired, the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> should be performed for the accomplishment of that.

children.text: ekamapi sadvṛṣṭyādiphalaṃ yadā yadā kāmyate, tadā tadā kārīrīṣṭiḥ punaḥ punaḥ prayujyati |
children.translated_text: Even for a single [fruit] such as rain, whenever it is desired, the <s>Kārīrī-iṣṭi</s> is performed again and again.
How much more so [is it clear] that when the fruits differ, the performances differ.
Therefore, there is a separate performance for each fruit. || MJaiNyC_4,3.14-15 ||

Just as the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> serves all desires, so too the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> serves all desires — this is established by the preceding <s>adhikaraṇa</s> itself. In both cases, the desires are occasioned [by the rites]. The essential nature of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like is fixed. And that [nature] is not different for all desires. For when the occasion is common, there is no alternation among the occasioned [results] — just as when fire is near, burning and illumination are not observed to alternate. Therefore, when the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is performed once, just as one fruit is produced, so too, since other fruits cannot be prevented, all fruits are accomplished simultaneously — having arrived at this position, we say: The desires are not enjoined by taking the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> as the occasion — because desires are not things to be performed. Rather, the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is enjoined as the means of accomplishing those desires that arise spontaneously in the person. Although from '<s>sarvebhyaḥ kāmebhyaḥ</s>' (for all desires) it appears that the fruits — heaven, cattle, and the like — are indicated together by a single expression, nevertheless this togetherness is not [intended]. Because the togetherness, being in the object-position, is not intended to be expressed. Nor should one say that although there is no fixing of togetherness from the word, there is togetherness from the meaning because [all fruits] are fruits of a single action — because the fruits of heaven, cattle, and the like are independent of one another. Therefore, the action is enjoined as the means of accomplishing each fruit individually. And precisely for this reason, the reference '<s>sarvebhyaḥ</s>' (for all) is appropriate — for otherwise, if togetherness were fixed, this combined [set] would be a single accomplished fruit, and the word '<s>sarva</s>' (all) would be inappropriate.

children.text: adhikaraṇe varṇakāntareṇa te eva tatra sarve 'viśeṣāt // MJaiNyC_4,3.27 //
children.translated_text: In the [same] <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, with a different reading, those very [sūtras]: therein, all [fruits], because of the absence of specification. // MJaiNyC_4,3.27 //
(In the twelfth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on optional rites having both this-worldly and other-worldly fruits, <s>sūtras</s> 27–28:)
Or individual accomplishment, because the meaning is not connected with origination [simultaneously]. // MJaiNyC_4,3.28 //
START MJaiNy 4,3.16-17
He composes the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
From the <s>citrā</s> (variegated) [sacrifice], are animals [to be obtained] only in the next world, or not fixed?
The first [alternative], because of equality with heaven; because [the citrā sacrifice] produces the body [in the other world]. // MJaiNy_4,3.16 //

children.text: citrotpattau tu niyamo na śrato nāpi kalpanam /
children.translated_text: But in the production by the <s>citrā</s> [sacrifice], there is no restriction — neither from the <s>śruti</s> nor from postulation;
when the obstacle is removed by human effort and the like, the fruit would [arise even in this world]. // MJaiNy_4,3.17 //

children.text:
kāmyakarmāṇyevaṃ śrūyante - 'citrayā yajeta paśukāmaḥ' aindramekādaśakapālaṃ nivapetprajākāmaḥ' iti |
tatra-yathā svargaphalasyā'muṣmikatvaṃ niyatam, evaṃ paśvādiphalasyāpi |
yadi svargaheturjyotiṣṭomo dehāntarasyotpādakaḥ, tarhi citrādirapi tathāstu iti cet |
maivam |
vaiṣamyāt |
asmindehe svargasya bhoktupraśakyatvādaśrutāpyanyadehospattirarthāpattyā kalpyate |
'citrayā tvanyadeho 'vaśyamutpādyate' iti niyamo na śrutaḥ, nāpi kiṃcittasya kalpakamasti |
anenāpi dehena paśvādiphalasya bhoktuṃ śakyatvāt |

children.translated_text: [Objection:] Since cattle and the like cannot be obtained in this body without visible means such as accepting gifts and the like, the fruit of the Vedic <s>Citrā</s> and other [rites] must be pertaining to the next world — if so argued,
no.
Because the visible means such as accepting gifts are useful for removing obstacles [to the fruit].

children.text: tasmāt- asati pratibandhe phalamaihikam, sati tvāmuṣmikam || MJaiNyC_4,3.16-17 //
children.translated_text: Therefore — in the absence of obstacles, the fruit is of this world (<s>aihika</s>); but when obstacles exist, it pertains to the next world. || MJaiNyC_4,3.16-17 ||

Desire-based (<s>kāmya</s>) rites are heard thus: '<s>citrayā yajeta paśukāmaḥ</s>' (one desiring cattle should sacrifice with [the <s>Nakṣatra</s>] <s>Citrā</s>), '<s>aindramekādaśakapālaṃ nivapetprajākāmaḥ</s>' (one desiring offspring should prepare an eleven-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] for <s>Indra</s>). Therein — just as the fruit of heaven (<s>svarga</s>) is necessarily pertaining to the next world (<s>āmuṣmika</s>), so too the fruit of cattle and the like. If the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, whose result is heaven, produces another body, then the <s>Citrā</s> and other [rites] should also do so — if so argued, that is not so. Because of the dissimilarity. Since heaven cannot be enjoyed in this body, the production of another body, though not heard [explicitly], is postulated through presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>). But 'by the <s>Citrā</s> [rite], another body must necessarily be produced' — this restriction is neither heard nor is there any basis for postulating it — because the fruit of cattle and the like can be enjoyed with this very body.
(In the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> and the like are accessories of the fire-building (<s>cayana</s>) and the like, <s>sūtras</s> 29–31)
In [the case of] co-occurrence, because of the purposefulness of the connection with the injunction. / Jaim_4,3.29 /
If [it be argued that] when time is heard, it is [merely] a time-[prescription] — / Jaim_4,3.30 /
No, because without the co-occurrence, it would be [established] by the purpose. / Jaim_4,3.31 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.18-19
He composes the thirteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Having sacrificed with the <s>Vājapeya</s>, one should sacrifice with the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s> —
does the sentence convey a time [prescription], or does it convey accessory status? // MJaiNy_4,3.18 //
The <s>ktvā</s>-suffix (<s>ktvāśruti</s>) indicates time here; but no — it conveys accessory status;

children.text: śrutermukhyaṃ prakriyā ca tathā satyanugṛhyate // MJaiNy_4,3.19 //
children.translated_text: the primary meaning of the Vedic statement [supports this], and the context too is thereby confirmed. // MJaiNy_4,3.19 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate- 'vājapeyeneṣṭvā bṛhaspatisavena yajeta' iti |
'āgniṃ citvāsautrāmaṇyā yajeta' iti |
tatra- 'iṣṭvā' iti ktvāpratyayo vājapeyasya pūrvakālīnatāṃ brūte |
tasmādvākyamidaṃ bṛhaspatisavasya vājapeyottarakālīnatāṃ bodhayati- iti prāpte, -
brūmaḥ- bṛhaspatisavastha vājapeyāṅgatvabodhanameva ktvāśrutermukhyor'thaḥ, |
'samānakartṛkayoḥ pūrvakāle' (3 | 4 | 21) iti (pāṇini) sūtreṇa kriyādvayasyaikakartṛkatāyāṃ tadvidhānāt |
yadyapi sūtre 'pūrvakāle' ityuktam, tathāpi tanna niyatam |
'mukhaṃ vyādāya śrvapiti' ityatra kālaikye 'pi prayogāt |
vājapeyaprakaraṇamapyaṅgatve 'nugṛhyate |
anyathā tvaprakṛte bṛhaspatitame kālavidhānātprakaraṇaṃ bādhyeta |
aṅgatve karmāntaratvena prasiddhabṛhaspatisabandhābhāvāttacchabdo 'nupapannaḥ- iti cet |

children.translated_text: no.
Because, by the principle of the monthly <s>Agnihotra</s>, [the word] serves the purpose of extending the properties of that [<s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>] [to the accessory rite].
Therefore — this sentence conveys accessory status.
In '<s>agniṃ citvā</s>' (having built the fire[-altar]) also, the same construction should be applied. || MJaiNyC_4,3.18-19 ||

This is taught in the Veda: '<s>vājapeyeneṣṭvā bṛhaspatisavena yajeta</s>' (having sacrificed with the <s>Vājapeya</s>, one should sacrifice with the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>). And: '<s>agniṃ citvāsautrāmaṇyā yajeta</s>' (having built the fire[-altar], one should sacrifice with the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>). Therein — the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix (absolutive) indicates the temporal priority of the <s>Vājapeya</s>. Therefore, this sentence conveys the post-<s>Vājapeya</s> timing of the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s> — having arrived at this position, we say: the primary meaning of the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix is to convey the accessory status of the <s>Vājapeya</s> to the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>. Because by the <s>sūtra</s> (<s>Pāṇini</s> 3.4.21) '<s>samānakartṛkayoḥ pūrvakāle</s>' (the <s>ktvā</s> [suffix is used] when the two actions have the same agent, in the prior time), the [<s>ktvā</s>-suffix] is ordained for expressing the identity of agent between two actions. Even though the <s>sūtra</s> says 'in the prior time,' that is not fixed — because in '<s>mukhaṃ vyādāya śrapayati</s>' (he cooks with [the pot's] mouth open), it is used even when the times are simultaneous. The <s>Vājapeya</s> context too is confirmed if [the <s>Vājapeya</s>] is an accessory. Otherwise, if a time-prescription were intended for the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s> — which is not under discussion [in the context] — the context would be overridden. [Objection:] If accessory status is accepted, since [the <s>Vājapeya</s>] would be known as a different rite, the connection with the established <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s> [name] would be absent — so the word [<s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>] would be inappropriate — if so argued,
(In the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the <s>Vaimṛdha</s> and the like are accessories of the full-moon [sacrifice] alone, <s>sūtras</s> 32–35)
If [it be argued that] it serves both purposes — / Jaim_4,3.32 /
No, because of the unity of the word. / Jaim_4,3.33 /
If [it be argued that] from the context — / Jaim_4,3.34 /
No, because of the connection in the origination-[sentence]. / Jaim_4,3.35 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.20-21
He composes the fourteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Having concluded the full-moon [sacrifice], the <s>Vaimṛdha</s> [offering] is prescribed thereafter —
is it an accessory of both [<s>Darśa</s> and <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s>], or of one alone? It would be of both, by the force of the context. // MJaiNy_4,3.20 //
From the origination-sentence, since the connection with the full-moon [sacrifice] is evident,

children.text: tasyaivāṅgaṃ na darśasya prakriyā vākyabādhitā // MJaiNy_4,3.21 //
children.translated_text: it is an accessory of that [full-moon sacrifice] alone, not of the new-moon [sacrifice]; the context is overridden by the sentence. // MJaiNy_4,3.21 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇamāsaprakaraṇe śrūyate- 'saṃsthāpya paurṇamāsīṃ vaimṛdhamanunirvapati' iti |
tatra-iyaṃ baimṛdhoṣṭiḥ prakaraṇabalātprayājādivaddarśapūrṇamāsayorubhayorapyaṅgam- iti cet |
na |

children.translated_text: Because the sentence is stronger.

children.text: na ca- 'saṃsthāpya' iti paurṇamāsyāḥ samāptyabhidhānāttadaṅgatvamayuktam- iti vācyam |
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that because '<s>saṃsthāpya</s>' (having concluded) indicates the completion of the full-moon [sacrifice], accessory status to that [sacrifice] is inappropriate —
because [the word '<s>saṃsthāpya</s>'] can be understood as referring to the completion of the accessories common to the new-moon [sacrifice as well].

Therefore — from the origination-sentence, and from the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix which indicates unity of agent, [the <s>Vaimṛdha</s>] is an accessory of the full-moon [sacrifice] alone. || MJaiNyC_4,3.20-21 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context, it is heard: '<s>saṃsthāpya paurṇamāsīṃ vaimṛdhamanunirvapati</s>' (having concluded the full-moon [sacrifice], he prepares the <s>Vaimṛdha</s> [offering] afterward). Therein — this <s>Vaimṛdha</s> <s>iṣṭi</s>, by the force of the context, would be an accessory of both the <s>Darśa</s> and <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s> [sacrifices], like the <s>prayājas</s> and the like — if so argued, no.
(In the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings) and the like [occur] after the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> [recitation], the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: anutpattau tu kālaḥ syāt prayojanena saṃbandhāt / Jaim_4,3.36 /
children.translated_text: When [accessory status] is not produced, it would be a time-[prescription], because of the connection with the purpose. / Jaim_4,3.36 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.22-23
He composes the fifteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Does the statement 'after the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> [recitation], one should perform the <s>anuyājas</s>' [convey]
accessory status, or a time [prescription]? If accessory status, there would be excessive dependence on another. // MJaiNy_4,3.22 //
The <s>Soma</s>-accessory status of this <s>Āgnimāruta</s> [recitation] is already known from before;
the <s>anuyājas</s> likewise are [already known as] accessories of the animal [sacrifice]; the connection serves to establish the time. // MJaiNy_4,3.23 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate -'āgnimārutādūrdhvamanuyājaiścarati' iti |
āgnimārutaṃ nāma kiṃcicchastram |
anuyājāḥ 'devaṃ barhiḥ'- ityādibhiḥ pāśukahautrakāṇḍapaṭhitairekādaśabhirmantraiḥ sādhyā homāḥ |
tatra-'āgnimārutaśastrasyānuyājā aṅgam' ityevamaṅgāṅgibhāvabodhanāyāyaṃ saṃyogaḥ |
yadi-anuyājānāmayaṃ kālopadeśaḥ syāt,tadānīmāgnimārutopanyāsasya svārtho na kaścit- ityatyantapārārthya syāt |
tasmāt- bṛhaspatisavavat, vaimṛdhavacca, anuyājā aṅgam- iti prāpte-
children.translated_text: Therefore — like the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>, and like the <s>Vaimṛdha</s>, the <s>anuyājas</s> are accessories — having arrived at this position,
we say: the accessory status of the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> <s>śastra</s> to the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] is already understood from before, like the other <s>stotras</s> and <s>śastras</s>.

The accessory status of the eleven <s>anuyājas</s> to the principal animal [sacrifice] is also already understood, through extension (<s>atideśa</s>) from the <s>Savanīya</s> animal, which is a modification of the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [sacrifice].
Therefore, since a mutual accessory-principal relationship between them is impossible, this connection serves the purpose of a time-prescription. || MJaiNyC_4,3.22-23 ||

In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, it is heard: '<s>āgnimārutādūrdhvamanuyājaiścarati</s>' (after the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> [recitation], he performs the <s>anuyājas</s>). The <s>Āgnimāruta</s> is a certain <s>śastra</s> (recitation). The <s>anuyājas</s> are oblations to be accomplished with the eleven <s>mantras</s> beginning with '<s>devaṃ barhiḥ</s>' recited in the animal-sacrifice <s>Hautra</s> section. Therein — this connection serves to convey the accessory-principal relationship: 'the <s>anuyājas</s> are accessories of the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> <s>śastra</s>.' If the <s>anuyājas</s> were [merely] a time-prescription here, then the mention of the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> would serve no purpose of its own — there would be excessive dependence on another.
(In the sixteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, on [whether] the <s>Soma</s> and the like [occur] at a time after the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: utpattikālaviśaye kālaḥ syād vākyasya tatpradhānatvāt / Jaim_4,3.37 /
children.translated_text: When the subject is the time of origination, it would be a time-[prescription], because the sentence has that as its principal [content]. / Jaim_4,3.37 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.24-25
He composes the sixteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Having sacrificed with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [sacrifices], should one sacrifice with <s>Soma</s> —

children.text: aṅgāṅgibhāvaḥ kālo vā hyapārārthyāya cāṅgatā // MJaiNy_4,3.24 //
children.translated_text: is [the connection one of] accessory-principal relationship, or time? The accessory status would [serve] to avoid excessive dependence. // MJaiNy_4,3.24 //
The <s>Soma</s> sacrifice is enjoined at a time characterized by [having performed] the <s>Darśa</s> and other [sacrifices];
since both [<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and <s>Soma</s>] have independent fruits, an accessory-principal relationship between them is not appropriate. // MJaiNy_4,3.25 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate- 'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāmiṣṭvā somana yajeta' iti |
tatra- ubhayorāgnimārutānuyājavadanyādhīnatvābhāvāddarśapūrṇamāsokteḥ pārārdhyaparihārāya somasya darśapūrṇamāsāṅgatvabodhako 'yaṃ saṃyogaḥ - iti cet |
maivam |
svatantraphalavataḥ somasyāṅgatvāsaṃbhavāt |
phalavatsaṃnidhāvaphalaṃ tadaṅgaṃ bhavati, iti nyāyāt |
na ca- atra bṛhaspatisabanyāyena somadharmakarmaphalaṃ karmāntaraṃ vidhīyate- iti śakyaṃ vaktum |
somaśabdasya bṛhaspatisavaśabdavaśvāmatvābhāvena dharmātideśakatvābhāvāt |
ktvāpratyayastvasatyapyaṅgāṅgibhāve kartraikyamātreṇopapadyate |
tasmāddarśapūrṇamāsaśabdasya pārārthyamabhyupetyāpi tadiṣṭyupalakṣita uttarakāle somavidhirayam |
etadevābhipretya rathatvarūpamasyā'mnāyate- 'eṣa vai devaratho yaddarśapūrṇamāsau |
yo darśapūrṇamāsābhyāmiṣṭvā somena yajate rathaspaṣṭa evāvasāne vare devānāmavasyami' iti |

children.translated_text: '<s>Avasāna</s>' means 'determined.'
'<s>Vara</s>' means 'path.'

children.text: 'yathā rathena kṣuṇṇe mārge gantuḥ kaṇṭakapāṣaṇādibādhārāhityena sukhaṃ bhavati, tathā prathamaṃ darśapūrṇamāsāviṣṭavata uttarakāle tadiṣṭivikṛtiṣu somāṅgabhūtadīkṣaṇīyaprāyaṇīyādiṣu dharmānuṣṭhānaṃ sukaraṃ bhavati' ityarthaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Just as when the path is smoothed by a chariot, the traveler experiences comfort due to the absence of obstruction from thorns and stones, similarly, for one who has first sacrificed with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, the performance of the properties [that appear] in the modifications of those <s>iṣṭis</s> at a later time — such as the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s>, <s>prāyaṇīyā</s>, and the like that are accessories of <s>Soma</s> — becomes easy' — this is the meaning.
Therefore, the connection serves the purpose of a time-prescription. || MJaiNyC_4,3.24-25 ||

This is taught: '<s>darśapūrṇamāsābhyāmiṣṭvā somena yajeta</s>' (having sacrificed with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>). Therein — since neither [of the two] depends on the other — like the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> and <s>anuyāja</s> — the mention of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, to avoid excessive dependence, would convey the accessory status of <s>Soma</s> to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> — if so argued, that is not so. Because the <s>Soma</s>, having an independent fruit, cannot be an accessory. By the principle: 'in the proximity of what has fruit, that which is fruitless becomes its accessory.' Nor can it be said that — by the principle of the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>, a different rite having the fruit and properties of the <s>Soma</s> is enjoined. Because the word '<s>soma</s>' — unlike the word '<s>bṛhaspatisava</s>' — is not an unfamiliar term, and therefore cannot serve to extend properties. But the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix is appropriate even without an accessory-principal relationship, merely through identity of agent. Therefore, even accepting that the word '<s>darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' serves another's purpose, this is an injunction of <s>Soma</s> at a subsequent time characterized by [having performed] those <s>iṣṭis</s>. With this very intent, its chariot-nature is taught: '<s>eṣa vai devaratho yaddarśapūrṇamāsau</s>' (the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> sacrifices are indeed the chariot of the gods). 'He who, having sacrificed with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, sacrifices with <s>Soma</s> — [travels] as if on a well-made chariot-path, [saying] "I settle on the determined path of the gods."'
(In the seventeenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, contained within the <s>Jāteṣṭi</s> principle, on [whether] the fruit of the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>iṣṭi</s> pertains to the son, <s>sūtras</s> 38–39)

children.text: phalasaṃyogas tv acodite na syād aśeṣabhūtatvāt / Jaim_4,3.38 /
children.translated_text: The connection with the fruit — when [the rite] is not enjoined [for that person] — would not exist, because [the son] is not a subsidiary. / Jaim_4,3.38 /
But for the accessories, the connection of mutual interference serves the purpose of the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>). / Jaim_4,3.39 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.26-27
He composes the seventeenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Does the purity [conferred] by the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>iṣṭi</s> belong to the father or to the son? The first [alternative holds],

children.text: kartureva phalaṃ yuktaṃ kartṛtvaṃ pitureva hi // MJaiNy_4,3.26 //
children.translated_text: because the fruit appropriately belongs to the agent, and the father alone has agency. // MJaiNy_4,3.26 //
Since he performs this <s>iṣṭi</s> when [the son] is born — for that [son] is the purity;

children.text: taccepsitaṃ pitustena pitā tatra pravartate // MJaiNy_4,3.27 //
children.translated_text: that is desired by the father — therefore the father engages in it. // MJaiNy_4,3.27 //

children.text:
kāmyoṣṭikāṇḍe 'vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nivaṣetputre jāte' iti prakṛtya śrūyate- 'yasminjāta etāmiṣṭiṃ nirvapati pūta eva tejakhyannāda indriyāvī paśunānbhavati' iti |
tatra- pituḥ prabuddhasya kartṛtvam, na tu mugdhasya putrasya |
tato 'nuṣṭhānaphalayorvaiyadhikaraṇyaparihārāya pitureva pūtatvādi phalam- iti cet |
maivam |
'yasmiñjāte nirvapati sa pūtaḥ' iti vākyena phalasya putrasaṃbandhāvagamāt |
children.translated_text: Because from the sentence '<s>yasmiñjāte nirvapati sa pūtaḥ</s>' (he for whom, when born, [the father] performs — he is pure), the connection of the fruit with the son is understood.

children.text: na ca- atra niṣphalasya piturapravṛttiḥ- iti vācyam |
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that the father, having no fruit, would not engage [in the rite] —
because his engagement is possible through the belief that it is his own fruit, due to the purity and the like of his son being desired [by him].
Therefore — the purity and the like belong to the son. || MJaiNyC_4,3.26-27 ||

In the section on desire-based <s>iṣṭis</s>, after introducing '<s>vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapetputre jāte</s>' (one should prepare a twelve-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] for <s>Vaiśvānara</s> when a son is born), it is heard: '<s>yasminjāta etāmiṣṭiṃ nirvapati pūta eva tejakṣyannāda indriyāvī paśunānbhavati</s>' (he for whom, when born, one prepares this <s>iṣṭi</s> — he becomes indeed pure, radiant, food-eating, possessed of vital powers, and having cattle). Therein — agency belongs to the father, who is awake [to ritual], not to the infant son. Therefore, to avoid the incongruity of the performer and the fruit-enjoyer being different, the purity and the like would be the fruit of the father — if so argued, that is not so.

(In the eighteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, contained within the <s>Jāteṣṭi</s> principle, on [whether] the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>iṣṭi</s> [occurs] at a time after the <s>Jātakarman</s> (birth ceremony), the <s>sūtra</s> already stated under a different heading is:)
But for the accessories, the connection of mutual interference serves the purpose of the occasion. // MJaiNyC_4,3.31 //
START MJaiNy 4,3.28-29
He composes the eighteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Should the <s>iṣṭi</s> [be performed] immediately after birth, or after the <s>Jātakarman</s> (birth ceremony) has been performed?
Since the occasional rite should be performed immediately after the occasion, the first [alternative holds]. // MJaiNy_4,3.28 //
Since the breast-feeding is observed [as occurring] after the completion of the <s>Jātakarman</s>,
the <s>iṣṭi</s> should be [performed] before the infant's [possible] harm; let it be after [the <s>Jātakarman</s>]. // MJaiNy_4,3.29 //

children.text:
putrajanmano vaiśvānareṣṭinimittitvāt, naimittikasya kālavilambāyogāt, janmānantaramevoṣṭiḥ- iti cet |
maivam |

children.translated_text: Now, breast-feeding is enjoined immediately after the <s>Jātakarman</s>.

children.text: yadi jātakarmaṇaḥ prāgeva vaiśvānareṣṭirnirupyeta, tadā stanaprāśanasyātyantavilambātputro vipadyeta |
children.translated_text: If the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>iṣṭi</s> were prescribed before the <s>Jātakarman</s>, then the breast-feeding would be excessively delayed, and the infant would perish.
In that case, for whom would the fruit of the <s>iṣṭi</s> — purity and the like — exist?

children.text: tasmāt- na janmānantaram, kiṃtu jātakarmaṇa ūrdhva streṣṭhiḥ || MJaiNyC_4,3.28-29 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — not immediately after birth, but after the <s>Jātakarman</s> is the <s>iṣṭi</s> [to be performed]. || MJaiNyC_4,3.28-29 ||

Since the birth of the son is the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>) for the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>iṣṭi</s>, and since an occasional rite should not be delayed, the <s>iṣṭi</s> should be performed immediately after birth — if so argued, that is not so.
(In the nineteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, contained within the <s>Jāteṣṭi</s> principle, on [whether] the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>iṣṭi</s> [occurs] at a time after
the expiry of ritual impurity (<s>āśauca</s>), the <s>sūtra</s> already stated under a different heading is:)
