But for the accessories, the connection of mutual interference serves the purpose of the occasion. // MJaiNyC_4,3.39 //
START MJaiNy 4,3.30
He composes the nineteenth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Should [the <s>iṣṭi</s> be performed] immediately after the <s>Jātakarman</s>, or after the ritual impurity (<s>āśauca</s>) has passed?
The first [alternative holds] from proximity to the occasion; the second, for the purpose of the performer's purity. // MJaiNy_4,3.30 //

children.text: yadyapi jātakarmānantarameva tadanuṣṭhāne nimittabhūtaṃ janma saṃnihitaṃ bhavati, tathāpyaśudhinā pitrānuṣṭhoyamānamaṅgavikalaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: Although the birth, which is the occasion for performing [the birth rite (<s>jātakarma</s>)], is present immediately after the birth rite itself, nevertheless, if performed by the impure father, it would be deficient in its limbs.

children.text: jātakarmaṇi tu vipattiparihārāya tātkālikī śuddhiḥśāstreṇaiva darśitā |
children.translated_text: But in the birth rite, the purification at that very time is shown by scripture itself, for the purpose of averting calamity.

children.text: tato mukhyasaṃnidheravaśyaṃ vādhikatvācchuddhilakṣaṇāṅgavaikalyaṃ vārayitumāśaucādūrdhvamiṣṭiṃ kuryāt || MJaiNyC_4,3.30 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the primary proximity inevitably has greater force, or in order to prevent the deficiency of limbs in the form of [ritual] purity, one should perform the <s>iṣṭi</s> after the period of impurity (<s>āśauca</s>). || MJaiNyC_4,3.30 ||
(In the twentieth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> and other accessories being performed at their own proper time, <s>sūtras</s> 40–41)
Because of the connection with the principal, the accessories [would be performed] at the time of the principal. / Jaim_4,3.40 /

children.text: apravṛtte tu codanā tatsāmānyāt svakāle syāt / Jaim_4,3.41 /
children.translated_text: But when [the principal] has not commenced, because of the similarity of the injunction, [the accessory] should be [performed] at its own time. / Jaim_4,3.41 /
START MJaiNy 4,3.31-32
He composes the twentieth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
'Having constructed the fire-altar, one should sacrifice with the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>' — this subsidiary <s>iṣṭi</s> is of such a nature;
should it be [performed] at the principal's time or at its own time? The first [view is] accepted, like other accessories. // MJaiNy_4,3.31 //
But when the fire-altar construction and the like have been completed, since another rite is being enjoined [separately],
the performance at its own time, obtained from the enjoining authority, is established. // MJaiNy_4,3.32 //

children.text:
'agniṃ citvā sautrāmaṇyā yajeta' 'vājapeyeneṣṭvā bṛhaspatisavena yajeta' ityatra sautrāmaṇībṛhaspatisavayāreṅgatvaṃ pūrvamuktam |
taccāṅgamaṅgikāle 'ṅginā saha prayoktavyam |
itareṣāmaṅgānāṃ tathā prayujyamānatvāt- iti cet |
maivam |
ktvāpratyayena pūrvakālavācinā sāṅge cayanādau nirvṛtte sati paścātkarmāntaratvena sautrāmaṇyādervihitatvāt |
yadi-aṅginā sahaikaprayogaḥ syāt, tadā ktvāpratyayaprāpitaḥ pūrvottarakālavibhāgo bādhyeta |
na hi- aṅginā saha prayoktavyānāmukhāsaṃbharaṇādīnāṃ cayane nirvṛtte paścādvidhānaṃ śrutam - tataḥ pṛthagprayoge 'vaśyabhāvini sati svasvacodakaprapite tadanuṣṭhānaṃ yuktam |
sautrāmaṇyā iṣṭiprakṛtikatvātparvakālaścedakaprāptaḥ |
cayanena sahaikaprayoge tu parvaṇyukhāsaṃbharaṇādividhānādanyasmindana sautrāmaṇī vrasajyeta |
tathā bṛhaspatisavasya jyotiṣṭomavikṛtitvāt, vasantakālaścodakaprāptaḥ |
vājapeyena saha prayogaikye śaradi vājapeyasya vihitatvādbṛhaspatisavo 'pi śaradi prasajyeta |
tasmāt- atidiṣṭe parvaṇi vasante ca tadanuṣṭhānam |
nanu sarvatrāṅgāpūrvaiḥ pradhānāpūrva janayitavyam, iha tu pūrvakālīnena sāṅgapradhānānuṣṭhānena phalāpūrvasya niṣpannatvāduttarakālīnapraṅgaṃ nirarthakam- iti cet |
children.translated_text: [If it is argued:] Everywhere, the subsidiary <s>apūrva</s> (originating potency) generates the principal <s>apūrva</s>; but here, since the fruit-<s>apūrva</s> has already been produced by the prior performance of the principal with its accessories, the subsequent accessory is purposeless — if so,
no.
Because it is precisely that <s>apūrva</s> whose state of strength is to be posited through this accessory.

children.text: tasmāt- nāṅginaḥ kāle 'nuṣṭhānam, kiṃtu svakāle- iti sthitam || MJaiNyC_4,3.31-32 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — the performance is not at the principal's time, but at its own time — this is established. || MJaiNyC_4,3.31-32 ||

In '<s>agniṃ citvā sautrāmaṇyā yajeta</s>' (having constructed the fire-altar, one should sacrifice with the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>), '<s>vājapeyeneṣṭvā bṛhaspatisavena yajeta</s>' (having sacrificed with the <s>Vājapeya</s>, one should sacrifice with the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>) — the subsidiarity of the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> and <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s> sacrifices was stated earlier. And that accessory should be employed together with the principal at the time of the principal. Because other accessories are so employed — if so [it is argued], that is not correct. Because the <s>ktvā</s> suffix, denoting prior-time, indicates that after the fire-altar construction and its associated [rites] have been completed, the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> and the like are enjoined subsequently as separate rites. If there were a single employment together with the principal, then the division into prior and subsequent times conveyed by the <s>ktvā</s> suffix would be overridden. For it is not heard that the face-anointing (<s>mukhāsaṃbharaṇa</s>) and the like, which are to be employed together with the principal, are enjoined after the construction is completed — therefore, since separate employment is inevitable, the performance at the time obtained from each one's own enjoining authority is appropriate. For the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>, being an <s>iṣṭi</s>-type sacrifice, the time obtained from the enjoining authority is the <s>parvan</s> (juncture day). But if there were a single employment together with the construction, then since the face-anointing and the like are enjoined at the <s>parvan</s>, the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> would be relegated to another day. Similarly, since the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s> is a modification of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the time obtained from the enjoining authority is the spring season. If there were a single employment with the <s>Vājapeya</s>, since the <s>Vājapeya</s> is enjoined in autumn, the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s> too would be relegated to autumn. Therefore — the performance is at the transferred <s>parvan</s> [day] and in spring respectively.

children.text: iti śrīmādhavīye jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistare caturthādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> in the illustrious <s>Mādhavīya Jaiminīyanyāyamālāvistara</s>.
Now begins the fourth <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s>. /
(In the first [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on whether the sacrifices in the <s>Rājasūya</s> are accessories of the dice-playing and the like, <s>sūtras</s> 1–2)
Because of the generality of the context and the word, the injunctions are not [merely] accessories. / Jaim_4,4.1 /

children.text: api vāṅgamanijyāḥ syus tato viśiṣṭatvāt / Jaim_4,4.2 /
children.translated_text: Or they would be accessories — the non-sacrifices, because of their being distinguished [from the sacrifices]. / Jaim_4,4.2 /
START MJaiNy 4,4.1-2
In the fourth <s>pāda</s>, he composes the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
In the <s>Rājasūya</s>, the <s>Anumati</s> [offerings] and the like, and the dice-playing (<s>devana</s>) and the like — both of these:
are they both principal, or is one principal? The first [view], because of the unity of the context. // MJaiNy_4,4.1 //
The sacrifices have <s>Rājasūya</s>-nature and hence principality, because of their fruitfulness;
the dice-playing and the like, being fruitless, are accessories of the fruitful sacrifice. // MJaiNy_4,4.2 //

children.text:
rājasūyaprakaraṇe yāgarūpā anumatyādayo bahavaḥ śrutāḥ- 'anumatyai puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapati' 'naiṛtamekakapālam' 'ādityaṃ caru nirvapati' 'āgnāvaiṣṇavamekādaśakapālam' ityādayaḥ |
yathaitā iṣṭayaḥ, tathā paśavo 'pi śrutāḥ- 'ādityāṃ malhāṃ garbhiṇīmālabhate, ' 'mārutīṃ pṛśrim' 'praṣṭhauhīmaśvibhyām' ityādi |
malhā maṇilā galastanayuktetyarthaḥ |
tasyā aditirdevatā |
pṛśriralpatanuḥ |
tasyā maruto devatā |
yāvatā vayasā varṣatrayarūpeṇa pṛṣṭhe bhāraṃ voḍhuṃ śaktirbhavati, tāvadvayaskā praṣṭhauhī |
tasyā āśvinau devatā |
evamabhiṣecanīyadaśapeyādayaḥ somayāgāḥ śrutāḥ |
tathā 'valmīkavapāyāṃ homaḥ' ityādayo darvihomāḥ |
yathaita iṣṭipaśusomadarvihomāścaturvidhā yāgarūpāḥ, evamayāgarūpā api dyūtādayaḥ śrutāḥ- 'praṣṭhauhīṃ dīvyati' 'akṣairdīvyati' 'rājanyaṃ jināti' 'śaunaḥ śepamā khyāpayati' ityādayaḥ |
tatra yāgā yathā mukhyāḥ, tathā devanādīnāmapi mukhyatvaṃ yuktam |
children.translated_text: Therein, just as the sacrifices are principal, so too the principality of the dice-playing and the like is appropriate,

children.text: prakaraṇapāṭhasyobhayatra samānatvāt- iti prāpte, brūmaḥ- 'rājā svārājyakāmo rājasūyena yajeta' ityatrā'khyātavācyāyāṃ bhāvanāyāṃ dhātuvācyo yāgaḥ karaṇam |
children.translated_text: because the contextual recitation is the same for both — having arrived at this position, we say: In '<s>rājā svārājyakāmo rājasūyena yajeta</s>' (the king who desires sovereignty should sacrifice with the <s>Rājasūya</s>), the sacrifice denoted by the verbal root is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) in the injunctive activity (<s>bhāvanā</s>) expressed by the finite verb.
And the word '<s>Rājasūya</s>', since its meaning is not well-known [independently], becomes the designation of the sacrifice through co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) with it.

children.text: tathā sati 'rājasūyena yāgena svārājyaṃ bhāvayet' iti vākyārthaparyavasānādanumatyādīnāṃ yāgānāmeva phalavattvādaṅgitvam, tatsaṃnidhau śrūyamāṇamaphalaṃ devanādikaṃ yāgāṅgam || MJaiNyC_4,4.1-2 ||
children.translated_text: This being so, since the sentence culminates in the meaning 'one should bring about sovereignty through the sacrifice called <s>Rājasūya</s>,' the sacrifices such as the <s>Anumati</s> offerings are principal because of their fruitfulness, and the fruitless dice-playing and the like, heard in proximity to them, are accessories of the fruitful sacrifices. || MJaiNyC_4,4.1-2 ||

In the <s>Rājasūya</s> context, many [offerings] in the form of sacrifices — <s>Anumati</s> and the like — are heard: '<s>anumatyai puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapati</s>' (he prepares an eight-<s>kapāla</s> sacrificial cake for <s>Anumati</s>), '<s>nairṛtamekakapālam</s>' (a single-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] for <s>Nirṛti</s>), '<s>ādityaṃ caruṃ nirvapati</s>' (he prepares a <s>caru</s> for <s>Āditya</s>), '<s>āgnāvaiṣṇavamekādaśakapālam</s>' (an eleven-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>) and so on. Just as these <s>iṣṭis</s>, so too animal sacrifices are heard: '<s>ādityāṃ malhāṃ garbhiṇīmālabhate</s>' (he consecrates a pregnant cow with a dewlap [as an offering] to <s>Āditya</s>), '<s>mārutīṃ pṛśrim</s>' (a thin [cow] to the <s>Maruts</s>), '<s>praṣṭhauhīmaśvibhyām</s>' (a draught-cow to the <s>Aśvins</s>) and so on. '<s>Malhā</s>' means 'maṇilā' — having a dewlap on the neck. Its deity is <s>Āditya</s>. '<s>Pṛśri</s>' means one of slender body. Its deity is the <s>Maruts</s>. One who has reached the age — in the form of three years — at which she is capable of bearing a load on her back is a '<s>praṣṭhauhī</s>' (draught-cow). Its deities are the <s>Aśvins</s>. Similarly, <s>Soma</s> sacrifices such as the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s>, <s>Daśapeya</s>, and the like are heard. Likewise, <s>darvihomas</s> (ladle-oblations) such as '<s>valmīkavapāyāṃ homaḥ</s>' (an oblation on an anthill excavation) and so on. Just as these four types of sacrificial rites — <s>iṣṭi</s>, animal sacrifice, <s>Soma</s> sacrifice, and <s>darvihoma</s> — so too non-sacrificial [acts] such as dice-playing and the like are heard: '<s>praṣṭhauhīṃ dīvyati</s>' (he gambles for a draught-cow), '<s>akṣairdīvyati</s>' (he plays with dice), '<s>rājanyaṃ jināti</s>' (he defeats the nobleman), '<s>śaunaḥśepamākhyāpayati</s>' (he narrates the story of <s>Śunaḥśepa</s>) and so on.
(In the second [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on whether the dice-playing is an accessory of the entire <s>Rājasūya</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 3–4)
What is in the middle [belongs] to that in whose midst [it is]. / Jaim_4,4.3 /

children.text: sarvāsāṃ vā samatvāc codanātaḥ syān na hi tasya prakaraṇaṃ deśārtham ucyate madhye / Jaim_4,4.4 /
children.translated_text: Or [it belongs] to all, because of the equality of the injunctions, for the context is not said to be for the purpose of [fixing] the location; [it is heard] in the middle. / Jaim_4,4.4 /
START MJaiNy 4,4.3
He composes the second <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is [the dice-playing] an accessory of only the one <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> [sacrifice], or of the entire [<s>Rājasūya</s>]?
The first, because of restriction; the latter, because of the context. // MJaiNy_4,4.3 //

children.text:
yadetat-devanādikamaṅgam- ityuktam, tadetabhiṣecanīyasya somayāgasyaikasyaivāṅgam |
kutaḥ |
apakarṣāt |
yadyapi- abhiṣecanīyavidherūrdhve tatsaṃnidhau devanādayaḥ samāmnātāḥ, tathāpi- abhiṣecanīyamadhve te 'pakṛṣyante |
'māhendrasya stotraṃ pratyabhiṣicyate' iti vākyena rājño yajamānasyābhiṣeko mādhyaṃdinasavane stotrakāle 'pakṛṣyate |
tasminnapakṛṣṭe sati tataḥ pūrvamāmnātānāṃ devanādīnāmarthasiddho 'pakarṣaḥ |

children.translated_text: In either case, since the directly perceived greater context is stronger, the dice-playing and the like are accessories of the <s>Rājasūya</s>.
And the word '<s>Rājasūya</s>' denotes all the sacrifices — the <s>Anumati</s> offerings and the rest.
Therefore, this [dice-playing etc.] is an accessory of all of them.

children.text: anuṣṭhānaṃ tu rājasūyamadhye kvacidapekṣitamiti vacanabalādabhiṣecanīyagatamāhendrastotrakāle tadanuṣṭhīyate || MJaiNyC_4,4.3 ||
children.translated_text: But the performance is required at some point within the <s>Rājasūya</s>, and by the force of the verbal statement, it is performed during the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> at the time of the <s>Māhendra stotra</s>. || MJaiNyC_4,4.3 ||

That which was said — that the dice-playing and the like are accessories — that is an accessory of only the one <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> <s>Soma</s> sacrifice. Why? Because of restriction. Although the dice-playing and the like are recited after the injunction of the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> and in proximity to it, they are nevertheless attracted into the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> [itself]. The anointing (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) of the king who is the sacrificer is attracted to the time of the <s>Māhendra</s> <s>stotra</s> at the midday pressing, by the sentence '<s>māhendrasya stotraṃ pratyabhiṣicyate</s>' (he is anointed at the <s>Māhendra</s> <s>stotra</s>). When that is attracted, the attraction of the dice-playing and the like, which are recited before it, is established by implication. Therefore, like the <s>Māhendra stotra</s> and the like, since [the dice-playing] falls within the performance of the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s>, the dice-playing and the like are accessories of the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> alone — having arrived at this position, we say: Is proximity the evidence for its being an accessory of that, or is it the sub-context constructed through the employment [of the rite]?
(In the third [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>Saumya</s> and other [offerings] being markers of time for the <s>Upasads</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 5–6)

children.text: prakaraṇāvibhāge ca vipratiṣiddhaṃ hy ubhayam / Jaim_4,4.5 /
children.translated_text: And when the context is undivided, both would be contradictory. / Jaim_4,4.5 /

children.text: api vā kālamātraṃ syād adarśanād viśeśasya / Jaim_4,4.6 /
children.translated_text: Or it would be merely a time[-marker], because of the non-observation of the specific [accessory relationship]. / Jaim_4,4.6 /
START MJaiNy 4,4.4-5
He composes the third <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Does '<s>purastādupasadāṃ saumyena pracaret</s>' (one should perform the <s>Saumya</s> before the <s>Upasads</s>)

children.text: aṅgāṅgibhāvaḥ kālo vā vākyādādyaḥ pratīyate // MJaiNy_4,4.4 //
children.translated_text: [establish] a subsidiary-principal relationship, or [merely] a time? By the sentence, the first is understood. // MJaiNy_4,4.4 //
'<s>Purastāt</s>' (before) appears here as a time[-marker]; therefore, [it is] a time-injunction;
the <s>Saumya</s> and the like are not accessories of anything — they are principal, like other <s>iṣṭis</s>. // MJaiNy_4,4.5 //

children.text:
rājasūye saṃsṛcchabdavācyānyāgneyāṣṭākapālādīni |
teṣvaṣṭamanavamadaśamāni saumya- tvāṣṭra-vaiṣṇavāni |
tadviṣayamidaṃ vākyamāmnāyate- 'purastādupasadāṃ saumyena pracaranti, antarā tvāṣṭreṇa, upariṣṭādvaiṣṇavena' iti |
yo 'yaṃ rājasūye somayāgaḥ, tasminnatidiṣṭānāmupasadāmādimadhyāvasāneṣu saumyādīnāṃ trayāṇāmanuṣṭhānamanena vākyena codyate |
children.translated_text: In the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice that is part of the <s>Rājasūya</s>, this sentence enjoins the performance of the three — <s>Saumya</s> and the others — at the beginning, middle, and end of the <s>Upasads</s> transferred [to that context].

children.text: tato vākyātsaumyādīnyupasadāmaṅgāni- iti prāpte, brūmaḥ- 'upasadām' iti ṣaṣṭhyāḥ kālavācinā 'purastāt' iti śabdenānvayāt |
children.translated_text: Therefore, by the sentence, the <s>Saumya</s> and the like are accessories of the <s>Upasads</s> — having arrived at this position, we say: Because of the connection of the genitive '<s>upasadām</s>' (of the <s>Upasads</s>) with the time-denoting word '<s>purastāt</s>' (before),
this sentence pertains to the connection with a specific time for the <s>Saumya</s> and the like, not to a subsidiary-principal relationship.

children.text: tato na kasyāpyaṅgaṃ saumyādikam, kiṃtu- anumatyādivatpradhānam || MJaiNyC_4,4.4-5 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>Saumya</s> and the like are not accessories of anything; rather, they are principal, like the <s>Anumati</s> offerings. || MJaiNyC_4,4.4-5 ||

In the <s>Rājasūya</s>, those called <s>saṃsṛts</s> are the <s>Āgneya</s> eight-<s>kapāla</s> [offering] and the like. Among them, the eighth, ninth, and tenth are the <s>Saumya</s>, <s>Tvāṣṭra</s>, and <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> [offerings]. Regarding those, this sentence is recited: '<s>purastādupasadāṃ saumyena pracaranti, antarā tvāṣṭreṇa, upariṣṭādvaiṣṇavena</s>' (they perform with the <s>Saumya</s> before the <s>Upasads</s>, with the <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> in between, with the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> after).
(In the fourth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the <s>Āmana</s> oblations being accessories of the <s>Sāṃgrahaṇī</s> [<s>iṣṭi</s>], the <s>sūtra</s> is:)

children.text: phalavad voktahetutvād itarasya pradhānaṃ syāt / Jaim_4,4.7 /
children.translated_text: The other, being fruitful, would be principal, because of the stated reason. / Jaim_4,4.7 /
START MJaiNy 4,4.6
He composes the fourth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Is the <s>Āmana</s> oblation principal, or is it an accessory of the <s>Sāṃgrahaṇī</s> [<s>iṣṭi</s>]?
Principality, because of non-contradiction; but since it [serves] the fruit, it would be an accessory. // MJaiNy_4,4.6 //

children.text:
kāmyeṣṭikāṇḍe śrūyate- 'vaiśvadevīṃ sāṃgrahaṇīṃ nirvapedprāmakāyaḥ ' iti |

ta eta āmanahomāḥ sāṃgrahaṇyeṣṭyā saha samapradhānabhūtāḥ |
na hi teṣāṃ mukhyatve kaścidvirodho 'sti |
dṛṣṭaṃ hyāgneyādiṣvanumatyādiṣu ca bahūnāṃ mukhyatvam- iti cet |

children.translated_text: that is not correct.

children.text: 'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmaḥ' iti vākyena 'svārājyakāmo rājasūyena' iti vākyena ca yathā bahūnāṃ phalasaṃbandhāvagamaḥ, tathā'manahomānām |
children.translated_text: Just as through the sentence '<s>darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmaḥ</s>' (one who desires heaven [should sacrifice] with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>) and the sentence '<s>svārājyakāmo rājasūyena</s>' (one who desires sovereignty [should sacrifice] with the <s>Rājasūya</s>), the connection with fruit of many [sacrifices] is understood — [one might argue that] so too with the <s>Āmana</s> oblations.
But since principality is impossible without connection with fruit,

children.text: 'sāṃgrahaṇīṃ nirvapedgrāmakāmaḥ' iti vākyaṃ tu sāṃgrahaṇyāḥ saṃnidhāvāmnātā aphalā āmanahomāstadaṅgam || MJaiNyC_4,4.6 ||
children.translated_text: the sentence '<s>sāṃgrahaṇīṃ nirvapedgrāmakāmaḥ</s>' (one who desires a village should prepare the <s>Sāṃgrahaṇī</s>) [shows that] the fruitless <s>Āmana</s> oblations, heard in proximity to the <s>Sāṃgrahaṇī</s>, are accessories of it. || MJaiNyC_4,4.6 ||

In the section of optional <s>iṣṭis</s>, it is heard: '<s>vaiśvadevīṃ sāṃgrahaṇīṃ nirvapedgrāmakāmaḥ</s>' (one who desires a village should prepare the <s>Sāṃgrahaṇī</s> [offering] for the <s>Viśvedevas</s>). Therein, the <s>Āmana</s> oblations are heard: '<s>āmanasya — āmanasya devāḥ — iti tistra āhutījuhoti</s>' (saying 'of the <s>Āmana</s>, of the <s>Āmana</s>, O gods' — he offers three oblations). These <s>Āmana</s> oblations are co-principal with the <s>Sāṃgrahaṇī</s> <s>iṣṭi</s>. For there is no contradiction in their being principal. It is seen that many [offerings] are principal in the <s>Āgneya</s> and other [rites] and in the <s>Anumati</s> and other [offerings] — if so [it is argued],
(In the fifth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the permanence of the curd-cup (<s>dadhigraha</s>), <s>sūtras</s> 8–11)
The curd-cup is occasional, because of the connection with the <s>śruti</s>. / Jaim_4,4.8 /
And it is permanent, because of the word '<s>jyeṣṭha</s>' (eldest/chief). / Jaim_4,4.9 /
And because of its universal form (<s>sārvarūpya</s>). / Jaim_4,4.10 /

children.text: nityo vā syād arthavādas tayoḥ karmaṇy asaṃbandhād bhaṅgitvāc cāntarāyasya / Jaim_4,4.11 /
children.translated_text: Or it would be permanent, because the <s>arthavāda</s> of those two has no connection with the rite, and because the obstacle is of a contingent nature. / Jaim_4,4.11 /
START MJaiNy 4,4.7-8
He composes the fifth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —
Permanence or occasionality — in the curd-cup, permanence alone [holds];
because of [the prevention of] divine obstruction and because of seniority, it would have both natures. // MJaiNy_4,4.7 //
The conditional word '<s>yadi</s>' (if) and the like, which would indicate occasionality, are not present here;

children.text: ato 'sya na nimisatvaṃ kevalā nityatocitā // MJaiNy_4,4.8 //
children.translated_text: therefore, it has no occasionality — only permanence is appropriate. // MJaiNy_4,4.8 //

children.translated_text: Or the 'yat' particle should be used in co-reference (sāmānādhikaraṇya) with the Adhvaryu and sacrificer who are the agents of the offense.

children.text: 'yadi rathaṃtarasāmā somaḥ syādaindravāyavāgrāngarahāngṛhṇīyāt' 'bhinne juhoti, yo vai saṃvatsaramukhyamabhṛtvāgniṃ cinute' ityādiṣu saṃpratipannanimitteṣu taddarśanāt |
children.translated_text: In cases where an occasion is accepted — such as 'yadi rathantarasāmā somaḥ syād aindravāyavāgrān grahān gṛhṇīyāt' (if the Soma has the Rathantara Sāman, one should take the cup-drawings beginning with the Aindravāyava), 'bhinne juhoti' (when [the fire] is split, he offers), 'yo vai saṃvatsaram ukhyam abhṛtvāgniṃ cinute' (whoever, without carrying the vessel for a year, constructs the fire-altar) — such [conditional] usage is observed.
Therefore — only permanent status alone is appropriate for the curd-offering (dadhigraha).
The mention of deity-disturbance and its appeasement is a laudatory passage (arthavāda) in praise of the curd-offering that is to be enjoined. || MJaiNyC_4,4.7-8 ||

In the Jyotiṣṭoma, it is heard: 'yāṃ vai kāṃcid adhvaryu-yajamānaś ca devatām antarītaḥ, tasyā āvṛścyete | yat prājāpatyaṃ dadhigrahaṃ gṛhṇāti, śamayaty evainām' (when the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer have offended any deity whatsoever, they invite her wrath; when he takes the Prājāpatya curd-offering [cup-drawing], he appeases her). This curd-offering (dadhigraha) is of dual nature — both permanent (nitya) and occasional (naimittika). Why? Because both kinds of reasons exist. The offense against a deity is mentioned, and the cup-drawing is stated to appease it. The offense is the occasion (nimitta), and the cup-drawing is the occasional rite (naimittika) — this appears [to be the case]. Similarly, seniority (jyeṣṭhatva) is recorded: 'jyeṣṭho vā eṣa grahāṇām' (this is verily the chief of the cup-drawings). Seniority means being praiseworthy. And that is consistent with permanent status. For an occasional rite, being contingent, is not praiseworthy. Therefore — by the force of both reasons, it is of dual nature — if so argued, that is not correct. Because the offense against a deity is not an occasion (nimitta). For [it to be] an occasion, a conditional particle 'yadi' (if) should be appended, or the locative case should be heard.
(In the sixth [adhikaraṇa], on the occasional nature of the Vaiśvānara [offering], sūtras 12–13)

children.text: vaiśvānaraś ca nityaḥ syān nityaiḥ samānasaṃkhyatvāt / Jaim_4,4.12 /
children.translated_text: The Vaiśvānara too would be permanent, because of having the same number as the permanent [rites]. / Jaim_4,4.12 /
Or [it is performed] optionally, because of the connection with what has arisen [as an occasion]. / Jaim_4,4.13 /
START MJaiNy 4,4.9
He composes the sixth adhikaraṇa —
Is the Vaiśvānara sacrifice in the fire-altar construction (citi) permanent or occasional?
Permanent, as before; but because of the 'yat' particle [indicating a condition], the latter. // MJaiNy_4,4.9 //

children.text:
agnicayane śrūyate-'yo vai saṃvatsaramukhyamabhṛtvāgniṃ cinute |
yathā sāminarbho vipadyate, tādṛgeva tadārtimārchet |
vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ purastānnirvapet' iti |
ukhā piṭharaḥ |
tāmukhām 'yañjānaḥ prathamaṃ manaḥ' ityādiprapāṭhakāmnātairmantraiḥ saṃpādya, tasyāmukhāyāmagniṃ nidhāya, ṣaḍudyāme dvādaśodyāme vā śikye tāmukhāmavasthāpya, tacchikyaṃ svakaṇṭhe baddhvā, tamukhyamagniṃ saṃvatsaraṃ bhṛtvā paścādiṣṭakābhiragniścetavyaḥ |
abharaṇe tvapūrṇagarbhapātavadvināśaḥ syāt |
tato vaiśvānareṣṭiṃ cayanātprāgeva kuryāt, ityarthaḥ |
atrāpyantarāyavākyavadabharaṇavākyasyārthavādatvānnityā vaiśvānareṣṭiḥ- iti cet |

children.translated_text: that is not correct.

children.text: 'yaḥ pumānabhṛtvāgniṃ cinute, sa nivapet' iti kartṛsamānādhikṛtayacchabdabalādabharaṇeṣṭayornimittanaimittika bhāvābabhāsāt |
children.translated_text: Because from the force of the 'yat' particle in 'yaḥ pumān abhṛtvāgniṃ cinute, sa nirvapet' (the man who constructs the fire-altar without carrying — he should offer), being in co-reference with the agent, the appearance of the occasion-occasioned relationship between the not-carrying and the offering [is established].

children.text: kiṃca dadhigrahasya nitvasya pākṣikatvarūpaṃ naimittikatvaṃ viruddham |
children.translated_text: Moreover, for the curd-offering (dadhigraha), whose permanent status [is established], the occasional nature — which would mean contingent status — was contradictory.

children.text: iha tu nityatve pramāṇabhāvādekameva naimittikatvamitvavirodhaḥ || MJaiNyC_4,4.9 ||
children.translated_text: But here, since there is no evidence for permanent status, the occasional nature alone [applies] — hence there is no contradiction. || MJaiNyC_4,4.9 ||

In the fire-altar construction (agnicayana), it is heard: 'yo vai saṃvatsaram ukhyam abhṛtvāgniṃ cinute | yathā sāminar bho vipadyate, tādṛg eva tad ārtim ārchet | vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ purastān nirvapet' (whoever constructs the fire-altar without carrying the vessel [fire] for a year — just as a tree is ruined by its lord, so would he invite affliction — he should first offer a Vaiśvānara [cake] on twelve potsherds). The 'ukhā' is a pot (piṭhara). Having prepared that pot with the mantras recorded in the prapāṭhaka beginning with 'yuñjānaḥ prathamaṃ manaḥ,' placing the fire in that pot, setting the pot on a sling (śikya) [carried over] six or twelve stages, tying that sling around his own neck, and carrying that vessel-fire for a year — only afterward should the fire-altar be constructed with bricks. But if he does not carry [the fire for a year], the result would be destruction, as in the case of the fall of an unripened embryo. Therefore, the Vaiśvānara offering should be performed before the construction — this is the meaning. Here too, just as the sentence about deity-offense was a laudatory passage, so the sentence about not-carrying is also a laudatory passage — hence the Vaiśvānara offering is permanent — if so argued,
(In the seventh [adhikaraṇa], on the occasional nature of the sixth layer [of the fire-altar], sūtras 14–18)
The sixth layer — as in the previous [case]. / Jaim_4,4.14 /
And because of the equal number with those [five layers]. / Jaim_4,4.15 /
And because of the consistency of the laudatory passage. / Jaim_4,4.16 /

children.text: ekacitir vā syād apavṛkte hi codyate nimittena / Jaim_4,4.17 /
children.translated_text: Or there would be a single layer, for [the sixth] is enjoined when [the five] have been completed, with an occasion [specified]. / Jaim_4,4.17 /
Because of the conflict [between the two views], [the sixth layer] has the same number as those [five — making six total]. / Jaim_4,4.18 /
START MJaiNy 4,4.10
He composes the seventh adhikaraṇa —
Is the sixth layer permanent or not? Because of the [first five layers'] requirement [of the fire-altar];
since [the sixth is enjoined] when [the previous construction] has been completed without establishment, made into an occasion — the latter [i.e., occasional]. // MJaiNy_4,4.10 //

children.text:
agnau śrūyate- 'saṃvatsaro vā enaṃ pratiṣṭhāyai nudate, yo agniṃ citvā na pratitiṣṭhati, pañca pūrvāścitayo bhavanti, atha ṣaṣṭhīṃ citiṃ cinute' iti |
lāṅgalena kṛṣṭe vyāmamātre bhūpradeśe nānāvidhābhiriṣṭikābhiḥ pakṣyākāreṇa sthānaṃ niṣpādyate, seyaṃ citiḥ |
tādṛśyaḥ pañca citayaḥ pūrvāḥ kriyante |
tataḥ ṣaṣṭhī citiḥ |
tatra 'ṣaṇṇāṃ pūraṇī ṣaṣṭhī' iti vyutpattau pūrvāḥ pañca citūrapekṣatre |
anyathā ṣaṭsaṃkhyāpūrakatvāsaṃbhavāt |
tasmāt- ekaprayoganiyamāditaracitivannityā- iti cet |
maivam |
'agniṃ citvā' iti pūrvābhireva pañcamiścityasyāgnicayanasya samāptau stratyāṃ paścāt- 'yo 'tra na pratitiṣṭhati, asau ṣaṣṭhīṃ cinute' iti kartṛsamānādhikṛtena yacchabdenāpratiṣṭhāṃ nimittīkṛttya vidhānātṣaṣṭhī naimittikī |
tataḥ- pañcacitiko nityo 'gniḥ, naimittikastvekacitikaḥ, iti prayogaikyam |
children.translated_text: Therefore — the permanent fire-altar has five layers, while the occasional has a single layer — hence there is unity of performance.
And the ordinal suffix is explained with reference to the statement [of enumeration].
'Five prior layers have been stated.

children.text: athābhidhāsyamānāṃ ṣaṣṭhīṃ citiṃ cinute, iti vacanavyaktiḥ || MJaiNyC_4,4.10 ||
children.translated_text: Then he constructs the sixth layer that is about to be stated' — this is the explanation of the expression. || MJaiNyC_4,4.10 ||

In the fire-altar [section], it is heard: 'saṃvatsaro vā enaṃ pratiṣṭhāyai nudate, yo agniṃ citvā na pratitiṣṭhati, pañca pūrvāś citayo bhavanti, atha ṣaṣṭhīṃ citiṃ cinute' (a year pushes him toward establishment; he who, having constructed the fire-altar, does not attain establishment — there are five prior layers, and then he constructs a sixth layer). A layer (citi) is a structure fashioned in the shape of a bird with various kinds of bricks on a plot of land a vyāma (fathom) in extent, plowed with a plow. Five such layers are first constructed. Then the sixth layer [follows]. Therein, in the derivation 'ṣaṇṇāṃ pūraṇī ṣaṣṭhī' (the sixth is what completes six), the five prior layers are presupposed — otherwise, the completion of the number six would not be possible. Therefore — by the fixed rule of a single performance, the sixth layer is permanent, like the other layers — if so argued, that is not correct. By 'agniṃ citvā' (having constructed the fire-altar), with the five [layers] alone the fire-altar construction is complete; afterward — 'he who does not attain establishment therein constructs a sixth' — through the 'yat' particle in co-reference with the agent, the non-establishment being made into an occasion, the sixth [layer] is occasional.
The ancestral offering (pitṛyajña) would be non-accessory, because of having its own time. / Jaim_4,4.19 /
(In the eighth [adhikaraṇa], on the non-accessory nature of the Piṇḍapitṛyajña, sūtras 19–21)
Because of being enumerated as equal. / Jaim_4,4.20 /
And because of being observed when [the Darśa sacrifice is] prohibited. / Jaim_4,4.21 /
START MJaiNy 4,4.11
He composes the eighth adhikaraṇa —

children.text: kratvaṅgaṃ syānna vā piṇḍapitṛyajñaḥ kratau hi saḥ /
children.translated_text: Would the Piṇḍapitṛyajña (ancestral cake-offering) be an accessory of the sacrifice, or not? For it [occurs] in the sacrifice;
because the new-moon [day] is stated, [it is not an accessory] — the statement of its time [shows] it is for human purpose (puruṣārtha). // MJaiNy_4,4.11 //

children.text:
idamāmnāyate- 'amāvāsyāyāmaparāhṇe piṇḍapitṛyaccena caranti' iti |
tatra-amāvāsyāśabdavācye karmaṇi vidhīyamānatvādayaṃ piṇḍapitṛyajñaḥ kratvaṅgam- iti cet |
maivam |
amāvāsyāśabdasya kālavācitvāt |

children.translated_text: But its use for the rite is figurative (lākṣaṇika).

children.text: na ca - vākyena ktatvaṅgatvābhāve 'pi prakaraṇena tadbhevat- iti vācyam |
children.translated_text: Nor should one say that even in the absence of accessory-status from the sentence, it would be so from the context —
because [the Piṇḍapitṛyajña] is studied independently (anārabhyādhīta), not beginning from [the Darśa sacrifice].
Therefore — this is for human purpose (puruṣārtha). || MJaiNyC_4,4.11 ||

This is recorded: 'amāvāsyāyām aparāhṇe piṇḍapitṛyajñena caranti' (on the new-moon day, in the afternoon, they perform the ancestral cake-offering). Therein — since it is enjoined in the rite denoted by the word 'amāvāsyā' (new-moon), this Piṇḍapitṛyajña is an accessory of the sacrifice — if so argued, that is not correct. Because the word 'amāvāsyā' denotes the time.
(In the ninth [adhikaraṇa], on whether the rope (raśanā) is an accessory of the sacrificial post (yūpa), sūtras 22–24)

children.text: paśvaṅgaṃ raśanā syāt tadāgame vidhānāt / Jaim_4,4.22 /
children.translated_text: The rope (raśanā) would be an accessory of the animal, since [it is] enjoined upon the arrival of that [animal]. / Jaim_4,4.22 /
Or [it is] an accessory of the sacrificial post, because of the consecration of that [post]. / Jaim_4,4.23 /
And the laudatory passage [supports] that which serves that [post's] purpose. / Jaim_4,4.24 /
START MJaiNy 4,4.12
He composes the ninth adhikaraṇa —
Is the rope for the purpose of the animal or of the sacrificial post? Because of its connection with the animal, [it is] for the animal;

children.text: paśvarthā trivṛtrā yūpaṃ parivīyeti yūpagā // MJaiNy_4,4.12 //
children.translated_text: for the animal, [it is] a triple [rope]; but 'he wraps the post' — hence [it is] for the post. // MJaiNy_4,4.12 //

children.text:
jyotiṣṭome śrūyate- 'āśvinaṃ grahaṃ gṛhītvā trivṛtā yūpaṃ parivīyā'gneyaṃ sabanayiṃ paśumupākaroti' iti |
tatra- savanīyapaśoragnīṣomīyavikṛtitvāccodakaprāptaṃ yūpaparivyāṇaṃ kālopalakṣaṇārthamanūdya parivyāṇottarakāle trivṛdraśanopalakṣitapaśorupākaraṇaṃ vidhīyate |
tato 'tra raśanāyāḥ paśvanvayātpaśubandhanena paśoritastato 'pakramaṇanivāraṇarūpadṛṣṭārtha lābhācca paśvarthā raśanā- iti cet |
maivam |
'trivṛtā' iti tṛtīyayā 'yūpam' iti dvitīyayā ca śeṣaśeṣibhāvāvanamāt, avyavahitānvayalābhācca raśanā yūpārthā |
kālastu 'āśvinaṃ grahaṃ gṛhītvā ' ityanenaivopalakṣitaḥ |

children.translated_text: The firmness of the post, like preventing the animal from moving away, is also a visible purpose.

children.text: na ca- parivyāṇena dorḍhya codakādeva siddham - iti vācyam |
children.translated_text: Nor should one say that firmness is already accomplished by the initial wrapping through the injunctive force (codaka) alone —
because when that firmness is [already] accomplished, the acceptance of a second wrapping with a [second] rope follows from the earlier injunction itself.

children.text: tasmāt - iyaṃ dvitīyā raśanā yūpārthā || MJaiNyC_4,4.12 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — this second rope is for the post. || MJaiNyC_4,4.12 ||

In the Jyotiṣṭoma, it is heard: 'āśvinaṃ grahaṃ gṛhītvā trivṛtā yūpaṃ parivīyāgneyaṃ savanīyaṃ paśum upākaroti' (having taken the Āśvina cup-drawing, wrapping the post with a triple [rope], he initiates the Āgneya pressing-animal). Therein — the wrapping of the post by the pressing-animal, being a modification of the Agnīṣomīya [animal sacrifice] obtained by the injunctive force (codaka), is restated as a time-marker; and the initiation of the animal marked by the triple rope is enjoined for the post-wrapping time. Therefore, the rope here, because of its connection with the animal — and because tying the animal to the post prevents it from moving away in various directions — serves a visible purpose; hence the rope is for the animal — if so argued, that is not correct. Because from the instrumental case in 'trivṛtā' (with a triple [rope]) and the accusative in 'yūpam' (the post), the subordinate-superordinate relationship is understood; and because of the immediately contiguous syntactic connection, the rope is for the post. The time [marker] is already indicated by 'āśvinaṃ grahaṃ gṛhītvā' (having taken the Āśvina cup-drawing).
(In the tenth [adhikaraṇa], on whether the sacrificial peg (svaru) is an accessory of the animal, sūtras 25–28)
The peg (svaru) too, because of being a part [of the post]. / Jaim_4,4.25 /
And the ransom (niṣkraya), as pertaining to an accessory of that [post]. / Jaim_4,4.26 /
Or [it is] an accessory of the animal, because it serves that [animal's] purpose. / Jaim_4,4.27 /
The statement about ransom is figurative (bhakti). / Jaim_4,4.28 /
START MJaiNy 4,4.13
He composes the tenth adhikaraṇa —
Is the peg (svaru) an accessory of the post or of the animal? Because of the statement 'of the post,' the first [view];
because of the statement 'he anoints the animal with the peg,' the accessory-status to the animal is clear. // MJaiNy_4,4.13 //

children.text: agnīṣomīyapaśau śrūyate - 'yūpasya svaruṃ karoti' 'svaruṇā paśumanakti' iti |

children.translated_text: Therein — because of the statement of the peg's connection with the post, [the peg is] an accessory of the post — if so argued,
that is not correct.

children.text: 'svaruṇā paśum' iti tṛtīyayā dvitīyayā cāṅgāṅgibhāvāvagatau saṃvandhasāmānyavācinyāḥ ṣaṣṭhyā yūpīyacchedanajanyatvābhiprāyeṇāpi netuṃ śakyatvāt |
children.translated_text: Because from the instrumental case in 'svaruṇā' (with the peg) and the accusative in 'paśum' (the animal), the subordinate-superordinate relationship is understood; and since the genitive — which expresses connection in general — can be led [to mean] the origination of the peg from the cutting of the post,
therefore — the peg is an accessory of the animal. || MJaiNyC_4,4.13 ||
In the Agnīṣomīya animal [sacrifice], it is heard: 'yūpasya svaruṃ karoti' (he makes a peg for the post) and 'svaruṇā paśum anakti' (he anoints the animal with the peg).
(In the eleventh [adhikaraṇa], on the accessory-status of the Āghāra and the like, sūtras 29–38)
In the Darśapūrṇamāsa, the offerings (ijyā) are principals, because of non-distinction. / Jaim_4,4.29 /

children.text: api vāṅgāni kānicid yeṣv aṅgatvena saṃstutiḥ sāmānyo hy abhisaṃbanhdaḥ / Jaim_4,4.30 /
children.translated_text: Or some would be accessories, for which the praise as accessory is heard; the connection [with the principal] is general. / Jaim_4,4.30 /
And similarly, the observation of another purpose. / Jaim_4,4.31 /

children.text: avaśiṣṭaṃ tu kāraṇaṃ pradhāneṣu guṇasya vidyamānatvāt / Jaim_4,4.32 /
children.translated_text: But the remainder [is an accessory] because of being the cause — since the subsidiary is present in the principals. / Jaim_4,4.32 /
Not in the unstated [cases is there] observation of another purpose, because of serving another's purpose. / Jaim_4,4.33 /

children.text: pṛthaktve tv abhidhānayor niveśaḥ śrutito vyapadeśāc ca tatpunarmukhyalakṣaṇaṃ yatphalavatvaṃ tatsaṃnidhāv asaṃyuktaṃ tadaṅgaṃ syād bhāgitvāt kāraṇasyāśrutaś cānyasaṃbandhaḥ / Jaim_4,4.34 /
children.translated_text: But when [the offerings] are separate, by the designations, the establishment is from scripture and from designation; that which again bears the chief characteristic — that it possesses a fruit — in its proximity, that which is unconnected would be its accessory, because of participation; and the connection of the cause which is unheard. / Jaim_4,4.34 /

children.text: guṇāś ca nāmasaṃyuktā vidhīyante nāṅgeṣūpapadyante / Jaim_4,4.35 /
children.translated_text: And the subsidiaries connected with the name are enjoined [and] do not apply to the accessories. / Jaim_4,4.35 /

children.text: tulyā ca kāraṇaśrutir anyair aṅgāṅgisaṃbandhaḥ / Jaim_4,4.36 /
children.translated_text: The statement of the cause is the same [for all]; the accessory-superordinate relationship [is established] by others. / Jaim_4,4.36 /

children.text: utpattāv abhisaṃbandhas tasmād aṅgopadeśaḥ syāt / Jaim_4,4.37 /
children.translated_text: In the origination, the connection [exists]; therefore there would be instruction as accessory. / Jaim_4,4.37 /
And similarly, the observation of another purpose. / Jaim_4,4.38 /
START MJaiNy 4,4.14
He composes the eleventh adhikaraṇa —
Are the Āghāra and the like also principals? Or not? Like the Āgneya and the like, they would be [principals];
six principals are established by their names; the rest are otherwise, because of the praise as accessories. // MJaiNy_4,4.14 //

children.text:
darśapūrṇa māsayorāghārājyabhāgaprayājānuyājādayaḥ kālasaṃyogamantareṇā'mnātāḥ |
āgneyādayaḥ ṣaḍyāgāḥ kālasaṃyogena coditāḥ |
tatra - āgneyādīnāṃ yathā prādhānyamaṅgīkṛtam, tathaivā'ghārādīnāmapyaṅgīkartavyam |
yathā rājasūye parasparavilakṣaṇānāmiṣṭipaśusomānāṃ bahūnāṃ samaprādhānyam, tadvat |
ekaprakaraṇapāṭhaścobhayatrāpi samānaḥ |
tasmāt - āghārādīnāmāgneyādīnāṃ ca samapradhānyam - iti prāpte -
brūmaḥ- 'rājā svārājyakāmo rājasūyena yajeta' ityatra rājasūyaśabdo rājasaṃbandhātpravartamāno rājakartṛkāṇāmekaprakaraṇa paṭhitānāṃ sarveṣāṃ yāgānāṃ nāmadheyaṃ bhavati |
darśapūrṇamāsaśabdau tu kālavācinau santau kālasaṃyogena vihitānāmevā'gneyādīnāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ yāgānāṃ nāmadheyatāṃ pratipadyete |
tataḥ 'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta' iti vākyena tannāmadheyavaśādāgneyādayaḥ ṣaḍeva yāgāḥ phalasaṃbandhitvena pratīyamānā mukhyāḥ |
anye tvājyabhāgāghārādayastannāmarahitā niṣphalā āgneyādīnāṃ śeṣāḥ |
evaṃ satyaṅgatvena stutirupapadyate |
'cakṣuṣī vā ete yajñasya, yadājyabhāgau' ityājyabhāgau yajñaśarīrasyāṅgino 'ṅgatvena stūyete |
'yatprayājānuyājā ijyante varma vā etaścajñāya kriyate' iti yajñaśarīropakārakavarmatvena prayājānuyājāḥ stūyante |
children.translated_text: 'When the <s>prayājas</s> and <s>anuyājas</s> are offered, this armor of the sacrifice is made' — here, the <s>prayājas</s> and <s>anuyājas</s> are praised as serving the sacrificial body in the form of armor.
The same should be illustrated for the <s>āghāra</s> and the like.
And this [praise] is possible when there is a [genuine] resemblance.
Therefore — the <s>āghāra</s> and the others do not have principalness. || MJaiNyC_4,4.14 ||

In the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices), the <s>āghāra</s> (butter oblation), <s>ājyabhāga</s> (clarified butter portion), <s>prayāja</s> (preliminary offerings), <s>anuyāja</s> (concluding offerings), and the like are recited without connection with time. The six offerings — <s>Āgneya</s> and the others — are enjoined with connection with time [i.e., the new moon, full moon, etc.]. Therein — just as the principalness of the <s>Āgneya</s> and the others is accepted, so too the principalness of the <s>āghāra</s> and the others should be accepted. Just as in the <s>Rājasūya</s>, the many mutually distinct <s>iṣṭis</s>, <s>paśus</s>, and <s>Soma</s> sacrifices have equal principalness — so too here. And the recitation within a single context is common to both [groups]. Therefore — the <s>āghāra</s> and the others and the <s>Āgneya</s> and the others have equal principalness — having arrived at this position, we say: In '<s>rājā svārājyakāmo rājasūyena yajeta</s>' (a king desiring sovereignty should sacrifice with the <s>Rājasūya</s>), the word <s>Rājasūya</s>, operating because of its connection with the king, becomes the name-designation of all offerings recited in one context that are performed by a royal performer. But the words <s>Darśa</s> (new-moon) and <s>Pūrṇamāsa</s> (full-moon), being time-denoting, apply as the name-designation only to the six offerings — the <s>Āgneya</s> and the others — that are enjoined in connection with time. Therefore, by the sentence '<s>darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta</s>' (one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>), only the six offerings — the <s>Āgneya</s> and the others — are understood as principal, being connected with the fruit by virtue of the name-designation. But the others — the <s>ājyabhāga</s>, <s>āghāra</s>, and the like — lacking that name, are fruitless and are remainders (<s>śeṣa</s>) of the <s>Āgneya</s> and the others. This being so, praise in the form of subsidiary-nature is appropriate. 'The two <s>ājyabhāgas</s> are indeed the eyes of the sacrifice' — here, the two <s>ājyabhāgas</s> are praised as subsidiaries of the sacrificial body, which is the principal.
(In the twelfth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>], on the subsidiary nature of the <s>Dīkṣaṇīyā</s> and the like in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, <s>sūtras</s> 39-41:)

children.text: jyotiṣṭome tulyāny aviśiṣṭaṃ hi kāraṇam / Jaim_4,4.39 /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, [the <s>Dīkṣaṇīyā</s> and others are] equal [to the <s>Soma</s> offerings], because the cause [for principalness] is not differentiated. / Jaim_4,4.39 /

children.text: guṇānāṃ tūtpattivākyena saṃbandhāt kāraṇaśrutis tasmāt somaḥ pradhānaṃ syāt / Jaim_4,4.40 /
children.translated_text: But since the accessories are connected by the origination-sentence, and the [relevant] cause is heard [only for <s>Soma</s>], therefore <s>Soma</s> [alone] would be the principal. / Jaim_4,4.40 /
And thus the observation of a different purpose [confirms this]. / Jaim_4,4.41 /

He composes the twelfth <s>adhikaraṇa</s> —

children.text: mukhyā na vā dīkṣaṇīyā mukhyā syātsomasāmyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Are the <s>Dīkṣaṇīyā</s> [offerings] and the like principal or not? They are principal, because of equality with <s>Soma</s>;

children.text: jyortiṣi yasya stomāḥ syuriti somaikamukhyatā // MJaiNy_4,4.15 //
children.translated_text: but in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, [only] that [sacrifice] which has the <s>Stomas</s> — hence <s>Soma</s> alone is principal. // MJaiNy_4,4.15 //

children.text:
'jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajeta' ityasya prakaraṇe- aindravāyavagrahādayaḥ somayāgāḥ, dīkṣaṇīyādīṣṭayaḥ, agnīṣoyādi paśavaḥ, agnīṣoyādipaśavaḥ, āmnātāḥ |
tatra - āgneyādipakṣapātidarśapūrṇamāsanāmavajjyotiṣṭomanāmnaḥ somapakṣapāte hetvabhāvena rājasūyanāmavatprakṛtasarvayāgasādhāraṇatvāt, somasamānānāṃ dīkṣaṇīyādīnāmapyasti mukhyatvam- iti cet |
maivam |
somayāgapakṣapāte hetusadbhāvāt |
'jyortīṣi stomā yasya yajñasya so 'yaṃ jyotiṣṭomaḥ' iti hi tadvyutpattiḥ |
ata eva brāhmaṇam - 'trivṛt, pañcadaśaḥ, saptadaśaḥ, ekaviṃśaḥ, etāni vāya tāni jyotiṃṣi ya etasya stomāḥ' iti |
children.translated_text: Hence the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [states]: '<s>trivṛt, pañcadaśaḥ, saptadaśaḥ, ekaviṃśaḥ, etāni vāva tāni jyotīṃṣi ya etasya stomāḥ</s>' (the three-fold, fifteen-fold, seventeen-fold, twenty-one-fold — these indeed are the luminaries, which are the <s>Stomas</s> of this [sacrifice]).
The luminary-nature (<s>jyotiṣṭva</s>) of the <s>Stomas</s> is their capacity to illuminate the sacrifice.

children.text: na ceṣṭayaḥ paśavo vā trivṛdādistomayuktāḥ pratibhāsante |
children.translated_text: And neither the <s>Iṣṭis</s> nor the animal sacrifices appear to be connected with the <s>Stomas</s> — the three-fold and the like.

children.text: tasmāt - jyotiṣṭomanāmnā somayāgānāmeva phalasaṃbandhāvagamādaphalā iṣṭipaśavo na mukhyā iti somayāgānāmeva prādhānyam || MJaiNyC_4,4.15 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore — since the name <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> conveys the connection with fruit only for the <s>Soma</s> offerings, the <s>Iṣṭis</s> and animal sacrifices, being fruitless, are not principal — hence the principalness belongs to the <s>Soma</s> offerings alone. || MJaiNyC_4,4.15 ||

In the context of '<s>jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajeta</s>' (one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>) — the <s>Soma</s> offerings such as the <s>Aindravāyava-graha</s> (cup of <s>Indra</s>-<s>Vāyu</s>) and the like, the <s>Iṣṭis</s> (simple offerings) such as the <s>Dīkṣaṇīyā</s> (consecration offering) and the like, and the animal sacrifices such as the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> and the like — are recited. Therein — just as the name <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> tends toward the <s>Āgneya</s> and other [offerings], so too the name <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, in the absence of a reason for tending toward the <s>Soma</s> [offerings alone], should be common to all recited offerings — like the name <s>Rājasūya</s>; therefore, the <s>Dīkṣaṇīyā</s> and the like, being equal to <s>Soma</s>, also have principalness — if so it is argued, that is not correct. Because there is a reason for [the name] tending toward the <s>Soma</s> offerings. For the etymological derivation of that [name] is: '<s>jyotīṃṣi stomā yasya yajñasya so 'yaṃ jyotiṣṭomaḥ</s>' (that sacrifice whose <s>Stomas</s> are luminaries — that is the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>).
Thus ends the fourth <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> in the illustrious <s>Mādhavīya Jaiminīya-Nyāyamālā-Vistara</s>.
And the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> is concluded. //
